  has asked the colony for a meal. Ashford is struggling, since the plague, and their clothes show it."). The colonists
  see to it first by themselves (`OutsiderAutoMath`: a meal asked for weighs 8.5, hungry or not), or the player through
  the right-click's meal; the one who asked takes it whatever their mood and thanks them, and their people remember it
  ("gaveGift"). Asks are the session's only (a reload lets one lapse) and stand eighteen hours. From a flourishing town
  their clothes are a quality step better (never to legendary), and about a third of the time one of them carries in a
  small gift of 20 to 45 silver by the colony's wealth, set down at the colony (`Couriers.Deliver` with them as bearer).
  Decided here: only the two ends show (poor and thriving towns look ordinary), camps are dressed and lose a pack beast but
  don't ask for meals (their asks are their own), and the gifts are visitors'.
- **Ties make a people's own events and camps come (B14, `Peoples/PeopleTies.cs`).** What binds a people to the colony
  (`PeopleTies.Of`): a marriage between the two, a ward or hostage of theirs at the colony or the colony's at theirs, an
  envoy either way, a pact, fealty either way (the colony sworn to them, or a vassal town of theirs), a debt of honour
  either way. A broken word (`PeopleTiesMath.BrokenDeeds`: a pact or truce broken, the word broken, fealty renounced, a
  contract broken) counts while its memory is still 3 strong. The peoples' own events name their callings on their defs
  (`HappeningExtension.callings`, 77 events: every one that comes by itself; a follow-up comes of what started it, and the
  art handed on, which any of a dozen peoples sends, is weighed as ever): a bound people's come half again as often, a
  broken word's a third less (`PeopleTiesMath.Factor`, both together about even), on Rimfolk's own rhythm
  (`HappeningTracker.Weight`) and the storyteller's (`ChanceFactorNow`). The same for their camps: a kind only their
  calling sends (`CampKindDef.calling`), and the people a camp is drawn from. Their letters close with the tie in a line
  (`PeopleTies.LetterLine`, the strongest: a marriage, a ward, a hostage, fealty, a pact, an envoy, a debt; in the
  letters' style; each either way round where it can be: theirs at the colony or the colony's own with them, for a ward,
  a hostage, a spouse, an envoy and fealty). Their gifts go first to the colonist who carries the tie (`PeopleTiesMath.CarrierRank`: the ward's
  guardian, the one married in, the colonist a debt is about, else the colony's speaker for a pact, fealty or an envoy):
  the event is cast first with `PeopleEvents.Takers` yielding only them (`PeopleTies.Giving`), and when the event's own
  needs rule them out it is cast again as ever. Read once an hour; nothing saved.
- **Kin hear of their town's hard year (B17, `World/KinNews.cs`).** When a bad world event runs at a people, those at the
  colony's homes with a tie to them (`KinNews.KinOf`: their ward or hostage here, one of theirs married into the colony,
  their envoy here, a colonist who came from them, that is of one of Rimfolk's peoples' own kinds and theirs alone) hear
  of it with the next courier to reach the colony (`CourierTracker`, as they come in, beside the courier's own line) or by
  the road after two and a half days: a letter from home at each home with any of them (`CC_Kin_Letter_*`, by courier or
  road, the event's kind, the tie, one or several; the letters' style), a mood (`Rimfolk_KinWorried`, -3 for four days),
  and the worry on the heart's card while it runs (`KinNews.Worry`, the worry feeling's feed). Six times in ten, when food
  or medicine would answer it (`KinNewsMath.SendFor`) and a colonist is among them, the council is asked (when its pace
  allows: `Rimfolk_Dilemma_KinSendHome`, `DilemmaWorker_KinSendHome`): send a fifth of the stores' raw food (10 to 60) or
  medicine (2 to 6) home with the next courier, carried out to the gate for a runner of theirs
  (`DilemmaEffect_KinSendHome`, the carry's own play-out); it counts as the colony's help in the world event (its help,
  and its deed in the ending's letter), their people remember it ("hardship"), and the one who asked is glad
  (`Rimfolk_KinSentHelp`). The colony's own ward or envoy at the struck town writes of it after a day; from a plague town
  half the time they come home early (the card's own recall). Flavour and mood only: nothing binds a family line.
- **The neighbours for good keep the colony's days (B22, `Camps/HoldingDays.cs`).** The holding at ease with the colony
  (tension under 50) comes to a day of the calendar kept with a feast, a bonfire or games, or the harvest's day
  (`ColonyCalendar.KeepDay`), and to a custom whose kept answer gathers the colony (harvest home, the midsummer bonfire:
  `DilemmaTracker`'s tradition): within eighteen hours, once the gathering is under way, up to three of their grown
  walk over to join it as its guests (`LordJob_PlayOut.guests`, kept at places round it and served at a feast; a message
  says they are walking over), and the first of them to come within seven cells of its spot sets down a dish from their
  own stores (`HoldingDays.SetDownDish`: simple meals, one each, from their provisions, `HoldingDaysMath.Dish`), with a
  line and a message as it is set down; a gathering over before any of them got there leaves the dish at home. A colonist of the
  colony buried in the last two days brings two of them to the grave (the holding's errand to one spot, `"spot"`, a line
  or two while they stand there), each grave once. Their own good days (decided here: the day in the year they settled,
  from the first year on; a birthday of one of theirs; and, rarely, a wedding in the family when two of their grown who
  are free and not kin are there, made a marriage in the game) ask the colonist warmest with them (two or more) over to
  their fire for the evening (a visit play-out to the holding's own fire). Decided here: a birth is left out, as a camp's
  people can't care for a newborn on the map. Saved on the holding: what is due, the last grave, the last good day.
- **A feast's guests bring their town's year (B29, `Diplomacy/FeastYear.cs`).** A guest whose town has a world event
  running there now: a hard year (any bad world event) or a good one (their fair, a bumper harvest). As they come, a
  good year's guest hands over a gift of 60 to 120 silver by the colony's wealth (decided here: guests bring no gift
  otherwise, so the good year's is the gift), and the arrival's letter says each guest's year. The host's toast names it,
  one sentence. At the end a hard year's guest who ate thinks of the meal twice and of each contest half
  (`FeastYearMath.Welcome`). As the night begins after the feast, the hard years' guests who ate ask leave to carry home
  what is left: a free colonist brings two meals a party out of the stores to each of them, never past half of what is
  spare and only plain cooked meals (the keep-out errand's job for food to take home, `Rimfolk_BringOutToKeep`, which
  hands the meals into their pack instead of having them eaten), and they leave with them in the morning. A message
  names who brings what to whom as they set off (decided here: the host grants the ask; there is no question).
- **Camps that come back bring the world's news (B31, `Camps/CampMemory.cs`).** The letter of a remembered camp coming
  back already says what became of them; it now says what they lived through at home too: the newest world event that
  ended at their people since they left (the world events' history), told by its kind and ending (`CampNewsMath.Topic`:
  the fever and who they lost, the drought and whether the rains came, the fire and the new mill, a flood, a hard winter,
  the herds' sickness, a good harvest, the fair, a new head, a war, a raid held or not, rebuilding, holy days, mourning),
  and when the colony helped them in it, that they know. In the camps' style.
- **Seams with the world brought home (0.280.0).** B1 (world events in the peoples' own ways) and B3 (messengers telling
  the road's news) are its own and are reused, not repeated: the kin's word comes with the courier at the moment it
  reaches the colony, after the courier's own spoken line (`CourierTracker`), and touches neither the courier's lines,
  the road's news at the mailbag (`RoadNews`) nor the world events' paragraphs in the peoples' ways; a people's own event
  is cast with both the world event's steer (`WorldSteer.During`) and the tie's gift carrier (`PeopleTies.Giving`).
- **Dev mode** ("Rimfolk", "Peoples' ties: ..."): what binds each people (log); one of a bound people's own events now
  (the tie's line in its letter, the gift's carrier first); the new head comes to the gate now; a
  visitor from a struggling town asks for a meal; the visitors here dressed as from a flourishing town; the word of each
  hard year now; help sent home asked now; the neighbours join the gathering under way, come to a colony grave, ask the
  colony's friend over; a feast's guests and their towns' years (log); what each remembered camp would say of home (log).

## Layer 7: The heart (feelings and strain)

Comfort is easy to buy in RimWorld, so mood alone stops meaning much once a colony is rich. The heart adds a slower,
richer layer under it without touching the number the game runs on.

**The safety rule.** Vanilla mood stays the single number the game and every other mod use for mental breaks. Nothing
here patches the mood need, the mood calculation, the mental breaker or which breaks the game picks. The layer lives in
Rimfolk's own save data (`HeartTracker`, a game component of its own) and reaches the game only through things it
already supports: one situational thought (it reads the strain band each time and stores nothing), stat parts on global
work speed, learning, the need for sleep, healing and immunity (an XML patch, conditional so it never fails; see "The
heart, made to count"), one mental state started on purpose, time off through the colonist's timetable and a think-tree
node of its own, and Rimfolk's own systems (wishes, life goals, dreams, decrees, dilemmas, moments, the UI). With the
feature off, the thought and the stat parts contribute nothing and the hooks return 1.

- **Strain** (0 to 100) is a slow reservoir. Each colonist is looked at once an hour, a tenth of the colony at a time.
  Sources build it (19: small letdowns among them, see "One heart" below, and heavy things sinking in toward their
  weight, see "The heart, felt") with their own daily caps and a cap of about 25 a day for everything; new memories count
  once, when they're new (a renewed memory, like a second cold night, counts again). Drains are slow and steady (sleep,
  quiet hours, recreation), less the higher strain is (in full up to 30, 70% from 90) and never below the lasting weight
  of a heavy thing, with chunks for gatherings, good talks and catharsis. Small decaying totals per source and per kind of
  relief say what built it and what eased it lately. The pure math (bands, caps, trait factors, episode odds) is in
  `HeartMath`, covered by the tests.
- **Bands** give the only direct effects: a mood of -4/-8/-14 (the setting "How strongly the bands are felt": -3/-5/-8
  mild, as it shipped, or -5/-10/-18 strong), work speed -3%/-7%/-12% from strained and, from worn down, a little slower
  learning, healing and immunity and a little more sleep (see "The heart, made to count"), darker dreams.
- **The good side** is strain's other side, both at once since the player's change of 9 November 2026 (see "The
  heart's good side" and "The heart, felt" below): it fills slowly at any strain, slower the more there is, hardship
  spends part of it as a cushion, and its bands (steady, in good heart, in high spirits) give a second situational thought
  of the same kind (+3/+6/+10, +2/+3/+5 mild) beside strain's, the upper two brighter dreams, a quicker recovery and a
  little faster learning, healing and immunity, never work speed.
- **Episodes** are the pressure valve, not a punishment: a custom mental state on vanilla's hide-in-room class, started
  silently by the heart (its own letter) and never by the game's break picker, since no MentalBreakDef names it. A think
  tree inserted after the mental states gives it its behavior. Strict conditions (no danger, enough hands, cooldowns,
  nobody left uncared for), and it ends early when a threat appears, a doctor is needed or the room turns too cold or hot.
- **Feelings** are data (`FeelingDef`): thoughts that feed them (by name, pattern or a `HeartTags` extension on the
  thought), a worker for what thoughts can't say, a threshold, and nudges scaled by intensity. They never add mood,
  which would count their causes twice. Nudges stay small: wishes at most half again as likely, moments within half to
  double, strain a few points a day.
- **The heart's needs** (belonging, purpose, safety, freedom) are computed each hour, never saved, and give no mood:
  they show what a life is missing and point wishes and life goals toward it.
- **Removal.** No hediffs and no stored thoughts. The only trace is a colonist in the middle of an episode.

### Life goals that last (the player's decision 8, 6 November 2026)

A life goal is chosen from what fits a colonist (`AspirationDef.who`), made likelier by a spark lately (a memory, a
fight, a brush with death, a loss, a child born, a dream come true, someone close reaching the same goal). In the
player's save, of 38 goals chosen in 88 days 25 came after a battle or a brush with death ("bring down ten mechanoids"
five times), and Stace changed hers four times in 25 days: every raid was a spark for everyone who fought, and a goal
gave way to any spark after ten days. 0.112.0 let a fight spark only the one who brought down the most, at 0.4, and no
goal came from fights at all; the player's word the same day: "some lifegoals should be sparked by fights, no? not 0."
Now (`GoalMath`, pure):

- **A fight sparks those who fought hardest.** The three who brought down the most in it (`FightTop`, more first, the
  first noted of equals), anyone of its fighters downed in it (the goals' own "downed" event since the fight began,
  `AspirationTracker.HappenedSince`) and anyone of ours who carried someone out of it (`FightSides.Carried`) take the
  fight as a spark (`GoalMath.Hardest`, read in `SocialWeb.HardestIn` before the battle's count is reset and before the
  fight's sides are cleared). A brush with death and a loss are still each person's own.
- **The spark's weight spread over a life.** A fight's spark pulls a little less than the rest of life (`SparkPull`:
  0.7, it was 0.4; a nemesis 0.6, everything else 1), both in the chance a spark makes them choose at once (0.6 times
  the strongest pull of their sparks) and in which goal they take. A goal others of their colony hold now weighs less
  (`Shared`: half for one, a third for two), and a fight never sparks a goal someone else at home took up after a fight
  and is still at (`FightMaySpark`, from `Aspiration.spark`), so one fighting goal is never chosen by several at once
  and the colony doesn't fill with mechanoid hunters. Where a goal has several sparks that happened, a brush with death
  or a loss counts first.
- **A goal holds.** A change of heart only after twenty days with the goal (`HoldsDays`, it was ten), only while it's
  under a third done, only for a brush with death or a loss (`Big`), one chance in five a day, and once per goal: the
  goal it brings holds for good (`Aspiration.turned`, saved). A fight or a fine meal never changes a goal held.
- **Measured.** `FairCouncilTests` runs twelve colonists over the save's 88 days, fighting as often as the save (21
  fights in its 128 days, one every six days: nine fight, one is downed and another carries them out), goals reached in
  15 to 90 days and 20 days before the next, fifty runs of a colony under way: goals from fights were 53% under the
  rules before 0.112.0 (the save's own share was 23 of 47), 3% on 0.112.0's and 19% now (a fresh colony 11%: its first
  goals come before its first fight); never two holding one goal from fights at once (six before); changes of heart 16.5
  a run before, 0.3 now, never more than one for a colonist within 25 days. Goals held in an older save stay as they
  are.

### One heart: small letdowns, small joys and good things growing ordinary

Phase 3 of the review (`docs/review-2026-11/`), the player's decisions of 6 November 2026: small letdowns wear on the
heart ("the letdowns also make sense as mood impact, no? But I like strain too though!"), the good side the same way
("the positive mood buffs should also be adjusted accordingly and balanced"), every small mood by the same rule whoever
made it ("then we might also have to look at non-rimfolk moods, right"), and one rule for good things growing ordinary.
The game's mood stays the one number for breaks (the safety rule above): nothing here changes a mood the game or another
mod made.

- **Small letdowns** (`Moods/SmallMoments.cs`, `SmallMomentMath`). Rimfolk's five kinds (everyday pressures, setbacks,
  quiet troubles, nuisances, frictions: a `SetbackExtension`, a `Thought_Pressure`, `Thought_Setback` or
  `Thought_Trouble`, or a `Council_Friction_` or `Council_Nuisance_` name) are each felt as a short, small mood at the
  moment they happen: three points at most, half a day at most. What they would have weighed beyond that moment (their
  size times their days, less the moment's) goes to the heart as strain (`StrainSource.Letdowns`, at the end of the
  list, saved by position), 0.6 a mood-day, within the heart's caps (1.5 a day for the source, at 100% strength, their
  traits counted), so a run of them wears while one passes. The memory that brought it goes on without a mood (its
  `moodPowerFactor` 0) for what else it does: a friction's opinion of the other, what dilemmas, arcs, speech and
  journals look for. The hook is the one every memory passes (`Patch_GoodTimesFade`'s prefix); the heart leaves such a
  memory to its moment (`SmallMoments.Converted`).
- **A lasting one** (the same meal again, days of the same work, someone away, a crowded room, half-built work, a wish
  still waiting, a decree dragging on, a sick friend...) gives no mood of its own any more: a moment when it begins,
  gets worse or holds another day, and strain each hour while it holds at the same rate (its size a day). What the hour
  last saw is kept on the heart unsaved; after a load, what holds already brings no moment until it changes.
- **Small joys**, the mirror: Rimfolk's small good moments (its good memories that no council answer gave, a moment,
  a talk, a kindness, scaled as they're felt, of five points and two days at most as written; a varied table) are each a
  short, small mood at the moment, and what they'd weigh beyond eases strain (`StrainRelief.Joys`, at the end of its
  list), 0.6 a mood-day, within a day's cap of 3. Council rewards, life goals reached and dreams stay moods of their own.
- **A row each.** Each moment is a `Thought_SmallMoment` of one of two defs (`Rimfolk_SmallLetdowns`,
  `Rimfolk_SmallJoys`) carrying its own size, time, words and cause. It has a row of its own under its own name
  (`LabelCap`; the player's request, 6 November 2026: "i'd rather be able to see the small letdowns listed"): the game
  groups thoughts by `GroupsWith`, which here holds only for the same label, so the Mood tab and the game's Needs tab show
  "Not asked along" and "Argued about the temperature x2", added up as they are, and the row's tooltip says what it was
  ("My idea turned down: -2. The council chose the well.") and that the rest goes to the heart. What helps is the fix
  of the letdown behind the row (`SmallMoments.Advice`), else its own hint. Each one still feeds the
  feelings its own memory fed, at the moment's size; a lasting one at its full size while it holds.
- **Every small mood, anyone's.** Each hour the heart adds up every small mood on a colonist's mind, the game's and
  other mods' too, by size and length, not by name (`SmallMomentMath.IsSmall`: six points or less, three days or less
  or lasting): past 8 points of small bad moods each point builds 0.02 strain an hour, past 12 of small good ones each
  eases 0.02, through the same source and relief and their caps. The heavy kinds that have strain sources of their own
  are left to those, so nothing counts twice: the memories the heart counts by its own rules (losses, bad nights, the
  council's hard choices, gatherings, talks), hunger, rest and recreation, pain, the dark, the heart's own strain mood,
  and the moods that feed a feeling that wears (fear, grief, dread, despair). The moods themselves stay as the game and
  the mods made them; only Rimfolk's own became smaller, and only Rimfolk's share a row.
- **The heart's page** names what wore on them and what eased them: "small letdowns (the same meal and my idea turned
  down)", "small joys (a laugh with Ana)" (`PawnHeart.letdownsWhy`, `joysWhy`, saved words like `natureWhy`), and
  "fewer of the small things that keep going wrong" as what would help.
- **Good things grow ordinary** (`Moods/GoodLife.cs`, `GoodLifeMath`), one rule in place of four (standards shrinking the
  council's rewards by up to half and the game's comforts to 90, 80 and 70% on their first 10 points; good memories
  fading up to half sooner from 75% mood; good moods adding up slowly, the third to fifth at 60, 45 and 35% and a quarter
  after; used to the good life). The sum of every good mood on their mind counts in full up to a line their standards
  set, 45 for the modest, then 35, 25 and 15 for the spoiled (a colony used to the good life asks more); of what's above
  it, half of the first 20 points and three quarters of the rest no longer lift them, taken off the good moods by how
  ordinary each is: a fresh joy counts nearly in full and drifts down with its age, an everyday comfort (a lasting mood,
  a kind had often lately) shrinks most, a life goal reached never. One line in a good mood's tooltip says it ("Grown
  ordinary: counts as +3 of +5, part of everyday life now."), one line under the Mood tab gives the sum. One setting,
  "Good things grow ordinary" (`goodGrowsOrdinary`); an older settings file sets it on if any of the four was
  (`GoodLifeMath.MergedSetting`, `ordinaryMerged`). Standards stay (they set the line, sting letdowns up to 40% more and
  make wishes come sooner); rewards are given at the reward strength alone.
- **Off.** With the heart off, the deeper game hooks off or "Advisor only", small letdowns and joys are moods of their
  own as before. Older saves: memories given before keep their moods and run out as they were; a lasting one turns to
  moments at the next hour; the heart's lists grow by a source and a relief (padded with nothing); shortened memories
  from the old fading rule keep their time.

### The heart's good side: in good heart, in high spirits

The player's request of 6 November 2026, approved as proposed ("there should perhaps also be a counterweight/side to
strain, right? If they have positive impacts over an extended period"): one heart with two sides, not a new system.
`Heart/GoodHeart.cs` (the rules in `HeartMath`, "The good side"), `GoodRelease.cs`, `HeartCard.cs`.

- **Both sides at once** (the player's change of 9 November 2026, replacing the one axis it shipped with: "the good
  side should also be able to develop at the same time, not only when strain is at 0"). The good side (0 to 100,
  `PawnHeart.good`) and strain may both stand above nothing, and both band moods apply at once. Hardship spends part of
  the good side as a cushion (`HeartMath.Spend`): of each point of strain a source would build, after its own caps,
  `CushionShare` (35%) comes off the good side instead, a point for a point (`SpendShare`) as far as it goes, and the
  rest builds strain; the hour's sources, the weight sinking in, a moment's letdown from outside the hour
  (`HeartLogic.Build`) and an answer's strain (`HeartLogic.Change`) alike, on its record by strain's own source
  (`goodSpent`). (It shipped spending the good side first, half a point a point, strain building only once it was gone.)
  Good things ease strain and fill the good side together (`HeartFeltMath.Settle`): the hour applies rest first (sleep,
  quiet, recreation, the decree), then each good thing in turn (gatherings, good talks, small joys, the pile of small good
  moods); while there is strain, `GoodSplit` (35%) of each goes to the good side at its share (`GoodShare`: 45%, 60%, 60%
  and 15%) and the rest eases strain, and what can't ease anything (strain gone) goes to the good side too. Rest never
  fills it.
- **What fills it, slowly, mostly what can't be bought.** At any strain, slower the more there is
  (`HeartFeltMath.Growth`: in full up to 10, 30% from 85; good things through `Settle`, the rest through
  `GoodHeart.Growing`; it shipped filling only while strain was at nothing), within a
  cap a day for each source and 4 a day in all (`GoodCap`, `GoodDailyCap`; `goodToday`, saved): friends close by and a
  purpose (the heart's needs of belonging and purpose well met, 60 or more: 0.035 to 0.07 an hour each, 1.2 a day),
  a life goal moving on since yesterday (0.6 at the day's turn: `goalTick`, `goalProgress`), a deed of theirs the colony
  speaks well of (its sides add up to good, `RepMath.Valence`, and someone else knows of it: 1, up to 2, 2 a day; read
  from the reputations once a day, `deedTick`), gatherings (2.5 a day), good talks (1.5), a run of small joys
  (`StrainRelief.Joys` beyond the strain they have: 1.2), and the comforts of home (the pile of every small good mood,
  the game's fine rooms and meals among them: 0.4 a day, the smallest cap and share, so a rich colony doesn't simply
  buy it). The day's joys cap counts what a joy eased or filled. It fades slowly (about 3% a day, `GoodFadePerHour`).
- **The bands** (the player's names), as the player approved them (6 November 2026, "As I approved": three bands that
  each give a mood): steady from 20 (`SteadyAt`), in good heart from 45, in high spirits from 65; below 20 nothing to
  speak of yet (`GoodBand.None`, no mood, the meter says "nothing yet"). A good mood each, +3, +6 and +10 since the heart
  was made to count (+2, +3 and +5 before, now the mild choice; `Council_Heart_GoodSide`, one stage a band, a situational
  thought reading the band like strain's, nothing stored in memories; it grows ordinary like any good mood, kept in good
  things growing ordinary's sum as a lasting one, and the pile of small moods leaves it out, `SmallMoments.Heavy`). In
  good heart and in high spirits also brighter dreams (sweet dreams 1.2 and 1.4 times as likely, nightmares 0.85 and
  0.7, `Heart.DreamFactor`) and a quicker recovery from strain (rest eases 1.15 and 1.3 times as fast), read from how
  high the good side stood lately (`goodLately`, halving in about three days), so someone in good heart before a hard
  spell gets over it sooner; steady gives only its mood. No work speed. Shipped first (0.113.0) as two bands, +2 and
  +3, steady giving nothing, to keep a well-run colony on its target; the player chose the stronger reward as first
  approved, knowing Rimfolk's good moods at a high point rise with it (see "Balance targets"). The band is never saved
  (read from the value), so an older save's colonist above 20 is steady at once.
- **The release**, the mirror of strain's day off (`GoodRelease`): in high spirits, about once in four days held there
  (`ReleasePerHour`), at most once in 10 days for each colonist and once a day in the colony (`lastReleaseTick`,
  `HeartTracker.lastColonyReleaseTick`), only when it's safe, at home, awake, an adult free colonist, not drafted,
  downed, in a mental state or at a gathering. Either one of the game's own inspirations, which the game picks by their
  passions and its own rules (`InspirationHandler.GetRandomAvailableInspirationDef`, `TryStartInspiration` with its own
  letter and Rimfolk's reason at its foot; a word said as it begins), 12 off the good side; or a kind word for someone
  close (a partner, kin or a friend by opinion 20 or more, the one under the most strain first, then the lowest in
  spirits): `Together.When` with a walk over in their free time, the line said face to face (`Speech.Say`, one
  sentence, `Rimfolk_Pool_GoodHeart_KindWord`, by who hears it: under strain, grieving, low, hurt, a partner, kin, a
  child, a newcomer), and the other gets a small good memory (`Council_Heart_KindWord`, +3 for 2 days, opinion +6, which
  comes as a small joy and eases their strain or fills their own good side), 6 off the good side. A kind word is set
  going when chosen; if the two never meet within ten hours, it doesn't come. A small gift and a hand with the work
  weren't built: the game has no honest way to show either on the map.
- **Words** in every age: the heart's page (the Mood tab's Heart section) has a second meter, "Good heart", with what
  filled it ("friends close by (+6), a purpose (+4)") and what spent it ("fighting (-6)"), how much slower it grows while
  strain is on them, and the last release; the inspector line and RimHUD read both sides at once ("Heart: worn down, in
  good heart · grieving"; the good band alone from steady while strain is steady); the strain meter's tooltip names the
  other side; the colonist's card (the Now slot) says both, strain's band and why and the good side's band and what filled
  it; the council's Moods page counts who is steady, in good heart and in high spirits and shows the good band beside
  anyone strained; the band mood's tooltip says what filled it. Keys in `Rimfolk_GoodHeart.xml`, the bands' own in `Rimfolk_GoodHeart_Bands.xml` (the first
  file's band words, explanation and count left unused); the Almanac page "the heart's good side"
  (`Almanac_GoodHeart.xml`), the heart's page with its bands in the table.
- **The setting** "The heart's good side" (`heartGoodSide`, on), on the How hard page beside how fast strain builds and the day off (the heart's own switch is on What's on).
  Off (or the heart off): nothing fills it, what there was is gone at the next hour, the bands give nothing, hardship
  builds strain as before. Dev mode: fill it by 20, and overflow now.
- **Saves.** Values on the heart (`good`, `goodTodayTotal`, `goodLately`, `deedTick`, `goalTick`, `goalProgress`,
  `lastReleaseTick`, `releaseWhy`) and three short lists (`goodToday` and `goodRecent` by source, `goodSpent` by strain's
  sources; `Tools/save_estimate.py` models them). An older save loads with no good side and starts at nothing; the first
  look at deeds and the life goal only takes note.

### The heart, felt: it rises and stays, both sides at once, and it shows on the map (9 November 2026)

Release 1 of `docs/design/heart-felt.md`, after the player's word of 9 November 2026 ("i feel like this impact of strain
and all the emotions is currently neglible, or hardly noticeable. i really like the idea of it but it's not really
noticeable") and their change on the proposal ("the good side should also be able to develop at the same time, not only
when strain is at 0. perhaps it's more difficult, but pawns should still be happy about certain things even if others go
wrong"). In their save (day 35, four colonists after the plague, one dying of it in pain) all four sat at strain 5 to 20
and a good side of 0: below 30 nothing shows, rest drained about 10 a day against a cap of 25 built, so strain never
stayed, and the everyday trickle kept the good side from ever filling. The rules are pure (`Heart/HeartFeltMath.cs`,
linked in the tests and the balance simulator); the game side is `Heart/HeartFelt.cs` (the weight, messages, lines,
signs), `HeartActs.cs` and `HeartActJob.cs` (the acts), all from the heart's own hour (no Sched slot, no patch). The
safety rule holds: the game's mood need, mental breaker and break picker are untouched.

- **The lasting weight.** A heavy thing leaves a weight that rest can't ease strain below (`HeartFeltMath.Floor`); strain
  sinks toward it within a day (2.5 an hour at most, `SinkIn`, as hardship through the good side's cushion, on strain's
  record as "heavy things", `StrainSource.Heavy`, the 19th source at the end of the list; no daily cap, the weight bounds
  it). Deaths and losses by the game's memory, the heaviest of each person once in three days (`LossWeight`: a partner's
  or family's 58, seeing family die or a psychic bond torn 50, a friend's 45, a bonded animal 28, seeing an ally die 16,
  any colonist's 12, someone taken 10 to 30), and being downed 22 (`Weigh`, `HeartFelt.WeighLosses`, `Downed`). It lifts
  slowly (0.8 a day) for 3.5 days and a day more for every 12 of weight, then 7 a day (`HoldDaysFor`, `Eased`), and good
  things and a cry lift it by 15% of what they ease (`GoodEasesWeight`; an answer that comforts and the day off too,
  `HeartFelt.Lift`). What lasts while it lasts is held apart (`held`, `HeartFelt.Hold`): their own sickness that can kill
  (the game's `makesSickThought` with a `lethalSeverity`: 12 plus 40 times how far along), someone close badly ill on the
  same map (a partner, kin by blood or opinion 20 or more; from a third of the way, 14 plus 36 times it), a fight at home
  with some of the colony down (12, and 8 each, 36 at most); lifted to its weight each hour while it lasts, slowly a day
  and a half after. Two weights together are the heavier and 35% of the other (`Combine`), and the weights alone never
  hold strain above 76 (`FloorMax`), short of the day off. Traits take their share (a psychopath nothing from a death),
  and the strength setting scales them. Words: "losing Ana", "the plague", "Ana being so ill", "being hurt", "the fight
  going badly" (`weightWhy`, `heldWhy`), on the strain tooltip and the heart's page ("A weight of 45 from losing Ana:
  rest won't ease strain below it."), in the messages and the card.
- **Rest under real strain** (`RestFactor`): in full up to 30, 70% from 90. Kept mild: the weight is what holds strain up
  after a heavy thing, and a much slower rest feeds on itself in a colony neglected day after day.
- **The two sides at once**: above, in "The heart's good side".
- **Small acts by band** (`HeartActs`, setting "Small acts by how they are", `heartActs`): strained, a while in a chair
  or by the fire staring at nothing, or just outside the colony looking out; worn, a few minutes outside from ordinary
  work (building, growing, mining, cutting, making, cooking, hauling, cleaning, research; never a fire, a patient, a
  prisoner, a child, a hunt or an animal at hand, nor while carrying something), pacing their room when awake at night, a
  short word at someone near; in good heart, humming at work (two notes, `VisualTouches.Notes`) and staying at the table
  to talk after a meal (queued after the meal); in high spirits, singing at work (four notes) and a dance where they stand
  at a gathering. **Strong feelings act** (`heartFeelingActs`), a feeling at 60% of full or more: grief, the small habit's
  own visit to the grave (its joy giver) or a while beside the bed where the one lost slept (their own room, from the death hook's look,
  `Patch_FamilyDied`) or sitting; fear, out after dark, in near someone indoors; anger, a sharp word to whoever it is
  about, or through a door that slams (the door's own sound, a puff of dust); love, a while beside a partner at leisure or
  resting in bed (and a chat); homesickness, of an evening at the colony's lit fire talking of home, or the small habit's
  look out; joy, walked over to a friend to share it (`Together.When`, a chat). Each a job of its own
  (`Rimfolk_HeartAct_*`, `JobDriver_HeartAct`, `HeartActExtension`) with its line on arriving. Only safe and free (a home
  map, not drafted, downed, in a mental state, hungry, exhausted or in need of a doctor, at nobody's play-out, no danger;
  in free time, at a break in ordinary work, after a meal or at the gathering), by a chance an hour by band and feeling
  (`ActChance`: strained 7%, worn 12%, near breaking 16%, in good heart 5%, in high spirits 9%, a strong feeling up to
  12%), one act a colonist in 16 hours and one in the colony in 3 at most (session memory). Eating alone and sleeping in
  weren't built: the game has no honest way to show either without patching where they eat and sleep.
- **They say how they feel** (`heartSays`, `HeartFelt.Lines`, `Rimfolk_Pool_HeartBand`): when strain's band turns
  either way or the good side's rises to in good heart or high spirits, a line waits up to 8 hours for them to be in view
  and free; while a band holds, now and then another, once in a day and a half at most. Tagged by the side that speaks
  ([band:...] or [good:...]), [both], [turn], [back], and the cause ([why:loss] with {LOST}, [why:sickself] with
  {ILLNESS}, [why:sickclose] with {SICK}, downed, raid, fight, sleep, letdowns, pain; friends, purpose, gathering for the
  good side), in the speaker's tone; every line has a band, [both] or [back], so nobody is given a heart they don't have.
  Through the touches' one rate for what is said over a head (`VisualTouches.Free`, `Spoke`). The acts' lines are
  `Rimfolk_Pool_HeartAct` ([act:...] with the band or feeling, [with], [about], [lost]).
- **Seen at a glance**: a sign over the head for a strong feeling (`heartSigns`, `HeartFelt.Sign`): the game's own
  thought bubble (a good one for a bright feeling, a bad one for a hard one) with a shape in the feeling's colour
  (`FeelingIcons`: a tear, a bolt, a heart, a sun, a house, one figure, two, an exclamation, a star or a cloud;
  `Textures/ColonyCouncil/Icons/Feelings`, drawn by `Tools/make_feeling_icons.py`), when it grows strong and now and then
  while it holds, once in 8 hours at most, on the map being looked at. A thin heart line under each name on the colonist
  bar (`barHeartLine`, `BarBadges.HeartLine`, `BarBadgeMath.HeartLine`): strain in its band's colour (softer below
  strained), the good side in green under it, each from 8 and as long as it is full, from a cache built once a second.
- **Messages** (`heartMessages`, `HeartFelt.Tell`, `HeartFeltMath.Tell`): when someone becomes worn down or near breaking,
  saying why ("Bautista is worn down: the plague and losing Ana."), when they come back from it (5 below worn), and in
  good heart or in high spirits, saying what filled it; the bands told are saved (`toldStrain`, `toldGood`) so a load
  tells nothing, hovering at a line tells once, and the first look only takes note.
- **Measured** (`Tools/Tests/HeartFeltTests.cs`: colonists looked at hourly through the same pure rules over weeks, 40
  runs a case): a calm colony of eight steady on day 6 (median; 98% within eight days), in good heart on day 18, never
  strained, no day off; one friend's death (day 21 of 42): those close strained 7.2 days (median), a partner 9.8, the
  rest at 12 at most and none strained, the good side still filling 2.4 a day while strained against 3.8 while not; a
  plague season like the save's (four friends, two ill for ten days, rising to 0.9): all of the colony worn three days or
  more (median), none near breaking, no day off, most still in good heart at some point in it; real disasters (a plague
  that kills two of six, a raid that kills two and downs one then a siege): someone near breaking in every run, about one
  day off a disaster. In the balance simulator (`Tools/Balance/HeartSim.cs`, brought to the same rules; 40 runs of six):
  a well-run colony strained 4% of the time, steady 44%, in good heart 35% and in high spirits 5% (48/28/3 before); an
  average one strained, worn and near breaking 12%, 4% and 1.6% (6/1/0 before), 0.14 days off a colonist-year; a
  neglectful one 32%, 25% and 18% (29/17/8), 1.6 (0.72). The balance report (`docs/balance-report.md`) was written again with release 2 ("The heart, made to count").
- **Saves.** Values on the heart only (`weight`, `weightUntil`, `weightWhy`, `weightAbout`, `weightKind`, `held`,
  `heldUntil`, `heldWhy`, `heldAbout`, `heldKind`, `toldStrain`, `toldGood`); no new collection. An older save loads with
  no weight, and its bands are taken note of at the first look. What the hour notes on the side (whom a loss already
  weighed for, a downing seen, the last band and strong feeling for lines and signs, the acts' cooldowns, the beds of the
  dead) is session memory.
- **Dev mode**: "Heart: a heavy loss weighs on them (45)", "a small act now (if one fits)", "say how they feel now", "a
  sign over the head now".

### The heart, made to count: stronger bands, effects beyond mood, bad afternoons, hearts spreading, advice and a day off (9 November 2026)

Release 2 of `docs/design/heart-felt.md` (points 9 to 14), after the player had played release 1: "i think you can go
ahead with this, if the strain is not noticeable it doesn't make too much sense. also include recommendations and advice
on potential actions i can take to reduce strain. for example certain decrees. or i could for example also just grant a
single stained pawn a break day or stuff like this". With it, the player's two requests for the same screens: "review
the "mood" uI for colonists, so the most relevant details for strain and mood are visible at first glance, with
additional details below that. also perhaps revisit the rimui integration to see if it could be improved as well". The
rules are pure (`Heart/HeartCountMath.cs`, linked in the tests and the balance simulator); the game side is
`HeartEffects.cs` (the stat parts and what the bands do in words), `HeartTimeOff.cs` (the bad afternoon and the day off,
the think tree's node, the gizmo), `HeartAdvice.cs` (advice and its buttons), `Moods/MoodGlance.cs` (the Mood tab's top)
and `Integrations/RimHud.cs`. The safety rule holds: the game's mood need, mental breaker and break picker are untouched;
everything goes through the heart's two situational thoughts, stat parts, the timetable, a think-tree node of Rimfolk's
own and Rimfolk's own acts. No new Sched slot; one Harmony patch (the gizmo on a colonist, `Pawn.GetGizmos`).

- **Stronger bands** (9). Strain -4, -8 and -14 mood (strained, worn down, near breaking); the good side +3, +6 and +10
  (steady, in good heart, in high spirits). The thoughts' stages are these, the default; the setting "How strongly the
  bands are felt" (`heartBands`: Mild, Felt, Strong) sizes them in code through the thought itself
  (`Thought_HeartStrain.BaseMoodOffset`, `Thought_HeartGood.BaseMoodOffset`, `HeartCountMath.StrainMood`, `GoodMood`):
  mild is release 1's -3, -5, -8 and +2, +3, +5, strong -5, -10, -18 and +4, +8, +13. They go through the game's own mood,
  so the worn down break more often, as they should. **The good side still grows ordinary** like any good mood: good
  things growing ordinary (`Moods/GoodLife.cs`) keeps it in its sum as a lasting good mood (`SituationalOf`), the
  everyday kind that shrinks most above the line their standards set, as it did; there is no exemption (the pile of small
  moods leaves it out, `SmallMoments.Heavy`, as before). The bands' own words carry what they do by the settings as they
  are (`{EFFECTS}`, `HeartEffects.DoingStrain`, `DoingGood`), so the mild and strong choices read true. Light touch sets
  the bands mild and no bad afternoons.
- **Effects beyond mood** (10), each a stat part in the heart's pattern (an XML patch with conditional operations in
  `Patches/Council_Heart.xml`, contributing nothing with the setting "Effects beyond mood", `heartEffects`, or the heart
  off): work from the first band (strained 3% slower, worn 7%, near breaking 12%; with the setting off, release 1's 5% and
  10% from worn), learning (`GlobalLearningFactor`: worn 6% slower, near breaking 10%), the need for sleep
  (`RestFallRateFactor`: worn 6% more, near breaking 10%), healing (`InjuryHealingFactor`: worn 5% slower, near breaking
  10%) and immunity (`ImmunityGainSpeed`: worn 3% slower, near breaking 5%, never more: the player lost colonists to the
  plague, `HeartCountMath.ImmunitySlowest`, tested at every pair of bands); in good heart and in high spirits a little
  faster learning (4% and 8%), healing (3% and 6%) and immunity (2% and 5%). Both sides together are kept within bounds
  (`HeartCountMath.Factor`). The good side never touches work or sleep. Each shows in the stat's own explanation ("Strain,
  worn down: x94%", "Good side, in good heart: x104%", `HeartEffects.StatLines`), in the band's words on the heart's page,
  on the card and at the top of the Mood tab ("Worn down: -8 mood, work -7%, learns 6% slower, needs 6% more sleep, heals
  5% slower, fights off illness 3% slower, nightmares 1.6 times as likely").
- **A bad afternoon** (11, `heartBadDays`). From worn down (55), in the afternoon (12 to 16), a chance an hour of 1 in 50
  rising to 1 in 25 at 85 (`BadDayChancePerHour`), at most once a week for each colonist and once in two days in the
  colony (`lastBadDayTick`, `HeartTracker.lastColonyBadDayTick`), under the day off's safety rules (`HeartTimeOff.Unsafe`:
  at home, a free adult, not drafted, downed or in a mental state, no danger, not needing a doctor, not nursing a baby,
  two others able to work; awake, at no gathering, not in the middle of caring for or carrying someone or fighting a fire,
  `Episodes.Busy`). Off work for three to five hours, played out on the map: a while beside their own bed in their room
  (a new act, `Cry`, else a quiet seat), a while looking out, a drink if they drink (alcohol from the stores or lying about
  at home, any mod's by its chemical, only where their drug policy allows it for fun, they aren't teetotal, addicted or
  just clean, and their faith allows it: `FirstPot.WillDrink`, `Beliefs.MindsEating`), the grave (the small habit's own
  visit) or the bed of someone they grieve when the weight on them is a loss. A message says why ("Avila has had enough
  for today (the plague and losing Ana) and leaves her work for the afternoon."), a line as it begins. It ends early when
  danger comes, and eases 30% of their strain when it runs its course (half when cut short), below the weight too, as a
  cry does.
- **Hearts spread a little** (12, `heartSpread`). Each hour, the colony's people on the same map close to them
  (`HeartCountMath.Closeness`: a partner 1, kin by blood 0.8, a friend by opinion 0.4 at 20 rising to 0.8 at 80; the
  colony is the family, never a house): each worn down wears on them 0.06 an hour at full closeness (near breaking 0.1),
  all together at most 0.15 an hour and 2.5 a day (a new source at the end of the list, `StrainSource.Spread`, "someone
  close worn down"), and never past 45 (`SpreadCeiling`, short of worn down): since only the worn spread, one worn
  colonist can't wear another down on their own and the colony can't spiral (tested: one colonist held near breaking for
  eight weeks among seven close friends, none ever worn down). Each in high spirits lifts them 0.05 an hour (at most 0.1),
  a good thing as a talk is (`GoodSource.Lifted`, `StrainRelief.Lifted`, both at the end of their lists): it eases strain
  and fills the good side together, a share each (`GoodShare` 0.5, `GoodCap` 0.6 a day). A psychopath takes none of it.
  The heart's page says who ("Bautista being worn down wears on her a little.").
- **What would help** (13, `heartAdvice`, `HeartAdvice`). For each strained colonist, the few things that would ease
  them most, ranked from what is wearing on them now (`HeartCountMath.Rank`: strain built lately by source, and how they
  are, hungry, in pain, short of recreation, without a bed of their own, lonely, grieving) and what the colony has: a day
  off (from strained), a gathering (a party, where there is a gathering spot), time with a friend (the one closest to
  them who isn't worn down themselves), a proper meal, a better bed, recreation they like (naming what they're tired
  of), their pain treated, a rest from fighting, time to grieve, more light; and **the council's decrees that ease
  strain**, the best two for what wears on them (`HeartAdvice.Easing`: days of rest, with its strain relief, eases all of
  strain; the others name what they answer in their defs, `heartEases`, with what they do and what they cost,
  `heartHelp`, `heartCost`: festival days, quiet hours, days of mourning, shared meals, rest when ill, a feast day, a work
  song, holy days). Each where Rimfolk can act has a button, greyed with why not: **give the day off**; **propose** a
  decree, which puts it to the council through its own path, a petition by them (or by someone who likes it, if they
  would rather not; `DecreeTracker.Petition`, a message and their line, lapsing after a few days as any petition does)
  and opens the Decrees page where it is declared; **call a party** (the game's own, hosted by them if they can); **send
  a friend over** (`HeartActs.FriendVisit`: one walks over in their free time for the game's deep talk, `Together.When`).
  Where it can't act it says plainly what to do ("keep cooked meals in store and a table to eat at"). Built at most once
  a game hour for each colonist (unsaved), never per frame. Shown on the heart's page (the Mood tab) with its buttons,
  on the colonist's card (a section with its buttons, and the day off among the card's acts), in the message when
  someone becomes worn down ("What would help: a day off, days of rest and a proper meal."), on the council's Moods page
  for the whole colony (each decree and a party once, with everyone it would ease; each colonist's own first two) and in
  RimHUD's tooltip.
- **A day off for one colonist** (14, `heartDayOff`). Given by the player from strained on (the choice: a day off is for
  someone the days have worn on, and the button on every colonist would only crowd the bar), from the Mood tab, the
  card, the advice or a button on the selected colonist (`Patch_HeartDayOffGizmo`; while one runs, it ends it; since the
  meters below, the Mood tab's button sits beside them and the colonist's is behind a setting, off), once in
  five days for each colonist (the button says when: "A day off (in 3 days)"), under the same safety rules (one other
  able to work is enough). For a day their work hours (Work, Anything) are recreation in their timetable and their first
  two waking hours a lie-in; a node of Rimfolk's own in the game's think tree (`Rimfolk_Heart_TimeOffTree`, inserted at
  `Humanlike_PreMain`, before the colonist's main work: `ThinkNode_ConditionalHeartTimeOff`) keeps them from ordinary
  work while their timetable says recreation: emergencies first (the game's own emergency work, a fire, someone needing
  a doctor now), then food and sleep as they need, then now and then an act (a walk, their partner's company, the fire,
  a friend sent for), then their recreation, then a wander about the colony. Their recreation runs its full length
  though their recreation is full (`Patch_HeartTimeOffFullJoy`, a prefix on the game's `JoyUtility.JoyTickCheckEnd`
  that turns its "end the job when full" into "carry on" while time off runs in a recreation hour,
  `HeartTimeOff.KeepsAtRecreation`; the player, 15 November 2026: "they start a recreation and then immediatelly stop it
  again ... they should be able to do recreation for as long as they want to reduce strain"), so its hours count toward
  easing strain (recreation under way, each hour, `HeartLogic`). It stands down when they are drafted,
  downed, need a doctor or danger comes, and the day off ends at once when danger comes (checked every slice of the
  heart's hour, 250 ticks), so they can be drafted. The timetable's hours changed are saved on the heart (`offHours`,
  "9=Work>Joy"), put back when it ends only where nobody changed them since; an hour the calendar's rest day had given is
  taken over from it (`ColonyCalendar.TakeRestHour`), so each is put back once. While it runs rest eases a quarter faster
  and time to themselves eases 0.3 an hour besides; when it runs its course it eases 12 more (half when cut short, below
  the weight too). A line as it begins ("I'm going to sleep late and nobody can stop me."), a message, and one when it
  ends. The work missed is real: they do no ordinary work for a day.
- **The Mood tab, at a glance** (`ITab_Pawn_Mood`, `MoodGlance`). Its top answers without scrolling or opening
  anything: the bar with the break lines and the sentence of where their mood is heading; the heart now ("Heart: worn
  down 61, up 12 today · in good heart 48", strain in its band's colour and the good side in green, as the colonist bar's
  heart line draws them, its tooltip strain in full), the weight under it ("Under it, a weight of 45 from losing Ana,
  lifting over the days."), time off under way (these three are meters and the day off's place since "The heart at a
  glance" below); what weighs on them and what lifts them most (the top three each across
  the game's moods, other mods' and Rimfolk's, the heart's own two with what is behind them: "worn down (the plague) -8"),
  each with its size as the list below has it; what each side is doing to them now, a line each; and the top advice with
  its buttons. Below, in order of use, sections that fold and are remembered between sessions (`Folds.Remembered`, kept
  with the settings through `PageMemory`, "mood.sections"): every mood (compact rows by what can be done, or every mood as
  a card), the heart (strain and the good side, what built and eased it, the weight, who close wore on or lifted them,
  what the bands do, what would help), its feelings, its needs, what has grown ordinary and where the moods come from,
  and lately (strain against the day's start, the last day off, bad afternoon, day to themselves, overflow and break).
  Built with the tab's model twice a second at most; every number is the sections' own (the moods' sizes from the same
  lines, strain and the good side to the point, the weight as the page says it). Works at the inspect pane's width and as
  the tab is resized (everything under the bar scrolls; `TabFitMath` sets its height).
- **RimHUD** (by name, as before: its custom value and bar widgets, `GetParameters(Pawn)` by reflection; its DLL wasn't
  in the player's upload and isn't needed). The strain line (`Council_Hud_Strain`) now reads like the summary: strain's
  band and value in its colour, the good side's in green, the top cause while strained, and a day off or a bad afternoon
  under way ("Worn down 61 · in good heart 48 · the plague · day off"); its tooltip leads with what would help, and a
  click opens their Mood tab. The strain bar says time off in its value and opens the tab too (since "The heart at a
  glance" below, the line is shortened to its cell and the bar's value is the number alone). Two new widgets: the good
  side as a bar (`Council_Hud_GoodBar`, marked at 20, 45 and 65) and what would help (`Council_Hud_HeartAdvice`, its
  tooltip the advice in full).
- **Measured** (`Tools/Tests/HeartFeltTests.cs`, 40 runs a case, the same pure rules hour by hour, release 1's targets
  still held; `Tools/Balance`, `docs/balance-report.md` "The heart, made to count"). Breaks by the game's own lines and
  mean times (35%, 20%, 5%; 4, 0.8 and 0.5 days), a colonist-year, with the bands felt against felt mildly: a calm colony
  none either way; a plague season like the save's 0.32 against 0.14 (under the minor line 2.1% of the time against
  1.0%); real disasters 0.55 against 0.27; in the balance simulator a well-run colony none, an average one 0.01 against
  0.00, a neglected one 9.8 against 6.3 (under the minor line 46% against 35%). Bad afternoons: none in a calm colony,
  0.01 a colonist-year well run, 0.26 average, 1.4 neglected, 0.34 in a plague season, about one for every two colonists
  after a real disaster. A day off at strain 61 eases 45 in the day against 30 on an ordinary one (43 against 30 with a
  weight of 30 under it). Spreading: one colonist held near breaking for eight weeks among seven close friends, none
  ever worn down, spread building about 1 a day each. The day off at 85 a colonist-year: average 0.10, neglected 1.2
  (release 1: 0.14 and 1.6), the bad afternoons easing some of it first. Rimfolk's mood in a well-run colony rises to
  +7.3 (+12 or more 29% of the time), above the old target of +3 to +6: the good side's +3, +6 and +10 as the player
  asked, still growing ordinary.
- **Saves.** Values on the heart (`offKind`, `offStart`, `offUntil`, `offWhy`, `lastDayOffTick`, `lastBadDayTick`) and one
  short list (`offHours`, the hours a day off changed, only while it runs; modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`); the
  tracker's `lastColonyBadDayTick`. The heart's lists grow at their ends, padded with nothing on an older save
  (`StrainSource.Spread`, `StrainRelief.Lifted`, `GoodSource.Lifted`). An older save has no time off under way and every
  wait past. What advice there is, who spread or lifted this hour and when the time off's last act was are worked out
  again (unsaved).
- **Dev mode**: "Heart: a bad afternoon now (if safe)", "a day off now (the wait aside)", "end their time off now".

### The heart at a glance: meters, and the day off beside them (9 November 2026)

The player's words on Avila's Mood tab, where the heart was a line of red text ("Heart: Worn down (60), down 7 today") and
the day off a big heart on the colonist's command bar: "the strain level etc. should be graphically more easier to see,
perhaps also like a level bar or so. the "give day off" should also be in this menu and not in the pawn bar". Their
RimHUD panel showed "Strain  jown (60) · fighting ...": the value cut from the left. The rules are pure
(`Heart/HeartMeterMath.cs`, linked in the tests); the drawing is `Heart/HeartMeter.cs`. No saved data, no Harmony patch,
no Sched slot.

- **Two meters, drawn like the mood bar** (`HeartMeter.Draw`), right under it at the top of the Mood tab, as tall as it,
  in the game's look or Rimfolk's own (the kit's track, the fill rounded in its own look). **Strain**: 0 to 100, filled
  in its band's colour as the colonist bar's heart line draws it (a band's colour from strained, strained's faintly
  below); a faint wash where each band lies; ticks in the colour of what begins there, with small labels under the bar,
  at strained 30, worn down 55, near breaking 75 and 85, where a day to themselves may come (only while that setting is
  on); the band and value on the bar ("Strain: worn down 60"); a mark with a foot under the bar for **the lasting weight**,
  the floor rest can't take strain below, the part of the fill it holds shaded; beside the bar **how it moved today**,
  an arrow and "-7 today" (up in sour, down in warm, from a move of 2). **The good side** the same way in green, ticks at
  steady 20, in good heart 45 and in high spirits 65, shown at any strain since both sides can be up at once. The labels
  that would touch give way, the later first (`HeartMeterMath.LabelLefts`: at the tab's width all four show; narrow, 85
  goes first). **Hovering** a tick says what begins there and what that band does by the settings as they are ("From 55,
  worn down: -8 mood, work -7%, ..."); the mark says the weight and why ("A weight of 45 from losing Ana: ..."); the rest of
  a meter its tooltip: the band and value, what it does to them now (the effects line), how it moved today, what built it
  lately, what eased it, the weight, and what would help (the advice, or the plain words below strained); the good side's
  is its own tooltip as before. One tooltip at a time. Built at most twice a second for each colonist and again after a
  click (`HeartMeter.For`), nothing translated while drawn.
- **The day off's place** at the meters' right on the Mood tab, always in the same spot (`HeartMeterMath.Lay`: as wide as
  its widest button, so it never moves; under the meters where the width is short): "Give a day off", greyed with its
  reason, the whole of it in the tooltip and a few words under it ("not strained enough", "again in 3 days", "not while
  in danger", "needs a doctor first", "a baby to feed", "nobody to carry on", "away from home", "a child";
  `HeartTimeOff.WhyNotDayOffKey`, `HeartMeterMath.ShortWhy`). While a day off or a bad afternoon runs, the same place says
  until when in the day's hours ("Day off until 9h tomorrow", "Bad afternoon until 16h"; `HeartTimeOff.UntilText`) with
  "End it early" (`HeartTimeOff.EndEarly`: either kind, counting for half, "called back to work", as when danger cuts it
  short). Only for the colony's free people; hidden for prisoners and slaves, and with days off switched off unless a bad
  afternoon runs. The advice's own day off button stays.
- **The summary under them** keeps what adds something: the mood's sentence, what weighs and lifts most, what each band
  does now and the top advice with its buttons. The "Heart: ..." line, the weight's line and the time off's line gave way
  to the meters, the mark and the day off's place. Fits the inspect pane's width (464 inside the scroll view: bars 275,
  the trend 72, the place about 110) and the tab squeezed above a tall pane (the meters scroll with the rest).
- **The same meters** in the heart's section below (in place of its two plain meters; no day off's place there) and on
  the colonist's card, before its lines (`HeartCard`, "heart-meters"; the day off stays among the card's acts).
- **The colonist's command bar**: the day off's button is gone from it by default. The setting "Day off button on the
  colonist too" (`heartDayOffGizmo`, How hard, under the day off; off; needs the deeper game hooks) brings it back for
  players who want it there (`Patch_HeartDayOffGizmo.Wanted`).
- **RimHUD** (`Integrations/RimHud.cs`; its source read: a value widget draws a value too wide for its cell right-aligned
  and clipped, then "...", and a value widget can draw no bar of its own). The strain line is now short enough for its
  cell: the band in a word and its value in its colour, then as much as fits of time off under way, the top cause while
  strained and the good side ("Worn 60 · fighting"; the good side's band and value alone while strain is steady), cut
  to 112 in the small font without cutting a word (`HeartMeterMath.Fit`, measured without the colour tags, fitted once
  each time the heart's line changes). The whole line leads the tooltip when it was cut. Strain's bar
  (`Council_Hud_StrainBar`, the bar version) gets the meter's ticks (85 added) and its value is the number alone: its
  value cell is 40 wide by default, so "61, day off" was cut too; time off is in its tooltip.
- **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/HeartMeterTests.cs` (the ticks against the bands, the labels at every width, the layout from 120
  to 900 wide, the trend, until when, every reason's few words, the HUD line against the player's case, and the seams).

## Layer 8: Social life

One feature in four parts, under one setting (`socialLife`, "Personalities and social life"): **character**
(`Persona/`), **conversations, views and shared memories** (`Social/Talk/`), **groups** (`Social/Groups/`) and
**reputation and gossip** (`Social/Gossip/`). Character is the root everyone reads: its sides give the tone of every
line (`Persona.ToneOf` in `ToneUtility.ToneFor`) and the `persona:*` tags, so a colonist sounds the same in a talk, a
story passed on and at their group's fire. The parts never call each other's internals for what they say: groups and
names reach the lines as tags (`group:`, `grouprole:`, `rep:`), and the shared pieces sit in the foundation
(`SharedMemories`, stances, `CharacterPage`). Rules that hold across all four:

- **One happening, told once.** A fight has one name everywhere (`FightNames`: who came and the day, kept while it
  lasts), so a mark, a shared memory and a deed name the same raid, and two raids by the same people are two
  memories. A happening gets one journal line (`JournalTracker.WroteWithin` for lines written in the same moment,
  `FirstOnLoss` for a death, which several memories and systems notice): a mark's line, the council's, the grief, the
  bond lost and the group's step back for the one written first.
- **One pace for Rimfolk's talk.** Moments (the groups' and names' moments are moments), conversations and gossip keep
  their own waits, and on top `SocialPace`: an hour between any two of them started by the same colonist, and none
  with someone mid-conversation. Their lines go through the talk's queue in turn (`ExchangeQueue`, gossip included).
  Measured against the picker's rhythm (0.6 started a waking hour), a colonist is in about 5 Rimfolk-made exchanges a
  day next to about 14 of the game's own, a quarter of all; `momentFrequency` scales every one of them.
- **Opinion is explainable.** Each part adds its own labelled line in the Social tab, small and short: a talk's 1 to 6
  (2-4 days), a name's -12 to +7, "one of us" +4 and "one of that lot" -5/-10, the group moments' -8 to +6 (1.5-3 days),
  next to the bonds' own (friends up to +18, rivals down to -18). One happening reaches a pair through few of them,
  each saying why: a rescue under fire is the game's own "rescued me", a deed that adds to a name, and the fight's
  comradeship; the memory of it only counts again when they talk about it (a few points, for days).
- **Roles follow character.** A group's role never goes against what shows (no cold anchor, no dour joker), and the
  crowd's in-joke is only for two with none of their own (conversation brings up theirs).
- **Off means off.** With the setting off nothing new is said or kept, the old circles come back at once, talks under
  way stop, and the page shows nature alone; old saves and removed defs load (records of missing defs are dropped).

- **Said once** (0.188.1, the player: "there should be no redundancy if there's no good reason for it"). Under the
  summary the Heart section adds only what the summary leaves out: what built strain lately and what eased it, the weight
  under it, who close wore on or lifted them, and what filled the good side (`HeartView.DrawHeartDetail`). The meters,
  the band's effect lines, time off and the advice are the summary's alone.

### Character: nature, marks and the character page
A colonist's character is eight sides from -100 to 100 (`Persona/`). Nature is worked out from the game (traits through
`PersonaNatureDef`s, the Social skill, age, a stable personal lean) and never saved; what happened to them is (lasting
and fading moves, the marks themselves). Marks (`PersonaMarkDef` with a `PersonaMarkExtension`) are data: a family, the
memories that bring it, a condition on nature ("nerve>=10"), a lean that scales it by nature (0.4 to 1.6), journal lines
and news for turning points.

- **One way in per happening.** Memories as they're gained (the one Harmony hook, shared with good times); otherwise
  one-line calls where the colony already notices things: a fight won and a breakdown (WorldReactions), the downed
  during a fight (quirks' hourly look), elections and the speaker's death (Offices), bonds lost (SocialWeb), vengeance
  sworn, the sick pulled through, fine work, and a daily look in the council's day for the slow ones.
- **A fight won** is one with a real threat (`Battle.WasThreat`, `BondsMath.WasThreat`): the storyteller's big threat, or
  a raid Rimfolk sent itself (`Raids.Send` notes it on the home's fight, `Battle.raidSent`, saved), told to the
  storyteller or not. A raiders' camp's raid isn't told to the storyteller, so its fights were never won before: no
  victory, no marks, no deeds, no calendar day (the player's save: the marks' last fight day 114, the camp's raid day 124).
- **Nature picks, then scales.** The first mark of a family whose condition fits is given; the same raid hardens one
  colonist and shakes another. Nothing is random but a few small kindnesses (2 in 5 leave a mark).
- **Rare enough to read.** `MarksMath.Blocked`: one small mark per three days, a turning point never twice within its
  keeping, one happening one mark (a story and who it was about), two turning points a day at most. A person keeps 12
  marks; small ones go first.
- **The one reading of who someone is** (phase 3 of the review, November 2026). The colony's ways read a colonist's
  eight sides, not a table of their own from traits (`PersonaMath.WayLean`, `CharacterTracker.Affinity`): mercy is
  warmth without a temper, generosity warmth without pride, tradition the set in their ways, openness to strangers warmth,
  trust and curiosity, hard work pride in it while the joker takes it easy; a side counts past 15 (the personal lean says
  nothing) and in full at 55. Who minds an answer ("not my choice", "told them so") and the ways' mood follow, and change
  as marks move a person. A stranger's fighting temper reads temper, nerve and warmth (`PersonaMath.FightTemper`). The
  game's traits are the input to character, not a second reading: what the ways' table read and character didn't
  (industriousness, a bloodthirsty temper, a few mods' traits) is in `Rimfolk_PersonaNature_Ways.xml`; a mod's personal
  trait no longer leans the ways by itself (`ModPeople.OnlyTraits`), a kind or a belief still does.
- **Soft feedback only.** Character tips weights already there and never adds mood: moment weights 0.7 to 1.35
  (`Heart.MomentWeightFactor`), soreness half again for hot-heads (`MomentTones`), confiding 0.4 to 1.6 and mentors
  0.5 to 1.6 (with the systems talking to each other). Conversation, groups and gossip read character through their
  own code and the `persona:*` tags.
- **The page.** StoryView draws the sections of `CharacterPage` (character 10, what shaped them 20, then the other parts'),
  with eight bars and per-side tooltips worked out the same way as nature. With social life off only nature shows.
  Each section carries its registry key, so a page picks its parts (`CharacterPage.Make` asks one): the People roster
  shows them all, the Story tab character, shaped and traits, the Culture tab views and ideoligion, and the Social tab's
  column groups, reputation and memories (see "A colonist's tabs").

### Groups

The social web's circles used to be rebuilt every day from strong friendships, with no identity or memory. With
"Personalities and social life" on, they are persistent groups (`Social/Groups/`, saved in `GroupTracker`, a game
component of its own, so an old save just starts without it and finds its groups quietly on the first day).

- **Forming.** Once a day, with the social web's day, every pair gets an affinity from the game (`GroupFacts` →
  `GroupMath.Affinity`): friendship and rivalry most, then shared work (sampled hourly), comrades, the night hours,
  likeness (`Persona.Likeness`), an ideoligion held hard, arriving together or the same kind of life before, age. A cluster of
  three to seven with no rift becomes a group; someone joins the group they hold to (and never one they left) and drifts
  off after days of not holding to it. Two groups each at most.
- **Real divides** (the player's decision 13, 6 November 2026). In the player's save one group held 7 of 12 while Barr,
  whom everyone fights with, belonged to none: after every raid everyone was everyone's comrade, and what everyone shared
  bound one big group. Groups now form, take people in and keep them by what binds some of the colony more than the rest
  (`GroupMath.Distinct`: each pair's pull less three quarters of the colony's mean pull, `GroupFacts.distinct`); how close
  a group already is still reads the plain pull, so friends stay close while those who only fought beside them find
  their own way. A group holds well under half the colony (`GroupMath.MaxFor`: 45%, three to seven; five in a colony of
  twelve): a group grown past it lets its loosest member go, one a day at most, and merges stop there. Someone outside
  every group is shown as outside, with why (`GroupMath.WhyOutside`, `GroupText.OutsideWhy`: at odds with some who are
  in one, new here, or their own way): under their name on the People table, on the Bonds page ("Outside every group:
  Barr (at odds with Toni, Penguin and Macy)"), and on their character page. An older save's groups regroup by these rules
  over ten days (`GroupMath.RegroupDays`, `GroupTracker.regroup`), quietly at the usual pace, told once in the news; a
  new game's groups form as ever. The names stay as they were given (named for what they share, 0.101.2).
- **Identity.** The kind is what binds most of it (`GroupKindDef`: 26, lowest order wins, friendship last); it gives a
  name picked once, in the colony's era, and kept. A group is never named after one of its people (the colony is the
  family, and its groups are of the colony, not of a person: the player's report of "Stace's friends", 5 November
  2026). A friendship group is named for what its people share (`GroupShareDef`, `Rimfolk_GroupShares.xml`, ranked by
  the pure `GroupNaming`): the night hours or a work more than half of them keep or do, a side of character two in
  three have (only sides no kind is named for), else its habits in its own order with their place ("the fireside
  circle", "the long table"), else their friendship ("the old friends"); several names per idea and era, one picked
  by the group's id among those no group now or lately has, and its card's line says what it's named for ("They are
  friends, and most of them keep the night hours."). A kind whose own names are all taken does the same (it was
  "Hector's hunters"). The anchor is a role on the card, never the name. Older saves: a group whose name reads as one
  after someone (the friends kind's old names, kept in its def only to find them, `CC_Group_NameOf`, `CC_Clique_Name`;
  `GroupNaming.AfterSomeone`, never a name a kind or share gives) is named this way once when the game is loaded
  (`GroupTracker.LoadedGame`, and the day's pass if groups were off then), quietly: no news, no history line, nothing
  else changed. The older circles (social life off) take a friendship name the same way, stable while their leader
  leads them. Roles come from character and behaviour (`GroupMath.AssignRoles`:
  one anchor, joker and peacemaker each; a change waits three days; the incumbent keeps a unique role against a near
  rival). Ways (`GroupNormDef`, at most three) come from the members' average character or tags, with hysteresis; views
  from members' stances (`Persona.Stance`, any topic key). Members drift towards both (`Persona.Nudge`, `SetStance`).
- **Life.** Cohesion (0-100) settles towards the members' mean affinity and moves with habits kept, shared memories,
  quarrels and mends (read from `MomentTones`), losses and separation. Habits (`GroupHabitDef`) are kept when members are
  really together doing them (hourly, `Together.Can`), or called on the map as a play-out by the anchor: a close group
  only (cohesion `GroupMath.CloseAt` 50, the card's "close"; until 5 November 2026 a loose one from 35 was called too,
  more often than the words said), `CallAfterDays` 8 days at least since the last and then 1 in 5 a day (about 12 days
  on average, `DaysBetweenCalls`: every week or two), one group at a time, three of them at home at least, its first
  habit with a play kind, for its own people only. The gathering says what it is where the player meets it
  (`GroupHabits.BeginText`, `Does`, `Tip`; `Rimfolk_Groups_Gatherings.xml`): as it begins, who gathers where (their
  anchor by name when it's them leading), the group's line and "those who come feel they belong, and their strain eases
  a little"; in This week's list, its people and how often; at its end (`play.outcome`), how many of them came and that
  the group is closer for it; the founding news says once what keeping habits does and whom the anchor calls to what;
  a habit's pill on the card says what keeping it does and whether the anchor calls them to it. The label on the map
  stays short ("an evening at the fire for the fireside circle"). The words are the same in every age; the age is in
  the names. Newcomers
  integrate by opinion, memories, work, a sponsor and welcomes, scaled by how open the group is; a closed group gives the
  cold shoulder and the old left-out feeling. Rivalry between groups grows from feuds, opposed views and ways, and spats,
  and reaches votes, petitions and objections through `SocialWeb.Warmth`. Splits (loose and riven), merges (overlapping
  or close) and ends are told once.
- **Contracts.** Other parts read groups only through tags: `group:<id>`, `grouprole:<role>`, `ingroup`, plus
  `outsider`, `groupkind:`, `groupnorm:`, `grouprival` (`Groups.AddTags`, one line in `PeopleTags`). `SocialWeb.cliques`
  is built from the groups, so older code that asks about circles still works. The pure arithmetic is `GroupMath`,
  covered by `Tools/Tests/GroupTests.cs`.
- **Balance.** Belonging is company, not mood (`RewardInstead` on the habit, welcome and role moments); what a group does
  against someone is small and short (-1 to -3).

### Reputation and gossip

What people did, who knows it, how the story spreads, and the name that follows (`Social/Gossip/`; pure arithmetic in
`RepMath.cs`, checked by `Tools/Tests/ReputationTests.cs`).

- **Deeds** (`DeedDef`, 44): facets per side of a name (courage, kindness, diligence, skill, discretion, temper), a
  theme for lines, a fade half-life, merging of repeats. Recorded where the event is already noticed (one-line calls
  in WorldReactions.Victory, Moments' contests, Secrets.Reveal, Offices, Patch_ArcMade, Ambitions, Encounters,
  MeetingAttendance), by four light postfixes (a memory gained, a mental break, a history event, a social fight; one
  dictionary look each) and by the reputation's own hour (rescues under fire, the brave's company, idling, tending).
  Each keeps doer, victim, when, a name ("the raid on the 5th of Aprimay"), size, and its knowers: witnesses, and those who
  heard, from whom, in what version, believed how far. The newer systems' deeds (13: a camp friend or quarrel, a lost
  child found, a pilgrim walked home, a harvest worked, neighbours let down, a call answered, a day seen to, a feast
  dish burned, a quarrel at the feast, the night watch, the dead carried out, rounds) come through
  `Social/Talk/SharedTimes.cs` and `Setbacks/SetbackTimes.cs`, from the same one-line hooks as their memories.
- **Gossip** is an InteractionDef in the game's picker (`InteractionWorker_Gossip`, separate from the council's
  `CouncilGossip`). Weight: there's a deed the teller knows and the listener doesn't, by someone else (or the proud
  teller's own good one), its subject absent unless the teller is a hothead or their rival; fresher, juicier, more
  from the talkative, much more to newcomers. Slant from the teller's opinion, ties, group and humour; a version grows
  or shrinks within 40%-160% of the truth and never turns round; belief from the listener's trust and opinions. Lines
  via `Speech.Say` (pools by valence and slant, tagged by deed and persona); the log line from slant and topic packs.
- **A name** is what each person makes of another (deeds known × version × belief × fade × their character's weight),
  capped at ±40 a side, and the colony's view is that summed and shared over everyone. It gives a small social thought
  (-12..+7, the bad sooner), rep: tags, moments that read them, a vote lean (±2), fewer secrets told to a gossip, an
  epithet's bar 7-15% lower, strain eased beside the brave in a fight (through `Interplay.Ease`), and news when a side
  forms or fades.

### Conversations, views and shared memories

What colonists talk about, the views they hold, and what they went through together (`Social/Talk/`; the arithmetic in
