`TalkMath.cs` and the lines' queue in `ExchangeQueue.cs`, checked by `Tools/Tests/TalkTests.cs`).

- **Topics** (`TopicDef`, 24, a worker each) say when they come up, what's news (`TalkNote`s from the game's events and
  the talk's hour, and the game's state: the food, a disaster, traders; and in `TalkScene`, found once an hour: a
  calendar day from three days before to two after it was kept, the newest world situation, the camp on the map), who
  or what a talk is about, and what a
  colonist's life adds to a view. A view (-1..1) is kept with `Persona.SetStance` under the topic's defName
  (`defName:id` for a newcomer, let go once they're settled). It's seeded from the topic's weights per side of a person,
  its leans (traits, passions, memes, precepts) and that life, drifts 4% a day back toward it, is pushed by events (a
  fight, a death) and moved by talk (`TalkMath.Pull`, at most a quarter of the way in one talk).
- **Children** talk only of growing up (`TopicDef.forChildren`, `TopicWorker_Growing`): a pair with a child
  (`Talk.EligibleChild`) weighs only the topics for children, at half the pair's budget (`Talk.ChildShare`), and a pair
  of grown-ups never weighs them. Their lines say who speaks ([child], [!child]; a test checks every line does).
- **Not about everything**: a topic's worker can rule out teasing for the moment (`TopicWorker.NoTease`: a day of
  mourning on the calendar, as the dead always).
- **In the game's picker.** One InteractionDef per topic, and one each for remembering, an in-joke and comfort
  (`InteractionWorker_Talk`). They share one budget, 0.08 next to chitchat, times the moments frequency, the pair
  (friends, rivals, dislike) and `Heart.MomentWeightFactor` (which carries the persona's talkativeness, counted once),
  split by salience (`TalkMath.Shares`): more to talk about means livelier talk, not more of it. Worked out once per
  pair and tick. A starter waits 4 hours, a pair 10, a topic between the same two is rarer for two days (not saved).
  `ModOverlapDef` lowers it to 0.4 with RimTalk or Speak Up.
- **How it goes** (`TalkMath.Outcome`): a joker who likes the other teases (never someone low, never about the dead);
  close views agree; otherwise heat (the gap, both tempers against warmth, liking and humour, ties, a sore spat from
  `MomentTones`) decides a debate or an argument, and with frictions off nobody argues. Effects come in `Interacted`:
  small social thoughts (opinion only; the warm ones count for the heart through `RewardInstead`), views moved,
  `MomentTones` warm, friction or mend, tie bumps, now and then a `Persona.Nudge` (arguing hardens temper, a long
  friendship warms, jokes lighten), and a quarrel made up is remembered.
- **Lines** (`TalkLinesDef`: a topic or memory, a turn, outcomes, toned lines with tags): the turn's own pools (twice as
  likely) and the generic ones together, filtered by the moment (both sides, the outcome, their tie, the topic's news,
  the other's group and name read from tags only), in the speaker's voice (`TalkMath.Voice`: their tone, sharpened by
  how it goes), not a line said lately. Two to four lines, said through `Speech.Say` by `TalkTracker` (every 15 ticks,
  only while a talk is under way), dropped as soon as `Together.Can` fails. The game's own log entry for the
  interaction is the one summary (with a sentence on how it went, from a rule pack): a second one through
  `Speech.Logged` would only repeat it, and show twice with Interaction Bubbles.
- **Shared memories** (`SharedMemoryDef`, 17 here, 3 more from groups) come from one-line hooks where the colony
  already notices things (a fight over in SocialWeb, a death, a wedding, a birth, a caravan home, a breakdown), two small
  postfixes of its own (`Frame.CompleteConstruction`, `TendUtility.DoTend`), the talk's hour (night shifts, disasters
  lifting, gatherings ended, fires beaten out, food poisoning, a tame gone wrong from the play log; mentors and secrets
  daily) and a social event's effect (`DilemmaEffect_SharedMemory`). A mishap only becomes a joke an hour later, with
  everyone in it up and nobody of the colony dead meanwhile. A fight is remembered only by those seen side by side in
  it (sampled every 250 ticks while it's on, `TalkMath.BattlePairs`: three partners each, one memory a pair a day), and a
  pair keeps three of a kind at most, so a season of raids never pushes out a funeral, a quarrel made up or a joke. A
  fight is said aloud without its date (`FightNames.Spoken`).
- **What the newer systems leave behind** (`SharedTimes`, 14 more memories): one line where each system already says a
  thing is over, and nothing that ticks of its own. `CampLife.Finish`: evenings at the camp's fire (warmth 2 or more),
  the healer's farewell round (those it looked in on), the smith's mending (those about the camp). `Missions.Finish`:
  the lost child (the finder with three at home), the pilgrim's road and a neighbour's harvest (the caravan, read from
  the ending's look target). `CalendarKeeping.KeepDay`: a day kept without a gathering; with one, `PlayOutTracker.Done`
  knows it by name (`SharedTimes.DayOf`: a calendar day kept this year whose label the gathering carries) and gives
  it to those who came. `PlayOutTracker.Done` also gives the pyre (a haul), the night watch (a patrolling vigil) and
  lantern night (a gathering that ends while `OnMapTimed` keeps lanterns on that map). `WorldSituations.End`: the
  colony's part, when it counted. Labels are made unique enough that `AddOnce` never blocks a later one (a name, a
  date, a year). Two mishaps at a day's gathering (rain on it, a burned dish) wait half a day in an unsaved list,
  looked at in the setbacks' hour, before they become jokes.
- **Jokes passed on** (`JokesRetold`, `InteractionWorker_JokeRetold`): an InteractionDef in the game's picker, weight
  0.04 (x1.6 for a joker, x0.3 for the dour) while the teller has an in-joke with someone else, recalled once and not
  worn, from the last 60 days, that the listener isn't in on (by its label), both at opinion 10 or more; a teller once
  a day, a pair once a week, picks cached per pair for `Sched.RareTicks` (not saved). The teller and the friend share
  a `Rimfolk_Mem_JokeHeard` memory under the joke's own label, which is never passed on again.
- **The character page**: views (section 30, with what each rests on and the last talk that moved it) and shared
  memories (40).

### New moments of life together (the player's request, 6 November 2026)

"Do another big content update to existing mechanics": this part, what happens between colonists, in the existing
frameworks at their existing rates. Every piece starts from something on the map and takes a share of a draw that
doesn't read the defs, so none of them makes the colony busier; none stages a scene, hurts anyone or is saved. The pure
rules are `Social/TogetherFourMath.cs` (checked in `Tools/Tests/TogetherFourTests.cs`).

- **Social events** (`Rimfolk_SocialEvents_Together.xml`, 25; their rewards `Rimfolk_Thoughts_Together.xml`, mostly a
  few points of opinion and belonging instead of mood). New conditions on `SocialEventDef`, read where an event is cast:
  `bMemoryAboutA` (B's memory, `bMemories`, is of A: the game's `HadAngeringFight` after their fight, `Council_SavedMe`
  for the one who came for them), `sameWork` (both at the same work right now, side by side, of the listed work types;
  `{WORK}` its gerund, its first skill the event's for a lesson; `TogetherFourMath.SameWork`), `bMadeFineDays` (B
  finished something excellent or better within the days, `{THING}`: `Patch_ArcMade` tells `SocialEvents.Notify_Made`,
  kept unsaved by pawn) and `bHurtDays` (a hurt of everyday life within the days, `Harm.DaysSince`, with a wound that
  still shows). Role tags of the moment (the weather, the hour, at work or at the table, a newcomer:
  `TogetherFourMath.NeedsMoment`) are now read from the moment (`PeopleTags.MatchesNow`, `Flavor.TagsFor`) in
  `DilemmaRole.Extras`: before, the mud's in-joke (`Rimfolk_Soc_Mud`, roleA "rain|snow") fitted nobody, since who
  someone is has no weather. Texts take the age's form ([tribal], [medieval], [industrial], [spacer], [lowtech]), with
  untagged ones for any age.
- **Shared memories** (`Rimfolk_SharedMemories_Together.xml`, 6; lines `Rimfolk_Talk_Lines_Together.xml`), from one
  line each where the colony already says the thing happened (`Social/Talk/SharedTimesTogether.cs`): an illness nursed
  (`HealthTracker.PulledThrough`: the doctor who tended it twice or more, Rimfolk's serious illnesses and the game's
  own), a close call (`MapDangers.Wound`: the one hurt and whoever is in talking range, `Together.Company`, by the
  danger's name `CC_Times_Close_*`), a colony founded (`Foundings.Founded`: the party, each with the three closest), a
  debt remembered and two in-jokes (the downpour, the snowball fight) from social events.
- **The sick and the hurt** (`Rimfolk_Topic_Health`, `TopicWorker_Health`, its lines `Rimfolk_Talk_Lines_Health.xml`):
  comes up only while someone of the colony on the map is ill or healing from a hurt (looked up hourly a map), about the
  worst off when it isn't one of the two, more while something that can kill goes round (then nobody teases). A topic
  takes a share of the talk's one budget (`TalkMath.Shares`); it steps back with RimTalk or Speak Up.
- **Group habits** (`Rimfolk_GroupHabits_Together.xml`): an hour with a book (`read`: the game's reading), keeping the
  sick company (`sickbed`: one of them abed and healing, the others on the game's visit to the sick), music of an
  evening (`music`: one playing an instrument, Royalty's, the others at leisure within earshot) and the night sky
  (outdoors, 20 to 1). None has a `playKind`, and each comes after a kind's own habits, so what an anchor calls the
  group to and the colony's gatherings are as they were; a group still keeps one habit a day at most. Each is something
  a friendship group may be named for (`GroupShareDef`). A kind of group, the wardens (`Rimfolk_Group_Wardens`, the
  Warden work), and its share.
- **Dreams** (`Rimfolk_Dreams_Together.xml`, 11) after the new moments' memories ({OTHER} the one it was with) and after
  a founding (`Rimfolk_Parted`, `Rimfolk_Uprooted`); three of them nightmares.
- **A personal story**, back to it (`Rimfolk_Arc_BackToIt`, `ArcWorker_BackToIt`): a close call within three days
  (`SharedTimesTogether.RecentCloseCall`, unsaved), the one closest to them; a shaken day, a talk between the two, 800
  experience at the work it happened at (`TogetherFourMath.CloseCallSkill`: mining, plants, crafting) or what they do
  best, then it's just work again. Its gates never pass on time alone, so what its words say happened did.

### Traits that change
The game's traits can grow, appear or fade at the end of a stretch of life the player can read (`Persona/TraitChanges.cs`,
`TraitChangeMath.cs`). Each rule is a `TraitChangeDef`: a trait, gain, loss or a step of one degree (through none, so a
nervous colonist steadies to no nerves trait before steadfast), and what it asks for: marks (defNames, families or
stories), sides moved from nature (lasting plus fading) and where they stand, deeds counted on separate occasions (and
marks counted as they come, breakdowns, or a stretch with none), the game's records, a share of time from record
snapshots every ten days, calm days, skills, the faith they hold, a friend, an animal bonded to them (a dog or a cat of
the colony's, for so long), a trait they have; guards for DLC, mods and tech. 112 rules (20 November 2026): 41 give a
trait, 45 take one away, 26 move a trait one degree; 60 of them are ways out of a bad trait (`wayOutOf`, below).

- **Rare.** Checked in the council's day: when the colony has had no change for 10 days, every rule that holds for a
  colonist rolls its chance (3 to 15% a day) and one of those that come up happens; a way out of a bad trait doesn't
  wait for the colony's 10 days (see "More traits that come and go" below). Nobody twice in 60 days (except to
  take away a trait Rimfolk gave, see "Vengeful from Rimfolk" below); the same
  trait in a person waits its rule's gap (90 to 150 days). Only marks and deeds since that trait last changed count,
  so a stretch of life earns one change. Psychopath and cannibal need an extreme history and come once per colony.
- **Never touched.** Sexuality, the body and inborn gifts (`TraitChangeMath.Untouchable`), traits from genes, a
  backstory or the scenario, suppressed traits, an ideoligion role whose requirements speak of traits. The game's conflicts,
  exclusion tags, conflicting passions, backstory and gene rules hold; nobody gains past four traits.
- **Nothing doubles.** Nature is read from traits, so the shift a trait brings (worked out from nature before and after)
  is taken out of the person's moves, the fading part first, then the lasting part (`TraitChangeMath.Absorb`): every
  side stays put and the change is now held for good. A loss gives the shift back the same way.
- **Ways in.** The daily pass (one line in `CouncilDynamics.DailySecond`), the memory hook it shares with marks (one
  line), a postfix on `HistoryEventsManager.RecordEvent` for deeds with a doer, and the day's tales for executions.
- **Told.** A letter (good, bad or neither by rule) with the news, what it means and what led to it with dates, a
  journal line by tone, the chronicle, "Traits gained and lost" (page section 25) and a line in each side's tooltip
  for what went into a trait. Setting "Traits can change", under social life.

### Vengeful from Rimfolk, and a way out of it (the player's go, 17 November 2026; released 0.265.4)

The player: "i think two of my colonists became vengeful as a result of rimfolk, is that possible? ... now they have some
rivals within the colony and it gives them quite a huge debuff ... I've only had this vengeful one come up twice and
now i don't really know what I can do against it, as i don't want to evict any pawns"; the go on the lead's proposal:
"your fix sound great for the vengeful traits again, also please". Rimfolk's rule `Rimfolk_TC_VTE_Vengeful` gave
Vanilla Traits Expanded's `VTE_Vengeful` (its `VTE_MyRivalsAreAlive` is -20 mood while any rival lives, a rival being
the game's opinion of -20 or less) to someone who swore vengeance after a loss, at 8% a day, and nothing ever took it
away. In their save Avila (vengeful since day 100) and Bautista (since day 112) swore on the mechanoid hive Armmurd for
Alder (killed day 98.27); the vow is open with no kills, and Avila has Rimfolk rivalries with three colonists.

- **Reined in** (the same rule): only of a vow of vengeance that has stood 30 days unpaid (open against a people still
  at war with the colony, none of them fallen to the avenger yet), at 3% a day instead of 8 (about a month on average
  once everything holds, against twelve days before), never for someone with a rival among the colony's people (an
  announced rivalry on the Bonds page, or the game's opinion of -20 or less of a colonist, slave or prisoner), and one
  person at most for each loss. The marks, sides and Kind block are as they were. The loss behind it is kept with the
  change (`TraitChangeRecord.about`, the lost one's id or name); for a change from before (their two), it is read from
  the vows that person had sworn by then, so Alder's loss has made someone vengeful and makes nobody else so.
- **Two ways out**, each only for a vengeful Rimfolk gave (`onlyGiven`: the newest change of the trait kept for them
  gave it), each with no gap since it came (the default 120 days would hold it past day 220 in their game):
  `Rimfolk_TC_VTE_VengefulVowOver`, at 15% a day once no vow of theirs stands (avenged, three of them fallen to the
  avenger; laid down; lapsed two years after it was sworn; the one taken brought home; a blood price or an apology; or
  those who did it at peace with the colony); and `Rimfolk_TC_VTE_VengefulCalms`, at 5% a day after 45 days without a
  breakdown counted from when it came (`calmSinceChange`), with one good mark since (a kindness remembered, forgiven,
  nursed back, carried to safety or carrying someone out of a fight, a promise kept, a wedding, a child born or grown, a moving ritual, a student taught,
  a year of peace), whatever the vow: a mechanoid hive never makes peace.
- **Why these numbers.** 45 days is three quadrums, a real calm, and with the 5% after it the trait goes about two
  months after it came, about as long as the new way in takes. One mark rather than two: Avila's good marks came about
  one in forty days (three in his first 124), so two would put it near day 180, close to the vow's own lapse. In their
  save: Avila can be past the calm on day 145 and Bautista on day 157, each then needing a good mark since becoming
  vengeful (none yet on day 124); the vow on the hive ends at the latest when it lapses on day 218.3, earlier if three
  of the hive fall to each of them in fights against it or they lay it down (0.8% a day, 1.2 in a good mood, not within
  15 days of fighting the hive).
- **The person's 60 days** don't hold back a change that takes away a trait Rimfolk gave (`TraitChangeMath.RateBlocked`
  with `undoing`, `TraitChanges.Undoes`); the colony's 10 days and the rule's own gap still do.
- **Older saves.** A vengeful Rimfolk gave fades on the first way once no vow of theirs can be found standing: a
  vendetta that is gone, or vendettas switched off, count as over. A vengeful the colonist came with, or one whose change
  is no longer kept (eight later changes), is theirs and stays. `Vendetta.settledTick` (new, saved) dates an ending, so
  the letter names the vows that ended since the trait came.
- **Told and shown.** The gain's words now say what the trait does ("has started holding grudges, and is unhappy for as
  long as any of his rivals is alive"); the two fades have their own letters, journal lines in six voices, and the vows
  behind them in "What led to it" (how long the vow has stood unpaid; how each ended). A loss's letter now says the
  character stays where it was because what the trait held is counted with what life changed (`CC_TC_AbsorbedLost`; the
  gain's line was used for losses too). On the character page "Where life is taking them" shows a way out of a trait
  Rimfolk gave from the day it came (other rules still need a third of their evidence), and a marks line names the
  marks that count.
- **Code**: `Persona/TraitChangeMath.cs` (pure: `Vow`, `Unpaid`, `AnyStanding`, `LossesBehind`, `GaveIt`, `IsRival`,
  `CalmDays`, `RateBlocked(undoing)`), `Persona/TraitChangeDefs.cs` (`vendetta`, `vendettaDays`, `noRival`, `onlyGiven`,
  `calmSinceChange`), `Persona/TraitChanges.cs` (the daily pass, the gate, `Vows`, `LossesTaken`, `UnpaidVow`, `VowLines`,
  `HasRival`, `MarkNames`), `Secrets/Vendettas.cs` and `VendettaEnds.cs` (`settledTick`),
  `Defs/PersonaDefs/Rimfolk_TraitChanges_Mods.xml`, `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_TraitChanges.xml`, the Almanac page
  "traits that change". Tests: `TraitChangeTests` (the vows from their save, the limits, the rules).

### More traits that come and go, the first batch (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.275.0)

The player, 17 November 2026: "while i generally like the idea of traits emerging and/or disappearing (we shouild also
build up on this as to do)"; 19 November 2026: "More trades come and go sounds great"; 20 November 2026: "go ahead with
the next tasks, including the traits" (and later the same day, "go ahead with all the traits": the other 26 proposals
follow in two more builds). This build is the lead's recommended first batch of `docs/traits-proposals.md`: 37, 38, 1,
2, 4, 5, 6, 14, 10, 16, 26 and 27, each marked there. Harm: none of it gives a bad trait; every new rule takes one away
or gives a good one.

- **37, a way out isn't held back by the colony's 10 days.** A rule names the degrees it leads out of (`wayOutOf`; 0 for
  a trait without degrees). A change from one of them, for someone who has the trait there (`TraitChangeMath.IsWayOut`:
  nervous steadied to none is one, none to steadfast from the same rule is a gain, industrious to hard worker is
  not), doesn't wait for the colony's 10 days (`RateBlocked(..., wayOut)`); the person's 60 days and the rule's own gap
  still hold, and a way out still counts as the colony's change, so gains wait 10 days after it. The daily pass now
  runs within the colony's 10 days too, for the rules that lead out of something only. The 15 ways out already there
  are marked (nervous, volatile, pessimist, depressive, lazy twice, chemical interest, chemical fascination, abrasive,
  wimp, greedy, coward, vengeful twice, craven), so 30 in all.
- **38, every way out on the character page from the start.** "Where life is taking them" shows every way out of a
  bad trait the colonist has, first and whatever is there yet (`TraitChangeMath.BuildingShows`), then up to three other
  rules with a third of their evidence, as before. Under each way out, a line of what is still missing in plain words,
  one short phrase per part ("Still missing: one of: given a seat; 120 days without a mark of these: lost the vote,
  voted out of a seat (30 so far)"); the tooltip lists every part. A way out that grows from a habit shows once they
  have the habit (they can't be steered toward one). Its gap since the trait last changed is shown as a part while it
  lasts (`Gate(..., gapAsPart)`). New parts on the page for every rule: the marks it waits out (`notMarks`, which the
  rules checked but the page never showed), a stretch without something (a zero count), the faith it asks for. Parts
  that hold by default (nothing of a kind lately, a stretch without something, the gap) don't count as evidence toward
  showing a rule that isn't a way out, so an idle colonist isn't shown "1 of 2" toward idleness.
- **1, jealous fades** (any jealous): two rules, `Rimfolk_TC_JealousFadesSeat` (given a seat) and
  `..._JealousFadesPromises` (two promises kept to them); each with no seat or vote lost on their page in the last 120
  days and trust moved from their nature 0 or more ("back to where it was"), 8% a day, no gap.
- **2, bloodlust Rimfolk gave fades** (`Rimfolk_TC_BloodlustFades`, `onlyGiven`): no fight mark (held the line, hardened
  by the raids, went down and got up harder, swore vengeance) on their page in the last 120 days, a long peace since it
  came, warmth moved -5 or more ("near where it was"), 5% a day.
- **4, cannibal Rimfolk gave fades**, each for the cannibal its own rule gave (`givenBy`, new: `GaveIt` reads the rule of
  the newest change): famine's (`Rimfolk_TC_CannibalFamineFades`) after 180 days without eating human flesh (a zero
  count, new: a tally with `noneDays`, counted from the newest meal or from when the trait came, whichever is later,
  `TraitChangeMath.NoneDays`; the meals are the game's three history events and every human-flesh memory, a cannibal's
  own among them) and no hungry season in 120 days, 6% a day; a faith's (`..._CannibalFaithFades`, Ideology) once they
  took up a new ideoligion since it came and it holds none of the precepts that call for human flesh (new:
  `notPrecepts`, with its words for the page `notPreceptsLabel`), 8% a day.
- **5, world weary lifts** (`Rimfolk_TC_VTE_WorldWearyLifts`, Vanilla Traits Expanded, any): two long peaces, one good
  mark (moved by a ceremony, mastered a craft, a legendary piece, freed, overcame an addiction, given a seat, saw a
  student through), no death that marked them in 60 days, outlook moved -5 or more, 6% a day. A long peace leaves the
  page after 60 days and the next can only come 60 days later, so two can't be on the page at once: they are counted as

  240 days like any deed).
- **6, rebel settles** (Vanilla Traits Expanded, any): `Rimfolk_TC_VTE_RebelSettlesPromises` (two promises kept) and

### More traits that come and go, the new traits (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.277.1)

The player, 20 November 2026: "go ahead with all the traits". This build is the new traits of
`docs/traits-proposals.md`, 28 to 36, each marked there, and with it the whole list of 38 is built. 12 new rules (112 in
all): 10 give a trait, one more way out of a bad trait (60 in all), and desensitized going again. Harm: no new bad
trait. The good ones (healer's hands, dog and cat person, fisherman, mountain lover) come of good things; perfectionist
and wanderlust are neither good nor bad; the three that come of hard times (desensitized, drunken master, occultist)
are neither good nor bad, rare or uncommon (3 to 5% a day once everything holds), and come only of what already
happened on the map: fights the colony won but lost people in and its burials, fights won drunk, the colony's own dark
study and brushes with the unknown. Every trait from a mod by its defName in `docs/player-mods/traits.tsv` (active rows);
each rule does nothing without its mod. These are gains, so they wait for the colony's 10 days, and show under "Where
life is taking them" once a third of their evidence is there.

- **New parts.** A mark for the nurse (`Rimfolk_Mark_NursedSomeone`, family `NursedSomeone`: "nursed someone back to
  health"), the other side of "nursed back to health": given to the doctor in `HealthTracker.PulledThrough`
  (`PersonaMarks.Notify_Nursed`), after the doctor's own journal line so one happening is one line; a turning point kept
  180 days, each patient once while it lasts, the next patient a day later (`repeatDays` 1). An animal bonded to them of a

  counted only while they were drunk (`whileDrunk`, the game's alcohol high on them when the mark comes;
  `TraitChangeMath.TallyCounts`). Time awake under a rock roof (the practice `rock`: hours under a mountain's roof,
  mined out or overhead, `RoofDef.isNatural`; looked at hourly with the rest of the practice log, and fading the same
  way). And a count of marks now also reads the marks of its kind still on their character page (a masterwork made

### The animals' natures (the player's picks, 7 November 2026)

The player chose three from a brainstorm: temperaments (A1), friendships, rivalries and grief among animals (A3, "do it
a way where i don't have any more pop ups for this appearing") and animals that speak (B, rare and behind a setting).
None of it sends a letter or a message: it shows on the map, on the animal's card (`Patch_AnimalNatureInspect`, one
line under its inspect text, rebuilt every 250 ticks at most) and in what the colonists say (`Speech.Say`, the shared
once-a-day rate of everything said on screen) and write in their journals. The rules are pure in
`Animals/AnimalNatureMath.cs` (tests: `AnimalNatureTests`).

- **Who.** Every named or bonded animal of the colony has a temperament; friendships and feuds are the companions'
  (bonded, or not livestock: a herd the herdmaster names would otherwise pair off in every barn); grief is any named
  or bonded animal's.
- **Temperaments** (`Animals/AnimalTempers.cs`): brave, timid, greedy, gentle, proud, mischievous, loyal, lazy, curious.
  Given once from the animal's id and its kind's lean (`AnimalNatureMath.Weights`: its family read from its words, a
  dog loyal, a cat proud, a muffalo gentle, a thrumbo gentle and proud; predators brave and proud; the big gentle, the
  small timid; the most teachable loyal; a Pokémon's types: fire brave and proud, ghost mischievous, psychic proud and
  curious...), then kept. Each moment is something the animal does, by the game's own jobs or two of Rimfolk's
  (`JobDriver_AnimalLinger`: walk to a cell and stay, standing, lying, or holding its ground; `JobDriver_AnimalKnockOver`):
  | Temperament | What it does | Every |
  |---|---|---|
  | brave | stands between its person and the nearest attacker and fights what comes at it there (the fight's look); out of a fight, between its person and a wild predator near them | 2 days, when there is one; once a fight |
  | timid | bolts from the shooting within 20 cells (the fight's look); shies away from a stranger within 8 | 2 days; once a fight |
  | greedy | eats a meal or 3 to 6 of what it eats from the stores or off a table, within 30 cells | 5 days |
  | gentle | the game's nuzzle for someone sick, hurt or low; lies down by a patient asleep in a sickbed | 3 days |
  | proud | follows its person close while they milk, tend or train another animal; stands before a visitor | 3 days |
  | mischievous | a grazer eats a crop in a growing zone; else noses a light stack off a shelf onto the floor beside it | 5 days |
  | loyal | waits at the door to the outside (or by the bed) while its person is away; the game's nuzzle on their homecoming | about twice a day while away |
  | lazy | naps (the game's lying down, asleep) by a fire or heater below 8°C, under a roof above 30°C, else in the sun | 3 days |
  | curious | follows a visitor about; watches someone building, mining, repairing or at a bench | 3 days |

  Days at the setting's 100% (`animalMoments`, How much happens, 0 to 200%, light touch 50%, story-rich 150%; the
  hour's chance `HourChance`, half again as likely in view), a gap of two fifths of that after each, one moment an
  hour on a map, none in danger; the fight's look (three in five each 250 ticks at 100%) once in eight hours each.
- **Friends and rivals** (`Animals/AnimalBonds.cs`): two companions asleep within 1.9 cells on three nights (a night
  counted once, the small hours with the evening before) are friends, two at most each; by day one follows the other
  a while (`FollowClose`) with a heart and a nuzzle in the log (`SocialLog.Add`, only when they are close and in
  sight), about every day and a half; at bedtime a tired one lies down beside its sleeping friend. Two of different
  kinds about each other by day (within 6 cells) roll once a day (`RivalChance`: one day in 250, ten times that for a
  cat and a dog, more for two hunters and for the proud, the greedy and the mischievous, less for the gentle; never
  friends or the same kind), one rival each; rivals in sight hiss, growl, snort or squawk at each other in the log
  (by voice), one flees and the other chases a moment, about every two days. Nobody is hurt (no `Harm` here). Not seen
  together 40 days, they drift apart.
- **Grief**: a bonded animal whose person died and lies in a grave on the map (the body's own time of death) goes to
  lie on the grave (`Rimfolk_AnimalVigil`) about every two and a half days for 60 days, about every eight until 120;
  whoever mourns the dead most (partner, kin, the warmest) may say so and write it, once in twelve days. A friend of
  an animal that died misses it 30 days (its card) and goes to its grave if it has one.
- **Old animals**: one of the colony's named or bonded animals that leaves alive (the pets' watch: sold, given,
  released, gone wild) is kept with the person it was last seen with; meeting them again on any map 2 to 120 days
  later, within 30 cells, it trots over and stays at their side a while with a heart, once in ten days; the handler
  says something, and writes the first meeting down.
- **Speaking animals** (`Animals/AnimalVoices.cs`), a fantasy part, the setting "Animals speak" (`speakingAnimals`:
  Auto, the default, on only while PokéWorld or A RimWorld of Magic is loaded or someone of the colony has a psylink,
  looked at hourly; On; Off). Who, softly by mod and by age: a psychic-type Pokémon (`PokeWorldLink.TypesOf`) to its
  trainer, in the mind; a druid's or a ranger's bonded animal (A RimWorld of Magic's class traits by name); a bonded
  animal of a psycaster of psylink level three or more (Royalty); Vanilla Genetics Expanded's humanoid hybrids, read by
  their comp's name (`CompProperties_HumanoidHybrid`: their own defs give them conversation with the colony; the
  manbear, manwolf, manchicken and the rest), aloud to their person or whoever is with them; in a tribe (the colony's
  age neolithic or below) or for a colonist whose faith has Ideology's animal personhood, a bonded animal is a spirit
  animal that speaks only in their dreams (`DreamAbout.SpiritAnimal`, `Council_Dream_SpiritAnimal`). What it does: a
  line in its own voice (`Council_Pool_AnimalVoice`, tagged by voice, temperament, gift and a Pokémon's types) to its
  person when the two are together and in view (a chance in five each hour, a day apart at least); a warning over its head of
  raiders in a fight or a predator about within 45 cells (an angry beast, one hunting, or one near its own size), with
  the compass word for where, once a day for the same danger and half a day apart for predators; at a council meeting
  its person sits in, it comes to the table at their heels and has one line, its person's side or its own, written
  with the meeting's remarks, and never votes; on half the council's questions about its person or itself, a word in
  the question's letter, said over its head too when its person is beside it.
- **Saved** (`AnimalBook`, a GameComponent: an older save gets an empty one): temperaments by id (300, let go 120
  days unseen; a PokéWorld evolution carries its own over with its ties), pairs and ties by id with names (80, pairs
  first to go), animals gone with their handler by reference (30, forgotten after 120 days or when the handler dies).
  What it did lately, the waits, the homecomings watched and the animals let speak by a dev action are not saved.
- **Ticking**: in the animals' hour and day (`AnimalLife`, the council's people pass) and, for the fight, on the fight
  sides' 250-tick look (`Sched.RareFightSides`): no new slot.

### The animals, made more visible (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.241.0)

The player: "i must say that i can't really see a lot from the animal features we included, please add to to-do list to
enhance and build up on these", then "do ... making animals more visible". The reasons, from the code and the player's save
(League of Toba, 14 November 2026: twelve animals, a horse, a thunderox, an ankylosaurus, two giant crowned silkies, two
titanis, a dusk prowler, a blood scarab, a raccoon and two companion dryads): nobody was bonded to any of them and only the
dusk prowler had a master, so everything that needed "its person" never happened (a pet following, the loyal one at the
door, the brave one's stand, five of the ten temperaments, grief, the old companion's story); six colonists filled six
seats, so there was no herdmaster and none of the herdmaster's work; friendships needed two pets asleep side by side, and
the three pets slept apart, so in 99 days not one pair formed; and the animals' encounters, which did come often (seventeen
of them fired), were only words in the news, never anything on the map, and some could say what wasn't so: the new litter
(which fired) could be told of any animal, newborns or not, the animal on guard (which fired) with no stranger about, and
the old friend slowing down of a young animal. There were no children, so a child's play could not come either.

- **Every animal has its person** (`AnimalFacts.PersonOf`): the one it is bonded to, its master, else the colonist it is
  fond of (`AnimalFacts.FondOf`, `AnimalDaysMath.Favourite`). Among the colony's people living where it lives (and those
  away from there, not another colony's), weighted by `FondWeight` (1, plus a fifth of their Animals level, 1.5 for a
  passion, 2 for a child, 1 for Kind; a quarter for someone who never handles animals, a child aside), and fixed for the
  pair: each person's score is an even draw from the two ids stretched by their weight (`-ln(u)/w`), lowest wins, so the
  animal keeps the one it took to and a newcomer only ever wins an animal from the rest. Worked out at most once an hour,
  not saved. Its card says "fond of" whom. The temperaments use it (`AnimalTempers.TryMoment`, the loyal one's wait and
  homecoming), as does a pet following its person (`AnimalLife.Follow`); only a bond or a master takes an animal into a
  fight (`FightBrave` keeps `PetTracker.PersonOf`), so no animal is put in harm's way that wasn't before.
- **Friends across kinds** (`AnimalBonds.Nights`, `AnimalDaysMath.MayBefriend`): two that sleep side by side on three
  nights may be friends when they are two pets or two of different kinds (the horse and the barn's goat), never two of the
  herd's own kind. Feuds stay the pets' own.
- **Their days on the map** (`Animals/AnimalDays.cs`, from the animals' hour; the pace `animalMoments`, "Animals' moments
  on the map", 100% by default; all under "Pets as companions"):
  | Moment | What is seen | How often at 100% |
  |---|---|---|
  | home again | its person back after four hours or more away (a caravan, a site), the animal runs to them (`JobDriver_AnimalRunTo`, `Rimfolk_AnimalGreet`) and gives the game's nuzzle as it gets there, and they say hello then; the loyal ones have their own homecoming; out of danger only, the welcome waiting for it to pass | 8 in 10 for a pet, 4 in 10 for the herd's ones, within three hours of their return |
  | the foot of the bed | at bedtime (ten to one) a pet up to 1.6 body size goes into its person's room and sleeps on the cell just past the foot end of the sleeper's place (`Building_Bed.GetFootSlotPos`, `AnimalDaysMath.FootCells`; a bed's own cells can't be stood on), else beside its foot, else beside the bed in the same room; they mention it when they wake (five to ten), a journal line now and then | about every three nights |
  | a meal | a pet goes to sit at the elbow of someone eating (sat with their food), its own person first, facing them a while; they tell it no as it sits down, if still eating | about every two days, half again for a greedy one |
  | play | a child with free time and a calm animal within 25 cells (up to 2.5 body, no hunter over 1.2): the animal bounds about the child (`JobDriver_AnimalPlay`) and the child chases it (`JobDriver_PlayWithAnimal`, some recreation), both at a run, 1,200 ticks | about daily for each child |
  | the herd | in the early morning (six to nine) a herd of two or more grown of one kind (herd animals) follows its eldest, the herd's leader when it is one of them, to fresh grazing 5 to 30 cells off in its area and pen | about every day and a half for each kind |
  | the rounds | in their free time the herdmaster, else whoever is best with animals and handles them, goes round up to five of the colony's animals, nearest next (`JobDriver_KeeperRound`), 300 ticks beside each while it holds still, a little handling practice and a little of the recreation the free time would have given; a word to the first (sick, hurt, in young) | about every two days, half again for a herdmaster |
  | rain and snow | when rain or snow (rate 0.5 or more) comes on by day, up to three named pets out in it go in under a roof in the home area and lie down a while, the first remarked on as it lies down there; in the snow up to two young ones play in it | when the weather turns |
  | a bitter night | below -8 °C at night, each herd of one kind out in the open lies down close round its eldest | once a night |
  | raiders | as they come (the fight's 250-tick look), up to two named pets, never a timid one, turn to face the nearest and give their own call (`Pawn_CallTracker.DoCall`), and someone says where (`AnimalNatureMath.Compass`) | once a fight |
  | a strange sky | a god's presence on the map (its condition, `GameCondition_GodPresence`), out of danger: up to three pets go to keep close to their person a while (`Rimfolk_AnimalKeepClose`), the first crying out as it goes, and someone says the animals are restless once it is at their side; the god is never named | once a presence |
  | a death | when its person dies (the animals' hour keeps whom each is with, `AnimalDays.Deaths`, and sees it before another takes their place, with or without temperaments), the animal goes to lie by the body or the grave it is in (`Rimfolk_AnimalMourn`), cries out as it lies down and every 1,500 ticks (the linger's `callEvery`), and stays 7,500 ticks, once the danger is past, within half a day; whoever sees it says so as it lies down; the bonded ones' grave visits go on as before | once a death |

  Each is noted on the animal's card ("lately") and said in one plain sentence (`Rimfolk_Pool_AnimalDays`, tagged by
  moment, temperament, family, body), through `Speech.Say` at the shared once-a-day rate. One of each a map an hour at
  most; nothing in danger but the alarm; never a mount carrying its rider (Giddy-Up's mounted job, `AnimalDays.Ridden`).
- **Said as it is seen** (`AnimalArrivals`, `Animals/AnimalDayJobs.cs`): what is said about a moment waits for the animal
  to get there, so the words and the sight come together: `AnimalDays.StartThen` sets what is said for the job's id before
  the job starts (one already there arrives at once), and `JobDriver_AnimalLinger` (as it starts to stay),
  `JobDriver_AnimalRunTo` (as it reaches them) and `JobDriver_SitWithAnimal` (as they sit down) say it. Jobs cut short
  never arrive, and their words are never said; after a load the jobs play out without them.
- **Encounters that happen on the map first** (`Animals/AnimalScenes.cs`): an encounter with an animal's scene
  (`DilemmaEffect_AnimalScene`) is played out and only then told, its words, moods and journal line coming as it is seen
  (`Strangers/Encounters.cs` calls `AnimalScenes.Begin`; told once at most); one whose moment never comes is never told.
  Fifteen of the seventeen with the colony's animals: the welcome (it runs to them and nuzzles them, told as it reaches
  them), warm feet (it sleeps at the foot of their bed that night, told in the morning), the stolen dinner (at their next
  meal it sits at their elbow, told as it sits down, then runs off), a child at play (chase), adopted by an animal and
  company at work (it keeps at their side a while, told as it reaches them), comfort (it walks over, nuzzles them and stays
  at their side), a new trick (it bounds about in front of them, and they stop to watch in their free time), the larder
  raid (it makes for the stores, never a table, and eats there, the game's own eating, in place of food taken off the
  count; told as it sets off, its words saying that much), confiding in it (in their free time they sit with it a while,
  told as they sit down), the grudge (it runs at their heels and off again, told as it reaches them), the old friend
  slowing down (an animal old for its kind only, `moment` `x:oldanimal`: it walks over to them and stays at their side),
  the new litter (only an animal with newborns of its own on the map, born within six days, `AnimalDaysMath.Newborn`, in
  any season: it lies by them, they keep close to it, and the colonist comes over in their free time to look, told as they
  get there), the animal on guard (only with a stranger, a visitor or trader, within 18 cells and in sight: it goes and
  stands between them, facing the stranger, `Rimfolk_AnimalGuard`, told as it takes its place) and the noise in the night
  (it goes a few steps further out under the open sky, faces the dark and cries out every 300 ticks, `Rimfolk_AnimalCry`,
  told at its first cry). An encounter whose words need newborns or a stranger is cast only with them there
  (`AnimalScenes.Fits`, in `Encounters.Cast`), so it is never told without them, scene or not. Their words were rewritten
  to say only what the scene shows. A meal, a night and a free hour are waited for, a day and a half at most. Left as
  words: the gift from the hunt and the chewed belongings, which would need things made or spoilt.
- **The personal stories' steps, on the map**: every step of the animals' stories before the last now has something seen
  (the old companion at its person's heels; the orphan following them, then visited in the evening; the stray watched at
  dusk and visited before the handlers try it; the feud's ambushes, an evening in each other's company, then the animal at
  their heels; PokéWorld's partner at the trainer's heels and a visit once friends).
- **Families from the mod pool**: Vanilla Animals Expanded's dogs by their breeds (beagle, chihuahua, corgi, bulldog,
  shepherd, Great Dane, poodle, pug, rottweiler, shih-tzu), the Maine coon, Odyssey's greatwolf and prairie dog, and the
  big grazers, small animals and snakes of the game, Odyssey and Vanilla Animals Expanded have their families
  (`AnimalNatureMath.Family`), so their lines and leans fit; a temperament already given is kept.
- **Nothing saved**: the person is worked out; what waits (a homecoming, a morning's word, a scene, a death, the words
  for an arrival) is this session's; the jobs keep only their own timings (`until`, `about`, `nextCall`, `looked`). No Sched
  slot: the animals' hour and the fight's look. No harm, no letter, no message.
- **Dev mode** (`Animals/AnimalDaysDebug.cs`): whom each animal is with (bond, master, fond of), any daily moment now, an
  encounter's scene for a colonist and an animal picked.

### The colony's animals hunting for themselves (the player's request, 7 November 2026)

The player's husky starved: the game never lets a tame animal hunt unless its kind is flagged a predator, and then only
as `JobGiver_GetFood`'s last resort (`FoodUtility.TryFindBestFoodSourceFor` falls to `BestPawnToHuntForPredator` when no
food at all is found, by the game's prey rules: combat power and size against the hunter's). A husky isn't flagged, can't
graze, and its area ("Animals") left out the stores. The player: "can you make animals hunt if they would do in reality,
and your judgement for fictive species, and that they hunt what they would normally would, or hunt things below them in
the food chain, not above". The pure rules are `Animals/HuntMath.cs` (`HuntTests`, which judge every animal of the base
game, the DLCs and the player's 29 animal mods from their own defs, `Tools/Tests/HuntKinds.txt`); the game's side is
`Animals/PetHunts.cs`, `PetHuntsPatches.cs` and `PetHuntsDebug.cs`.

- **Who hunts** (`HuntMath.Judge`), in this order: a dryad, a kind that eats nothing and one whose diet has no meat (it
  couldn't eat its kill) never; a Pokémon by its species in the table, else by its type, a legendary never; any other kind
  by its defName in the table, else by a word of its name (the last word first: a red fox is a fox, a sabertooth squirrel
  a squirrel), else by the rule. Each entry gives a step and a reason, and whether the kind hunts in packs, takes insects
  or takes venomous prey.
  | Who | Step | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | dogs (husky, labrador, terrier, retriever, shepherd, corgi, beagle, the hounds, dingo, dhole...) | by size, in packs | they chase down and kill small game; the game doesn't flag them |
  | lapdogs (pug, French bulldog, shih-tzu, chihuahua...) | prey | bred for company, they barely hunt |
  | wolves, hyenas, coyotes, jackals, the African wild dog | by size, in packs | |
  | foxes, the thylacine, weasels, ferrets, martens, badgers, wolverines | by size | |
  | the mongoose | hunter | takes snakes too |
  | house cats (whatever their size: a Maine coon too) | small hunter | they keep the mice and birds down |
  | wild cats (lynx, caracal, serval, ocelot) | by size | |
  | big cats, smilodons; lions (in prides) | apex | |
  | bears (the panda aside) | apex | |
  | birds of prey (eagle, hawk, falcon, owl) | by size | carrion birds (vultures, condors) are prey |
  | snakes; crocodiles; monitors | by size; apex; by size | |
  | raptors (in packs) and the hunting dinosaurs | by size | |
  | fish eaters (penguins, seals, otters, herons), lizards and tortoises, apes and monkeys, rooters (pigs, boars, raccoons, rats), grazers, browsers, fowl, small grazers | prey | the game's flag on a mod's twist (a vampire deer) still stands over a prey word |
  | Megafauna's giant penguin and walrus kin; Alpha Animals' plasmorph (a snail) and frostmite (a scavenger) | prey | the game flags them, but they fished, dug or scavenged |
  | Megafauna's meganeura | small hunter | a giant dragonfly |
  | A RimWorld of Magic's minions, demons, elementals, sentinels and golems | prey | summoned or made: they don't feed themselves (over the game's flag) |

  **The rule** for every kind the table doesn't name (most of Alpha Animals, ReGrowth, Vanilla Genetics Expanded's hybrids,
  Odyssey's and any later mod's): no meat, no hunt; the game's predator flag, or a meat-only diet with teeth or claws, a
  hunter by its size (under 0.7 a small hunter, under 1.6 a hunter, else apex); an omnivore the game doesn't flag doesn't.
  **Pokémon** by species: the canines (Growlithe, Houndour, Poochyena, Rockruff, Lillipup, Electrike, Yamper, Riolu...,
  in packs), foxes (Vulpix, Zorua, Nickit, Fennekin), cats (Meowth, Glameow, Skitty, Purrloin, Litten... small hunters),
  lions (Shinx, Litleo, in prides), Sneasel and Weavile (packs), the mongooses (Zangoose, Yungoos: snakes too), bears,
  birds of prey (Pidgeotto, Fearow, Noctowl, Staraptor, Braviary, Talonflame, Decidueye, Corviknight...), snakes (Ekans,
  Seviper), crocodiles (Sandile, Totodile lines), the hunting dragons (Gible, Bagon, Deino, Axew, Trapinch lines,
  Druddigon), the fossil hunters (Tyrunt, Aerodactyl, Archen, Kabutops, Tyranitar), the hunting bugs (Scyther, Spinarak,
  Galvantula, Skorupi, Sizzlipede, Venipede lines), Pawniard's packs, Heatmor (it eats Durant); a Pokémon the table
  doesn't name hunts only when it is a Dark type of 0.4 or more or a Dragon type of 1 or more (by its size), and the Dark
  and Dragon kinds that don't hunt are named as prey (Dratini's line, Altaria, Goomy's line, the apple dragons, the
  fighters, the sea hunters, the tricksters, Stunky, the vultures). Over the player's game: 16 of the base game's and the
  DLCs' 71 animals hunt, 194 of the other mods' 575, and 119 of PokéWorld's 898 species.
- **What it takes** (`HuntMath.WhyNotPrey`): only a wild animal (no faction, no host), never a person, anyone's tame or
  penned animal, one of Rimfolk's stories (`PackAlphas.Storied`: a named alpha or its pack, a beast nemesis, also one that
  fled, the beast that stays, a legend, anything named), a sacred one, a legendary, one with a group (a herd crossing: a
  stampede waiting), one marked for taming, a manhunter or one in any mental state, one that bursts, splits or vanishes
  when it dies (a boomrat); never an insect or a venomous animal unless its kind's entry says so; only a lower step; no
  bigger than its limit (its size times 0.8, or 1.2 for two of a pack kind together; the game's own maxPreyBodySize where
  its kind has one; a small hunter 0.4 at most, a hunter 1.25, 1.6 in a pack; small game 0.4 for a fed one); and, unless
  the prey is down already, less of a fight than 0.6 of its own (the game's combat power times health times size; 1 in a
  pack) and unlikely to turn on it: the game's revenge chance against it in melee (three times the kind's, with PokéWorld's
  level factor) at most 0.1 for prey a third of its size or more, 0.35 for smaller. Then inside its allowed area, not
  forbidden, reachable, within 120 cells (30 for a fed one), the best by the game's own prey score (`GetPreyScoreFor`).
  For example: a husky takes hares, squirrels and foxes, never a deer alone (two huskies may take an ibex), never a wolf or
  a cobra; a cat takes rats, squirrels and hares, not a wild hen or a fox; a wolf alone takes hares and foxes, two wolves an
  ibex or a gazelle, never an elk or a caribou (its herd would turn); a grizzly takes a deer, never an elk alone or a wolf
  (wolves turn on what hurts them); an Arcanine takes a Rattata or a Pidgey but leaves a Growlithe (it would fight back) and
  a Houndoom (its equal); a Growlithe takes a hare but leaves a Rattata near its own size.
- **When** (`HuntMath.WhyNot`): hungry (past its kind's wish to eat, as the game's food search asks, within that node's
  bounds) with nothing the game's food search found inside its area: `Patch_PetHuntsHungry` (a postfix on
  `JobGiver_GetFood.TryGiveJob`) gives it the game's own `PredatorHunt` (kill, then eat) on the prey above, with one free
  of its pack kind beside it joining; the game's own hunt for a flagged predator is replaced by the same choice (none when
  the rules allow nothing), and food the game found always stands. An animal that looked and found nothing doesn't look
  again for 600 ticks. Fed, a hunter idle in its area sets out about once in four days (1 in 96 an hour, a day and a half
  apart at least, one a map an hour, the people's hour of `CouncilGameComponent`), for small game only; a third of the time,
  with its person up on the map and in reach, it carries the kill to them (`Rimfolk_PetBringsKill`,
  `JobDriver_PetBringsKill`: the game's chase and blows as `JobDriver_PredatorHunt`'s, then the body taken up, carried and
  set down at their feet; their thought "a present from my animal", +3 for 2 days, the pet's present event's). Never with
  the setting off or its "May hunt" off, young, away, downed, drafted, following its master into work or a fight (the game's
  `ShouldFollowMaster`), roped or penned, with a group, in a mental state, ill enough for bed, under 0.6 of its health,
  without an attack, or with danger on the map; a hunt under way is given up when one of those comes up, or when its hunter
  has strayed 6 cells or more outside its area (the wild's short pass, every 250 ticks, `BeastBook.Rare`: no new slot).
- **Harm.** The hunt is the game's own fight, so prey fighting back can hurt a pet now and then, as it does the game's wild
  hunters; the choice of prey (smaller, much weaker, unlikely to turn on it, never venomous) keeps that small. Rimfolk rolls
  nothing of its own here, so the shared budget (`Harm/HarmBudgetMath.cs`) doesn't count it, as it doesn't count the game's
  own predators, raids or the colony's hunters: none of it goes through `Harm`. Starting a hunt needs 0.6 of its health
  and nothing to rest for; a hunt under way has its own rule (`HuntMath.StopChase`, 0.168.1, after the player's dog went
  home hungry): a bite that wants tending or the prey turning on it (which the game counts as danger) doesn't end it, and
  it breaks off only for the player's word, being downed, badly hurt (under 0.35 of its health), bleeding out within a
  day, unable to fight or move, or another danger on the map. Once the prey lies dead, the meal is eaten.
- **Seen.** At the kill, someone in view says a word (`Council_Pool_SeeHunt`, through `AnimalTempers.Remark`: the shared
  once-a-day rate of things said on screen; tagged eat or carry, hungry or sport, small or big, pack, body, Pokémon), and the
  animal's card says what it caught; the carried kill gets its person's word to it (`Council_Pool_PetBringsKill`). No letter
  and no message. Fresh carcasses (`Alert_FreshCarcass`) leave a kill alone while a colony animal is eating it.
- **The alert** (`Alert_NoFoodInReach`, the game's alert list): one of the colony's animals hungry (Hungry or worse), not
  fed by someone in bed or downed, not penned or hitched (the game has its own alerts for those), not with a group, with
  nothing the game's food search finds in its area (reservations ignored) and no hunt to go on (its kind doesn't hunt, it
  is kept or young, the setting is off, it can't now, or there is nothing it may take in reach), on two looks in a row.
  It names each (twelve at most, then "and N more"), says why (food it eats lies outside its area; the food inside it is
  forbidden; there is nothing it eats on the map, with what it eats) and how to put it right (the area Unrestricted or
  wider; unforbid; a stockpile of what it eats inside its area). A click selects them. Its bonded person says so aloud
  once (`Council_Pool_SayPetNoFood`), within six hours while they are up on the map being looked at, not again within 12.
- **Control.** The setting "Pets hunt for themselves" (`petsHunt`, What's on, on by default; off, the game's own rules
  stand untouched), "An animal with no food in reach" (`noFoodAlert`, Alerts, on), and on each animal whose kind hunts a
  "May hunt" button (`Patch_PetHuntsGizmo`, a `Command_Toggle` on `Pawn.GetGizmos`, the game's hunt icon). Off, it never
  hunts, the game's own last-resort hunt included.
- **Saved**: only the ids kept home (`AnimalBook.keptHome`, 200 at most, let go when the animal dies or leaves). The hunts
  under way, the waits and the alert's looks are not: a hunt running at a save goes on as the game's own job.
- **Softly.** Every kind by its def and words, nothing required; PokéWorld by its species and types
  (`PokeWorldLink.TypesOf`, `PokeWorldLegends`) and its own revenge patch; Hunt for Me's trained hunts for the colony are
  its own jobs and stay its own (this is the animal feeding itself); a mod that gives a hungry animal another food job
  (foraging, fishing) wins, since food found always stands.

### A bleeding animal's body taken when it dies (the player's request, 8 November 2026)

The player: "if i see a wild animal is bleeding out, can i give a command to haul it's corpse once it's dead? not to hunt
it, in case it's a strong one, but just to wait for it to die. if the animal recovers from bleeind comehow, this job
shouild be cancelled." The pure rules are `Animals/BodyWhenItDiesMath.cs` (`BodyWhenItDiesTests`); the game's side
`Animals/BodyWhenItDies.cs`, `BodyWhenItDiesPatches.cs` and `BodyWhenItDiesDebug.cs`; the mark
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_BodyWhenItDies.xml`.

- **The order.** On a selected animal that isn't the colony's (wild or another people's), alive, on the map and bleeding
  (the game's `BleedRateTotal` at its own floor of 0.0001), the button "Take the body when it dies" (`Patch_BodyWhenItDiesGizmo`,
  a `Command_Action` on `Pawn.GetGizmos`, the game's haul icon). It puts Rimfolk's designation `Rimfolk_TakeBodyWhenDead`
  on it (the haul icon again, no new art): the game draws it over the animal, saves it with the map, and its Cancel tool
  (and the Cancel button that then shows on the animal) takes it off. It replaces a hunting or taming order on it, as the
  game's own animal orders replace each other (`RemoveAllDesignationsOn`).
- **Its tooltip** says what it does, the bleeding rate, and how it will likely go (`BodyWhenItDiesMath.Outlook`, the game's
  rules): it bleeds to death in about the health tab's own figure (`TicksUntilDeathDueToBloodLoss`: blood left over the rate
  now), or it shouldn't, because its wounds stop bleeding on their own first (an injury after 1.5 days, up to 3 days for a
  wound of 30, `Hediff_Injury.AgeTicksToStopBleeding`; a missing part after 1.5 days) or because under 10% a day the blood
  comes back (`HediffGiver_Bleeding`). The wounds are followed one by one as they close, the game's factors scaling them
  alike.
- **While it lives** nothing is done: nobody hunts or hauls it, the colony's pets leave it out of their prey
  (`HuntMath.PreyFacts.markedForBody`), and Rimfolk's own hunts already skip an animal with another order on it
  (`PlayHunt.ChooseGame`, the wishes' prey).
- **When it dies**, however it dies (`Patch_BodyWhenItDiesKill`): the game's `Pawn.Kill` puts the body down, forbidden
  outside the home area unless a hunter killed it or it was marked for hunting, and only after that, destroying the animal,
  removes every order on it (`Thing.Destroy`, `RemoveAllReservationsAndDesignationsOnThis`). So the prefix reads the mark on
  the map that holds it and the postfix, once the animal is really dead (another mod may stop a death), unforbids the body
  and gives it the game's own `Haul` order unless it already lies in storage; a hauler takes it to the best storage by the
  usual rules. With no storage on the map that takes it (`StoreUtility.TryFindBestBetterStorageFor`, no carrier), the
  player is told once (`Notify.Message`, the body the look target) and the body waits, unforbidden and marked.
- **Cancelled on its own**, looked at on the wild's short pass (`BeastBook.Rare`, every 250 ticks, no slot of its own):
  `BodyWhenItDiesMath.Judge` drops the order with one message naming the animal and why when it stopped bleeding (its wounds
  aged out, were tended or healed), was tamed or came over to the colony (the game takes every order off an animal that
  changes hands, so this is read from its faction and whether it was wild when marked), or left the map (also with its
  order still on it, carried off or walked out). Cancelled by the player, or replaced by a hunting or taming order, it is
  dropped without a word; the setting or the deeper hooks off, every mark is dropped without a word.
- **Saved**: nothing of its own. The mark is the game's designation; whether each marked animal was wild is session
  memory, filled again from the marks (by the animal's faction then) on the first short pass after a load. No new Sched
  slot, two Harmony patches.
- **Control**: the setting "Take a bleeding animal's body when it dies" (`bodyWhenItDies`, What's on, Strangers and
  creatures, on by default, under the deeper hooks). Harm: none of its own; the animal bleeds from what already happened on
  the map.

### Riding out to far work and back with Giddy-Up 2 (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.258.0)

The player, 15 November 2026, with their save `League_of_Toba`: "pawns should really use mounts whenever they walk away
out of the base range. sometimes they do, but sometimes they don't, i don't uinderstand. for example now avila did not
mount up despite going really far to mine. it should mount to go there, and mount back up aftr finishing work. same for
all other activities where they walk out further out of the base." And on 16 November 2026: "please also do your
implementation of the pawn mount logic for further distances, it's not really working for all movement orders via giddy
up default settings." The game's side is `Integrations/GiddyUpRideOut.cs` (with `GiddyUpMounts.MountFirst`), the pure
rules `Integrations/RideOutMath.cs` (`RideOutTests`).

**How Giddy-Up 2 - Continued rides by itself** (read from its source, version 2.2.5, and the 1.7 assembly the player
runs, which matches it; `MountUtility.TryAutoMount`, `IsMountableUtility`, `JobDriver_Mounted`, `JobDriver_WaitForRider`,
its settings in `ModSettings_GiddyUp`):

- **When it looks.** As a colonist's next job is chosen (`Pawn_JobTracker.DetermineNextJob`, a postfix), for a colonist
  the player controls who is not drafted, not in a mental state, not riding already and not travelling with a caravan,
  on a map not in a vacuum, with its Ride and Roll part on.
- **The distance.** A straight line from where the colonist stands to the job's first target (for tending, refuelling
  and repairs the second target; for a bill its first ingredient), plus, for a haul to a cell or a container only, the
  carry from the thing to where it goes. Only when that is longer than its setting "Find a mount if trip is longer
  than..." (`minAutoMountDistance`, 120 cells by default, 20 to 500) does it look for a mount at all. Then the colonist
  must be "allowed to ride" (its column on the Assign tab), old enough for handling work and not in a wheelchair, not
  lent to another faction and not forming a caravan.
- **The beast** (`IsMountable` with every check on): the colony's own; on its list of animals to ride (body size over
  1.2 by default, or as the player set it in its settings); grown, unless "disregard age"; tame (it asks for Tameness,
  though its menu line says obedience); the rider's mass within its carrying capacity, unless "disregard carrying
  capacity"; not carrying someone, laying an egg, nuzzling, mating, vomiting or downed; not led on a rope; not in someone
  else's forming caravan; not below "Too injured threshold" (75% health), with a wound needing tending, on fire,
  urgently hungry or very tired; its research done; not reserved by anyone but someone roping it. Then the automount
  column on the Animals tab (anyone, colonists, slaves, or nobody; "Automount disabled by default" makes new animals
  nobody's).
- **Which, and whether.** The beast that gets them there soonest (the walk to it to the power 1.05, the ride 5% longer
  than the straight line, at its speed under that rider), only when that beats walking, and never when the beast already
  stands within a quarter of the setting (30 cells) of the work. The rider is given its "Mount" job in front of the
  chosen job.
- **On the way and at the work.** The beast carries them while the job is one it lets a rider do in the saddle (going
  somewhere, hauling, hunting unless "No mounted hunting", fighting, waiting, rescuing, arresting, carrying the downed,
  trading, roping, a bill not done at its workbench, and a few more). For any other job (mining, building, cutting,
  growing, cooking and the rest), once within 25 cells of where they are going, they park the beast: at the mount spot
  nearest the work, else a pen; if that is more than "Autohitch threshold" (50 cells) from the work, at a free cell 5 to
  35 cells from it, hitched there if the beast needs a pen. Heading into its "forbid riding area" parks the same way.
- **The wait and the way back.** The parked beast waits for its rider (`WaitForRider`) for "Wait for rider timer"
  (10000 ticks, 4 hours), keeping within 8 cells of them (or of its hitching spot). Its own lengthening of that wait only
  happens when under about 60 ticks are set, so with the default it never does; after 4 to 8 hours (the game ends a job
  on its own interval) the beast stops waiting. While it waits, when its rider's next destination is more than 50 cells
  from it and the rider is within 15 cells of it, the rider gets on again; further off, the beast walks after them. It
  also stops when its rider is in bed, downed, in a mental state or gone, when it is hurt, urgently hungry or very tired,
  or in a barn; then it gives its rider a job to lead it home on a rope that names no pen, which the game's rope job
  needs, so as the code reads it that job ends at once and the beast stays where it was.
- **Drafted.** Never by itself. A drafted colonist gets on only by the right-click "Mount" on a beast or its "Mount"
  button (the nearest free beast, its master's first), and stays in the saddle while drafted. A right-click "Prioritize"
  order to an undrafted colonist goes through the same 120-cell look.
- **Why Avila walked.** In the save of 15 November 2026 her steel at (93, 259) lay about 71 cells from the middle of the
  home area (about (64, 194); 13 cells past its edge), and Bautista's at (137, 260) about 98 (47 past the edge): both under
  120, so Giddy-Up never looked for a mount. Each later mining job is the next cell of the vein, a few cells off, so no
  later look passed either, and with no beast brought out there was none to ride back on. In the save of 16 November
  2026 Bautista was mining components at (96, 85), about 114 cells from the middle and 56 past the edge: still under.
  Avila was on a titanis there, hunting: she had got on for an earlier, longer job, and hunting is done in the saddle. On
  the 275-cell map 120 cells is close to half the width. The colony's beasts Giddy-Up lets be ridden by default (body
  size over 1.2): the horse, the two titanis, the thunderox, the ankylosaurus, the dusk prowler and the companion dryads;
  the silkies, the blood scarab, the raccoon and the arctic wolf are too small. Which of them have learned tameness, and
  what the player set in its settings, the save alone doesn't say for certain (its settings live in the player's own
  config file).

**What Rimfolk adds:**

- **When.** At the same moment, after Giddy-Up's own look (`Patch_RideOutNextJob`: `HarmonyAfter("GiddyUp")`, last), and
  only when nothing is under way (the last job ended, or the player gave one), never on the game's regular look for a
  better job. Where Giddy-Up mounted them, nothing changes.
- **Who.** One of the colony's own free colonists the player controls (no slave, guest, prisoner or quest lodger), up
  and in their right mind, not with a group (a caravan forming, a ritual, a party), not lent out, not carrying anything,
  not on the colony's own post rider's errand; and Giddy-Up's own rules for a rider (allowed to ride, old enough, not in
  a wheelchair, not riding already). Undrafted only with its Ride and Roll on. Drafted only for the player's own
  movement order (a Goto they gave), and only with its battle mounts on.
- **Which trips** (`RideOutMath.Kind`). Where the job goes, Giddy-Up's own way; the trip in a straight line plus a haul's
  carry, 40 cells or more (`TripMin`); and the work, where a haul ends, or the colonist 10 cells or more past the home
  area's edge (`OutMin`; measured per map in steps any of the eight ways from the home area, again when it changes or
  after an hour, `BaseEdge`). Work that ends out past the base counts the way back (they ride back on the same beast):
  `Out`. From out there to anywhere else is one way: `Back`. A movement order is one way: `Order`. Not fleeing, idle,
  sick, leaving the map, setting out as the post rider, or one of Giddy-Up's own jobs; not where Giddy-Up found no place
  to leave a beast before (its bad spots). Inside the base, nothing.
- **Which beast.** Each of the colony's animals on the map that Giddy-Up's own `IsMountable` (all its checks, with the
  map's reservations as it reads them) and its automount column allow; and Rimfolk's: not downed, not with a group, not
  led on a rope, not carrying a rider, not kept for another rider (Giddy-Up's own mark: waiting for them, or they are
  getting on), not at work (a job a work giver gave it, hauling, rescuing, capturing, fighting, hunting, mating, laying,
  fleeing), not the mother of a baby on the map, not kept for the colony's own post rider, not one that colonist failed
  to get on in the last hour (`RefusedTicks`), and in reach. Of these, the one that gets them there soonest by Giddy-Up's
  own sums (`RideOutMath.RideSeconds`: the walk to it to the power 1.05; getting on by its own curves for the "Mount" job,
  200 to 300 ticks by size, times 0.8 to 2 by wildness, times 1.4 to 0.33 by the rider's Animals skill; the ride 5% over
  the straight line at the beast's speed under them, its `StatPart_Riding`), when that is no slower than walking by
  `Slack`: for work, up to a quarter longer (the player wants them in the saddle out past the base, and the waiting beast
  makes every later trip back and forth quicker; a beast far off the other way isn't fetched), and a movement order only
  when it gets them there sooner. Since 19 November 2026 out to work rides whenever a beast near enough is free, and the
  slack holds only for the way back and movement orders (the next section, "Riding out to far work: the beast taken
  first").
- **Getting on.** Giddy-Up's own `GoMount` with its `Inject` (`GiddyUpMounts.MountFirst`, by name): the chosen job becomes
  its "Mount" job and waits first in their queue, as its own auto-mount does. Nothing is taught the beast.
- **After.** Giddy-Up's own driver does the rest as for its own riders: the ride, parking near the work (a mount spot, a
  pen, or hitched close by), the wait. The way back is Giddy-Up's own (the rider walking off more than 50 cells from the
  waiting beast) or Rimfolk's next look (the rider out past the base and the next job 40 cells or more off: the waiting
  beast is the nearest, so it is the one), whichever comes first.
- **The wait kept** (`KeepWaiting`). Each time a colonist starts a job while they or their work are out past the base,
  a beast waiting for them within 60 cells has its wait set to Giddy-Up's own timer from now, never shorter than it was
  and a day at most (`RideOutMath.WaitExpiry`). Giddy-Up still ends it for its own reasons (its rider in bed, the beast
  hurt, hungry or tired). Since 19 November 2026 also every 250 ticks, and the day counted from the rider's last job (the
  next section).
- **A handler's rope job home** (`RopedHome`). The game's own job to lead one of the colony's beasts to its pen (with the
  pen named), the handler 10 cells or more past the base and the pen 40 or more away, becomes: get on that beast, ride
  it to the pen and get off there (Giddy-Up's own "Dismount" job), when Giddy-Up and Rimfolk let them ride it. Giddy-Up's
  own rope job for a beast that stopped waiting is left as it is.
- **Saved:** nothing (who tried which beast is kept in memory for the session only). No new Sched slot (one since 19
  November 2026, the next section); one Harmony patch, on the same method as Rimfolk's hauling hook (which runs first).
- **Control:** the setting "Ride out to far work and back" (`rideOut`, Your other mods, under Giddy-Up 2, shown only with
  it, on by default, under the deeper hooks). Dev mode: "Riding out: why a colonist rides or not (log)..." writes, for a
  colonist's job now, Giddy-Up's settings, the trip and how far past the home area each end lies, whether Giddy-Up's own
  look would mount them, every beast with why it may or may not be ridden and its sum, and Rimfolk's answer.
- **Words and harm:** nothing is said or sent; what shows is the riding. No harm of its own.
- **Not run in the game** (none of it could be): the patch on the private `DetermineNextJob` beside Giddy-Up's; its
  `Inject` by reflection with a `ThinkResult` boxed for its `ThinkResult?`; its `IsMountable` with the `out` reason by
  reflection; the parked beast's wait lengthened while the rider works; a drafted colonist getting on before a movement
  order and staying mounted at the spot; the handler riding a beast to its pen; how often the quarter's slack has them
  ride when the pen lies the other way.

### Riding out to far work: the beast taken first (the player's report and go, 19 November 2026; released 0.266.5)

The player, 18 November 2026, with their save `League_of_Toba_7`: "WHY DOES bautista still walk halfway across the map to
mine without mounting up first? then the mount should wait for him until he's done". The go, 19 November 2026, on the
lead's fix: "yes, sounds good". A bug fix to the section above; the code is the same files.

- **What the save showed** (tick 7668315). Bautista mined steel at (136, 264), 44 cells past the home area's edge, and
  had chosen the job in the dining hall about (62, 205) after a meal, about 95 cells off: under Giddy-Up's own 120, so
  Giddy-Up never looked. He was not drafted, Animals 4, walking 4.6 cells a second, nothing stored against riding. The
  colony's 18 beasts were in or by the pen in the base, about 34 cells the other way from the vein. Giddy-Up refused the
  horses, the thunderox and the yak (tameness not learned), and Tatyana, Mare 1 and Tara were with young. Giddy-Up's
  saved data still kept Tatyana for Soot (Tatyana's `reservedBy`) and Zoe, a titanis, for Wyninn (Wyninn's
  `reservedMount`; Zoe's own `reservedBy` is saved empty), with everyone at home. Calvin, the other titanis, about 6
  cells a second under him, was the best left.
- **The cause.** `Decide` asked riding out and back (`RideOutMath.Worth`) to be no more than a quarter slower than
  walking there and back, counting the walk to the beast first. To the pen, getting on a titanis (body size 3), then 119
  cells from the pen to the vein and 95 back at 6 cells a second, came to about 52 seconds against 41 on foot (for any
  wildness from a half up), over the quarter's 51: "walking is quicker". Rimfolk kept no record of the decision, so the
  save alone couldn't prove it. Its wait was kept up only as a job was chosen with nothing under way, and ran out a day
  after the beast was left, whatever the rider was doing.
- **Out to work: the beast taken first.** For an `Out` trip they now ride whenever a beast is free whose walk to it is
  no longer than the trip itself (`RideOutMath.NearEnough`: straight lines, the trip plus a haul's carry) and that
  carries them at least as fast as they walk (`FastEnough`; Giddy-Up passes slower ones over too; decided by the
  builder, not asked); of those, the one that gets them there soonest by the same sums as before (`RideSeconds`). The
  pen on the way, beside them or the other way within the trip's length all count; a beast further off than the work is
  never fetched. `RideOutMath.Rides`: out to work, any beast found; the way back (`Back`) and the player's movement
  orders (`Order`) keep `Worth` with their slack (a quarter longer, and only when sooner). In their save Bautista now
  rides Calvin out.
- **Giddy-Up's old marks left aside** (`AnimalWhyNot`, `KeptFor`, `RideOutMath.KeptFor`). A beast marked by Giddy-Up as
  kept for another rider (`ReservedBy`) is passed over only while it waits for that rider (`WaitingFor`), carries them
  (`Riding`) or they are getting on it, now or next in their queue (`GiddyUpMounts.MountingOnto`); otherwise the mark is
  old and left aside (Tatyana's for Soot; Zoe's for Wyninn, where Giddy-Up links it to her when the game loads). The dev
  action names such a beast and the old mark. Giddy-Up's own `IsMountable` still has its say; where it refuses such a
  beast, the dev action gives its reason.
- **The wait kept while they work out there** (`GiddyUpRideOut.Rare`, `GameComponent_RideOut`, every 250 ticks at
  `Sched.RareRideOut` = 143, timed as `Pass.RareRideOut`, only with riding out on): each of the colony's beasts on any
  map doing Giddy-Up's "WaitForRider" for a rider of the colony who is up and out past the base (they, or where their
  current job takes them, 10 cells or more past the home area) has its wait set again, as at each job chosen
  (`KeepWaiting`). The cap now counts from the rider's last job (`RideOutMath.WaitExpiry(start, now, expiry, timer,
  lastJob)`): Giddy-Up's timer from now, never past a day after their current job began, never shorter than it was,
  never at or below the time already waited (the game ends a job when that reaches its length), and a wait with no end
  of its own left alone. Two days of mining cell after cell keeps the beast there throughout; a single job lasting more
  than a day lets it go a day after the job began; once the rider has gone back into the base, it ends within Giddy-Up's
  timer.
- **The last decision kept** (`RideOutNote`, `RideMount`, `GiddyUpRideOut.Note`, `LastOf`; memory only, cleared when a
  game is loaded or begun, 64 colonists at most). Each colonist's last decision on a trip of 40 cells or more (or a
  ride), except while they are in the saddle: the tick, the job, the trip's kind and cells, why not, the quickest beast
  found with its seconds against walking, and what came of it (Giddy-Up didn't take the order, sent, in the saddle at
  their next job choice, or not, so the beast is passed over by them for an hour). The dev action "Riding out: why a
  colonist rides or not (log)..." writes it first, then the look at their job now (the rule for the trip's kind, each
  beast with its reason).
- **Check myself** (`UI/SelfCheck.cs`, under "Mods Rimfolk works with", only with Giddy-Up; `GiddyUpRideOut.CheckLine`):
  riding out on or off and why (its setting, the deeper hooks, switched itself off for the session after an error,
  `Patch_RideOutNextJob.Broken`; Giddy-Up's `GoMount` with `Inject` not found or failed, `GiddyUpMounts.InjectFailed`;
  its rules not all found; its game hook not applied), that nobody rides out when Giddy-Up's `canRide` or
  `IsCapableOfRiding` wasn't found (`GiddyUpRules.CanRideFound`, `CapableFound`), and the other members not found with
  what is done instead (`GiddyUpRules.Missing`). A warning colour when riding out can't work.
- **Saved:** nothing. One new 250-tick slot (`Sched.RareRideOut`, in `RareOffsets`, on its own tick of the cycle and off
  every hourly pass), one game component with nothing saved; no new Harmony patch.
