    while it has one here); or it's left to them.
  - The faith without a guide (Ideology): the moral guide's role empty and two of the faith could take it (grown, free,
    no other role, the role's requirements met). Either named (the game's own `Assign`), or nobody.
- **Customs of the autumn and the winter** (`Rimfolk_Dilemmas_Customs_YearFour.xml`), the seasons that had fewest (seven
  and six before, against ten each in spring and summer). Each is a seasonal custom like the rest: one a season, on the
  calendar once kept, a tradition three years running; the full keeping, a smaller one (silence), a refusal.
  - The woodpile day (fall, the stores short of the winter's wood as wood for the winter reckons it, `woodShort`): a work
    party of six for the woodpile (logs carried in, a tree or two felled where none lie about), cutting and hauling, the
    lazy minding it; or three for a morning. Never asked by someone whose ideoligion holds trees sacred.
  - The night of lights (fall and winter, graves of the colony's own): a light by each such grave at dusk until first
    light (`DilemmaEffect_Lanterns` "graves", `OnMapTimed.GraveCells`) and a short vigil among them; or the lights alone.
    Never asked by someone whose ideoligion despises fire.
  - The mending day (winter): a work party repairing, cleaning and hauling, and a lesson at the bench from the colony's
    best crafter to one of thirty or under, the lazy minding it; or three mending for a morning.
  - The winter tales (winter, someone with a love of talk): the best talker tells the year by the fire (words, with lines
    of its own); or one tale at supper.
  - Each smaller form pleases most of the colony (as lantern night's one lantern does) and each refusal disappoints some
    and satisfies the industrious or the thrifty, so no answer is plainly best (`dilemma_balance.py`: trade-offs).
- **Decrees that each mean one thing on the map** (`Rimfolk_Decrees_YearFour.xml`; the player's decision 13). Three of
  the land's year mark the game's own work each morning and the day they're declared (`DecreeDef.daily`, run by
  `DecreeWork.RunDaily` from the decrees' day): a hunting season (six days, two head of safe game, `DilemmaEffect_Hunt`),
  wood for the winter (eight days, up to six of the nearest wild trees outside the home area until the stores hold 150
  a colonist for a tribe or a village, 80 for any other colony, `DilemmaEffect_MarkTrees` with `forWood`) and foraging
  days (six days, up to twelve wild plants ripe for picking within 45 cells, never a drug, `DilemmaEffect_Forage`).
  Saving the power (`lightsOut`, Electricity researched; asked for when the batteries are under a third full, the new
  `DecreeMoment.PowerShort`): the colony's lamps (a light of 150 W or less with a switch) switched off from eleven to five
  in the decrees' hour, never in a room with a patient abed, and only those switched back on (`DecreeTracker.lampsOff`,
  saved; the switch's wanted state set with it, so nobody is sent to flick it). Every faith its evening (`everyFaith`,
  Ideology and more than one faith at home, as one faith for the colony is listed): declared, the largest faith that isn't
  the colony's holds an evening of faith; each morning those of other faiths trust the council a quarter to a half point
  more by their openness, the colony's own devout a quarter less; never in force with one faith for the colony
  (`DecreeMath.Apart`). Every age's form is in its words: the hunters' moon, a village's open season, a game licence, a
  cull; axes or saws; the berry days or a survey of the land's harvest; a tribe or a village banks its fires instead of
  saving the power. None calls a gathering of its own, and none hurts anyone of Rimfolk's own (a hunted animal may fight
  back as the game has it, and says so).
- **The advisor** (`Advisor/AdvisorSignals_YearFour.cs`, `Rimfolk_Advisor_YearFour.xml`), in its thin parts: hay short of
  the herd's winter (food), animals in a cold they can't bear (temperature), a generator with under half a day's fuel and
  none in store (power), four or more blueprints waiting on stuff the stores don't hold (work), five grown trees close
  outside the walls (defence; a button marks them, never for a colony whose faith holds trees sacred; the look is kept
  six hours a map), deep snow and nowhere set to clear (work; a button marks the paths) and, with Ideology, a faith without
  a moral guide when someone could take the role.
- **Rates**: no new schedule slot, no new setting; one saved list (`lampsOff`, modelled). The questions take a share of the
  council's draw (the balance model knows how often each can be asked, `Rates.WorkerGates`), the customs a share of the
  one-a-season rule's, the decrees only what the player declares. The numbers before and after are in the HANDOFF entry.

## Goods and people that come and go on the map

The player gave 250 corn to a village and later got silver back: the corn vanished from the stockpile and the silver
appeared by the trade spot. With **Goods and people come and go on the map** (Events & world, on by default) whatever
Rimfolk's events move across the colony's edge is carried by people on the map (Couriers/). Off, it's all instant.

- **One shared system.** `Couriers` is the API the effects and workers call: `Deliver`/`PaySilver`/`Hand`/`Loot`
  (things for the colony), `Collect`/`TakeFromStores`/`TakeFor`/`TakeFromStoresFor` (goods it gives, sells or pays),
  `Exchange`/`Sell`/`CollectOrder`/`CollectThings`/`CollectGoals` (both in one visit; a neighbour's cargo; a mission's
  order in the missions' own words for goods), `Fetch` (a prisoner sold, an animal given back), `Await` (an errand's
  courier at the gate), `BringHome`/`TellWhenThere` (a letter held until the goods are set down). Each returns false
  when nobody will come, and the caller does exactly what it did before, so no event changes when the setting is off.
- **A trip** (`CourierTrip`, kept by `CourierTracker`, a game component checked every 250 ticks at tick 59 of the
  cycle, only while there are trips) waits 3 to 9 hours (an errand's or an order's courier under an hour and a half),
  comes only by day (7:00 to 18:00) and only when the map is safe (no danger, no toxic fallout, -25 to 45 degrees),
  and gives up after three days. Its people walk in by the way in nearest the colony's mailbag, else its gate
  (`PlaySpots.GateCell`), else `DropCellFinder.TradeDropSpot` (`CarrierSpots`, since 10 November 2026: "Straight to the
  mailbag" below) as a `LordJob_Courier`: straight to their own places beside it (`LordToil_CarrierTravel`), then work
  there (`Council_CourierWork` duty: `JobGiver_CourierWork` sets down what they carry with `JobDriver_CourierDrop` onto
  the cells beside the bag, fetches from the stores with `JobDriver_CourierLoad`, takes someone along with
  `JobDriver_CourierFetch`, else they wait in their place, `JobGiver_CarrierWait`), then off by the nearest way, a rider
  back in the saddle first (`LordToil_CarrierLeave`). Harmed by the colony or their people turned hostile, they leave
  defending themselves. A pack animal waits in its place beside the bag (`Rimfolk_CarrierWait`).
- **Who and how many** (`CourierMath`, pure and tested): the event's own people if usable, else the nearest of a
  fitting tech (a pre-industrial colony: tribes and medieval folk; otherwise a step either side); with Giddy-Up a
  medieval or industrial people's couriers ride (below). Each person is made new, of a kind drawn from their people's
  range of those sent on the road (`CarrierKinds.Person`, `CarrierMath.KindPool`: their caravans' guards and their
  visitors, light, never a trader, a child, a leader or a noble), else the faction's ordinary member
  (`Arrivals.PersonKind`); a pack animal from the trader group's carriers that the biome allows and the season suits. One person per 35 "bulk" (kilograms plus 10 per stack), at most three; an animal when their
  caravans use them and the load is more than one person's, which spares one porter. Their own inventory is cleared
  when they're made, so everything they carry is the trip's; the load is shared by carrying capacity.
- **Robustness.** Every end is a `CourierEnd`, settled once (`settled`): goods still owed to the colony are set down
  (at the courier's feet if the colony can reach it, else where traders leave goods) unless the colony hurt them or
  the map is gone; goods owed by it leave the stores the old way unless the colony hurt them, their people turned
  hostile or the map is gone. Can't reach the stores: six hours at the gate, then settled. Goods used up meanwhile:
  they take what there is and the deal stands. Someone they came for who is gone: they don't pay. Exiting couriers'
  packs are cleared (`Notify_PawnLost`, and every pass for anyone already gone). A trip whose record is gone (mod
  removed) sends its group home from the lord's own toil. The setting turned off mid-trip: settled at once, and they go.
- **Merging.** Effects of one answer that go to the same people the same tick are one visit: paying for goods bought
  (`WorldEffect_Pay` + `DilemmaEffect_Spawn`) is an exchange; the silver paid for an errand's goods rides with the
  courier who waits at the gate for them.
- **Visitors in person.** An event's own visitor at the colony hands things over at once (at their feet, with a line);
  one still walking in carries it and sets it down when they arrive (a bearer trip: the goods stay in the trip until
  then, so the visitor's own pack is never touched). Goods for a visitor who is here go by errand (a colonist carries
  them out, PlayOut/), never by a courier.
- **Which effects.** `<by>Outsiders</by>` marks the uses of `DilemmaEffect_Consume` (75), `DilemmaEffect_Spawn` (9),
  `DilemmaEffect_Loot` (9), `WorldEffect_Pay` (4) and `WorldEffect_Medicine` (1) where the goods cross the colony's
  edge; the rest are used up or found at home (a feast, fuel, medicine for a patient, a find). `WorldEffect_Loot`
  defaults to outsiders and its four finds say `<by>Home</by>`. `WorldEffect_Silver`, `_Sell`, the owed payout,
  `DilemmaEffect_Gift`, `_Goods` and `_SellHeirloom` always come from outsiders. Pods stay pods in an industrial colony.
- **Speech** goes through `Speech.Say` (the pool `Rimfolk_CourierLines`, by moment, goods and their people's era);
  messages through `Notify` with LookTargets. **Saved:** at most `CourierMath.MaxTrips` (12) trips at once (the oldest
  waiting is settled when more come), each with up to three people, a pack animal and the things it brings in a
  `ThingOwner`; ended trips are dropped once their people are gone, two days at most.

### Visitors on the map

The people a letter speaks of, there in person (Visitors/), under the same setting as the couriers. Three generic
effects, wired from defs: `VisitEffect_AtGate` (in a beat's or an event's effects, which run just before the letter:
the rider, driver, envoy or family walks in with it and waits at the gate), `VisitEffect_Stay` (in an answer: those
waiting stay N nights, by the gate or moved to the far ground or the road) and `VisitEffect_Come` (a group comes in
its hours: mourners or a band passing to the far edge, a herd grazing the far meadow or drinking at the water for a
night, a lord's retinue staying by the gate).

- **One record, one group.** A `VisitorTrip` (kept by `VisitorTracker`, a game component checked every 250 ticks at
  tick 131 of the cycle, only while there are visits) is made when the effect runs; an AtGate group sets out at once
  if the map is safe and has room, else the letter alone tells it. The people (the people's ordinary member, or a
  caravan guard for an armed group; dressed for the weather; a family related and sharing a name; a robbed merchant
  stripped to the shirt) and animals (a pack beast for peoples of the old ways, the family's dog or goat, a herd of
  farm beasts that suit the weather, likelier those wild on this land) walk in as one `LordJob_RimfolkVisit`: travel
  to the spot, keep close to it (`Rimfolk_VisitWait` for people, `Rimfolk_VisitBeasts` for animals: the game's own
  `JobGiver_GetRest` within the flag radius, then wander near; never its food search, so nobody eats the colony's
  meals or crops: `Visitors.Feed` has the hungry eat from their own packs, or keeps them fed out of sight), then walk
  off, by the nearest edge or on to the far side (`VisitorMath.Opposite`). Hurt or turned hostile: they leave defending themselves. Danger: they leave at a jog.
  Three and a half days at the spot, or the record gone: they leave whatever happens.
- **The letter.** The effect keeps the letter's context (not saved) and finds its letter by it on the next frame, so
  an answer given at once is still theirs; after a reload, by the letter whose X is one of them. The first of them is
  the event's X when it has none, so `Couriers.TakeFor`, `WorldEffect_Silver` and `DilemmaEffect_Spawn` hand things
  over in person and an answer's errand (`DilemmaEffect_CarryOut` without `to` Gate) carries what the colony sends to
  them; where a cartload should bring porters, the rider is not X (`stranger` false) and the gate courier still comes.
  If they go before the answer, the letter's X is cleared and it all goes the couriers' way. `WorldEffect_Join` takes
  in the family waiting for the same letter (`Visitors.TakeIn`), with their animal, instead of making new people.
- **When they go** (`VisitorMath`, pure and tested): someone at the gate half an hour after the answer, or once an
  errand bringing them something has reached them (eight hours at most), or after two and a half days whatever
  happens; with nothing asked, after their hours. Guests at first light after their nights (`HoursToDawn`, at most
  three), by the gate if every one of them, dressed as they are, is safe through the night to first light on the land's
  own reckoning (`Visitors.SafeOvernight`; under a roof, the room's temperature with a margin), else in a
  corner of the colony's dining or rec room that is (`Visitors.IndoorsCell`, `Rimfolk_VisitIndoors`: they keep within
  four cells of it), else they go on. Anyone hypothermic,
  heatstruck, starving or malnourished: they all go, with a message saying it was the extreme cold, the extreme heat or
  hunger (they came dressed for the weather: "Dressed for the weather as they come", below). A held beat (`holdBeat`: "the retinue stayed the
  night") waits until they've gone.
- **Limits.** At most three groups on a map at once (`MaxHere`), six people and eight animals in a group, eight
  records kept (`MaxTrips`; the oldest still waiting is dropped). Ended records go once their people are gone, a day at
  most. What they were handed is cleared when they leave the map. Speech through `Speech.Say` (the pool
  `Rimfolk_VisitorLines`, by moment and what they are); messages through `Notify` only for a group coming along the
  road and for one the weather drove off.

### Dressed for the weather as they come (the player's request, 14 November 2026; released 0.232.1)

The player: "so i just had an event from the aracoier league that they use my meadow for a heard or something like
this, and they appeared on the map but left it again soon after due to "weather conditions". it was -20 degrees cold.
in general i really want that the people who spawn from events, visitors, caravans, camps etc. just dress appropriately
for the weather, so that they don't have to leave because of it. of course if it's super cold or any other extreme
conditions that's fair, but not when it's "hard weather" that they could however do well in proper clothing"; then
"make sure this weather resilience update is applied to all kinds of occurences that make people come to my map, as long
as the faction/type of event etc. reasonably allows this and makes sense from a "realism" perspective"; and "so for
raiders it would also make sense if they come dressed for the weather, assuming their faction actually fits the
clothing". On 15 November 2026 (released 0.242.0): "regarding the weather clothing, i'd want not everyone to just wear
only a parka against cold, but the clothing should always be varied. of course there should be parkas, but also other
clothing combinations to counter the cold", and of the great caravan whose rider never came at -36 °C: "again, people
should just be dressed for the weather as much as possible, counts for all events". So now: varied outfits (**Varied
clothes**, below), their warmest even past what keeps them safe (**The line**), the cold or the heat never keeping
Rimfolk's own people from the gate, and Rimfolk's own going at the game's own line (**Still going for the weather**);
the visitor at the gate who never came is the next section.

- **The cause** (their save, League of Toba, 14 November 2026). The world event *a great caravan*
  (`Rimfolk_WS_Variety3_Roads`, "the hauler convoy" of the road league "Ararcoler League"): its outriders' beat asked
  for the far meadow, and "The meadow is theirs for the night" sent `VisitEffect_Come` (caravan, three people, four yaks,
  the far spot, one night). Trip 3 in `VisitorTracker`: three `Rimfolk_League_Wayfarer` under `LordJob_RimfolkVisit`
  (Lord_209), set out at tick 5962631, gone at 5965881 (1.3 hours), end `Weather`, never at the meadow. One wore a cloth
  sash, a fox-leather duster and a visage mask, and had hypothermia 0.0525: past Rimfolk's own line
  (`Visitors.Suffering`, 0.04), so they all turned back with "couldn't stay out in this weather". The game had dressed
  them for the season's average at the tile (`PawnApparelGenerator.ApparelWarmthNeededNow`, safe only at that average),
  not for a -20 day and its night; its free warm layer never gives an industrial people the parka (tribal work by its
  age, `CorrectFactionForApparel`), and gave another of them a Vanilla Anomaly Expanded straitjacket instead (any warm
  torso piece cheap enough, tags unchecked). Rimfolk's arrival check for a night out also wanted every one of them safe
  at eight degrees below the hour's temperature.
- **One hook, everyone.** `Patch_ArrivalDress`, a prefix on `GenSpawn.Spawn` (the overload every other calls), looks at
  each pawn about to appear on one of the colony's homes, before it shows, never on loading (`WeatherDress.OnSpawn`):
  who, by `WeatherDressMath.Qualifies`, from how the game holds them that moment (`HowCame`: nothing or the world,
  walked in; a drop pod or a falling thing; a shuttle; carried, in someone's pack, in something spawned on the map).
  Dressed: the game's visitors, trade caravans and travellers, quest guests, lodgers, refugees and beggars, Royalty's
  envoys and bestowers, allies sent to help, raids, sieges and ambushes (on foot, by pod or shuttle), Hospitality's
  guests (its `SpawnVisitor` spawns through the game), other mods' arrivals that come through the game's spawning (VE
  Events and the like), Rimfolk's own visits, envoys, herders, drovers, pilgrims, camps, riders, couriers, the peoples'
  events, war bands and bandits, the gods' strangers (what a god puts on is locked, so kept), and a wanderer who joins,
  new to the colony and walking or flying in. Left as they are: animals, insects and mechanoids (`NotAPerson`),
  Anomaly's entities and the walking dead (`Entity`), anyone down as they appear (a crashed pod's survivor, someone
  carried in: no time to dress), prisoners and slaves, babies, the factionless, the wild and peoples of no age with
  clothing (`NoWays`), someone already on the map or off one within the hour (`AlreadyHere`: set down, out of a casket,
  a growth vat or a jump), the colony's own coming home or bought and sent down in a pod (`OwnPeople`), anyone on a map
  in space (the game's vacuum gear counts there), while the game starts or a map is made, and a visit's robbed merchant,
  who comes as the robbers left them (`WeatherDress.AsTheyCame`).
- **The line.** The stay's weather is the land's own reckoning of each hour ahead (`CampWeather.StayRange`, as the camps
  read it, with what a cold snap or a heat wave adds now and three degrees more), two days ahead as they arrive
  (`ArrivalHours`), a Rimfolk visit its hours and nights and half a day (`VisitHours` in `Visitors.MakePeople`, at least
  two days, at most a season). Four degrees or less short of comfortable (the game's own line for dressing warmer): as
  they are. Further: they are dressed as their people's age allows, safe through it where that can be done (the game's
  safe range, ten degrees past comfortable); past that, the extreme cold or heat, they still come in their warmest
  within the worth (since 15 November 2026; until then they came as they were), and the game's own leaving stays
  (`WeatherDressMath.Outcome`: `AsTheyAre`, `Dressed`, `PastTheirClothes`; `PutOn` for the last two). Someone dressed
  for their whole stay before they appear (a Rimfolk visit in `Visitors.MakePeople`, a camp's people) is left alone by
  the arrival hook, so their warmest isn't put on twice over.
- **What comes off, what goes on.** Never off: armour (the game's armour kinds or a mod's named so, a make armoured by
  0.45 of its material or more, or 0.3 sharp armour of its own: a duster and a parka are 0.3 and 0.2, plate 0.9), belts,
  gear (a shield, a jump pack, a piece with an ability), a mod's special kind of apparel, what is locked on them (the
  gods' robes), what their title (the Empire keeps its own) or their role in the faith asks of them. On: plain layers
  that keep out cold or heat, that the game itself would hand out for warmth and that people are made wearing, with no
  armour, belt, gear or anything that slows or hinders (no straitjacket); from the whole loaded mod pool
  (`WeatherDress.Pairs`: every such piece in its cheapest, warmest and coolest material, none dearer than a cloth parka
  and a half), so the player's parkas, tuques, Vanilla Christmas Expanded's warm jackets and hats, Vanilla Apparel
  Expanded's scarves and gloves, dusters and cowboy hats; theirs by size, age and shape, not barred to their kind, of
  their people's age and the colony's era, with the game's rule against tribal hides for those past them unless the
  piece carries their kind's own tags (a parka is tagged for outlanders: `AgeFits`). Their kind's tags count first, then
  a look in their faith's style (`Fit`); each goes on in their kind's colours (the league's teal coat becomes a teal
  parka) and the faith's style (`PawnApparelGenerator.PostProcessApparel`), at their kind's quality
  (`PawnGenerator.PostProcessGeneratedGear`), only if the game lets them wear it (`EquipmentUtility.CanEquip`, so
  another mod's race rules hold). What it replaces is gone, never dropped or packed: nothing is given to the colony.
- **The worth.** New pieces less what came off, at most (`Room`): for anyone at peace, the game's own free parka and
  tuque and a little more, or what their kind would have spent on clothes and didn't; for raiders a tuque's worth or
  15% of what they wear, so a raid's loot is what it was.
- **The pick** (`WeatherDressMath.Choose`), a layer at a time, five at most: each brings them at least half a degree
  nearer comfortable, never takes off a kept piece and stays within the worth. Of those that would make them
  comfortable enough, their kind's and then the cheapest; else the one that leaves them least short (within two degrees,
  their kind's, then the cheapest). A layer of their own gives way only to one two degrees better. Camps dress through
  the same pick (`CampWeather.Dress`, after their winter folk's own clothes, which now never go over armour). This plain
  pick is the first of the outfits drawn below, and their warmest when none is warm enough.
- **Varied clothes** (15 November 2026; `WeatherDressMath.Choose` with the person's seed, their thing ID, and their
  people's, their faction). Besides the plain pick, twelve outfits are drawn for each person, a layer at a time: among
  the layers that bring them nearer comfortable, each weighs 0.3 for itself and 0.7 for how much of what they still
  need it brings (`BringsShare`), half again for each point of fit (`FitShare`: their kind's tags 2, their faith's style
  1), their people's liking for that kind of piece (`Liking`, from half to one and a half, by the def's short hash, the
  same for every one of that people and different from people to people) and the draw's own (a hash, no game
  randomness). Only outfits warm enough (or cool enough) for the stay are kept, each once; one of them is chosen by its
  pieces' fit and their people's liking, the person's own seed deciding (`Liked`). So a group of the league's wayfarers
  in a night of -24 comes in a parka, a warm jacket over a fleece shirt, a jacket over a fleece and a quilted vest with a
  scarf, a cape over a hoodie and a vest with a tuque, a pelt coat and a vest: some twenty outfits among twenty-four
  people in the tests, each warm enough, within the worth, never two coats or two hats at once. Every piece is drawn
  from the whole loaded pool as before (the player's: the game's parka, duster, jacket, cape, robe, tuque and hood,
  Vanilla Apparel Expanded's pelt coat, poncho, fleece shirt, hoodie, scarf, gloves and boots, Vanilla Armour Expanded's
  quilted vest and balaclava, Vanilla Christmas Expanded's warm jacket and warm hat, Ideology's headwrap and broadwrap,
  Vanilla Ideology Expanded's headscarf and wide hats, Medieval 2's mantle, the elves' cloaks; whatever fits them by age
  and kind). The same person gets the same outfit each time; in the heat, the same with hats and light layers. Mods
  that add fur hats, earmuffs and winter cloaks join in as soon as they are in the player's list (none of the active ones
  has earmuffs or fur hats).
- **A piece that hinders them** (the coordinator's follow-up, the same day). The game's free warm layer takes any cheap
  warm torso piece without looking at its tags, and put Vanilla Anomaly Expanded's straitjacket on one of the convoy's
  wayfarers (Human531631). Whatever the weather, a piece someone came in that lowers their moving, work, aim, hit or
  dodge (the same rule that keeps such pieces off the offer), that their kind neither requires nor asks for (its
  `apparelRequired`, its `apparelTags`, a specific requirement's piece or tag) and that isn't kept (armour, a title's or a
  role's apparel), is swapped first for a plain piece of their age that takes exactly its place and keeps them as warm for
  the stay (no more than half a degree further from comfortable, and still safe if they were): their kind's first, then
  the one leaving them least short, then the cheapest, within the same worth budget, the old piece gone
  (`WeatherDressMath.OutOfPlace`, `Swap`; `WeatherDress.SwapHindering`, at the head of `ForStay`). With nothing as warm
  on offer, it stays on rather than leave them colder. On a mild day the wayfarer comes in a jacket of their kind, on a
  night of -24 in a parka.
- **Never kept away by the cold or the heat** (15 November 2026). Rimfolk's own people come whatever the temperature:
  the shared gate of visits, couriers, the post and invited guests (`CourierTracker.Safe`, `Visitors.Safe`) keeps out
  only danger on the map, a map in space and toxic fallout; its -25 to 45 degrees is gone (it refused the great
  caravan's rider at -36 °C). They come in their warmest, and an event that brings someone to the gate in code
  (`HappeningWorker_AtGate2.CanCome`) comes in a frost too.
- **Still going for the weather.** Rimfolk's own visitors go on at the game's own line, 0.15 hypothermia or heatstroke
  (`WeatherDressMath.Suffering` = `GameLeaves`, as `Trigger_PawnExperiencingDangerousTemperatures` for the game's own
  groups; it was 0.04 until 15 November 2026), so they come and are seen, and go only when the weather really gets to
  them; a courier the weather gets to that far sets off home with what it carries set down first (`CourierEnd.Weather`,
  `Visitors.WeatherHurts`, "went home early because the cold was getting to them", `CC_Courier_End_Cold`, `_Heat`).
  Rimfolk's night-out check follows the same line: safe through the night to first light on the forecast, as
  dressed (`Visitors.SafeOvernight`, out in the open). The messages say it: Rimfolk's "couldn't stand the extreme cold
  (heat) any longer" or "had nothing left to eat" (`Visitors.WeatherWhy`, `CC_Visit_Weather_cold`, `_heat`, `_hunger`);
  the game's own "leaving the map because of dangerous temperature", for any group whose lord sends it, is said as the
  extreme cold or the extreme heat, whichever has taken hold of them (`Patch_WeatherLeaveWords` on
  `TransitionAction_Message.DoAction`, `CC_WeatherLeave_Cold`, `_Heat`). Nothing else is shown, and nothing is saved.
- Code: `Visitors/WeatherDressMath.cs` (pure, linked: who, the line, the pieces, the age, the worth, the pick, the
  draw of varied outfits, the swap of a piece that hinders, the leaving), `Visitors/WeatherDress.cs` (the pool, the
  pieces, the stay, the plan and putting it on, the person's and people's seeds, the arrival hook, the words),
  `Visitors/Visitors.cs` (the visit's own dressing, `Suffering`, `WeatherHurts`, `WeatherOf`, `WeatherWhy`,
  `SafeOvernight`), `Couriers/CourierTracker.cs` (`Safe`, the courier's weather leaving), `Couriers/CourierWords.cs`,
  `Visitors/VisitorWords.cs`, `Camps/CampWeather.cs`, `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_Visitors.xml`,
  `Rimfolk_Couriers.xml`; tests `Tools/Tests/WeatherDressTests.cs`. Under the deeper game hooks setting; no Sched slot.

### The visitor at the gate who never came (the player's report, 15 November 2026; released 0.242.0)

The player, with the council's answer list showing "A great caravan · Guido tells them the hill road · As answered ·
Guido goes out to the rider at the gate and draws the old hill road in the dust, twice, until the rider has it.": "just
had this event but it didn't play out on the map and also there was no real effect from it?"

- **The cause** (their save, League of Toba, 15 November 2026, tick 6113704). `Rimfolk_WS_GreatCaravan`'s beat "hills"
  (Bandits in the hills) was due at 6117214; its `VisitEffect_AtGate` brings the master's rider, and the answer sends A to
  him (`DilemmaEffect_Visit` to `Stranger`). The base advisor's freezer note at 6111544 read "-36 °C beyond the door"
  (FogSnow, no cold snap, no danger: the sleeping mech cluster isn't counted). `VisitorTracker.ComeNow` refused the trip
  at `!Visitors.Safe(map)`, which is `CourierTracker.Safe`: outdoor temperature below -25. The beat's letter went out all
  the same (`WorldSituations.Run` never looked), so the answer's visit had no X (`Fill` returned false) and only the
  words happened. Its effects were real but unseen: +4 goodwill at once, and the flag `warned` that makes the ending
  "safe" (+4 goodwill, +6 prosperity at Laestelia Wells) when the event runs out.
- **The rider comes.** The cold no longer keeps him away (the section above); he comes in his warmest.
- **The beat waits for him** (`WorldSituations.Beats`, `Run`, `AtGate`, `Postpone`). A beat whose letter says someone
  is at the gate (a `VisitEffect_AtGate` that would apply now: `VisitEffect_AtGate.Brings`, the setting on, its people
  at peace, the colony's era, its flags) waits while they can't come (`HappeningWorker_AtGate2.CanCome`: danger, room for
  another group, too many visits), every six hours, eight times at most, while the event runs. When it comes, those it
  brings come first: if nobody reached the map (no way in from the edge), or the event's own person who walks in at
  their head isn't free (`withStranger`), nothing of the beat happens yet and it tries again (`VisitorTracker.CameWith`).
  With the setting off or a people at war, the letter alone tells it, as before.
- **An answer without its visitor.** A visit to the event's visitor (`to` Stranger, or `whom` X or the new Group) never
  goes out to someone who isn't on the map: with `orTo`, it goes on its own to the first of those places instead (the
  new place `Edge`: out at the edge of the colony's land, a few steps in from where the road comes in, `PlaySpots.EdgeCell`,
  "out at the edge of the colony's land."); without, the answer can't be given while they're gone ("{0} is no longer
  here.", or "The visitor is not on the map now." once their letter let go of them: `DilemmaEffect_Visit.Unavailable`;
  the default answer always can). A world event's answer is told with the tag `visitorGone` when its visitor isn't on
  the map (`WorldSituations.VisitorGone`), so its words can say what happens instead.
- **The great caravan's answer.** "{A_nameDef} tells them the hill road": out to the rider at the gate, or, if he has
  gone, "The rider had already gone, so {A_nameDef} writes the old hill road down and takes it out to the edge of the
  colony's land, where the train's road comes in, and waits there for its next rider." (`orTo` Edge); the default's
  words likewise. Its card shows the goodwill now and what it does later (`WorldEffect_Foretold`, ending `safe`: "When
  the hauler convoy reaches Laestelia Wells by the hill road: +4 goodwill with Ararcoler League", "...: +6 prosperity
  at Laestelia Wells"). When the train comes through, its letter says "the colony's road saved the train, and Ararcoler
  League think better of the colony for it", then "What it changed: +4 goodwill with Ararcoler League and +6 prosperity
  at Laestelia Wells." Every world event's ending letter now says what it changed, as its effects apply
  (`WorldSituations.Moved`, `CC_WS_Moved`: goodwill with a people, with the peoples nearby or at war with them, and the
  prosperity at the event's town or its people's towns, with the towns' fortunes on).
- **Every beat checked.** Of the world events' 127 `VisitEffect_AtGate` (and their `VisitEffect_Come`), seven answers
  walk out to their visitor: the hill road, the comet's scholar, the market days' quarrel, the warlord's son's two (he
  walks in at their head, `withStranger`), the rival colony's turning (its leader at their head) and its hunters. All
  but the last were sound once the rider comes and the beat waits for him. The hunters came by `VisitEffect_Come` and the answer went out to the
  rival colony's leader, who wasn't there: the hunters are now the letter's group once on the map (`VisitEffect_Come`
  `group`, `VisitorTrip.groupFor`) and the answer walks out to the first of them (`whom` Group, `PlayWho.Group`). The
  play-out audit checks it on every run (`Tools/playout_audit.py`, `strangers()`: each world event's answer that walks
  out to its visitor is in a beat that brings them, or has a place to go instead; it fails the run otherwise), and
  `Tools/Tests/GateVisitorTests.cs` does too. Rimfolk's own events bring their visitor in code (91 such answers), and
  the guard above greys any of them out while the visitor isn't on the map.
- Code: `World/WorldSituations.cs`, `World/SituationEffects.cs` (`WorldEffect_Foretold`, the moves told),
  `Visitors/VisitEffects.cs`, `Visitors/VisitorTracker.cs`, `Visitors/VisitorTrip.cs`, `PlayOut/PlayOutEffects.cs`,
  `PlayOut/PlayOuts.cs`, `PlayOut/PlaySpots.cs`, `PlayOut/PlayOutTracker.cs`, `PlayOut/PlayOutJobs.cs`; defs
  `Rimfolk_WS_Variety3_Roads.xml`, `Rimfolk_WS_World.xml`; keys in `Rimfolk_PlayOut.xml`, `Rimfolk_DilemmaImpact.xml`,
  `Rimfolk_WorldSituations.xml`, `Rimfolk_Couriers.xml`. Nothing new saved (the group's reference is not saved), no
  Sched slot.

### Guests who help out (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.205.0)

The player noticed two Hospitality guests cooking, butchering and hauling: "is this a guest hospitality feature by
default, or what's causing this? ... I really kind of like the idea that the guest does certain kind of work, for example,
if they really like doing this work anyways ... or if they for example see that I'm in need and need help in like a crisis
moment, that they help out." It is Hospitality's own "guests help out": its guest duty (`Duties_Visit.xml`) runs the game's
`JobGiver_Work` behind `ThinkNode_ConditionalWantsToHelp` (a mood over 75%, unless its "Disable guests helping"), and its
prefix on `JobGiver_Work.PawnCanUseWorkGiver` decides each work giver for its guests: skill at least its
`minGuestWorkSkill` (7), no talks, warden's work or feeding, no art and crafting or surgery by its settings, and a roll of
goodwill, passion (40 burning, 20 minor), the visit's score times 100 and 75 for an emergency giver against 100 plus a
seeded 0 to 100 (its `&&`/`||` keeps every tending out, whatever its medical setting). Rimfolk's own visitors' work at
their spot (`Visitors/VisitorWork.cs`) is another thing and stays as it was. The player approved all seven ideas; the
pure rules are `Integrations/GuestHelpMath.cs` (`GuestHelpTests`), the game side `GuestHelp.cs`, the tab `GuestHelpTab.cs`.
Two settings on Your other mods, under Hospitality, both on and behind the deeper hooks: "Guests help with what they love"
(`guestHelp`: points 1 and 3 to 7) and "Guests pitch in when the colony is in trouble" (`guestsPitchIn`: point 2).

1. **Work they love.** In everyday times a guest only takes up work that fits them (`GuestHelpMath.Fit`, strongest
   first): a burning passion for one of its skills, the work their people live by (one of Rimfolk's peoples,
   `CallingWork`: the order tends the sick, herders and tamers handle animals, the league and the enclave carry, pilgrims
   cook and sweep, scholars, seers and the Helix Works study, the river folk fish and cook, the wardens hunt, the Quiet
   Bell sweeps, the Wheel welds and makes, the Mossborn grow, the Kiln Guild builds, makes and carves, linesmen and the
   Vault mend and build, the union mines, citizens and the Fleet's deckhands carry and clean, the Lattice crafts, the
   Choir makes art), their faith (`FaithWork`: learning prized, mining's yield, trees desired, art desired, dumb labour
   exalted, crafting by hand, a strong bond with animals; each an active PreceptDef of the player's), a minor passion,
   or a hard worker's hauling and cleaning (Industriousness above zero). No fit, no everyday work, even where
   Hospitality would allow it. The first time they take up a kind of work they say why in one sentence
   (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpFit`, by the reason, the work and their people's ways). A postfix on `PawnCanUseWorkGiver`
   (`Patch_GuestHelpWorkGiver`, after Hospitality's own prefix) narrows its answer; their own care (Patient work) is
   never touched. Hospitality's switch and minimum skill hold.
2. **Pitching in during a crisis** (`ForGuest`, `CrisisOf`; each start and end a pure rule, worked out per map every
   250 ticks): a fire in the home area within 20 cells of them (`FightFires` and mods' own fires); someone of the colony
   downed outside a bed (Rimfolk's `JobGiver_GuestRescue` makes the game's rescue job, since its work giver only rescues
   one's own people, and never while an enemy is within 40 cells, the game's own rule); the colony's people waiting to be
   tended within a day after a raid, no enemy about (`DoctorTendToHumanlikes`, `DoctorTendEmergency`, Medicine 4 or more,
   tending only, never surgery, an animal or themselves); crops the frost harvest marked still standing
   (`GrowerHarvest`, `PlantsCut`); the food under three days (`MapFacts.FoodDays`) until four again (cooking and
   butchering, never brewing; Cooking 4 or more). In trouble they pitch in to, whatever their mood and Hospitality's
   roll, they do only that trouble's work (`Allow`) until it ends; a trouble's job still running when it ends is put
   down (a fire's and a rescue's end by themselves). Hospitality's mood line is opened by name
   (`Patch_GuestHelpWantsToHelp` on `ThinkNode_ConditionalWantsToHelp.Satisfied`), and since its guest duty puts their
   needs first (its `JobGiver_Relax` asks for them whenever joy is under 90%), Rimfolk's own step sits on the game's
   `Humanlike_PreMain` hook that Hospitality's duty offers before their needs (`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_GuestHelp.xml`:
   `ThinkNode_GuestPitchIn`, the rescue, then `JobGiver_Work`), unless starving or exhausted. The trouble's work types
   (Doctor, Growing, Plant cutting, Cooking) are turned on in their guest's work settings while it lasts and off again
   (`WorkTypesFor`, saved so a load still turns them off). Each says why (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpCrisis`) and a message
   names who helps and with what (one a trouble a map). **With Hospitality's own helping switched off, guests still fight
   fires and carry the downed in, nothing more** (`WithHospitalityOff`): saving a life isn't chores, and the player
   switched the chores off.
3. **Thanks paid in work.** A guest the colony carried in (Hospitality's rescued guest), once set free (a notable met
   as freed), tended (KinMemory's note of a colony doctor), feasted (their people's notable feasted within three days)
   or hosted very well (Hospitality's score 0.9 or more) offers, once a visit, on a morning (6 to 11) with no trouble
   on, a day of their best-loved work (`BestLoved`: the highest passion, then the best skill; never tending, never what
   Hospitality's settings or minimum skill keep from them). That work goes on in their area for a day, beyond the cap and
   Hospitality's roll. A line over them (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpThanks`), the evening's news and their history
   (`guestHelp:thanks`, the guest and their people) keep it.
4. **Some guests won't** (`Refuse`, `RefuseGiver`). The titled (the Empire's own titles), and notables who are their
   town's head or heir or proud (the persona's Pride at 30) never do menial work (hauling, cleaning, plant cutting), and
   in trouble only pitch in to save a life (a fire, a rescue, the wounded). Each faith keeps its customs (no mining, no
   study, no dumb labour, no hunting or slaughter where killing animals is wrong, no butchering where meat is, no tree
   ever where felling is), and each people its own (the Mossborn never fell a tree, the Ashen Banner does no everyday
   work, being for hire, though it pitches in). No guest ever goes into a bedroom, barracks or cell for work, does
   surgery, prisoners' or entities' work, the colony's children's or its management, or touches the dead (corpses,
   graves, stripping, cremation), a rescue aside (`Vetoed` on the job `JobGiver_Work` chose, `Patch_GuestHelpJob`).
5. **Limits.** About three hours of everyday work a day (`CapTicks`; the trouble's and the thanks day's apart): they
   put it down with a word (`s:enough`). Under Hospitality's own line (75%) they put everyday work down (`s:unhappy`).
   Past six hours of work in a day (the cap and a trouble on top) they're overworked: only a life-saving trouble until
   tomorrow, a small bad mood for two days (`Rimfolk_GuestOverworked`, -4: Hospitality's score of the visit reads their
   mood, so it costs the colony a little at their leaving), regard lost with them if they're a notable, a line
   (`s:overworked`) and the evening's news.
6. **It counts both ways.** A guest and a colonist at the same work within six cells think a little better of each other,
   both ways, once a day each pair (`Rimfolk_GuestWorkedBeside`, +3 opinion, six days: the game's own opinion, which
   Hospitality counts toward its friends). A guest who helped and leaves as a friend (not dead, taken in or a prisoner,
   their people not at war) speaks well of the colony at home (`SpeakWell`: 1 for an hour of everyday help, 2 for four, 2
   for a trouble, 1 for a thanks day, 4 at most) with each of their people's notables (six at most, and themselves if
   one), through the notables' own regard and memory. A guest hurt at the colony's work (a new wound while at it, or one
   that ended the job: the game's own fire, a raider's shot at a rescue, an animal's bite; Rimfolk adds no harm of its
   own, so it comes at the game's rate) costs 2 regard with each of them, once a day, told as harm is (a message,
   Important).
7. **You can see it.** On Hospitality's guest tab, above Rimfolk's recruiting checklist (`GuestCheck.cs` draws both
   from its one patch, and the tab grows for either): "Let them help" (on by default; off, no work at all, even in
   trouble; their own care stays theirs), the trouble they're pitching in to, the day of thanks, today's
   hours ("Today: 1 h of 3", or overworked), what they'd help with and why ("Cooking: burning passion", "Handling: what
   the herding folk live by", a note where Hospitality's minimum skill stops it), what they won't ("No hauling:
   titled (Baron)", "Never fells a tree"), and the never line.

- **Every age.** It works the same in every age; what they say takes their people's ways (`their:tribal`, `medieval`,
  `industrial`, `spacer`, the Empire's own), never the colony's age.
- **Saved** (`GuestHelpBook`, a game component): one record per guest staying (`GuestHelpMath.MaxGuests` 30 at most):
  the switch, the day's and the visit's hours, the overworked day, the kinds of work said (`MaxTold` 12), the work types
  turned on (`MaxEnabled` 5), the thanks day, the troubles said. Let go at the pass after they leave (their farewell),
  and never saved once gone. Modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.
- **The clock:** `Sched.RareGuestHelp` (tick 119 of the 250-tick cycle, only while guests are on a home map or a record
  waits to be let go).
- **Soft.** Hospitality is read by type name (its think node, its settings, its guest comp's "rescued"); the three patch
  classes stand down without it ("Hospitality isn't loaded"), and the think tree's step says no at once for anyone who
  isn't its guest.

- **Tending by skill** (0.205.1; the player: "i'd rather not have visitor tend the wounds if they're not good doctors. or they
  should only tend bruises and minor injuries otherwise", then "not if every wound is minor, but they should just treat the
  minor ones and leave the others for better doctors"). A guest with a good doctor's Medicine (8, `GuestHelpMath.TendAnyMedicine`)
  tends anything; from Medicine 4 to 7 only a patient's minor conditions (bruises, cuts, everyday ailments, as Rimfolk's
  medicine rules judge them: `MedicineChoice.Judge`), the serious ones left for a better doctor even on the same patient.
  `Patch_GuestHelpTendFit` (postfix on `WorkGiver_Tend.HasJobOnThing`) passes over a patient with nothing they may tend
  (`MayTakePatient`); while such a guest tends (`Patch_GuestHelpTendDoctor`, on `TendUtility.DoTend`), the game's choice of
  what one treatment covers (`Patch_GuestHelpTendMinorOnly`, on `GetOptimalHediffsToTendWithSingleTreatment`) is given only
  the minor conditions tendable now in its own order; nothing minor left when they reach the patient, nothing is done and
  no medicine used. The guest tab says so ("Tends only bruises, cuts and other minor ailments").

### Invited visitors are Hospitality's guests (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.209.0)

The player: "visitors that you invite with diplomatic actions should also be treated as guests with hospitality". With
Hospitality loaded, those the colony invited come and stay as its guests, so its guest area, guest beds, guest tab,
recruiting rules and Rimfolk's guest help (above) apply to them; Rimfolk's purpose for the visit stays on top. The rules
are `Integrations/InvitedGuestsMath.cs` (`InvitedGuestsTests`), the game side `Integrations/InvitedGuests.cs`; the setting
"Invited visitors are guests" (`invitedAsGuests`, on, Your other mods under Hospitality, with the deeper hooks).

- **Who is invited** (`ArrivalWhy`, `Invited`): a notable (or one of their town who can travel) who took up a letter's
  invitation (`NeighbourLetters.TryVisit`: any letter that invites, a pen friend's, a gathering day's); a town's folk asked
  to the colony's feast or fair, or come to a fair it proclaimed (`Dealings.Guests`); a guest of note who wrote ahead and
  was told yes (`HappeningWorker_NotableGuest`); a feast's or a wedding's guests with their retinue (`Feasts.Arrive`); an
  envoy and attendant for a season (`Envoys.Arrive`, `Regroup`). Not invited, and Rimfolk's own as before: a hosting
  mission's guests (a dignitary, refugees, an apprentice, a choir: their people asked, and the mission counts the
  colony's own table and beds, `Hosting.Tend`); errands at the gate with their own ending (a ward's party, a match's
  escort, a parley, an oath, a ransom's messenger, couriers and riders); the strangers stories bring; and those asked to
  live here (kin invited to stay, a visitor asked to join), who join rather than visit. There is no festival's return:
  the colony's entertainers go to the town's festival by caravan and nobody comes back with them. Pen friends visit by a
  letter's invitation.
- **Handed over** (`InvitedGuests.HandOver`), once the group is on the map, when `HandOver` says so (invited, Hospitality's
  way found, the setting and hooks on, their people at peace, every one of them a person of theirs on the map): by name,
  Hospitality's incident's `CreateLord(faction, spot, pawns, map, showLetter: false, getUpsetWhenLost, duration)` (its
  `LordJob_VisitColony`, guest comps, trader status and its map component's guest list), after its own `GiveItems` (the
  food, money and wares its visitors carry). Rimfolk's letter says they came, so Hospitality's isn't shown. Taken whole,
  their group is returned; otherwise any half-made group is let go and the caller makes Rimfolk's own as before
  (`Arrivals.Invited` the game's visit at an errand's pace, the feast `LordJob_FeastGuests`, the envoy
  `LordJob_EnvoyStay`), and everything that touches Hospitality is caught and logged once.
- **How long** (`StayTicks`): the hours Rimfolk planned (a letter's guest 8 to 14, a town's folk 9, a guest of note 18 to
  26; never under 4), and Hospitality's own rule ends it (in daylight). Where Rimfolk ends the stay itself (`RimfolkEnds`:
  the feast's guests, two days; the envoy, the season of 15), a day more, so Hospitality's clock never sends them first;
  never past 16 days. Hospitality's displeasure at losing the whole group (`getUpsetWhenLost`) only where Rimfolk keeps no
  count of its own.
- **The feast on top**: its groups are found among Hospitality's too (`Feasts.Lords`, `LordOf`). Where the day takes them
  (`Feasts.Focus`: the gate, a contest, the table, indoors for the night) is kept with the feast (`GuestFeast.focus`,
  `focusRadius`, saved) and given to Hospitality's guests as the feast's own duty (`InvitedGuests.Steer`,
  `Rimfolk_FeastGuest` at the place, `Rimfolk_FeastIndoors` in danger) at each look, only while they're settled at
  their stay (walking in and out is Hospitality's). The feast's 250-tick look, which its own group gave, comes from the
  guests' pass (`GuestHelpBook`, `Sched.RareGuestHelp`, while a feast's guests or an envoy are at a home:
  `InvitedGuests.Following`, `Rare`). Settled and free to be fed and bedded count Hospitality's stay
  (`InvitedGuests.Staying`), so the feast's hosting rules feed them at its table and put them to bed (Hospitality's guest
  beds first) as before; the play-out's feast keeps them at the table by its own jobs. At first light
  (`Feasts.LeaveAll`) their stay ends as Hospitality's own does (`InvitedGuests.GoHome`, `Leave`: the transition out of
  the stay that its length sets off, with its message, its reckoning of the visit, its gift and its next visit; still
  walking in, straight to its way out).
- **The envoy on top**: found among Hospitality's groups (`Envoys.LordOf`); Hospitality's guest area and rules lead their
  day (the envoy's own common rooms were the same place in effect), indoors in danger by the stay's own duty
  (`Rimfolk_EnvoyIndoors`, `Envoys.HostedLook` every 250 ticks). The stay's hour still feeds them at the colony's table,
  beds them (the bed set aside first), seats the envoy at a council meeting and sends their letters home (`Envoys.Free`
  counts Hospitality's stay); a meal of the colony's or a night in one of its beds that Hospitality gave the envoy first
  still counts for the day. One of them up again with no group goes back the way Hospitality takes a guest in late
  (`LordToil_VisitPoint.JoinLate`, `OnGuestJoinedLate`), else a new group, Hospitality's or the stay's own. The season
  over, the envoy dead or the home lost: `GoHome`.
- **Hurt by the colony**: their own groups heard it from the game's harm trigger; for Hospitality's, a postfix on
  `Lord.Notify_PawnDamaged` (`Patch_InvitedGuestHarmed`) takes outside violence by the colony's people (never a blow in
  an agreed bout, `Outsiders.InBout`) to `Feasts.Harmed` or `Envoys.Harmed`, which end the visit as an insult and send
  them home. Deaths and arrests are seen by the feast's look and the stay's hour as before.

### Every visitor shops the market (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.228.0)

Nobody is made to shop (the player: "the visitors are not forced to shop, only if i have products that ar actually
interesting to them"): a visitor walks over only when an open stall has an article on its counter that fits what they
want and they can pay for (`VisitorTrade.ShopJob` is null otherwise), and goes on with their visit when nothing does.

The player: "do visitors also shop the markets? if not please implement that", then "later, to do", then "continue
with the other tasks". With RimMarket, those camped on the colony's land, people from a camp near it and a market day's
buyers already walked over to the colony's stalls (`Visitors/VisitorTrade.cs`, `Camps/CampMarket.cs`), and
Hospitality's guests shop by RimMarket's own duty (`Integrations/MarketGuests.cs`). Now every other visitor does too:
the game's visitor groups passing a day, a trade caravan's people, Rimfolk's envoys, notables, guests and callers, the
guests the colony invited without Hospitality, and a feast's guests. The rules are in `Visitors/VisitorTradeMath.cs`
(`VisitorTradeTests`), the game side in `Visitors/VisitorTradeGuests.cs`; the setting "Visitors shop at RimMarket's
stalls" (`marketVisitorsBuy`, on, Your other mods under RimMarket, with the deeper hooks).

- **The way in**: a postfix on `ThinkNode_Duty.TryIssueJobPackage` (`Patch_VisitorsShop`, applied only with RimMarket
  loaded, else it stands down with why) looks at the job a visitor's duty chose, and only an idle wander near their spot
  (`GotoWander`, `Wait_Wander`, what the game's `Defend` duty and Rimfolk's envoy and feast duties end in) may become the
  walk to the market (`VisitorTrade.GuestJob`). Fighting, eating, sleeping and whatever else their duty has for them come
  first, and the duty itself is never touched: the walk is a job of theirs, with the lord's own `lord`, `source` and
  `dutyTag`. When their group sets off, the walk ends within a second (`JobDriver_MarketBuy` fails on
  `VisitorTrade.GuestGoing`: the lord off its stay, or the pawn leaving), so a caravan's people leave with the caravan
  (its time up goes to `LordToil_ExitMapAndEscortCarriers` without ending jobs) and a visit's lord gathers its people
  for the way out as always (its leaving transition doesn't end jobs either).
- **Which groups** (`GroupOf`, `GuestGroup`): `LordJob_TradeWithColony` (a caravan), `LordJob_VisitColony` and what
  derives from it (the game's visitors; Rimfolk's `LordJob_VisitOnErrand`, which nearly every happening's visitors,
  invited guests without Hospitality and the peoples' callers come in), `LordJob_EnvoyStay`, `LordJob_FeastGuests`; never
  RimMarket's or Hospitality's own lords (by namespace), Rimfolk's own visits and camps (which keep their own turn,
  `VisitorJob`, `Camp.MarketJob`), raiders, a quest's or anyone else's. At their stay only (`AtStay`): a visit or a
  caravan at its spot (`LordToil_DefendPoint`, the caravan's own derives from it), envoys at `LordToil_EnvoyStay`, a feast
  at `LordToil_FeastGuests`.
- **Who may go** (`VisitorTradeMath.WhyNot`, `GuestFacts`): a person, grown, not the trader (who keeps to the trade),
  never a caravan's pack beasts or what it has for sale (the game's caravan roles); their people at peace, the map quiet
  (`MapFacts.ThreatOn`, the danger rating), at the stay and not leaving (`Outsiders.Leaving`); up, awake, not hungry or
  worn out or due to sleep or ought to be in a sickbed; in the market's hours (RimMarket's `ShopHoursStart`, an hour
  before its end); and nothing holding them (`Held`): Hospitality's stay, a quest, a lodger; a question's letter about
  them still open (the stranger or the group of a `ChoiceLetter_Dilemma`); a caller's work (`Callers.tasks`); a
  happening's visit under way (`happenings.visits`, its visitor or group); a god's stranger or anyone in the gods'
  affairs in the world; a trade, a talk or a scene with the colony; their hands full.
- **When** (`VisitorTradeMath.Turn`, `MarketCall`): a group's first look comes half an hour to an hour and a half after it
  settles; one of them at a time; never more than three at the stalls in all, campers and market days counted
  (`MostAtStalls`); two hours after a try that came to nothing (the campers' wait), four to eight after a purchase
  (`NextTryHours`); two purchases a day at most (`GuestBuys`, `ShoppedToday`). A game's visit stays three to nine hours
  and a caravan eleven to eighteen, so most buy once and some twice; envoys and feast guests who stay longer buy a
  purchase or two a day. The record, one a group by its lord's load id, is saved in `VisitorTracker.calls`
  (`marketCalls`), the records of groups gone from every map dropped when a new one is made, sixteen at most.
- **What they look for** (`VisitorTradeMath.Wants` by what they are, `WhoOf`): a trader's people (any group with a trader:
  a caravan, a visit's small trader, a people's factor with goods) what their trader deals in, `TraderWants` over the
  game's own test of what the trader takes (`TraderKindDef.WillTrade`) for every article of the game and the mods, the
  three biggest shares of a kind first, then food that keeps, worked out once a trader kind; an envoy or a notable (a
  people's leader, one with a title, a notable the colony knows by name) something fine, art, clothes and drink of good
  quality or better (`GoodEnough`); a feast's guests something to take home; one of Rimfolk's peoples by its calling
  (healers medicine, tamers feed, artisans and linesmen metal, mercenaries medicine, fishers cloth, traders and brokers
  art and cloth, the learned art and drink); anyone else on the road food that keeps (`RoadNeeds`). How many: as campers,
  by the mouths in their group and its beasts (`Need`).
- **Their coin** (`GuestCoin`, `OtherCarries`, `FromTrader`): their own silver first; someone else grown of theirs who has
  some goes instead, and the turn waits for them; a trader's people take theirs from their trader's silver and their pack
  beasts' (never while the colony trades with that trader, and never a pack beast's last coin, which would leave it
  counted as a beast for sale), the purse by what they are; anyone else counts out their coin for the road once a visit
  (`Purse`: an envoy or a notable 80 to 240, a trade 60 to 160, a traveller 30 to 100). Paid in silver as campers pay:
  RimMarket's payment can take goods when silver is short, but its own shoppers never do, it takes things by their full
  worth one by one so it seldom comes to the price, and visitors seldom carry goods of their own, so there is no barter.
- **At the counter**: the campers' own path (`ShopJob`, `JobDriver_MarketBuy`, `Buy`, `RimMarketStall.SellTo`,
  `BoughtTouches`): they stand at the counter a while, the article goes off the counter and its sale line into their
  pack, their silver is set down at the stall, the coins' sound, the price over their head, the colony's message. A line
  now and then goes through `Speech.Say`, one sentence: the buyer's from `Rimfolk_Pool_MarketBuy` with what they are as a
  tag (caravan, envoy, notable, guests, travellers, a calling), or, a little over a third of the time when the colony has
  a keeper at the stall, the keeper's word as the sale is made (`Rimfolk_Pool_MarketKeeper`, moment `sold`, by the kind
  of goods and the buyer; campers and market days hear it too).
- **Dev mode**: "Market: send this visitor to the stalls now" (the group's turn and the hours aside, everything else as
  always, why not in the log), "Market: every visitor and why (log)" (`Visitors/VisitorTradeDebug.cs`).

### The stall shows how worn weapons and apparel are (the player's request, 15 November 2026; released 0.254.0)

The player, with RimMarket's sales table open in Rimfolk's window (`UI/Window_StallCounter.cs`): "the market ui should
show how much health that armor and weapons still have". Now every weapon and piece of apparel shows its health on both
sides: on the left, each article's row has a pill "health 62%" (one piece, or several alike) or "health 45-100%" (the
lowest and highest of several), in plain grey from 80%, amber from 50%, red below, and a red "tainted" or "2 tainted"
pill for apparel taken from the dead (the game's own `Apparel.WornByCorpse`); its tooltip adds what they mean (worn
pieces sell for less, a tainted one for a tenth of its price, as the game's `StatPart_WornByCorpse` makes it, and
colonists don't like to wear one). On the right, a line's card has the same pills for the pieces it covers: those on the
counter and those in the colony in its quality range, each told apart in the tooltip. The pure part is
`StallCounterMath.Wear` (`Add`, by piece and merged), `Percent` (never 100% for a piece that has lost any, never 0% for
one with some left), `HealthText` and `HealthTone` (`StallCounterTests`); the counting is in the window's own count every
two seconds (`Good.wearOnMap` by quality slot, `Good.wearHeld` for the counter).

A line held to pieces above a condition ("only above 50%") is not offered: RimMarket 1.0.13's sale line
(`RimMarket.Buildings.StallOrder`) keeps a quality range and nothing else, and `StallOrder.Allows(Thing)`, which both its
stocking (`Building_MarketStall.Accepts`, the haulers' `WorkGiver_StockColonyStall`, the nearest piece first) and its
trimming of the counter (`TrimStock`) ask, checks quality only. The card's tooltip says so: the haulers bring the nearest
pieces in the range, worn or not. Rimfolk could add its own floor with a patch on `StallOrder.Allows` and a value of its
own for each line; not built.

### Guests keep out of bedrooms and the cold store (the player's request, 13 November 2026; released 0.230.1)

The player: "guests should not step into my pawns rooms when they're sleeping and also not into the fridge (even though
my fridge is detected as kitchen because of the butcher's table in it.", then "you can go ahead with the guest fixes".
In their save the guests were Hospitality's, with the Home area as their guest area, idling with the game's own colony
wander: a random cell within seven of the colony's gathering spot (the hall's table), which took in the bedroom off the
hall and, through the kitchen, the freezer; nothing in the game or in Hospitality asks whose room a cell is in or what
the room holds. So the rule is Rimfolk's, for every visitor, and it is told by what a room is, never by the role the
game gives it (a freezer with a butcher's table is a kitchen to the game). The pure rules are in
`Visitors/KeepOutMath.cs` (`KeepOutTests`), the game side in `Visitors/KeepOut.cs`.

- **Who keeps out** (`KeepOut.IsVisitor`): anyone of another people on a home map, not hostile, not the colony's
  prisoner or slave, up and in their right mind: the game's visitors and caravans, Rimfolk's visits, callers, envoys,
  feasts' and hosted guests and camps, Hospitality's guests, and their animals. Allies come to fight with the colony
  (`LordJob_AssistColony`) are left to the fight.
- **The rooms** (`KeepOutMath.Kind`): only a proper room (closed in, not out of doors, not huge). A **bedroom of the
  colony's people**: a bed of a colonist's, a slave's or a child's stands in it; guest beds alone (the guests' own
  room), sickbeds and cells don't make one. A **cold store**: below 5 degrees (`ColdBelow`), counted so until it warms
  to 8 (`ColdLeaves`, so a cooler cycling or a door held open doesn't flip it), with a stockpile or shelf in it that
  takes food (a meal, raw vegetables, raw meat or plant food: `AllowsFood`) or three stacks of food lying there
  (`FoodStacks`; a meal on a cold table isn't a store). A room with a colony bed is a bedroom first.
- **Who may go in** (`KeepOutMath.Barred`): nobody into a cold store. Into a bedroom, at any hour, only those whose bed
  is in it (a guest bed given to them, a lover's place in their partner's bed, as the game or Rimfolk gives it), and,
  while nobody of the colony sleeps in it, a doctor's work (`KeepOut.Care`: Rimfolk's round of doses for a patient in it,
  the animal doctor's patients, a people's worker sent to a colonist or the bed of their work, a visitor already at the
  game's own tending or rescue). Someone already inside (or in its doorway) always has the way out.
- **How** (`Patch_KeepOutDoors`): a postfix on the game's `ForbidUtility.IsForbiddenToPass` makes the doors of such a
  room forbidden to that visitor, as a forbidden door is to a colonist. The game's paths cost it as a wall, its reach
  stops at it (so its wandering, a joy or a job inside, a chair or food inside are out of reach and passed over), and a
  path through it is found again another way. One narrow hook for every kind of visitor, the doors of every mod that
  are the game's doors underneath (Doors Expanded's, More Door Variants'), and Hospitality's own area untouched. Under
  the deeper game hooks (`RimfolkPatches.On`); no setting of its own, as a fix.
- **The look** (`KeepOut.Rare`, `KeepOutBook`, every 250 ticks on the visitors' tick of the cycle, `Sched.RareVisitors`,
  timed as `Pass.RareKeepOut`; only on a home map with visitors on it): each room's kind, its cells and doorways, its
  doors and a way out by each, whose bed is there, whether one of the colony sleeps in it, who a doctor's work lets in;
  a `Snap` replaced whole, never changed after, since the game works out paths on worker threads and the door hook reads
  only it. When what the doors allow changes (a visitor comes or goes, someone falls asleep or wakes, a room turns cold),
  the game's reach, kept per pawn, is cleared (`Changed`); `KeepOut.Refresh` looks again at once (a people's worker sent
  to a colonist, so their way in counts from the start).
- **Walking out** (`WalkOutAll`): a visitor standing in a room they couldn't go into now (its owner fell asleep, it
  turned cold, a reload) walks out to the nearest door's outside cell, with no words; not while asleep, in bed, at an
  order of the player's or with the map in danger.
- **Food brought out** (`KeepOut.Fetch`, `JobDriver_BringOutFood`, the job `Rimfolk_BringOutFood`): food a visitor may
  not go in for is carried out by the nearest free colonist (`PlayOuts.CanTakePart`, able to haul): a meal, or enough of
  the raw food for one, taken up in the cold store, walked over to the visitor and handed over into their pack, and they
  eat it then (the game takes it to a table if one is near). Not handed over, it is set down where the colonist stands,
  still the colony's. Where the colony serves its guests: a feast's guests (`PlayGuests.Keep`, `PlayOutLord.Serve`),
  envoys and their party (`Envoys.Eat`, counted when the colonist sets off with it), a feast's visiting parties
  (`Feasts`), the herders' rider's supper (`HerdersBeast`), all through `Hosting.Brought` in the order `Hosting.Meal` and
  `Raw` pick; a meal shared with an outsider (`Outsiders.Portions` and `Meal`: the colonist brings the outsider's portion
  first, then eats their own, `OutsiderMeal.brought` giving both longer to begin). And anyone starving with nothing of
  their own and no food elsewhere in reach (`FeedHungry`: the game, and Hospitality for a starving guest, would have them
  take the colony's food then), once in two hours at most.
- **Rimfolk's own choices** never pick such a room (`KeepOut.IsKept`): a guest's corner for the night
  (`VisitorServices.Fits`), a corner indoors (`Visitors.IndoorsCell`), Hospitality's guest beds for a visit
  (`VisitorBeds.Free`), a spare bed for a hosted guest (`Hosting.Beds`: before, an empty bed in a barracks beside
  sleeping colonists would do), a helping guest's work (`GuestHelp.Bad`, besides its rooms by role); and the market opens
  only a stall's own place to Hospitality's guests, never one inside a kept room (`Patch_MarketGuestsReach`).
- **Dev mode**: "Visitors: rooms kept from them (log)" and "Visitors: look at the kept rooms again now"
  (`Visitors/KeepOutDebug.cs`).

### Visitors' idle hours: their own day (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.239.0)

The player: "guests should spend more of their time doing things. i don't want them to generate value for me, but it
just looks a bit weird when they spend most of their day just standing and walking around. they can talk, do actions,
recreation, many things that don't make them work for me", then "do the one that visitors fill their idle hours". Before,
the game's visitors and traders stood about and wandered near their spot, Rimfolk's own visits had their duties
(`Rimfolk_VisitWait`, `Rimfolk_VisitWork`) and a fire and a seat now and then, and envoys wandered. Now a visitor's idle
moments are filled with things of their own, none of it work or value for the colony. The pure rules are in
`Visitors/IdleHoursMath.cs` (`IdleHoursTests`), the game side in `Visitors/IdleHours.cs` (who, what is about, the places),
`Visitors/IdleHoursJobs.cs` (the stints and the hook) and `Visitors/IdleHoursDebug.cs`; the jobs in
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_VisitorIdle.xml`, the lines in `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Pool_VisitorIdle.xml`.

- **The way in** (`Patch_VisitorsIdle`): a postfix on `ThinkNode_Duty.TryIssueJobPackage`, at low priority so it comes
  after the market's (`Patch_VisitorsShop`). Only when the duty's answer is an idle wander (`GotoWander`, `Wait_Wander`)
  of someone not of the colony does `IdleHours.JobFor` look for something of their own; the job keeps the wander's lord,
  source and duty tag. Fighting, eating, sleeping, the market and whatever the duty has for them (a visit's work, its
  fire) come first, and the duty itself is left as it is.
- **Who** (`IdleHours.GroupOf`, `AtStay`, `WhyNot`): on a home map, at peace with the colony, not held or a quest's, up and
  about, no danger on the map, not leaving, not trading or in Rimfolk's outsider talk, not held by a story
  (`VisitorTrade.HeldByStory`, shared with the market), not hungry, worn out or due to sleep. The groups: the game's
  visitors (`LordJob_VisitColony`) and trade caravans (`LordJob_TradeWithColony`) at their spot (`LordToil_DefendPoint`,
  the caravan's own toil included), a caravan's goods and pack carriers aside; Rimfolk's visits at their spot out of
  doors (`LordToil_VisitHere`, not those shown a corner inside); envoys staying the season (`LordToil_EnvoyStay`); and
  Hospitality's guests relaxing (its `Relax` duty). The trader keeps near the trade (`IdleRole.Trader`, 9 cells), a
  caravan's guards stay on watch (no games, no nap, no drink). Quest lodgers are the colony's own for their stay and take
  its recreation already; callers, camps, feasts' and hosted guests and stories' strangers have their own plans.
- **What they do** (`IdleDoing`, each a JobDef of its own with `VisitIdleExtension`, run by `JobDriver_VisitIdle`):
  talk with one of their own who is idle near (the two stand together, the game's own chats come of it), keep one of the
  colony's people at their leisure company (`SmallHabits.CanListen`; not followed about once they walk off), sit in the
  ring round a lit fire (their own camp's first for a Rimfolk visit), warm their hands right by it below 5 degrees, take
  a free seat (out in the open in fair weather, under a roof in foul; never a work chair), get under a roof near them in
  rain or snow (a porch or eaves for Rimfolk's visits, which keep out of doors), eat a bite from their own pack at a meal
  hour when peckish, nap in a tree's shade at midday in fair weather when a little tired (`JobDriver_VisitNap`, the
  game's own lying down, which doesn't look for another job meanwhile), play the colony's games, its instruments and its
  telescope on a clear night while nobody of the colony wants them, look at its art, pray at a shrine of their god (the
  colony's dedicated shrines, Gods/Worship) or an altar of a faith the colony holds and they share, see to their own
  animals (the beast waits while they brush it down), run about at play (the children, `JobDriver_VisitIdlePlay`), have a
  smoke or a drink of their own from their own pack, smoke a pipe or whittle a bit of wood.
- **Fitted to them** (`IdleHoursMath.Weights`, `NotFor`, `CallingFactor`): by the hour (meals at breakfast, midday and
  supper, prayers morning and evening, games and music from morning to mid-evening, the telescope after dark, the nap
  from noon to four, the fire most of an evening), the weather (shelter first in the rain, the fire on a chilly day, no
  nap in rain or cold), who they are (children play and see to the animals and nothing grown; a titled visitor never
  dozes on the ground or whittles and looks at the art more; a scoffer doesn't pray, the devout pray more; a teetotaller
  or a faith against drugs has no smoke or drink; nobody who can't talk, see or use their hands does what needs it), their
  people's age (a thing of the colony's fits them when it is of their age or older, by its own tech level, its research,
  its components or plasteel and its power: a tribal visitor plays horseshoes and the royal game of Ur, not chess or a
  spacer screen; whittling and a pipe among the older ages most) and their calling (herders see to their animals,
  pilgrims pray, scholars look at the stars and the art, artisans at the art, traders and mercenaries play).
- **Nothing for the colony**: nothing made, hauled, cleaned or built for it; nothing of its stores used (what they eat,
  drink or smoke comes out of their own pack, one portion, and what isn't finished goes back into it; a trader's pack is
  the trade's goods and never touched); no fuel, power or wear asked of anything beyond what it already uses; and no
  recreation taken from the colony's people. Nothing is reserved (`TryMakePreToilReservations` is true), so one of the
  colony's people who wants a game, a seat or a place finds it free; the moment one of them reserves the thing, the cell
  or the seat, or sets out to walk there (`IdleHours.ColonyWho`: the colony's reservations and destinations), the visitor
  stands up and gives it to them, now and then with a word, and leaves it be for four hours (`GiveWayHours`). A joy thing
  is free only when nobody of the colony has it, it isn't forbidden or switched off, it has its power and there's room at
  it (`IdleHoursMath.Free`: two at a chess table, one at a telescope). Nobody idles on a cook's or a crafter's spot (the
  colony's buildings' interaction cells, `Places.workCells`). Every stint is casually interruptible, so a trader can
  still be traded with and anyone talked to.
- **The colony's things** (`IdleHours.JoyThings`, `PlacesOf`, looked at once an hour per map): every building a joy giver
  of the game or a loaded mod uses (`JoyGiver_InteractBuilding` and its kinds), so the player's whole pool counts: the
  game's horseshoes, hoopstone, chess, Ur, poker, billiards, screens, telescope and Royalty's instruments; Vanilla
  Furniture Expanded's arcade, roulette, piano, computers, radio and Spacer's interactive table; the Settlers' faro and
  five-finger fillet; Boglegs' tongo; the quests' foosball and wargaming tables. Left out (`IdleHoursMath.Excluded`):
  baths, hot tubs, saunas, pools and swimming, the washing machine, shooting, archery, darts, sparring, dummies and
  punching bags (the game shows the throw or the blow, which a visitor's stint doesn't), a stage that needs a performer, a
  therapist's couch, a corpse on show, the market's stalls and auction, and Rimfolk's own habits. How each is used comes
  from its joy giver (`ShapeOf`: a watching spot, a seat beside it, its own spot, an instrument), with the game's look of
  it: the horseshoes and stones thrown, the cards at a poker table, a screen's glow at the screen, the instrument played
  with its own music (`Building_MusicalInstrument.StartPlaying`), notes over a piano, the report the game's own job uses
  ("playing chess."). Fires (`IdleHoursMath.SitByFire`, over `Sauna.IsFire`): a campfire, a brazier, a hearth, a large
  fire, a grill, not a torch, lamp or candle, a stove or smithy, or anything with power. Seats: anything sittable but a
  bed, a toilet, a throne, a saddle or a pew. Art: what the game's own looking at art takes (`canBeEnjoyedAsArt`).
- **Where** (`PlaceOk`, `StandOk`): near their spot (`IdleHoursMath.Reach`: 20 cells for the game's visitors, 16 for a
  caravan, 9 for its trader, 14 for Rimfolk's visits, 24 for envoys, 6 for Hospitality's guests from where they stand;
  round two below widens these and spreads them over the colony),
  never in a cell, a sickroom, a bedroom or a barracks, nor in a room visitors keep out of (`KeepOut.KeptFrom`: the
  colony's bedrooms and cold stores, whose doors are barred to them anyway), out of doors and off the fields for
  Rimfolk's visits, on nobody's cell, not one another of them is going to, and within reach.
- **Hospitality's guests** keep Hospitality's own recreation: only what it has nothing for is filled
  (`IdleHoursMath.ForHospitality`: warming their hands at a fire in the cold, shelter from the rain, a prayer at their
  god's shrine, their own animals), less often (`FillChance`), and close to where they stand. Round two below gives
  them all of Rimfolk's doings, within their guest area.
- **How often and how long** (`FillChance`, `Stint`, `NextLook`): three idle wanders in four by day become something of
  their own, fewer at night and for Hospitality's guests; a stint lasts from a few minutes to an hour and a half of game
  time (a bite 400 to 700 ticks, a game 1,500 to 3,000), then a little wandering (150 to 400 ticks) before the next look,
  longer (500 to 1,000) when nothing came of it. Round two below: most of the day, a look at once.
- **What's said** (`IdleHours.Say`, `Rimfolk_Pool_VisitorIdle`): now and then a line as a stint begins, one plain sentence
  through `Speech.Say` (a greeting to the colonist they keep company more often, said only when the two are together),
  tagged by the moment, their people's age and calling; a word to the colonist they give way to; never from one visitor
  more than once in six hours, or on one map more than once in half an hour (`MaySpeak`).
- **The cost**: each visitor looks at most once in a stint and a wander (their next look by `thingIDNumber`, per
  session), what is about from the hour's list of the map's things, the way there checked only for the doing picked; a
  stint's own checks once a second (`IdleCheck`). Nothing is saved but the game's own job.
- **The setting**: "Visitors fill their idle hours" (`visitorsIdle`, on by default; the What's on page, Neighbours and
  letters, after the outsiders' settings; under the deeper game hooks).
- **Dev mode**: "Visitors: fill this visitor's idle hour now" (the chance and the next look aside) and "Visitors: idle
  hours of everyone here (log)" (each visitor's group, role, age, calling, the hour, the weather, what fits and how much,
  or why nothing does).

### Visitors' idle hours, round two: busy most of the day, over the colony (the player's go, 15 November 2026; released 0.255.0)
