The player: "guests still just wait around most of the time it feels. they could read books, take walks, interact with my
pets, write letters, train, fish, work on and use items themselves etc.", then "ok looks like they already read books
sometimes, but they generally just chill around the same room (my eating room)", and to the proposal "and yes, your
suggestions all sound great". Why they waited: a look came only now and then (three in four by day, Hospitality's guests
45% of that), a stint ended in a wander of 150 to 1,000 ticks before the next look, and for Hospitality's guests Rimfolk
filled only warming, shelter, prayer and animals, within six cells of where they stood, while Hospitality's own duty
(`Relax`, in its `Duties_Visit.xml`) has them stand about being sociable a third of the time and wander the colony the rest
once its recreation is done (its `JobGiver_Relax` only gives a job while their recreation is below 90%), which drew them
all to the dining room. The same files as the first round: `Visitors/IdleHoursMath.cs` (`IdleHoursTests`),
`Visitors/IdleHours.cs`, `Visitors/IdleHoursJobs.cs`, `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_VisitorIdle.xml`,
`Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Pool_VisitorIdle.xml`, `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_VisitorIdle.xml`.

- **Most of their waiting filled** (`FillChance`, `NextLook`, `NextLookAfter`, `Stint`): nine idle moments in ten by day
  and six in ten at night become something of their own (Hospitality's guests nine tenths of that); the next look comes
  the moment a stint ends (a stint that ended within 250 ticks of starting waits 300 to 700, so nobody starts and stops
  over and over); stints are longer where it fits (an evening at the fire up to 3,200 ticks, a game 3,400, a book or
  fishing 3,500). The night is quieter: only the fire, a seat, shelter, the stars, a little talk, and sleep.
- **Hospitality's guests** (`ForHospitality`, `GuestArea`): every doing but the night's sleep (their nights are in
  Hospitality's guest beds), alongside Hospitality's own recreation, which comes first: Rimfolk fills only the moments its
  duty would have them wander (`GotoWander`, `Wait_Wander`) or stand about (`StandAndBeSociallyActive`, filled for its
  guests only). Within the guest area set in Hospitality's guest tab (its `CompGuest.guestArea_int`, found by name as the
  market finds it; Hospitality's own reach patch keeps them in it too), reaching 50 cells over the colony from where they
  stand. The game's visitors now reach 24 cells, envoys 30.
- **Spread over the colony** (`IdleHoursMath.PlaceScore`, `IdleHours.Spread`): every seat, fire, game, instrument, telescope,
  piece of art, table, target, book, fishing place and walk's end is ranked by its distance over their reach, a penalty
  for the room they are in now (0.8 for Hospitality's guests, 0.25 for the rest), 0.3 for each other visitor within five
  cells or in the same room indoors (where those at a stint are going counts), and a little chance; a seat for a bite, a
  smoke or mending is looked for up to 20 cells off for Hospitality's guests (8 for the rest). So after a while in the
  dining room the next thing is somewhere else: another room, the grounds, the fire, the garden.
- **New doings**, each a job of its own with its own words (`Rimfolk_IdleRead` to `Rimfolk_IdleSleep`), none working for
  the colony or using up its things, each giving way to the colony's people as before, by their people's age and calling:
  - **A book** (`Read`): one of their own from their pack (any `Book`; taken out once they sit down, put back after), or
    one of the colony's lying about (a shelf, a table, the floor) or in its bookcase, taken up, read on a seat within
    eight cells (else beside where it lay) carried open as the game's readers carry it (`Book.IsOpen`), and put back into
    its bookcase or onto the cell it lay on; cut short away from there, it is set down where they stand, still the
    colony's. The book's own outcomes (research, skill, a quest) are never run, so reading gives the colony nothing; dark
    tomes that can break a mind are left alone (`BookOk`). A tribal people reads only a book of its own; the children,
    a guard on watch and anyone who can't see don't read.
  - **A walk** (`Walk`): two to four places on the colony's laid paths out of doors (or open ground), nearest first at a
    stroll, a moment at each, ending at a garden (flowers in a pot or a bed of beauty plants), a grave with someone in it,
    or a view (the water's edge, the edge of the home area looking out), where they stand a while looking at it. In fair
    weather by day, mornings and evenings most; not the children (they play), not a trader or a guard.
  - **The colony's pets** (`Pet`): a small animal of the colony's (a dog, a cat, a guinea pig: `IsPet`, body size up to
    1.3, a pet by the game's petness or one that nuzzles; not roped or penned stock), awake, idle and calm, nobody of the
    colony after it: petted (it waits with them, a heart over it), or, for a dog out of doors, a stick thrown a few times
    within its allowed area, the dog running after it and bringing it back by the game's own going somewhere
    (`JobDefOf.Goto`). Never tamed, trained or bonded. A word to it now and then; the children most.
  - **A letter or their journal** (`Write`), sitting at one of the colony's tables (a table to eat at, not a work bench),
    from the medieval age on.
  - **Training** (`Train`): at the colony's training targets from the player's mods (Misc. Training's martial arts target,
    Vanilla Factions Expanded - Medieval 2's training dummy; `IdleHoursMath.SparTargets`, by name), blows struck with the
    game's own lunge and sound; or shadow sparring on open ground in fair weather, the body thrown forward with each blow
    (`ForcedBodyOffset`) and turning now and then. Not the children, not a trader or a guard; mercenaries and hunters
    most. **Archery** (`Archery`): with their own bow or crossbow (`IsBow`), at the colony's archery target (Misc. Training's,
    Medieval 2's) from its own stand, Misc. Training's arrow (`Mote_ArcheryArrow`) flying and striking with the bow's own
    sound; with Misc. Training not loaded there is no arrow to show, so no archery.
  - **Fishing** (`Fish`): at the water's edge with fish in the water (Odyssey's fish stock, or Vanilla Fishing Expanded's
    open water on its own; `CampLand.Fishable`), never in one of the colony's fishing zones or beside a colonist fishing,
    with Odyssey's fishing line shown at the water; at the end one to three of the water's own fish go into their pack
    (theirs, taken with them), with the game's sound of a catch. The colony's fish stock is left as it was. The river
    folk (`fishers`) three times as often; never against their faith (Odyssey's fishing precepts).
  - **Their own gear**: mending the most worn piece of their clothes (below four fifths), a tenth of its hit points made
    good at the end (`Mend`; not a titled one); seeing to their weapon (`Sharpen`, the weapon in hand): a blade sharpened
    with a few sparks, a bow oiled and restrung, a gun cleaned. Their own pack animal is seen to as before (`Animal`).
  - **A game of their own** (`Cards`) with one of their own idle near, the two facing each other: cards (the game's cards
    over them and the chips' sound), dice among the medieval half the time, a game of stones for a tribal people (the
    stones thrown between them). Grown-ups only; of an evening most.
  - **A song** (`Sing`), sung quietly to themselves, notes over them; of an evening most. No mod in the player's list adds
    an instrument a person carries, so their own instruments wait for one; the colony's instruments are played as before.
  - **A night's sleep** (`Sleep`): the game's visitors and a caravan's people (not its trader or guards), tired at
    night, lie down on the ground near their spot, out of doors (a porch or a shed's eaves in rain, snow or the cold),
    the game's own lying down, till rested. Rimfolk's visits, envoys and Hospitality's guests keep their own beds and
    bedtimes.
- **The log** ("Visitors: idle hours of everyone here"): a first line for the map (how many are up and about, how many
  at something of their own, how many standing or wandering, and the share of their idle time filled this session), and
  for each visitor what they are at now, their share filled (the ticks at stints against the ticks left standing or
  wandering, each such moment counted up to 1,000 ticks: `IdleHoursMath.FilledShare`), what is about for the new doings
  (their book, the colony's books, pets, fishing places, a target, a bow, a table, walk ends, worn clothes, a weapon),
  and what fits now. Per session, nothing saved.

### Neighbours' requests and callers at the gate (the player's request, 6 November 2026)

"Do another big content update to existing mechanics": this part the neighbours and the people who come to the colony,
in the frameworks that were there (missions, data events, letter variants), at the rates there were. The pure rules in
`Missions/NeighboursFourMath.cs` (`NeighboursFourTests`), the workers in `Missions/Workers_MissionNeighbours4.cs`, the
texts in `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Missions_Neighbours4*.xml`, `Defs/IncidentDefs/Rimfolk_Events_Neighbours4*.xml`.

- **One draw for every mission.** Every mission offer's base chance is scaled so the missions together weigh what the
  thirteen kinds offered weighed before this round (`MissionPoolWeight`, 6.8; `MissionPool.Factor` in the storyteller's
  draw and Rimfolk's own, `Happenings.cs`; the balance model the same). A new kind takes a share; one mission at a time
  as always.
- **Hands lent to a neighbour's town** (`HappeningWorker_MissionHands`, data `MissionHands`): the harvest hands' way for
  any skill. One or two of the colony's people good at it (a level, the work not disabled), the colony's caravan at the
  people's nearest town within three days, staying there `hours`; the whole stay earns the silver into the packs, a gift
  of things of the colony's era (`Loot`) and the skill's experience; half the stay half the silver, less goodwill lost.
  Builders after a storm or a fire (Construction 5, two, 36 hours), a healer for their sickhouse (Medicine 6 and
  doctoring, one, 48), a teacher for their young (Intellectual 7, one, 36), a witness at a truce or a boundary (Social 6,
  one, 12), a smith before the harvest or the sowing, or a mechanic for a hightech town's pumps (Crafting 6, one, 24). Each
  is remembered as `lentHands` (a debt of honour where those are kept). Every one's forms are by the asking people's age
  (`their:tribal` to `their:spacer`, `their:lowtech`, `their:hightech`, added to every mission's tags) and the Empire's
  own lines keep its knights, stewards and heralds.
- **A store kept** (`HappeningWorker_MissionKeep`): their carts bring grain, timber, steel or cloth to the gate
  (`Couriers.Deliver`), and when the season is up come back for as much (`Couriers.CollectGoals`), paying a quarter of
  its worth (`KeepFee`). What the stores hold then counts, the colony's own the same as theirs, as the terms say. Short,
  the colony pays the rest in silver at its plain worth (`Shortfall`, their carts take it); without the silver they take
  what there is, and remember it.
- **A young beast raised** (`HappeningWorker_MissionBeast`): a foal (lowtech peoples), a calf, a kid or a pup of a kind
  that suits the weather and the land. Their drover walks it in with them to the gate (`Arrivals.Visit`), hands it over
  there (`SetFaction`) and goes; at the end of the season their drover comes for it (the runaway's `HandBack`, its
  `Couriers.Fetch`) and pays all of it kept well (no malnutrition of 0.2, nothing sick, no wound untended) or half kept
  poorly. Dead or lost, goodwill and the memory; bonded to one of the colony's, it stays and they are glad.
- **Someone of theirs lost on the land** (`HappeningWorker_MissionLost`, the lost child's worker with its ages, finder,
  deed and memory as virtual hooks): an old one who wandered off (66 to 86) and a hunter overdue (20 to 55), found by
  whoever comes within six steps in sight, then their kin come; remembered as `foundLost`.
- **A traveller seen home** (`HappeningWorker_MissionEscortWho`, the pilgrim's escort with its ages and variant as hooks):
  a trader with the season's silver past a bandit road, a healer bound for a sickhouse, a scholar with a chest of books.
- **Goods** in the delivery framework, data only: the timber and stone of a wall (a palisade, a wall, a watchtower with
  steel and components for an industrial colony), fodder for their herds (hay and kibble in the fall and winter, hay in a
  dry summer), stores for a long road (pemmican or meals and cloth for pilgrims, meals, cloth and timber for a trek,
  survival packs and medicine for an expedition), and seed after a blight or a flood (corn, rice, potatoes).
- **In the town head's name.** The hands, the store, the beast and every delivery name the town's head by their title
  when the region's ledger knows them (`InviteForms.Host`, `{HOST}` and the tag `host`), the Empire's title for the
  Empire. No line counts the days down: the Quests tab shows the time; endings say what is happening as it happens
  (their carts coming, their drover on the road).
- **Callers at the gate** (data events, `HappeningWorker_Setting`, people of about the colony's age): a herb-gatherer (a
  lesson at their side for the colony's grower, or herbal medicine bought), drovers on the road to a fair (a young beast
  bought, handed over beside them, or a meal carried out), a seed-seller in spring and summer (a patch sown by the grower,
  or a young tree planted at the field's edge), a neighbour's patrol after bandits (fed, a drill for the best shot, or
  medicine sold), a traveller on the wrong road (a meal and the roads gone over at the table), a petitioner with a
  grievance against their own head (heard out at the table), a brewer's cart (beer bought, or brewing secrets for the
  cook). Silence sends them on; nothing gathers the colony, nobody is hurt.
- **More ways to tell the callers** that had one (`LetterVariantsDef`): the barber, the animal doctor, the undertakers, a
  captive's kin and the art collector, by the season, the age and what they find, with an ending for each answer.

#### The missions' endings told as they happen (released 0.269.4)

Found in the plain-words pass on the missions (19 November 2026). A mission's ending letter (`Missions.Finish`) comes the
moment the mission is settled, before anything of it is seen on the map, so the older missions told as done what had
only just been set going: carts that "took everything" and drivers who "counted out" the silver (`Couriers.CollectGoals`
sends the carts some hours later), a runaway that "went home to where the herder was waiting down the road"
(`Couriers.Fetch` brings the herder to the colony), a lost child's family that "came running" (they walk in from the
edge then), guests and hands lent to a town who "came home" or "are coming home" with their gifts (the caravan is still
at the town, the gifts in its packs, and it comes home when the player sends it), a runaway "off into the hills and
gone" (it leaves within the hour). The words now say what is happening: the carts, the herder, the family are coming;
the gifts and the pay are in the caravan's packs. The same pass put right the shrine's pilgrims (they come and spend the
day beside the shrine, `Arrivals.Visit`; they don't sing or kneel, and nothing brings them back each year, so neither the
singing nor "they'll stop here every year now" is told), the Wardens' gift (a gift of the colony's era, `Loot`, not "a
hide"), the tamed runaway's herder (not on the road until the colony answers), and the old one lost on the colony's land,
who was always "an old man" whoever was lost. Nothing in the code changed; the newer missions (the quests at home and the
storylines) already told it this way.

### Quests at home, round 1: six single quests (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.261.0)

The player, 16 November 2026: "go ahead with quests and storylines, make sure they are written in the more clear style i
mentioned earlier on", and "while quests that require you to go out of your base are interesting, i hardly ever reach the
stage where I can consistently go out of base and it's worth it, so keep these quests to a minimum". The plan and its eight
rules are `docs/quests-proposals.md`; this is its round 1's single quests (Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q9, Q10), beside the storyline
frame. Each is a mission kind of its own on the missions framework (offered in the Quests tab, accepted or let expire,
ended with success or failure), and each plays out on the colony's own map: nobody of the colony goes away. The pure
rules in `Missions/HomeQuestsMath.cs` (`HomeQuestsTests`), the workers in `Missions/Workers_MissionHome.cs` (Q1, Q2, Q5)
and `Workers_MissionHome2.cs` (Q7, Q9, Q10), what they share in `HomeQuests.cs`, the texts in
`Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Missions_Home.xml`, the letter, keepsakes, search job and quarrel in
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_Missions_Home_Misc.xml`, the lines over a head in `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Lines_HomeQuests.xml`.

- **Who asks.** Any people at peace with a town on the map may ask (the missions' `Neighbor`), one of a fitting calling
  five times likelier (`MissionPeople.prefers`): the Last Republic's citizens a prisoner kept, the road league's traders a
  dispute judged, the Signal Line's linesmen a wounded messenger, the Ashen Banner's mercenaries an outlaw, the pilgrim
  fellowship a keepsake, the Circuit of Tamers an animal. Every age asks in its own words (`their:tribal` to
  `their:spacer`, the Empire with its officers, stewards and retainers apart), and what they bring or lose is of their
  age: a message stick, a sealed letter or a dispatch case; a painted hide, a family book or a photo album.
- **Plain terms.** The quest's description says who asks and why, then what to do, for how long, what the colony gets
  and what failing costs, in that order; the reward in words (`RewardWords`: silver, or a tribe's goods of their own
  making worth as much), and, where favours are kept, that the people will owe the colony one (the missions' own
  "mission" deed). Numbers the player needs are stated (the days held, the six wet hours); nothing else counts down.
- **The reward.** The quest's own range (100 to 340 silver before the rest) times the asking people's age (a tribe 0.8,
  medieval 1, industrial 1.15, spacer and the Empire 1.3) and the colony's wealth (`WealthFactor`, 0.6 to 2), rounded to
  tens; a tribe pays in things of the colony's era (`Loot`), everyone else in silver, carried in by their people
  (`Couriers/`) or set down at once when goods don't come and go. Goodwill for it done (8 to 12, `GoodwillWhy.Task`), a
  cost for failing it (4 to 8, a death or a broken word twice that).
- **Q1, their prisoner kept** (`HappeningWorker_MissionPrisoner`, needs a free bed in a prison cell). Someone of a people
  at war with the colony (the asking people's own enemies likelier, their age nearest; `HomeQuests.Enemy`), disarmed, is
  walked in by two of theirs as one of their own (so the colony's doors open for them) to the room of a free prison bed
  and handed over inside it (`SetGuestStatus(..., Prisoner)`, their own people again, kept and not recruited:
  `MaintainOnly`, the bed claimed). Half a day without reaching it, they hand them over where they stand, and say so. The
  colony holds them 4 to 7 days as the game holds any prisoner: the game's own prison breaks at its own odds. Then their
  people come for the prisoner and pay (`Couriers.Fetch`, as a prisoner sold). Escaped, dead, let go, recruited or
  enslaved, it fails.
- **Q2, a dispute judged** (`HappeningWorker_MissionDispute`, the card `HappeningWorker_MissionJudgement`). Two of a
  people come to the gate with a quarrel of their age (an elk's hide, a boundary stone, a tractor part, a salvaged power
  cell, a seat at the lord's table), each with a poor opinion of the other for it (`Rimfolk_HomeQ_Quarrel`, -25). A card
  tells each side's claim and asks the colony: for one, for the other, split between them, or (unanswered) no judgement.
  The colony's peacemaker (else its best talker) goes over in their free time and says it to their faces; the one it went
  for thanks them, the one it went against says so and has three tries of the game's own insult at the other before they
  leave (`Insults`), each with the game's own odds of a social fight, shown by the game; a split sends both home grumbling.
  Their town pays for the judgement; a split pleases it most, a side taken a little less, none costs.
- **Q5, a wounded messenger** (`HappeningWorker_MissionMessenger`, needs a bed and a doctor). Attacked on the road by
  raiders or by wild animals, the messenger comes in from the edge with two or three of the game's own wounds (cuts and
  stabs from a low-tech band, gunshots from a modern one, bites and scratches from animals; never so bad they can't walk
  or would bleed out within a day and a half: `HomeQuests.Wound`), hands over the letter at the gate, and is taken in as
  the colony's guest to a patient's bed, tended and fed by its doctors as the game does a guest. Mended, they wait at the
  colony as a visitor, eating at its table and sleeping in a free bed (the hosting missions' `Tend`). After 4 to 6 days
  their people come for the letter (`Couriers.CollectThings`) and pay; the messenger goes home with them, or, still in
  bed, stays the colony's guest until they can walk. The messenger dead, or the letter burned, rotted or carried off,
  fails it.
- **Q7, an outlaw on the colony's land** (`HappeningWorker_MissionOutlaw`, drawn within the shared harm budget:
  `HarmKinds.Outlaw`, system "quests", off with the world's battles). One of a hostile people's own fighters, as strong
  as a third of the storyteller's threat points (45 to 180 combat power: `OutlawPower`), with the game's own gear, hides
  at the foot of the hills or near the edge of the map, at least 35 cells out, which way named in the terms; lying low
  (asleep: no threat to anyone) until someone of the colony comes within ten cells in sight, or they are hurt. Found,
  three times in four they fight where they stand (the game's own `LordJob_DefendPoint`), through the budget's roll;
  else they run for the edge. Captured and held, their people collect them and pay half as much again; killed, they pay
  the price. Gone off the map, never found in 5 to 7 days, or taken into the colony, it fails.
- **Q9, a lost heirloom** (`HappeningWorker_MissionKeepsake`). It lies somewhere in the open, at least 25 cells out, in
  an area of radius 7 drawn on the map (`HomeQuestOverlay`), never at its middle. Right-clicking inside the area with a
  colonist selected searches it (`JobDriver_SearchKeepsake`: walk to the spot, an hour's look with a progress bar),
  covering 2.9 cells around each spot and going on to the nearest spot not yet covered until it is found (`Covers`; the
  whole area in about a dozen looks). Every hour of rain or snow on it in the open counts; six of them ruin it, and it is
  then there to be found, ruined. Found, it is set down where it lay and kept until their people come for it and pay.
  Not found in 3 to 4 days, one of theirs comes to search the area, finds it and takes it home.
- **Q10, tame one for them** (`HappeningWorker_MissionTameFor`). A grown wild animal of the colony's land the colony's
  tamer could win over (the game's `TameUtility.CanTame` and handling skill), one of the finest there; else one of the
  land's own kinds (`BiomeAnimals.Of`, every mod's) wanders in. Tamed the game's way, their handler comes for it within
  half a day and pays (`Couriers.Fetch`); bonded to someone of the colony, they leave it and pay nothing. Killed, gone, or
  still wild after 6 to 9 days, it fails.
- **Pace.** Each takes 0.3 of the missions' one draw (1.8 in all), so missions as a whole come no oftener than before
  (`MissionPool`: they still weigh 6.8; the way to play leans them as it leans every mission); one mission at a time; the
  same quest not again for 75 days.
- **Shared files, small.** `Mission` keeps four more things for them (`cell`, `area`, `thing`, `other`, saved), the
  quest's look targets show its thing and its area, and `Missions.Tags` adds their tags (`HomeQuests.AddTags`: `goods`,
  `favour`, `scuffle`); nothing else of the missions changed.
- **Dev mode** (Debug actions, Rimfolk): "Quests at home: offer one now...", "accept the open one", "what it waits for
  comes now", "end the open one as..." (each quest's own outcomes), "what the open one keeps (log)".

### Quests at home, round 2: seven single quests (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.263.0)

The player, 16 November 2026, after round 1: "great, do some more"; the go for the quests: "go ahead with quests and
storylines, make sure they are written in the more clear style i mentioned earlier on", and "while quests that require
you to go out of your base are interesting, i hardly ever reach the stage where I can consistently go out of base and
it's worth it, so keep these quests to a minimum". This is round 2's single quests of `docs/quests-proposals.md` (Q3, Q4,
Q6, Q8, Q11, Q12, Q13), built the way round 1's six were: each a mission kind of its own in the Quests tab, played out on
the colony's own map (their people come to the colony; what they leave or want is collected by them; nobody of the colony
goes away). The pure rules in `Missions/HomeQuests2Math.cs` (`HomeQuests2Tests`), the workers in
`Missions/Workers_MissionHome3.cs` (Q3, Q4, Q6, Q8) and `Workers_MissionHome4.cs` (Q11, Q12, Q13), what they share and
their jobs in `HomeQuests2.cs`, the texts in `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Missions_Home2.xml`, the jobs and the work giver in
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_Missions_Home2_Misc.xml`, the lines over a head in `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Lines_HomeQuests2.xml`.

- **Who asks, and plain terms.** As round 1: any people at peace may ask, one of a fitting calling five times likelier
  (the Ashen Banner's mercenaries a young fighter, the river folk a wedding's piece, the herding folk a sick animal, the
  road league a camp guarded, the Mossborn's grove-keepers seed kept, the learned society a book copied, the Choir's
  listeners musicians). Every age asks in its own words, the Empire with its knights and stewards apart. The quest's
  description says who asks and why, then what to do, by when, what the colony gets and what failing costs, in that order;
  the numbers the player needs are stated (two hours an evening, the copy's hours, six hours to carry the seed in, twelve
  warm hours) and the rules hold them (tested). Rewards on round 1's scale (the quest's own range, 60 to 240 silver
  before the rest, times the asking people's age and the colony's wealth; a tribe pays in goods of its own), round 1's
  goodwill and costs, and the favour owed where favours are kept.
- **Q3, a young fighter trained** (`HappeningWorker_MissionTrainee`, a hosted guest). One of their young fighters
  (16 to 21, one of their own fighter kinds) stays 3 to 5 days, the colony's guest at its table and in its beds, to learn
  from the colony's best shot or best melee fighter; they come knowing three levels less at most. Each evening from four
  to nine, when the teacher is free (nothing pressing, not hungry or worn out: the drills' own test), the two train for
  about two hours: side by side at the colony's shooting or archery target when it has one (Misc. Training's, Medieval 2's;
  `JobDriver_HomeQuestTrain`: the weapon's own sound, a flash from a gun, the hit on the target) and the young one has a
  ranged weapon and the best shot is as good as the best fighter; else sparring with pulled blows on open ground (the
  lunge and the sound, the drills' places). Sparring rolls once a day for a blow that lands for real, at the colony's own
  drills' rate (one bout in 25, `HarmKinds.Drills`, through the shared budget and its cap; off with the drills' system):
  a bruise or a cut by the colony's means, said, shown with a message, and the evening ends there. Both learn the game's
  own way (`Learn`, its passions and daily limit: 0.12 a tick for the one taught, 0.06 for the teacher, about the game's
  research rate). At the end of the stay they pay for the hours (all, half for half, none for less: then it fails), the
  young one handing it over; the letter says the skill's levels from and to. Dead or taken prisoner, it fails.
- **Q4, a piece for a wedding** (`HappeningWorker_MissionWeddingPiece`). Someone of theirs is to be married in 6 to 9
  days, and they ask for one piece the colony can make now: clothes of their own age (`HomeQuests2.PieceOptions`: a tribe's
  headdress; Medieval 2's dame dress, the settlers' great dress, the fairycore dresses, a robe, a cape, Royalty's formal
  shirt or corset; the modern formal shirt, formal vest, corset, button-down shirt or vest; Royalty's prestige robe and
  formal wear for the Empire and spacers; each by name, only where loaded, only with the research done), a small work of
  art when it can sculpt (`ThingRole.SmallArt`, every mod's), or furniture for the couple's home (a double bedroll for a
  tribe, a double bed, the Empire's royal bed) packed up for carrying. Good quality or better (the game's own), not
  forbidden. The quest's progress shows whether one is ready; on the day their people come for the best of them
  (`Couriers.CollectThings`) and pay half as much again as it is worth at good quality and the quest's own sum on top.
  None ready on the day, it fails. The words say only what they wrote: who is marrying and where.
- **Q6, a sick animal tended** (`HappeningWorker_MissionSickAnimal`). One of their own animals (a pack animal their
  caravans use on this land, else a farm animal fine here now, every mod's) comes with the game's animal flu, its plague
  (only when the colony's doctor has Medicine 6, one time in four), or underfed from the road. Their drover walks it in
  and hands it over at the gate; it is the colony's to tend (its doctors tend it as any of the colony's animals, its
  handlers feed it). Well again (no illness, not underfed, nothing waiting for a doctor), their drover comes for it within
  the day and pays (`Couriers.Fetch`); still sick when the days are up (8 to 12), they take it as it is for half. Dead or
  no longer the colony's, it fails; bonded to someone of the colony, they leave it there and pay nothing (as round 1's
  animal).
- **Q8, guard their camp for a night** (`HappeningWorker_MissionCampGuard`). Three or four of their people, with a pack
  animal where their caravans use one, come in the late afternoon and camp at the edge of the land at least 30 cells
  out, which way in the terms, by a campfire of theirs (gone with them). They eat what they carry; after ten all but
  their leader lie down by the fire, the leader keeping watch. One roll at the camp's start, within the shared harm
  budget (`HarmKinds.CampNight`, system "quests", off with the world's battles; 0.35 at its base, its scale and pass
  making it rarer), decides whether something comes between ten and three: raiders of a people at war with both (the
  game's own fighters, a quarter of the threat points, one to three, the game's assault; three times in five where
  predators could come too) or the land's own predators gone manhunter. Everyone at the camp is woken and the colony gets a threat letter. At
  dawn, with nothing hostile still about the camp, they pack up and go, leaving the pay at their camp (a quarter more
  for a night fought through). One of theirs dead (or taken) in the night, it fails at once.
- **Q11, seed kept cold** (`HappeningWorker_MissionSeedGrain`, offered in autumn and winter and only when the colony has a
  room at freezing or colder now). 50 to 75 of a crop of their age that rots (`ThingRole.Produce`, every mod's), their
  seed for the sowing in 10 to 14 days. Their carts set it down at the gate; the colony carries it into its cold store
  (a cold room, an ice house or a freezer in the words, by the colony's age) within six hours and forbids it there. Every
  hour after those six, the temperature where it lies is read: more than 12 hours warmer than freezing in all, any of it
  used (put with the colony's own of the crop, the stack it went into counts while it holds as much), rotten, or gone, it
  is no good as seed and the colony may keep what is left. At the sowing one of the colony's haulers carries it out to a
  free place by where traders leave goods (visitors keep out of cold stores: `Visitors/KeepOut.cs`), it is forbidden again,
  and their carts come for it and pay. Not round 1's "store to keep": that one counts goods in the stockpiles.
- **Q12, their book copied** (`HappeningWorker_MissionBookCopy`, a hosted guest). Their scholar brings a book of theirs
  (their stories for a tribe, their learning, a technical manual for the modern) and stays 3 to 4 days. The copy takes 10
  to 16 hours of work at a research bench: a job of its own (`JobDriver_HomeQuestCopy`, the game's look of research and
  its learning, 0.1 Intellectual a tick) given by a work giver under research work, before the research
  (`WorkGiver_HomeQuestCopy`), so whoever does research copies. Done, the scholar pays and the colony keeps the copy: a
  book of the game's own (a novel, a textbook or a schematic), its quality from the copier's Intellectual, written by the
  scholar, set down by the bench. Half done when the scholar leaves, half the pay and no copy; less, it fails.
- **Q13, musicians for a night** (`HappeningWorker_MissionMusicians`, hosted guests; needs a gathering spot). Two or three
  of their musicians come in the afternoon. From six the colony throws the game's own party (`GatheringDefOf.Party`, its
  own letter, its own joining and moods), and they play at it (`JobDriver_HomeQuestPlay`): on the colony's own instrument
  near the party (the game's own or a mod's, the game's own playing) where there's one for them, else on their own,
  drums for a tribe and harps for the rest (the sound of Ideology's drum or Royalty's harp where those are loaded, and the
  notes over them). No party possible by ten, they play for whoever comes. They eat at the colony's table, sleep in its
  beds (half the goodwill if one had none), and leave in the morning paying for their keep.
- **Pace.** Each takes 0.3 of the missions' one draw, round 1's own share (2.1 for the seven): `MissionPool` still scales
  every mission to weigh 6.8 together, so missions as a whole come no oftener than before; one mission at a time; the
  same quest not again for 75 days. Their kinds are their own (the old delivery mission "seed after a blight" keeps
  `seedgrain`; this one is `seedkept`).
- **Shared files, small.** `HomeQuests.IsOurs` takes round 2's kinds in (so round 1's tags and the dev actions cover
  them), the dev actions list the seven, and the harm budget has one more kind (`HarmKinds.CampNight`); nothing of the
  missions themselves changed, and no new saved field (each quest keeps its state in the mission's own fields).
- **Dev mode** (Debug actions, Rimfolk): round 1's "Quests at home: offer one now...", "accept the open one", "what it
  waits for comes now", "end the open one as..." (each quest's own: "train now", "make it now", "the day now", "well now",
  "attack now", "dawn now", "set down now", "evening now", "morning now", and every ending), "what the open one keeps (log)".

### Quests and storylines: the frame, the factor's goods, the beast and the children (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.262.0)

The player, 13 November 2026: "the next thing to include will be more quests, and quests that are storylines across
multiple quests"; the go, 16 November 2026: "go ahead with quests and storylines, make sure they are written in the more
clear style i mentioned earlier on", "and while quests that require you to go out of your base are interesting, i hardly
ever reach the stage where I can consistently go out of base and it's worth it, so keep these quests to a minimum",
"unless it's like within only very few tiles". The list and the eight rules are `docs/quests-proposals.md`; this is round
1's storyline frame with S1, S4 and S8; its single quests are "Quests at home, round 1" just above, on the same
missions framework. Everything here plays out on the colony's own map: people come to the colony, and nothing sends
colonists away.

- **A storyline** (`Storylines/Storylines.cs`, saved in `StoriesComponent.storylines`, a `StorylineBook`) is a run of
  missions told over weeks. Each part is a mission in the Quests tab (or a letter with the setting off), offered by an
  event of its own (`Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Storyline_*.xml`, a `StorylinePart` extension): titled "Part 2: The
  rival's offer", its description the storyline's name and part ("The factor's goods, part 2."), then its text, which
  opens with one or two plain sentences on what happened before, then its terms (who asks, what, by when, what the
  colony gets, what happens if it fails). The first part is drawn by the storyteller like any Rimfolk event (base chance
  0.4, the story direction's levers apply; the beast's leans to "beasts"); the later ones have no chance of their own and
  are fired by the storyline when they're due, never while another mission is open, a question waits or a fight is on
  (tried again every few hours; after 20 days of waiting it fades with a plain ending).
- **When a part ends** (`Missions.Finish` tells `Storylines.MissionEnded`: done, failed, declined or let expire, its
  people broken with the colony, or the answer of a card inside it), the storyline's own rules (`StorylineMath.Next`, pure,
  tested) pick the next part and how long until it comes (one to six days for most, a season for the beast that comes
  back, two to four seasons for the eldest child grown), or the ending. A long wait is quiet: it doesn't hold another
  storyline back. Every part and outcome leads somewhere.
- **A card inside a part** (`HappeningWorker_StorylineCard`): an event letter with answers, asked while the part runs
  (the rival at the gate; the children's grown-up at the end of their stay; the eldest asking to join). Each answer
  shows what it will do (`DilemmaEffect_StorylineChoice`: silver, goodwill, who joins; and the game's own carrying where
  goods are carried out), and the part plays the answer out on the map before it ends.
- **Endings** (`Defs/StorylineDefs/Rimfolk_Storylines.xml`, a `StorylineDef` each): a line in the chronicle for every
  ending, and a letter of its own for those that play out at their own time (the factor coming for her crates, her
  guards, the beast gone for good, the people who asked turned against the colony); the rest were told by the part that
  led to them. Their people gone, destroyed or at war (`StorylineMath.GiverGone`): a plain ending at once, never stuck.
- **The World page** (the region window's Neighbours page, "Storylines" under the missions, `StorylinePanel.cs`): each
  storyline running, and each ended in the last fortnight, with its parts so far ("Part 1: Keep the factor's crates: all
  the crates kept, sealed and dry"), what is on its way as the colony knows it, or how it ended. Click opens the part's
  quest.
- **Pace** (`StorylineMath.CanStart`): one at a time; a second only once the first has run a season (15 days); two at
  most; the same storyline not again for 60 days after it ended.

**S1, the factor's goods** (`Storylines/StorylineFactor.cs`). A factor of a trading people (the road league and any people
of the traders' calling first, else the brokers or any people at peace whose traders come with caravans) asks the colony
to keep five to eight sealed crates until the end of the season, for an eighth of their worth (40 silver at least). Taken
on, she comes with two porters (a lander's pods for a people of the spacer age) and the crates, the road league's sealed
crates with goods of her people's age (`PeopleTrust`), are set down by the stores, with a trust record of their own so
opening, selling and burning are noted as they happen. A crate under the open sky in rain or snow is wet (told at its
first hour and halfway), and after 12 hours its goods are spoiled. After eight to ten days her clerk walks in and counts
them where they stand. Part 1 ends **kept** (every crate there, sealed and dry) or **lost**.
- Kept: two to five days later, **part 2, the rival's offer**: a trader of another trading people (else another people,
  else another house of hers) asks to meet at the gate. Taken on, the rival walks in and the card asks: **sell** (1.3
  times their worth, paid into the colony's hands, and the crates carried out to the rival), **refuse**, or **refuse and
  tell her** (her people +8, the rival's -5). Not met, or refused: three to six days later she comes with porters, the
  crates are carried out to her, she pays the fee (less what went missing since the count) and comes by once a season for
  a year with a share of her trade (7 % of the crates' worth a season, 10 % when the colony told her; at least 30), her
  people +8 (+12 told). Sold: she finds out seven times in ten (**part 3, pay the factor**: their whole worth within 8
  days, collected from the stockpiles by her people; paid, the matter is settled and her people trust the colony less;
  not paid, three of her guards come to the gate with her word, -40, and no traders of her people for a year); else she
  comes, finds them gone and believes they were stolen (no fee, -5).
- Lost: a day or two later, **part 2, pay for the lost crates**: what they were worth, within 10 days. Paid, her people
  collect the silver and the crates that are left; not paid, they take what is left, -15, and no traders for a year (the
  game's caravans of her people held back, `Patch_StorylineNoTrade`).
- The league's own crates in trust wait while hers are kept (`FactorRules.CratesHeld`). Her people gone or at war: nobody
  will come for the crates, so the colony opens them.

**S4, the beast coming down the valley** (`Storylines/StorylineBeast.cs`). A hunting people (the Lantern Wardens and any
of the hunters' calling first, else a people of the tribal or medieval age, else any at peace) sends a runner or a radio
call: a huge beast is coming down the valley. The beast is one of the region's legends (`LegendWorker.Kinds`: the biggest
animals loaded that could live here, from every mod enabled, never a Pokémon), the strongest whose combat power fits
85 % of the threat the storyteller would send now, else the weakest (`StorylineMath.BeastPick`); named from the legends'
pool, old, scarred and legendary like them. It starts only with fights possible and no region legend running.
- **Part 1, get ready**: within six to eight days, build at least three to six traps (by the colony's size) or 24 to 60
  lengths of wall or fence from now, and keep three in four of the colony's animals in a pen or a room. Both: ready
  (+10); one: partly (+5); neither: unready. Declined: the hunters turn it away themselves.
- **Part 2, look at its kill** (two to four days later): a wild animal of the land bitten to death at the edge of the
  map, with blood and a line of tracks to it, there as soon as the hunters speak of it. Someone of the colony who walks
  within six cells of it within two days has found it (the beast will come from that side); else missed.
- **Part 3, the beast comes** (one to three days later; a fight, so only with battles possible and nothing else on): it
  comes within a day of the colony taking it on, enraged (the game's manhunter), from the side of its tracks when they
  were found. With goodwill 25 or more, two to four hunters of theirs come with it on the game's own assist-the-colony
  duty (three when the colony got ready, four for a friend at 75). Below 35 % of its health it turns and flees (the
  game's panic flee); still here a day and a half after it came, it goes off on its own; down at the end of that time,
  it dies of its wounds. Killed (or tamed): the colony keeps the body and a trophy (its horns or tusks, else a part of its
  hide), +15 (+20 with their hunters beside it). Driven off or gone: it comes back next season (13 to 17 days, a quiet
  wait), at most twice, then it stays away. Declined: the hunters turn it away.

**S8, the children from the burned village** (`Storylines/StorylineChildren.cs`; needs Biotech, for the children). A
small village of a people at peace burned down (never one of their towns on the world map), and one of its grown-ups
brings two to four of its children (the eldest 12.4 to 12.9 years old) and asks for shelter.
- **Part 1, shelter them**: they come within a day and stay three or four days as every hosting mission's guests
  (`HappeningWorker_MissionHost`, `Hosting`): a bed or sleeping spot each and meals from the stores, their own packs when
  there's nothing; each day counted fed and sheltered or short, and told. Then the grown-up asks (the card): **take them
  in** (each child joins the colony as a colonist, +10; the colony is the family, so nothing more is tied to it), **find
  them a home with neighbours** (another people at peace, else another town of their own: two of theirs come to the gate
  within a day and the children go with them, joined to that people; +15, the neighbours +5; the default), or **send them
  on with food** (three meals each carried out to the grown-up, +4; they go a few hours later). Half or more of the
  children dead or taken prisoner in the colony's care ends it.
- **Part 2, the eldest comes back grown** (two to four seasons later, placed or sent on): at least 13, the game's adult
  age; to visit with a gift of thanks (about 150 to 350 silver's worth by the colony's wealth, in their own hands), to trade at the gate from a pack of
  their people's caravan goods, or to ask to join (the card: a colonist, or they go on). Placed, more often to join; sent
  on, more often to trade. If they can no longer come (dead, their people gone or at war), it ends quietly.

**The rules held.** At home: every part plays out on the colony's own map. Every age: the factor's means and goods, the
hunters' runner or radio and their weapons, the burned village or settlement and the trader's stock are their people's
age's. Harm only where the plan says (the beast's fight, shown, scaled to the colony, only with battles on and nothing
else on the map); the shared everyday harm budget is untouched. Plain words: titles say what the part is, descriptions
open with what happened before, then who asks, what, by when, for what, and what if it fails; no em dashes or
exclamation marks; spoken lines one sentence. Every mission rule holds: one at a time, the Quests tab or a letter, the
people's memory of a promise kept or broken.

Code map: `Storylines/StorylineMath.cs` (pure: kinds, parts, endings, pace, `Next`, the numbers; linked in
`Tools/Tests/Tests.csproj`), `Storylines.cs` (the def, the saved records, the book, the hourly step, endings, words,
`Patch_StorylineNoTrade`), `StorylineParts.cs` (the part extension, `StorylineKit` shared by both kinds of part worker,
`HappeningWorker_StorylinePart`, the card worker, `DilemmaEffect_StorylineChoice`), `StorylineFactor.cs`,
`StorylineBeast.cs`, `StorylineChildren.cs`, `StorylinePanel.cs`, `StorylinesDebug.cs`. Changed: `Missions/Missions.cs`
(`Finish` tells the storyline), `Missions/StoriesComponent.cs` (the book saved, the hourly step; an older save loads with
none), `World/Ledger/LedgerKeep.cs` (`KeepFor.Storyline`), `UI/Region/HereAndAwayView.cs` (the section),
`Peoples/Events/PeopleTrust.cs` (the league's crates wait), `Tools/DefValidator/Program.cs` (the storylines' names in
words). Defs: `Defs/StorylineDefs/Rimfolk_Storylines.xml`, `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Storyline_Factor.xml`, `_Beast.xml`,
`_Children.xml`; Keyed `Rimfolk_Storylines.xml`. Saved: the storylines (two running at most, ended ones 60 days) with
their parts, flags, people and the crates' hours in the rain, and what an ending leaves for a year (`Tools/save_estimate.py`).
Dev mode (Debug actions, Rimfolk): "Storylines: start the factor's goods now", "... the beast coming down the valley
now", "... the children from the burned village now", "Storylines: end the current part with..." (the branch only),
"Storylines: the next part (or ending) due now", "Storylines: what stands (log)". Tests: `Tools/Tests/StorylineTests.cs`.

### Storylines, round 2: the sickness, the strayed herd, the pilgrims' relic and two towns' quarrel (the player's "great, do some more", 16 November 2026; released 0.264.0)

After round 1 the player said "great, do some more" (16 November 2026), with the go's words still binding: "make sure they
are written in the more clear style i mentioned earlier on", and away from home only "within only very few tiles". Round
2's storylines of `docs/quests-proposals.md` (S2, S3, S5, S7), on the frame above; its single quests are their own entry.
Everything plays out on the colony's own map but one optional part of S5, and only when the place is within three tiles.

**Each storyline's rules a class of its own.** The frame's shared switches (the kinds, parts, endings, what follows a part,
the endings with a letter) moved out of `StorylineMath` into one pure class per storyline (`Storylines/Flows/`,
`StorylineFlow`: `FactorFlow`, `BeastFlow` and `ChildrenFlow` unchanged in what they say, then `SicknessFlow`, `HerdFlow`,
`RelicFlow`, `QuarrelFlow`, each with its own numbers), found by the frame by reflection (`StorylineFlows`, by their number
in the plan); `StorylineMath`'s static calls answer from them, so nothing that read them changed. The game side likewise:
each storyline's `StorylineRules` (now with its `Kind`) is found by the frame (`GenTypes.AllSubclassesNonAbstract`), and
gained `After` (what an ending leaves behind, by its kind: the relic at the shrine) and `DebugEnded` (what the dev menu
sets for a branch). The dev menu's outcomes come from the flows. A later storyline adds a flow, a rules class and its defs,
and touches nothing shared. Parts whose people stay at the colony share `HappeningWorker_StorylineHost`
(`StorylineHost.cs`): the hosting mission's guests (`Hosting`: the colony's table and beds), each day counted fed and
housed or short and told.

**S2, the sickness in the next town** (`Storylines/StorylineSickness.cs`). A town of a people at peace with a town near
(the hospitaller order first) has a sickness: the game's own flu or plague, never one made up; the plague four times in ten
for the tribal and medieval peoples, three in twenty for the industrial, never the spacer age, likelier in a plague year
among the region's world events (`SicknessFlow.Illness`). The mod pool was checked (`docs/player-mods`): the enabled mods'
human illnesses (Alpha Biomes' spore allergies, gangrene, parasites and viral abasia; A RimWorld of Magic's mana sickness)
belong to their biomes or their magic, not to a town's sickness passed from one person to another, so none is used.
- **Part 1, medicine for the town**: six to fourteen medicine of any kind, by the colony's size, in its stockpiles within six
  to eight days; their carts collect it within half a day of it being ready (`Couriers.CollectGoals`) and pay half again
  over its worth. Half or more by the date: they take it at its plain worth; less: none, and it ends.
- **Part 2, the sick in the colony's beds** (two to five days later): three to six of their sick come within a day, the
  illness well along (severity about a quarter, their immunity a third or more), and are taken in as the colony's guests,
  each walked to a patient's bed: the game's own care for a guest, its doctors tending them and feeding them in bed. Each
  who is well goes home, told; each death is told. Settled when all are well or dead, or after nine days (anyone still in
  bed stays until they can walk, as any guest). **Catching it**: the game's tending (`Health/HealthPatches.cs`) reaches
  `SicknessRules.Tended`: the physician's chance (`HarmFourMath.PhysicianChance`, a serious illness: gloves and masks in the
  industrial age and after, a sterile room and the quarantine or sick-bay decree lower it), through the shared harm budget
  (`Harm.Roll`, the physician's kind) and the illness budget (`IllnessBudget.Allows`, and `Owe` when it comes), shown a day
  or two later with the physician's own message and line (`HarmFour.Wait`); the everyday rule (`Catching.Tended`) leaves
  the town's sick to it. One of them taken prisoner: harmed.
- **Part 3, all recovered: a healer teaches** (three to eight days later): the order's healer (medicine 12 to 15) stays five
  or six days as a hosting guest, and each day between 8 and 15 o'clock the colony's best doctor works at their side for
  two and a half to three and a half hours (the play-out's lesson, `DilemmaEffect_Lesson`: 150 to 320 experience an hour by
  how far the healer leads, at the game's own pace); with answers not played out, the doctor learns as much by the day.
  A lesson on half the days or more: taught. Declined: the order sends medicine in thanks a few days later.
- **Part 3, some died: their families** (a day or two later): one of the family for each of the dead (two to five) come to
  the gate, and a card asks: **hand the bodies over** (each carries one home off the map, the game's own carrying: the
  default) or **bury them here** (graves laid out beyond the gate as frames for the colony to dig, `PlayBurial.Plot`; they
  take the strangers' bodies, the colony's haulers carry them in, the families wait by them about a day; not done in time,
  they take them home after all). Already in the colony's graves: they visit them. The bodies gone: nothing to take home.

**S3, the strayed herd** (`Storylines/StorylineHerd.cs`). A herding people (the herding folk first, else a tribal or
medieval people, else any at peace). Only asked in summer or autumn (or where the year has no seasons), so the keeping is a
winter. The herd's kind: any herd animal the game or an enabled mod adds that roams (so a pen holds it), of a farm's kind
(milk, wool or farm stock), calm enough (wildness 0.6 at most), no predator, insect, dryad or Pokémon, able to live outside
here now; the people's age's own animals (`HerdFlow.Kinds`: muffalo, goats, yaks, dromedaries, muskoxen, Megafauna's
aurochs and Alpha Animals' thunderox and mouflon for the tribal; sheep, goats, cows, yaks and Vanilla Animals Expanded's
camels for the medieval; cows, sheep, alpacas, goats and yaks later) four times likelier, the land's own twice.
- **Part 1, pen the strays**: five to nine head, there at the edge of the map as soon as the herders' word comes. Taken on,
  they are the colony's animals for three or four days (the game's own pen animals: its handlers rope them into a pen;
  outside one they may roam off the map; the land's predators may take them as any animal); turned down, they wander off.
  Then the herders come to the gate and count: every one in a pen or a barn, penned (+8); half or more still here, most
  (+4); fewer, lost (and it ends, -14 in all). Each animal is led out to them (`Rimfolk_Storyline_LedOut`, a walk that crosses
  fences and gates as a roped animal does, while it is still the colony's so its doors open), then all go home together.
- **Part 2, keep part of the herd** (two to four days later): three to five of the herd, until spring (10 to 32 days; a
  season where the year has none), brought onto the colony's land and the colony's to pen and feed (grazing, hay or kibble:
  the quest shows the hay and kibble in store against what they eat, `SimplifiedPastureNutritionSimulator`, and every three
  days in winter a word when it won't last). At the end: kept (every one alive and here), or some died.
- **Part 3, the herders in spring** (a day or two later): kept, they lead them home and leave one or two young animals of
  the herd with the colony (real animals, the colony's); some died, a card: **pay for the dead** (their worth, the silver
  carried out to the herders), **buy the ones left** (nine tenths of their worth; they stay the colony's), or **refuse**
  (the default; -23 in all). Not answered: they take the herd home anyway, and leave nothing.

**S5, the pilgrims' relic** (`Storylines/StorylineRelic.cs`). Pilgrims of a faith (the pilgrim fellowship first, else any
people at peace) with a relic, Rimfolk's own (`Rimfolk_PilgrimRelic`, a small carved reliquary; `Tools/make_quest_items.py`).
- **Part 1, shelter the pilgrims** (the card inside it): their keeper and two or three more stay two or three days as
  hosting guests; the keeper sets the relic down where they sleep. The thief is one of them half the time, else a
  traveller who comes to their fire on the evening before. On their second night, in the small hours, the thief (an outlaw
  now: one of the region's raiding peoples, so the colony may stop them) takes the relic and runs for the edge of the map
  with it (the game's own carrying off, at a jog); a letter says so. Caught (downed, or the colony's prisoner): a card,
  **hand them over** to the pilgrims (they take the thief with them; the default), **keep them as the colony's prisoner**,
  or **let them go**; the pilgrims' goodwill by the judgement and whether the thief was one of their own. Killed with it, or
  gone without it: the relic is back too. The keeper takes it again, and they rest out their stay. Off the map with it:
  escaped (-8). Still running after a day: they slip away.
- **Part 2, after the thief** (escaped; a day or two later). The pilgrims blame the colony. **Where a place for the thief's
  camp can be found within three tiles** (`TileFinder.TryFindNewSiteTile`, one to three), it is there for eight days: the
  game's own bandit camp of the thief's people (six tenths of the threat now), the thief and the relic inside when the
  colony's caravan gets there (`Patch_StorylineRelicCamp`); recovered once the relic is on the colony's map (a caravan on
  its way home with it has three days more). This is the storylines' one away part, optional, and the only quest of round 2
  that sends anyone from home. **Otherwise** the pilgrims go after the thief themselves and ask for food for the road (four
  meals each, collected from the stockpiles); they send word three to five days later, finding the thief seven times in ten
  with the food, about one in three without.
- **Part 3, the relic at the shrine** (two to five days after it is back): they ask to leave it at the colony's shrine for a
  year (`Shrines.Is`: an altar, a shrine, a ritual focus or a work of art; with none, the colony has three days to put one
  up). The keeper sets it down beside it. For the year (`StorylineAfter` "relic"): once a season two or three pilgrims come
  to see it and leave an offering (40 to 90 silver by the colony's wealth); then the keeper comes and carries it home, with
  thanks (+10). The relic gone meanwhile: the pilgrims who come find it gone (-15).

**S7, two towns' quarrel** (`Storylines/StorylineQuarrel.cs`). Two peoples at peace with the colony and at odds with each
other (at war, or their goodwill toward each other below nothing, and the game lets it change); those at war likelier.
- **Part 1, the truce** (built on the witness mission, at home): their envoys come to the gate within a day, and someone of
  the colony must spend two hours with both (anyone grown within eight cells of the two; the colony's best speaker goes out
  to them, the play-out's visit). Made: their goodwill toward each other rises to peace (at least 10, the game's own
  relations between peoples, shown on the World page), +6 from each, the witness the witness mission's memory. Not within a
  day: they go home without it. Two peoples at war with each other meet under a ceasefire (their goodwill toward each other
  at nothing while their envoys are at the colony, or they would fight at the gate; back where it was if no truce is made).
- **Part 2, the pledge** (two to four days later): someone of the first people (16 to 28) stays four to six days as a
  hosting guest. Kept (every day fed and housed, +8), poorly (some days short, +2), or harmed (dead or taken prisoner: the first
  blame the colony, -26 in all, and their goodwill toward the other falls 20). Declined: the pledge stays with another town, and
  the story goes on.
- **Part 3, the fighters** (three to eight days later; only with battles on): three to six fighters of the second people
  (by the threat now, about 120 points each), who don't hold with the truce, come onto the colony's land and rest at its
  edge; the card asks: **let them pass** (the default: they cross as the game's travellers do, and a day or two later the
  two peoples are at war, their goodwill toward each other -80), **warn the first** (they cross, the strike fails; the
  first's goodwill toward the other falls 30, the first +12, the second -10), or **stop them at the gate** (they wait there
  two hours and turn back, the peace holding, +10 and -5; or they force their way in, 15 % plus 8 % for each of them over
  the colony's people able to fight, 5 % to 50 %: cast out by their own people as outlaws, a fight at the gate, shown;
  fought off, +12 and -8). All with the reasons of `Rimfolk_GoodwillReasons` (the peoples' relations change by the game's
  `TryAffectGoodwillWith` between them, war at -75, which the World page's web of peoples and their page show).

**The rules held.** At home, but S5's one part within three tiles. Every age: the illness by the people's age, the herd by
their age and the mod pool, the fighters their people's own. Harm only where the plan says: the illness caught at the
physician's rate through both budgets, the land's predators and roaming as the game has them, the thief's chase and the
fight at the gate (only when they force it), each shown. Plain words, spoken lines one sentence. One mission at a time.

Code map: `Storylines/Flows/` (pure: `StorylineFlow` and `StorylineFlows`; `RoundOneFlows.cs`; `SicknessFlow.cs`,
`HerdFlow.cs`, `RelicFlow.cs`, `QuarrelFlow.cs`; linked whole in `Tools/Tests/Tests.csproj`), `StorylineHost.cs`,
`StorylineSickness.cs`, `StorylineHerd.cs`, `StorylineRelic.cs` (with `Patch_StorylineRelicCamp`), `StorylineQuarrel.cs`.
Changed: `StorylineMath.cs` (the switches now ask the flows), `Storylines.cs` (rules found by kind, `After` and
`DebugEnded`, `Storyline.site`, `StorylineAfter.thing`), `StorylinesDebug.cs`, the three round-1 rules (their `Kind`),
`Health/HealthPatches.cs` (the tending reaches the sickness first). Defs: `Defs/StorylineDefs/Rimfolk_Storylines_Round2.xml`,
`Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Storyline_Sickness.xml`, `_Herd.xml`, `_Relic.xml`, `_Quarrel.xml`,
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_Storylines_Misc.xml` (the led-out job, the relic); Keyed `Rimfolk_Storylines2.xml`; the relic's picture.
Saved: nothing new collected (the sick, the herd, the pilgrims and the fighters in the storyline's people; the graves laid
out in its list of marks; the thief's camp's id and the relic at the shrine as single values). Dev mode: "Storylines: start
the sickness in the next town now", "... the strayed herd now", "... the pilgrims' relic now", "... two towns' quarrel
now", "Storylines: the pilgrims' relic stolen tonight, now", and the frame's. Tests: `Tools/Tests/StorylineTests2.cs`
(and every storyline's shape in `StorylineTests.cs`).

### Storylines, round 3, and the one away quest: a dream of the gods, raiders settling nearby, the town's well, the vault's sealed case, the lost founder's grave and a cache in old ruins (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Quests round 3 sounds great"; released 0.267.0)

Round 3 of `docs/quests-proposals.md`: the storylines S6, S9, S10, S11 and S12 on the frame above, and Q14, the one single
quest that sends the colony's people out. The go's words still bind ("make sure they are written in the more clear style",
away only "within only very few tiles"). Everything plays out on the colony's own map but two optional parts: S9's strike
on a raiders' camp and Q14's ruins, each only when the place is within three tiles. Each storyline adds its own flow
(`Storylines/Flows/`), its own rules and parts (`Storylines/Storyline*.cs`) and its own defs; what the round's parts share
is `Storylines/StorylineRound3.cs`: an area marked on the map (`IStorylineArea`, drawn as the keepsake's search area is,
`StorylineAreaOverlay`), a search of it spot by spot (`IStorylineSearch`: right-click inside it with a colonist, an hour a
look, `JobDriver_StorylineSearch`), goods collected by the people's carts, and the dev actions (a start for each, and "what
the open part waits for comes now", `IStorylineDebugNow`). Two small shared changes: a mission may be **the colony's own**
(`HappeningWorker_Mission.OfTheColony`: nobody of the world asked it, so no people must stay at peace with the colony for it
to go on; `Missions.Accept` and `Missions.Tick` read it), for the dream and the raiders' price; and the harm budget has a
new kind, `HarmKinds.StoryFight` (system "quests", off with the world's battles), for a fight a storyline brings.

**S6, a dream of the gods** (`Storylines/StorylineDream.cs`). The colony's own faith, and the gods unseen (CLAUDE.md): the
whole of it is the dreamer's own account, and the god is named only by the name the colony knows it by (`Worship.Called`).
The dreamer is one of the colony's own, devout and no scoffer, whose god the colony knows by name and takes offerings (the
priest three times likelier). Its parts are the colony's own missions.
- **Part 1, the place in the dream**: the dreamer told it at breakfast (their journal, and the colony's book of the gods as
  a dream told, `GodLore.Dreamt`): a place on the colony's land, well out from its middle (an area of radius 4 marked on the
  map), and a place for the god there. Within six to nine days the colony builds an altar, a shrine or a work of art inside
  it (`Shrines.Is`, any age's: a ritual focus, art, a nature shrine, anything called an altar or a shrine); once one stands
  there, the worship's own dedication gives it to the god (`Shrines.Ask`: someone walks over and says the words). Given:
  built. Nothing given there in time: not built, and the dreamer is troubled.
- **Part 2, the watch** (a day to three later): someone of the colony at the new place for two hours of the night (nine to
  four), within three nights; the dreamer walks out each night to keep it (the play-out's visit), and anyone of the colony
  within five cells counts. Partway through it, a light comes over the place for a short while: the god's own sign
  (`Worship.Sign`, the presence's moment, else a glow and a line in the news), named after it only as the colony may name
  it ("some say"), and kept in the colony's book through those who saw it. No watch kept: nothing is seen, and the dream
  comes back all the same.
- **Part 3, the offering** (two to five days later): the dream comes back (told again, the book's dream) and asks for an
  offering of a kind the god likes (`GodWorshipDef.Likes`) at the place within three days: the worship's own demand of a
  dream (a `DemandRecord` and a planned offering, the dreamer carrying it first). Set down there: given, and the colony's
  book keeps it as the dreamer believes it ("{GOD} asked me in my dreams for a shrine and an offering, and we gave both",
  `GodLore.Believes`), the dreamer honoured (a mood, +5, eight days). Refused, or not brought: the dreamer troubled for a
  while (-4, six days). What the god does with it is the worship's own, never told here; no favour, want or rule is shown.
- The dreamer dead or gone from the colony: it ends plainly.

**S9, raiders settling nearby** (`Storylines/StorylineRaiders.cs`). A people at peace with a town near the colony warns it;
the raiders are a people at war with it that can raid and hold a camp, nearest the neighbours' age, and their camp is the
region's kind by their age (`RaidersCamps.KindWord`: a war camp, a brigands' hold, a bandit camp, a raider base). Never
while one of the region's own raiders' camps stands near the home; only with battles on.
- **Part 1, defences**: within five to seven days, three to six traps or turrets, or 24 to 60 lengths of wall, fence or
  barricade, by the colony's size (counted from the day it agreed). Ready (either goal), partly (half of either), unready.
  Ready, the colony's watch sees the raiders coming: a letter a few hours before they come.
- **Part 2, the raid that tests the colony** (two to five days later): taken on, a small raid comes within one to three days
  (half the threat the storyteller would send now, the game's own raid with Rimfolk's letter above its own,
  `Raids.Send`), within the shared harm budget (`HarmKinds.StoryFight`, 85 in a hundred; held back, they don't come:
  quiet). Beaten off (half of them or more fell, or more of them than of the colony's people): repelled; else overrun.
  Turned down, the colony keeps out of it and the raiders turn to the neighbours: no fight comes unasked.
- **Part 3, the strike** (two to six days later): **within three tiles** (a place found for the camp, two to three tiles
  off), the camp is the game's own bandit camp of the raiders' people (six tenths of the threat now) on the world map for
  eight days, and the neighbours ask the colony to join them: when the colony's caravan is on the camp's map, two to four
  of the neighbours' fighters come in beside it and go after the raiders (the game's assist duty). Every fighter of the camp
  fallen: cleared. Not joined in time: the neighbours go alone (45 in a hundred). **Farther off**, the neighbours go and
  ask for food and medicine for their fighters (meals and medicine by how many go), collected by their carts within three
  days; word comes two to four days later, cleared 75 in a hundred with the colony's food and medicine, 45 without. Turned
  down: the neighbours alone clear it about a third of the time.
- **Endings**: the camp gone (the neighbours thank the colony, more when it joined in person); or **the raiders' price
  each season for a year** (a part of its own each season, a quiet wait between): paid (a colonist carries the silver out to
  the edge of the colony's land and leaves it, the region's camp's own errand; about half their raid's strength in silver),
  or refused (or the silver not there when it agrees), and a band of them comes for it a day or two later (the game's raid,
  within the harm budget). After the fourth season they move on.

**S10, the town's well ran dry** (`Storylines/StorylineWell.cs`). The Deepwell Union's town first (the drillers), else any
people with a town near the colony.
- **Part 1, water or food**: water where the colony keeps it (Dubs Bad Hygiene's bottled water, enabled in the player's
  list), else meals, by the colony's size, within four to six days; collected by their carts and paid a fifth over its
  worth; half or more by the date, its plain worth; less, none, and it ends.
- **Part 2, a hand lent** (two to five days later): the colony's best at Mining or Construction (6 or more; never one of the
  colony's last two hands). Their foreman comes to the gate within a day, and the colonist walks out with them to the edge
  of the map (`JobDriver_StorylineLentOut`) and is away four to six days: kept in the world as the game keeps lent
  colonists, no caravan of the colony's going anywhere. Then they walk home from the edge with a day's wage for each day and
  1,500 experience a day in the skill they were lent for (400 in the other). The new well found: the lent hand's chance (two
  in five at 6, nine in ten from 16). Kept at home by the colony for most of a day when the foreman comes: the foreman goes
  without them. A part that ends any other way, or their people gone, brings a colonist away home at once.
- **Endings**: found, the town grows and remembers the help (+15, a letter a day or two later); nobody lent, they find it
  themselves three times in ten; not found, **part 3, refugees**: two to four of the town's people on the road, taken in
  (they come to the gate and join the colony) or turned away (-8).

**S11, the vault's sealed case** (`Storylines/StorylineVault.cs`). The Sunken Vault first (the vaultfolk), else any spacer
people at peace.
- **Part 1, power cells** (the vault's own power cells mission's ask): six to twelve components by the colony's size within
  six to nine days, collected by its runners and paid two fifths over their worth (half or more: their plain worth); the
  parts keep a declining people's age, as the vault's own mission's do (`VaultSupply.Noted`).
- **Part 2, the engineer** (two to six days later): one of their engineers stays four to six days as a hosting guest, and
  each day from eight in the morning takes a component from the colony's stores and works about four hours at one of the
  colony's work benches (a fabrication bench, a machining table, a smithy, a tailoring bench, a crafting spot: any age's),
  the game's smithing look and sound (`JobDriver_StorylineBenchWork`); no component in the stores, that day's work is lost.
  On leaving they pay for the components used (half again over their worth). Every day worked, or short; dead or taken
  prisoner, harmed.
- **Part 3, the sealed case** (two to six days later): their runner brings a sealed case (Rimfolk's own, a picture of its
  own) and sets it down by the colony's stores for five to seven days. Half a day later a card asks: **keep it sealed**
  (the default: their runner comes back for it at the end of the days, +16 in all, and the vault owes the colony a favour,
  the missions' deed big enough to be one), or **open it**: a sleeper of their people (joins the colony half the time, else
  leaves at once), a machine (the game's own mechanoid, by a third of the threat now, within the shared harm budget; held
  back, old goods instead), or old goods (by the colony's wealth and age). Opened, the vault hears of it when its runner
  comes (-15). The case lost: they hold it against the colony.

**S12, the lost founder's grave** (`Storylines/StorylineGrave.cs`). The Quiet Bell first (the keepers of the dead), else any
people at peace with a town near.
- **Part 1, the search**: their elders say one of their founders (a name of their people) lies on the colony's land; an
  area of radius 7 is marked well out from the colony's middle, and the colony searches it as the lost keepsake's (an hour
  a look, about three cells around). Found within four to six days: a grave marker (Rimfolk's own, the colony's) is set on
  it (+8). Not found: one of theirs comes, searches some hours and finds it. Something of the colony's built on the very spot
  first: built over, and they hold it against the colony (-20).
- **Part 2, the mourners** (three to six days later): three to five come to the grave early on the set morning, stay about
  ten hours and eat at the colony's table (beds don't matter for a day); fed when hungry: hosted (+10), else poorly. One of
  them dead or taken prisoner: harmed. The marker gone or built over: built over.
- **Endings**: kept, and for three years (`StorylineAfter` "grave", once a game year) two or three of theirs come to the
  grave for a few hours (+4 each time); the marker gone or built over when they come, they hold it against the colony and
  come no more. Turned away: refused (-12).

**Q14, a cache in old ruins** (`Missions/Workers_MissionHome5.cs`, `HomeQuests3Math.cs`). A neighbour's old map, by their
age (painted on a hide, drawn on parchment, a survey map, a data slate), shows a cache in ruins close by. Offered only when
a place is found within one to three tiles, and at half a quest at home's chance (0.15): with the thirteen at home, under one
single quest in ten sends anyone out (rule 2). Taken on, the ruins are the game's own item stash site, the cache (Rimfolk's
own old chest) and a few things worth half the reward among its things, set down inside the ruins by the game's map making
(and by `Patch_HomeQuestRuinsCache` if not). Six to ten days by the distance (three more for a caravan on its way home with
it). Brought home: their people come for it within half a day and pay (the quests at home's reward by their age and the
colony's wealth, a tribe in goods); what else lay there is the colony's. Destroyed, or not home in time: -6. No fight of its
own: the ruins hold the cache and the land's own animals.

**The rules held.** At home, but S9's strike and Q14's ruins, each only within three tiles and each optional. Every age: the
place for a god, the camp's kind, the water or meals, the bench, the old map, each its age's. The mod pool: Dubs Bad
Hygiene's water where the colony keeps it; the shrines, benches and fighters any mod's. Harm only where the plan says: the
raids and the machine through the shared budget, the strike the colony's own choice, each shown. The gods unseen: the dream
is the dreamer's, the god named only as the colony knows it, nothing of its mind. The colony is the family: the founder is a
people's founder, mourned by that people, with no line or house tied to it. Plain words, spoken lines one sentence each.

Code map: `Storylines/Flows/` (`DreamFlow.cs`, `RaidersFlow.cs`, `WellFlow.cs`, `VaultFlow.cs`, `GraveFlow.cs`; pure, linked

`StorylineWell.cs`, `StorylineVault.cs`, `StorylineGrave.cs`; `Missions/HomeQuests3Math.cs` (pure, linked),
`Missions/Workers_MissionHome5.cs`. Changed, small: `Missions/Workers_Missions.cs` and `Missions.cs` (`OfTheColony`),
`Missions/HomeQuests.cs` (`IsOurs`), `Missions/HomeQuestsDebug.cs`, `Harm/HarmBudgetMath.cs` (`HarmKinds.StoryFight`). Defs:
`Defs/StorylineDefs/Rimfolk_Storylines_Round3.xml`, `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Storyline_Dream.xml`, `_Raiders.xml`,
`_Well.xml`, `_Vault.xml`, `_Grave.xml`, `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Missions_Home3.xml`, `Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_Storylines3_Misc.xml`
(the case, the cache, the grave marker, three jobs, the dreamer's two moods); Keyed `Rimfolk_Storylines3.xml`,
`Rimfolk_Missions_Home3.xml`; pictures `Things/VaultCase.png`, `QuestCache.png`, `FounderGrave.png` (`Tools/make_quest_items.py`).
Saved: nothing new collected (the dreamer, the lent hand, the engineer and the mourners in the storyline's people; the god,
the place and the camp in its single values; the grave's yearly visits a `StorylineAfter`). Dev mode: "Storylines: start a
dream of the gods now", "... raiders settling nearby now", "... the town's well ran dry now", "... the vault's sealed case
now", "... the lost founder's grave now", "Storylines: what the open part waits for comes now", and "Quests at home: offer
one now..." for the cache. Tests: `Tools/Tests/StorylineTests3.cs`, `HomeQuests3Tests.cs` (and every storyline's shape in
`StorylineTests.cs`).

### The right-click's things, done by themselves (the player's request, 7 November 2026)

"I'm not really using the right click conversation options, so please integrate them to be done automatically by pawns
when there is a good moment, while still having the gameplay impact and limits in mind." The pure rules in
`Outsiders/OutsiderAutoMath.cs` (`OutsiderAutoTests`), the look in `Outsiders/OutsiderAuto.cs`.

- **The same way as the right-click.** A colonist who does one by themselves goes through `Outsiders.WhyNot` (the menu's
  own reasons: willing, the waits, patience, the thing's own conditions), never one `OutsiderTalk.Repeat` would answer
  with "you asked me that already", and the same jobs (`Outsiders.StartTalk` and `StartGift` with `byThemselves`), so the
  scene (`OutsiderTalk.Begin`: patience spent, the ask noted), the outcome (`Outsiders.Talked`) and the record
