  every deed `KinMemory.Name` gives a colonist goes in too, so one way names colonists. Read by `KinMemory.Friend` (the
  warmer of a deed's name and this), `KinMemory.AddTags` (`their:foe`, `their:foe:KIND`, `their:foeA`), the facts
  (`FOE`, `you:foe`, `you:remembered`; seven talk pieces), a notable's `OpinionOf` (the good as a deed, the wrongs
  1.5 a point off, 40 at most) and `Known`, and the trade: at -12 or less `FactionUtility.CanTradeWith` says no with the
  reason (`Patch_ColonistMemoryTrade`), so the option is greyed out and a caravan's negotiator is someone else. No raid
  of its own.

### Rimfolk's peoples

New peoples of peaceful callings the world lacked (the player's request, 7 November 2026; `docs/design/peoples.md`
has the whole design, the softness and the templates for release B). Release A: three peoples a new world is made with;
release B, peoples that arise during play, builds on them. `Defs/PeopleDefs/`, `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/`, the
pure rules in `PeoplesMath.cs` (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesTests.cs`, "peoples: ").

- **The peoples.** The road league (`Rimfolk_League`, industrial, outlander parent, calling `traders`), the hospitaller
  order (`Rimfolk_Order`, medieval, tribal parent, `healers`), the herding folk (`Rimfolk_Herders`, neolithic, tribal
  parent, `herders`). Each a FactionDef on the game's abstract parent with its own pawn kinds (gear by the game's tags,
  which the VE sets add to, a few required pieces, all dyed its colour), traders, names (its own rule packs), a fixed
  faith (Ideology: the game's memes, VE Memes' where loaded, a style), a xenotype share (Biotech, Alpha Genes),
  `colorSpectrum`, and an emblem and town icon drawn in code (`Tools/make_emblems.py`, preview
  `Tools/emblems_preview.png`). Listed once among a new world's peoples at the game's usual chances
  (`startingCountAtWorldCreation` 1), never required (`requiredCountAtGameStart` 0); never natural or permanent
  enemies, no sieges, raids a quarter to a half of another people's commonality, and only once the colony has turned
  them hostile. Few towns for the league (`settlementGenerationWeight` 0.4).
- **The template** (`PeopleExtension` on the FactionDef): the calling, the town's word, the notables' titles (head and a
  woman's, heir and a woman's, envoy, trader), the messengers' word, the caravan weight, the camp kinds it favours, the
  town plan, the town's goods and herd. `Peoples` reads it: `Of`, `CallingOf`, `Title`, `Courier`, `CaravanFactor`,
  `CampFactor`, `Preference`, `Fits`, `CanSend`, `TendsLodgers`, `CaravanCanCome`, `Make` (a people made now, the game's
  way, its town near a home and clear of the game's nearness rule: the dev tools). Nothing saved, no clock of its own
  (release B's book aside, below).
- **Words.** Notables titled by their ways (`NotableBook.TitleOf`, `RegionFaces.TitleOf`: waymaster, prior or prioress,
  camp elder; caravan master, cellarer, drover). Their messengers by their own word (`CourierWords.Noun`: road riders,
  postulants, riders). The tag `their:traders`, `their:healers` or `their:herders` (`PeoplesMath.Tags`) in the facts
  (`Facts.People`), the asks' tags, the events', the camps', the bubbles', the visitors', the messengers', the letters'
  and the world events'; their letters (`Rimfolk_Pool_NeighbourWrites`), their messengers' lines and nine pieces of talk
  in their own voices.
- **How often.** The game's trader caravans weigh each people's `caravanWeight` (`Patch_RiseFallCaravans`: the
  league's 3, the herders' 1.5). A camp kind a people favours comes from them four times as often (the league's
  market folk, salt caravans, far merchants and road wardens; the order's healers, herb-gatherers, pilgrims and
  penitents; the herders' drovers, shearers and catchers). A world event's people (`SituationFactionNeed.calling`) and
  an ask (`MissionPeople.prefers`) prefer a calling five times: by patch (`Patches/Rimfolk_Peoples.xml`), the drove
  roads and the great herds the herders, six road and trade events the league, a healer lent the order, fodder the
  herders; a caller's people (`HappeningSetting.prefers`): a thirsty herd, a sick herd and drovers on the road to a fair
  the herders.
- **Theirs only.** `MissionPeople.only` and `whileKind`: the order's medicine for the sickhouse in a plague year (a
  delivery, their carts at the gate) and the league's factor to see home (the traveller's escort); an ask only theirs
  takes no share of the missions' draw while no people of its calling is at peace (`MissionPool`). `HappeningSetting`
  `people` `calling:CALLING`: the order's hospitaller at the gate (free care for an ailment, medicine sent back, the
  doctor learning) and the league's outrider (the need `caravan`: bidden, the league's own trader caravan comes).
  `CampKindDef.calling`, `seasons`, `maxAnimals`: the herders' winter herd (fall and winter, up to twelve head and a dog,
  `CampLookMath.MaxHerd` 14).
- **Their towns.** `TownPlanDef` (`Defs/PeopleDefs/Rimfolk_TownPlans.xml`): rows of keys read into the kept-layout grid
  (`PeoplesMath.Grid`, the game's footprint rule `PeoplesMath.Footprint`) and placed by `TownLayouts.Place` from
  `Patch_TownLayoutSettlement` (`PeopleTowns.PlaceTown`, after a town the colony was), near the map's middle where at
  most 6% of its cells are bad ground; then the game's loot and the people's goods in the storehouse, the herd in the
  pens, the healroot in the garden, the notables and the game's settlement group under its defend-the-town lord
  (`TownLayouts.AtHome`). The power step stands down for it (`TownLayouts.NotePlaced`). Else the game's own base.
- **Elsewhere.** A sickhouse of the order sees to the colony's lodgers as medicine would (`SickHome`); the hand-over's
  peoples never borrow these peoples' kinds (`HandOverPeoples.Lend`). The Almanac's page *the road league, the
  hospitallers and the herders*.
- **Release B: peoples that arise during play** (`Peoples/Arising.cs`, `ArisingMath.cs` pure and tested in
  `Tools/Tests/ArisingTests.cs`, "new peoples: "; `ArisingWords.cs`, `ArisingBook.cs`, `ArisingDebug.cs`). Four causes
  read from what the world keeps: a fight's ruin within reach (`LedgerRuin.Fight`, from three days after the fall to
  sixty, two in five: `ArisingMath.Fated`, the same answer each time it is asked), three or four towns of two peoples or
  more at 62 or more within 18 tiles of the most prosperous and at peace with each other and the colony
  (`ArisingMath.LeagueOf`, a fifth of the looks), one the council sent away (`BanishRecord`, alive in the world and of no
  people, 15 to 300 days after, half of them), and with Ideology the end of a war of words (`Council_WS_HolyWar` in the
  world events' history, within 30 days, half of them). The template by the cause's age (`ArisingMath.Template`: the
  calling a cause may take nearest its age), made the game's way (`FactionGenerator.NewGeneratedFaction`, hidden while
  made, no leader until its faith is set: `Arising.Making` in `Patch_HandOverLeader`), its name from its cause, its
  colour the palette's farthest from the world's (`Faction.color`), its faith (survivors keep their old people's, a band
  its leader's, a league another league's, the splinter a reformed creed: `IdeoUtility.RandomizeNormalMemesForReforming`),
  goodwill by what happened (`ArisingMath.*Goodwill`, never past the game's -75 or 75), its town by `Arising.TryTownTile`
  (a few days off, clear of `RiseFallMath.ClearOfHomes`, on no land but its own peoples', `NewTowns.MakeTown`), the
  region's faces (`RegionFaces.Founded`) and the founding pace (`RiseFall.NoteFounded`), a letter
  (`Importance.Important`, the founding's means and rite), the history's `world:arose`, a line on the people's and the
  towns' cards. The one sent away leads the band (`Faction.leader`), rides with no one else's raid (`JoinArrivingRaid`) and
  doesn't ask at the gate to come home (`HappeningWorker_Prodigal`). Run by the
  region's day (`RegionBook.Daily`), one a day at most; the pace `ArisingMath.PaceAllows` (40 days between any two, 90
  between two of a cause, none before day 15, six standing), scaled by the setting `newPeoples` (0 to 200%). Saved: the
  records in `ArisingBook` (one per people, `ArisingMath.MaxRecords`). The Almanac's page *new peoples that arise*.
- **Release C: four more peoples** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesCTests.cs`, "peoples, release C: "). The pilgrim fellowship
  (`Rimfolk_Pilgrims`, medieval, tribal parent, calling `pilgrims`), the learned society (`Rimfolk_Scholars`, industrial,
  outlander parent, `scholars`), the spacer enclave (`Rimfolk_Enclave`, spacer, outlander parent, `brokers`), the river
  folk (`Rimfolk_RiverFolk`, medieval, tribal parent, `fishers`), on release A's template with three new fields:
  `ariseAges` (the ages a template arises in, wider than its own: `PeoplesMath.AgeSpan`), `byWater` (its towns by a
  river: `PeopleTowns.ToTheRivers` from `ArisingBook.StartedNewGame` moves a new world's landings to a river tile within
  twelve, a new people's town is looked for on one) and `fish` (Odyssey's fish of the map's own waters in the stores).
  Their plans (`Rimfolk_TownPlans_PeoplesC.xml`) and a new plan mark, `dock`: `PeopleTowns.Spot` looks wider for a place
  where most docks are water (`PeoplesMath.DockSpot`), `LayDocks` lays the game's bridge over water a bridge can stand
  in and planks on dry ground. Callers (`Peoples/PeoplesCallers.cs`): the pilgrims' night (`HappeningWorker_PilgrimShelter`:
  dusk, a band of three to five, each lodged by `VisitorServices.Lodge`, the morning a memo of the living events,
  `LivingEvents.Shelter`, with the blessing said, the colony's feeling, and one night in ten a cough caught through
  `Harm.Roll`/`Harm.Ail`), the society's copyist (`HappeningWorker_ScholarCopyist`: a book of the colony's age by
  `DilemmaEffect_Goods`, or a lesson), the river folk's catch (`HappeningWorker_RiverCatch`, the biome's fresh-water fish),
  the enclave's lander (`HappeningWorker_EnclaveLander`, an industrial or spacer colony: `DilemmaEffect_EnclaveLanding`
  drops the factor with the stock in its pack, the marshals and the beasts by drop pod, under the game's visitors' lord,
  as its visiting traders trade). Asks (`Rimfolk_Missions_PeoplesC.xml`): the hostel's food in a holy year
  (`whileKind` `faith`), the river folk's timber and net cloth. By patch (`Patches/Rimfolk_PeoplesC.xml`): nine world
  events prefer a calling, and five visitor events (`HappeningExtension.prefers`, read by their own workers through
  `Peoples.Weigh`). Release B's causes may take their ways (`ArisingMath.Leans`, `Lean`, `Wanted`; the cause's `lean`):
  survivors near a river (half of them, `SaltRiver`) river folk, a band led by a learned one (Intellectual 10)
  scholars, a league of the spacer age an enclave, faithful who broke away in an industrial or spacer world pilgrims; a
  lean with no river in reach is let go. Release B's pace and caps unchanged. The Almanac's page *pilgrims, scholars,
  the enclave and the river folk*. Fixed on the way: a caller of a calling (`HappeningSetting.people` `calling:`) could
  be a Hospitality guest of any people already on the map, standing in under that people's name.
- **Their gear, their kinds of people and their gifts** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesGearTests.cs`, "peoples' gear: ";
  docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name). No kind has `apparelColor`: each people's base kind dyes its
  signature pieces by name (`specificApparelRequirements` with an `apparelDef` and a `color`), a civilian kind picks its
  signature garment by `alternateTagChoices`, the rest comes from wider tags and money by role. Soldiers wear a common
  kit (`apparelRequired`), a religious habit is shared but not its cut or age, civilians vary. A mod's tags and pieces
  only with `MayRequire` on it, every name in `Tools/Tests/PeopleGear.txt`; medieval and tribal peoples off
  `IndustrialBasic` (Vanilla Apparel Expanded's modern clothes). `inventoryOptions` for what they carry, never on a
  trader. `xenotypeSet` a real mix of Biotech's, Vanilla Races Expanded's, Alpha Genes' and the xenotype mods' kinds of
  people, three in four or so baseliners. `PeopleKindExtension` (gifts: a class of A RimWorld of Magic by its trait's name,
  or a psylink, with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded a path by name) given by `Patch_PeopleGifts`, a postfix on the game's
  `GenerateNewPawnInternal` (fresh pawns only, the deeper game hooks on); `PeoplesGearMath` (one roll against the shares,
  never more than 60% of a kind, the psylink's levels, the class's setting). Pawns already in a game keep theirs.
- **Their stories, sayings and touchpoints** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesLoreTests.cs`, "peoples' lore: "; docs/design/
  peoples.md, the section of that name). A founding story in each faction's description (its middle paragraph), and
  `PeopleExtension.honours`, `fears`, `sayings` shown on the people's card (`PeopleLore`, a lines section in the card's
  story slot; a saying picked by the faction's id, so it reads the same). Their voices in the existing pools by
  `their:CALLING` (letters' condolences and warnings, messengers, `Rimfolk_VisitorLines`, `Rimfolk_Pool_OutsiderSays`),
  three talk pieces each, `Rimfolk_Pool_PlayDisputation`. Touchpoints, each only from a people of its calling:
  `HappeningWorker_OrderNurse` (a fever: the hospitaller goes from bed to bed by `VisitorServices.Dose` with
  `Rimfolk_OrderNursed`), `HappeningWorker_LongWalk` (a file of pilgrims at the graves, a walk together or food carried
  out), `Rimfolk_Evt_Disputation` (data only: an evening gathering with the fellow as guest), `HappeningWorker_EnclaveSalvage`
  and `DilemmaEffect_EnclaveSalvage` (salvage by drop pod at the trade spot, by `PeoplesLoreMath.SalvageGoods` of the
  colony's age; a runner on foot for a colony without radio), `HappeningWorker_RiverNets` (boatmen on the dry bank by the
  water), the league's camp `Rimfolk_Camp_LeagueWinter` (winter, trading, guards if asked, the Waystone Book) and the
  winter herd's young beast. A camp's gift (`CampGift`) may now be `young` (a young beast of the camp's own grazing kinds,
  the colony's, handed over at the gate on the farewell walk) and kept for a good stay (`maxTension`: no walk to the gate
  without it). Faiths gain a soft meme or structure each where thin, checked against the memes' exclusion tags. Arising
  names gain a third form carrying their ways. Nothing saved, no clock, nobody hurt.
- **Release D: the Lantern Wardens, the Quiet Bell, the Circuit of Tamers and the Wheel** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesDTests.cs`,
  "peoples, release D: "; docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name; the first four of `docs/design/peoples-next.md`).
  `Rimfolk_Wardens` (medieval, tribal parent, calling `hunters`), `Rimfolk_QuietBell` (medieval, tribal parent,
  `sextons`), `Rimfolk_Tamers` (industrial, outlander parent, `tamers`), `Rimfolk_Wheel` (industrial, outlander parent,
  `salvagers`), each arising in every age (`ariseAges` 0~3), drawn only from the player's active mods
  (`docs/player-mods/`). Every age: `Peoples.AgeOf` (an arisen people keeps the age of what it came from,
  `PeoplesDMath.PeopleAge`), `PeopleKindExtension.ageArms` (a kit's weapon tags for other ages and what it may cost,
  `AgeArms.Arm` as a pawn is made) and `PeopleGift.ages`. Callers (`Peoples/PeoplesD.cs`, `PeoplesD2.cs`): the Wardens'
  hunt on a legend, nemesis or alpha on the land (`HappeningWorker_WardensHunt`, `DilemmaEffect_WardensHunt`: the game's
  assault-things lord, the colony's shot on the game's hunt; the kill seen in `HappeningTracker.Notify_Killed`, the
  carcass skinned by `JobDriver_PeoplesWork` and its butchering split, `PeoplesD.Divide`; given up after two days, they
  walk home), the pelt-buyer, a lantern for one a beast took; the Bell at the enemy's dead (a subclass of the
  undertakers' worker, `DilemmaEffect_BellForTheDead`'s goodwill with the dead's peoples), its funeral at a fresh grave,
  the void's signs (Anomaly); the tamer's bout (`JobDriver_TamerBout` by the Fighting-type spar's rules, `HarmKinds.TamerBout`
  through `Harm.Roll`/`Injure`), eggs swapped or sold, a stray brought home; the Wheel's fixer (a subclass of the
  tinker's worker), its scrap-runners (`PlayCarry.Scrap`), a mechanoid wreck stripped half and half (`StripJob`). The hunt
  and the bout are visits of the happenings' tracker (`Visit` kinds `wardenHunt`, `tamerBout`). The Wheel's towns move
  (`WheelTowns.Daily` from `RegionBook.Daily`: on each town's own day of 30, two to five tiles by `Arising.TryTownTile`,
  never with a map, a caravan or a quest on it). Asks, the patch (four world events, the undertakers, the tinker and the
  vet prefer them: `Undertakers.People`, `Tinker.People`), release B's leans (`ArisingMath.Lean`: survivors to the Bell on
  a fated quarter, `SaltBell`, or in a later age to the Wheel on a fated third, `SaltWheel`; a band led by one good with
  beasts to the Circuit, by a good shot to the Wardens). Nothing saved.

  (`Rimfolk_StormglassRod`; `Patch_GlassRodStrike` and `Patch_GlassRodExplosion` take the strike within 18 cells, no

  Fleet's shuttle (Royalty's, else drop pods) with a casket to sell, its salvage (`PlayCarry.Salvage`; chunks cut where

  (`ArisingMath.Lean`, 17 arguments: survivors raise masts or keep a ship's watches, a band digs or votes). Their callers

- **The peoples' own events, round 1** (11 November 2026; released 0.213.0; `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 10, 5, 47, 83, 51, 1,
  19, 17, 34 and 95, approved in full; `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEventsMath.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEventsTests.cs`, "the peoples' events: "). The player: "I'd first like more faction specific events,
  interactions etc. like this event i had with these gene guys who gave my pawn a new gene", and "also some
  faction-specific camps can be included in the events". Each only from a people of its calling at peace with the colony
  (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors group at the touchpoints' rates (base chance 0.5 to 0.8, 20 to 60 days apart),
  every age in its own form, played out on the map. Rounds 2 to 10 stay on the to-do list.
  - **Shared shapes, for the later rounds.** *The visitor who works on a colonist* (`PeopleWorkOn.cs`): release G's gene
    work made general: a JobDef with `PeopleWorkJob` (where the colonist is while it is done: `here` a forced wait, `bed`
    laid in the bed, `beside` walked to the place, `sky` out under the open sky; its mark: the healing cross, sparks, the
    hum, the storm, earth turned; its `PeopleWorkDone` handler), `JobDriver_PeopleWorkOn` (to them, wait until they are in
    place, the work with a bar, the handler), `JobDriver_PeopleKeep` for the colonist kept at a place; the order kept as
    one of the events' visits (`pev:work`, its place a thing or a cell: `Visit.cell`, saved), a worker pulled away sent
    again four times, given up after its hours with any silver paid given back. *Goods held in trust* (`PeopleTrust.cs`):
    `TrustCrate` (a sealed crate of goods, `Rimfolk_TrustCrate`, its contents its own; opened by its own button, sold or
    destroyed, it notes how in its record as it happens; burned by harm told at once), `TrustRecord` in the book, the fetch
    a visit (`pev:trust`), the verdict `PeopleEventsMath.Verdict`. *A reading of what the map holds* (`OldPlaces.cs`): the
    old places (a fogged room holding an ancient danger's caskets, sealed crates, hives or sleeping enemies; the tile's
    landmark, the game's and Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's; Geological Landforms' landform by name in code), `Reading` (the
    contents counted exactly: mechanoids by kind, fleshbeasts, hives and insects, caskets and those in them, crates) and
    its words (`ReadingParts`), `Open` (the fog lifted, the dormant woken with `CompCanBeDormant.WakeUp`, the caskets
    opened). *The legend beast trigger* (`LegendBeasts`: release D's quarry rule, the nemesis optional, `Tameable`,
    `EdgeToward`). *A camp kind with ways of its own* (`Camps/CampWorker.cs`): `CampKindDef.workerClass`, a `CampWorker`
    (its land, its site, its start, hour, day and night jobs, its going, its farewell's marks, its placeholders, its own
    asks' needs) hooked beside the land kinds' in `CampKindsLand.cs`, `Camp.Format`, `CampLook.FarewellText` and
    `CampAsks.AskBlocked`, and `Camp.workState` (a `CampWorkState`, saved with the camp). The events' visits dispatch
    through one line in `HappeningTracker.VisitsHour` (`PeopleEvents.Owns`).
  - **Gifts** come once a colonist each and never within 20 days of another (`PeopleEventsBook`: `gifts` "kind:id", the
    newest 120 kept, `lastGift`). *A beast for a colonist* (herders): `HerdersBeast.KindFor` (the land's animals,
    `BiomeAnimals.Of`, fitting `BeastFits`, the base game's horse, yak, dromedary, muffalo and alpaca beside them; ridable
    ones twice as likely with Giddy-Up), a young beast just grown; nine tenths of its worth, or one of the colony's young
    beasts worth half (`OurYoung`, it joins their party); tameness and obedience trained, the game's bond and master, led
    home (`RopeToPen` for a roamer, else following), the rider's supper (`pev:supper`, `Hosting.Meal`). *A limb fitted*
    (order): `OrderLimb.Need` (the missing part's recipe by the order's age, `LimbRecipe`: peg leg or wooden hand before
    the industrial age, simple prostheses after, never bionics), the colony's bed (`Bed`), the surgeon of Medicine 10 to
    16; the wood carried out for a wooden limb; the doctor at the bedside; `RecipeWorker.ApplyOnPawn` with the surgeon
    (the game's own success and failure), the chance on the card from `SurgeryOutcomeEffectDef.GetQuality`; a deed `aid`
    (a debt of honour by `FavoursOwed`) or, with medicine sent back, `gift`. *Storm-sense* (Conclave): a thunderstorm now
    (a weather with lightning), the most sensitive (`Hears`), an hour out under the sky by the colony's rod (`sky`), a
    lightning flash, `ChangePsylinkLevel(1)` and `PsycastPaths.Follow` (Staticlord, Frostshaper), or without Royalty A
    RimWorld of Magic's `BookOfStormBorn` handed over; silver, or a vial (needs the colony's rod; a `gift` deed). *A
    mechlink* (Lattice, Biotech): the colony's best mind and hands, `MechlinkImplant` on the brain, the mech walked in with
    them (`StarterMechs`) made the colony's with the colonist its overseer; silver or two subcores; a tribal colony's
    `Rimfolk_Thought_MechlinkStrange` (-3, three days, its mood hint). *A Gauranlen seed* (Mossborn, the ledger warm:
    `LedgerWarm`): the spot chosen by the game's targeting with the seed's own `CompPlantable.CanPlantAt`, or hers (away
    from buildings within the tree's reach), planted together (`DoPlant`, `ConnectToPawn`); without Ideology a healroot
    grove of nine; the promise reckoned with the ledger (`MossLedger.Reckon` calls `MossPromise.Reckoned`: kept +2, broken
    -6 and `wordBroken`).
  - **Crates held in trust** (league): six to ten crates of its age's goods (`CrateGoods`), set down by the stores by its
    porters (by drop pod for a league of the spacer age), the fetch 20 to 30 days on; for the fee, a tenth of their
    worth, or free. Good ink: the fee, +6 (+10 free), `keptWord`, a year of +3% prices with every league
    (`Patch_TrustTermsPawn`, `Patch_TrustTermsTown`). Red ink: -15, `robbed`, no league caravans for a season
    (`Patch_TrustRedInk`). One open with the league at a time; with the league gone or at war the trust lapses.
  - **What lies in the old place** (society): an unread old place, two fellows at the gate; let measure, they become a camp
    beside it (`Rimfolk_Camp_ScholarsMeasure`, `CampWorker_Measure`, four days, measuring by day at its walls), then the
    reading told in a letter, research (`DilemmaEffect_Research`, a share 0.3, 1200 at most), the place noted read; let
    open, `OldPlaces.Open` as they go.
  - **The hostel** (pilgrims; `Rimfolk_Camp_PilgrimHostel`, `CampWorker_Hostel`): called by a beat of the great
    pilgrimage and the holy year (`Patches/Rimfolk_PeopleEvents.xml`, `WorldEffect_Camp`); by the road where the tile has
    one; travellers of any people at peace every 8 to 16 hours, four at most, a night or two (`Arrivals.Visit` to its
    fire), their news from the facts service told and its place marked (`OutsiderTalk.Heard`); bread asked once and then
    carried out each morning; the blessing (a gathering, the pilgrims' cough at 0.05 through the budget); feuding peoples'
    travellers (goodwill -20 or less between them, never at war) quarrel once a stay, a brawl at the camp brawl's rate.
  - **The lantern post** (Wardens; `Rimfolk_Evt_LanternPost` makes the camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_LanternPost`,
    `CampWorker_LanternPost`): at the edge nearest the beast, ten days at most; trackers watch it by day, a keeper by the
    lantern at night; a warning when it comes within 30 cells of the colony (every 12 hours at most); the meat ask (a new
    errand word, `PlayCarry.Meat`); the trail ask (two hunters under `LordJob_AssaultThings`, the colonist's hunt, a day at
    most, skinned by them if it falls); once a stay the beast at their fire at night (0.12 a night) or a hound lost on the
    trail (0.06 a day); the beast fallen or the trail cold, the lantern out.
  - **Kill it or win it over** (Wardens and Circuit): a legend or an alpha, tameable; the hunt (release D's
    `WardensHunt.Hunt` with only the Wardens), the taming (the game's `Tame` designation and job from its own work giver,
    the tamer beside a day, `pev:coach`), or the bout (`JobDriver_PeopleBout`, `WardenWins` by Melee); the tamer's own
    tries for the Circuit (`pev:tame`, every two hours, six at most, `TameChance` the game's, the beast's revenge at its
    `GetManhunterOnTameFailChance`). Passed over -5, sided with +4, a bout's loser -2; a news line on the roads.
  - Nothing else is hurt by Rimfolk: the surgery, the fights at the fire, the hunt and the taming are the game's own.
    Saved: `PeopleEventsBook` (gifts, trusts, the promise, places read; modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`) and a
    camp's `workState`. Dev actions "Peoples' events: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and
    camps*.
- **The peoples' own events, round 2** (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.229.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 14, 22, 26, 59, 12, 25, 3, 20, 40 and 63, on "you can go ahead on the todos";
  `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events2/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents2Math.cs`, `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents2Tests.cs`
  ("the peoples' events, round 2: "). As round 1: only from a people of its calling at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the
  Visitors group, base chance 0.4 to 0.7, 30 to 60 days apart and never in the first ten days, every age in its own form,
  played out on the map or the world's own roads.
  - **The season away** (`SeasonAway.cs`, the shape for 67 and 98 later): release F's conscript made general. One of the
    events' visits (`pev:away`, its text "people|kind|tile|place|days|extra"): the colonist walks to the map's edge
    (`JobDriver_SetOut`), a beast at heel or ridden with Giddy-Up (`GiddyUpMounts.MountNow`), and sets out as a caravan of
    their own (`CaravanExitMapUtility`) to a town or a tile; there they are kept in the world (`KeepFor.Lent`) for their days;
    then `CaravanMaker` and the game's roads bring them home, and the kind's `AwayKind.Home` says what it was for. Lost on
    the road, told as such; turned back by the player, the season ends. `PeopleEvents2.MayLeave`: never one of the colony's
    last two grown-ups.
  - **A pilgrimage** (pilgrims; a gift): a shrine within reach (`PeopleEvents2Math.ShrineInReach`: both roads and two days
    there in thirty): a fellowship town, a town whose faith keeps a relic (Ideology's `Precept_Relic`), an old shrine at a
    landmark (Odyssey's `WorldLandmarks`). The one who'd go: whoever carries a grief or a guilt (a memory feeding the heart's
    Grief or Shame, `Feelings.Feeds`), else the shakiest faith; or the colony's most faithful. Ten to thirty days away in all
    (`ShrineDays`). Home: `Rimfolk_PilgrimShell` at their feet (with Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Relics and Artifacts a token
    of a relic's shrine), `Rimfolk_Thought_Pilgrimage` (+5, forty days), `Faiths.Steady` 0.15, the heaviest grief or guilt
    worn to three quarters of its time (`EasedAge`), the fellowship +6; the pilgrims' cough at 0.08 through the harm budget.
  - **One guard, one wagon** (league): a great caravan or a trading season running (`Rimfolk_WS_GreatCaravan`,
    `Council_WS_TradeBoom`) and its town in reach; the colony's best fighter or its best talker who fights, with its
    strongest pack beast (ridable first with Giddy-Up); four to seven days with the caravan; home with `GuardShare` (by days,
    Social and the league's age) set at their feet, 2400 Social practice, +8, and `guardUntil`: the league's caravans weigh
    half again for sixty days (`LeagueGuard.CaravanFactor` in `Peoples.CaravanFactor`).
  - **The body made better, on terms** (enclave; a gift): the game's bionic eye, arm, leg or spine for a part missing or
    scarred (`EnclaveBody.Need`), else the best fighter's arm or leg made better; with Alpha Implants one of its animal
    bionics for a colonist's bonded beast. `BionicPrice` now, or `TermsTotal` (a fifth more), a fifth down and four
    `Instalment`s: `TermsRecord` in the book, a visit (`pev:terms`) that fires `Rimfolk_Evt_EnclaveInstalment` each fifteen
    days (base chance 0), the silver carried to the gate for their courier. Not paid: `EnclaveTerms.Default`, -15,
    `contractBroken`, a debt tie in the world's ledger (origin "enclaveTerms"), and no lander (`HappeningWorker_EnclaveLander`)
    or trader caravan (`Patch_EnclaveDefaultCaravans`) until all is paid. The surgeon (Medicine 14 to 18) by pod by the trade
    spot, on foot into a tribal colony; `Rimfolk_PEv2_Bionic` at the bed or `_BeastBionic` where the beast stands, the game's
    own surgery and its chance on the card.
  - **A crossing on the colony's river** (river folk): `RiverCrossing.Line`, the narrowest straight line (a row or a
    column: nobody walks a diagonal of spans) over bridgeable river water near the colony, at most 22 cells, two planks on
    each bank; `CrossingWood` by the bridge's and the floor's own costs. The boatmen lay it from both banks
    (`JobDriver_LayCrossing`, an hour a span, half on a bank, the next cell queued) with `PeopleTowns.LayDocks` and the bridge
    of their age (`Bridge`, Odyssey's `HeavyBridge` from the industrial age); the colony's builder may learn beside them.
    `CrossingRecord`; their knot night (`KnotDay` by their people) fires `Rimfolk_Evt_KnotNight` while it stands: a night's
    rest at it (their lord by it until morning), supper if the colony sends it.
  - **The guild's mark** (Kiln Guild; a gift): `GuildMark.Plan`: a bow or a gun's unique kind by name ("_Unique",
    Odyssey's and Vanilla Weapons Expanded's, with Odyssey), else a blade in the sharpest stuff the colony has enough of
    (`Better`), else a masterwork of what it is. `MarkPrice` and the main material (half its makings, or the new stuff).
    The weapon handed over; `Rimfolk_PEv2_Mark` (`PeopleWorkJob.atPlace`: the master at the bench, the colonist beside it)
    a working day; `GuildMark.Remake`: the unique piece's own name made "Alder's ..." (`CompUniqueWeapon.name`), a blade's
    label by `Patch_GuildMarkLabel` (the book's `marks`). With the colony's crafter at the bench, a quarter off and 2000
    Crafting.
  - **Water in the dry year** (herders; a camp): a drought (Odyssey's `Drought`, VEE's `VEE_Drought`, or
    `Council_WS_Drought`) and fresh water; let in (or for a `Toll`, -3), `Rimfolk_Camp_DryWater` by the water
    (`CampWorker_DryWater`): hay asked (60, carried out) or the colony's grazing (the herd out on its ground each morning);
    milk, a herder's lesson with the colony's beasts, the young beast at the gate after a good stay; once a stay the herd
    strays into the fields (`StrayChance`, the camps' own `StrayHerd` and `EatCrops`), and a predator of the land follows it
    in (`HarmKinds.CampLeft`, 0.3, the game's own hunt). Leaving after a good stay: +10, `campHelped`, a region news line.
    Turned away: -4 and a news line (`pev:lost`) of `LostOnRoad` head.
  - **A pad by the colony** (enclave; a camp): `Rimfolk_Camp_EnclavePad`, two factors and two marshals, ten to fifteen days,
    `PadRent` (never a round figure) through the camps' fee every five days (or none, as friends); a marshal lays a five by
    five pad of metal tiles (`JobDriver_LayPad`); at six a pod of fresh stock (their trader kind's, 250 to 450 silver) lands
    on it and an hour later goes into the factor's stock; asks: keep off the pad (watched), ten meals at `MealsPrice`, and
    the colony's own "Raise their rent" (`PaysRaise`: they pay half again, or go). The camps' terms bend now and then
    (breakTerms 0.15), and the stock draws a band against the camp (`PadBandChance` on top of the camps' own).
  - **Books kept from the fire** (society): a ruin of theirs in the ledger within a month (not the colony's doing) or a
    great fire near one of their towns; four to eight of the game's books by their age (Vanilla Books Expanded's papers)
    and with Anomaly the tome in a `TrustCrate`; a `TrustRecord` of real books (means "cart") set down by the stores,
    read, or locked away (forbidden); `Patch_ArchiveSold` notes one sold; the cart 12 to 18 days on (`pev:archive`): every
    book there (`Kept`) is +8, `keptWord` and the best book left; one lost, sold or the tome's seal broken is -8 and
    `robbed` (20). The books carried out are only theirs (`PlayCarry.Archive`).
  - **A leg for a lame beast** (Circuit): a colony beast missing a leg; Alpha Implants' `AI_AnimalProstheticLeg` from the
    industrial age (`BeastLeg`), fitted where it stands (`Rimfolk_PEv2_BeastLeg`); in any age the stables: the beast to
    their people and at the beast-doctor's heels, and the young one of its kind brought along the colony's.
  - **News for sale** (Signal Line): two of the kinds the game can make now (`NewsKinds`: the item stash, Odyssey's orbital
    wreck, the bandit camp) at `NewsPrice` (60 to 200); bought, `QuestUtility.GenerateQuestAndMakeAvailable` and the new
    site marked heard of (`HeardPlaces.Heard`, "site:id") from the masts at their town. No ground site for a downed
    shuttle's cargo exists in the player's mods, so the wreck is Odyssey's in orbit, offered only when the game would send
    the colony there.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: only the pilgrims' cough and the predator the herd draws, through the harm budget; the roads,
    the surgery and the bands are the game's own. Saved: `PeopleEvents2Book` (crossings, terms, marks, the league's year)
    and the pad's state, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Dev actions "Peoples' events 2: ...". The Almanac's peoples'
    pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps*.
- **The peoples' own events, round 3** (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.230.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, on "you can go ahead on the todos";
  `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events3/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents3Math.cs`, `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents3Tests.cs`
  ("the peoples' events, round 3: "). As rounds 1 and 2: only from a people of its calling at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in
  the Visitors group, base chance 0.5 to 0.7, 30 to 60 days apart and never in the first ten days, every age in its own
  form, played out on the map. Three come from code at their moment (base chance 0, `PeopleEvents2.Fire`): the litters an
  hour or so after a raid, the riders the morning after a theft, the herder with a hard birth; the first two at a small
  chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors (`StoryDirection.Factor(StoryWaysMath.Visitors)`, never below a quarter).
  - **Red ink** (league): an unsettled "robbed" or "caravanRaided" wrong of the colony's against any people but the league,
    2 to 120 days old (a "killed" wrong within two days of it names the page when it is the bigger), not the crates in
    trust (round 1's own red ink). Paid: `Restitution` (twelve silver a point of the wrong's weight, more for a run, 80 to
    1500) carried out, the wrong settled (`FactionMemory.Settle`), `GoodwillBack` to the wronged and +2 the league. Argued:
    the talker's Social on the card (risk 0.7, 3.5% a level): struck out, or written twice and owed double. Refused, or
    written twice: every league 5% worse (`LeagueRedInk.Terms` on round 1's `PeopleTrust.Terms`) until paid, the factor
    back to ask (`RedInkRecord`, `MaxRedInk` kept).
  - **The road gang** (league; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_RoadGang`, `CampWorker_RoadGang`): while `Council_WS_NewRoad` runs.
    The waymaster asks leave: through the fields, round them (their way unless let through), or not across the colony's
    land (laid round it, kept `AroundMargin` cells from its home area and buildings, -5). The way from edge to edge
    (`PeopleEvents3Math.Route`, four ways only, a turn dearer, a field `FieldCost` dearer unless let through; `Widen` two
    wide) on ground that takes the floor (`RoadGang.Takes`); the floor by the league's age (`RoadFloor`: packed earth,
    flagstones of the land's stone, concrete, paved tile). Waymaster, two road wardens and two or three labourers camp at
    the edge eight to twelve days and lay it a stretch a day (`Stretch`, `JobDriver_LayRoad`, plants cleared, the colony's
    own floors left alone), the day's stretch told at dusk. Asks: a day's food sold (eight meals at their worth and a
    tenth), the colony's builder for the day (`BuilderWage`, practice a cell, straight on to the next), a spur from the gate
    for silver (`SpurPrice`) or the colony's stone blocks (`SpurStone`). A robber band (`GangBandChance` on top of the
    camps' own). The road stays; +3 when let across.
  - **Nobody on a sickbed is anyone's enemy** (order): raiders lying downed (humanlike, at war, never everyone's enemy for
    good), the fight over, 0.45 a raid, an hour to three on, fifteen days apart; two or three bearers (`Litters`), litters or
    a stretcher cart by the age. All, or only the worst hurt (`WorstHurt`), carried to the edge (`JobDriver_LitterCarry`) and
    off; each people `PeoplesDMath.GoodwillFor` by how many (the Bell's rule), the order +5. Kept: counted in the book
    (`kept`), nothing said.
  - **The sick room** (order): a serious spreading sickness (`AilmentInfo.spreadPerHour`) and a room with two medical beds or
    the hospital. The sick carried (the game's rescue) or sent to its beds; her rounds at 7, 12, 17 and 22 (`VisitorServices.Dose`
    with `Rimfolk_OrderNursed`); `AilmentTracker.Spread` at a third (`SickRoom.SpreadFactor`) for three days; from the
    industrial age the colony's medicine carried to her. The colony's doctor may walk the rounds (practice). She may catch it
    (`HarmKinds.Physician` 0.06 a day, the illness budget) and is nursed as the colony's guest until well. +3, `relief`.
  - **A field sickhouse** (order; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_FieldSickhouse`, `CampWorker_Sickhouse`): a plague running or a war
    ended within a month. A long hut (`sleep` Hut, left standing) and the lamp at its door; two to six of the region's sick
    or wounded (`Patients`) walk in or are carried in by one of their own (`JobDriver_CarryToWard`), each a bed in the ward,
    tended and dosed on rounds (`JobDriver_WardRound`), home when well. Asks: medicine, food, clean cloth, the doctor's day
    in the ward (`WardXp`, the sickness home at `DoctorCatch` through the budgets), the colony's own sick taken in. It can
    turn: the sickness crosses (`HarmKinds.CampFever`, `CrossChance`), a patient dies and the Quiet Bell's sexton comes for
    them (else a sister carries them home), a band for the medicine. Gone: +8, `campHelped` ("the field sickhouse"), each
    people whose sick it fed +3.
  - **Grazing across the land** (herders): spring to autumn, a drove of twenty to forty head of the land's beasts by name
    (`DroveKinds`: the game's, Odyssey's muskox, Vanilla Animals Expanded's camel, Alpha Animals' thunderox and mouflon,
    Megafauna's aurochs) walks in at one edge (`LordJob_Drove`, its ground moved across the map each hour, eased in and out,
    `DroveShare`), the drovers' fire at the far edge, two or three days. Let across: a young beast of the drove (0.6) or
    hides and milk at the fire, the colony's best hand rides a day with it (`RideXp`). Unfenced fields within reach grazed at
    noon (`Grazed`, told); a kick once a drove at most (`HarmKinds.DroversBull`). Toll (`DroveToll`, -3) or turned away (-6).
  - **The thief on the drove road** (herders): a raid's group on its way out (exit, flight, kidnap or steal cover) may drive
    off one to three of the colony's stock within 22 cells (`DriveOffChance`: 0.3 with beasts of its own, Animal Husbandry
    Raids, else 0.12), told; left behind by fallen or fled drovers, the colony's again; off the map, kept in the world
    (`TheftRecord`). The next morning, 6 to 10, at 0.6: the riders at the gate (mounted with Giddy-Up). The colony's rider: the
    game's own bandit camp of the thieves a tile or two off (`ThiefPoints` of the threat, `CampDays` before it goes cold),
    a caravan of one to it (`JobDriver_RideOut`, `CaravanArrivalAction_VisitSite`), and on its map (`Patch_ThievesCampMapMade`,
    under `RimfolkPatches.On`) the herders' riders beside the colony (`LordJob_AssistColony`) and the beasts there, the
    colony's again to take home; won, +6. Alone: one to three days, each beast back at 0.6, one kept as their due, led home by
    a rider, +2. Or the beasts let go.
  - **Spring calving** (herders; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_SpringCalving`, `CampWorker_Calving`): in spring, eight to twelve days.
    Four to seven grown beasts of the herd given the game's pregnancy (`GestationAt`, births over the stay's first two
    thirds); calves born by the game's own `DoBirthSpawn` join the herd; the count at dusk spoken aloud. Once a stay at 0.35 a
    birth goes hard (held at 97%): the herder at the gate (`Rimfolk_Evt_HardBirth`), the colony's best hand (with the next
    best learning) or the herders themselves, the roll on the card (risk 0.55 less 3.5% a level of Animals; 0.27 for the
    herders): both live (the colony's hand: the calf the colony's) or the mother lost, worked at her side
    (`JobDriver_HardBirth`). Hay asked, milk offered. It can turn: the afterbirth's predator at night (`HarmKinds.CampLeft`,
    the offal rule), a calf missing (0.18) and two herders with lanterns walking toward it at night
    (`JobDriver_LanternSearch`, the fire glow), found or back at first light. Gone after a good stay: +6.
  - **An old shrine on the colony's ground** (pilgrims): something holy (`OldShrine.Holy`: an ancient building out of the
    fog, a grave not the colony's with someone in it, a tree three years old, the landmark), a free cell beside it. Two
    pilgrims set stones three days (two with the colony's helper; `JobDriver_SetStones`), counted at dusk; blessed, the
    `Rimfolk_OldShrine` is the colony's (a lamp's glow; a dignified meditation focus with Royalty), with Ideology an inert
    relic of Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Relics and Artifacts at its foot. Pilgrims stop in spring and summer (0.1 a morning,
    ten days apart) and leave 15 to 40 silver or 2 to 5 herbal medicine. The colony prays there (`JoyGiver`, meditative,
    `Rimfolk_Thought_PrayedAtShrine` +4 for those of a faith, or anyone without Ideology). It wears 2% a day out in the weather;
    below a third it is mourned (-3), above three fifths kept again (`OldShrineRecord`).
  - **Two faiths at one table** (pilgrims, Ideology): two faiths clashing with a quarrel lately (`FaithClash`), or the
    colony's largest faith near a split (`NearSplit`: three believers or more, a third wavering below 0.3, as Splits and
    Schisms splits). The palmer: an evening gathering (`DilemmaEffect_Gathering`, the palmer a guest), each side's best
    speaking; the roll on the card (risk 0.67 less 3.5% a level of the better Social): settled (`settledUntil` fifteen days,
    the clash dilemma rests; certainty +0.1 for those who came; +3), or the split anyway, said plainly (certainty -0.08),
    applied when the gathering ends (`TwoFaiths.GatheringOver`). Or the palmer blesses each believer apart (+0.05).
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: only the sister's and the doctor's catching, the sickness crossing, the drove's kick and the
    afterbirth's predator, through the harm and illness budgets; the fights, the births and the roads are the game's own. The
    raiders driving off beasts is a loss of stock, not a hurt, at a raid's small chance. Saved: `PeopleEvents3Book` (red ink,
    shrines, thefts, the table) and the camps' states, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Dev actions "Peoples' events 3:
    ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps*.
- **The peoples' own events, round 4** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.268.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32 and 33 (the society, the enclave, the river
  folk and the Wardens); `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events4/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents4Math.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents4Tests.cs` ("the peoples' events, round 4: "). As rounds 1 to 3: only from a people of its calling
  at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors group, base chance 0.4 to 0.6, 30 to 60 days apart and never in the first
  fifteen days, every age in its own form, played out on the map. Four come from code at their moment (base chance 0,
  `PeopleEvents2.Fire`): the contract's day, the knot night's lanterns, the Wardens' page and their run to a manhunt; the
  last two at a small chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors.
  - **The fellowship examined** (society; a gift, `Fellowship`): a colonist at Intellectual 12 (the summer school's best
    student at 10), never named, not examined in the last sixty days. A fellow or a don at the gate. Before the colony: an
    evening gathering (the night of the fire's disputation pool), the verdict kept and given at its end
    (`Fellowship.GatheringOver`), the roll on the card by Intellectual and Social (`ExamFail`: 0.95 less 3.5% a level of
    each). Quietly: the fellow at the colonist's side (round 1's `PeopleWorkOn`, `Rimfolk_PEv4_Examine`), Intellectual alone,
    a fail heard by nobody. Passed: a corresponding fellow (`Rimfolk_Thought_FellowNamed` +6 for sixty days, the society's
    word naming them, +4, the gift noted), a book carried to the gate each season by the post (`Couriers.Deliver`; the
    game's textbook, schematic or novel, Vanilla Food Variety Expanded's recipe book; never Anomaly's tome), and with Vanilla
    Skills Expanded the Researcher expertise (`Expertise.Give`, the mod's own tracker by reflection, when there is room).
    Failed before the colony: "Strictly speaking, that is two questions," and stung (-4, six days, with its mood hint).
    600 Intellectual either way.
  - **The summer school** (society; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_SummerSchool`, `CampWorker_SummerSchool`): in summer, two or three
    fellows for a week, their table, a lesson each afternoon (13h to 18h) at most two a day: learning, medicine or
    speaking (`DilemmaEffect_SchoolLesson`, the play-outs' lesson, 150 an hour, 225 with the colony's books on the table).
    Books lent (the event's second answer or the camp's page: up to three of the kind the colony has most of, carried out
    by the camps' own carrying, set down for the colony as the school goes); six meals asked. Once a stay after the second
    day at 0.35, two fellows argue at their table: the colony's talker walks over (`Rimfolk_PEv4_Settle`, `SettleOdds`
    0.35 plus 4% a Social level), or after four hours a sulk: no more lessons that day, the camp's tension up. Going: the
    best student (two lessons or more) left a textbook and examined sooner; +4 after lessons.
  - **A contract to the last digit** (enclave; `EnclaveContract`): something the colony makes, found on its benches and
    stores (meals, cloth from its cotton or stores, beer from a fermenting barrel, the dearest drug a recipe of its makes,
    art from a sculptor's bench, components), `ContractWorth` by wealth and the last contracts' size, due on a set date
    fifteen to thirty days on, a fifth over its worth (a tenth after a default, for sixty days). Half the contract may be
    signed. On the day (`Rimfolk_Evt_ContractDue`): their marshals by pod at the trade spot (a runner and porters on foot to
    a tribal or medieval colony), the goods carried out (`DilemmaEffect_ContractCarry`). In full: paid, +4, the next half
    again bigger (three times at most). Short: what came at its worth less the fee. Not delivered (or no letter possible a
    day after): the fee carried out if the stores hold it, else a debt tie in the world's ledger; -6, the first size again.
  - **Stranded with something to sell** (enclave; `BrokerPod`): the broker hurt until downed in a pod with slag, two or three
    pods of spacer goods (`CargoDefs`, worth `CargoWorth`) beside them, sealed. Brought in: the colony's doctor carries them
    to a bed (the game's rescue; tended there by the game's own doctors), or tends them at the crash without a bed; the
    lander two or three days on: two marshals by pod, the broker carried to the edge (round 3's litter job) or walking with
    them, each crate lifted aboard (`Rimfolk_PEv4_Lift`), a fifth paid (`Share`), +10, the care remembered. A crate gone by
    then is taken. Taken: unsealed, `robbed` weight 25 and -20, the lander for the broker alone the next morning. Left: the
    lander the next morning, nothing owed.
  - **Fouled water** (river folk; `FouledWater`): a flesh body half a day or more in water, Biotech's poisoned ground or a
    wastepack within three cells of it. The river warden walks to the spot. With the colony's hands: the warden and a
    colonist go spot to spot (`Rimfolk_PEv4_Clean`, a bar): a body or wastepack carried up onto dry ground away from the
    water, the bank cleared of poison; +5. The warden alone: +2. Left: `polluted` weight 8, and the boat-trader and the nets
    (`HappeningWorker_RiverCatch`, `HappeningWorker_RiverNets`) stop until a day's look finds it clean, sixty days at most.
  - **Lanterns on the water** (river folk; `KnotLanterns`): on a river folk people's knot night (round 2's `KnotDay`) at dusk,
    the colony's bank (`HappeningWorker_RiverNets.Bank`), once a year. Boatmen set their light on the bank and come with a
    lantern for each of the colony's lost (its graves and dead) and taken in, three to twelve, at most six set. Gather: an
    evening gathering at their light (17h to 23h, the boatmen its guests), `Rimfolk_Thought_KnotLanterns` +4 held for those
    who came (the play-outs' held moods). With Goji's
    Fantasy Race: Merren its floating lanterns set on the water, fuelled, the colony's; otherwise torches along the bank,
    taken back with the light in the morning. Where a crossing of theirs stands, round 2's knot night rest sets them there
    instead (`KnotLanterns.AtCrossing`). Unanswered, they set them.
  - **Flooded out** (river folk; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_FloodedOut`, `CampWorker_FloodedOut`): while `Council_WS_Flood` runs,
    five to eight of the families by the colony's fresh water five to ten days; they fish (the camps' own fishing), ask for
    eight meals a day their first three days, offer their catch, mend what is worn, put up two drying racks (VFE Classical's,
    else Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Props and Decor's) left standing, may join (0.2), and ask to stay longer (0.4, the camps' own). With
    Hospitality (the invited guests' setting on): their old and young, three at most, handed to it as the colony's guests
    (`InvitedGuests.HandOver`) until the camp goes. Once a stay at 0.06, flu through the harm and illness budgets
    (`HarmKinds.CampFever`). Going on good terms: a knot in the net, +12, `sheltered`. Turned away -3.
  - **The boat-builders** (river folk; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_BoatBuilders`, `CampWorker_BoatBuilders`): spring to autumn, fresh
    water and ten grown wild trees. Three or four for a week, a shed (`sleep` Hut, left standing), the camps' own felling (none
    if the colony refuses its trees: -2). The hull on the bank by days worked (`HullStage`: keel, frame, planked hull, three
    drawn stages), the builders at it (`Rimfolk_PEv4_Hull`), the colony's crafter beside them (a lesson). Heavy rain (0.5)
    costs a day once and a day more of stay. With Vehicle Framework and Vanilla Vehicles Expanded the finished hull sold as
    `VVE_Dinghy` for silver (350 by wealth) and 60 wood, set on the water (`Vehicles.VehicleSpawner.GenerateVehicle` by
    reflection); otherwise floated home. +3.
  - **A page in the book** (Wardens; a gift, `WardensPage`): a legend of the region, a beast nemesis or a pack's alpha killed by
    one of the colony (its kind read before its death: `HappeningTracker.DeathNote.great`). Six hours to ten days on, at
    0.15 an hour: a keeper of the book at the gate. The cord tied there (`PeopleWorkOn` beside the gate, `Rimfolk_PEv4_Cord`):
    `Rimfolk_RedCord` on the arm (shown in health, no effect), `Rimfolk_Thought_PageInBook` +6 for sixty days, the Wardens'
    word naming them, +6, Vanilla Skills Expanded's Hunter expertise when there is room, else a passion in Shooting or Melee
    by the weapon that made the kill. The pelt (the beast's leather, as much as its hide gave and the stores hold) bought at
    twice its worth.
  - **Wardens at the manhunt** (Wardens; `WardensManhunt`): a manhunting pack (three or more) or a mad beast of body size 1 or
    more, once a manhunt at 0.4, an hour or two in, fifteen days apart. Two to four of their fighters come in at the edge
    nearest the beasts straight into the game's assault on them; the letter asks the terms (no answer: the hunt's own):
    hides theirs and meat the colony's (round 1's `PeoplesD.Divide`, `Rimfolk_PEv4_Dress`), all of it theirs (+2 more), or
    sent home. Their kills counted from the death hook; the last beast down, they gather at the carcasses. +3.
  - **The hive burned** (Wardens; `HiveBurned`): the game's hives and Vanilla Factions Expanded - Insectoids 2's wild hives
    and burrows (`HiveDefs`, never a colony's artificial one), seen. Three to five come in at the edge nearest it, armed by
    their age (`Fire`: their own arms and torches, molotovs, an incendiary launcher for one). Together: they wait at the edge
    up to three hours for the colony's drafted fighters within 15 cells of the hive, then the game's assault on the hives and
    the insects about them; alone: at once; refused: a day's watch at the edge. With torches, a Warden by a hive and not
    fighting holds one to it (`Rimfolk_PEv4_Burn`, the game's fire). The hives gone: +4.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: only the flooded families' flu, through the harm and illness budgets; the broker's crash is the
    game's own pod crash; the fights, the fire and the insects are the game's own. Saved: `PeopleEvents4Book` (fellows,
    examined, best students, contracts, pods, fouled water, lanterns, pages, the examination waiting) and the camps' states,
    modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: `PeopleEvents3.Hour`/`Hourly`, `HappeningTracker.Before`/`Notify_Killed`,
    `Interplay.Notify_GatheringOver`, the river folk's catch and nets, round 2's knot night rest, `FactsMath`, round 1's
    `PeopleWorkOn` ("quiet" mark), `Expertise` (giving one). Dev actions "Peoples' events 4: ...". The Almanac's peoples'
    pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps*.
- **The peoples' own events, round 5** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.269.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45 and 46 (the Quiet Bell, the Circuit of
  Tamers and the Wheel); `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events5/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents5Math.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents5Tests.cs` ("the peoples' events, round 5: "). As rounds 1 to 4: only from a people of its calling
  at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors group, base chance 0.4 to 0.7, 30 to 60 days apart and never in the first
  ten days, every age in its own form, played out on the map. Six come from code at their moment (base chance 0,
  `PeopleEvents2.Fire`): the gravewardens when the dead rise, the mourners a season on, the dead's people at the field, the
  tamer back to see the hatchling grown, the night crew after a raid and the yard when its town moves near; the
  gravewardens and the crew at a chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors.
  - **The field that stirs** (Bell; with Anomaly; `FieldStirs`): each hour Rimfolk notes who lies dead and unburied on a home's
    land (humanlike bodies), so a shambler up and hostile whose body lay there is one of the colony's risen dead
    (`PeopleEvents5Math.Risen`). Once a rising at 0.5, within the hour, fifteen days apart: three gravewardens (their kind's own
    arms by their age: maces and spades, firebombs and flamers from the industrial age) in at the edge nearest them, straight
    into the game's assault on every shambler up. The letter asks what follows (no answer: the first): when the shamblers are
    down, a grave each beyond the wall for their humanlike bodies, twelve at most (the undertakers' own play-out,
    `Callers.Graves`; at once with the play-outs off), the game's small bell rung over each grave as it is filled; then their
    word, "Bury your dead from now on, and the ground will stay quiet", +3. Or the same and the colony's promise to bury its
    dead (+2 more; should its dead rise again within sixty days after the gravewardens have gone, the Bell hears of it, -5,
    once). Or thanked and sent off.
  - **Mourners from the other side** (Bell; `OtherSideMourners`): when the Bell's bell for the dead buries raiders beyond the
    wall (its first answer), each of their peoples (three at most, never one that is everyone's enemy for good) is due a
    season (fifteen days) on, while their graves still hold them. A bell-keeper and two mourners of that people walk in;
    mourners of a people at war with the colony come as the Bell's guests (`SetGuestStatus`, as a parley's envoy), their own
    lord beside the keeper's. Let through: all walk to the graves, the bell rung as they reach them, an hour there, then +5
    with their people and a `mourned` deed; with one of the colony (the best talker) sent to stand with them (kept beside the
    grave), +8 and the deed naming them. A people at war may then offer a truce by its own letter (`Truces.Offer`: at 0.5,
    always with the colony's talker there). Turned away: the Bell -3. Unanswered thirty days past their day, let go.
  - **A grave-garden for the colony** (Bell; `GraveGarden`): three or more of the colony's graves together (the most within ten
    cells of one), no garden standing there. Two sextons. The whole garden for six meals: three days' work by day
    (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Stone`, `_Rose`, `_Post`): up to thirty flagstones of the land's own stone (`Flagstone` + its rock, else
    granite's) on the open cells round the graves, up to ten roses (the game's `Plant_Rose`, in bloom) beside them on good
    soil, and the bell-post (`Rimfolk_BellPost`, drawn, the colony's, beauty 6, not buildable by hand) by the graves' middle,
    its ground reaching the farthest grave (6 to 14 cells); +4. Or the bell-post alone in an afternoon, +2. Called away before
    the post is up, there is no garden (what was laid stays). While the post stands: anyone of the colony at their leisure in
    its ground (any recreation, a grave visited) gets `Rimfolk_Thought_QuietGround` (+3, a day); a funeral at one of its
    graves (the game's ritual with Ideology, or the Bell's funeral or any vigil Rimfolk plays out at the grave) is watched, and
    those who were there when it ends get `Rimfolk_Thought_FullerRite` (+4, six days), the post rung. With Anomaly and the
    deeper game hooks, a body lying in its ground does not rise (`Patch_GardenQuiet` on `MutantUtility.CanResurrectAsShambler`;
    the buried never rise by the game's own rule).
  - **The field of the fallen** (Bell; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_FieldOfFallen`, `CampWorker_FieldOfFallen`): a dozen humanlike dead
    or more lying on the land, not the colony's own, no threat on. Four to six bell-keepers and sextons camp three to six
    days; a row of graves beyond the wall for the dead (sixteen at most, `PlayBurial.Plot`), dug (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Dig`, the
    game's grave, the colony's) and filled one by one (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Bury`, carrying the body in); the bell at each dusk (a
    bell-keeper walks to the row, `Rimfolk_PEv5_Ring`). They ask for forty wood and twenty cloth (the camps' own asking; sent
    with them by the second answer, +2). From a day and a half, mourners of up to three peoples among the buried walk in to
    stand at the row five hours (the Bell's guests if at war with the colony), each people +3 to +8 by its dead and
    `mourned`. It can turn, once a stay each: at night after the first day, with Anomaly, the void awake and Rimfolk's world
    events allowed to bring a fight, at 0.12 up to three of the dead still lying out rise (told as a threat; the gravewardens
    may come to them); by day, at 0.2, the dead's people come for them: a people at peace with the colony at the gate (their
    own event, `Rimfolk_Evt_FallenClaimed`: let them carry their dead off the land, one each, the game's own taking-away, +4;
    send the colony's talker, by Social, `ClaimTalkFails` 0.75 less 3.5% a level, and they leave the dead with the Bell, +2,
    else as refused; or refuse: -4, and if at war with the Bell a band against its camp (`CampRaids.Send`), else they take
    them anyway); a people at war with the colony and the Bell sends a band against the camp straight away. Going: +2 when
    any were buried.
  - **The bond freely given** (Circuit; a gift, `BondGiven`): the colony's best hand with animals (never given this gift) and a
    beast of the colony's, grown, with tasks left it can learn and free to bond with them (a Pokémon first with PokéWorld).
    A roaming tamer spends the afternoon with it where it stands (round 1's `PeopleWorkOn` on a beast, `Rimfolk_PEv5_Bond`,
    a new "train" mark: dust at its feet), the hand kept at its side. Then every task it can learn is trained (the game's
    own training, prerequisites first), it bonds with the hand (`RelationsUtility.TryDevelopBondRelation`) and takes them as
    master, the hand learns (1,500 Animals) and with Vanilla Skills Expanded gets the Trainer expertise; +3. Or only a few
    pointers at the gate (500).
  - **An egg from the crater** (Circuit; a gift, `CraterEgg`): a fertile egg of a beast that neither lives wild on the land nor
    is kept by the colony, its young able to stand the weather, never an insect's, a dryad's or a legendary Pokémon's; from
    Dinosauria, Megafauna, ReGrowth, Alpha Animals or PokéWorld first (`EggPackages`), else the game's own, weighted by worth.
    Handed over at the gate, its young the colony's (`CompHatcher.hatcheeFaction`), +3 (+2 more with food for the road).
    Each hour whoever of the colony is within three cells of it or carries it has tended it an hour; when it hatches (the
    game's own hatching, kept warm or not: a cold egg spoils and is told), the newborn by where it lay bonds with who tended
    it most, else the keeper named on the card. A season on, the tamer comes back (`Rimfolk_Evt_CraterEggGrown`): an hour
    with the grown beast where it stands (a step of its training, +4), or only told how it does (+2).
  - **The Circuit's ring** (Circuit; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_CircuitRing`, `CampWorker_CircuitRing`): while a world event of the
    fair's kind runs. Six to ten tamers four to six days, four torches, their animals (dogs and wolves, Vanilla Animals
    Expanded's German shepherd; Pokémon with PokéWorld). Each afternoon (13h to 17h) the colony's challengers sent from the
    camp's page (two a day) step up to one of their animals in turn, the friendly bout's own job (`JobDriver_TamerBout`) and
    rules (`CircuitRing.BoutDone`, asked first by `HappeningWorker_TamerBout.Done`): won by `PeoplesDMath.WinChance`, a lesson,
    one in 25 a bruise through the harm budget (`HarmKinds.TamerBout`), told; otherwise the tamers spar among themselves now
    and then. Going: the challenger with the most wins (one at least) has `Rimfolk_CircuitToken` tied on (shown, no effect),
    `Rimfolk_Thought_RingChampion` (+6, thirty days), an egg of the hatchery, a `duel` deed naming them; +5, +2 to the ring
    besides when any fought.
  - **Mend it tonight** (Wheel; `MendTonight`): the night after a raid (the storyteller's last big threat within a day, now
    between 19h and 23h, no threat on), three or more of the colony's buildings damaged; once a raid at 0.5, ten days apart.
    A fixer and two hands with lamps. Paid in the raiders' broken gear (weapons and clothes lying forbidden outside the stores,
    below 60% or tainted, twelve at most) and `MendSilver` (40 to 250 by the hit points missing), or `MendSilverOnly` and the
    gear kept. Through the night each takes the three damaged buildings nearest them (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Mend`, sparks and a
    lamp's glow, a bar, each mended whole), the last of them gathering the gear into their pack (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Gather`);
    gone at first light whatever is left, +3.
  - **Made better** (Wheel; a gift, `MadeBetter`): a colonist's own equipped weapon or worn armour (sharp armour 0.2 or more)
    with a quality below masterwork, the dearest. Paid `BetterSilver` (80 to 800, three tenths of its worth) and
    `BetterSteel`, or half again in silver alone. The fixer takes it at the colonist's side (`Rimfolk_PEv5_HandOver`), the
    piece kept by the record off every map (`PeopleEvents5Book.held`), and walks off to their cart beyond the edge; a day on
    walks back in and hands it back (`_HandBack`): a quality higher (masterwork at most), whole, worn or carried again; +2.
    Should the fixer not come back (dead, their people at war, the colonist away), a runner brings it to the gate, made
    better all the same.
  - **A wagon of our own** (Wheel; with Vehicle Framework and Vanilla Vehicles Expanded; `WagonOfOurOwn`): by the colony's age,
    `VVE_Wagon` before the industrial age (120 wood and 30 steel), `VVE_Mule` (else `VVE_Highwayman`) after (150 steel and five
    components), and 150 or 350 silver; open ground by the gate for it. The goods carried out to the fixer and set down
    where they build; a day's work in turns (`Rimfolk_PEv5_Frame`, sparks), the colony's crafter beside them learning if sent
    (the second answer, 2,500 Crafting over the day); then the goods are used up and the vehicle stands there, the colony's
    (`BoatBuilders.MakeVehicle`, Vehicle Framework's own way by reflection). Never finished: the goods left for the colony.
    +4.
  - **The Wheel stops by** (Wheel; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_WheelYard`, `CampWorker_WheelYard`): a Wheel town's move
    (`WheelTowns.Move`) to within six tiles of a home brings its yard within the day (`Rimfolk_Evt_WheelStopsBy`). Five to
    eight for three days at the edge nearest the colony: their trader (the game's trading), a stall, a mending tent, pack
    animals; nothing left behind. Asks: the colony's worn clothes and weapons mended where they are (the fixer's own mending,
    `VisitorServices.Mend`, at `YardMendPrice`, a third of the wear's worth), its scrap sold (the scrap-runners' price), forty
    wood for their forge (theirs to ask). It can turn, once a stay each: when one of the colony is at the stall beside the
    fixer, at 0.3 they argue over a price (the camp's tension +6, the mending a tenth dearer); on the second day at 0.35 the
    yard stays two days longer. +3 going when they traded or mended.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: only the ring's bruise, the friendly bout's own kind through the harm budget; the fights (the
    gravewardens', a band against the field's camp) and the field's stirring are the game's own (the stirring only with
    Anomaly and while Rimfolk's world events may bring a fight). No new harm kind. Saved: `PeopleEvents5Book` (the burials,
    the promise, the mourners, the gardens, the eggs, the pieces at the cart and the cart's holder, the yards, the raids
    rolled) and the camps' states, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: `PeopleEvents4.Hour`/`Hourly`,
    `HappeningWorker_BellForTheDead.Resolved` (the mourners' day), `HappeningWorker_TamerBout.Done` (the ring's bouts),
    `WheelTowns.Move` (a yard due), `FactsMath`, round 1's `PeopleWorkOn` ("train" mark), round 4's `BoatBuilders` (a vehicle by
    name). One game hook, `Patch_GardenQuiet`. Dev actions "Peoples' events 5: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their
    own: gifts, trust and camps* (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).
- **The peoples' own events, round 6** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.270.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 48, 49, 50, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57 and 58 (the Stormglass Conclave, the Mossborn
  and the Ashen Banner); `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events6/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents6Math.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents6Tests.cs` ("the peoples' events, round 6: "). As rounds 1 to 5: only from a people of its calling
  at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors group, base chance 0.4 or 0.5, 45 to 90 days apart and never in the first
  fifteen days, every age in its own form, played out on the map. Six come from code at their moment (base chance 0,
  `PeopleEvents2.Fire`): the storm-walkers in a dry spell, the reader when a foreseen drone comes, the thorn-guards at a
  fire, the grove-warden after a fire or a blight, the Banner's muster, and the sergeant of a raid the Banner was hired for;
  the code-fired comings at a chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors, the hire times their lean on arms. Two letters
  come once their people are at work, so no answer means the first answer: the reader's and the thorn-guards'.
  - **Breaking the drought** (Conclave; `DroughtBroken`): a drought (Odyssey's `Drought`, `VEE_Drought`) or the game's heat wave,
    not one of the land's for good, run half a day; the land has a rain of its own and nothing else keeps the rain off; once
    a dry spell at 0.5, twenty days apart. Two storm-walkers; a fee of 200 silver times the colony's wealth factor (120 to
    400). The colony's high ground is the relay mast's choice of it (`RelayMast.Site`: eight to forty cells out, by natural
    rock first), named on the card "the high ground by the rocks" or "the open ground by the colony" as it is. From dusk
    each sets a rod of theirs there (`Rimfolk_PEv6_Rod`, the Conclave's own `Rimfolk_StormglassRod`, theirs, so it takes the
    lightning near it as the colony's rod does), then they keep the night beside them (`_KeepNight`, sparks and the vials'
    glow); with the second answer the colony's best at the fields sits up with them (kept beside the rods) and at first light
    learns (900 Plants) and reads the glass for a season (`Rimfolk_GlassTaught`, the Conclave's lesson). At first light (6h)
    every dry spell on the map ends (`GameCondition.End`) and the land's own rain begins, its length the rain's own; one time
    in four the land's own thunderstorm instead, its lightning the game's. The fields by the weather reckon it. Two hours on
    they take the rods down and go, +3.
  - **The tide read** (Conclave; `TideRead`): while a season's watch runs on a home (`GlassWatch`) and nothing is held there,
    the game's `PsychicDrone` or `PsychicSoothe` the storyteller sends (not a quest's) goes into the game's own queue 18 to 30
    hours on, as a condition of the sky does (`Patch_TideHold`, beside `Patch_GlassHold`, leaving a firing another hold took).
    The sex it will touch is picked then as the game picks it (a free colonist's), kept (`TideRecord`) and given to the tide
    when it comes (`Patch_TideTouchesDrone`, `Patch_TideTouchesSoothe`: prefixes on the workers' `DoConditionAndLetter`), so the
    vial-runner's letter names everyone it will touch; the runner says it at the gate. When a held drone comes, a reader comes
    within the hour (`Rimfolk_Evt_TideReader`): an hour sitting with the colonist it touches worst (their mood the lowest;
    round 1's `PeopleWorkOn`, `Rimfolk_PEv6_SitWith`, held where they stand) and `Rimfolk_Thought_SatThroughDrone` (+8, two
    days); or with the two worst one after the other; +2. A held tide that never comes is let go after three days.
  - **The storm tower** (Conclave; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_StormTower`, `CampWorker_StormTower`): spring and summer, on land with
    thunderstorms of its own, a high ground. Two readers and an apprentice a week, in tents at the high ground; once settled
    they set up a glass mast (`Rimfolk_StormglassMast`, drawn by `Tools/make_storm_glass.py`) and two of their rods, which take
    the lightning near them. Each storm over the land is counted once and written down (told, the count in their farewell).
    By night one reader at a time keeps the watch at the mast (`_TowerWatch`). Asks: the colony's best at the fields sits the
    night watch (an evening lesson, 200 Plants an hour, and reads the glass for a season when they go); the colony's doctor
    sees to them when one is ill. Going (on good terms): the rods and mast taken down, a sealed vial (`Rimfolk_StormVial`,
    drawn, sellable) handed in at the gate, and the season's forecast: a season's watch begun free (`GlassWatch.Begin`); +3 (+2
    more with the second answer's eight meals). It can turn, once a stay each: in a storm, at 0.3 through the shared harm
    budget (the camps' embers' kind, `HarmKinds.CampLeft`), one of the game's lightning strikes lands on open ground with
    something to burn 20 to 28 cells from the camp, past every rod, never within five cells of anyone and never in the
    colony's home area; they beat the fire out (told). After the second day, at night in the rain or below ten degrees, at
    0.25 the apprentice takes a chill (the game's flu, mild; `HarmKinds.CampFever` and the illness budget; told, the doctor's
    ask open).
  - **Fire in the canopy** (Mossborn; `CanopyFire`): six fires or more on trees or among them on a home map (Seasonal
    Weather's wildfire, a dry storm, anything); once a fire (two days) at 0.6, fifteen days apart. Three to five thorn-guards in
    at the edge nearest it, straight to the fires (`Rimfolk_PEv6_Firefight`, `JobDriver_PEv6Firefight`: the nearest fire within
    45 cells of where it was, beaten with the game's own beating, `Pawn_NativeVerbs.TryBeatFire`, then the next). The letter
    asks what follows (no answer: the first): when no fire is left within their reach they say so and go, +4, the trees burned
    told; with the second answer their people come back half a day after it is out to replant the burn (the camp after the
    fire, due at once); or thanked, they go now.
  - **Seeds of the old wood** (Mossborn; `OldWoodSeeds`, the egg-trader's shape): a plant the colony grows nowhere (no zone,
    no pot), sown in the ground (not a tree, not a cave plant), its research done, its season now, within the best grower's
    skill; the player's plant mods first (`SeedPackages`: Vanilla Plants Expanded, More Plants, Succulents, Flowers, Alpha
    Biomes), the game's own after; and a plot for it: four by four of good soil (three by three at a pinch), out of every zone
    and building, near the colony's nearest field. The price a quarter of the plot's first harvest (60 to 300), or a quarter
    again of it in the colony's raw harvest it has most of (carried out). The herb-trader and the grower walk to the plot, the
    trader sows it with the grower beside them (`Rimfolk_PEv6_Seeds`, round 1's work at a place, three hours); then each cell
    is planted (what grew wild there cut), the cells become the colony's growing zone of that plant, the grower learns (1,200
    Plants); +2.
  - **After the fire** (Mossborn; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_AfterFire`, `CampWorker_AfterFire`): ten new burned trees or more on a
    home map (every tree's burned form, the game's `BurnedTree`), the fire out; or a blight on six plants; once each at 0.5,
    thirty days apart; or due from the thorn-guards' second answer. A grove-warden and seed-carriers, three to five, a week in
    the burn (its middle, reaching its farthest: 6 to 30 cells). By day: any fire there again first, then each burned tree
    cut (`_CutBurned`; its wood the colony's, lying where it stood) or each blighted plant cut out, then saplings (`_Sapling`,
    the land's own tree, sown: the colony's planting in their ledger), up to 24, three cells apart, out of the colony's home
    and fields. At night they sing at their fire (19h to 22h, `_Sing`). Asks: food for the week (theirs to ask, ten meals; or
    sent with the second answer); the colony's planter beside them (a lesson, +2 more going). The term: a tree felled by the
    colony within the planting while they are there (`MossLedger.Notify_Felled`) is a wrong: -6, a `slighted` deed, they leave
    (`CC_Camp_End_felled`). It can turn, once a stay after the first day, by day in dry weather above fifteen degrees, at 0.15
    through the shared harm budget (`HarmKinds.CampLeft`): the fire starts again in the ash, out of the colony's home and four
    cells clear of anyone, and they beat it out (told). Going: +4 when they cut or planted.
  - **A contract on the colony's enemy** (Banner; `BannerContract`): a camp within twelve tiles of a people at war with the
    colony and the Banner both (a site first, from the game's quests and sites, else a town), no other contract open, a
    fighter who may leave. A captain; the price by the storyteller's points (0.6 a point for a camp, 0.9 for a town, 200 to
    2,000), or half again with the company's share paid up front. The colony has fifteen days to get a caravan there with at
    least one of its people; once the colony's people are on the site's map (the game's own, made when they arrive), the
    company (three to eight by the points, a sergeant, soldiers and shots, their age's issue) comes in beside them within the
    hour and goes for everyone up and hostile there (the game's assault). When nobody hostile is left up, half the silver
    lying there is the company's (taken, told) unless paid up front; its dead are named for the Roll; `contractKept`, +4;
    they march off. Not reached in time: they keep their pay, -3. The camp gone first: half the price back by their courier.
  - **An old soldier settles** (Banner; `OldSoldier`; adds a person): a soldier of the Banner, 45 to 62, good with a blade and a
    gun, with a war-horse (`Mounts`: the game's `Horse`; Vanilla Genetics Expanded's `GR_ParagonHorse` in the spacer age) and
    the kit of the Banner's age. Taken in: they join; the horse is the colony's, tame, obedient, bonded to them and theirs
    (with Giddy-Up 2, a mount); +2. Once a year (sixty days) a runner calls them to the muster at the Banner's nearest town
    (`Rimfolk_Evt_BannerMuster`): sent (round 2's season away, the horse with them; a week there; home with 1,500 Melee and
