    `Rimfolk_Thought_Mustered`, +3), the fee (150 times the wealth factor, 100 to 300), or neither (-5, `refused`). Bought out
    when they settle (three years' fees), never called. Sent on, the horse goes with them.
  - **The other side's contract** (Banner; `OtherSideContract`): a raid the storyteller sends to a home (`IncidentWorker_RaidEnemy`,
    not a quest's), the Banner at peace and not hired these 45 days, a people that could have hired it (at war with the colony,
    at peace with the Banner, able to raid; the raid's own people if it is one): at 0.25 times the lean on arms the raid is
    held in the game's queue 18 to 30 hours, set to come from that people (`Patch_BannerHired`, after the holds for a warning,
    leaving a firing another hold took). The sergeant comes under a white flag (if he can't, nothing is held). Buy the
    contract (0.6 silver a point, 200 to 2,500): when the raid comes, two to six of the company come in on the colony's side
    (the game's allies), +3. Pay them to stand aside (0.3 a point, 100 to 1,200): the raid comes as sent, +1. Let them march
    (no answer): the raid comes at the storyteller's own size, a little over a third of its points the Banner's soldiers under
    that people's colours in the raid's own lord. A held raid that never comes: the colony's silver back by courier.
  - **A company on the march** (Banner; a camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_CompanyMarch`, `CampWorker_CompanyMarch`): a people at war with
    the Banner to march against. Eight to twelve soldiers (a sergeant, soldiers and shots) a night or two at the edge nearest
    the colony, bedrolls round their fire, a pack animal; they take up arms against any threat on the map (`fights`), buy
    meals and road food at the colony's market, and drill at dawn (5h to 7h, `_Drill`). The second answer sells them twenty
    meals at the gate for a quarter over their worth. Asks: the sergeant drills one of the colony (a melee lesson); they ask
    whether one of the colony's fighters would enlist for the season (round 2's season away to the Banner's town, fifteen
    days, home with 150 silver, 2,500 Melee and Shooting). A soldier who asks to stay and is taken in (the camps' own joining)
    costs 4 with the Banner, told. It can turn, once a stay each: by day, only while Rimfolk's world events may bring a fight,
    at 0.2 the people they march against catches them here (a band against the camp, `CampRaids.Send`; the colony asked what
    to do); in the evening with one of the colony at their fire, a bet, and at 0.3 through the shared harm budget
    (`HarmKinds.CampBrawl`, the outsiders' quiet brawl so neither people counts a blow as an attack) the two come to blows
    (the game's own social fight; the camp's tension +10; told). Going: +2 when nobody stayed.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: none of a new kind. The stray strike and the fire in the ash are the camps' embers' kind
    (`CampLeft`), the apprentice's chill the camps' fever (`CampFever`) with the illness budget, the bet's brawl the camps'
    brawl (`CampBrawl`), each through the shared budget and told; the fights (the contract's, the hired raid, the band against
    the company), the storm's lightning and the fires the thorn-guards fight are the game's own, and shown on the cards.
    Saved: `PeopleEvents6Book` (the dry spells, fires and blights rolled, the burns reckoned, the tides held, the camps after
    the fire asked for, the contracts, the old soldiers, the hired raids) and the camps' states, modelled in
    `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: `PeopleEvents5.Hour` and `Hourly`, round 2's `SeasonAway.Kinds` (the muster, the
    season enlisted), `MossLedger.Notify_Felled` (the planting), `FactsMath`, the def check's camp counts. Four game hooks:
    `Patch_TideHold`, `Patch_TideTouchesDrone`, `Patch_TideTouchesSoothe`, `Patch_BannerHired`, each off with the deeper game
    hooks. Dev actions "Peoples' events 6: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps*
    (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).
- **The peoples' own events, round 7** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.271.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 60, 61, 62, 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69 and 70 (the Kiln Guild, the Signal Line and the
  Deepwell Union); `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events7/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents7Math.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents7Tests.cs` ("the peoples' events, round 7: "). As rounds 1 to 6: only from a people of its calling
  at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`, `PeoplesD.Theirs`), in the Visitors group, base chance 0.3 to 0.5, 40 to 60 days apart (the
  Line's call once a season, 15) and never in the first ten days, every age in its own form, played out on the map. Four come
  from code at their moment (base chance 0, `PeopleEvents2.Fire`), each at a chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors:
  the guild's master after a fine piece, the journeyman a year after a wander-year, the union's shift-captain when the
  colony's people are worn down, and the strikers when a strike is called. Round 6's hour hands on to round 7's
  (`PeopleEvents6.Hour` and `Hourly`, one line each).
  - **The master's mark** (Guild; `MastersMark`): the fine-piece hook (`Patch_ArcMade`) notes a masterwork or a legend made by
    one of the colony at a home (six kept). A day or more after, while it is ten days fresh, the piece still the colony's at
    that home (lying there, or held, carried or worn by someone there) and its maker home, it is rolled once at 0.6, twenty
    days apart: a master of the guild (`Rimfolk_KilnGuild_MasterTrader`, 14 to 18 in the piece's skill) comes to the gate.
    Let in, they walk to the piece (or to whoever holds or wears it) and go over it for an hour (`Rimfolk_PEv7_Judge`), the
    maker standing by (`_StandBy`); with the second answer the maker learns from it (800 in the piece's skill: Artistic for a
    work of art, else Crafting). The verdict: a fault found at one masterwork in five and one legend in twelve, a sting
    (`Rimfolk_Thought_MarkFault`, -5 for 8 days); else the guild's mark (`Rimfolk_Thought_MarkTrue`, +6 for 20 days), the guild
    remembers the maker by name for it (the new deed `markTrue`, through `KinMemory.Note`, which the colony's renown reads),
    and with Vanilla Skills Expanded the quality expertise (`QualityExpert`) for a piece made at a bench, where the maker has
    room for it. Either way +2, and the master says the verdict and the maker answers where they stand.
  - **Come back better** (Guild; `ComeBackBetter`): a wander-year that ended well (the mission's end, `Patch_FactionMemory`) notes
    its journeyman, kept in the world by the ledger (`KeepReason` "comeBack", in `LedgerKeep`) for a year (sixty days). Then, the
    guild at peace, the maker home, the journeyman free in the world and still the guild's, they come back to the gate, their
    Crafting and Artistic at a master's 14 or more, with a masterwork of their own making (the guild's small art of its age, of
    marble, granite or wood, `ThingRoles.SmallArt`) as a gift, set down at the gate whatever the answer; the maker gets a
    lasting memory (`Rimfolk_Thought_ApprenticeMaster`, +5 for 60 days), +4. The first answer has the maker sit with them a
    while, the second has them work a morning at the bench together (a Crafting lesson, the teacher taught), the third thanks
    them at the gate. The guild at war when it is due puts it off a season; two years on it is let go.
  - **A work that stays** (Guild; `WorkThatStays`, `CampWorker_WorkThatStays`): what they build is the guild's choice by
    what the colony has, within forty-five cells of its middle: a carved bridge first (marked like the one at
    Hardwater), across the water nearest the colony from bank to bank, two cells wide and two to twelve long, every cell
    one the bridge can stand on, no bridge within four cells; of Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Architect's stone bridge
    of the stone the colony holds most of, else the game's wooden bridge, at its own cost a cell (laid as the game lays
    a bridge, a foundation over the water). Else a great work of art in its hall, its largest dining, recreation or
    throne room, clear of doors: Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Art's grand statue or monument, or the game's grand
    sculpture, which comes first changing with the season; else a fountain where the colony gathers (by its gathering
    spot, else its middle): Alpha Props - Parks' fountains, then Dubs Bad Hygiene's. Only of stone or wood the colony
    holds enough of, and only what the colony itself could build (its research done). The card names the work, the stone
    and how much (the work's own cost, fifty at least). Three journeymen camp five to eight days nearby; once settled,
    the stone is carried out to them from the stores (round 1's carry-out to a camp, taken at once and set down there if
    nobody can carry it) and stacked at the work, theirs; they carve at it by day (8h to 17h, `_Carve`, chips of stone),
    a day counted once, and it stands once two thirds of their stay are worked: the building spawned, the colony's,
    excellent, its art a journeyman's (`CompArt.JustCreatedBy`), or the bridge laid cell by cell; the stone used, any
    over left for the colony; told, the guild remembers it (`campHosted`), +4 as they go. The second answer (or the
    camp's ask) has the colony's best at the art work beside them through the working hours (round 1's work beside, 120
    Artistic an hour). It can turn, once a stay each: after a day's work at 0.3 a block cracks and the work needs a
    quarter more (carried out the same way); when the stores don't hold what the work still needs, they wait a day, then
    a second (their stay the longer), then make do with what they were given (it stands good, a grade plainer), or go if
    they were given none; after two days' work at 0.2 the oldest judges a journeyman's day bad and has it torn down
    (`_TearDown`, rubble; the day lost, a day longer).
  - **A voice for the colony** (Line; `VoiceForColony`): once a season (15 days) an operator comes with one call on the Line's
    masts at the Line's price (50 silver, its price for news; 150 for hands): a trader of goods or of arms (the game's own
    caravan of that kind, `TraderCaravanArrival` with its trader kind, from the nearest and friendliest people at peace that
    sends one, never slavers, pirates or tribute collectors: `PeopleEvents7Math.TradeKind`), hands (the game's own wanderer
    who joins), or a good word to the people the colony stands worst with (+6). With a radio (a powered comms console, else
    the colony's own relay mast while it sings) the operator walks to it and calls an hour (`_Call`, sparks), answered three
    to six hours on; without one (as a colony before the radio has none) a runner of the Line carries it off,
    answered in a day or two. Unanswered (nobody could come), the Line sends the silver back.
  - **A mast at a friend's town** (Line; `TownMast`): the friend is a notable alive and not at war with the colony whom it has
    written to, at a town of theirs that stands, not one of the Line's; the one written to most, the nearest next. For 150
    silver and ten a tile (200 to 450), or as many components as that is worth, a lineman walks there (a walking caravan's
    days) and raises a mast in a day, told when it stands; from then the colony's letters to that town and the answers take
    half the days (`NeighbourLetters` through `PeopleEvents7.Relays`, the colony's own mast's rule beside it; the two together
    still half), while the Line is at peace. It stands at the town on the world, not on the colony's map, and the words say so;
    lost with the town, told.
  - **The line crew** (Line; `LineCrew`, `CampWorker_LineCrew`): three or four linesmen (a relay-keeper, an operator,
    linesmen) camp a week on the colony's high ground (round 6's `HighGround`, the relay mast's choice) and the keeper raises a
    mast by their fire in two hours (the Line's own `Rimfolk_RelayMast`, theirs; before the industrial age a flag-and-lamp
    tower, `Rimfolk_SignalTower`, drawn by `Tools/make_signal_tower.py`). By day they string wire out toward the colony
    (`_String`, sparks); while it stands the colony's letters go by their wire (half the days); once a night one of them sits at
    the radio by the fire (`_Listen`; the tower's watcher reads the next tower's lamps) and the region's news comes in: a line
    of the facts service's news for the Line's nearest town, told, the place it names heard of (`HeardPlaces.Heard`, from the
    Line, through the listener). They ask for food (eight meals; not when it went with them from the gate, the second answer)
    and four components; the colony may keep the mast as its own relay mast for 300 silver (by its wealth), only while it has
    none and only a mast (the tower goes with them). It can turn, once a stay each, by day in a thunderstorm: a lineman climbs
    the mast to make it fast (`_Climb`) and at 0.15 through the shared harm budget (the dangers on the map, `HarmKinds.Dangers`)
    falls when the climb is done (a cracked or bruised leg, 4 to 10; told; the colony's doctor may tend them); with nobody
    within four cells of it, at 0.25 (the camps' embers' kind, `CampLeft`, for the fire it may start) the game's own bolt
    comes down on the mast and breaks it, and they raise another half a day on, beating out any fire. Going: the mast taken
    down (or left, the colony's), +3.
  - **The pit's cave-in** (Union; `PitCaveIn`, `CaveInAway`): a union pit within twelve tiles (its nearest town). The runner
    asks for the colony's best miner and its best doctor besides, for four to six days, for 40 silver a day each. Sent (both,
    never two of the colony's last three grown-ups; or the miner alone), each sets out as a caravan of one (round 2's season
    away, key "cavein") on the game's own roads. At the pit each day is a shift: the miner learns Mining, the doctor
    Medicine (450 a shift); one shift in twenty (the drill rig's own chance and kind, `HarmKinds.UnionDrill`, through the
    shared budget and the hurt cap; at most once each, kept in the visit's touched) a fall of rock crushes a foot or a hand
    (3 to 9), told as word from the pit at once and bound there (by the colony's doctor if they are at the pit, their skill
    the tending's quality). The crush happens away, at a real place on the world; the colonist comes home with the bound wound.
    Home: the union's pay at their feet, a good memory (`Rimfolk_Thought_DugThemOut`, +5 for 15 days), and +6 each (twelve for
    the two sent, six alone).
  - **Oil in the ground** (Union; `OilInGround`): two events, one a form. With Rimefeller and its wells open to the colony
    (`OilWell`, else `DeepOilWell`, their research done), `Rimfolk_Evt_OilInGround`: the oil is the cell nearest the colony's
    middle (within fifty) where Rimefeller's own well may be placed (`GenConstruct.CanPlaceBlueprintAt`, its placing reading
    its deposits), looked for once an hour. An assayer and a driller drill there six hours (`_Sink`), and Rimefeller's well
    stands there, the colony's, told; for 450 silver by the colony's wealth (300 to 900), or for a year's share: four
    seasons, each the union's courier collecting thirty chemfuel from the stores (`Couriers.TakeFromStores`), else its worth
    in silver, else it is let go, told each time. Without it, `Rimfolk_Evt_DeepSeam`: the assayer marks the deep seam nearest
    the colony (round F's `Seam`, the game's deep resources) for 60 silver, an hour's survey there, told with its ore and
    amount, and the union's drill for a share (`Rimfolk_Evt_UnionDrill`) comes for it a day later; with the second answer
    the colony's best miner walks the ground with them (900 Mining). +3.
  - **The organizer's evening** (Union; `OrganizersEvening`): at a home at 16h, once a day, the colony's people worn down
    (the heart's strain of the colony at forty or more, or the long hours in force) and a petition the council could grant
    (to lift the long hours when they are in force; else the days of rest, `Council_Decree_Rest`, not in force and enactable
    through its cooldown), at 0.4, thirty days apart: a shift-captain at the gate. The first answer: they speak at the
    colony's fire that evening (a gathering, the captain its guest, their lines about the union's shifts); the second gives
    them supper too (+1). The next morning (7h to 10h) the colonist under the most strain brings the petition through the
    council's own (`DecreeTracker.Petition`, or a request to lift the long hours with their own line), told and said where they
    stand. Granted while it stands (the decree declared, or the long hours lifted): those under strain (30 or more, and the
    one who asked) get `Rimfolk_Thought_PetitionHeard` (+4 for 6 days) and the union +4; refused or lapsed (the council's
    five days, watched for six): `Rimfolk_Thought_PetitionTurnedAway` (-4 for 6 days). "A day of rest a week" in the proposal
    is the council's days of rest: a council keeps no weekly calendar, and the words say "days of rest".
  - **The picket** (Union; `Picket`, `CampWorker_Picket`): a strike called by a union at peace (round F's `UnionStrike`) is
    rolled once within its first three days at 0.5: the strikers ask at the gate for a picket by the colony's road (the second
    answer sends thirty wood for their fire). Four to seven strikers (a shift-captain, miners, a shot-firer) camp beside the
    road where it comes in nearest the colony (else the edge toward it), a fire and songs in the evening (`_Sing`), and they
    take up arms against any threat on the map. They stay while the strike lasts: when it ends they go with their own
    farewell (settled, or by the union's vote when its days run out, marching home singing). Their asks: food for the picket
    line (fifteen meals carried out to them; the strike is settled three hours later, as at round F's gate, and the one who
    went remembers it), and the colony's best miner at their fire of an evening (a visit to the camp); round F's strike visit
    at the gate waits while a picket of that union camps by the road (`!Picket.Here`). It can turn, once a stay, by day after
    their first, only while Rimfolk's world events may bring a fight: at 0.15 strikebreakers of a people at war with the union
    (one at war with the colony too first) come against the camp (a band against a camp, `CampRaids.Send`; the colony asked
    what to do). Going: +3.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: none of a new kind. The crush at the pit is the drill rig's kind (`UnionDrill`), the fall from the
    mast the dangers on the map (`Dangers`), the lightning's fire the camps' embers (`CampLeft`), each through the shared budget
    and told; the strikebreakers' fight, the storm's lightning and the roads to the pit are the game's own, shown on the cards.
    Saved: `PeopleEvents7Book` (the fine pieces, the journeymen due back, the masts at towns, the wells' shares, the evenings,
    the strikes rolled for a picket) and the camps' states, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: round 6's `Hour`
    and `Hourly`, round 2's `SeasonAway.Kinds` (the pit), `Patch_ArcMade` (a fine piece), `Patch_FactionMemory.MissionEnded`
    (a wander-year ended well), `LedgerKeep.StillHolds` (the journeyman kept), `NeighbourLetters` (the letters' road both ways),
    `HappeningWorker_UnionStrike.CanHappen` (the picket's captain settles it), `FactionMemory` (the deed `markTrue`),
    `FactsMath`, the def check's placeholders. No game hooks of its own. Dev actions "Peoples' events 7: ...". The Almanac's
    peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps* (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).
- **The peoples' own events, round 8** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.272.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 71 to 82 (the Last Republic, the Hollow Fleet and the Helix Works);
  `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events8/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents8Math.cs`, `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents8Tests.cs` ("the
  peoples' events, round 8: "). As rounds 1 to 7: only from a people of its calling at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors
  group, base chance 0.3 or 0.4, 45 to 60 days apart (the deserter 50) and never in the first fifteen days (the sleeper and the xenogerm twenty, the order thirty), every
  age in its own form, played out on the map. Four come from code at their moment (base chance 0, `PeopleEvents2.Fire`), each at a
  chance times the storytellers' lean on visitors: the Republic's clerk on polling day, its medal after a deed, its ration post in a
  famine, and one of the hungry at the post asking to join. Round 7's hour hands on to round 8's (`PeopleEvents7.Hour` and `Hourly`,
  one line each). The gifts (the medal, the gene taken out, the xenogerm) keep the peoples' gift rule (`PeopleEvents.MayGive`: once a
  colonist, the gap since the last gift).
  - **An observer at the vote** (Republic; `VoteObserver`): a contested election at a home (`OfficeTracker.election`, not a
    ceremony), rolled once at 0.5, thirty days apart, on polling day morning (two hours before the polls open until four before the
    count): a clerk (`Rimfolk_Republic_Clerk`) at the gate. Let in, the clerk walks the roll (`Rimfolk_PEv8_Roll`, a quarter hour with
    each voter at home, eight at most), waits by the meeting place, and stands by the count (`_StandBy`) while it is read. While the
    clerk is on the map a heckle at the count's speeches comes to blows half as often (`HustingsBrawls`,
    `PeopleEvents8Math.BrawlFactor`). When the result is in (the count seen as a gathering, then the election settled) the clerk calls
    it fair: with a radio at home (a powered comms console, or the relay mast while it sings, `RepublicRadio.HasRadio`) the Republic's
    evening broadcast says so in a letter and everyone at home has `Rimfolk_Thought_FairVote` (+3 for 5 days); without one the clerk
    says they will report it. With the second answer the result goes into the Republic's register: the council's members have
    `Rimfolk_Thought_InTheRegister` (+3 for 15 days). +3 (+5 with the register). A count put off past a day and a half, or read at
    the table without a gathering, sends the clerk home without a word on the radio.
  - **A medal** (Republic; `RepublicMedal`): the colony's deeds (`Reputations`, Social/Gossip/Deeds.cs) of a rescue under fire
    (`Rimfolk_Deed_Rescue`) or the line held in a hard fight (`Rimfolk_Deed_HeldLine`), half a day to four days old, the doer at home
    and free for a gift, rolled once at 0.5, thirty days apart: a clerk and a guard at the gate, the card saying the deed in the deeds'
    own words (`Deeds.TextOf`) and the fight's name. The colonist walks out to the clerk at the gate (since 20 November 2026 the
    clerk waits there for them: "The medal read at the gate" below), the guard stands by, the clerk reads the citation for an
    hour (`_Citation`); with the second answer up to eight free colonists come to stand by and hear it
    (`Rimfolk_Thought_HeardCitation`, +2 for 3 days, for everyone within nine cells). The medal: `Rimfolk_Thought_RepublicMedal` (+6
    for 60 days), the Republic's memory of them by name (the new deed `medal`, `KinMemory.Note`, which the colony's renown reads), and
    from the industrial age on with Vanilla Books Expanded the Republic's newspaper (`VBE_Newspaper`) set down by them. +3. Without
    the colony's talk of deeds (the reputations setting off) no medal comes.
  - **A fugitive of the Republic** (Republic; `RepublicFugitive`): a deserter of the Civic Guard (`Rimfolk_Republic_Guard`) at the
    gate asking to join, a detail of two or three of the Guard close behind (their own visit). Pay the fine (250 silver by the
    colony's wealth, 150 to 500, carried to the detail): the deserter joins, +2. Shelter them: they join, -10
    (`GoodwillWhy.Deserter`), the colony's citizenship papers struck if it holds them (`Papers.Strike`); if that turns the Republic
    against the colony, the detail at the gate fights (the game's own assault), and the card says so beforehand. Hand them over (the
    default): the detail leads them away together, +8.
  - **A ration post** (Republic; `RationPost`, `CampWorker_RationPost`): a world event of hunger in the region (famine, blight,
    locusts: `WorldSituations`, kind "hunger"), rolled once within its first five days at 0.5: a clerk at the gate. A clerk and two
    guards keep a post a week by the colony's road (the picket's own site, `Picket.Site`) with 24 rations (and the colony's ten meals
    with the second answer). By day, every three to six hours, a hungry traveller (or two) of a people at peace with the colony and
    the Republic walks in from the road (`Arrivals.Visit` to their fire), waits half an hour at the fire for a ration (`_Ration`) and
    walks on; with none left they go hungry. Once a stay one of those fed asks the colony to take them in
    (`Rimfolk_Evt_RationJoin`: take them in, give two meals for the road, or not now). Asks: the post buys twenty meals at the
    Republic's fixed price (8 a meal, paid by its clerk), a colony holding the papers draws rations on its ration cards (a survival
    meal each, 4 to 12, from the post's stack, set down by its fire), and the hurt are tended. It can turn, once a stay each: the
    rations run out with someone waiting and, at the camp brawl's rate (`HarmKinds.CampBrawl`), they and a guard come to blows (the
    game's social fight), else words; or, at 0.3, one of a people the Republic is at war with comes and a guard turns them away at the
    fire. Going: +3.
  - **The colony's gravship** (Fleet; `GravshipLog`; Odyssey): the colony's grav engine at home and its pilot (who wears Odyssey's
    pilot assistant, else the best at Intellectual): the Fleet calls the ship on its own channel (no visitor at the gate). Bidden, two
    officers (`Rimfolk_HollowFleet_Officer`) come down near it by shuttle (Royalty's transport ship), by drop pod without Royalty, on
    foot for a Fleet before the industrial age; they walk from part to part (`_Deck`, a quarter hour each: the engine, then Odyssey's
    own list of the ship's parts, five at most) with the pilot standing by at the engine. Then the part from the hull's stores is set
    down by the engine (a minifiable ship's upgrade by the trade tag `GravshipUpgrade`, Odyssey's and Vanilla Gravship Expanded's, one
    the colony hasn't got, under 3000 silver; else 25 gravlite panels), or with the second answer the pilot learns 3000 Intellectual.
    The pilot: `Rimfolk_Thought_ShipLogged` (+4 for 10 days). +10.
  - **A sleeper of theirs** (Fleet; `SleeperOfTheirs`): one of the game's ancient cryptosleep caskets at home with a sleeper in it,
    out of the fog and in reach from the gate: a deck-runner at the gate. The Fleet's sleeper (a deckhand, asleep
    `PeoplesFMath.SleptYears`) is laid in the casket in place of whoever lay there (nobody had seen them), and the casket set apart
    from its group so opening it wakes no other (`groupID`). Handed over: the runner opens it (`_OpenCasket`, an hour), the sleeper
    wakes (the game's cryptosleep sickness) and walks home with them, the Fleet pays 200 silver by the colony's wealth (150 to 400),
    +12. Kept: the colony's doctor opens it and the sleeper joins, -4 (`KeptTheirs`). Left shut: kept on record (`SleeperRecord`);
    woken later at the colony, they walk off to find the Fleet, told.
  - **The order to disembark** (Fleet; `OrderToDisembark`, `DisembarkAway`; Royalty): a colonist holding an Empire title of knight
    or higher (`RoyalTitleDefOf.Knight`'s seniority) who may leave, a Fleet hull within 20 tiles, the Fleet's order not yet given: an
    officer at the gate. Sent, the colonist goes as a caravan of one (round 2's season away, key "disembark") and stays a day and a
    half; home, three to five of the crew (deckhands, an engineer, one of the ship's guard) come in with them and join, and the rest
    found a people of their own near the hull (release B's arising, a cause of its own, `ArisingMath.Disembarked`, never looked for by
    the region's day: a template of scholars, salvagers or traders by the Fleet's age, its faith the Fleet's, warm toward the colony,
    30, or 45 when the second answer let them all find their own way and nobody came home with the colonist), its letter the
    arising's own. Only while new peoples may arise (the setting); without it, the rest stay at the hull. The colonist:
    `Rimfolk_Thought_GaveTheOrder` (+8 for 60 days). +10. Once a Fleet.
  - **A landing party** (Fleet; `LandingParty`, `CampWorker_LandingParty`): four to six crew (an officer, a guard, an engineer,
    deckhands, one of them their medic, one a sleeper lately woken) walk in from where their shuttle set them down and camp five to
    seven days, bunks under one roof (`Hut`), the watch bell rung at 8, 12, 16 and 20h (a moment line), and by day they survey places
    a walk from their camp (`_Survey`, half an hour each, counted in their farewell). Asks: they buy twelve meals at 12 silver each
    (also at the gate, the second answer), their medic sees to the colony's sick (the camps' own tending at a colonist's side), and
    the colony's doctor sees to theirs. Their watch, once a stay, spots a raid the storyteller sends first (`Patch_LineMastWarns`,
    where no mast sings: the raid held a couple of hours in the game's own queue and their warning told now). It can turn: the
    sleeper falls ill (the game's flu, the camps' fever kind, the illness budget; 0.2, once); a deckhand asks to disembark here and
    join (the camp's own join, 0.3 a day), against the officer's wish: the officer has words and the Fleet -3. Going: +3.
  - **A gene taken out** (Works; `GeneTakenOut`; Biotech): a grown colonist free for a gift, no xenogerm replicating, with a harmful
    gene (metabolism above zero, not archite, no other gene of theirs needing it): a sequencer at the gate offers to take the worst
    out, two hours where they stand (`_GeneOut`, the healing cross, the colonist held: round G's hold), for 160 silver and 70 a point
    of metabolism (600 at most), or a genepack. The gene removed, the game's mark of a xenogerm replicating, told. +2.
  - **A whole xenogerm** (Works; `WholeXenogerm`; Biotech): a grown baseliner with nothing put in, free for a gift: a sequencer
    offers a whole xenogerm of one of the Works' own kinds (Biotech's nine, Odyssey's starjack, Alpha Genes' helixien, animusen,
    fleetkind and nereid, Vanilla Races Expanded - Hussar's uhlan; only those in the Works' own set, none with archite genes), for 300
    silver, 15 a gene and 20 a point of complexity (400 to 1500) and two genepacks, or all in silver (300 more). Three hours where they
    stand (`_Xenogerm`): the kind's genes written in as xenogenes, the xenotype set, the game's xenogermination coma and its
    replicating mark. A colonist whose faith holds to other kinds (Biotech's preferred xenotypes) is named on the card; the game's own
    mood follows. +3.
  - **A hybrid beast** (Works; `HybridBeast`; Vanilla Genetics Expanded): a vat-keeper (Animals 9 to 14) at the gate leading a young
    hybrid (twelve of the mod's beasts of the farm and the road, never its odd ones, one that can stand the weather), sold for its
    worth and a fifth (150 at least); bought, it is the colony's, the handler its master; the second answer adds a lesson in Animals
    at the gate. Not bought, the vat-keeper leads it home. +2.
  - **A field lab** (Works; `FieldLab`, `CampWorker_FieldLab`): two sequencers and a vat-keeper camp a week, sampling wild beasts and
    plants a walk from their camp by day (`_FieldSample`, never the colony's fields), with a young hybrid of theirs (Vanilla Genetics
    Expanded). Asks open all week: gene work (300 silver by the colony's wealth; one of round G's genes written into a colonist who
    could take one, at their side, `_LabGene`), the sample (from the rarest blood at home, round G's draw and price, `_LabSample`), a
    genepack sold (180 silver), and their sick tended. It can turn, once a stay each: their hybrid gets loose and turns manhunter at
    0.12 (the camps' beasts' kind, `HarmKinds.DroversBull`, in the shared budget; told as a threat), or a vat-grown of theirs falls
    ill with round G's gene fault at 0.15 (the camps' fever kind and the illness budget). Going: +3.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: none of a new kind. The queue's blows at the post are the camp brawl's (`CampBrawl`), the sleeper's flu
    and the vat-grown's fault the camps' fever (`CampFever`), the loose hybrid the camps' beasts' (`DroversBull`), each through the
    shared budget and told; the detail's fight and the roads to the hull are the game's own, shown on the cards. Saved:
    `PeopleEvents8Book` (the elections and famines rolled for, the deeds rolled for a medal, the sleepers left asleep, the Fleets
    ordered to disembark) and the camps' states, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: round 7's `Hour` and `Hourly`,
    round 2's `SeasonAway.Kinds` (the hull), `HustingsBrawls` (the clerk's calming factor), `Patch_LineMastWarns` (the watch's
    warning), `FactionMemory` (the deed `medal`), `ArisingMath` and `Arising` (the disembarked), `FactsMath`, the def check's
    placeholders. No game hooks of its own. Dev actions "Peoples' events 8: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts,
    trust and camps* (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).
- **The peoples' own events, round 9** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.273.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 84 to 94 (the Lattice, the Choir of the Spire and the Sunken Vault);
  `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events9/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents9Math.cs`, `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents9Tests.cs` ("the
  peoples' events, round 9: "). As rounds 1 to 8: only from a people of its calling at peace (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors
  group, base chance 0.2 to 0.4, 30 to 90 days apart and never in the first ten days (the Lattice's twenty, the vault's fight
  twenty-five), every age in its own form, played out on the map. Two come from code at their moment (base chance 0,
  `PeopleEvents2.Fire`): the Choir's listener for a mind in a long break (at 0.5 times the storytellers' lean on visitors, twenty
  days apart) and the overseer's runner at the end of the evenings at the console. Round 8's hour hands on to round 9's
  (`PeopleEvents8.Hour` and `Hourly`, one line each). The gifts (the link, the hum, the last part) keep the peoples' gift rule
  (`PeopleEvents.MayGive`). Three use round 1's work on a colonist (`PeopleWorkOn`); the rest a job driver of the round's own
  (`JobDriver_PEv9Work`: up to a thing, a person or a cell, a while there with a bar and a mark, the time left kept with the game; with
  `follow`, a person who walks off is followed and the work goes on at their side).
  - **Linked into the Lattice** (Lattice; `LatticeLinked`; Biotech): a mechanitor of the colony's (a mechlink) not linked yet: a
    mech-tender at the gate links them in where they stand (`Rimfolk_PEv9_Link`, two hours, sparks and a bar). The link
    (`Rimfolk_LatticeLink`, `Hediff_LatticeLink`, the Lattice named on it) gives +2 bandwidth (its stages' Biotech stat put on at
    startup, so the def loads without Biotech) for as long as that Lattice is at peace with the colony: the hour it isn't (hostile,
    gone), the link goes quiet for good, told. With the whole link, at dawn about one night in seven they have dreamed another linked
    mind's dream, half good (`Rimfolk_Thought_LatticeDreamGood`, +3 a day) and half bad (`_LatticeDreamBad`, -3). The second answer
    links them for work only: +1 bandwidth, no dreams. +3 (+2).
  - **A mech gone feral** (Lattice; `FeralMech`; Biotech): one of the Lattice's light war mechs (Biotech's militor, scorcher and
    legionary, the game's pikeman, Alpha Mechs' bellicor, artilleron, daggersnout and blitzkrieg, Rimsenal Spacer's psiloid, Advanced
    Armaments' legionary fusilier: the strongest within 0.35 of the home's threat points, else the weakest) comes in at the edge and roams open ground a fair walk out from the colony, attacking whatever comes near (it answers to
    nobody: the game's own hostile mechs, a defend-point group), and two link-wardens come to the gate. The drovers' bull's kind in
    the shared harm budget (`HarmKinds.DroversBull`, at 0.8), only where fights are allowed. Relink: a warden calls it over the link (it
    is the Lattice's again and walks to the gate), relinks it there (`_Relink`, sparks) and they walk home together; the Lattice pays a
    tenth of its worth (60 to 300 silver) for the trouble, +4. Take it down: the wardens assault it (`LordJob_AssaultThings`), the
    colony's fighters free to join (the game's fight); downed, it is finished; its wreck is the colony's, unforbidden. Or the wardens
    go home and it wanders off after a day and a half. `pev:feral`.
  - **A mech yard** (Lattice; `MechYard`, `CampWorker_MechYard`; Biotech): a mech-tender and two link-hands camp five to seven days
    with four to six labour mechs in their group: half rock-cutters (Biotech's constructoids and tunnelers, Rimsenal Spacer's borers),
    half haulers (Biotech's lifters, Rimsenal Spacer's omniservants). By day the rock-cutters cut plain rock
    near the camp by the camps' own rule for what may be taken (`CampTake.PlainRock`, `CampTake.May`, the site's fate), six loads a
    day at most (`_CutRock`, an hour, dust; the game's own `DestroyMined`), and the haulers carry the chunks to a pile beside the camp
    (the game's haul); the rock is left to the colony when they go. The tender and the link-hands see to the mechs (`_TendMech`).
    Ask: hire the mechs for a day (120 silver by wealth; also from the gate, the second answer): the haulers carry the colony's loose
    things into its stockpiles (the game's own storage haul), the rest mend its worn buildings to full (`_Mend`). It can turn, once a
    stay each, by day after their first: a mech slips its link and goes feral (0.25, the drovers' bull's kind; told as a threat, the
    camp's people go after it), or a band of a people at war with the Lattice (an industrial or spacer one first) comes against the
    camp for its mechs (0.3, `CampRaids.Send`). Going: +3.
  - **The hum deepened** (Choir; `HumDeepened`; Royalty): in the evening (16 to 21h) a cantor comes for the colonist whose psylink is
    the highest below six (else the most psychically sensitive without one, 1.3 or more) and sits at their bed through the night,
    humming while they lie listening (`Rimfolk_PEv9_Hum`, five hours, the meditation's mark). By morning the psylink is a level higher
    (with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded, the level's point for one more power) or a first level wakes on the Choir's paths (Harmonist,
    Empath). The price: the colony's dearest piece of art (200 silver's worth at least), carried out; or an evening in which the
    cantor listens to the colony: once the night is over, everyone at home feels it by the listening's own rule (round G's
    `ChoirListening.Heard`, `PeoplesGMath.Felt`: a calm for most, an unease for some), the colonist always calm. +3.
  - **The void listens back** (Choir; `VoidListens`; Anomaly): a colonist shaken by the void (Vanilla Anomaly Expanded - Insanity's
    sanity below half, or one of Anomaly's own memories of the void on them: the inhuman rambling heard, the disturbing talk, the
    darkness, the harbinger's scream, a ritual done on them): a warden of the quiet stays at their side through the day (`_SitWith`,
    eight hours, following them), and three tenths of their sanity returns, those memories are lifted and they have
    `Rimfolk_Thought_QuietWarden` (+4 for 3 days). At the end, or with the second answer after only an hour at the colony's edge
    (`_ListenEdge`), the warden names the void's next threat: one of Anomaly's own threats the game could send to the home now, by its
    own weight, told in a letter. The word holds a month: the storyteller's next threat of the void at that home (an Anomaly threat it
    fires anyway) takes the form named when that one can come then (`VoidListens.Steer`, at the start of the mast's own hook on
    `Storyteller.TryFire`: nothing is added, nothing held), and a message says the warden named it. +3. `pev:void`.
  - **A mind that shouts** (Choir; `MindShouts`): a colonist three hours into a mental break that turns on nobody (not an aggressive
    one, not panic), rolled once a break at 0.5, twenty days apart: a listener at the gate, who heard it from the road. Let in, the
    listener sits beside them two hours, following if they wander (`_SitWith`), and the break ends there (the game's own recovery,
    `Rimfolk_Thought_ChoirSatWith`, +4 a day). With the second answer the colony's best talker sits with them too and learns how
    (1500 Social). A break that ends by itself sends the listener home. +2. `pev:shout`.
  - **A listening ring** (Choir; `ListeningRing`, `CampWorker_ListeningRing`): three to five (a cantor and listeners) camp three to five
    days at the colony's quietest place (of six sites a long walk out, the one with the fewest of the colony's buildings near, then
    the farthest) and sing at their fire at dusk (`_Sing`, the meditation's mark). Late in the evening everyone at home feels it by
    the listening's rule (`PeoplesGMath.Felt`): `Rimfolk_Thought_RingCalm` (+3) or `_RingUnease` (-3), a day; told the first night,
    the moods after. Asks: a psycaster of the colony's (the one with the least focus) sits with them two hours (`_RingSit`) and comes
    back with a full focus and a calm; they ask, by letter, that loud work be kept away at night (also promised at the gate, the
    second answer): a colonist mining, building or taking down within 25 cells of the ring at night is heard there, once a night,
    the camp the tenser (more for a broken promise, told); a promise kept leaves them +2 warmer. It can turn, with Anomaly while the
    void stirs, once a stay at 0.35: their song goes strange, everyone at home who can hear it has `_RingStrange` (-4 a day), told,
    and they pack up and leave. Going: +3.
  - **The seal broken** (Vault; `SealBroken`, `SealRecord`): the vault's town within 30 tiles, fights allowed, three grown colonists
    or more: a surface-runner with the overseer's call. What came up from the lower level: at 0.6 insects (the game's and Vanilla
    Factions Expanded - Insectoids 2's of up to the royal megaspider's weight), else mechs (the game's mechanoid group). Answered, the
    caravan window opens and the call is kept five days (longer while a caravan of two or more grown colonists is on the road to the
    town, the calls to arms' `Answering`); within a tile of the town, the fight is on the game's caravan battle map beside it, what came
    up at 0.6 of the home's threat points assaulting, four of the vault's security at most beside the colony's people
    (`LordJob_AssistColony`). Won (none of what came up on its feet, some of the colony's still), the vault's last goods twice over
    (`HappeningWorker_VaultBarter.Crate`, by its age) and two advanced components are set down by the colony's people, +15, and the
    vault remembers its town defended (`townDefended`). Left before it was won, nothing; nobody came by the day, -3. Or the colony
    sends components (4 to 10) and five medicine for the security instead, remembered as supply, +3.
  - **The last part** (Vault; `LastPart`): a colonist missing an eye, an arm, a hand, a leg or a foot, for whom the colony holds no part
    of any kind (any item an install recipe of any mod puts on that part or what it hangs from), a bed: the vault's medic (Medicine 8
    to 13) with one of the vault's last bionics (the game's bionic eye, arm or leg: no mod in the player's list adds one; the vault
    can't make them, so in every age it is one kept from before). The price: 15 to 30 components and 200 to 500 raw food by the
    colony's wealth, carried out, remembered as a year's supply (a memory of the age rule's gifts at its full weight, 30, which stays
    within a few hundredths of a full year's supply for the year). Fitted by the game's own surgery: by the medic at the colony's bed,
    the colony's doctor at the bedside learning (`Rimfolk_PEv9_Bionic`, round 1's limb fitting), or with the second answer handed over
    at the gate and the game's surgery bill set on the colonist for the colony's own doctor. The card shows the surgeon's chance. +5.
  - **The console that talks to nobody** (Vault; `ConsoleTalk`): the colony's best talker. With a radio (a powered comms console, or the
    Signal Line's mast singing: `VoiceForColony.Radio`) the overseer comes over it (nobody at the gate); without one a surface-runner
    brings a letter. Three evenings (or one, the second answer), at dusk the talker goes to the radio, or writes back at the colony's
    table while that evening's runner waits (`_Console`, an hour; 400 Social each), each evening told. At the end of three, half the
    time the overseer asks for 4 to 10 components or 3 to 8 medicine (`Rimfolk_Evt_ConsoleAsk`: a runner at the gate; give all, half
    or none; remembered as supply, +5 or +2), else tells where an old supply cache of the vault's lies 3 to 9 tiles off: the game's item
    stash with components, survival packs, medicine and one of the vault's last goods, kept 25 days, a place heard of (`HeardPlaces`),
    told in a letter. +4 (one evening +1). `pev:console`.
  - **Surface scouts** (Vault; `SurfaceScouts`, `CampWorker_SurfaceScouts`): three scouts camp a week. Each afternoon (12 to 15h)
    they ask to be taught, by letter, plants, animals or shooting in turn: the colony's best at it teaches two hours at their fire
    (`_Lesson`, the scouts sat round it), each scout 1500 in it, the teacher 250 Social, the vault remembering it as supply (150 silver)
    and, the first time, as one of theirs who learned at the colony (`learnedHere`): both hold its age. Asks besides: their last odds
    and ends set down at their fire for 200 silver by wealth (the vault's goods by its age, components, medicine, survival packs), and
    their hurt tended. One may ask to stay (the camp's own join, 0.15). It can turn, once a stay each: one is sky-sick in the morning
    and keeps to the tent a day (0.4; the camp asks someone of the colony, its best talker, to talk them out, an hour, `_TalkOut`); one
    goes out at dusk in mild weather and is lost, lying out a long walk from the camp (0.3; the camp asks the colony's best with
    animals to look, `_Search`; else they find their way back at first light); one walks up to a wild beast they don't know to fear
    (a hunter or a big one) and it turns on them (0.25, the wild one too close's kind, `HarmKinds.TooClose`, in the shared budget: the
    game's own attack, told as it happens). The second answer sends 80 raw food with them, remembered as supply. Going: +3.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: none of a new kind. The feral mechs (the event's and the yard's) are the drovers' bull's kind
    (`DroversBull`), the beast that turns on a scout the wild one too close's (`TooClose`), each through the shared budget and told;
    the fight with the feral mech, the vault's fight, the band against the yard and the surgery are the game's own, shown on the
    cards. Saved: `PeopleEvents9Book` (the breaks rolled for, the void's word, the vault's calls and their fights), the link (a hediff)
    and the camps' states, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: round 8's `Hour` and `Hourly`, `Patch_LineMastWarns`
    (the void's word, before the mast's own), `FactsMath`, the def check's placeholders. No game hooks of its own. Dev actions
    "Peoples' events 9: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps* (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).
- **The peoples' own events, round 10, the last** (the player's go, 19 November 2026: "Events sounds great"; released 0.274.0)
  `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 96 to 99 (between peoples) and 100 (every people's art handed on), the whole list of 100
  now built; `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events10/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEvents10Math.cs`, `Tools/Tests/PeopleEvents10Tests.cs`
  ("the peoples' events, round 10: "). The first four come from two of Rimfolk's peoples at once (`PeopleEvents10.Pair`: one of each
  calling at peace with the colony, and the second not at war with the first), {FACTION} the first and {ENEMY} the second; each
  arrives under its own lord, and the last answer sends both on. All in the Visitors group, base chance 0.3 to 0.5, 60 days apart, never
  in the first twenty days (the art thirty), every age in its own form by the first people's age, played out on the map. Round 9's hour
  hands on to round 10's (`PeopleEvents9.Hour`, `Hourly` and `WorkDone`, one line each), and round 10's jobs are round 9's work at a
  place (`JobDriver_PEv9Work`, eight jobs of the round's own). Four answers each for the events between peoples (the rule's three and
  a fourth for the second people), three for the art.
  - **The moot over the old wood** (the Deepwell Union and the Mossborn; `WoodMoot`): a shift-captain of the union and a grove-tender
    of the Mossborn at the gate together, the union's pit wanting to sink a shaft under an old wood by a Mossborn grove. The answer
    is the ruling, given after the hearing: the colony's best talker (Social) and both envoys at the colony's table nearest the gate
    (else at the gate, and the card says which) two hours (`_Hear`, the envoys `_Plead`, each saying their case). For the shaft: the
    union +6, the Mossborn -6, remembered as a side taken (`sidedWith`, `tookSides`), and steel a fifth cheaper with every trader for a
    season (15 days). For the wood: the reverse, and herbal medicine a fifth cheaper (the old wood's herbs, the Mossborn's trade). A
    bargain by the talker's Social (25 in 100, 4 a level, at most 85, on the card): struck, the shaft at the wood's edge and a seedling
    for every tree felled, both +3 and `mediated`, steel a tenth cheaper; failed, both -2. The talker learns 500 Social. A letter with
    the ruling, a line of news on the roads, the envoys home. Not heard within eight hours (the talker away, a threat, the envoys
    gone), the ruling goes to them by word, the same. `pev:moot`.
  - **The season's prices** (`Patch_SeasonPrices`, the round's one game hook): a postfix on the game's `Tradeable.GetPriceFor`, idle
    unless a ruling moved a price (`PeopleEvents10Book.AnyPrice`) and with the deeper hooks on; buying and selling move together, so
    the spread stays the game's. At most four kept; one whose season is over is told and dropped.
  - **A toll on the road** (the road league and the Wheel; `RoadToll`): the league's factor (and a guard) at the gate, and a cart train
    of the Wheel stopped just inside the edge of the colony's land: its wheelwright, one or two hands and two or three pack beasts, half
    the time of the Wheel's own caravans (its faction's carriers that suit the land and season, `Couriers.AnimalKind`), else any pack
    beast of the game's or the player's mods big enough to carry that the land allows or that lives wild there and that can stand the
    season (never a predator, an insect, a dryad or a Pokémon), their packs loaded with 25 steel of salvage so they show. Let through: the carts walk across the colony's land to the farthest edge they can reach and off
    (`LordJob_ExitMapNear`, a great herd's crossing), the Wheel +5, the league -5, a side taken. Turned back: out the way they came, the
    reverse. A fair toll: a meal carried out to each, the talker with both at the gate two hours, the toll 35 silver a pack beast which
    the wheelwright pays the factor, both +3 and `mediated`, the talker 400 Social; the carts then go on by the road. Stayed out of:
    both go home, the carts the long way round. The region hears. `pev:toll` for the fair toll.
  - **The lamp and the bell in a plague year** (the hospitaller order and the Quiet Bell; `PlagueYear`): a town of a people at peace
    within 15 tiles under a plague (the region's world event as the illness budget reads a town, `SickHome.TownSickness`). A hospitaller
    and a sexton at the gate together; the order asks for the colony's best doctor, the Bell for its two best at building (the game's
    graves are dug as building), never the doctor. All three, the doctor only, or the diggers only; never so many that fewer than two
    grown-ups stay at home. Each goes as a caravan of one (round 2's season away, kind "plague") for four to six days: each day there
    the doctor 800 Medicine, a digger 500 Construction. As they get there each is lodged at the town for the illness budget's own
    sickness brought home (`SickHome.Lodged`, a journey of its own: the homecoming's one roll, one in six for a stay of a night or more,
    halved with the order's sickhouse for the doctor and again for a colony of the industrial age, half again under the quarantine
    decree; its letter names the town). Home again: the order +8 for its doctor, the Bell +4 a digger, a good mood (`PlagueTown`), the
    plague's world event counts the colony's help (so the town's own people remember it when it ends), and with all three sent each
    people notes a deed of its own, `plagueYear` (+25, slow to fade, a debt of honour, naming the colonist).
  - **Learning traded through the colony** (the learned society and the Sunken Vault; `LearningTraded`): a copyist of the society and a
    technician of the vault ask to sit at the colony's table nearest the gate for three days. Hosted (each under a lord of their own at
    the table): each morning (8 to 11h) the copyist copies four hours with the technician reading the records out (`_Copy`,
    `_ReadOut`); each afternoon (13 to 16h) the colony's best crafter teaches them both two hours at the crafter's bench (`_Teach`,
    `_Learn`; the crafter 250 Social and 150 Crafting, the visitors 800 Crafting). They eat the colony's meals and sleep in its beds,
    else on the floor, as a feast's guests are seen to (`Missions/Hosting.cs`). Three mornings make the copy whole and the society
    leaves a book of it at the table (a textbook for a colony before the industrial age, a schematic after, of good quality); with the
    lessons the vault's craft is remembered as supply (300 silver, which holds its age) and both peoples remember one of theirs who
    learned here (`learnedHere`), which moves both ages by the teaching rule. Thanks +4 each (the copying only, +2). They stay a day
    longer at most if they came late or the work was interrupted. `pev:learning`.
  - **Their art handed on** (every people; `ArtHandedOn`): once a game a people (any of Rimfolk's, or one that arose in their ways) at
    goodwill 50 or more offers the colonist it remembers best for a good turn (`KinMemory.Friend`, at home, grown, under the peoples'
    gift rule) its own art: one of theirs (each calling's own kind) at the gate, and the two of them there three hours (`_ShowArt`,
    `_LearnArt`). With A RimWorld of Magic loaded, the people's class switched on in its settings, and the colonist carrying the latent
    gift its book needs (`TM_Gifted` for a mage's tome, `PhysicalProdigy` for a fighter's), it is the people's class book, set down by
    them and read by the game's own use of the item (`CompUsable.TryStartUseJob`, the mod's own learning effect giving the class). The
    books: the order the Priest's, the herders, the river folk, the Circuit and the Mossborn the Nature tome, the Wardens the Ranger's,
    the Bell and the union the Earth tome, the Banner the Gladiator's, the Guild the Enchanter's, the Lattice, the Wheel and the Signal
    Line Technomancy, the Choir and the Republic the Bard's, the league and the Fleet the Commander's, the pilgrims the Paladin's, the
    society the Arcanist's, the enclave the Psionic's, the Conclave the Lightning tome, the Works the Chronomancer's, the vault the Super
    Soldier serum; each a class among the people's own kinds. Otherwise a passion in their calling's skill (none an interest, an
    interest a burning passion; the league, the pilgrims, the enclave and the Republic Social; the order and the Works Medicine; the
    herders, the river folk and the Circuit Animals; the society, the Conclave and the Fleet Intellectual; the Wardens Shooting; the
    Bell and the Signal Line Construction; the Wheel, the Lattice and the vault Crafting; the Mossborn Plants; the Banner Melee; the
    Guild and the Choir Artistic; the union Mining), or where it burns already (or is a mod's own) a long lesson (6000). A good mood,
    +4 (+8 with the colony's gift in return, 250 silver by wealth), and the colony owes them a lesson (`taught`, which moves their age by
    the teaching rule). Not now: they go home, and the offer may come again. `pev:art`.
  - Harm of Rimfolk's own: none. The sickness from the plague town is the illness budget's own (`HarmKinds.SickHome`, its chance, its
    cap and its letter); the roads are the game's own. Saved: `PeopleEvents10Book` (the season's prices, the peoples that handed on their
    art), modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Small hooks: round 9's `Hour`, `Hourly` and `WorkDone`, round 2's `SeasonAway.Kinds`
    (the plague town), `SickHome.Lodged`, `FactionMemory` (the deed `plagueYear`) and `FavourMath` (a debt of honour). One game hook,
    the season's prices. Dev actions "Peoples' events 10: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and camps*
    (Almanac_PeoplesD.xml).

### The peoples' descriptions, each in its own words (the player's request, 14 November 2026; released 0.252.0)

The player's words (14 November 2026): "i really like the different factions you created, but when i look at their
faction and read the description text with their history etc., it really reads like AI gibberish and I don't understand
what is really meant. also they all follow the same structure and it's always one named individual who started the
faction somehow. can you redo these descriptions and do a better job? each faction shoud have it's own description &
history, written and tailored for it exactly." Built 15 November 2026.

- **Where.** The `<description>` of each of the 23 FactionDefs in `Defs/PeopleDefs/Rimfolk_People_*.xml`, the text of the
  faction's info window (a people that arose in their ways shows its template's). Only the descriptions changed: the
  peoples' talk, faiths, sayings, events, letters and Almanac pages keep their founding stories and founders as they were.
  (Since 20 November 2026 those tell the descriptions' own history: the next section.)
- **How each is written.** In plain words (CLAUDE.md, "Plain, neutral text"): what they do, where and how they live, the
  age they live in, said plainly, what they want from their neighbours and how they treat outsiders, each of those one of
  their events, asks or trades on the map. Their history has a shape of its own: the end of a king's war (the Ashen
  Banner), a place that changed its people over generations (the Choir of the Spire), a vote (the Deepwell Union), a crash
  and a trade (the spacer enclave), an abandoned lab (the Helix Works), a drought and a custom (the herders), an order
  never given (the Hollow Fleet), a flood and an oath (the Kiln Guild), a battlefield (the Lattice), a pact at a ford (the
  road league), a war and a replanting (the Mossborn), a plague (the hospitallers), a quarrel over a shrine (the pilgrims),
  a war's unburied dead (the Quiet Bell), a collapse and a broadcast (the Last Republic), a flood (the river folk), a fire
  (the learned society), a war that cut the roads (the Signal Line), a three-hundred-year record (the Stormglass Conclave),
  an opening and a decline (the Sunken Vault), a contest (the Circuit of Tamers), a vow (the Lantern Wardens), and a
  flight from fire (the Wheel). A founder is named only where the people keep the name in a custom (Aldith's lamp, Tamsa's
  count, Old Brannoc's walk, Captain Imre Sallow's order, Nessa Pell's challenges, Tobin Garrow's lantern); the others are
  told by what happened, never against the founders their talk, faith and page name. No two open the same way; they run
  from about 140 to 190 words, each no longer than it was, with leaders' titles where they help, said differently each
  time.
- **Checked against the map.** Each claim against the people's honours, fears, sayings, titles, faith, events, letters,
  camps, towns and code: the Banner's Roll is read for any colonist who died holding a wall (`Rimfolk_Evt_BannerRoll`),
  the Wheel's towns move a few tiles every 30 days (`WheelTowns`, where the old text said it circled the region every few
  years), the Republic's broadcast is heard with a comms console or the Line's mast (`RepublicRadio`), the Conclave's
  runner comes ahead of a cold snap, heat wave or fallout (`Rimfolk_Evt_GlassReading`). The river folk's free crossing on
  the night of the flood, which nothing in the game plays, is left out; their knot night (`Rimfolk_Evt_KnotNight`) is in.
- **Test.** `Tools/Tests/PeoplesLoreTests.cs` pinned the old shape (three paragraphs, the middle one opening "Their ways
  began" with the founder). Now: two paragraphs or more, each ending a sentence, at most 1200 characters, no "Their ways
  began", no em dash or exclamation mark, the age said, and no two descriptions opening with the same three words. The
  founders' list stays for the talk's check (one piece of each people's talk tells how their ways began).
- **What can't be checked without the game:** how each text sits in the faction's info window.

### The peoples' own beginnings, each told its own way (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.277.2)

The player's words (14 November 2026): "it really reads like AI gibberish and I don't understand what is really meant.
also they all follow the same structure and it's always one named individual who started the faction somehow. can you
redo these descriptions and do a better job? each faction shoud have it's own description & history, written and
tailored for it exactly." The descriptions were rewritten in 0.252.0 (the section above); the go for the rest came on 20
November 2026 ("go ahead with the next tasks"). Until now the faith, the talk and the Almanac page of seventeen peoples
still told their start through a founder their description no longer has, so the two disagreed in the game.

- **What changed.** For each of the seventeen peoples whose description names no founder (the road league, the learned
  society, the spacer enclave, the river folk, the Quiet Bell, the Wheel, the Stormglass Conclave, the Mossborn, the
  Ashen Banner, the Kiln Guild, the Signal Line, the Deepwell Union, the Last Republic, the Helix Works, the Lattice,
  the Choir of the Spire, the Sunken Vault), every text that told their start through a founder now tells the
  description's history: the faith's description (`ideoDescription`, fifteen of them; the league's and the society's
  named nobody, and the society's now says where the fire was, Hesk), the piece of talk on how their ways began (uses
  `chat,know`), their words about their faith face to face (`faithtalk` in `Rimfolk_Pool_OutsiderSays`), the
  Almanac page's point under *Where their ways began*, and every other place that named the founder: the league's call
  for a guard and a beast (`Rimfolk_Evt_LeagueGuard`, its text and a line) and its road gang's farewell
  (`Rimfolk_Evt_RoadGang`), the society's books saved from a fire (`Rimfolk_Evt_ArchiveTrust`), the schoolteacher in the
  society's voice (`Patches/Rimfolk_PeoplesLore.xml`), the society's letter of greetings, the guild's mark
  (`Rimfolk_Evt_GuildMark`) and its work that stays (the bridge "marked like the one at Hardwater", on the page and in
  two code comments), the camps' tales (`Rimfolk_Camp_StormTower`, `_AfterFire`, `_FieldLab`, `_ListeningRing`,
  `_SurfaceScouts`), the enclave's talk of being stranded, the defs' header comments, and the words their towns' and
  peoples' names are made from (`King's Fort`, `Humming Hall`, `Union Seam`, `Winter Garden`, `Mason's Kilns`,
  `Deserter's Field`, `Planter's Grove`, `Lower ...`, `Lineman's Ridge`, `Glassblower's Tower`, `Overseer's Seal`,
  `Cartwright's Yard`, `Chapel Bell` in place of the old founders' names; a town already named keeps its name). The six
  who keep the name (Aldith, Tamsa, Old Brannoc, Tobin Garrow, Nessa Pell, Captain Imre Sallow) keep it everywhere;
  their Almanac points were written again so that no two points open alike, and the pilgrims' talk and page now say what
  the description says (Old Brannoc asked at a door each dusk and blessed the house in the morning, whether it had let
  him in or not).
- **Each in its own voice.** The Almanac in plain words (CLAUDE.md, "Plain, neutral text"); the talk as speech, each
  line one sentence of 90 characters at most, in the people's own manner (the league practical, the enclave dry, the
  river folk easy, the Wheel quick); the bubbles one sentence each; the faiths' descriptions in their creed's own voice,
  the old voice the player enjoys in the religions, still saying plainly what happened. Each beginning keeps its
  description's shape: a pact at a ford, a fire, a crash and a trade, a flood, a war's unburied dead, a flight from
  fire, a three-hundred-year record, a war and a replanting, the end of a king's war, a bridge and an oath, a war that
  cut the roads, a vote, a collapse and a broadcast, an abandoned lab, a battlefield, a place that changed its people
  over generations, an opening. The talk opens on a pin, a vial, a seed, a mark or a number, or with the visitor
  speaking first (the society, the enclave, the Banner), in five or six lines; the Almanac points open each their own
  way, from a short paragraph (the Wheel) to a long one (the pilgrims).
- **True to the description and the map.** No founder's name where the description has none, and nobody new named: those
  the description leaves unnamed stay unnamed (the clerk, the glassblower, the lineman, the postmaster, the deserter,
  the overseer, the woman who began the planting), and what it tells as many people's doing stays theirs (the nine
  waymasters, the hauler's crew, the ferries, the soldiers, the miners' vote, the masons, the lab's own grown, the
  valley on its carts, the Choir's generations). What the old texts claimed and the descriptions don't is gone: a purser
  who sold the cargo, a quartermaster's five hundred unpaid soldiers, a shift-captain's call, the postmaster's election
  in the spring, one night at the Spire's foot, the overseer's name. Every saying, honour, fear, title, event and letter
  of theirs reads the same as before and agrees (the Line's copper aerial from the first coil, the guild's fourth
  bridge, the vault's number on the suit, the Bell's cracked bell, the Wheel's vote never taken).
- **Kept.** Every defName (the talk pieces' names still end with the old founders' names,
  `Rimfolk_OT_PeoplesE_GuildKell` and the like, never shown), tag, placeholder and Almanac keyword; the descriptions
  themselves; nothing in code but comments, nothing saved.
- **Tests.** `Tools/Tests/PeoplesLoreTests.cs`: the founders' list is the six; each of the 23 has a word of its
  beginning (`Beginnings`) that its description, its faith, its talk on how their ways began and the Almanac pages all
  say, and the six founders are named in all four; no def, patch or keyed text names any of the seventeen old founders
  (`Unnamed`); the 23 talk pieces open with 23 different first three words, and the 23 Almanac points too, at 20 lengths
  or more. `PeoplesETests`, `PeoplesFTests` and `PeoplesGTests` read their page for the beginnings in place of the old
  names.
- **What can't be checked without the game:** how the talk reads over the heads at the gate, and the faith's description
  in the Ideology window.

### Magic among the peoples, seen (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.225.0)

The player: "one thing i want to ask whether you integrate rimworld of magic "classes" & spells into our custom made
faction? i don't think i've seen any of them, but they should surely be thematically fitting. since these spells can be
quite strong or even broken, just use them sparingly overall, unless of course the faction revolves around magic or so,
so that it's thematically fitting always"; on the five parts proposed, "yes, that sounds great. add everything ...
visitors should be able to cast benefitial spells if they are happy or allied with me. raiders should be able to cast
harmful spells, although there we might need to revisit because some spells are quite broken, but let's give it a try".
Before this, a share of the peoples' kinds were given a class of A RimWorld of Magic as they were made
(`PeopleKindExtension.gifts`, `Peoples/PeopleGifts.cs`), and nothing showed it: in the player's save 3 of 25 peoples'
pawns had one, unseen. All of it reads the mod by name (`AccessTools.TypeByName`, defs by name); without it nothing
happens. The rules are pure, in `Peoples/Magic/PeoplesMagicMath.cs` (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesMagicTests.cs`, "peoples' magic: ").

- **The peoples built on magic, and the shares** (`PeoplesMagicMath.MagicCallings`, `ShareCap`). By each people's lore,
  four revolve around what the mod does: the Stormglass Conclave (weather felt in the mind), the Mossborn (the forest
  remembers), the Choir of the Spire (they touch other minds) and the Quiet Bell (they listen to the ground for what
  should not stir). Their kinds may have a class up to 15 in a hundred, their leader up to 40; every other people's
  kinds up to 6, their leader up to 15. The defs were reviewed against it: the order's healers 15 to 6 and its prior 35
  to 15, the herders', river folk's and tamers' elder druids 30 and 25 to 15, the wardens' master 25 to 15, the Banner's
  captain 35 to 15, the guild's master 30 to 15, the league's master 20 to 15, the Wheel's 28 to 15, the Line's chief 18
  to 15, the Deepwell boss 18 to 15, the pilgrims' keeper 30 to 15, and their ordinary kinds above 6 brought to 6; the
  Mossborn's tenders, thorns and seed-carriers 10 to 14 (from 4 to 7), their eldest 35; the Conclave's readers 12 (ice
  mages for the rain among them), walkers 11, apprentices an ice mage share of 4, the first reader 15; the Choir's cantors
  and wardens 8, the first voice a minstrel's 5; the Bell's gravewardens 10, sextons 5. A test checks every kind's shares
  against its people's cap.
- **A caster looks like one** (`PeoplesMagic.Dress`, from `PeopleGifts.Give` as a new pawn of the peoples is made,
  whoever gave the class, the gift or the mod's own roll; `PeoplesMagicMath.Garb`). The class's own piece from the mod,
  by the age the people lives in: a priest's or monk's disciple hood, a druid's, geomancer's or summoner's hood of
  protection, an arcanist's arcane hood, a chronomancer's, enchanter's or minstrel's wizard hat, a wandering mage's
  wanderer's cloak; a paladin's Helm of the Valiant in the tribal and medieval ages and the Mantle of Protection over a
  later age's armour; a fire, ice or lightning mage's wand in the old ages in place of their weapon (only one already
  armed), their arcane hood once the age's guns take its place. Worn in place of what it can't be worn with; a signature
  piece it replaces gives it the people's colour. The fighters and the technomancer have no piece of their own in the
  mod, so none. Every piece is in the player's active mods (checked against `docs/player-mods`).
- **Said aloud** (`PeoplesMagicWatch`, every 250 ticks at `Sched.RarePeoplesMagic` = 179). A visitor of the peoples
  with a class, in their first six hours on the map, names their craft to the first colonist with them, who remarks on
  it, the two lines in turn over their heads (`OutsiderTalk.Play`; `Rimfolk_Pool_MagicName`, `Rimfolk_Pool_MagicSeen`,
  by class); a colonist who sees a raider of the peoples with a class within 28 cells names it
  (`Rimfolk_Pool_MagicFoe`), once a people a map every six hours. The people's card (the diplomacy page) says "A few
  among them are druids and rangers." ("Among them are ..., more of them than among most peoples." for a people built
  on magic), the commonest three crafts of its kinds that fit its age and that the mod has switched on for it
  (`PeoplesMagic.Among`, `CardLines`); their letters carry the same words for an aside to mention now and then
  (`among:magic`, `{AMONG}`: "Our druids and rangers send their regards").
- **A spell in peace** (on the pass's tick of the hour). A visitor of a class with a helpful spell (`PeaceSpells`: the
  priest's Advanced Heal and Purify, the paladin's Heal, the druid's Cure Disease and Regenerate, the ice mage's
  Rainmaker) who may (`MayCastInPeace`: not hostile, up and about, no danger on the map, not leaving, not yet this visit,
  and content on the map, mood at half or more, or of a people allied with the colony), rolls 6 in a hundred an hour
  among the peoples built on magic and 3 elsewhere, and casts for whoever needs it: the colony's most hurt (bleeding,
  or wounds of 4 or more), an infection or a flu (what the druid's cure takes at the mod's first level), an old scar, or
  rain in a heat wave, a fire or a week with nothing fallen (not freezing, not while it rains). The cast is the mod's
  own (`RomSpells`: the ability by name, its own `CanCastPowerCheck`, its `GetJob` as its casting for those not of the
  colony asks it, `TryTakeOrderedJob`), so its walk into range, its motes, sounds, mana and cooldown are the mod's.
  Once the mod has the ability on its cooldown and the job is over, it is told: a message
  (`CC_PeoplesMagic_Did_*`; a cure that didn't take is told as tried), a word from the caster and from the one it was
  for, or a colonist out under the rain (`Rimfolk_Pool_MagicCast`, `Rimfolk_Pool_MagicThanks`); a try the mod didn't carry
  out is let go unsaid after an hour. Each visitor at most once a visit (`PeoplesMagicBook.cast`, saved, dropped when they
  leave). With the mod's "AI can cast" off, no visitor is asked to. The enchanter's, geomancer's and technomancer's
  workings last only while their maker keeps them, and the chronomancer's Accelerate Time ages anyone in its field, so
  they have none.
- **In a fight** the mod's own AI casts for every people's casters, as allies and as raiders, by its own settings (AI
  casting, aggressive casting, hard mode, death retaliation): the peoples built on magic bring many, the others few.
  Rimfolk only keeps the mod's most broken spells out of the peoples' hands (`PeoplesMagicMath.KeptOut`, with why;
  `Patch_PeoplesMagicKeptOut` on `TM_Calc.HasResourcesForAbility`, which the mod's casting for those not of the colony
  asks before it casts by itself, and `Patch_PeoplesMagicKeptOutCheck` on `MagicAbility` and `MightAbility`'s
  `CanCastPowerCheck`, which its decision tree for fights asks; both say no, so its AI picks another): the masters'
  Firestorm, Blizzard, Eye of the Storm, Meteor, Holy Wrath, Orbital Strike, Gateway (Fold Reality), Resurrection,
  Summon Poppi, Blood Moon, Scorn, Lich Form and Grave Blade; Lightning Storm, Chronostatic Field, Polymorph, Summon
  Elemental, Sabotage, the Mark-IV turret, Raise Undead and Psychic Shock; the sniper's Headshot, the super soldier's
  60mm mortar and breaching charge, the psionic's storm. Off with the deeper game hooks. A pawn of the peoples who joins
  the colony is the colony's, and the mod's own rules hold. The list is to be watched in a play test.
- Nothing else is saved. The pass's clock is "The peoples' casters" on Rimfolk's clock. Dev actions "Peoples' magic:
  ...": the casters on this map (log), a caster of theirs here now as a visitor, a spell in peace now, what each people
  is known for (log). The Almanac's peoples' pages, *What they wear, carry and know*; README "Magic among the peoples".

### The Stormriders: their gear, their looks and some magic (the player's request and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.266.0)

The player: "And then also in regard to the Storm Riders, I mean, at the moment, most of the NPCs joining my camp as
visitors, etc., are Storm Riders. I mean, I have good relations with them. They have camps nearby, so it makes sense
that they're, you know, largely represented. So I wonder if we maybe can enhance on them a little bit, you know, bring a
little more variety to maybe their gear, how they look like, um, kind of potentially some maybe can do magic and just
kind of spice up the Storm Riders and make them a bit more interesting since they're such an important factor in my
current save. ... And please go ahead with all the changes right now that I told here."

- **What the save showed** (`League_of_Toba_5`). The Stormriders are `Faction_25`, of Elves (Continued)'s
  `DevDesigner_DarkElvesFaction` (an ally, goodwill 64), the dark elf xenotype, a medieval people; not one of Rimfolk's
  peoples. Of their 13 people on the map, 8 were Dreadspears, 2 Darkshards, 2 penitents and a trader, and every one wore
  the same tunic, trousers, boots and cape in the same three colours; the soldiers all the same chainmail, Dreadspear
  armour and helmet and dark elven shield, with a spear or a crossbow. Their hair varied (ten styles among thirteen), no
  one had a tattoo, one had a class of A RimWorld of Magic by the mod's own roll (a chaos mage). The cause is the Elves
  mod's own pawn kinds (its 1.6 `PawnKinds_DarkEvles.xml`): each kind lists its whole outfit as required apparel with
  fixed colours, so the game has nothing left to choose.
- **How it is done.** A profile for another mod's faction by its def's name: `ForeignPeopleDef`
  (`Defs/PeopleDefs/Rimfolk_ForeignPeoples.xml`, `Rimfolk_Foreign_DarkElves`; `Peoples/Foreign/ForeignPeopleDef.cs`),
  read by `ForeignPeoples.Fit` from `Patch_ForeignPeoples`, a postfix on the game's `GenerateNewPawnInternal` like the
  peoples' gifts (fresh pawns only, with the deeper game hooks on: visitors, camps, caravans, guards, raids, town
  defenders made from now on). The pure rules are `ForeignPeoplesMath` (`Tools/Tests/ForeignPeoplesTests.cs`, "the
  Stormriders: "). Every name of another mod is MayRequire'd on it; without the Elves mod nothing matches. Their xenotype,
  race and the kind's own kit stay; no letter, nothing saved.
- **By role** (the pawn kind; a kind no role names, such as a camp's, plays the folk's or, for a trader, the trader's).
  Each piece is a chance of one of a short list, taken among those loaded and wearable by the pawn. A piece is worn only
  where it takes the place of nothing the kind's own kit requires (unless the role names that piece: a civilian's cape or
  tunic) and of nothing that protects more (sharp armour, a hundredth or two of slack: `MayDisplace`), so no one ends up
  less protected or armed than the Elves mod made them.

| Role (kind) | More pieces | Colours | Class of A RimWorld of Magic (share) |
|---|---|---|---|
| trader | 60% a chaperon (Medieval 2), a masked hood, a wide hat (Hats and Rags) or a hood; 50% a vest (Settlers) or quilted vest (Armour Expanded); 40% a backpack (Accessories); 25% the high elven cloak in place of the cape; half carry a dark elven dagger | tunic, trousers, vest, pack in the look's main colour, cape, cloak and hat its second | enchanter 4% |
