  full; `Shown` maps the level onto the picture's height, its lines checked against the script's shapes), the glass in
  light grey on top. The tube's inside is a fifth of the picture's width, so the colour still shows at the smallest
  scale.
- **The game's readout** (`Hud/Patch_TemperatureReadout.cs`, the setting "The game's temperature in colour", with the
  deeper game hooks): `GlobalControls.GlobalControlsOnGUI` draws the line with `Widgets.Label(Rect, string)`, its words
  from the private `TemperatureString`; a transpiler sends that one call (the first label call within three instructions
  of the words) through `Label`, which draws the words a light touch toward the colour (35% of the way from white, so
  they read as the game's white do) and the thermometer, 11x22 (less on a shorter line), just left of where the
  right-aligned words begin (their width measured once per new words and font). Hovering the thermometer or the words
  says the temperature, its word and the colonists' comfortable range. The temperature is the game's own
  `cachedTemperatureStringForTemperature`, the value its words were made from, so colour, height and number always
  agree; the colour, level, tooltip and width are worked out again only when the game's words change (the same string
  until then). Should a game version draw the line some other way, nothing is swapped and a postfix on
  `TemperatureString` wraps the words in the full colour as rich text instead (no thermometer), kept by the words it was
  made from. Off, or should the temperature not be readable, the line is the game's.
- **On a coloured field** (11 November 2026, released 0.213.1; the player, after 0.208.0: "great start! I'd just like a
  larger surface that's colored so it's more clearly visible, perhaps behind the text could be a colored background
  around the size of the field or so"): `Label` draws a rounded field (`UiKit.Round`, the small radius; a plain box
  where the skin's pictures are missing) in the scale's colour at 90% behind the thermometer and the words, from five
  units left of the thermometer to five past the words, the line's height less a unit top and bottom. On it the words
  are drawn in `FieldText`, dark ink (`161616`) or white, whichever reads better (dark on every colour of the scale, at
  least 4.5 to 1), in place of the light tint; the thermometer's fill is the colour halved toward black (`FieldThermo`),
  so it stands out from a field of its own colour (at least 2 to 1). The vitals panel keeps its thermometer icon and
  coloured value, as before.
- **Rimfolk's own panels**: the vitals' outdoor temperature (`HudVitals.Temperature`) takes the same colour
  (`TemperatureScale.Of`) for its value and the same thermometer, filled to the temperature, in place of its icon
  (`HudLine.thermo`, drawn by the classic panels and the own look alike, the icon kept should the pictures be missing);
  its earlier banded scale with green in the middle is gone. Its tooltip still names the band (`HudRank.Band`) and
  the row still turns orange and red at hard frost, fierce heat and beyond. No other panel shows a temperature.

### Vegetarian and carnivore simple meals (the player's request, 11 November 2026; released 0.214.0)

The player: "can i please have dedicated recipes for vegetarian & meat simple meals? so i actually have a dedicated slot
for it and can better manage different diets". The game has vegetarian and carnivore fine and lavish meals but one
simple meal, and none of the player's active mods adds simple variants.

- **The meals** (`Defs/Food/Rimfolk_DietSimpleMeals.xml`): `Rimfolk_MealSimple_Veg` "vegetarian simple meal" and
  `Rimfolk_MealSimple_Meat` "carnivore simple meal", simple meals in every way (`MealCooked`, `MealSimple`
  preferability, 0.9 nutrition, worth 15, work 300), eaten as `EatVegetarian` or `EatMeat`; no DLC, as the game's own
  `_Veg` and `_Meat` meals are base game. Bills `Rimfolk_CookMealSimple_Veg`/`_Meat` (one meal from 0.5 nutrition) and
  `Rimfolk_CookMealSimpleBulk_Veg`/`_Meat` (four from 2, work 1200).
- **Finished at startup** (`Integrations/DietMeals.cs`, the table in `Things/DietMealsMath.cs`): each bill's ingredients,
  fixed and default filters are those of the game's `CookMealFine_Veg`/`_Meat` (or the bulk ones), so other mods' foods
  count as the game counts them; every work table with the game's `CookMealSimple` (or `CookMealSimpleBulk`) gets the
  bill (the game's stoves and campfire, other mods' benches); the meal takes the simple meal's graphic and icon in a
  green or red tint. The fungus meal's rule (other meal bills start with fungus unticked) applies to these as to every
  meal bill.
- **Older saves** (`DietMeals.AllowWhereSimple`, once, `CouncilGameComponent.dietMealsVersion`): a filter saved before
  a def existed leaves it out, so every food policy and every shelf or stockpile (the maps' haul destinations) that
  takes simple meals takes these too; the player then takes them off where they don't belong.
- Rimfolk counts them as simple meals wherever it reads a meal's preferability (feasts, hosting, the road food, the
  rider's supplies, the stores panel); the storage review groups them with the meals. Tested in `DietMealsTests`.

### The gods: fourteen, unseen, and the colony's own book (the player's requests, 11 November 2026; released 0.217.0)

The player approved nine hand-made gods ("alright, great! you can go ahead with full implementation"), then made them an
unseen presence: "the gods should also feel like an ominous presence ... more kind of seen as a sort of storyteller
style aspect of the game ... but not in a way that I see what's going on", and the book only from the pawns' side:
"information about the gods should only ever be like from the point of view of a the pawn. what they know, experienced,
heard, believe, feel like doing etc. ... the gods should be above me as the player as well as the pawns". Then: "I mean
in events etc the god can be named, if we know it's them that caused something". Five more joined the nine: the sun and
the moon (Helios and Selene, the Gift and the Return), a cat (Mog), the rain toad (Murmur) and the restless gold (Ducat).
The characters are `docs/gods-pantheon-brainstorm.md`; the contract the parts build to is `docs/design/gods.md`, its
last section. The generated pantheon of 0.215.0 (below, retired) is replaced; the machinery stays as hidden state.

- **The gods as defs** (`Gods/GodDef.cs`, `Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Gods.xml`): `Rimfolk_God_<Key>` for Hollin, Smoulder,
  Bellwether, Morel, Ennu, Pip, Cirrus, Hush, Undertow, Helios, Selene, Mog, Murmur and Ducat. Each has its short name
  (the label and the `key`), an epithet, names among the peoples by age (the first of each is what a speaker of that age
  says), what it is, how it is seen, its character, what it wants, what pleases and angers it, sayings, believers' lines
  (tagged `[gift]`, `[sign]`, `[wrath]`, `[near]` since 12 November 2026, `[meeting]`), scoffers' answers, what a neighbour writes of its
  hand, two to five stories (one-sentence pieces, a retelling for letters, the signs a story teaches), authored ties with
  words (`GodTieSpec`; a kind of their own for the sun and moon, `GodTieKind.Return`: what is meant for Helios reaches
  Selene, and Helios, `unmoved`, is never moved by favour), who reveres it (Rimfolk's 23 peoples and some of the player's
  mods' factions by name, the rest by kind: `GodLoreMath.Reveres`, `Pantheon.KindsOf`), its colours, a domain and second
  (the stage 2 fallback key only), nature, kind (Undertow the Hunger), its look and sacred animals, and what is seen of it
  before anyone has heard of it (`unheard`).
- **The pantheon from the defs** (`Gods/Pantheon.cs`, `GodBook.version`): one `God` a def (`God.def`, `FromDef` on every
  load), the ties made from the defs on every load and never shifting. An older save's generated gods are dropped on load
  with their standings, acts, ties and vows; one line in the world's voice the next hour (`CC_God_Retired`). Ideology's
  deities are ignored for now. The colony holds the gods of its age's kind.
- **Unseen** (the rule for every part): no page or list of the gods, no favour words, no news line saying what a god
  thinks (favour, a god known, a tie, a fading god are hidden state); the god's card is cryptic, the world's voice, no
  why; a felt god's card is unnamed. `Gods.CardName(god, home, sign)` names a god plainly only when the colony knows it
  was its doing: the colony saw it act plainly (a manifestation, a god drawn near enough to show itself, a disguised god revealing itself:
  `GodLore.MarkActing`), or it learned the sign as the god's own (`GodLore.LearnSign`, also when a story that teaches it
  is heard whole). The name over a god on the map is the colony's name for it, or what is seen of it
  (`GodLore.LabelFor`; a disguised god shows only the name it gives).
- **The hands in the game's events** (`Gods/GodHands.cs`, `GodHandsMath.cs`): a postfix on `IncidentWorker.TryExecute`
  (off with the deeper hooks) notes an event of the table (by def name, else worker class; the game's, the DLCs',
  Rimfolk's own and the player's mods'); the region's hour remarks on it, if the god's quiet spell (20 days) and the home's
  (4 days) are over and the event's own chance holds. A believer (by credence: psychic sensitivity, certainty, age, being
  too clever, what they have seen) says whose hand they take it for, over their head; they may be wrong
  (`GodLoreMath.Attribute`: a god they know of, one they confuse it with, or "something"); while the gods are felt a
  scoffer near them answers. Known for the god's own (`CardName`), it is named plainly and nobody doubts it. Selene's
  hand is seen only at night. The act goes into the hidden history with its witnesses, the book has it as they saw and
  said it, and a neighbour of a people that reveres the god may write of it a few days later (`{GODHAND}`).
- **The colony's own book** (`Gods/GodLore.cs`, a GameComponent): entries with a date, witnesses (colonists by name) or a
  teller (a visitor, a neighbour, a colonist), written once in the voice of its keeper (the chaplain, else Ideology's moral
  guide, else the most devout, else the most lettered: devout, learned or plain; bare with nobody), the hand marked where
  it changes. A god is in it only under the names the colony heard it by, each a page (`LoreName`), until someone works
  out that two names are one (a colonist, `GodLoreMath.ConnectChance`, or a teller saying so). Beliefs side by side, the
  scoffers too; mistakes written as believed, the truth never marked. The API for the other parts: `Saw(pawns, god,
  words)`, `Heard(teller, god, words)`, `Believes(pawn, god, words)`, `Dreamt`, `Prayed`, `LearnSign`; every act
  remembered through `Gods.Remember` gets witnesses when the caller gave none (the colonists awake in sight within 20
  cells, or everyone for a sign with no place) and reaches the book if someone saw it.
- **Stories through people** (`Gods/GodTales.cs`): at the evening fire someone who believes tells another near them the
  next piece of an old story of their gods (in order, never all at once, `GodLoreMath.Next`), a saying, or a word on two
  gods (the keeper, when devout, as a sermon); a visitor near a colonist tells their own gods' stories by their own names
  for them; a neighbour's letter retells one whole (`{GODTALE}`), written into the book only once the words are in the
  letter (`LetterForm.Compose` → `GodTales.Written`). A name heard in a story becomes a page.
- **The book's page** (`Gods/GodLorePage.cs`): the region window's fifth view (address `Gods`, tab "Gods' book"): the
  names down the side, the whole book, the things nobody could name; a page set large with its other names in italics,
  when and from whom it was first heard, what people here believe, and every entry dated, in a readable column. No
  favour, no colour that would give away which names are one.
- **Retired:** the generated pantheon, the patrons (`GodPatronDef`), the domains' names, epithets and symbols (the
  domain table stays as a fallback), the Gods page under Peoples, `GodSymbols` and its textures and script, the card's
  emblem. Dev actions "Gods: ..." (show the gods, favour, how near each god is and a god drawn near (since 12 November
  2026, in place of the realness one), a hand here, every story, work out a name, open the book, make the gods again). Tested in `GodsTests`; saved state modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.

### The gods: the pantheon (0.215.0; retired: the generated pantheon, its patrons and the Gods page, replaced by the section above)

The player: "the concept of gods within RimWorld ... like a pantheon of gods ... that they actually are and interact and
are into the lore and get referred to, and pawns react to gods", and "when I think of gods as kind of one reference, you
know, it's the Greek pantheon ... there's drama between the gods ... there could definitely be also outliers". The whole
design, its decisions, its stages and the contract between the parts are in `docs/design/gods.md`; the brainstorm is
`docs/gods-brainstorm.md`. This is stage 1's core (`Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/`, not `Gods/Presence/`, which the
presence part builds against the same contract).

- **The pantheon** (`Gods/Pantheon.cs`, saved in `Gods/GodBook.cs`): built once per world (an older save on its first
  load), the same for the same world's seed, and kept in the region's day (`RegionBook.Daily`; no pass of its own) as
  peoples and faiths come and go. With Ideology each faith's deities are gods, their domain from their own words, the
  meme they came from, the faith's memes (the game's, Alpha Memes', Vanilla Ideology Expanded's, by defName, others by
  their label's words) and precepts (`GodsMath.DeityDomains`); an animist faith gets spirits, an archist one an
  archotech, an ideological one none. Without Ideology (and for a people with no faith to read) Rimfolk's makers give
  two or three gods by age, ways and land (`GodsMath.MakerDomains`; raiders always a war god). Rimfolk's peoples each
  have a patron (`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Pantheon_Patrons.xml`, `GodPatronDef`), one of their faith's gods where it fits,
  else added to it. The fourteen domains (`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Pantheon_Domains.xml`, `GodDomainDef`) give colours,
  a symbol, names per age form, epithets, a newborn's name and sacred things (animals and plants by defName, from the
  player's active mods). Forms by age (`GodsMath.FormOf`): spirit, old god or saint, half-forgotten or machine god,
  archotech.
- **The ones who don't fit** (`GodKind`): archotechs (every spacer god's form; ignore offerings, judge deeds), the Hunger
  (the Choir's patron, else the world's darkest void god), one trickster, a dead god and a fading god made with the
  world (the old places), the Sleeper imprisoned (the Sunken Vault's), and a newborn of the colony's own faith when its
  deeds keep serving a domain the faith has no god of (`GodsMath.NewbornDue`; three at most, 120 days apart; it grows
  with favour into an ordinary god). A god nobody holds fades, and in time falls silent (`GodsMath.KindNow`).
- **Ties** (`Gods/GodTiesMath.cs`): rivals, lovers, estranged, parent and child, siblings, twins, allies, cast down,
  stole the people; from the natural table by domain, a faith's family, peoples at war or allied, a people that arose
  from another, and chance; four a god at most and one lover; shifting about once in two years each.
- **Natures** (`GodNature`): how fast favour moves (`GodsMath.Speed`, `HalfLifeDays`), what offends most
  (`GodsMath.Offends`), how loudly it answers (`GodsMath.Loudness`).
- **Favour** per god per home, -100 to 100 inside, words outside (`GodsMath.Word`: wrathful, displeased, unknown,
  noticed, pleased, favoured, beloved), drifting back toward unknown (worked out when read, `GodsMath.Drift`), weighed by
  nature and kind (`GodsMath.Scale`), spilling to tied gods (`GodTiesMath.Spill`), remembered as acts, told in the news
  when a known god's word changes. The first sources (`Gods/GodDeeds.cs`): a big
  harvest, a threat beaten off, the dead left lying (the region's day), a great beast brought down, a sacred animal
  slaughtered or hunted (Happenings' death hook), a funeral's eulogy (`Secrets/Vendettas.cs`).
- **The public face** (`Gods/Gods.cs`): `All`, `Of(Faction)`, `OfIdeo`, `ColonyGods(home)`, `Patron(home)` (a known god
  from noticed up), `Favour`, `FavourValue` (for rules, never shown), `AddFavour(god, home, amount, why, source)`,
  `Deed(domain, home, amount, why)`, `Remember(GodAct)` (`Realness` retired 12 November 2026: `GodNear`), `ActsOf`, `TiesOf`, `Rivals`, `Allies`, `NatureOf`,
  `KindOf`, `Loudness`, `Name`, `Epithet`, `GodOf`, `FullName`, `SwearBy(pawn, domain)`, `Fill`/`Args` for `{GOD}`,
  `{GODEPITHET}`, `{GODOF}` (taught to the DefValidator), `Learn`, `Vow`/`EndVow`.
- **The seams** (`Gods/GodPresenceSeam.cs`): `GodPresenceSeam.Manifest` (`Func<PresenceSpec, bool>`) with the plain
  `PresenceSpec` (god, map, cell, kind, avatar, title, text, veiled) and `GodLookSeam.MakeAvatar`
  (`Action<Pawn, God, bool>`), null until the presence part sets them; `Call` and `Make` do nothing then.
- **What the colony knows**: its own faith's gods from the start; others from the neighbours it knows by name, their
  letters, their people on its land (the region's hour), one line in the news a people. Unknown gods are rumours on
  the page.
- **Felt from day one**: colonists swear by their god now and then (`Gods/GodSpeech.cs`, `Rimfolk_Pool_SayGod`) in
  StateSpeech's look and in place of WeatherTalk's storm, cold, heat and first-snow words; letters fill `{GOD}`,
  `{GODEPITHET}`, `{GODOF}` from the writer's god (`GodWords.Letter`), with a handful of lines in the close, the
  postscript and the sermons.
- **The Gods page** (`Gods/GodsPage.cs`): the region window's Peoples view, third mode (address `Peoples/Gods`): the
  colony's gods, the others known, the rumours; the whole pantheon as a web; a god's page with its symbol in its
  colours, what it is, its kind, the colony's standing at each home, who holds it, its domain and sacred things, its
  nature, its ties as a small web and in words, its lore and its remembered acts. Symbols by `Tools/make_god_symbols.py`.
- **Settings**: "Gods" (on), What's on, The gods. "How real are the gods" (Believed, Felt, Walking) was retired on
  12 November 2026: one way, felt, each god as near as what happens draws it (the section "Gods: one way" below).
- Dev actions "Gods: ...". The Almanac page "the gods" (`Council_Alm_C_Gods`). Tested in `GodsTests`.

### Gods: how a god looks and comes (the player's request, 11 November 2026; released 0.216.0)

The presence part of the gods (docs/design/gods.md, "Presence"; brainstorm sections F and G). The player: "they should
then always carry some kind of weight and ominosity with them ... like a godly presence ... imposing sound effects or
really kind of epic ones", and "if I look on the map ... and I see a regular pawn and a god next to it, the god should
... clearly have something about it that shows its godly presence, unless it's actually trying to hide". No generated
music: the game's, the DLCs' and the player's mods' own sounds and songs (A RimWorld of Magic's motes, effecters and
sounds used heavily, the player's word), plus a folder the player fills. Code in `Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Presence/`,
pure rules in `GodPresenceMath.cs` (linked, `GodPresenceTests`).

- **The looks** (`GodLookDef`, `Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_GodLooks.xml`): `Rimfolk_GodLook_<Domain>` for the fourteen
  domains, and age variants where the age changes the god (`_Machine_Old` to the medieval age, `_War_Spacer` and
  `_Craft_Spacer` from the spacer age; `GodLooks.For(domain, age)` takes the narrowest that holds the age,
  `GodPresenceMath.Choose`). Each: two colours, a light's colour and reach, a size, a person's skin, hair and eyes, an
  animal's tint, robes and head pieces in order, a trail, motes, a flash (effecters), a circle, spirits that run out
  (A RimWorld of Magic's spirit and blood wolves), the sky's colour and the wind's stillness, a mark and a wrath's
  mark, the sounds of a sting, a wrath, an omen, a departure and a hum, tracks and darker tracks, and the animals it
  walks as (the player's mods' first: the elves' ancient deer, Odyssey's greatwolf, Alpha Animals' thunderox, night
  ram and phoenixes, Alpha Mechs' aura). Everything is named as text and looked up softly once; `GodPresenceTests`
  checks every name against the player's enabled mods (docs/player-mods/defs.tsv.gz), and each look has a robe of the
  game's own to fall back on.
- **The avatar** (`GodAvatar`, hediff `Rimfolk_GodAvatar` and `HediffComp_GodAvatar`): `GodAvatar.Make(pawn, look,
  name, disguised, colorA, colorB)`, `Reveal`, `Disguise`, `Unmake`, `Of`. Shown (severity 1): a person's skin and hair
  take the look's, a robe and a crown are made (masterwork, the finest stuff allowed, recoloured, locked) and worn, the
  first of each list whose picture exists for the body (`ContentFinder`, so a robe for one body type is skipped for the
  others), what they cover kept in the pack and given back at the end (saved: `given`, `stored`); the hediff's stage
  slows the walk to 0.8; the health page shows "something within (the colony's name for it)". In disguise (severity 0.5) nothing shows, the
  hediff included. The registry (by pawn id) is what every hook looks at first.
- **Drawn larger** (`Patch_GodDrawParms` on `PawnRenderer.GetDrawParms`): the root matrix scaled and lifted, never for
  portraits or the game's cached pictures; an animal's whole body tinted. The game draws pawns on worker threads, so
  the size is worked out each frame on the main thread (`GodAuraDrawer.MapComponentUpdate`, `RefreshSize`) and only
  read by the hook; a shown god is never drawn from the game's small cached picture (`Patch_GodNotCached`).
- **The aura** (`GodAura`, `GodAuraDrawer.MapComponentDraw`; textures by `Tools/make_god_auras.py`): a halo and a
  turning carved ring on the ground (`MoteLow`), a tall glow and a breathing ring behind the body (`PawnRope`), all on
  one 3.2-second pulse, stronger at night; at night a shine over the dark (`VisEffects`, which the night doesn't dim)
  and the light in a person's eyes; a pale god's colours pulled toward their own light by day
  (`GodPresenceMath.DayTint`). The light that follows it is the game's glower on an unsaved, unselectable thing
  (`GodLight`), moved to its cell every quarter second and re-registered. Motes rise every 35 to 55 ticks (the look's,
  with one of Rimfolk's own in its colour). Over it (`MapComponentOnGUI`, at the zooms where names show) the colony's
  name for it, or what is seen of it when nobody here has heard of it (`HediffComp_GodAvatar.Label`, set to
  `GodLore.LabelFor`); in disguise only the name it gives.
- **The trail** (`GodTrails`, `GodPresenceMath.TrailAt`): what lasts (a flower or grass grown at once, a little snow,
  a scorch mark, ash, a puddle) on one step in three, forty a day at most, only on open natural ground, never a field,
  a floor or under a roof, the filth only outside the home area; flecks that fade otherwise.
- **The world turning to it** (`GodReactions`, `JobDriver_BeholdGod`, jobs `Rimfolk_BeholdGod`, `_PrayToGod`,
  `_LieBeforeGod`): as a shown god passes (a look every 250 ticks), up to two who see it within nine cells stop and
  face it for a few seconds, once a day each; a line said aloud at most once in two hours, the same person once in two
  days (pools `Rimfolk_Pool_GodAwe`, `_GodPrayer`; one sentence each, a line naming the god only for a named god). A
  disguised god's tells: a shimmer at night, an animal following it now and then, a remark once a day by a colonist
  with sight 120% (110% at night) or psychic sensitivity 150% within ten cells (`_GodTell`), and no footprints or
  splashes (`Patch_GodNoFootprints`). Never sold, stripped, tamed, captured, arrested, recruited or eaten (patches on
  `TradeUtility.PlayerSellableNow`, `Pawn.AnythingToStrip`, `TameUtility.CanTame`, `GenAI.CanBeCaptured`,
  `GenAI.CanBeArrestedBy`, `Pawn_GuestTracker.Recruitable`, `Corpse.IngestibleNow`).
- **The moment** (`GodPresence.Manifest(look, godName, epithet, map, at, kind, avatar, title, text, veiled, colorA,
  colorB)`, run on real seconds by `GodPresenceComponent`): an omen plays a soft sound and a glimmer, those within
  sixteen cells look up and one speaks (`_GodOmen`), and its text is a line in the news. Every other kind: normal speed
  and the camera there; the music fades over 2.5 seconds and stays silent (`ForceFadeoutAndSilenceFor`); after a 1.6
  second beat the sting (the kind's sounds, then the look's, then the game's start sting, the first two that exist,
  layered; a sustained one held seven seconds), the sky's flash (`GodFlashEvent`), the look's effecters, a burst of
  rays, its circle and spirits, a disguised god revealed and growing over 2.2 seconds, the presence on the sky
  (`GameCondition_GodPresence`: the god's colour, darkened for a wrath, the wind stilled by the look's stillness
  through `Patch_GodStillsWind`, an hour to five by the kind, named plainly or "a strange stillness"), everyone on the
  map turning (animals within forty cells; the devout pray, calm animals lie down, shy wild ones within 22 cells run;
  three speak, `_GodMoment`), and the mark (`GodPresenceMath.MarkFor`: a ring of flowers or scorch marks, frost, ash, a
  spring of shallow water, a tree of the biome, lightning, or the goods of a mark worth having, chosen as the moment
  begins and said on its card: "A god's mark worth having" below); 1.2 seconds later the
  track (`MusicManagerPlay.ForcePlaySong`: the player's own from `Sounds/Rimfolk/Gods/<Domain>/` first, else the look's,
  a wrath's darker ones first, varied by the god and the hour); four seconds after the sting the card. With the music
  off, no fade, silence or track: the sting at once.
- **The card** (`GodCard`, `GodLetter`, `GodCardWindow`, letter `Rimfolk_GodCard`, frame key `GodCard`): sent through
  `Tell.Letter` (important, never held), gold in the stack with a small bell, pausing only for those who pause for
  every letter (a paused game silences the music); opened, dark paper in a double gold border, no symbol: the god named
  set large in its colour only when the colony knows it was its doing (`Gods.CardName`), else veiled and unnamed
  ("Nobody could say what it was"), the words in their own ink, cryptic and in the world's voice (what was seen and
  heard, never why), "Go there" and "Close". Its words by kind and veiled are `CC_GodP_Card_*` when the caller gives none.
- **Settings** (How you're told, On the map): *Gods' auras* (the halo, rings, motes, light and shine) and *Gods'
  music* (the fade, the silence, the track and the hum), both on. Dev actions *Gods: ...* make any person or animal a
  god's (shown or in disguise), bring an animal of a look's kinds, reveal, disguise and unmake, play each kind of
  moment of each look at a cell (veiled or plain), and log what each look finds in the game.
- **The seams** (stage 2's wiring, docs/design/gods.md): the core's `GodPresenceSeam.Manifest` and
  `GodLookSeam.MakeAvatar` are set to `GodPresence.Manifest` and `GodAvatar.Make` (the kinds share their names; a god's
  look is `GodLooks.Named(god.look)` or `GodLooks.For(domain, age)`). The presence builds on its own types and needs
  nothing of the core's.

### Gods on the map (the player's request, 11 November 2026; stage 2; released 0.218.0)

Stage 2's "on the map" part of the gods (`docs/design/gods.md`, "The parts and who builds what", and its last section, the
pantheon; `docs/gods-pantheon-brainstorm.md`, the gods by their short names; brainstorm items 7, 8, 9, 23 and 26). The
player: gods "real and present on the map, with weight", never a plain pawn unless hiding on purpose; "each god should be
individual in what it looks like and whether it has any form at all"; and, binding, the gods are an ominous, unseen
presence, like a storyteller: never show the player what a god thinks, wants or feels about the colony, spell out no
rule, explain nothing. So no favour words where the player reads them (news, cards, inspect lines, This week), no
Almanac page, and This week never names a god; what happens is seen on the map and said by the colonists (one-sentence
bubbles, supper, letters, visitors' tales), and the cards say only what was seen and heard. The colony's book (the
god's acts, `Gods.Remember`) is written from the pawns' side: `GodsOnMapWords.Saw` keeps what someone saw in their own
words ("Tamsin saw frost by a wall in lines that looked like writing"), the core filling in who else could see it.
Favour still moves underneath (`Gods.AddFavour` with no words), and drives what comes.

Code in `Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/OnMap/`, pure rules in `GodsOnMapMath.cs` (linked, `GodsOnMapTests`); defs
`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_GodsOnMap.xml` (the event, three jobs, three memories, the history event, the shared memory, five
deeds), `_Shapes.xml` (who comes as what, and the looks of the beasts and true forms), `_Lines.xml` (the pools said
aloud, the dreams, the memory's talk); keys `Rimfolk_GodsOnMap.xml`; textures `Textures/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Sky/`
(`Tools/make_god_sky.py`). It calls `Gods`, the two seams and the presence part's `GodAvatar`, and compiles against the
core as it stood at its base, reaching each god by its short name.

- **The rhythm** (`GodsOnMapBook`, `GodComings`): kept in the gods' own day and hour (`GodBook.Daily`/`Hourly`, one line
  each; no pass of its own). A coming is planned in the day, a few days ahead, never two at once, from
  day 20, 40 days at least between any two, 120 between strangers and 90 between beasts, one chance in thirty a day
  (`GodsOnMapMath.Due`); a rising after 300 days and at 0.4% a day (`RisingDue`). Its omens are planned with it; the
  coming waits up to a day for a quiet map (and the stranger for `Tell.CanAsk`), then lets go. Short steps run on a due
  tick of the component's own.
- **Who comes as what is data** (`GodShapeDef`, `GodShapes.Of`): a god's own shape by its short name (Hollin, Smoulder,
  Bellwether, Morel, Ennu, Pip, Cirrus, Hush, Undertow, Helios, Selene, Mog, Murmur, Ducat; also its patron's, look's or
  own def's name; `GodShapes.Override` for the hand-made pantheon), else its domain's, else the default: `stranger`,
  `beast`/`beasts`/`look`/`kin`/`kinCount`/`leads`/`feeds`/`sitNear`/`harmIsWorst`/`peace`/`stayDays`, `weather`/
  `voices`, `bodiless`, `omens`, `rises`, `trueForm`/`trueLook` (a creature by name, so a mod's can be it when loaded),
  `returns`, and a `lineTag` for its own lines. Only Ennu comes to the gate; only Bellwether and Mog walk as beasts.
- **The stranger at the gate** (`GodStranger`, `HappeningWorker_GodStranger`, `Rimfolk_Evt_GodStranger` with chance 0):
  made a person of a people at peace, disguised (`GodAvatar.Make` with the name it gives at the door; the god's own name
  over it only once it shows itself), waiting while the colony answers: a bed (Hospitality's guest when it is loaded,
  else `VisitorServices.Lodge`), the gate (the default) or away. Over the stay each hour reads how it goes for them, the
  meals, where they sleep, the talk, kindnesses, the animals' keeping, any blow or theft; every few hours they say
  something a traveller couldn't know (a dead relative's name), the first such kept in the colony's book; the Guest
  remembers the colony's last welcome (`GodsOnMapMath.Remembers`: the event's words at the gate and its own lines say
  so) and a good one is answered seasons later by something left at the gate (`GodGifts.LateGift`). At the end
  (`GodsOnMapMath.Judge`), as the gods are felt it is simply gone; when the god was drawn near enough as it came
  (`StrangerStay.plain`, `GodNear.Plain`) it shows itself at the gate. What follows happens without a
  word of why (`GodGifts.Outcome`): a find, the kindest's lasting gift (felt, said, journalled, never named), its answer
  in the weather, or its domain withheld and a fever on whoever struck it (`Harm.May`, `IllnessBudget`, `Harm.Scale`).
- **The beasts** (`SacredAnimal`): in from the edge with the Appear moment and all a god's presence, wild, the game's own
  leaving, kept fed; over it the colony's name for the god once one of them has heard of it, else what it is seen as
  (`SacredAnimal.Label`). Bellwether, a great white thrumbo (`Rimfolk_GodLook_Bellwether`) with other thrumbos following
  at a distance; someone may sit near him an hour (`JobDriver_SitNearSacredAnimal`; a child on their own now and then)
  and come away changed (`GodsOnMapMath.Sat`: a child touches the horn, a grief eased, a nervous nature gone, a passion
  found); let pass, a strange peace on the colony for a season; harming him or his kin is the worst thing: every god
  colder and every people with someone on the map hears of it (`Rimfolk_HarmedSacredBeast`, the game's own goodwill
  line). Mog, a gray cat (`Rimfolk_GodLook_Mog`) staying a season with one chosen colonist, her own and the colony's cats
  following her, taking food she didn't ask for; marked to be tamed, she goes. Her chosen one has a lucky season while
  she stays (`SacredAnimal.Lucky`): Rimfolk's everyday hurts pass them by (`HurtBar.Lucky`) and every disease event,
  the game's, the mods' and Rimfolk's own, picks someone else (`Patch_MogsLuck` on `IncidentWorker_Disease`); nothing
  says so, and people only remark that her favourite has all the luck. She sees Ennu for what it is: in her season Ennu
  may come to the gate (`GodsOnMapMath.GuestInHerSeason`, past the stranger's own gap, about one season in three), and
  while any stranger stays she leaves her chosen one to trail it a few steps behind, staring; someone who sees it says
  so (`Rimfolk_Pool_MogStares`) and the colony's book has it (`CC_GodM_Saw_Stare`). A large beast of another god may lead
  someone to a find, a cure or a vein. Hurt: the game's revenge, a Wrath moment, a fever at the game's rate; slain, its
  body to ash.
- **Rising and waking** (`GodRising`, `GodWaking`): Hollin's roots drawn up into a shape taller than any tree for an hour
  (`GodSky`, `Rising.png`); Murmur surfacing in the wet ground as Odyssey's colossus toad by name, two hours, then
  sinking. Smoulder: mining under thick rock makes the rock rumble over the miner days apart (`GodsOnMapMath.Warned`),
  stone may fall from the third time (`Harm.Injure`, `HarmKinds.Dangers`, `StoneFalls`), and past every warning
  (`Wakes`, years apart) the deep working closes behind collapsed rock (never on anyone) and, when the deep has drawn
  him near enough (`GodNear`, `TrueForm` by his nearness), Dragon's Descent's true dragon comes up out of the mountain
  for three hours, else the mountain quakes and the winged shadow passes. The rumbles come days apart at a small chance
  in each hour of deep mining, growing after (`DeepNow`), never on a day anyone could name.
- **The sky and the night** (`GodSky`, `GodSkyDrawer`, `WeatherEvent_StillSun`): signs drawn softly on the map, never
  saved: the winged shadow at noon (Dragon's Descent's flight sprites when loaded, else Rimfolk's), a shadow too large, a
  star crossing the wrong way, a white figure at the night's edge that fades as the view comes near, a dark a lamp
  doesn't reach, white threads, the huge moon (as large as its face), a golden beetle; the sun standing still holds the
  shadows through the game's own override for a weather event. The moon's face (`GodsOnMapMath.Face`, one round each
  fifteen-day season) is felt only in words and signs: full, the dreams have their own lines and the moon's returns are
  likeliest; dark, nothing returns and Undertow's signs come half a day early.
- **The moon's return** (`GodReturn`): in the small hours, around the full moon only and a cycle apart at least, for a
  deed of the colony's that day out of the ordinary (`ReturnTrigger`) or its day with the peoples (since 12 November
  2026: `ReturnTonight`, the section "Gods: one way" below), the deed comes back to whoever did it (`ReturnFor`, leaning
  away from the moon's last forms, the next step for the same person again): something found by their bed, a good dream,
  a wound healed; a nightmare, a hard frost about where they sleep, an animal at their door. Whoever was awake sees it,
  it goes in the book, and it is spoken of at breakfast. Selene also notices those who keep the night (`GodOmens.NightWatch`), unseen.
- **Weather as a voice** (`GodWeather`): a god whose shape speaks in the sky answers a change of favour by chance with its
  shape's voices or its domain's (rain, thunder, an eclipse with everyone out of doors stopping to watch, an aurora, a
  cold snap, snow, a heat wave, clear skies, a night of nightmares), as the land and the game's conditions allow. A
  colonist out of doors names it as a belief; there is no news line. Fifteen days apart at a home (ten and a half for a
  god of the sky), its chance growing back after (`GodPaceMath.Ramp`), in a voice it didn't use there last time.
  `GodWeather.Answer(god, map, amount)` is for the worship's festival nights.
- **The omens** (`GodOmens`, `GodOmensOwn`; `GodOmens.Before(god, map, days)` for the other parts): one a day before a
  coming, at most four, the god's own signs (`GodShapeDef.omens`, 26 kinds) or the five any god may send, each at its
  hour (`OmenHour`). Each shows on the map, through the presence's omen moment veiled, a colonist who
  saw it says what they make of it, and the book keeps it; no news line, no god named.
- **What remains** (`GodMarks`): the colony's book, the chronicle, the mark on the land (twenty-four kept five years),
  `Rimfolk_Mem_GodSeen` for those who saw it, deeds for the kindest, the follower, the feeder and whoever struck a god;
  a quiet-day visit to a mark, supper talk, visitors asking.
- **This week** (`GodsOnMapPanels`): Under way lists the stranger staying and the beast on the land as the colony sees
  them, never a god's name, never a coming. Dev actions *Gods: ...* for each part.
### The gods in the world (the player's request, 11 November 2026; released 0.219.0)

Stage 2's world part of `docs/design/gods.md` (brainstorm items 17, 18, 19, 21 and 22, and the drama between the gods),
for the fourteen of `docs/gods-pantheon-brainstorm.md`, built on the core's `Gods` API and the presence seam only
(`Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/World/`; defs `Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_GodsWorld_*.xml`). The gods are unseen (the player's
rule, `docs/design/gods.md`, "The gods are unseen"): no card says why or puts a god's standing, mood or price in words,
and a card names the hand only where the colony knows it (`Gods.CardName`), else "some say" when someone saw it at Felt;
otherwise a god is named only in people's mouths (bubbles, supper, letters, pilgrims, the seer). Favor, ties and
the ways below are hidden state.

- **The frame** (`GodWorld.cs`): kept in the region's day and hour (`RegionBook`, no pass of its own); `GodWorldBook`
  saves the gifts, what is under way (`GodDoing`, bounded), the illnesses eased, when each kind last came, the Hunger's
  account and the day's kindness and cruelty. A god's moment goes through `GodPresenceSeam.Call`; while the presence
  part isn't there, a plain card of what was seen (`GodWorld.Moment`). What is seen and told is kept with
  `Gods.Remember` in the world's voice ("as Mirel of Karond-Keth wrote", `CC_GW_Seen_*`, `CC_GW_Told_*`) for the
  colony's book of the gods. Questions through `Tell.Ask` as one letter class (`GodAsks`, `ChoiceLetter_GodWorld`),
  always asked by a person; questions that can wait wait for `Tell.CanAsk`. Each god's own doings a little more often
  the nearer it is drawn (`GodWorld.Factor(god, map)`, `GodNearMath.WorldFactor`, at most two fifths more); anything
  that hurts someone keeps the game's own rate.
- **A god's ways** (`GodWays.cs`, `GodWaysDef`, `Rimfolk_GodsWorld_Ways.xml`): keyed on the god's short name ("Hollin"),
  the domain tables in `GodWorldMath` only as the fallback. What it gives and to whom, its price and offering, its dream
  (unnamed), its anger at a home (one shape or several), a grudge's shape, its kindness, its temper, its kin, its holy
  place, its feast, its sides in a quarrel, whether it gives blindly (Helios), returns the day (Selene), watches debts
  (Ducat), and the gods that turn from a bargain with it (Undertow).
- **Letters** (`GodLetters.cs`; hooks in `LetterFormShapes` and `LetterForm.Answer`): their letters tell of their god by
  their town's facts (`LetterTells`), in sermons, stories (`st:god`) and chronicles (`chs:god`), each kept with its
  writer's name. The colony's letter written by a rival's faithful or a scoffer may slight their god; their answer says
  they took offense. A friend's invitation to its god's feast by the feast's own name.
- **Diplomacy** (`GodPeoples.cs`): a people sharing a god warms a little each season, a feud that is the gods' cools
  one (never below 0); a holy war; a temple's envoy for a relic. A debt of honour the colony owed, kept or broken
  (`FavoursOwed.Close` calls `GodPeoples.DebtClosed`), moves the standing of the god who watches debts (Ducat).
- **Camps** (`GodCamps.cs`, two `CampWorker`s): pilgrims at a holy place by their god's site (an old tree, a steam
  geyser, a wreck, the graves, the water's edge); a hermit seer whose words are true and dark (`GodCamps.Signs`: a
  quarrel, a grudge, the Hunger owed, the shape of a god's anger or kindness to come, never a god's name or mood).
- **Kindness and anger** (`GodHealth.cs`): each god in its own shape, the game's own incident where there is one (blight,
  cold snap, heat wave, flashstorm, short circuit, solar flare, drought and flood, meteorite, trader) with the game's own
  letter, else a plain card (wild growth, a vein of silver, a machine mended, a cold snap broken, a cat wandering in,
  rain, silver missing from a hoard, a freezer failing); a fever broken in the small hours; a grudge's lightning or
  beasts; Bellwether's kin killed (every people colder) and Mog's (the cats leave, the rats come). Helios gives blindly
  at his own rate. Selene returns the day at night (`FactionMemory.Note` and a prisoner executed fill
  `GodHealth.Deed`) on a night the moon's return chose (`GodReturn`, one rule for both since 12 November 2026): a wound
  healed or something found, or bad dreams. Hurts in the shared
  harm budget (`godBeasts`, `godLightning`, `godPrice`, system `gods`).
- **Gifts** (`GodWorldGifts.cs`): a dream told at breakfast (the god unnamed, `GodWays.Dream`; Selene's tell the gift), a
  night under the open sky, and by morning the change with nothing said of why: a blessing on the body, a RimWorld of
  Magic class or spell scroll (Druid, Necromancer, Technomancer, Storm Born, Heart of Frost, Chronomancer), a gifted
  trait, a psylink and a Vanilla Psycasts Expanded path, gold for silver, a passion, a relic; the price paid the same
  way (an offering left at the gate, a mark, years, a cut). A rival's second dream asks for the gift back.
- **The void** (`GodVoid.cs`): Undertow hears the desperate (easier at the dark of the moon), pays at once and takes
  more each time; Hollin, Bellwether and Ennu turn away, Pip goes quiet; the Choir of the Spire write.
- **The drama** (`GodDrama.cs`): a quarrel seen on opposed sides (`GodWorldMath.Opposed`: storm and dry, cold and warm,
  cold and rain, growth and rot, sun and spark, flow and hoard), each turn the game's weather or a sign on the ground;
  one hunted at the gate; a sentence of an old story at supper (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodMyth`, by the god's key).
- Dev actions "Gods in the world: ...". No Almanac page. Tested in `GodWorldTests`.

### The gods: worship (the player's request, 11 November 2026; released 0.220.0)

Stage 2 of `docs/design/gods.md` ("Worship"): shrines and offerings, prayer in hard moments, festivals, vows, a priest
and the council's questions about the gods, the gods in dreams, and the heart of it (comfort, crises of faith, turning
to another god, scoffers, couples of two gods). The code is `Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Worship/`, the defs
`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Worship*.xml`, the words `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_Worship.xml`. It reaches the gods only
through the core's `Gods` and the two seams: a god's sign goes to `GodPresenceSeam.Call`, and while the presence part
isn't there, to a plain card (`Tell.Letter`) or the news.

- **The unseen rule** (the player's, 11 November 2026): nothing the player reads tells a god's favour, standing, mind
  or rules: not the place's button or inspect line, This week, the news, the cards or the council's questions. A
  question comes from a person, in their words. What people do (a place given, a prayer, a vow, a festival) names the
  god they do it for, by the colony's name for it (`Worship.Called`: its page in the colony's book). What a god may have
  done (an offering gone, a fever eased, a shadow, the clouds turning aside) is told as what was seen, and the hand
  behind it is added after only as the core allows (`Worship.Hand` with `Gods.CardName`: "It was Hollin." where the gods
  walk, the colony has seen the god act plainly or knows the sign; "Some say it was Hollin." at Felt when someone saw
  it; else nothing); a believer says the rest in a bubble. Worship never marks a god as seen acting. The gods' history
  through `Gods.Remember`; the colony's book (`GodLore`) through those who saw a sign, a place given, a festival kept, a
  vow kept or broken or a beast let go (`GodLore.Saw`), a prayer and what followed as the one who prayed tells it
  (`GodLore.Prayed`, a few days apart a person), and a dream told at breakfast (`GodLore.Dreamt`). An offering left, a
  festival let pass and favour stay hidden. Worship has no Almanac page: the gods are learned in play.
- **Places** (`Shrines.cs`): anything with a ritual focus (Ideology's and the mods' altars, ideograms, lecterns,
  slabs), art, Royalty's nature shrines, an ancient terminal, or a building called an altar or a shrine can be given
  to a god the colony knows: a button on it, and a colonist (the priest first, else one who prays to that god) walks
  over and says the words there. In the colony's age it is a shrine, a chapel, a church or a terminal; one in a fine
  room indoors (impressiveness 50, 16 cells) is a temple.
- **Offerings** (`Offerings.cs`): about once a day a place, someone carries something the god likes from the stores
  and sets it down there, forbidden, with a word. Then it is gone by morning, as the gods are felt, or, when the god is
  drawn near enough to show itself, before everyone's eyes in a breath of light (decided once an offering). An animal or
  someone passing may get to it first. Never the flesh of people or insects. Favour by its worth, how well
  it suits the god and the god's nature, hidden.
- **Prayer** (`Prayers.cs`): someone gravely ill, a death, raiders at the gate, a drought in the growing season. The
  devout pray most, a scoffer never; they walk to the god's place in their free time, or kneel where they stand, or say
  it in bed or in the fight. A prayer comforts (in the heart's daily cap). Sometimes something follows (a fever eases at
  night, the grieving are consoled, a fighter's nerve, rain), stronger the nearer the god is, at most once in ten days a
  god at a home and its will to answer growing back slowly after,
  told as what happened after; later the prayer comes good on its own or goes unanswered. The Hunger is never answered
  here: it bargains with the desperate on its own terms (`Gods/World/GodVoid.cs`).
- **The heart** (`FaithHeart.cs`): an unanswered prayer is a crisis of faith about a third of the time (-4, four days;
  with Ideology their certainty shaken); two in a month and they may turn to another god, a rival of the one that
  failed them first. Scoffers (a faith that despises religion, with Ideology one far from sure, else about one in
  seven by who they are; Ideology's deities play no part) mock what believers saw, face to face and once in ten days
  a home (-2 and an opinion). A couple who pray to different gods bicker over whose god sent the rain after a dry
  spell of five days or more, once in ten days a couple (an opinion only).
- **Vows** (`Vows.cs`, made with the core's `Gods.Vow`): no meat until the sick one is well (vegetarian meals asked for
  as a wish), a pilgrimage on foot to the god's holy place on the colony's land (a life goal), a temple (a life goal,
  also vowed before the council), and a beast spared for a season. Kept: +3 and pride; broken: -4, and a god that takes
  a broken word hard may cast a shadow on them.
- **Festivals** (`Festivals.cs`, a part of the calendar): the colony's gods (the one honoured this year, then the most
  widely held, three at most) each have a day (`CalendarKind.GodFestival`) kept with a feast and a rite at the god's
  place, with a chant from Alpha Memes or Ideology by the god, and visitors from the peoples who hold it. A god no
  longer the colony's has its day taken off, unless it has become a tradition.
- **The priest** (`Rimfolk_Worship_Office.xml`): an elected seat by Social, only with the gods on and never beside
  Ideology's chaplain; A RimWorld of Magic's priests, paladins and brightmages first. In the colony's age a shaman, a
  priest, a pastor or an oracle. Dedicates the places, carries the offerings, leads the rites.
- **The council** (`WorshipCouncil.cs`, four questions): which god the colony keeps the year for; a temple vowed; a god
  in a dream asking for the colony's finest beast or the rain stays away (as the dreamer fears); two rival gods' people
  wanting the next rite. Every answer plays out: words said at the god's place, an offering carried, the beast walked
  out and let go.
- **Dreams** (`GodDreams.cs`): a share of waking dreams are a god's (more for the priest, a psychic or a mage): a
  warning of something real now, an offering asked for at its place within three days (This week shows it as the
  dreamer's dream), a god's name the colony didn't know, a vision. A dream mood that gives awe, not mood.
- **A RimWorld of Magic** (`WorshipMore.cs`, by name): a caster's mana comes back faster or slower by how the colony
  stands with the god their class serves; hidden, felt most of the way, all of it when that god is drawn near.
- **Each god's own worship** (`GodWorshipDef`, `Rimfolk_Worship_Gods.xml`): keyed by the god's short name, from its
  character in `docs/gods-pantheon-brainstorm.md`: what it likes offered and refuses, its festival's day, name, dishes
  and chant, its people's vows, and a few of its own ways (Smoulder takes silver first; Ducat wants it given away, so
  an offering that goes back to the stores is nothing to it; Mog keeps no calendar and never asks; Helios takes
  nothing and is moved by nothing; Selene hears by night and in dreams told; Undertow takes anything; Morel takes what
  rots; Murmur and Cirrus are believed to keep the rain). A god no def names falls back to its domain's tables
  (`WorshipMath`). A handful of lines in the pools are a god's own (`[godkey:smoulder]`).
- **Saved**: `WorshipBook` (places, offerings, prayers, vows, dream demands and marks, each capped; modelled in
  `Tools/save_estimate.py`).
- **Balance** (`Tools/Balance`, `Rates.Worship`): an answer +4, a crisis of faith -4, mockery -2, a vow kept +3 or
  broken -4, at a few a colonist-year: worship adds about +0.17 and takes about -0.1 a colonist (well run to neglected),
  inside the targets as before.
- **Setting**: "Worship of the gods" (on), under The gods; nothing without "Gods". Dev actions "Gods: a prayer now...",
  "a vow now...", "a god's dream now", "a crisis of faith", "offerings at every shrine now", "worship's hour now",
  "worship's day now", "the gods' festivals onto the calendar now", "show worship (log)". Tested in `WorshipTests`.

### Gods: one way, each god's own presence, and variety first (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.224.0)

Two of the player's wishes of the day, built together, the bug first.

**Variety first** (the player: "important is that there is enough variety that i don't have the same events etc. within a
short time. just had the selene night event twice within a few days"; then "it just shouldn't feel like events are
repeating unless there's an actual 'lore' reason for it", "if it's triggering on something where no other events
really trigger, it shouldn't like 'auto-trigger' this event automatically when it's free"; the gods' happenings only).
- **Why it repeated.** The moon returned the day twice over, each on its own: the night's return (`GodReturn`, every
  third night, 70% on a full moon, for any day's deed of enough kindness, and tending the injured is one nearly every
  day) and the world's mirror (`GodHealth.Mirror`, every night with no gap at all, for the day's good turns and wrongs
  to the peoples, raiders killed among them). Both preferred an injured colonist (a wound healed by morning, a deep rest).
- **The shared pace** (`Gods/GodPaceMath.cs`, pure; `Gods/GodPace.cs`): no blanket cap; each happening keeps its own
  gap, by what it is. Once free, its chance starts at a quarter and grows over a long window (`Ramp`), so the first
  chance is the least likely and nobody can tell when it will come. A condition nearly always true is no trigger
  (`Trigger`: none, ordinary, strong). A short memory of the last twelve happenings (`GodsOnMapBook.lately`,
  "what|form|who") makes the next lean to a different form (`Lean`, `Pick`: the last form hardly, the one before half);
  a story that comes back for a reason the player can see takes its next step (`NextStep`).
- **The moon's return**, one rule for both (`GodsOnMapMath.ReturnTonight`): only around the full moon (full 0.2 a
  night, half 0.05, else none), a cycle apart at least (`ReturnGapDays` 12), its chance growing over the next thirty
  days, and only for a reason: a deed of the day out of the ordinary (`ReturnTrigger`: from 3 of kindness or cruelty,
  strong from 7; none for a kind of deed the colony did three times in fifteen days or one running three days, so daily
  tending is no reason), or the colony's day with the peoples (`WorldTrigger`, the seat's, reset each night). The
  world's mirror plays only on a night the moon's return chose (`GodHealth.Mirror(map, kind, cruel)`). What comes back
  leans away from the moon's last forms; back to the same person for the same kind of deed it is the next step of their
  story (a kindness: something found, a good dream, a wound healed; a cruelty: a nightmare, a frost, an animal at the
  door), written and spoken of as happening again (`CC_GodM_Saw_Return_*Again`, talk lines `[again]`). The same cruelty
  done again by one the moon already came back to is a strong reason even as a habit. About once a colony-year.
- **The other short gaps**, each now far longer than three days and growing back after: a myth at supper twelve days
  (`MythGapDays`, and not the god of the last one told at that table), the rock over deep mining five days and then a
  small chance in each hour of mining (`DeepNow`; the warnings now kept thirty days), a prayer answered ten days a god
  at a home (`AnswerGapDays`), mocking and a couple's bickering ten days (and bickering only after five dry days), a
  god answering in the weather fifteen days (ten and a half for a sky god) in a voice it didn't use last time, a mark
  visited twelve days and brought up at supper six, a fever eased five days at a home, a god's dream ten days a person.
  The comings, risings, gifts, kindness, anger and the world's other doings already came as small chances after long
  gaps, and the gods' hands after their own quiet spells; they stay.
- **The check** (`Tools/Balance/GodsSim.cs`, `--gods`): each happening a colony-year by the mod's own rules, the closest
  two, the same form twice running, and a check each must keep (at most so many a year, never two within so many days);
  a check that fails ends the run with exit code 1. The moon's return comes about once a colony-year, never within 12 days.

**One way, each god's own presence** (the player: "yes, let's stick to one level and use felt as primary reference. i
just want the 'walking'-exclusive options also to be able to appears, like smoulders true form. i guess the level could
be dynamic, some gods might become more present depending on situations, relations, actions etc. also the 'cards' level
on felt is great, the god should only be named if it's sure it was them").
- **Felt is the base.** The setting "How real are the gods" is gone, with the Believed and Walking branches and their
  line tags; an older settings file's choice is read and let go (`CouncilSettings`, `retiredRealness`).
- **How near each god is** (`Gods/GodNear.cs`, `Gods/GodNearMath.cs`; hidden state, never shown), 0 felt to 1, worked
  out at most once an hour a god a home, from three things: the situation on the land (six tenths of it: each shape's
  `nearWhen`, `GodStir`: a drought for Murmur, the deep for Smoulder and heat, a hard winter for Hush, a storm for
  Cirrus, the full moon for Selene, the dark of the moon and the desperate for Undertow, an anima tree and the growing
  season for Hollin, the dead left lying and sickness for Morel, guests for Ennu, machines for Pip, a hoard and a trader
  for Ducat, a thrumbo or a great herd for Bellwether, cats for Mog, heat for Helios); its relations (a quarrel it is in,
  the most stirred of the gods tied to it); and what the colony does (offerings to it in ten days, harm in fifteen, its
  entries in the colony's book in thirty, a standing strong either way; two fifths at most).
- **What nearness does** (all exactly felt at 0): a moment plain rather than veiled (`PlainChance`, from two fifths
  near, sure from four fifths; `PresenceSpec.For` rolls it, so the colony sees it plainly, is sure, and names it from
  then on through `Gods.CardName`), the stranger showing itself at the gate (`StrangerStay.plain`), Smoulder's true form
  on waking and Murmur surfacing a little more readily (`RisingDue`), stronger answers (a sickness eased up to 15%, rain
  within the hour with thunder, a longer dry spell), an offering gone in a breath of light, less disguise, a caster's
  mana by the whole of the standing, and the god's own doings in the world up to two fifths more often. One god can
  walk plainly while another stays hidden.
- **Cards stay felt:** a god is named only where the colony is sure it was that god (`Gods.CardName`: seen plainly or
  revealed, or the sign learned), else unnamed or "some say".
- **Lines:** `[walking]` became `[near]` (the god drawn near, seen plainly), `[felt]` and `real:felt`/`step:felt`
  became `[veiled]`, the Believed lines became `[doubt]` (said by one who believes little: a scoffer in the world's
  lines, a waverer in worship's) or fit everyone; the worship keys' `_Walking` became `_Plain`, the `_Believed` ones went.
- **Dev:** "Gods: how near each god is here (log)", "Gods: draw a god near (or let it be)..." in place of the realness
  one; the gods on the map's log shows the short memory.

### The Gods' book, a holy book (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.226.0)

The player, with a picture of Ducat's page (two dated entries, a trader's words at the gate and Avila's at supper): "the
god's book should not only be a log of events, but more like a wiki page basically building each up based on gained
knowledge, only a more mysterious and ominous wiki, you know like a religious text-style wiki". Built on "you can go
ahead on the todos", to the plan agreed in the to-do. The unseen rule holds (docs/design/gods.md, "The gods are unseen"
and "The colony's book"): only what the pawns know, each line as theirs, no favour, no truth marked, no Almanac page.

- **A chapter a name** (`Gods/GodLorePage.cs`): the list numbers the names as they were first heard (I, II, III); a
  chapter opens with its number in small capitals, the name set large, the names it was worked out to be, when and
  from whom it was first heard, and the book's ornament (two rules, a gold diamond, two small ones), then its parts in
  order (`GodBookMath.Order`): of its names; of what it is; of how it is known; of what it loves and what it hates; the
  sayings; the tales; of its kin and its enemies; its feast and its rites; and the witnesses (every entry by date, as
  before) last. Verses are numbered through the chapter in the gutter, the first opening with a drop capital in the
  book's gold (two lines beside it, then the full column). On a page wide enough the margin keeps each verse's date, a
  change of the keeper's hand and the keeper's notes in their own voice (devout, learned or plain: "Both are set down;
  the faithful will know which to keep."; none with nobody keeping the book); narrower, a change of hand and a tale's
  teller go under the verse. The page is a card (`UiKit.Card`) in either look, every colour a token.
- **The verses** (`Gods/GodLoreVerses.cs`, `LoreVerse : BookVerse`, `GodLore.verses`, saved, `GodBookMath.MaxVerses`
  720; a second teller of one thing only while the book has fewer than 640, two tellers at most, a god's rites six):
  each the words as said, who said them (a colonist by name, anyone else by name and people with the people's age), where
  (`how`: Fire, Gate, Letter, Supper, Sermon, Saw, Holds, Kept, Joined, Tale), when, under which name, and whose hand set
  it down. Set down only through `GodLore.Set` and its callers, each at something that happens in play:
  - **Of its names** (`GodLore.Called`): every time the book writes under a name, the name as the one who said it uses
    it, once a people and once for the colony's own; two names worked out to be one (`Connect`), with the later name's
    verses moved under the earlier. A name the book has with no verse (heard in a tale, kept before) shows as first heard.
  - **Of what it is** and **how it is seen** (`GodTales.WhatOf`): a new kind of talk at the evening fire (12 in a hundred
    each, `GodLoreMath.Talk`) and from visitors (`VisitorTalk`: 15 each): the teller says the next line the colony hasn't
    heard of one of their gods (the def's `whatLines` and `seenLines`, three each, one sentence of at most 90 letters,
    by the teller's name for it), over their head to the one near them; the book has it as heard and as a verse.
  - **Doubts** (`GodLore.Disputed`): a scoffer's answer to a believer at a god's hand, beside what it is.
  - **Signs** (`GodLore.LearnSign(g, sign, story, ...)`): learned when a tale is heard whole at the fire or retold in a
    letter, set down with the tale and its teller ("Its sign is a trader's caravan come at just the right hour, as the
    tale of the beetle on the ledger has it; so Mirel of the Silver League told it at our gate."), in words of their own
    (`CC_GodBook_Sign_*`, one for every sign a tale teaches, the event's name otherwise).
  - **Seen plainly** (`GodLore.Sighted`, from `Gods.Moment`): who saw the god plainly and what they saw.
  - **Loves and hates** (`GodLore.Inferred`): after a god's hand (`GodHands.Show`, a gift or an anger) or a kindness or
    anger of the gods' own seen (`Gods.Remember`, `Gods.Moment`), the believer among those who saw it comes to hold one
    of the things the hand's own god cares for (its def's `pleases` or `angers`, one not yet held there first), set down
    under the god they took it for (which may not be the god it was: then it sits under the wrong name, and nothing says
    so), "after" the event where there is one.
  - **Sayings** (`GodTales.Saying`, now one not yet heard first and from visitors too), **tales** (`GodTales.Tell`, each
    piece; `Written`, a letter's retelling whole), **kin** (`TieWords` at supper and a tale that names another, in both
    chapters), **rites** (`Worship.Booked`: a festival kept, a place given, a vow, a beast let go, with someone there to
    see it; `GodLetters`: a neighbour's invitation to their god's feast).
- **Laid out** (`GodBookMath.Compose`, pure): nothing that isn't a verse given, except headings, a begun tale's gaps,
  silences and tears and the keeper's notes; a part's verses in its order (names: the colony's own, then by age, then
  worked out; loves before hates; kin by the other god); a disputed claim opens "Some say:" with the doubt "Others hold,
  with ..." after it and the keeper's note; a second holder of what it loves "Others hold, with ..."; a tale's pieces in
  order with a run of missing ones as a gap (a row of dots each, "Here the telling breaks off."), none once retold whole,
  a piece told twice once; one empty part a silence ("Silence.", "Nothing is written here yet.", "Of this, nobody here
  has heard a word."), two or more together a torn page between two ragged edges ("Here the leaves are torn away: ...").
- **Said as theirs** (`GodBookWords`, pure, the page's words through a translator): every verse ends with who said it
  and where (`AttributionKey`: says, preached, holds, told it at our gate, wrote, their letter said, or, said through two
  mouths of one people, "so they say among the people of ..."; "who told it is not written" for an older book's).
- **An older book** (`GodLore.Migrate`, once, the first time it is opened or written in): its tales from each story's
  count and the entries that told them (with their tellers), the stories retold in letters, and the signs learned.
- **Dev:** "Gods: tell of a god here (testing)...": a colonist tells another one of each (what it is, how it is seen, a
  saying, a piece of a tale) of the god picked. Tested in `GodBookTests` (the rules, nothing unearned, the words, the
  defs' lines, the seams, the page); `GodLore.verses` modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.

### The gods understood: fixes, signs, plain lines, shrines made clear (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.232.0)

The player, 14 November 2026: "the god signs are awesome, go ahead! should be seen in the book and on cards. also like
the one-line meaning for the chapter ... gods effect should be noticeable"; rounds 0 and 1 of
`docs/gods-next-proposals.md` (section H). The unseen rule holds: the sign is the colony's own drawing of what it
believes, never a portrait; the plain line is what the colony takes the god to be, in the keeper's hand; a shrine says
what the colony's people do there, never what the god makes of it.

- **A work of art can be given** (round 0; `Offerings.Offered`, `WorshipMath.ArtGiven`): a sculpture packed away in the
  stores (a minified art piece) is offered as the art inside it, so Cirrus (art first) and Smoulder (art second) get
  more than cloth. One piece at a time, of good quality at most, worth at most two and a half times a gift's cap (600 at
  the most, `ArtValueCap`), and only while the colony keeps another piece packed away (`ArtKeptBack`). Nothing on show
  is taken from its place; anything else packed away (a table, a bed, a machine) is never offered, nor a place given to
  a god. Its label is the piece's own, with its title ("wood small sculpture (good), "Lonely Moon"").
- **Words for every gift** (round 0; `Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Offer`): every line now says why this thing is brought, one
  sentence: two for each kind (cloth had none), each god's own for the kinds its people give it (Ennu's "Cloth for the
  guest bed, Ennu, whoever comes tonight."), a demand's and the Hunger's. No untagged line, so the words always fit
  what lies there (tested: every god-and-kind line names a kind its worship def likes).
- **A small mood** (round 0; `Rimfolk_Worship_Thoughts.xml`, `WorshipMath.PrayedMood` and the like): a prayer +1 for
  half a day, +2 said at the god's own place (`Rimfolk_Worship_PrayedAtShrine`), carrying a gift +1 for a day; all
  smaller than an answered prayer (+4). They were 0 with something else instead; modelled in `Tools/Balance`.
- **The signs** (round 1; `Gods/GodSigns.cs`, `GodSignsMath`, `Tools/make_god_signs.py --textures`): each god's sign in
  `Textures/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Signs/`: `<Key>.png`, the sign in the god's colours as on the draft sheet, 128 by 128, and
  `Unknown.png`, a plain wax seal. (The ages' grey forms, stone, shield, badge and ring, were dropped in 0.238.1 at the
  player's word, "these are not the icons you created here??": they stay on the draft sheet only.) Shown:
  - in the Gods' book, over the chapter's name (56 px) and small at the end of its row in the list
    (`GodSignsMath.SignGods`, 0.238.2, the player: "god's book still shows the same icon for many"): a chapter told what
    its god is (`GodSignsMath.Tells`: a verse of what it is that isn't a doubt, or the god seen plainly by the colony's
    own people) shows the god most of those verses are of (`GodSignsMath.Believed`; on a tie the first told), so a
    chapter told of wrongly shows the wrong one; any other chapter shows the sign of the god its name belongs to, the
    earliest heard first, unless that god's sign already shows on a chapter told of it or on an earlier name; only those
    keep the unknown seal (`GodSigns.Unknown`), so two untold names never show they are one god;
  - on a god's card, over its name, only when the card names it and the colony knows its sign (`GodSigns.Known`); a
    veiled card ("some say") shows none (`GodsWiring`, `GodPresence.Manifest`'s overload with a sign, `GodLetter.sign`);
  - nowhere else: not on a shrine, not over a god on the map (the player's pick).
- **Large letters measured at their size** (0.238.1): the chapter's name (26), the card's god name (28) and the
  chapter's first capital (38) are drawn and measured with one style of the game's medium font at that size
  (`UiKit.Sized`, `UiKit.SizedLabel`), since the game's own measuring (`Text.CalcSize`, `Text.CalcHeight`) strips size
  tags first: drawn with "<size=26>" the name was measured at the small size, wrapped and cut to its first word ("The"
  of "The Stranger"), and the capital was clipped to an L-shaped mark.
- **The plain line** (round 1; `GodDef.plain`, `GodLorePage.PlainLine`): each chapter opens, under its head, with
  "As the colony understands it, so Avila keeps it:" (the keeper's name, `CC_GodBook_Plain`; "As the colony understands
  it:" with nobody keeping the book) and the believed god's plain line from section B of the doc ("The mother of all
  roots and growing things. ..."), gated as the sign is. The page reads nothing else of a god's def.
- **Shrines made clear** (round 1, section D; `Shrines.cs`, `Offerings.cs`):
  - the dedication is a card now (`Tell.Letter`, titled "Ennu's chapel"): what was done, then "From now on this is
    where the colony's people now and then leave Ennu a small gift the stores can spare, come to pray in hard times,
    and keep the Open Door each winter. What Ennu makes of it, nobody here can say." (`Shrines.Doings`,
    `WorshipMath.ShrineDoings`): gifts only for a god the colony carries any to (none for Helios), the feast only where
    this home keeps it (`Festivals.GodsFor`, three at most); the place's button says the same once it is given;
  - its inspect line: whose place it is, then the gift waiting there, or the last one ("Last left here: muffalo wool x16,
    by Mira, 3 days ago; it was gone soon after.", `ShrineRecord.lastWhat` and the like, saved), then what someone of the
    colony holds: the newest "what it loves" of the god's chapter as its holder holds it ("Mira holds that Ennu loves a
    bowl set out for whoever comes."), else the words the last gift was set down with;
  - the carrier's one sentence of why (above), said as it is set down and kept for the inspect line;
  - a gift gone in the night is noticed by day (`Offerings.Notice`, `WorshipMath.Notices`, within two days, 6 to 20
    o'clock): the first of the colony's people who passes within 7 cells in sight of the place, else from 9 o'clock its
    carrier or one who holds the god walks over to look (`Rimfolk_Worship_Look`, `WorshipAct.Look`), stops, a small light
    settles on the place, and they say whose doing they take it for (`Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Noticed`: their own god's,
    the place's as the others hold it, a doubter's maybe, a scoffer's fox, none of it the god's mind). Seen going
    plainly, nobody needs to notice it;
  - the small mood (above). The Almanac's page on the gods now says plainly what a shrine is for, as the colony's own
    practice; the gods themselves stay unexplained.
- Tested in `GodsUnderstoodTests` (the art rules, the words for every kind, the moods, the textures and their names, the
  believed god, where the sign shows and where it never does, the plain lines, the card, the inspect line, the noticing,
  the saved fields). Not done here (later rounds): each god's own way of taking a gift and its own signs after, the
  fourteen presences, each pawn's belief (a colonist's god is still picked as before), the happenings, the saints.

### Tamiu, the Keeper of the Threshold: Mog remade (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.233.0)

The player, 13 November 2026: "the cat card we have. Let's remake it into something new. Still a cat card, but kind of
one inspired by, you know, Egyptian mythology and the Sphinx, you know, with an Egyptian name. And I don't know if we have
like a god of the dead in that sense already, but maybe the cat god could be, you know, with mummies and like Egyptian
gear wearing zombies style followers, you know. Perhaps that is the god, and there's also some sort of cult behind it";
14 November 2026: "yes, remake mog and create a corresponding sign for it", "gods effect should be noticeable". The
pantheon had no god of the dead as such: Morel is the rot that takes the body back into the earth, Undertow the hunger
under the world. Tamiu is the one who keeps the dead whole and lies across the door between them and the living.

- **Her name and what the colony takes her to be** (`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Gods.xml`): Tamiu ("the she-cat"), the Keeper
  of the Threshold; her defName and key stay `Rimfolk_God_Mog` and `Mog`, so saves, the parts that key by her and her
  textures keep her. Her plain line: "A great cat who keeps the dead. She guards the graves, sets riddles at the
  threshold, and every cat is hers." Every age keeps her its own way: the Grave-Cat on the tribes' cairns, the Lady of
  the Tombs carved at the old kingdoms' crypt doors, the Cemetery Cat the towns keep, the Sphinx of spacers' cold berths;
  her old hearth-name Mog stays among her other names, so an older save's chapter of Mog is still hers. Domains Dead and
  Hearth (the fallback key), proud, her own look. Ties: Morel's rival over the dead (the rot against the wrapping),
  the Hunger's at the door of the dead, still staring at the Guest (Ennu), allied with Helios and Selene. Six stories (the
  tomb robber, the riddle at the door, the cats she sends ahead, the stare, the quarrel over the dead, the cat at the door
  of the dead), told by her name so a teller says their own. Revered by the river folk, the Quiet Bell and the Circuit
  of Tamers, and by the tribal, medieval and industrial kinds.
- **The god's name is its label** (`God.FromDef`): a god's short name people say is its def's label, its key for every
  other god; parts that key by a god read its key (`GodShapes.Of`, `GodWays`), and `Gods.ByKey` finds it by either.
- **Her walking form** (`Rimfolk_GodShape_Mog`, `Rimfolk_GodLook_Mog`): a great sand-gold cat, larger than any lion,
  gold-eyed, with a collar of lapis and gold: Vanilla Animals Expanded's lion first, Alpha Animals' sand lion, else the
  game's cougar or lynx, whichever is at ease in the season, drawn larger and tinted; sand rising off her (Odyssey's
  `SandBits`), a lion's call and A RimWorld of Magic's gong at her coming, Alpha Memes' Kemetic chant while she is near.
  The colony's cats follow her. She walks to the graves and keeps among them (`MogsWays.Keep`), lying beside one an hour
  or two; she still trails a stranger at the gate and stares (`SacredAnimal.Stare`).
- **Her favour, Mog's luck carried over** (`MogsWays.Favour`, `SacredAnimal.Lucky`): the one who answers her riddle well,
  else the one who brought her a bowl, has her favour while she stays: she walks at their heel, a sickness passes them by
  and Rimfolk's everyday hurts don't land (as Mog's chosen one before). Kept as it was: she can't be tamed or kept, and a
  cat harmed sends the cats off in one night and brings the rats (`kinWrath`).
- **The riddle at the threshold** (`MogsWays.Ask`, `HappeningWorker_GodRiddle`, `Rimfolk_Evt_GodRiddle`, `MogMath`): once
  a stay at most, from her second day, in the day (`RiddleDue`: about three seasons in four), she lies across the way in
  (outside the colony's outermost door) and a card puts her riddle, heard though nobody speaks it, one of the colony's age's
  four (`CC_Mog_RiddleQ_<age>_<i>`): send the sharpest wits (Intellectual), the best talker (Social), or let her lie.
  The one sent walks out to her and says their answer aloud; it is wrong by the card's risk, at their own skill
  (`WrongChance`: three in four with none, one in three at ten, one in ten from fifteen), told only when they reach her.
  Right: she gets up, puts her head under their hand and walks at their heel (+6 for six days, a card). Wrong: she looks
  at them a long while and walks back to the graves (-3), and at the shared harm budget's rate (`HarmKinds.GodRiddle`)
  cuffs them across the arm first, a scratch, on a card that says so. Nobody sent: she lies a while longer and goes.
- **A new grave kept, her cult** (`MogsWays.Daily`, `Graveside`): a colonist's new grave is kept the first night a fifth
  of the time, more where the colony holds her and the nearer she is drawn (`KeptChance`). At dusk one of her keepers
  comes in from the road, from a people at peace that holds her, in undyed linen with a cat at their heel (a plain card
  in the age's words), sits the night by the grave, rings a small bell and says one sentence over it (the colony's book
  has it, as heard at the gate), and goes at dawn; the cat stays on the grave a day or two and then goes its way. With no
  keeper able to come, one of the colony's cats (else a stray in from the edge) keeps the grave instead, and someone who
  sees it says so. Those fond of the dead are comforted (+3, "a grave kept").
- **The wrapped dead stand guard** (with Anomaly; `MogsWays.Hourly`, `Rise`, `HediffComp_WrappedDead`): in a raid that
  comes within 30 cells of a home's tombs (graves and sarcophagi holding the dead, Alpha Memes' mummies; two at least),
  weighed once a raid, while she is on the land (half the raids) or drawn near (a little to a third), at the shared harm
  budget's rate (`HarmKinds.GodDead`; never with hurts switched off), two to four of the land's old dead stand up among the
  tombs: the game's shamblers, of the entities, wrapped in gray cloth (Ideology's broadwrap and headwrap, else the game's
  robe or tribalwear and veil), with the game's rising effect. They keep to the graves (`LordJob_DefendPoint`) and turn
  on anything that comes near them, raider or colonist; the card says so, in the age's words. They lie down as dust an
  hour after the last raider is gone (or after half a day), and one that falls is dust too, so nothing of them is
  stripped or butchered. Those who saw them stand: -4 for three days; the place is remembered as her mark.
- **Her own signs** (`OmenKind.CatsFacing`, `GoldEyes`, `Sand`; `GodOmensOwn.cs`) in place of the shared ones: every cat
  on the land sits facing the graves; at night, two gold eyes low in the dark by the graves, and gone; fine pale sand
