  across a grave where no wind blows sand. Each is said aloud and kept in the book.
- **Her presence on the land** (`Rimfolk_GodPresence_Mog`): from her coming to her going, "the cats keeping watch" (by the
  colony's name for her once it knows it is her: "Tamiu keeping watch"). The land's rats and mice run off it as she comes,
  and every few hours the cats go and sit facing the graves. Released as a condition of its own; since round 2 one of the
  gods' own presences (`GodDef.presence`, effect `Watch`; "The gods each their own" below).
- **Her offerings and worship** (`Rimfolk_Worship_Mog`, `Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Offer`): fish for her cats, linen for the
  wrapping, meat; her keepers chant Alpha Memes' Kemetic chant; she keeps no calendar and never asks.
- **Her sign** (`Tools/make_god_signs.py`, `mog()`): a cat seated in profile on a tomb's door, upright and watchful as the
  old kingdoms carved her, her eye cut bright and painted long, a collar at her neck, her tail curled up behind her; in
  in her colours (`Textures/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Signs/Mog.png`).
- Tested in `MogTests` (the pure rules, her def, shape and look, her omens and presence, the card, every age's words, the
  seams); `GodsTests`, `GodsOnMapTests`, `GodWorldTests` and `HarmBudgetTests` follow her. Not built: her own festival
  (she keeps none), a cult people of her own (her keepers come from the peoples that hold her).

### The gods each their own: presences, ways of taking, own signs (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.234.0)

The player, 14 November 2026: "gods effect should be noticeable"; "the "Each god its own" proposals sounds great too! go
ahead with all of this"; their complaint: "when a godly event happens, there is kind of a presence on the map, which is
seen in the bottom right corner, and I think it's kind of the same description for this effect for each different god
... each of the gods should feel really unique in what it does and whether or how it interacts with the world, what the
impact is, how these things play out on the map". Round 2 of `docs/gods-next-proposals.md` (sections C and D). The unseen
rule holds: a presence is named only when the colony is sure whose it is (`Gods.CardName`, looked at again as a long stay
goes on), else by what anyone can see; its words say what is seen, its numbers are shown under its label as the game
shows any condition's, never as a god's favour or mind.

- **How a god plugs in** (declared per god, nothing in code by name):
  - its presence: `GodDef.presence`, a GameConditionDef of class `GameCondition_GodPresence` (parent
    `Rimfolk_GodPresenceOwnBase`) with an `OwnPresence` extension: `god` (its key), `effect` (one `PresenceEffect`),
    `named` and `namedText` (with {NAME}), `neverNamed`, `motes` and `sounds` by name; the def's label and description
    are the unnamed form. A god whose def names none keeps the shared `Rimfolk_GodPresence` (the sky and the stilled
    wind), as every god did before. Checked when the defs load (`GodDef.ConfigErrors`);
  - its way of taking: `GodWorshipDef.taking` (an `OfferingWay`; `Vanish`, the shared way, by default);
  - its signs: `GodShapeDef.omens`, as before.
  A new effect is a `PresenceEffect` value with its sizes in `GodPresenceOwnMath`, its show in `GodPresenceShows` and
  any hook in `GodPresenceOwnPatches`; a new way an `OfferingWay` with its rules in `OfferingWayMath`, its taking in
  `OfferingWays.Take` and its words (`CC_Wsh_Taken_Way_<Way>_<Felt|Plain|...>`, `CC_Wsh_Inspect_Fate_Way_<Way>`,
  `Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Way` lines tagged `way:<way>`).
- **The presence** (`Gods/Presence/GodPresenceCondition.cs`, `GodPresenceOwn.cs`, `GodPresenceShows.cs`): a god's moment
  (`GodPresence.Manifest` through the seam, `GodsWiring` passing `GodPresenceOwn.DefOf(god)` and its key) leaves the god's
  own presence after it, one a map as before. Its strength by the moment (`GodPresenceOwnMath.Strength`: a blessing 1, a
  coming or a reveal or a wrath 0.85, an act 0.7, a departure 0.4); a wrath (`Harsh`) turns its kindly side off and its
  hard side up. Its length is the moment's (one to five hours) unless its nature asks for another (`Ticks`): Selene's
  begun at night until seven in the morning, Murmur's six hours at least; the Old Horn's, the Guest's and Tamiu's held
  while they walk the land (two hours left at least, `Held`; Tamiu's ended once she has gone, `EndsWhenGone`) and begun
  again on the hour when another god's has passed (`GodPresenceOwn.Hourly`). The Guest's and Tamiu's begin quietly as they
  come (`GodPresenceOwn.Quiet`, never in place of another's). Each shows at its start, as motes where the player is
  looking (every 40 to 60 ticks on the map in view), at each of its turns (`Sched.RareGodPresence`, a waiting pass on
  tick 91, timed by the clock) and on its hour; someone of the colony who sees it says so once (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodPO_Say`,
  `notice:<effect>`, named lines only when the colony is sure). Its numbers are written under its words
  (`GodPresenceOwn.NumberLines`, `CC_GodPO_Num_*`), and its stats' breakdowns name it by its label (`StatPart_GodPresence`).
  The fourteen (at full strength):
  - **Hollin, "the green leaning"** ("Hollin listening"): plants grow a third faster (`Plant.GrowthRate`, shown in the
    plant's growth breakdown); green motes drift to one tree (the anima tree, else the oldest near the colony); the
    dryads stand facing it; Alpha Biomes' petal storm in spring; a tree felled under it: "the axe felt wrong" (-2 a day,
    -5 two days in her wrath) and a line. None of it in her wrath but the axe.
  - **Smoulder, "warm stone"** ("Smoulder breathing"): 4 degrees warmer out of doors (7 in his wrath), heat pushed into
    the rooms under thick rock each turn, snow melting off the rock, steam from the geysers and the foot of the rock, a
    fine ash and ore glinting in the faces; mining yields a quarter more (`MiningYield`); at six someone who slept under
    the mountain says a warm voice spoke in their dream (the dream book, the journal, the colony's book).
  - **Bellwether, "the white beast grazing"** ("Bellwether passing"), while he is on the land: no animal turns
    manhunter (`MentalStateHandler.TryStartMentalState`), one that had turned near him calms, wild beasts near him lie
    down facing him (three a turn), insults half as likely and fights a quarter (`InteractionWorker_Insult`, `Slight`,
    `SocialFightChance`), a thrumbo's call now and then.
  - **Morel, "spore-fall"** ("Morel close"): pale spores drifting (glowing after dark), a ring of mushrooms at a grave or
    a body; food out of the cold and the dead rot half again as fast (twice in her wrath; `CompRottable`), mushrooms
    grow half again as fast, sicknesses pass 15 percent faster (`ImmunityGainSpeed`).
  - **Ennu, "a warm evening"** ("Ennu under our roof"), from the stranger let in to the stranger gone: 2 degrees
    warmer, hearths keep three fifths of what they burn and give more heat, insults half as likely and fights rarer, a
    colony animal follows the guest a while, "a warm evening" (+2 for the colony's own, +5 for visitors). Nothing when
    the Guest was wronged.
  - **Pip, "a hum in the wires"** ("Pip awake"): the lights pulse in a pattern and the machines spark; batteries keep
    half of what they give out (`CompPowerBattery.DrawPower`), powered benches a tenth faster
    (`WorkTableWorkSpeedFactor`); one door won't open for one person (`Building_Door.PawnCanOpen`): they walk to it,
    it won't budge, they say so; it ends when someone else opens it (`StartManualOpenBy`), within the hour, or at once
    when they must pass (drafted, hungry, hurt, danger). Sulking (wrath): the lights flicker slow, nothing held.
  - **Cirrus, "a sky too high"** ("Cirrus looking down"): the sky clears and is lighter, the weather holds (Clear; in
    its wrath the weather as it was), the birds leave, the vast shadow passes, lightning and thunder far off with no
    rain, looking at the sky twice as likely and half again as enjoyable (the condition's own skygazing factors), and a
    stargazer "watched from very high" (+3).
  - **Hush, "a white silence"** ("Hush near"): nobody starts a conversation (`TryInteractRandomly`) and nobody remarks on
    it until it lifts, the music falls silent, 5 degrees colder (8 in its wrath), frost along the walls, a fine snow
    (Seasonal Weather's fog-snow, else the game's) where it is cold and fog where it isn't, nothing out of doors rots,
    and the old, the sick and babies feel the cold 4 degrees sooner (`ComfyTemperatureMin`).
  - **Undertow, "the dark"** (never named): the sky darker, lamps reach a third less far (half in its wrath;
    `CompGlower.GlowRadius`, the lamps re-lit as it comes and goes), the corner of the home ground farthest out stays
    dark (the dark sign held there), shadow motes there, psychic sensitivity +20 percent, the most desperate hear a
    sweet voice once by night.
  - **Helios, "the long noon"** ("Helios staring"): the light of the hour it came holds (only when it came by day; the
    night stays night), the shadows stand still, 4 degrees warmer (8 in his wrath), solar panels a quarter more
    (`CompPowerPlantSolar`), crops a quarter faster (never in his wrath), heat shimmer, and night owls and those the sun
    burns (Biotech's and Alpha Genes' UV sensitivity, Vanilla Races Expanded's photophobia) "the sun won't go down" (-3).
  - **Selene, "a moon too close"** ("Selene watching"): the night as light as her face is full (up to dusk), silver over
    the sleepers and on still water, wounds heal half again as fast in sleep (`InjuryHealingFactor`), and at six after a
    full-moon night a true dream told at breakfast: a raid queued for the colony within two days, else visitors on
    their way, else a beast with teeth on the land and where, else the stores going soft, else someone sadder than they
    let on, else only the moon (`TrueDream`, read from the storyteller's queue and the map).
  - **Tamiu (Mog), "the cats keeping watch"** ("Tamiu keeping watch"): folded in from 0.233.0's own condition (effect
    `Watch`): from her coming to her going the rats and mice run off the land and every few hours the cats sit facing
    the graves (`MogsWays.CatsWatch`).
  - **Murmur, "a croaking in the wells"** ("Murmur singing"): water standing at the well, Odyssey's bullfrogs out on the
    wet ground, a deep croak (the camera shakes, ripples, a frog's call) at its start and now and then, rain from its
    first hour (Odyssey's torrent in his wrath), plants on wet ground three tenths faster, and with Dubs Bad Hygiene
    nobody comes down with cholera, dysentery or diarrhoea on the map while it lasts (`AddHediff`, by name).
  - **Ducat, "a glint"** ("Ducat going by"): coins glinting in the stores, the golden beetle across a table, a few single
    coins out of the biggest store lying in a line toward the nearest edge (moved, not lost), traders deal 8 percent
    better (`TradePriceImprovement`; 5 worse in its wrath).
- **Each god's own way of taking** (`Gods/Worship/OfferingWays.cs`, `OfferingWayMath`; `GodWorshipDef.taking`), in place of
  the shared "gone by morning ... Nobody saw it go" (which stays for a god whose worship names none): Hollin's sinks into
  the soil and a young tree of the land stands there (else the soil turned dark); Smoulder's goes down a crack, rubble and
  a warm floor; Bellwether's grazed, a hoofprint beside it; Morel's rots into black soil (rich soil where the ground is
  natural) with a mushroom; Ennu's gone with footprints in from the land's edge and none away (in the snow, else the dirt);
  Pip's part gone and the nearest broken machine mended (else a light winks three times); Cirrus's taken up by night in a
  streak of light; Hush's frosted over in the night and gone at dawn; Undertow's gone and one to three of a stack beside
  it with it; Helios's never taken: the noon light lies on it and at dusk it goes back to the stores, still there
  (gifts are left for him now, as people don't know better: `GodWorshipDef.GiftsLeft`, chosen by what they believe he
  likes, `Believed`); Selene's gone only on a night her moon shows (it waits out a dark week, then goes back); Murmur's
  down into the well or the wet ground with a croak; Ducat's handed to the nearest visitor or trader by day and carried
  off in their pack (after three days with nobody, back to the stores, counting for nothing); Tamiu's eaten at dawn by
  the nearest cat, which walks over and eats it (else gone at dawn, paw prints where it lay). Plainly (a god drawn near),
  each goes its own way before everyone's eyes with the god's moment. The news, the inspect line and the next day's
  notice (round 1's sign, `Offerings.Notice`) say it in the way's own words (`Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Way`); what was seen
  going (a cat eating, a visitor given it) or never goes needs no noticing. Saved: `OfferingRecord.stage` and `cat`.
- **Bellwether's and Ennu's own signs** (`OmenKind.ThrumbosFace`, `GrassBowed`, `Hoofprint`, `Knock`, `Footprints`,
  `DogsSilent`; `GodOmensOwn.cs`), in place of the five shared ones: every thrumbo on the land standing facing one way; the
  grass bowed flat in one long line across the land; at dawn a cloven hoofprint the size of a table near the colony's
  edge; a knock at the colony's outer door at dusk and the nearest one walking out to find nobody; at dawn footprints up
  to the door from the land's edge and none away; the colony's dogs gone silent, all facing the gate. Each said aloud
  and kept in the book.
- Dev mode: "Gods: a god's own presence here now..." (any god and kind, as the colony knows it or named), "Gods: end the
  presence here", "Gods: the presence here (log)", "Gods: offerings here taken now, each god's own way".
- Tested in `GodsOwnTests` (the sizes and lengths, the weather, the dreams, the fourteen declared and all different,
  every name in the player's mods, every effect shown and said, the hooks, the slot, the saved fields, every way's rules,
  words and show, the next day's notice, the new signs, how a god plugs in); `MogTests` follows her presence folded in.
  Not seen in a real game (none of it could be): see the handoff's entry.

### Each one's gods: a colonist's own belief in each god (the player's go, 14 November 2026; round 3; released 0.235.0)

The player: "and then also kind of the interactions between pawns and the gods, you know, I guess pawns should have and
develop kind of a relationship in a way, or rather a belief to gods. You know, if maybe they feel attached to a specific god
for because of their characteristics or history or whatever, and that they kind of, the more they pray and interact to a
god, that they kind of, yeah, get a stronger belief in that god, kind of develop a relationship"; then "pawn belief should
be reflected in book and culture tab", "gods effect should be noticeable". Section E of `docs/gods-next-proposals.md`.
A belief is the pawn's own, a pawn fact the unseen rule allows: how they hold a god, in words, never the god's favour,
wants or rules, and never a number in play. The colony's own people only (`Worship.Ours`): guests and prisoners hold
nothing here.

- **What it is** (`Gods/Belief/PawnGodsMath.cs`, pure; `PawnGodsBook`, saved): for each colonist, at most six gods
  (`MaxHeld`), each with how strongly they hold it (0 to 100), how much they dread it (0 to 100), what their character
  drew at first, when it last grew, and a short line of why. In words (`Word`): leans toward (10), holds to (30), devoted
  to (55), wholly given to (80); uneasy about (dread 20) and in dread of (45) where the dread is as strong as the belief
  (they still believe, in fear). A scoffer "doubts them all".
- **What draws them** (`PawnGodsMath.Draw`, once, the first time they are among the colony's people;
  `PawnGods.Sketch`): their traits (the game's, Vanilla Traits Expanded's, Anomaly's, Rimfolk's own and A RimWorld of
  Magic's classes: kind to Ennu, greedy and tycoon to Ducat, night owl to Selene, ascetic and cold-inclined to Hush,
  pyromaniac and mountain lover to Smoulder, too smart and body modder to Pip, ecologist and green thumb to Hollin, animal
  lover and menagerist to Bellwether, cat person to Tamiu, ocean lover to Murmur, psychic sensitivity and the tortured
  artist to Cirrus, sanguine to Helios, cannibal, psychopath and void fascination open to Undertow); their passions (a
  burning one twice a minor one: plants to Hollin and Murmur, mining to Smoulder, animals to Bellwether, medicine to Selene
  and Morel, crafting to Pip, social to Ennu and Ducat, art to Cirrus); what they are (the player's xenotypes by name:
  phytokin and wood elves to Hollin, fungoid and mycomorph to Morel, lycans to Selene, androids to Pip, the merren and
  boglegs to Murmur, yttakin to Hush, stoneborn and drakonori to Smoulder, starjacks to Cirrus); their past (a backstory's
  words from their start: a miner, a farmer, an undertaker, a sailor, a trader); the gods of the people they came from
  (three at most); their faith's memes and precepts (Ideology, `GodsMath.ScoreMeme` by domain, `FaithLean`); a bond with a
  cat (Tamiu) or another animal (Bellwether). Every trait and xenotype named is an enabled one in the player's list
  (tested against `docs/player-mods`). Never their parents or kin: nothing here reads a family, only a bond with an
  animal. Character alone takes them past holding to a god and short of devotion (`DrawCap` 48); devotion comes from what
  they do and see. An older save's turning after a crisis of faith carries over as a belief held.
- **How it grows** (`Amount`, `Grow`: each step smaller the more they hold): a prayer (+2, +3 at the god's place), an
  answer (+9), what they prayed for come to pass (+5), an offering carried (+3), a vow kept (+8, a temple or pilgrimage
  +12), a festival kept at home (+3, half for one who holds the god little), leading its rite (+5), their own small rite
  (+1.5), a god's moment seen (+4, plainly +10, a kindness +6, a sign +2), a gift of a god's (+12), a dream of it (+4), a
  tale, a line of what it is or a saying told to them (+1.5), something lived through (+6: the cold that nearly took them
  for Hush, the heat for Helios, a deadly sickness got over for Morel, once a month each), a god's own presence lived
  through on the land to its end (+3, and now and then won over, where the colony was sure whose it was; in anger, dread
  instead: `PawnGods.PresencePassed` from `GameCondition_GodPresence.End`), a gift found taken by day in the god's own way
  (+3, `PawnGods.SawTaken` from `Offerings.Noticed`). A moment counts for the god its
  witnesses took it for (`GodLoreMath.Attribute`, as the book does), so a belief can grow in the wrong god; a gift too, as
  the dream that brought it may not have named it. A scoffer is moved only by a god seen plainly, and half.
- **How it fades** (`Fade`, `FadeDread`): unused twelve days, half a point a day, down to half of what their character
  drew (a kind heart still leans toward the Guest); a prayer unanswered (-4), a crisis of faith (-12), a vow broken (-10,
  and a little fear), a scoffer's mockery (-1). Two crises still turn them (`FaithHeart.TurnAway`), now through their
  beliefs: to another god they hold where they hold one, never to one they dread; the god turned from -25, the one turned
  to their first from then on. Dread lingers fifteen days, then fades.
- **Dread** (`DreadAmount`): a god's anger on them (+22, uneasy at once), beside them (+12) or only seen (+4), a believer
  of that god fearing it the more; a broken vow (+6). One in dread of a god keeps away from its place (`PawnGodsActs.
  KeepAway`: found within 8 cells of it in their free time, they look at it, say why in one sentence and walk 14 cells
  off, once a day at most) and flinches at its signs (`Flinch`: a sentence, a small bad mood, a step back from where it
  showed); they never pray to it, carry it a gift or turn to it. Passing into dread is in their journal.
- **Whom they turn to** (`PawnGods.Held`, `PawnGodsMath.Choose`; through `Worship.GodOf` and `Gods.SwearBy`, which every
  part already asks, so prayers, offerings, festivals' leaders, vows, dreams, the council's questions and every sworn
  line follow): their first god (the one they hold most, at least leaning toward it, not dreaded); for a moment with a
  domain (a sickness, a death, a raid, a drought) one of that domain they at least lean toward, unless they are devoted to
  their first, which they turn to in everything; drawn to none, the god of the moment's domain, or with none the domain of
  the work they're best at (`WorkDomain`). The pick by id number only stands where none of these finds a god. They pray at
  their own god's place.
- **Won over** (`PawnGodsMath.WonOver`, `PawnGodsActs.MaybeWonOver`): a strong moment of a god not their first (seen
  plainly, a gift, an answered prayer, a kindness seen, something lived through), by its strength about a third of the
  time at most, once in twenty days a person: it is their first god from then on, said in a bubble
  (`Rimfolk_Pool_Belief_WonOver`, by how it happened), their journal, a news line ("Mira holds to Hollin now, and says so
  to anyone who asks.") and the colony's book as their belief; +4 for three days. A scoffer is won over far more rarely, and
  scoffs no more after (`Worship.Scoffer`), unless their faith despises religion.
- **Their own small rite** (`PawnGodsMath.Rites`, `RiteHour`, `RiteChance`; `PawnGodsActs.Rites`,
  `JobDriver_BeliefRite`, `Rimfolk_Belief_Rite`): each god's devotees keep one, short and seen, in their free time at its
  hour: Hollin's lay a hand on a tree, Smoulder's drop a coin into the rock, Bellwether's stand with a grazing beast,
  Morel's bury scraps in the soil, Ennu's set an extra bowl at the table, Pip's tap a working machine twice (sparks), Cirrus's
  look up at the sky at dusk, Hush's keep a silence out in the cold (else at nightfall), Undertow's whisper into a dark
  corner at night, Helios's face the sunrise, Selene's look at the moon, Tamiu's sit by a grave at dusk or else feed a cat,
  Murmur's hum at the water's edge or Dubs Bad Hygiene's well, Ducat's turn a coin over at the stored silver. They walk
  there, stay a few seconds facing it, say one sentence (`Rimfolk_Pool_Belief_Rite`, each god's own words), and hold
  their god a little more surely. By how they hold it: about every few days for the devoted, nearly daily for the
  fervent, once a week or so for one who holds to it; once a day a person, two begun an hour a home at most. The job
  reports it ("laying a hand on a tree for Hollin."). With nowhere near to keep it (no tree, no machine), no rite.
- **Small moods** (`Rimfolk_Belief.xml`): the god they hold to acting before them +3 for a day (`GodActed`); slighted, its
  place gone (torn down, burned, broken in a raid: `ShrinesLost`, the one who holds it most saying so) -3 for two days, its
  feast day let pass -2 for a day; a flinch -2 for half a day. In `Tools/Balance` (`Rates.Worship`).
- **Rival devotees** (`InteractionWorker_RivalGods`, `Rimfolk_Belief_RivalGods`): two of the colony who hold rival gods
  (the gods' own hostile ties, `GodTiesMath.Hostile`; Tamiu and Morel over the dead, Smoulder and Hush, Murmur and Hush,
  Ducat and Smoulder, Undertow and the hearth's gods) bicker in the game's own social talk now and then (a weight of 0.02
  to 0.06 beside chit-chat's 1, the more devoted the likelier, once in six days a pair): the log line names no god, their
  words over their heads do, each by the colony's name for it (`Rimfolk_Pool_Belief_Rival`, `_RivalReply`); -4 opinion for
  three days; a scuffle at the game's own insult's rate (0.005); each holds their own the harder.
- **How it shows** (no number anywhere in play):
  - the Culture tab (`UI/ITab_Pawn_Culture.cs`, "Their gods", under their faith): each god the colony has heard of that
    they hold or dread, in words, by the colony's name for it ("Devoted to Hollin", "Leans toward Ducat", "In dread of the
    Hunger"), the line of why when hovered ("Since 5th of Aprimay, 5501: the roots rose and took the north wall.", "Drawn
    by who they are: kind."); a scoffer "Doubts them all" (and any god they still fear); drawn to none, "No god has drawn
    them yet";
  - the Gods' book (`GodLorePage.Holders`): each chapter, before its witnesses, "Of those who hold to it", in the
    keeper's hand ("As Avila keeps it:"), "Who holds to it here: Mira, devoted; Bram, who leans toward it." and "Who
    dreads it here: Ida, in dread of it.", under the name the colony keeps the god by (its first chapter for it; a second
    name not yet worked out to be the same has nobody, so nothing gives away which names are one). A god the colony hasn't
    heard of is named nowhere.
- **The seams** (so round 2's presences, offering ways and omens plug in): `Prayers.Said`, `TryAnswer`, `Credit`;
  `FaithHeart.Unanswered`, `TurnAway`, `Mock`; `Offerings.Placed`; `Vows.End`; `Festivals.Kept`, `Passed`, `RiteDone`;
  `GodDreams`; `GodTales.Tell`, `WhatOf`, `Saying`; `GodHands.Show`; `GodWorldGifts.Give`; `Gods.Remember` and
  `Gods.Moment` (every act and moment seen on the land, the gods' own omens among them); round 2's own presences
  (`GameCondition_GodPresence.End`) and ways of taking (`Offerings.Noticed`, and a gift taken plainly through
  `Worship.Sign`). Kept in worship's own hour and day (`Worship.Hourly`, `Daily`):
  no pass and no Sched slot of its own. Dev actions: "Gods: a colonist's own gods (log)", "Gods: set a colonist's
  belief...", "Gods: their small rite now", "Gods: win them over now...", "Gods: rival devotees bicker now".
- Saved small: one record a colonist, six gods at most, the departed let go each day and the discarded at saving
  (`Tools/save_estimate.py`). Tested in `PawnGodsTests` (324 checks).

### The saints: a faith's deities and the colony's own (the player's go, 14 November 2026; round 5; released 0.236.0)

The player: "And I guess in that regard, the whole ideology implementation, we can also think about how we adapt the
ideology system to integrate and relate to our gods instead of, you know, the ones that are created by the game. And one
idea I thought, maybe if we can, or if we need to reuse the god, so to say, or this, the way it's implemented now with
ideology, perhaps instead of these being the gods that are currently registered to an ideology, this could, for example,
be some sort of saints or important characters. So kind of a middle ground between God and the pawns and the ideology,
kind of saints or holy men or unholy men or whatever"; then "let's go with saints then". Section F of
`docs/gods-next-proposals.md`, option b. A saint is a person, named plainly; the gods behind them stay unseen, named only
by the colony's name for them and only where the colony knows them. A person honoured, never their kin: nothing of it
passes to anyone, and nothing reads a family.

- **A faith's deities are its saints, or its damned** (`Gods/Saints/Saints.cs`, `Of`; pure rules in `SaintsMath`): each
  of Ideology's deities (`IdeoFoundation_Deity`) is read, never changed, so the editor, a reform or a new roll simply gives
  new saints (the old ones kept in the book as kept no more). Its domains come from its own words, its meme, the faith's
  memes and precepts (`GodsMath.DeityDomains`), and it is tied to the god whose own domain is the deity's (3), whose second
  is (2), and so on, a domain no god holds first going to the nearest (war to Smoulder, then Cirrus; healing to Selene's
  second, then Morel), ties by the deity's name so it keeps its god (`SaintsMath.GodFor`). A saint is never the Hunger's.
  One of a dark meme (raider, cannibal, pain is virtue, bloodfeeding, Anomaly's inhuman and ritualist, the pirates', Alpha
  Memes' and Vanilla Memes Expanded's darker ones, every one enabled in the player's list), with dark words in its name or
  title, or of the void is one of the damned (`SaintsMath.Damned`), tied only to the dark gods (the Hunger, Hush, Smoulder;
  the Hunger where nothing else fits): feared, never prayed to, no statue raised to one. A faith with no deities (animist,
  ideological, archist) has no saints.
- **Their words, by age and culture** (`SaintsMath.WordSet`, `DamnedSet`; `CC_Saint_*`): the tribes' Ancestors ("Ancestor
  Aranea"), the medieval and industrial Saints ("Saint Aranea"), the spacers' Exemplars; the Corunan's Venerated and the
  Kriminul's Martyrs; the damned as the Forsaken, the Damned and the Fallen ("Vorgath the Damned"). A faith's age is the
  colony's where its own people hold it, else its people's.
- **Shown as saints** (`Patch_SaintsWord`, on `IdeoFoundation_Deity.DoInfo`): while the game draws a faith's deity box,
  its word "Deities" (found by the game's own English text, so a renamed key leaves it as it is) reads as the faith's own
  ("Saints", "Ancestors", "Damned" where every one is damned), swapped for the drawing and put back by a finalizer; under
  the box, in play only, "As the colony holds them: Saint Aranea, of the Old Horn; Vorgath the Damned, feared, of the
  Hunger.", each only where the colony knows that god by that name. A neighbour's sermon or hymn names its faith's
  saint by title ({DEITY}: "Praise to Saint Aranea in the morning"), now and then one of the colony's own where the writer
  shares their faith (`Saints.SermonName`, `Letters/LetterFormShapes.cs`), else the game's own name.
- **The colony's own saints** (`Saints.Died`, `SaintsMath.Merit`, `Patch_SaintDeath` on `Pawn.Kill`): a free colonist of
  the colony's own, grown, dies a remarkable death: carrying, rescuing or tending someone while an enemy's attack is on the
  colony (a saint's death on its own); holding the line, drafted, against one; the healer's years (medicine 12 and 80
  tended, or a passion, 8 and 150); two years devoted to a god, or as the priest. Each but the first needs a year with the
  colony besides (or a vow kept to the end, or a god's presence on the land). Never a scoffer, one who held the Hunger
  first, a child, a slave, a guest. Their god is the one they held first, else the one their deed speaks of. The death
  waits for the council's card at most twelve days (`SaintsMath.CandidateDays`).
- **The council's card** (`Rimfolk_Dlm_Saint`, `DilemmaWorker_Saint`, asked in its moment, `timely`, 30 days apart): the
  priest (else the most devout who holds the fallen one's god) asks the council to name them "a saint of Hollin" (by age:
  "an Ancestor who walks with Hollin"; "a saint" where the colony doesn't know the god). Named (`DilemmaEffect_NameSaint`,
  `Saints.Name`): the one who asked says the words at the grave that evening and those who come listen
  (`DilemmaEffect_SaintWords`, a play-out at the grave, else the god's place); the colony's people, never its scoffers and
  never more for kin, "one of ours named a saint" +3 for five days; a relic of theirs set by the grave; the colony's book
  under their god by those who saw it (`Worship.Booked`); a line in the asker's journal. Honoured without it: a few words
  at the grave. Let rest (the default): the asker trusts the council a little less.
- **Their places** (`Gods/Saints/SaintsPlaces.cs`), each a lesser shrine: a colony saint's grave; a statue raised to a
  saint (the button "Raise to a saint" on the game's sculptures, Odyssey's statue, Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Art's,
  Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Empire's, Vanilla Memes Expanded's and Props and Decor's statues and Alpha Memes' statue,
  sphinx, megalith, obelisk and stele: `SaintsMath.IsStatue`; the colony's own saints or its faiths' holy ones): someone
  walks over and says one sentence (`Rimfolk_Saint_Raise`), the art's title becomes the saint's ("Saint Mira") and is given
  back when cleared; an Odyssey statue of the fallen one's likeness is known for theirs (`LikenessComps`, the seam for
  Pawns on Display); the relic (`Rimfolk_SaintRelic`, `CompSaintRelic`: a lock of hair bound in cord, a small bone in a
  carved box, a lock of hair under glass, their voice sealed in a case, by the colony's age; never sold). Now and then
  (`PrayChance`, about once in two days at a home with one place) a devotee (one who holds the saint's god, the devout of
  the saint's faith, the priest) walks to one in their free time, faces it, says one sentence (`Rimfolk_Pool_Saint_Prayer`)
  and holds the saint's god a little more (a prayer at its place); +2 for a day, +3 before a relic where their faith keeps
  relics (Ideology's relic precept). The inspect line says whose it is, and "of Hollin" only where the colony knows it.
- **Their day** (`SaintsMath.FeastDue`, `SaintsPlaces.Keep`): each year, from the year after they were named, on the day
  they died, in the evening, the devoted gather at the grave (else the statue, else the god's place) for an hour's words led
  by the priest or the most devoted, the keeper's sermon on the saint (`Rimfolk_Pool_Saint_Feast`); +3 for those who came,
  belief as at a festival. With answers not played out on the map, they keep it quietly where they are.
- **What a saint gives their god** (`Saints.Lean`, from round 3's `PawnGods.Sketch`): a faith's saints lean its believers
  toward each saint's god a little more (`SaintsMath.WithSaints`, +0.35 of the strongest lean, never past it); its damned
  leave each believer uneasy about the god each is tied to, once (`SaintsMath.DamnedDread` 20, with its line of why).
- **The book** (`Saints.BookLines`, `GodLorePage.SaintsPart`): "Of its saints", in the keeper's hand, under the chapter the
  colony keeps the god under: its own ("Saint Mira, who cared for the sick for years, named by the council on 5th of Aprimay,
  5502. Her day is kept each year on the day she died."), its faiths' ("The faith of the Way of Ash holds Saint Aranea among
  its saints."), the damned ("The faith of the Way of Ash fears Vorgath the Damned, and never prays to them.") and those
  kept no more.
- Kept in worship's own hour and day (`Worship.Hourly`, `Daily`): no Sched slot of its own. Dev actions: "Gods: a faith's
  saints (log)", "Gods: a fallen colonist waits for the saint's card", "Gods: the saint's card now", "Gods: a saint's day
  kept now", "Gods: pray at a saint's place now". Saved small (`SaintsBook`: the colony's saints, the deaths waiting, the
  statues, the faiths' saints seen, who took the damned to heart, each with its cap: `Tools/save_estimate.py`). Tested in
  `SaintsTests`.

### Each god's own happenings, batch 1 (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.237.0)

The player, 14 November 2026: "each God's events and interactions and effects, etc., you know, feel unique to the god,
not like every god's effect is kind of similar, but it's just a different name attached to it ... each of the gods should
feel really unique in what it does and whether or how it interacts with the world, what the impact is, how these things
play out on the map"; "gods effect should be noticeable"; "the "Each god its own" proposals sounds great too! go ahead
with all of this". Round 4 of `docs/gods-next-proposals.md` (section C, each god's happenings), batch 1: Hollin, Smoulder,
Bellwether, Morel, Ennu, Pip and Cirrus; batch 2 (Hush, Undertow, Helios, Selene, Murmur, Ducat, and Tamiu's more)
follows. Each god does things no other god does, every one played out on the map: who goes where, what is seen and heard,
what changes. Built with the lore never built before: Hollin speaking through her dryads, Smoulder's bargains in dreams
and the bargain at the shaft, Morel's mourner at the graveyard.

- **The frame** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnHappenings.cs`, `OwnHappeningsMath.cs`; one file a god beside them, `Own<God>.cs`):
  - `OwnHappening`, 29 happenings, each named for its god (`HollinRoots` ...); `OwnHappeningsMath` has every rule, pure.
  - The pace every one keeps (`PaceOf`: a gap from its last, about how often once free and called for, how long its chance
    grows; `DayChance` through `GodPaceMath`): never within its gap, never without a reason (`GodPaceMath.Trigger`; a
    condition nearly always true is none, so nothing fires just because it is free), a strong reason likelier, its god's
    nearness only a little more often (`GodNearMath.WorldFactor`). The ones that answer something on the map (a rising, a
    sign, a death, a switch flicked, a fight) come only with it, at their own chance and gap. The rare ones far apart: the
    bargain 45 days, the wounded thrumbo 45, the mourner 30, the dryads 20, the old tree once a year.
  - Saved in `OwnHappeningsBook` (a GameComponent): when each last came (one entry a happening), what is under way (one of
    each at a time), the few children who touched the horn (`HornKept`, 8) and the sky's watches (`MaxWatches`, 8). Its
    steps run on a due tick only while something is under way; no Sched slot of its own (the gods' day and hour,
    `GodsOnMapBook.Daily`, `Hourly`).
  - Words: a card says what was seen, its title naming the god only where the colony knows it was that god
    (`OwnHappenings.Card`, `GodsOnMapWords.Title`; `CC_GodO_<what>_Text`, `_Title`, `_TitleNamed`); someone of the colony
    says it in one sentence (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodOwnSaid`, `Speech.Say`); the colony's book keeps it in its witness's words
    (`CC_GodO_Saw_*` through `GodsOnMapWords.Saw`, so `Gods.Remember` finds who else saw it: the seam a pawn's belief
    hooks). "Someone finds it": whoever can see the place says so at once, else the nearest walks over to look
    (`OwnHappenings.Found`).
  - Hooks, never forks: Hollin's rising (`GodRising.Rise`), Smoulder's turning (`GodWaking.Turned`), a god's own sign
    (`GodOmens.Seen`), the gods' anger and kindness (`GodHealth.Wrath`, `Bless`, `Shunned`), the white beast's stay
    (`SacredAnimal`), the stranger's judgement (`GodGifts.Outcome`), a festival kept (`Festivals.Kept`); and five game
    hooks, each off with the deeper hooks setting: a tree felled (`Plant.PlantCollected`), one of the game's events
    (thrumbos passing), a work of art made (`CompArt.JustCreatedBy`), a switch flicked (`CompFlickable.DoFlick`), a turret
    about to fire (`Building_TurretGun.TryStartShootSomething`).
- **Hollin** (`OwnHollin.cs`):
  - *The roots remember.* A season of many trees felled and few planted (the Mossborn's ledger, `MossLedger`: 15 felled
    with under a third planted back, strongly 40 with hardly any): for three mornings a floor tile breaks in the room
    nearest the last tree felled, roots and brambles up through it, dirt about it; the first morning a line in the news,
    each morning someone finds it and says so.
  - *The dryads' word* (her lore: she speaks through her dryads a word at a time). With an anima or gauranlen tree, its
    dryads (any mod's: the game's own mark, so Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Dryads' too) and something real to point at:
    every dryad stops and turns to one colonist out of doors, one walks up to them, and they say they heard one word,
    "spare" (trees marked to be cut), "wait" (the next season's frost while fields grow), "plant" (a field left bare in the
    growing season) or "burn" (blight), the card pointing at the thing; a different word than last time where there is
    one. Never without something to point at.
  - *The green walk.* Her rising (half her risings in the growing season, more the nearer she is) rises twice more along a
    line across the land an hour apart; new grass and wild flowers spring up between, the wild beasts nearby walk after her,
    and the last place is a mark on the land.
  - *The old tree spared.* The colony's oldest tree near it, noted; still standing in spring after fifty days and twenty
    trees felled round it, it has a ring of wild healroot at its foot, found and said.
- **Smoulder** (`OwnSmoulder.cs`):
  - *The bargain at the shaft* (his lore: bargains in dreams). A colony holding silver with someone sleeping or mining
    under thick rock: a miner dreams of a warm, reasonable voice and tells it at breakfast (the dream book, the journal);
    a card asks what to do (`Rimfolk_Evt_GodBargain`, every age's words): carry all of it down, carry half and keep the
    rest, or keep the silver. Carried, the dreamer takes it from the stores to the deepest cell under the mountain
    (`Shaft`) and sets it down; it sinks into the rock with heat, rubble and a warm floor. Days later a vein comes up in the
    rock beside the shaft: gold worth more than was thrown for a bargain kept to the letter, steel with a skin of gold
    worth no more than what went down for one bent (the tale of the chief and the gilded lead). Its card, and someone finds
    it. The silver asked: a seventh of what is held (600 at least), 150 to 400.
  - *His proper name.* An artist who holds him (or a colony that has heard of him) may name a new sculpture for Aurelian
    the Ninth (its title, said aloud, the journal); the next day a seam of silver glints in the rock face nearest where
    they worked.
  - *The heat from below.* On the turn before stone may first fall in the deep working (`GodWaking`), its floor grows hot
    for four hours: heat pushed up each half hour, the air shimmering, a line in the news, the miner says so.
  - *The stretching dream.* The night after his winged shadow crossed the land at noon, every miner (Mining 6, or a
    passion for it) wakes from the same dream of something enormous stretching under the mountain.
  - *Silver kept from the deep.* A hoard of 2000 unpaid for sixty days (a gift taken at his place or a bargain kept pays
    it), or a bargain bent: a miner wakes from a warm dream with a burn across the palm, at the shared harm budget's rate
    (`HarmKinds.GodBurn`), on a card; with harm off or the budget spent, only the dream.
- **Bellwether** (`OwnBellwether.cs`):
  - *His road.* On his last evening he stops at the colony's edge at dusk and lowers his head toward its youngest; at
    dawn he takes his road through the colony to the far edge. Walls or fences across it (a wild beast can't open a door):
    he walks as far as he can and waits there, and those who see him wait are ashamed (-2) until someone opens a way (a
    gate held open) and he passes; after ten hours he turns back the way he came.
  - *The child who touched the horn.* Remembered from then on (the newest eight); within the hour before the weather turns
    wet they stop, look up at the sky and say the rain (or snow) is coming, and it comes: the weather's own next turn,
    rolled and held to as a forecast is (`WeatherDynamics.Foreseen`, with the forecast setting on), each child six days apart
    at least.
  - *A wounded thrumbo at the edge.* Where thrumbos can live and none was killed lately (strongly after he was let pass
    in peace): a wild thrumbo, bitten and clawed, comes in and lies down at the colony's edge; a card asks whether to tend
    it (`Rimfolk_Evt_GodHurtBeast`). Sent, the colony's best with animals walks out, kneels by it and tends its wounds as
    well as their hands allow; it gets up and goes its way, and the strange peace settles on the colony. Left, it limps
    off by the next day.
  - *The last of something.* The night after thrumbos pass (the game's own event), someone dreams of a white beast
    searching the world for the rest of its kind.
- **Morel** (`OwnMorel.cs`):
  - *The mourner at the graveyard* (her lore, never built before). In the days after a death of the colony's, at dusk a
    figure of pale threads stands at the edge of the graves, still, all night (`GodSky`, `SkySign.Mourner`), with the
    moment's weight (her own presence, spore-fall, after it); those who saw it share the memory. At dawn it is gone, and a
    ring of mushrooms stands where it was: a mark on the land.
  - *The ring, pointing.* A ring of mushrooms comes up overnight round something real: a person's body left lying a day,
    the stores going rotten (white threads round it, indoors), else, only when she is drawn near, on open ground over a
    small thing buried long ago, which whoever goes to look kneels and digs up (gold, jade, silver).
  - *White threads before the freezer fails.* Her anger (the cooler's breakdown, `GodHealth`) is forewarned: white threads
    across the floor of the room the cooler keeps cold, and the breakdown comes the next day, in the small hours.
  - *Spores in the breath.* Someone walking through one of her rings (the mourner's, the pointing ring, her sign's) may
    hear her for a moment, soft and too close (-1 for a day), once in sixty days each.
- **Ennu** (`OwnEnnu.cs`):
  - *The small test.* While the stranger at the gate stays, it asks one small thing, a different one each time where it
    can: a story by the fire in the evening, the name of whoever cooked, to be shown the graves, a coat in the cold (only
    what the colony can answer). Someone of the colony answers it on the map: the best talker walks over to the fire and
    tells a story, the cook goes and says their name, someone walks it out to the graves, someone carries a coat from the
    stores and it puts it on. It thanks them by name, and it counts toward the welcome it judges (`StrangerStay.Credit`,
    a kindness).
  - *Tales by the fire.* In the evenings of its stay it sits by the colony's fire and tells a piece of another god's story
    to whoever sits near (`GodTales.Tell`, at our fire), two at most a stay: it carries news between the gods.
  - *The bowl set out.* On the Open Door night (its festival kept) and now and then in the ten days after a kind welcome,
    the cook carries a meal to the table at dusk and leaves it; by morning it is empty, a smear of chalk on the table, and
    the words "Thank you, (the cook)" read aloud by whoever finds it and on its card.
  - *The kindest carries something.* For fifteen days after the Guest judged a welcome kind, a visitor on the land seeks
    out its kindest and tells them the road's news.
- **Pip** (`OwnPip.cs`; a colony with no machines never meets it):
  - *The machine that would not stop.* Switched off, a machine (where Pip is known) may keep running an hour with a shudder
    of sparks, and stop on its own.
  - *Its message to the stars.* For a reason (the comms console used lately, Pip drawn near, an old terminal on the land:
    Ideology's and Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Props and Decor's), the console comes on by itself in the small hours, and
    an old terminal hums back; in the morning a half-written message to the stars is on its screen, the screen still lit,
    its words on a card and read aloud by whoever comes to it.
  - *The turret that held fire.* In a fight a turret of the colony's holds its fire a breath as a colonist crosses its
    line, and the colonist says so (+3), six days apart at least.
  - *Sulking, with a warning.* The day before its short circuit (its anger, the game's own) the colony's lights flicker
    slow and sad for hours.
  - *Mended overnight, shown.* Its kindness's mended machine winks its light as it comes back.
- **Cirrus** (`OwnCirrus.cs`; no body, all of it out of the sky):
  - *The star at the door.* Its kindness, the game's own meteorite, comes only to a colony that watches the sky (someone
    at a telescope or lying out skygazing, the game's or Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded's, twice in ten days, or its
    festival kept in fifteen), and the one who watched says they saw it fall.
  - *The wrong-way star.* Whoever saw its sign dreams that night of something falling, and says which way; the next day
    cargo pods (the game's own) come down just there.
  - *The aurora on the coldest night.* A night colder than any for ten days and below -5, someone out of doors: the sky may
    fill with light (the game's aurora) for five hours.
  - *Dry thunder.* After six dry days with nothing of the sky's for twenty: thunder and lightning roll over the far hills
    for a couple of hours, the sky clear, no rain, never on the colony.
- **Harm, the ages, the mods.** The only hurt is Smoulder's burn, through the shared budget and on a card; the wounded
  thrumbo's wounds are the wild's. Every age: what each needs is the colony's own (a floor or bare ground, a cooler, a
  console, a turret, a coat of its age from its stores, a fire or a hearth), so a tribal colony's Pip does nothing and its
  bargain's card speaks of the deep places; both cards have every age's words. The player's mods softly: any mod's dryads
  by the game's mark, Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Props and Decor's terminal by name, Vanilla Social Interactions
  Expanded's skygazing, A RimWorld of Magic's motes by name (green, blue and gray twinkles, heat, psionic current) with
  Rimfolk's own light where it isn't loaded.
- Dev mode: one action a happening, "Gods: <god>'s <happening> now" (and a few second steps: the vein, the mourner gone, the
  bowl found), and "Gods: each god's own happenings (log)".
- Tested in `OwnHappeningsTests` (the pace of each, every rule, the cards, the words, the lines, the seams, the save).
  Not seen in a real game: see the handoff's entry.

### Each god's own happenings, the second seven (the player's go, 14 November 2026; round 4, batch 2; released 0.238.0)

The player: "each God's events and interactions and effects, etc., you know, feel unique to the god, not like every god's
effect is kind of similar, but it's just a different name attached to it ... each of the gods should feel really unique in
what it does and whether or how it interacts with the world, what the impact is, how these things play out on the map";
then "gods effect should be noticeable", "go ahead with all of this". Section C of `docs/gods-next-proposals.md`, its
second batch: Hush, Undertow, Helios, Selene, Murmur, Ducat, and two more for Tamiu (defName and key `Rimfolk_God_Mog`).
Twenty-two happenings, each unlike any other god's, each played out on the map, each with its own card or news line and
its line in the colony's book; none hurts anyone.

- **In the first seven's frame** (the section above): the twenty-two are entries of the same `OwnHappening` list (after
  batch 1's, so a save's list of when each last came keeps its order; Tamiu's by her key, `MogThreshold`, `MogLostDead`),
  with their pace in the same `OwnHappeningsMath.PaceOf`, their saved state in the same `OwnHappeningsBook` (a part of it,
  `OwnSeven.cs`: one small record a god and the ruins' rooms heard), their hour and steps called from the frame's
  (`OwnHappenings.Seven`, `SevenSteps`), their feasts from its `FestivalKept`, and the frame's `Came`, `Due`, `Acts`,
  `Saw`, `Stand`, `GoTo`. Their own rules are a part of the same pure class (`Gods/OnMap/OwnSevenMath.cs`).
- **The pace** (`PaceOf`, `DayChance`): each happening its own gap, its chance small at the end of the gap and growing over
  a long ramp (`GodPaceMath.DayChance`), weighed by its reason (`GodPaceMath.Trigger`: none means never, however free)
  and its god's nearness (`GodNearMath.WorldFactor`), looked at once an hour (`OwnHappenings.Calls`), only where its god
  acts at the home (`Acts`). Six follow something else and have no chance of their own: the beasts keeping away (a
  bargain), the hollow ear (a room of ruins, at its own chance), the look back (an eclipse), the first fruit (Helios's
  feast), the morning card (the moon's return), the trail of coins (silver gone from a hoard). The rare ones far apart: the walk round the edge and the sun's return once a
  winter (40 days), the frogs once in 25 days at the soonest.
- **Hush, the Long White** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnHush.cs`):
  - *The word in the frost* (gap 12 days; first light, frost outdoors): a word written in rime beside the colony's outer
    door (on a window where a mod adds one, Open The Windows' by name), pointing at something real (`Word`): WARM for
    someone with hypothermia or sleeping in a bedroom under 8 degrees, BREAD for fewer than four days of food, WOOD for a
    colony that heats with wood and has under 60 logs, COUNT for food going to waste (a carcass rotting on the home ground,
    a stack three quarters spoiled and not kept cold). The first one up walks out to it, reads it aloud and says what they
    take it to mean; the card has the word and the plain fact beside it ("There are about 2 days of food left in the
    stores."). Melted before anyone comes, nothing is told.
  - *The old man's fire* (gap 15; at dusk in a cold snap, the old, a baby or the sick abed): the one of the colony fondest
    of them (the kind, Hush's believers a little more) walks to the bed and sits up the night with them, saying so; kept
    through most of the night (`VigilKept`, 70 percent) the cold snap ends at five o'clock, the frost on the ground runs
    off, the keeper has "sat up through the cold" (+4) and the one kept warm "someone sat up with me" (+5). The card's
    "keeping the fire fed" by the colony's age (`CC_GodHush_Warmth_0` to `_3`). The keeper is never pulled from food or
    sleep (`OwnHappenings.Yields`): too tired, the vigil just ends.
  - *The walk round the edge* (gap 40; the longest night, days 6 to 8 of winter, strongly; a night past -18 degrees
    ordinarily; from 22 o'clock): Hush's tall white figure (`SkySign.Figure`) walks all the way round the colony out past
    its farthest building, four cells every 300 ticks, leaving a line of rime an arm's width wide; anyone within twenty
    steps and it moves on, footprints leading to where it stood and then none, said aloud once. At first light the card:
    all the way round or part of the way, and who saw it. The morning after, Helios's sun comes back the likelier.
  - *Frost on the grave* (gap 20; a death of the colony's within two days, in winter or with food short, with food going
    to waste): at dusk rime lies on the new grave and nowhere else, the music falls silent, and Hush's own white silence
    comes down in its hard form (its presence, round 2). Two to four days later the frost melts and a ring of mushrooms
    stands round the grave (Glowstool, Agarilux, Bryolux): the soft mother taking back what the cold kept whole, in both
    gods' chapters, and one of her rings for batch 1's "Morel's breath" (`OwnMorel.Remember`).
- **Undertow, the Hunger** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnUndertow.cs`), never named on any card or line:
  - *The others turn away*: after a bargain (`GodVoid`, read from the world book's newest "take"), for eight days every
    beast that comes within five cells of the one who said yes (the colony's, the wild ones, the dryads, the cats) gets
    up and walks ten cells off, unhurried; someone who saw it says so once a day, and the first time a card.
  - *The dark that drifts* (gap 10; at night, someone at the edge of an extreme break or bleeding out strongly, a major
    break ordinarily; twice as likely on a night with no moon): a darkness (`SkySign.Dark`) comes in 28 cells from them
    and drifts two cells every 250 ticks toward them, the lamps it passes guttering (`GodOmens.Play`). Someone awake
    beside them stops it a few steps off; a lit lamp beside them stops it at the light's edge; else it reaches them,
    stands over them till dawn and, awake, they hear it, kindly. At dawn the card says which: stood over ("the dark stood
    over me" -4, and dread of it), held by the light, held by company (both "kept the dark off", +3). It never comes while
    someone keeps the dark face at the door (Selene's).
  - *The hollow ear* (gap 12): someone of the colony standing for the first time in a room of old ruins (indoors, 600
    cells at most, holding a thing of the ancients not the colony's; thirty rooms remembered) stops with a hand to one ear,
    one time in three: a hollow ear for ten days (`Rimfolk_HollowEar`, psychic sensitivity +15 percent) and a card.
- **Helios, the Giver** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnHelios.cs`):
  - *He looks back*: the day after an eclipse (the game's, Alpha Animals', Rimfolk's), from ten o'clock, his long noon in
    its hard form (eight degrees warmer, the light held white); everyone out of doors stops and shades their eyes, heat
    shimmer about them, someone says so; the card ("A white noon") is named where the colony has learned the eclipse as
    his.
  - *The first fruit in the sun*: his feast kept (`Festivals.Kept`), at noon, up to ten of the colony take a piece of fresh
    fruit from the stores (berries first) and walk out into the sun by the largest field, and eat it there (the game's own
    eating sound and effect); "the first fruit in the sun" (+4). With no fresh fruit in the stores, they stand out in the
    sun together and the news says there was none.
  - *The sun comes back* (gap 40; the morning after the longest night, or after Hush's walk): up to twelve of those up walk
    out to the east side of the colony and stand facing the sunrise, gold light lying on them; "the sun came back" (+3).
- **Selene, the Mirror** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnSelene.cs`):
  - *What came back, told plainly*: the morning after the moon returned someone's deed (`GodReturn`, read from the gods'
    short memory), once they are up, they walk to what was found or look at what changed, say it in one sentence, and a
    card says what was found and by whose bed (the newest thing there), a dream, a wound closed, frost about where they
    slept, an animal at their door; "It has happened to them before." when it has.
  - *Her face in still water* (gap 14; the full moon, a clear night, still water within 45 cells, someone up): the moon's
    light lies on the water (`SkySign.Moon`, small), the one up walks down to the water's edge and stands there a long
    while; "her face in the water" (+5) and a card.
  - *The watch she keeps company* (gap 6; the small hours under a moon at least half full, clear, someone up out of doors,
    under arms strongly): the moonlight about them for an hour, "the moon kept me company" (+3) and a moonlit watch till
    dawn (`Rimfolk_MoonlitWatch`: sight +10 percent, aiming time 15 percent shorter).
  - *The dark face kept* (gap 14; a night with no moon): a night owl (else one who holds her, else whoever is up and free)
    goes and stands outside the colony's door facing out until three o'clock, says why, and "kept the dark face" (+2);
    while they stand, the dark that drifts does not come.
- **Murmur, Old Croak** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnMurmur.cs`):
  - *Sung back to* (his feast, the Singing at the Wells, or gap 12 in a dry spell of six days, strongly in a drought or
    ten, with two of the colony who hold him): at dusk up to eight walk to the well (Dubs Bad Hygiene's, any well of the
    colony's) or the still water or marsh and stand round it singing, the game's music notes over them; "sang at the water"
    (+3), the colony's book keeps the rite. Answered (`SongAnswered`: 0.5, at his feast 0.65, more the nearer he is drawn),
    four to sixteen hours later the rain comes (snow in a frost), a drought ends, a deep croak comes up out of the water
    (Odyssey's or Alpha Genes' frog call), a card named where the long rains are known as his; when it stops, Seasonal
    Weather's double rainbow.
  - *The water gives back* (gap 20; the morning after two or three wet days, the rain stopped): on the mud at the water's
    edge near the colony, 12 to 40 silver and, half the time, an old worn thing of the colony's age at most from the
    whole of the player's mods (a weapon or a piece of clothing worth 15 to 250, poor, 40 percent worn); the first one free
    walks down and finds it, a gift of the god they take it for (`PawnGods.Gift`), and a card.
  - *The frogs come in* (gap 25; the evening the rain breaks eight dry days): six to sixteen of Odyssey's bullfrogs up out
    of the wet ground all over the colony, croaking, gone off the land at first light; without Odyssey, only their croaking.
- **Ducat, the Restless Gold** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnDucat.cs`):
  - *The trail of coins*: its anger at a hoard (`GodHealth.Missing`, as before) now leaves the way it went: of the silver
    taken, up to 18 lie as single coins every three cells from the store out through the outer door to the nearest edge
    of the land, the last ones gone over it; in daylight the first one free walks to the first coin and looks along the
    line, and the news says so. The coins can be gathered back.
  - *The open purse* (its feast, the Open Purse, or gap 15 with one of the colony devoted to it and a visitor on the land):
    the giver takes one to five coins from the stores, walks over to a visitor, says a word and presses them into their
    hand (into their pack); their people think 2 better of the colony, the colony's book keeps it, and the giver has led
    the rite (`PawnGods.RiteLed`).
  - *The beetle that leads* (gap 15; traders or visitors on the land strongly, a hoard of 1000 ordinarily): a golden beetle
    walks off a table and across the floor (`GodSky.Crawl`) to where a gold coin lies that nobody dropped, 5 to 12 cells
    off; whoever saw it follows and finds the coin.
- **Tamiu, the Keeper of the Threshold** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnTamiu.cs`; `MogsWays` keeps her stay, riddle, keepers and
  wrapped dead):
  - *The cat at the threshold* (gap 6; one of the colony bleeding out within hours or a sickness all but won): a cat of the
    colony's (else a stray in from the edge) comes and stays beside them, never pulled from its own food or sleep; someone
    says so. Died, it stays by the body two hours; come through and out of danger six hours, it gets up, stretches and
    walks off, "the cat let me go" (+4) and a card.
  - *The cat by the lost dead* (gap 5; a body of the colony's lying unburied 25 cells or more from the colony's middle for
    half a day): a cat walks out to it and sits by it crying (the game's cat call); the first one free goes to it and finds
    the body, which is no longer forbidden, and a card says who it is.
- **The unseen rule:** a card is titled by the god's name only where `Gods.CardName` allows (the colony saw it act plainly,
  or has learned the sign named: the eclipse, the long rains, the seasonal flooding), else by what was seen; a card's
  text never names it; Undertow is named nowhere. A line names the god (`{GOD}`) only when tagged named, which the code
  gives where the colony is sure. What is seen goes to the colony's book in the witness's words and moves each witness's
  belief in the god they take it for (`GodsOnMapWords.Saw`, so `Gods.Remember` and `PawnGods.Saw`); the colony's own rites
  (the song, the first fruit, the purse) as kept (`Worship.Booked`); the dark's standing over someone as dread
  (`PawnGods.Fear`); what the water gave back as a gift (`PawnGods.Gift`).
- **Every age:** the frost, the dark, the sun, the moon, the water, the coins and the cats are every age's; where the
  means matter the words take the age's form (the vigil's warmth, a tribal colony with no door has the word on the open
  ground), and the old thing the water gives back is of the colony's age at most.
- **Words match the map:** each card says only what happened there (the cold coming down only where Hush's presence began,
  the walk all the way round only where it went all the way, the lamps burning low only where some did, the first fruit
  eaten only by those who ate).
- **Where it plugs in:** the frame's hour, steps and feasts (`OwnHappenings.Hourly`, `Step`, `FestivalKept`: one line
  each), `GodHealth.Missing` (`OwnDucat.Trail`: one line). Saved in the frame's `OwnHappeningsBook` (its `last`, one
  entry a happening of both batches, and `ExposeSeven`: each god's record and the ruins' rooms; `Tools/save_estimate.py`
  models them); short steps on the frame's due tick, no Sched slot. Twenty-four dev actions "Gods: <god>'s ... now"
  (`Gods/OwnSevenDebug.cs`, out of the map's code as batch 1's are). Tests: `Tools/Tests/OwnHappeningsSevenTests.cs` (and batch 1's
  `OwnHappeningsTests`, widened to both). The twelve moods in `Tools/Balance/Rates.cs`.

### The gods felt, and what follows them (the player's go, 15 November 2026; released 0.256.0)

The player, with their save `League_of_Toba_2`: "so far i really like how the gods event appear, also with the sound,
visual effect and camera centering! if there's other similarly impressive visual effects, include some variety. but also
for many of the gods occurences i don't see any real game impact. it's a cool event but nothing rally comes from it, for
example the stranger one at the altar i have and had three times already this event. there should be more ingame effect.
also pawns seem to take no mood or heart/strain or other gameplay impact either. update this now"; then "effects can be all
kinds of things, be creative, not just what you listed", and "the effect can be something more impactful also, remember
these are gods. but keep it balanced, not that strong effects come up all the time. there should be range and variety".

- **Why, from their save.** Ennu's offering at the Stranger's church was taken before everyone's eyes three times
  (ticks 5767607, 6387607 and 6567607, the last two three days apart), each a full moment with the camera on it, because
  the colony kept offering and Ennu stayed drawn near; nothing followed but a little belief. Over the save's last 43 days
  about one occurrence of the gods a day was seen, and a mood came only to someone holding that god as their first
  (`Rimfolk_Belief_GodActed`); the heart never moved.
- **The frame** (`Gods/Touch/GodTouch.cs`, `GodTouchBook`): every occurrence someone of the colony saw reaches it through
  the seams already there (`Gods.Remember` for an act on the land with its witnesses, `Gods.Moment` for a god's moment,
  and an offering found taken); a moment and the words written of it a moment later are one occurrence (by god and
  home, two hours). Each says what it was (`GodAct.what`, `PresenceSpec.what`: its words key, CC_GodO_Saw_Roots..., or
  the part's own word, "world", "told", "taken", "prayer", "council", "vow", "mark"). It waits until the god's moment has
  played out (`GodPresence.Busy`, an hour at most), then:
  - **felt** by each who saw it (`GodTouch.Felt`, `GodTouchMath.MoodFor`), by how they stand toward the god they took it
    for (`StanceOf`: a scoffer, in dread of it, holding to it, or neither) and what it was like (`ToneOf`: a blessing
    kind, an anger dark, an omen a sign, a coming or a god at work a sight; the Hunger's signs and sights dark):

    | | kindness | sight | sign | anger |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | holds to it | my god was good to us +4 (seen plainly: +6) | my god showed itself +3 (plainly +6) | +3 | something angry was here -3 |
    | neither | saw something of the gods +2 (plainly: saw a god plainly +4) | +2 (+4) | an odd sign -1 | -3 |
    | dreads it | nothing | the one I fear came near -3 (showed itself -5) | the belief round's flinch | -3 (-5) |
    | scoffer | nothing | nothing | nothing | nothing |

    The heart through its own API: strain eased for a believer (1 to 2.5) and a little for anyone at a kindness or a
    sight (0.5 to 1), through the day's small joys and their cap (`HeartLogic.EaseJoys`); strain for one in dread when
    it comes or is angry (1 to 2) and a little for anyone at an anger (0.5 to 1), through dread and its cap
    (`HeartLogic.Build`, `StrainSource.Dread`). The kindness's mood takes the place of the belief round's smaller one.
  - **followed**, for an occurrence with no effect of its own (`GodTouchMath.HasOwnEffect`: the moments in the world, a
    prayer answered, the council's answers, the waking, the stranger's judgement, the weather's answer, the late gift,
    the sacred beasts, the moon's return, the great cat, and the own happenings that carry one: the bargain and its
    vein, the seam, the burn, the star and the pods, the aurora, the wounded thrumbo tended, the white beast kept
    waiting, the old tree, the green walk, the ring dug up, the bowl found empty, the turret, the small tests, the
    kindest's news, the sulk, the thaw, Murmur's rain, give-back and frogs, Ducat's trail and coin, the moonlit watch and
    the dark's happenings; a letter's tale and a mark talked of are no occurrence at all), by one of its god's own
    effects (`GodTouchMath.Table`, `GodTouchEffects`).
- **Three strengths** (`GodTouchMath.Tier`): an occurrence brings an effect nine times in ten for a kindness, eight for
  a sight, half for an anger and about a third for an omen; notable about a third of those (more for a god seen plainly
  or a coming, less for an anger), great one in twenty-five (four times that for a coming seen plainly, half for an
  anger, never for an omen); a god's small ones twice a day at most at a home, its notable 8 days apart and any god's 3,
  its great 120 days apart and any god's 40; a tier whose wait isn't past falls to the one below. At about one
  occurrence a day (as the save had) that comes to about 25 small, 6 notable and less than one great a colony-year, and
  a third or so leave the moods only. The god's effect for the tier is leaned away from what it did lately at the home
  (`GodPaceMath.Lean`), among those that can happen now (`GodTouchEffects.Can`); with none of a tier, one of the tier
  below. A small effect is the god's own look at the place and a message; a notable one also a sound and the colony's
  book; a great one is a god's moment of its own (its sound, the sky, the camera on it, its card, named only where the
  colony knows the god) and everyone of the home who believes at all remembers it (+4, three days).
- **Each god's own** (S small, N notable, G great, D an anger):
  - Hollin: S a good day for growing (plant work +15%, harvest +8%, a day), S flowers in a ring where it happened (Vanilla
    Plants Expanded - Flowers' first), S plants learned, N the crops near it grow on a fifth, N wild healroot, N an
    inspiration (Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded's planting, A RimWorld of Magic's farming), G her green stays on the
    land ten days; D brambles.
  - Smoulder: S warm hands (labour and mining +12%), S the fires near it full again, S crafting learned, N ore where it
    happened (steel, silver, a little gold), N an inspiration (creativity, mining), G a seam of gold in the rock nearby
    (`OwnSmoulder.Seam`), G warm stone a week; D the fires near it go out.
  - Bellwether: S a steady eye (hunting stealth, taming and training), S animals learned, N wild game of the land comes
    onto it, N an inspiration (taming, shooting), G animals wander in and stay (the game's own), G his calm ten days; D
    the wild game walks off.
  - Morel: S shaking off sickness (immunity +15%), S medicine learned, N mushrooms where it happened, N the ground there
    turned rich soil, G the fields' soil made rich; D food in the stores starts to go off (never to rotten).
  - Ennu: S easy company (social impact, negotiation), S social learned, N travellers come (the game's visitors, or
    Hospitality's), N a people at peace thinks better of the colony (+6, the game's goodwill), N a trader comes, N an
    inspiration (recruitment, Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded's party), G someone comes to join (the game's
    wanderer), G warm evenings a week.
  - Pip: S a feel for machines (research +12%, building), S the machines near it mended and worn buildings whole, S every
    battery full, N parts where it happened (by the colony's age: none before machines), N an inspiration (research,
    work), G the hum in the wires five days; D a machine breaks down (the game's breakdown).
  - Cirrus: S light on their feet (move speed), S the sky clears, N an aurora at night (the game's), N something falls
    from the sky (the game's ship chunk), N an inspiration (going, shooting), G the high sky a week; D fog.
  - Hush: S at ease in the cold (comfort 8 degrees colder), S snow where it is cold, N the stores' food set back two days
    from spoiling, N a cold snap broken (the stores kept if there is none), G everyone frost-hardy a season (10
    degrees); D the fires near it go out.
  - The Hunger (Undertow, its kindnesses rare): S hearing too much (psychic sensitivity, learning, a little more brittle),
    N an inspiration (learning, A RimWorld of Magic's enlightened); D the fires go out, D a tenth of a stack gone from the
    stores (never all), G (dark) its dark stays two days.
  - Helios: S sun-warmed (work +6%), S clear sky, N the crops near it grow on, N an inspiration (work), G every crop of
    the home grows three tenths in a day and everyone is warmed through five days (work +8%). No anger of his own.
  - Selene: S sleeping deeply (rest +25%, healing +25%), N the worst wounded's wounds heal four tenths, N an inspiration
    (surgery), G an old wound (a scar) gone in the night, G her close moon five days; D a bad night for those who saw it.
  - Tamiu: S calm (mental break threshold, pain shock), S the rats leave and the cats watch, N a cat walks in and stays,
    N an inspiration (taming), G one who saw it kept calm a season (pain less, steadier). No anger of her own; her watch
    is hers only while she walks the land, so it never stays.
  - Murmur: S a clean hand in the kitchen (food poisoning halved, cooking faster), S rain where it isn't freezing, N the
    crops near it grow on, N fish on the bank (Odyssey's), G a spring wells up where it happened (shallow water on open
    natural ground away from buildings and fields), G his rain four days; D fog.
  - Ducat: S a good eye for a bargain (trade price), N silver where it happened, N a trader (one in orbit for a colony with
    comms), N an inspiration (trade), G gold where it happened (15 to 30), G his glint a week; D a tenth of the silver
    gone.
  The god's own presence staying (`Linger`) is its round 2 presence (`GodDef.presence`) after a great moment of its own,
  for days (`PresenceSpec.lingerTicks`, `GameCondition_GodPresence.Begin`'s `linger`), its sky only lightly tinted and
  the wind as it is; never the long noon, the white silence, the rot or Tamiu's watch.
- **Less repetition.** An offering is taken before everyone's eyes (the god's moment, the camera on it) a month apart at
  most a god at a home, and any god's a week and a day (`GodTouchMath.PlainTaking`, `GodTouch.PlainTakingAllowed`);
  otherwise as the gods are felt, gone by morning in the god's own way, and what follows comes once someone sees it go
  or finds the place empty (`GodTouch.Taken`). The same occurrence at a home within ten days (an offering taken, four
  days a god) leaves the moods only (`SameKeyGapDays`). A god seen often at a home lately gives the others their turn:
  its own happenings that much less likely (`GodTouchMath.Turn`, by its occurrences there in the last ten days, never
  below a third; `OwnHappenings.Due`).
- **More to see** (`Gods/Touch/GodTouchFx.cs`): each god its own look where it acts, the game's own flecks and effecters
  and the player's mods' by name: Hollin's leaves and green flashes, Smoulder's embers and heat, Bellwether's dust,
  Morel's pale spores, Ennu's skip flash and footprints, Pip's sparks, Cirrus's lightning glow and a flash over the land,
  Hush's snow and frost on the ground, the Hunger's dark rings and smoke, Helios's light shafts and a flash, Selene's pale
  rings and twinkles, Tamiu's sand, Murmur's water, Ducat's gold glints (A RimWorld of Magic's motes, Vanilla Psycasts
  Expanded's cold glow, heat, sparks, black smoke and skip flash, Anomaly's and Biotech's flecks). Shown with every
  god's big moment and omen (`GodFx.Flash` with the god's key) and with each of its effects, the more the stronger. The
  camera goes to every god's doing but the small touches (0.256.1, "The camera for every god's doing" below).
- **The unseen rule holds:** what follows is told as what was seen ("Flowers came up in a ring where it happened at
  Mapa."), its words never name a god; a great one's card is named only where the colony knows the god; the blessings'
  labels say what is felt ("warm hands"); the colony's book keeps the notable and great as those who saw them saw them
  (`GodTouch.Write`). Nothing shows a favour or a rule.
- **No harm:** the angers spoil, break, chill and frighten (brambles, a fire out, food going off, a breakdown, fog, a few
  things gone, a bad night), never wound; nothing new in the harm or illness budgets.
- **Every age:** the effects are the land's and the colony's own things (a fire or a hearth, a machine only where there
  are machines, Pip's parts only from the industrial age, the find by the age), and the game's own incidents choose their
  people by the world.
- Saved in `GodTouchBook` (a GameComponent: `last`, a few keys a god and a home; `recent`, `GodTouchMath.RecentKept`;
  `seen`, a season and `MaxSeen`; modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`); its steps on a due tick of its own, no Sched slot.
  Dev mode: "Gods: a god's touch here now..." (any of a god's effects where the mouse is, or any of a tier, or an omen
  seen) and "Gods: the gods' touch (log)". Tests: `Tools/Tests/GodTouchTests.cs`. The moods in `Tools/Balance/Rates.cs`.

### The camera for every god's doing (the player's request, 15 November 2026; released 0.256.1)

The player, after 0.256.0 had kept the camera for the big moments only: "The camera should move for all non-trivial god
moments". `GodPresence.Look` (a place, or a card's first target) jumps the camera there, on a home's map only, and
leaves the game's speed as it is; only a god's coming (`GodPresence.Begin`) also drops to normal speed and fades the
music, as before.

- **Every moment of a god** goes through `Begin` again: `PresenceSpec.quiet` is gone, so a prayer's answers (the one who
  prayed comforted, a fighter given nerve in a raid) move the camera as every other moment does.
- **An omen** (`GodPresence.Omen`): the camera to where it shows, before its sound and the god's look.
- **The gods' own happenings**: every card of theirs (`OwnHappenings.Card`, letter or message, and `OwnHappenings.CardOf`
  for the seven later gods), the late gift left at the gate (`GodGifts.LateGift`), and the great cat's doings (her
  riddle answered right or wrong, a keeper at the grave, the wrapped dead risen: `MogsWays`).
- **What follows** (the gods' touch): a notable effect moves the camera to its place before the god's look plays
  (`GodTouchEffects.Show`); a great one is a moment of its own and already did.
- **Left where the player has it**: the small touches (a day of better work, a skill, snow or rain), dreams (the
  miners' dream, the last of its kind), what is only told (letters' tales, quarrels, marks remembered, the gods' hands
  in the game's events), an offering taken quietly and found gone, and what follows from an order the player gave (the
  silver set down in the shaft, the beast's road opened or not).

### A god's sign comes with its words (the player's report and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.264.1)

The player, with their save: "so my camera just changed to kasumi's corpse and there were mushrooms around them. i assume
this was some god event? however there was no indication about what happened exactly." Then: "yes, your fix! so regarding
the camera it has been that the camera first moves, and then there's a bit a short delay until the animation &
notification appear. I like this and keep it this way, as it creates an excitement for what it is to come".

- **The cause.** A god's moment moves the camera at once (`GodPresence.Look`, a coming's `Begin`), and its words follow
  through the teller (`Tell.Message`, `Tell.Letter`, `Tell.Minor`). On a busy day (a threat within six hours) or past the
  day's count, the teller held the land's news for the evening's colony news, so the camera went to Morel's ring round an
  unburied body and nothing said what it was until evening.
