- **The words come with it.** Where the camera goes, `Tell.CameraWent` notes the map, the place and the tick; a message,
  letter or line about a place within 20 cells of it on that map within the hour after (`TellMath.ByCamera`,
  `CameraTicks`, `CameraCells`), or naming no place, is shown, never held (`TellBook.Judge`'s `seen`) and never sent to
  the evening's news; the same words again soon are still told once. The order and the pause stay as they were: the
  camera first, then the god's look and the words.
- **Who finds it.** `OwnHappenings.Found` (what a god left: a ring, a root through the floor, the bowl, the old tree, the
  vein and so on) sends the nearest of the colony to look only from a short walk away (`OwnHappeningsMath.LookWalkCells`,
  40 cells; two hours to get there); farther, or if they never get there, the first of the colony to come within sight
  of it says it, within a day. The book's line ("Webb found a ring of mushrooms...") is written when someone has seen it,
  in their words, and in no one's if nobody has by then; so the moods and the god's small effects that follow a sign go
  to those who saw it, when they saw it. A ring on open ground is still walked to, to dig at its middle.

### Every god's doing leaves something real (the player's request and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.265.0)

The player, after the ring of mushrooms round an unburied body: "does anything about the body change? like faster decay or
something? is there a gameplay impact from this god event?"; on the proposals: "these proposals sound great! not every god
interaction with the world necessarily needs to have a strong impact, but it should also not be completely trivial"; and the
go: "yes, go ahead with all!". The proposals are `docs/gods-impact-proposals.md` (55 of them, all built).

- **One effect of its own, always** (`Gods/Touch/GodImpactMath.cs`, `Table`): 68 of the 98 kinds of occurrence that had no
  effect of their own now bring one, fitted to what was seen, every time (how often gods' things happen doesn't change). They
  count as having their own effect (`GodTouchMath.HasOwnEffect`), so the touch's random effect doesn't come on top; the moods
  stay as they were. The 21 the proposals leave as they are (`LeftAsTheyAre`: the freezer's threads, the roots through the
  floor, the heat and the warm voice under the mountain, the horn's weather, the white beast's road turned or opened, the
  half-written message and the console at night, the bowl, the dryad's word, the true dream, the roots rising, the wrapped
  dead, the traveller who knew, the body found by the crying cat, the breath in a ring) keep the moods and the random effect;
  the other nine (`NotCovered`: the book's own wordings of a sighting, the frost melted and the beast's road, two marks with
  nothing to feel; the mourner seen, the beast surfacing as a god rises, the god's beast staring) are untouched.
- **Where it lands** (`GodTouch.Resolve`, `GodImpact.Follow`): an effect on the place happens whether or not anyone of the
  colony saw it, there to be found: `Gods.Remember` and `Gods.Moment` now note an occurrence nobody saw when it has an effect
  of its own, and the touch's early return no longer stops it (the moods still go only to those who saw it). An effect on
  people goes to those it names (`GodTouch.About`, said by each happening just before its words: the dead one's closest, the
  dying, the binger, the dreamers, the miners, those who watched the sunrise, the line of frost's cells, the cup, the work of
  art) or to the one named in its words (`GodTouch.Saying`, from `GodsOnMapWords.Saw`). Only an inspiration, the sweet
  smoke's good mood and a bad night need someone to have seen it.
- **Morel.** The ring round an unburied body: the body rots to bones over a day and a half (the game's own rot moved on,
  `RotAt`), and the ground inside the ring turns rich soil (the touch's own, radius 1.5). The threads round rot in the
  stores: the rotten stack is gone and the floor under it clean (never a person's body). The ring where the mourner stood:
  every memory of grief for a death at the home ends sooner (three tenths of what is left, `GriefAge`), with a small
  "grief easing" memory (+2, a day) saying why. A ring of mushrooms overnight: the sign already brings up real glowstools;
  the soil inside the ring turns rich. Fine white threads across a floor: the food stored in that room keeps a day and a
  half less over three days (half again of its keeping each day, never to rotten from it; a small harm).
- **Hush.** Frost on a grave at dusk: the three of the colony closest to the dead (kin first, then those who thought most of
  them, opinion 30 or more) sleep deeply until morning ("sleeping well", rest x1.5). The ring where the grave's frost
  melted: flowers round the grave (the touch's bloom). The walk in the night: up to four tender crops within a cell and a
  half of its line of frost take the game's own cold and die (`MakeLeafless(Cold)`; a small harm). The word in the frost:
  a few pieces of jade or a little silver lie there (the touch's find, Hush's own now). Frost writing by a wall: the room
  behind it is held at 5°C for a day.
- **Helios.** The sunrise after the longest night: those who stood there are fully rested. The noon light after the eclipse
  and the sun standing still: every crop in the open grows a day ahead (a day of its growing), and the solar panels give
  their most until sundown (a hook on their output, as much as their roof lets them). The air shimmering at noon: a "warm
  afternoon" condition, +5°C on the open ground until evening (`GameCondition_GodWarmth`).
- **Selene.** The full moon in still water: the one who stood by it is inspired (the god's own kind, else the game's). The
  door kept on a night with no moon: while the keeper stands at the door, a threat that would come at the home waits on the
  game's own queue until a little after their night ends (`HoldTillDawn`, `OwnSelene.KeptNow`); at dawn a line says nothing
  came, only when something was held. The moon huge and close: everyone at the home sleeps deeper until morning (rest x1.4).
  A star moving the wrong way: the one who watched it is inspired, to research first (Vanilla Social Interactions
  Expanded's, by name).
- **Tamiu.** A cat beside someone near death: their pain is less (x0.6) while it stays, gone when the cat goes. The cat
  stayed to the end: those who mourn that one find their grief ends sooner (as the mourner's ring does). The cat walked
  away: the one who lived heals half again as fast for three days. Every cat facing the graves, a cat on a grave: the rats
  leave (the touch's own). Two gold eyes by the graves: a stray cat comes to stay (the touch's own).
- **Revel.** The binge laughing with an empty seat: the binge ends within two hours, and the binger's recreation is full. The
  horned man with a cup: a drink of his own cup's kind (the colony's kind, as `RevelGoods` picks it) lies where he stood. The
  drink knocked over: one is really lost, the last one too (the sign itself; a small harm). The sweet smoke: those who
  smelled it are cheered for the day (+3).
- **Ducat.** The gold coin at someone's feet: the sign already leaves a real one. The glint of gold: a trader comes (the
  touch's own). The golden beetle on a table: 10 to 25 silver under the table.
- **Pip.** The lights flickering in a pattern: the batteries on the same line take a quarter of what they hold. The light
  glowing with no power: it stays lit until dawn. The voice in the static: a trade ship within reach (an orbital trader where
  the comms work, else a caravan). The machine that ran on its hour: that hour draws no power, runs with or without it, and
  its fuel is given back at the end (hooks on its power while it lasts). The light going out again and again: the fires and
  torches in that room go out and have to be fed and lit again (a small harm).
- **Smoulder.** The rock rumbling in the deep workings: two or three chunks of the place's own rock come down near there,
  on nobody. The miners' dream: those miners dig a quarter faster for a day ("dreamt of the deep"). Steam from the ground:
  the ground round it stays warm for three days (no snow lies within five cells; the plants near it grown on a little).
- **Cirrus.** The wind dying: the calm's wind falls to almost nothing (the turbines stop), and while it lasts fire doesn't
  spread (a hook on the game's fire). Dry thunder, the smell of wet earth: rain comes two to eight hours later (snow where it
  is freezing), with its line. The winged shadow, the vast one: up to six of the wild game leave the land, and a day later as
  many of their kinds come back.
- **Hollin, Bellwether and the beasts.** The grass bowed flat, the giant hoofprint: game comes onto the land (the touch's
  own). Leaves and seeds drifting to one place: flowers come up there. The anima tree humming: up to five anima grass
  around it, and meditating at it +6% focus for a day (in the stat's own breakdown). A goat bleating in an empty room, the
  beast lowering its head to the young, the dream of the last white beast: one of the colony's female herd animals is with
  young (the game's own pregnancy, by a male of its kind where there is one). The animals all looking one way, the dogs
  silent, the thrumbos or dryads still, the birds all gone: everyone at the home handles animals better for a day ("calm
  animals", taming and training +15%). The god's beast fed: the colony's animals are frost-hardy for three days (the
  touch's own "frost-hardy").
- **The eerie signs.** A knock with nobody there, footprints to the door, a tall white figure: the one who saw it sleeps
  badly (the touch's own bad night; a small harm). A sweet voice: the one who heard it is inspired. A dark the light didn't
  reach: that spot stays dark until dawn and its light stays out. A deep croaking: fish by the water (the touch's own).
  Pale sand on a grave: the one closest to that dead person dreams of them kindly the next time they sleep (the dream book,
  their journal and the game's dream of someone lost). Two waking from the same dream: they think better of each other
  (+8 opinion, ten days). Everything going silent: everyone at the home works a fifth faster for the next hour. A work named
  for the god: its beauty x1.2 from then on (in the stat's breakdown; the colony keeps 30 such works at most).
- **Shown** (`GodImpact.Show`, through `GodTouchEffects.Show`): a line of what happened where it happened, with the god's own
  look; the camera moves only for the touch's notable effects it already moved for (the inspirations, a trader, a cat, game,
  fish). What lasts is on the map, or a condition or a memory with a plain label and description saying what it does and
  why. No line names a god; no favour is shown.
- **Running on** (`GodTouchBook.running`, `GodTouchRunning`, saved; at most 24, each ends with its time): the body rotting,
  the food keeping less, the cold room, the long noon, the still air, the humming tree, the free hour, a light held lit or
  dark, the warm ground, the rain on its way, the game coming back, a kind dream waiting for its night. The works admired are
  `GodTouchBook.admired` (references, 30 at most).
- **Dev mode**: Debug actions, Rimfolk, "Gods: an occurrence's own effect here now...": pick a key; it plays at the mouse
  with everyone near as having seen it (select the one it is about, or the body or the work, first). "Gods: the gods'
  touch (log)" lists what is running.
- **Tests**: `GodTouchTests` (every key in the Keyed files, one effect each, the 21 left with none, no key both an old
  own-effect key and in the table, all 98 accounted for, the harms only the proposals' own, the pure rules and sizes, the
  words and defs plain and naming no god, saved and capped).

### The log window at the start (the player's report and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.265.1)

The player, with their startup log: "got this log window pop up on the latest start"; then "alright" and "please fix the
bugs". The game opens its log window by itself whenever something logs an error while it loads. Of the red lines, three
touched Rimfolk; the others are other mods' own and stay (Lunar Framework's inlining fixer under Harmony 3.0 rc.6,
RealRuins' news file read by HugsLib, Map Mode Framework's ReGrowth layer; HANDOFF lists each).

- **The lands' wild animals, mended at load.** Two mods adding the same animal to the same land (ReGrowth's RG_Dodo,
  RG_Thrinaxodon and RG_Synthetion in TemperateForest, TemperateSwamp, TropicalRainforest, TropicalSwamp and
  AridShrubland) make the game's dictionary of that land's animals throw at the repeat and stay half filled, so the game's
  own wild spawns there and Giddy-Up's mounts missed every animal after it; 0.141.0 only read around it for Rimfolk.
  `Animals/BiomeAnimalsMend.cs`, queued from `ColonyCouncilMod`'s constructor (`LongEventHandler.ExecuteWhenFinished`,
  which runs once every def has loaded and before every mod's startup class), and run again harmlessly before
  `BiomeAnimals` first reads a land: in each land, the own list and the races naming it (`BiomeAnimalsMath.MendPlain`)
  and the pollution and coastal lists with their expansion (`KeepOnce`) keep each animal once at the mean of its
  listings. Where the land's list and the animal's race both name it, the land's record goes and the race's stays (the
  game's loop reads it for every kind of that race); it takes the mean only when the race has that one kind. Records
  whose animal's def is missing are dropped; a mended land's three cached dictionaries are cleared. One message line
  says what was merged. No Harmony; a pawn kind without a race still can't be mended, and `BiomeAnimals` reads around it.
- **A RimWorld of Magic in HugsLib's place.** A prefix on HugsLib's `ModBase.ApplyHarmonyPatches`, for that mod only,
  does what HugsLib 12 does there (`HarmonyAutoPatch`, `ShouldHarmonyAutoPatch`, `HarmonyInst` under the mod's
  `PackageIdPlayerFacing`) and applies its classes one at a time (`HarmonyRescue`), leaving out the two this Harmony
  refuses, so no error is logged. It steps aside when nothing of the mod is refused or a member isn't found, and the
  postfix rescue (0.140.0) still follows for when HugsLib ran first.
- **A Wanderer's caravan travel.** RoM's `CostToMove_Caravan_Patch` names the start tile a `PlanetLayer`; Harmony 3
  refuses it. `Patch_MagicWandererTravel`, a postfix on `Caravan_PathFollower.CostToMove(Caravan, PlanetTile,
  PlanetTile, int?)`, calls RoM's own postfix with no start layer (its body never reads it) while its own patch isn't
  on: a caravan with a `TM_Wanderer` crosses land without its movement difficulty, as RoM means.

### Ballrooms only for music rooms (the player's report and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.265.2)

The player: "as soon as I have this drum in the room, it's counted as a ballroom, which, you know, is not appropriate at
all. It's not even counted as kind of an ideology room ... it's definitely not a dining room ... I just want to have the
drum somewhere, but not immediately have that become a ballroom"; "ballroom seems to override temple, which is not
correct in my opinion"; then "if there's other things on the to-do list that make sense to also do at the same time, go
ahead".

- **The cause.** Vanilla Factions Expanded - Empire's `RoomRoleWorker_Ballroom` scores 10000 for any musical instrument
  (Ideology's drum among them), unless the room holds a bed, throne, work table or entity holder; the game's dining room
  scores 12 a table, the temple (Ideology's worship room) at least 2000 with an altar of the colony's faith. Only the
  highest shows. The game's eating and recreation moods read the room's impressiveness, not its name.
- **The rule** (`Integrations/BallroomMath.StandsDown`): the ballroom stands down where the game's worship room scores
  (an altar of the colony's faith), where there is a dining table (a building with an eating surface, as the game's
  dining room counts), or where every instrument is a drum (`BallroomByUse.IsDrum`: Ideology's `Drum`, or another mod's
  instrument named a drum). A room with a harp, harpsichord or piano and recreation stays the mod's ballroom, for its
  titles and balls.
- **The hooks** (`Integrations/BallroomByUse.cs`): postfixes on the worker's `GetScore` and
  `GetScoreDeltaIfBuildingPlaced` (the note while placing an instrument), found by name; they stand down quietly without
  the mod. The setting "Ballrooms only for music rooms" (`ballroomByUse`, on), on the "Your other mods" page under the
  deeper hooks.
- Left on the to-do list then, built since (19 November 2026): Rimfolk reading a room by what is in it rather than the
  one name the game shows ("Rooms judged by what is in them").

### Everything from a god told at once (the player's report and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.265.3)

The player, with their save `League_of_Toba_6`: "the camera just centered on a pawn and 8 green tea was there. nearby
pawns had some mood impact "my god was good to us", but it doesn't specify which god and what it did. also there was no
animation for this event, and also no alert for it." Then: "the evening column in use, I don't really look at anymore
... So please, any information from a god should kind of with its own dedicated pop up on the right, or it should be
visible on screen, after camera changes ... the visual aspect was there, but minor. I mean, then it, I guess, counts.
... if they don't know who it was, then, they should guess or say they don't know."

- **A message as it happens.** `Tell.FromGod`: a god's words are a message at once, at least notable, never held for the
  evening's colony news nor left only in the History tab. It carries every god's own happening (`OwnHappenings.Line`), a
  god's sign when no moment plays (`Worship.Sign`), a god keeping the rain away, an offering taken or left, and a god's
  demand ignored. The colony's own faith life (vows, saints, festivals, the peoples' gods) stays smaller news. With the
  colony news off, a camera's words come with it too (`Tell.Minor`'s Off branch checks `ByCamera`).
- **The camera first.** Revel's stash and Revel's vision handed their words over before the camera moved; now the
  camera moves first, as everywhere else. The small look they have (Revel's amber flecks) stays, as the player said.
- **The mood says what and whose.** A god's touch carries the words of the occurrence (the act's or the moment's
  text) to the moods it gives (`GodTouch.Pending.words`, `WhyFelt`): "Why: Lorena found green tea x8 hidden far out on
  the land ... Bautista holds it was Undertow's doing.", the god the colony took it for by the name the pawn knows it
  by, or "... doesn't know which god it was." when they took it for none or have no name for it. Never the true god
  unless that is their name for the god they took it for. "my god was good to us" now says "I believe it was the god I
  hold to".
- **Text.** The book's lines end with one full stop (`GodLoreMath.WithoutStop`; 49 of 111 lines in the player's save
  had two); the stash's book line has the find in lower case and its words fit one person ("at her feet").

#### The gods' words told as they happen (released 0.270.2)

Found in the plain-words pass on the gods and faith (19 November 2026). Many of the gods' cards and messages named an
hour, or told a thing the map doesn't show, and a few said more than the colony can know:
- **The hour.** The gods' kindnesses and angers in the world (`GodHealth.Kindness`, `Anger`) come on the region's day
  (`RegionBook.Daily`), at whatever hour that is on the map, so the wild growth, the vein, the mended machine, the full
  battery, the barrels finished early and the drink gone sour are no longer told as "overnight" or "this morning"; the
  same for a sour store and a crop grown on after a god's touch (`GodTouch`). The dream of a god's gift is told when
  the region's day comes (`GodWorldGifts`), not "at breakfast", and a gift taken back goes when the colony answers, not
  "in the night". The voice in the dark (`GodVoid`) speaks at any hour and pays the moment the colony answers, so its
  offer no longer says "tonight" or "by morning", the paid card is "{PAWN} said yes", and what it takes days later is
  told as seen then ("woke with" went). The moon's return of a kindness comes at three at night (`GodReturn`): the
  wounded colonist is still asleep, with the wounds already days better. A prayer is answered at any hour (the night
  only makes it likelier, `Prayers.Answer`), and the rain some six to fourteen hours after, or within the hour with
  thunder when the god shows itself (`RainComing`), not "in the night" and "the evening after". The stranger at the gate
  comes at any hour (`GodStranger.Fire`): no "as the light goes", no "heavy all afternoon". The gods' camps leave
  whenever their stay ends: the pilgrims' and the seer's farewells no longer say dawn (`CampLook.FarewellText`). One of
  the seer's sayings promised "tonight", and the moon's return comes on a night of its own choosing; it doesn't now.
- **What the map shows.** The beast the voice takes vanishes in a puff of smoke (`GodVoid.TakeDue`), it doesn't "walk
  into the dark"; the food it gives lies in the middle of the colony (`Feed`). The god's beast that "would not be kept"
  leaves because someone marked it to be tamed or took it (`SacredAnimal`), and its message says so. A presence's lines
  say what each does with its numbers' words: Pip's batteries lose less charge (`BatteryKept`, the drain cut), not "keep
  what they give out"; a god's clear days are dry for a while (`DisableRainFor`), not "long"; "Nobody can say why" went
  from the presences' descriptions. The temple vowed before the council has two seasons (30 days, as its impact line
  says), not "a month".
- **The unseen gods.** A card's named title said a god was "displeased", a god's mind: it is "A burn from {GOD}". The
  stranger's and the god's beast's deeds on a colonist's record called it "a stranger who was more" and "a god's beast";
  they say "a strange visitor at the gate" and "a strange beast", as the colony saw it.

Every line's tags, placeholders and keys kept; no code or def setting changed. Pronoun placeholders that opened a
sentence (shown in lower case) were rewritten with the name in the saint's, the temple's and the god's-ask questions,
the gods' camps, the stranger at the gate, the dream card, and the moon's and the dark's cards.

### The pact's cart and the schemes' thefts (the player's report and go, 17 November 2026; released 0.266.1)

The player, with their save `League_of_Toba_5`: "i somehow need to give 8 components regularly to my allies the
stormriders. why components exactly? did i select this at some point? since this is a very valuable good and I'd rather
give something else instead. can you update this?"; then, on the lead's fix: "it just shouldn't auto take valuable
materials, you know. If I have to confirm first, then that makes sense, but it shouldn't just take them automatically.
Instead, you know, wood and cloth and leather are more, I guess, okay. But then ideally, I still can confirm whether I want
to give it or whether I actually refuse and end the pact. Other than that, yeah, the letter should show what the card is
worth, change the card option, and please also change the existing pact. Now, the scheme of a Stormrider stealing, it
sounds very cool. I like it, but maybe they shouldn't steal components again and other valuable things."

- **The cause.** A trade pact's cart was fixed when the pact was made by `Pacts.CartGoods`: the stores ranked by total
  worth, so components (32 silver each, 68 in stores) came first, 8 a season. The letter's Ask list was pre-filled with
  the first and showed no worth or pay; renewals and hand-overs took the first with no choice; and each season the cart
  went out by itself. The thief of a scheme took a carving, silver, gold, jade or components by design.
- **Valuable and plain goods, one rule** (`Things/GoodsMath.cs`, read from the live game by `Things/Goods.cs`): of a
  person, never (unfit); money (silver), medicine of every kind, a drug of any kind (beer too), something special (a
  comp that is used, bonded or hatches, or a trade tag the game marks exotic or only a mod uses) or of the spacer age or
  later, valuable; food eaten for itself (raw food, meals, kibble, hay; not a condiment or plant matter grown for brewing
  or dye), plain whatever it is worth; a material worth 4 silver a unit or more (about twice steel: gold, plasteel,
  uranium, jade, devilstrand, synthread, a thrumbo's fur), valuable; then logs (wood), cloth and wool, leather, stone
  blocks and building stone, and a raw metal (steel, bronze) are plain; anything else (components, chemfuel, neutroamine,
  shells, wort, a mod's parts, fuels, boosters and potions) is a crafting input and valuable. By categories and def
  properties, never a mod's name; checked on the player's catalogue's active rows (`PactCartTests`). **Steel is plain**: it
  is the bulk metal the colony mines and the game's traders deal in by the hundred; the colony keeps the biggest reserve
  of it, and it comes last for a tribal or medieval partner. The offerings to the gods keep their own "precious" rule
  (`OfferingGiftMath.Precious`, which also asks whether the colony can make the thing again).
- **The carts offered** (`PactMath.CartPicks`, `Pacts.CartChoices`): the plain goods the colony can spare, the kinds the
  partner's age uses first (`GoodsMath.CartOrder`: tribal wood, leather, food, cloth, blocks, metal; medieval wood, cloth,
  leather, food, blocks, metal; industrial and spacer metal, cloth, food, wood, leather, blocks), then the most to
  spare; each counted above what the colony keeps (`GoodsMath.Reserve`: of each food five days for everyone; wood 150 and
  20 a colonist; cloth or leather 50 and 15 a colonist; blocks 100 and 30; metal 200 and 30), half of what is above it at
  most, about 250 silver's worth, a third of the stores at most; a cart under 60 silver's worth isn't offered. Then the
  valuable goods (the most in stores first, a third of the stores at most), marked "(valuable)" with a note, taken only
  when picked on purpose (`FavourCalls.Option.onPurpose`: the letter's list never starts on one; with nothing plain, it
  waits on "Choose one from the list"). At most six plain and four valuable. Each says what it is, what it is worth and
  what they pay: "102 plainleather a season, about 215 silver's worth; they pay 171" (`PactWords.CartLine`). The same
  list for a supply contract's load (`DealingLetters`), and face to face ("Speak of a pact", `DiplomacyActs`). A pact
  nobody chooses a cart for (their offer accepted, a hand-over's pact) takes the first plain one, never a valuable one;
  a renewal keeps its cart.
- **Each season the colony is asked** (`Pacts.AskCart`, `ChoiceLetter_PactCart`, letter def `Rimfolk_PactCart`): the
  season's letter names the cart, its worth and the pay, with "Send it" (carried out to the gate for their porters as
  before, their silver set down: `Pacts.SendCart`; closed while the stores hold less), "Choose other goods" (added after
  the release, the player: "can i just not always select what items to give whenever such a cart is required": a menu
  of `Pacts.CartChoices` with worth and pay, valuables marked, the pick sent this season only and written in the
  answers' log, the pact's own cart unchanged: `ChoiceLetter_PactCart.OtherCart`), "Not this season" (`Pacts.SkipCart`:
  no cart, the pact goes on, said in a message) and "End the pact" (`Pacts.RefuseCart`: ended without
  blame through the pact's own end, then a letter with their answer to an end, `CC_Pact_Ans_Ended`, and their head's
  own words for an end sent back with the porters, the "pactend" lines without a letter's or a call's tag, picked by
  `NeighbourLetters.TheirWords`). Unanswered when the letter goes (two days, `PactMath.CartAnswerDays`), no cart this
  season and the pact goes on; with too few of the usual goods in store the letter still comes, to choose other goods
  (`CC_Pact_CartAsk_Short`), and only with nothing at all to spare is nothing asked. In the inbox's
  "Needs you" while it waits; recorded in the answers' log as "pactCart".
- **"Change the cart"** on a trade pact's card (`PactsPanels`): a letter to their head with the topic "pactcart:ID", the
  new cart chosen in the Ask list from the same carts less the one it has; their answer agrees (`CC_Pact_Ans_Cart`, their
  own words under "pactcart", cordial or cool; overtaken by events, "pactcartmoot") and the cart changes when they read it
  (`Pacts.SetCart`).
- **Existing pacts** (`Pacts.PlainCarts`, once after loading and then each day): a live trade pact whose cart is a
  valuable good nobody picked gets the first plain cart, with one message saying what changed and why. A valuable cart
  picked on purpose is kept: the pacts that have one are saved in `DiplomacyBook.chosenCarts` (one id a live pact, dropped
  when the pact ends; an old save loads with none). In the player's save the Stormriders' tie 114 (8 components a season)
  becomes 102 plainleather a season, about 215 silver's worth, for 171 silver (their ten colonists and stores of day 124).
- **"8 components"** (`Couriers.Counted`): the label went through the game's language worker, which gave "component"
  back unchanged in the player's 1.7 game (the save's cart letters, written after the update to 0.265.0, say "8
  component"); the decompiled 1.6 English worker should pluralize, so the cause inside the game wasn't pinned down. In
  English Rimfolk now uses its own rule (`CourierMath.English`), the game's worker only in other languages.
- **The thefts** (`Diplomacy/Schemes.cs`, `SchemeMath.TheftOrder`): a thief takes plain goods only, never a valuable good
  (no components, medicine, silver, gold or jade) and no carving: what the colony's age keeps most of first (a tribe's
  food, leather and cloth; a medieval colony's cloth, leather, food and metal; an industrial or spacer colony's metal,
  cloth, food and leather), never logs or blocks, 3 kg a piece at most, about 60 to 180 silver's worth and no more than a
  pack of 35 kg holds (`LootCount`). The form is "Stores" ("stealing 40 cloth from the colony's stores"); the old forms
  (Totem, Purse, Tool) still read in a save. The rest of the scheme is as it was.
- **Not checked without the game:** the season's letter and its two answers on the map, the carry-out and the silver,
  the end's letter with their words, the Ask list's marks and default in the letter window, "Change the cart" and its
  answer, the message for the player's pact after loading, a thief carrying off cloth or steel, "8 components" in the
  player's 1.7 game.

### The brewery at home in the kitchen (the player's request and go, 18 November 2026; released 0.266.3)

The player: "so the brewery gets a debuff once it's not in the workshop, however, i think the brewery should also be able
to be placed in the kitchen, no? what makes more sense?"; then "please, go ahead".

- **The cause.** The game (1.6.4518 on) names one room for each production bench and slows it to 80% anywhere else
  (`StatPart_WorkTableRoomRole`, `workTableRoomRole`, `workTableNotInRoomRoleFactor`): the brewery's is the workshop,
  the stoves' the kitchen. A kitchen scores 28 a stove, a workshop 27 a bench (the brewery among them), the workshop
  first on a tie (RimWorld Wiki, "Room roles"), so a second brewery beside one stove turns the kitchen into a workshop and
  slows the stove.
- **A cooking bench** (`BreweryKitchenMath.CookingBench`): a workshop bench whose recipes are all Cooking work (the
  brewery's wort, and any mod's brewing bench read from its own def). Brewing is done by the cooks, by their skill.
- **At full speed in a kitchen.** Postfixes on the stat part's static `Applies(Thing)` (its speed and its line in the
  breakdown) and `WouldApplyToBuildingIfPlaced` (the note while placing): no penalty for a cooking bench in a room the
  game calls a kitchen.
- **The kitchen stays a kitchen.** A postfix on `RoomRoleWorker_Workshop.GetScore`: where the room holds a stove (the
  game's kitchen score above nothing), the cooking benches' share of the workshop score comes off
  (`BreweryKitchenMath.WorkshopScore`), so breweries beside a stove count toward the kitchen; and on
  `GetScoreDeltaIfBuildingPlaced`, so placing one there isn't shown as making a workshop. Breweries with no stove keep
  the game's workshop.
- The setting "Breweries work in the kitchen too" (`breweryInKitchen`, on), under the deeper hooks.

### Clothes made for someone, put on when they are back (the player's report and go, 18 November 2026; released 0.266.4)

The player: "the target pawn immediately gets a job into the queue to wear this item. But I think due to our change that
each pawn, after they do work, take the item to their inventory, this is now no longer happening ... And even better
would be that the pawn who's supposed to wear it doesn't immediately go ... they just wear it once they are kind of
close by again or back into the base"; then they sent Nice Inventory Tab's DLL.

- **The cause** (the mod's DLL, decompiled outside the game, never loaded): Nice Inventory Tab keeps which bill is for
  whom (`BillFinished_Patch.wearRequests`) and finishes such a bill itself (`ExecuteFinishRecipeLogic`): it makes the
  product, calls `RecordsUtility.Notify_BillDone`, places the piece by the crafter and orders the one it is for to wear
  it (`TryTakeOrderedJob`, queued, forced) with its message. Rimfolk's carrying (`Patch_HaulBillProducts`) pocketed the
  product inside `Notify_BillDone`, so the mod had nothing to place.
- **The fix** (`Integrations/MadeForWear.cs`): a prefix and finalizer on the mod's `ExecuteFinishRecipeLogic` note whom
  it is for; meanwhile the crafter keeps nothing, so the mod places and orders as before.
- **Put on when back** (the setting "Clothes made for someone, put on when they are back", Your other mods, on): the
  mod's order to wear (`Pawn_JobTracker.TryTakeOrderedJob`, the Wear job for that pawn, during the mod's finishing) is
  held when they aren't near (`MadeForWearMath.GoNow`: free, in the home area, the piece in the home area too or within
  40 cells); Rimfolk says the piece is ready (the mod's own message after it left out); `MadeForWearBook` (saved) keeps
  it, and when they next choose a job with nothing under way (`DetermineNextJob`) and are near, they put it on first,
  forced as the mod's order was; what they wear in its place comes off, as with the mod's own order. Let go of once
  worn, gone, after 15 days, when they can't wear it (`EquipmentUtility.CanEquip`) or when it would take off something
  locked on them (`WouldReplaceLockedApparel`). Someone nearby goes at once, as before.
- **Kept for them** (the player, 20 November 2026: "when the pawn that creates the item would also wear it, they
  immediately wear it ... instead of reserving it for the other pawn"): while a piece waits for someone, the game's own
  look for better clothes (`JobGiver_OptimizeApparel.ApparelScoreGain`, `Patch_MadeForWearKept`) scores it as worth
  nothing to anyone else, the crafter too (`MadeForWearMath.KeptFrom`: the one it is for alive, the wait not run out).
  An order the player gives still goes. Until 20 November a waiting piece was also let go of as soon as they wore
  something in its place, the usual case, so they never put it on.

### Choose the material when ordering a piece from the gear tab (the player's go, 19 November 2026; released 0.268.1)

The player: "when you know giving a order through the inventory to create like a piece of clothing or armor or
whatever, it would really be cool to also be able to select from which material that piece of clothing should be made
... when I select the open item slot, select the item that I want to create, and then I have to select where it's
created from, and then maybe I could also immediately select which material it uses. So it would just list or show
materials that I have enough of for the job, and then create the job, but only select this one material as a allowed
material and by default deselect everything else, so that I'm sure it doesn't use anything else." Their go on the
lead's proposal: "yes, please", "all the three".

- **The mod's own flow** (Nice Inventory Tab's DLL, decompiled outside the game, never loaded): an empty slot's menu,
  "Make", a piece, then a bench (or the piece's own line for its first bench), calls
  `NiceInventoryTab.CommandUtility.CommandCreate(Building_WorkTable, ThingDef, RecipeDef, ApparelLayerDef)`: it makes
  the bill, registers it as made for the colonist whose tab it is (`BillFinished_Patch.Register`, with
  `ITab_Pawn_Gear_Patch.lastPawn`), names it, adds it to the bench, says so and moves the camera there.
- **The material step** (`Integrations/MaterialChoice.cs`, `Patch_MaterialChoiceOrder`, a prefix on that call by
  name): for a piece made from a material (the product is made from stuff and the recipe takes its stuff from an
  ingredient), one more menu opens, titled "Material for the (piece)": "Any material" first, then each material the
  recipe takes (from its material ingredient, never a fixed one like components; allowed for the piece and by the
  recipe) that the colony has enough of for one piece, with how much one piece takes and how much is on hand ("Cloth: 60
  for one, 412 on hand", since 20 November 2026) and the material's own icon. On hand
  is what lies on the map, seen and not forbidden; one piece's need is the game's own count for that material
  (`IngredientCount.CountRequiredOfFor`, so gold and silver count in their own units). The order
  (`MaterialChoiceMath.Offered`, pure, in the tests): the material that makes the most pieces first, then by name. With
  none enough, a greyed line says so under "Any material". Each line's tooltip says what one piece takes. Clicking
  outside the menu orders nothing.
- **The bill.** Either choice calls the mod's own `CommandCreate` as it would have been called (the prefix lets
  Rimfolk's own call through), so the bill, the wear request, the name and the message are the mod's; it is made for
  the colonist the menu was opened for. For a material, the new bill's ingredient filter then allows only that one:
  every other material its material ingredient takes is unticked, the chosen one ticked, the rest of the filter (hit
  points, quality, other ingredients) left as it was. "Any material" leaves the mod's bill as it is.
- **Standing down.** A piece not made from a material goes straight on, as before. Without the mod the hook stands
  down; with the mod but its order not found, one warning in the log and the mod's own way; a failure while opening
  the menu, logged once, leaves the mod's own way for the session.
- The setting "Choose the material when ordering a piece" (`materialChoice`, on, under the deeper hooks), on the "Your
  other mods" page under Nice Inventory Tab.

### Rooms judged by what is in them (the player's go, 19 November 2026; released 0.266.6)

The player (17 November 2026): "I want the gatherings where food is involved, of course, happening in my dining room,
even if maybe another room is kind of the one for the ideological items"; then, on the overview of the open list (19
November 2026): "Rooms judged by what's in them. That sounds good."

- **The cause.** The game shows one role per room, the highest score: a dining table 12, a recreation building 7, an
  altar of the colony's faith at least 2000 (Ideology's temple), a stove 28, a work bench 27 (and Vanilla Factions
  Expanded - Empire's ballroom 10000 for an instrument, now standing down in a temple or a dining room: "Ballrooms only
  for music rooms"). Rimfolk read only that one role: council meetings, play-outs and feasts, visitors and the advisor
  looked for the room named dining room, then rec room. The player's dining room with an altar, lectern, ritual spot and
  drum shows as a temple, so its meetings and meals went elsewhere, or out into the open air; a rec room shown as
  something else brought the advisor's idea of building one.
- **The reading** (`RoomUseMath`, pure, in the tests; `RoomUtil.ServesAsDining`, `ServesAsRec`): a room serves as a
  dining room when it holds a dining table of the colony's (a building with an eating surface, as the game's dining room
  counts them), and as a rec room when it holds a recreation building of the colony's (one with a kind of recreation,
  `building.joyKind`, as the game's rec room counts them), whatever role the game shows: a temple, a ballroom, a throne
  room, a kitchen with a table. Built ones only, in a proper room (not the open air or a whole cave). Never a private
  room (`RoomUseMath.PrivateRoles`): a prison cell, or a room the game calls a bedroom, barracks, hospital, prison cell or
  prison barracks, Biotech's nursery or deathrest chamber, Anomaly's containment cell, Hospitality's guest room, Dubs Bad
  Hygiene's bathrooms and sauna, or the coma room of the framework some mods use. The reading is kept for a second of
  game time.
- **The order** (`RoomUtil.DiningRooms`, `RecRooms`, `RoomUseMath.Order`): the rooms the game calls a dining room (or
  rec room) first, then those that serve as one, the largest first within each; so every place keeps its own order of
  preference with the named room first. Also `IsDiningRoom`, `IsRecRoom`, `IsCommonRoom`, `AnyDiningRoom`,
  `AnyRecRoom`, `DiningRank` (a table's room: 0 named, 1 serving) and `RoomsFor` (a role named by an ambition or a room
  plan: the dining and rec rooms by use, any other by the game's role).
- **Where it is read so**: council meetings (`CouncilMeeting.FindVenue`: around the dining table, then the rec room,
  then a gathering spot, then the open air) and their announced venue (`Ambitions.MeetingVenue`); play-outs and feasts
  (`PlaySpots.TryFind`, Dining and Rec); visitors kept in from the cold (`Visitors.IndoorsCell`) and a guest's corner for
  the night (`VisitorServices.Corner`); a wedding needs a marriage spot or a room to eat in (`HappeningWorker_Wedding`);
  the advisor's idea of a rec room (only with no room that serves as one) and of dressing up the dining room, the rec
  room plan on the recreation advice (only with no rec room), the dining room's seats and cramped space, the rec rooms'
  games, the seats for those who ate without a table, and rooms with no light; the art wish (art where people eat and
  relax) and the roofed way's table; ambitions' rooms (`Goal_Room`, `Goal_RoomStat`) and a planned room's neighbours
  (`TemplatePlanner.RoleCenters`: a kitchen planned near the dining room, a latrine kept from it); the base review (a
  room of a kind it doesn't tell apart is read as a dining or rec room by what is in it, and its little map colours it
  so; a kitchen or rec room with tables also counts as a dining room for the walks to meals); a work of art's card (the
  game's moods for eating and relaxing read the room where it happens, so a temple with tables is "everyone who eats
  here feels its impressiveness"); a corner for each faith; the rec room a Hospitality guest may want of a home before joining;
  quarrels at a table; in from the rain to the table; a group's evenings in the rec room; crowded rooms.
- **The words match the map.** A rec room the game calls something else is named as the game shows it: "in the
  temple" (`CC_Venue_InRoom`, `PlaySpots.RecVenue`), "a corner of the temple" (`CC_FaithClash_CornerIn`). Around a
  dining table it is "around the dining table" in any room.
- **Kept on the game's one role, and why**: the game's own roles and moods (Rimfolk changes no role here; the game's
  eating and recreation moods already read the room's impressiveness wherever it happens); words that name a room as the
  game shows it (a guest lodged "in the temple", the crowded room's name, a god's doing, the room under the mouse on the
  base review's map, the name offered for a room of your own); where someone with no bed may lie down
  (`Autonomy.OkRole`: a kitchen or temple with a table stays out, by what the room is for); the rooms of every other
  role (bedrooms, barracks, hospitals, prison cells, kitchens, workshops, laboratories, barns) and the visitors' private
  rooms (`KeepOut`, `GuestHelpMath.PrivateRoom`); the journal's moods, which are the game's own thoughts.
- Tests: `RoomUseTests` (the reading, the order, the player's rooms, and every place above reading the rooms through
  `RoomUtil`; only the kept places compare the game's dining or rec role directly).

### A god's mark worth having (the player's go, 19 November 2026; released 0.268.3)

The player: "so the god events and occurences are super cool! but many of them just generate a single stone [chunk]??
it's a very anticlimatic item and doesn't thematically fit for most of them, let alone it being a really not interesting
or valuable item". The go, on the lead's proposal: "yes, please", "all the three".

- **The cause.** A god's moment (a blessing, a coming, a reveal, a departure; `GodPresenceMath.MarkFor`) leaves its
  look's mark (`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_GodLooks.xml` `<mark>`), and 10 of the 17 looks left one stone chunk of the land's
  rock (the Storm, the Hunt, War, the Way, the Hearth) or one steel slag chunk (War among spacers, the Craft and the
  fabricator, the Machine and the iron spirit). Nothing said what was left.
- **Each look its own mark** (`GodMark`, new values; the enum is never saved, and `Stone` and `Slag` are gone):
  - the Storm: `Lightning`, a flash in the sky, a glow and thunder at the place (the game's lightning flash and glow,
    no strike: no fire, nobody hurt) and a ring of scorched ground; no goods;
  - the Hunt: `Kill`, a fresh kill of the land's game: an animal of the land (`BiomeAnimals.Of`, the commoner
    likelier), flesh, not a person, an insect, a Pokémon or an animal the colony's faith holds sacred, from a fox's size
    to a deer's (0.5 to 1.5; 0.3 to 2 on a land with none such), grown, its meat and leather at their prices, as much
    of them as a butcher of middling skill gets (three quarters, `GodMarkMath.KillWorth`), worth no more than 360
    silver (a deer is about that), else the least worth of the few tried; laid on open ground near the place, killed
    there (the game's own death, the corpse fresh and not forbidden), a little of its blood beside it outside the home
    area;
  - War, and War among spacers: `Weapon`, a ring of scorched ground and a weapon in the middle of it: any weapon of the
    player's game carried in the hands (every mod's; no grenade, nothing that can't be dropped or traded, no persona
    weapon, nothing past the spacer age), of the colony's own age first (`PeopleAgesMath.AgeOfTech`), an earlier age's
    only when none of its own fits, the commoner likelier, of a material the age has (`GenStuff`, by the age's tech
    level), worth 100 silver up to the age's worth and a half (180 tribal, 240 medieval, 300 after), else the nearest to
    the age's worth; of poor or normal make, never poor where that takes it under 100; with no open ground for the ring
    (under a roof), the weapon alone;
  - the Way: `StandingStone`, a standing stone of the land's own rock: Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Art's obelisk, else
    the game's small sculpture, of the blocks the land's first rock is dressed into (granite blocks where none is), of
    normal quality, a work of art nobody of the colony made (the game's way with an outsider's work: no story of the
    colony's on it, its author unknown); set up on free open ground near the place as the colony's, packed up beside it
    where none is free;
  - the Hearth: `Hearth`, a bundle of firewood (25 wood) and three to eight warm meals of the colony's age: simple ones
    tribal, fine ones medieval and industrial, lavish ones spacer, Vanilla Cooking Expanded's stews, soups, grills and
    bakes or the game's own;
  - the Craft and the fabricator: `Metal`, a stack of the colony's working metal: steel, plasteel in a spacer colony;
  - the Machine and the iron spirit: `Components`, a few components, in a spacer colony an advanced one and two more.
  The other looks keep theirs (flowers, a tree, a spring, frost, ash, scorch; Revel's and Tamiu's none).
- **What it is worth** (`GodMarkMath`, by the colony's age, `Ages.Ours`: 120 silver tribal, 160 medieval, 210
  industrial, 260 spacer, never under 100 or over 300): 65, 85 or 110 steel, 30 plasteel; 4, 5 or 7 components, an
  advanced one and 2 in the spacer age; the firewood and 6 to 8 meals (6 lavish ones in the spacer age); the weapon
  within its worth; the kill by its size; the standing stone at normal quality (the obelisk only while it is within 300
  silver, else the small sculpture).
- **How often.** The moments that leave a look's mark are a god coming onto the land (a stranger at the gate or a
  sacred animal: one in 40 days at the most, about one a year), a great effect of the gods' touch (one in 40 days at a
  home at the most), an answered prayer of the sick, of a raid or of a drought (a god once in ten days at the most), a
  god's kindness in the world (a fever eased, a kindness returned, a gift) and the rare risings and wakings: in a colony
  that prays, five to ten a year. Only the looks above leave goods: of the colony's fifteen gods Smoulder (metal), Pip
  (components), Ennu and Ducat (the standing stone); the Hunt, War and the Hearth are the looks of the peoples' gods and
  of a god born to the colony in those domains. So one to four marks of goods a year, 150 to 800 silver. And a mark of
  goods comes at most once in ten days, any god, any home (`GodMarkMath.WorthGapDays`, kept with the game in
  `GodPresenceComponent.lastWorth`): six a year at the most, 1,800 silver at the very most; within the wait a moment
  leaves the mark's plain form (`GodMarkMath.Lesser`: war, the hearth, the forge and the machine a ring of scorched
  ground, the hunt and the way nothing).
- **Chosen first, laid at the sting.** `GodPresence.Manifest` asks `GodMarkGoods.Plan` as the moment begins: the
  goods are made (the animal not yet on the map), the ground is checked (`GodTrails.CanMark`: flowers and a tree only
  on fertile open soil, a spring on natural ground off the home area, scorch, ash, frost and lightning under the sky),
  and the words written; `GodTrails.Mark` lays it all at the sting, a glint in the god's colour on each thing. A mark the
  ground can't take, or goods that can't be had (no game on the land), leaves the plain form or nothing, and says so.
- **The words match the map** (`CC_GodP_Left_*`, one sentence each, the god never named): "When it was over, a stack of
  65 steel lay where it happened.", "...a freshly killed deer lay on the ground where it happened.", "...the ground
  where it happened was scorched in a ring, and a steel longsword lay in the middle of it.", "...an obelisk of the
  land's own granite stood where it happened.", "...a bundle of firewood and 7 fine stews, still warm, lay where it
  happened.", "Lightning struck the ground where it happened and left a ring of scorched earth.", and the ground's marks
  too ("...a ring of flowers had come up where it happened."). The sentence follows the card's words (`GodCard.Send`'s
  `left`), the line in the colony's book (`Gods.Moment`, through `PresenceSpec.left`, which the wiring fills in from
  `GodPresence.LastLeft`) and the "Why" of the moods of those who saw it (`GodTouch.NoteMoment`), joined by
  `GodMarkMath.WithLeft`.
- **Dev mode**: "Gods: a god's mark here..." lays any mark at a cell in the colony's age or any other, the wait set aside,
  and says its words and worth (also in the log); "Gods: a moment of a look here..." leaves a mark's goods whenever it is
  tried; "Gods: what each look finds in this game (log)" names each look's marks.
- Code: `Gods/Presence/GodMarkMath.cs` (new, pure, linked in the tests), `GodMarkGoods.cs` (new: `GodMarkPlan`,
  `GodMarkGoods`), `GodTrails.cs` (`Mark` by plan, `CanMark`, the lightning), `GodPresence.cs` (the plan, `LastLeft`,
  `GodPresenceComponent.lastWorth`), `GodCard.cs`, `GodPresenceDebug.cs`, `GodPresenceMath.cs` (`GodMark`, `MarkRadius`);
  `Gods/GodPresenceSeam.cs` (`PresenceSpec.left`), `GodsWiring.cs`, `Gods.cs`, `Touch/GodTouch.cs`; the looks' marks;
  `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_GodPresence.xml`. Tests: `GodMarkTests` (new).

### The gods' integrations, part 1: festivals, sacred beasts and art (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.278.1)

The player, on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "your content proposal overall sounds really good. You can go ahead with
this in the order you think makes most sense. In general, I just want additional God events, more immersion, more just
further also building up on the gods in general, how they're integrated, the effects they have, the relations between
pawns, the kind of events that generated from it", and "first do all the integrations that you proposed in your document
before we add additional content variety". Built: C1, C2, C3, C4, C16 and C17 of part C, as proposed there. The unseen
rule holds throughout: nothing says whose a beast really is, what a god wants or how it stands; a god is named only by
the colony's name where the colony knows it was that god, and in a believer's words by their own name for the god they
take it for, which may be wrong.

**C1, each god's festival kept as its words say** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnFeasts.cs`, `OwnFeastsMath.cs`). The eight festivals
that kept only the shared feast now play out on the map as their words (`festivalDishes`) say. Kept, a festival's custom
waits for its hour (`OwnFeastsMath.StartHour`); answered late in the day, it begins as soon as it may until its latest
hour (`LatestHour`), else the next day at its hour, then it is let be. Those who hold the god take part first (the god
they pray to, or one they hold plainly; `OwnFeasts.Holds`), then anyone free.
- Hollin's Greening: the colony's people count the trees they fell (`OwnHappenings.Felled`); on the day up to four
  planters set a sapling by hand (`Rimfolk_Feast_Plant`) for each tree felled since the last Greening, 20 at most, on
  open soil round the cleared ground (else round the oldest tree), each of a tree that grows wild there. Then up to ten
  take the plainest meal from the stores and eat it together under the colony's oldest tree. Nothing felled: no
  sapling owed, and the words say so.
- Smoulder's Deep Silver: one who holds him carries a twentieth of the stores' silver (5 to 40) to the deepest shaft (the
  thick-roofed rock his bargain uses), or in a colony with no mine to a crack beside the rock, and drops it: the silver
  is gone, with heat and dust where it went, and the mountain's names said over it. No silver: they go and say the names
  all the same.
- Bellwether's Letting Pass: a herder walks the colony's free grazers (not those kept in pens on a rope) out to the long
  grass at the colony's edge and leaves them to graze it; at dusk one who holds him (else the eldest) tells the old
  story there to the children (else to whoever came out).
- Morel's Turning Under: hay (else the plainest raw vegetables) carried out to the field and dug under
  (`Rimfolk_Feast_Dig`): the scraps are gone, and up to nine squares of the field's natural soil turn rich. Then a cook
  takes mushrooms from the stores (every raw fungus the game knows, `FungusMeals.IsRawFungus`) to a stove that cooks
  simple meals and cooks a pot of mushroom stew (`Rimfolk_Feast_Cook`): fungus meals (Ideology), else simple meals, of
  that fungus, up to six, set down by the stove.
- Pip's First Spark: a broken machine fixed (the game's own repair with a component from the stores), else a damaged
  building repaired (the game's own); the machines walked round one by one and looked over (`Rimfolk_Feast_Machine`), the
  work benches where there are none; at dusk a round of the lamps (below), left burning till dawn, when the ones lit for
  the night are switched off again. Told at dawn.
- Hush's Stillness: at supper up to twelve take the plainest meal (a simple meal before paste) to the seats by the fire
  (a fire of fuel, else any heater, else the table): the sick first, then the old (60 and over), nearest
  (`OwnFeastsMath.SeatOrder`), and eat it there in silence (nothing of Rimfolk's is said).
- Undertow's Shuttered Night: as night falls someone goes round the doors to the outside and the lamps
  (`Rimfolk_Feast_Lamp`): a door held open is let shut, a lamp switched off is switched on, and torches and braziers low on
  fuel are topped up with the game's own refuelling (a lamp lit in an age without switches). Told at ten with the lights
  burning then; at dawn the doors held open again and the lamps switched off again, only those nobody changed since.
- Selene's Longest Night: one or two who hold her keep watch on the walls from dusk till dawn: the night watch's own
  play-out (`DilemmaEffect_Vigil`, at the gate, patrolled, till dawn), so its cold on a frosty night is the shared
  budget's (`nightWatch`), nothing new; with answers not played out on the map they stand at the colony's edge instead.
  At breakfast up to three tell a dream to whoever eats beside them.
- Also: at every festival's rite the believers who are free walk over and stand in rows behind the one leading it, facing
  the god's place (`OwnFeasts.Gather` from `Festivals.Hourly`).
- What was done is told as it was seen, plainly (a message), and goes in the colony's book under the god it was kept
  for, in the old voice of the gods' texts. Each part leaves a small good mood with those who took part
  (`Rimfolk_Thought_Feast_*`, +2 to +3). Every age: torches topped up where there are no lamps, a crack in the rock where
  there is no mine, the work benches where there are no machines.
- Saved: the festival under way (`OwnHappeningsBook.feast`, `FeastState`): its step, who was sent, what was counted, the
  lamps and doors changed for the night (put back and let go at dawn) and Hollin's count of trees felled.

**C2, sacred kinds for every god** (`Gods/SacredKinds.cs`; `Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Gods.xml`). The ten gods without
sacred kinds get some from the player's animals, rare kinds only (never the land's common game), each soft
(`MayRequire`): Smoulder the drake, the ironhusk beetle, the monitor lizard and the mammoth worm; Morel the fungal husk,
the red spore and the decay drake; Ennu the donkey and the crow; Cirrus the thunderox, the thunderbeast, the shock goat
and the crane; Hush the frostbound behemoth, the frostling, the frost lynx, the arctic lion, the frost ave and the arctic
drake; Undertow the dusk prowler, the dusk rat, the night ram and the night mule; Helios the flamingo phoenix, the
phoenix owlcat and the peacock; Selene the angel moth, the crepuscular beetle and the owlbeast; Murmur, beside the toad,
the bullfrog, the heron, the otter, the sea otter and the beaver; Ducat the black scarab and the pangolin; Hollin, beside
her dryads, Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Dryads' castes and their awakened forms, the Merren's squid dryad and the elves'
ancient deer. Pip keeps none. What they drive, by the god's own kinds instead of its domain's (the domain's still for a
god with none of its own): a sacred beast killed is an offence to its god (`GodDeeds`, `GodHealth`), the vow to spare
a beast (`Vows`), the god's dream warning of a hunt (`GodDreams`), the beast a god's people bring (`GodWorldGifts`),
and the god's mark is never one of them (`GodMarkGoods`). One choice made here: the donkey is kept for Ennu as the
proposal's table has it, though a colony may keep donkeys; slaughtering one is an offence to Ennu, as for any sacred
kind.

**C3, a god's beast at home** (`Gods/OnMap/GodBeasts.cs`). One of the colony's own animals of a god's sacred kind (or of
the shape a god walks in). Each colonist takes it for a god by their own reading, fixed for the two of them
(`GodBeastsMath.Roll` with `GodLoreMath.Attribute`), sometimes wrongly. Those who hold the god they take it for:
- greet it the first time they see it close, in one sentence;
- now and then, in the animals' rounds hours, one of them brings it a bite by hand from the stores (two days apart at
  least at a home);
- on that god's festival one of them gives it a bite first and walks it to the god's place, and the book keeps it;
- one born on its god's festival day is an omen animal (`OmenAnimals`), named in the god's own words, while there is
  room among the living omens (the twenty days' gap gives way to the day);
- when it dies they grieve a little (-2 for 3 days), and the book keeps a believer's verse under the god they took it for.

**C4, the beast that stays, taken for a god's** (`ResidentBeast`, `Animals/ResidentBeastSacred.cs`). When the beast that
stays is named and is of a god's sacred kind or shape, a believer there says whose they take it for (a line, a sentence
in the naming letter, a verse in the book). The council's question about it is then `Council_DlmA_ResidentBeastSacred`,
with the believer's own answer first and as the default: leave it be, it is not ours to hunt (the believer walks out at
dusk and stands within sight of it a while; the god it is like is glad of it, hidden; the book keeps it). Hunting it is
the harm of a sacred beast to those who hold the god it was taken for (-4 for 5 days) and an offence to the god it is
like; if it stays a season, the book keeps that it stayed among them, under that god.

**C16, legendary Pokémon taken for a god's** (`GodBeasts.Legends`, `GodBeastsMath.Legends`). A wild one of the table's
kinds on a map where the colony's people are (PokéWorld's legendaries; Meowth and Persian for Ducat and Spiritomb for
Tamiu, though not legendaries): a believer there says whose they take it for, perhaps wrongly, a scoffer may answer,
and the book keeps it as a god's hand (`GodHands.ShowWith`); the same kind once in 30 days at most. Hunting it is the
harm of a sacred beast for those who believe it, and an offence to the god it is like.

**C17, the gods, the beasts and the land in the colony's art** (`Things/ArtTales.cs`, `ArtTalesMath.cs`;
`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_Tales.xml`). Eight of Rimfolk's moments are recorded as the game's own tales (`Tale_Rimfolk`), so a
sculpture made later may show one in the game's words for art: a god seen (by its first witness), a sacred beast's visit
(someone sat near it or fed it), an offering taken before everyone's eyes, a festival kept (its rite), a god's beast
walked to its place on its festival, the beast that stays given its name, the herd's old leader dying (with its keeper),
and a raid held at a line (they came through the gate and nobody fell). A god is named in them only by the colony's
name where the colony knew at the time it was that god, else as what was seen (`GodDef.unheard`). A kind comes at most
once in a few days at a home. Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Art's statues take the same tales. A ninth came with the land
and its life (0.279.1): a named season a believer took for a god's doing (C18, `SeasonGods.Named`), with the
believer as the one in it, the season's name as what it was about and the god by `ArtTales.GodWords` (said as the
believer's view: "took the season for the doing of ..."), once in a quadrum at most at a home.

- **Dev mode**: "Gods: a festival kept now, its custom at once...", "Gods: the festival's next part now", "Gods: a
  festival's rite now, the believers behind it...", "Gods: a god's beast at home: greeted, given a bite, walked to its
  place...", "Gods: the beast that stays here taken for a god's now, and its question", "Gods: a legendary on the land
  now, taken for a god's...", "Art: each of Rimfolk's tales now (for a sculpture to show)".
- Code: `Gods/OnMap/OwnFeasts.cs`, `OwnFeastsMath.cs`, `GodBeasts.cs`, `GodBeastsMath.cs` (new); `Gods/SacredKinds.cs`
  (new); `Things/ArtTales.cs`, `ArtTalesMath.cs` (new); `Animals/ResidentBeastSacred.cs` (new);
  `Gods/GodsIntegrationDebug.cs` (new); `Gods/OnMap/OwnHappenings.cs`, `OwnSeven.cs` (the feast saved),
  `Gods/Worship/Festivals.cs`, `Gods/GodHands.cs` (`ShowWith`), `Gods/GodDeeds.cs`, `Gods/World/GodHealth.cs`,
  `GodWorldGifts.cs`, `Gods/Worship/Vows.cs`, `GodDreams.cs`, `Offerings.cs`, `Gods/Presence/GodMarkGoods.cs`,

### Gifts worth what they cost (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.259.0)

The player: "so as of now i still don't really see or feel the impact of god offerings. sometimes they trigger an event,
but sometimes nothing seems to happen. i just wonder whether these offering ressources are "wasted", or if there is always
some benefit from them? since it's usually more valuable ressources also"; then "I don't necessarily need every offering
answered, as long as there is value to it still. sometimes a return in kind sounds great. the book should track the
offerings and in this case also the god's favour should be tracked in the book, but the wording should also be kept a bit
ominous, so not with a numeric value or so"; and "also it should please never take very valuable items like components
etc. as offering, or only if there is a proper payoff for it. but then it shouldn't take it automatically, but perhaps an
event where a pawn asks for approval first". The go: "go ahead with this".

- **None wasted** (`WorshipMath.OfferingFavour`): an offering's favour keeps growing with its worth instead of flattening
  past a few hundred silver: 1 + 0.35 √worth (a meal about 2.5, a hundred silver's worth about 4.5, five hundred about
  9, a thousand about 12), at most 14 (`OfferingWorthMost`), times the god's liking and nature, the year's honour and a
  priest's rite as before. Every taking still moves it; nothing shows it but the gods' doings and the keeper's reading.
- **What follows leans by the gift** (`OfferingGiftMath.Lean`, `GodTouchMath.TierFor`, `GapDays`): a gift's worth and fit
  give a lean (1 for an everyday gift of about 40 silver's worth that the god likes; a token gift down to a half; a rich
  or well-loved one up; a precious one asked first at least 2, at most 3). It makes the god's own effect after the taking
  likelier (its chance times √lean), notable and great ones likelier (times the lean and its square), the god's own waits
  for those shorter by it (the colony's waits stay), and the four days between two takings' effects shorter for a rich
  gift (a day and a half at the least), longer for a token one (six days), none for a precious one. Lean 1 is the old
  rule exactly. The gift's worth reaches the touch through `GodTouch.Taken` (found gone, seen going) and `GodTouch.Coming`
  (taken before everyone's eyes, its moment's note carrying it).
- **A return in kind** (`Gods/Touch/GodTouchReturn.cs`): now and then a taking is answered in kind, in place of any other
  effect: about one in eleven for an everyday gift, more the stronger the lean (at most three in ten), about half for a
  precious one (`OfferingGiftMath.ReturnChance`); a god once in ten days at a home, any god once in three, a precious gift
  whenever (`ReturnAllowed`). Worth about what was given (three quarters to a fifth more; a precious one as much to half
  again; at least 15), as many pieces as make it, a stack at most (`ReturnWorth`, `ReturnCount`, `PickReturn` by weight
  among the god's goods no single piece of which is worth more than the return). Each god's goods, by the colony's age
  and the player's mods (`Goods`): Hollin the land's wild plant food (its biome's wild plants' harvests) and herbal
  medicine; Smoulder steel, silver, gold from the medieval age, uranium from the industrial, plasteel from the spacer,
  and every mod's metal mined from rock at the colony's age; Bellwether hay, milk and every mod's wool; Morel raw fungus
  and every mod's raw mushrooms (Alpha Biomes', Alpha Animals'; Vanilla Plants Expanded - Mushrooms' raw blisscap and
  bileceps by name); Ennu pemmican (tribal and medieval) or packaged
  survival meals, and cloth; Pip steel, and from the industrial age components and chemfuel, advanced components in the
  spacer age; Hush the hides of the land's animals; Selene herbal medicine, industrial medicine from the industrial age,
  glitterworld medicine rarely in the spacer age, and silver; Murmur fish (the game's fish category: Odyssey's and
  Vanilla Fishing Expanded's) and rice; Ducat silver, gold from
  the medieval age. Cirrus, Undertow, Helios and Tamiu give nothing back in kind. It lies where the gift lay (by the
  shrine), with the god's own look and sound, the camera on it, a message ("Avila found silver x40 at Ducat's chapel,
  where the offering had lain."), the nearest colonist's line (`Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_ReturnFound`: their own god's, as
  others hold it, a doubter's maybe, a scoffer's someone), the colony's book as those who saw it saw it (a kindness, the
  moods of one), and the gift's own line in the book ("In its place lay silver x40.").
- **Precious, never taken unasked** (`Gods/Worship/OfferingGifts.cs`, `OfferingGiftMath.Precious`): what pawns carry on
  their own (`Offerings.Pick`) is only what isn't precious and the colony has plenty of (three times the gift and its own
  store, as before). Precious: the player's list by name (components, advanced components, plasteel, uranium, gold, jade,
  neutroamine), every mod's parts for machines (a manufactured piece worth 25 or more), medicine past herbal, glitterworld
  goods (traded as exotic, or of the spacer age), a material worth more than 5 a piece (devilstrand, hyperweave, thrumbo
  leather, a mod's rare metal), and anything the colony can't make now or gather again. Made now: a recipe of a bench it
  has built, the research done; a vat's beer where a barrel stands; a mod's cheap drink or smoke (20 a piece at most)
  where a mod's processor stands (Vanilla Brewing Expanded's stills and barrels). Gathered: a plant on its land or sown
  in its fields, a rock it can mine, an animal on its land (meat, hide) or of its own (milk, wool, eggs); and always
  food, herbs, wood, hides, wool, cloth and the plainer fabrics, stone blocks and silver. Read once a day a home.
- **Asked first** (`OfferingGifts.Daily`, `Ask`, the gods' questions' card `GodAsks.Precious`): now and then someone
  devout (the priest first) whose god has a place here and takes gifts comes to the player wanting to give something
  precious of the colony's that the god loves (or of the kind a dream asked for, `AskForDemand`, when nothing plain of it
  is left): a card with Yes and No ("Avila asks to give component x4 to Pip"), saying what, where, why in plain words
  (the everyday gifts are only what the colony can spare; or the god asked for it in a dream), what they hope it brings
  as they believe it ("Avila hopes Pip will keep the machines running.", each god's `GodWorshipDef.hope`), and what the
  colony holds and would keep; they say a line as it comes (`Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_AskGift`). How much: about four
  everyday gifts' worth (120 to 1000), never more than a third of what is held, never a piece worth more than 1500, only
  where the colony keeps twice the gift and its own store after it (`AskCount`, `Askable`). How often: a home's ask 12
  days apart at least, a god's 20, the same thing to the same god a month after a no, then a quarter's chance a day
  (`AskNow`): about one in a fortnight at most. Only when one of Rimfolk's questions may come (`Tell.CanAsk`); the card
  waits two days. **Yes**: they say so (`GiftYes`) and carry it from the largest stack they can reach (`SendPrecious`;
  the priest or another who holds the god if they can't, two days at most), set it down with a precious line of the offer
  pool, a better mood for it (`Rimfolk_Worship_OfferedPrecious`, +3, two days), for half again the favour of an everyday
  gift of its worth (`PreciousFavour`), its taking leaned at least 2. **No**: it stays in the stores; they say so
  (`GiftNo`), a devout one a little disappointed (`Rimfolk_Worship_GiftKept`, -2, a day, with its mood hint), and the same
  ask waits a month.
- **The book keeps every gift** (`Gods/GodLoreGifts.cs`, `GodLore.Gave`): each gift's fate once the colony knows it, under
  the name it gave it by, in the god's chapter ("Of the gifts given", oldest first, dated): what it was, who left it at
  which place (and home, with more than one), given with the colony's leave for a precious one, and what became of it:
  found gone by someone, gone and nobody saw it go, taken before whose eyes, seen going, given to a visitor, eaten by an
  animal, taken by someone passing, back to the stores, spoiled; and what was found in its place. 300 kept, 40 a god.
- **Each god's temper, as the keeper reads it** (`Gods/GodTemper.cs`, `GodTemperMath`, `GodLore.tempers`): every four to
  eight days the book's keeper reads each god the colony gives to, has a place for or holds to: one step from their last
  reading (from nothing known, the first time) toward the god's standing at the seat in its seven words, or a step beside
  it when they misread it (15 % with something of the god seen in the last 12 days, 35 % with nothing, and then said as
  "some say"). Late and sometimes wrong, as the pawns would read it. Shown in the god's chapter ("Of its temper toward us",
  "As Avila read it, on 3rd of Aprimay, 5502:") in five bands of the god's own words (`GodWorshipDef.temper`: angry, cold,
  silent, warm, glad), a little ominous ("Smoulder's fires have burned warm toward us since the steel was given.", "Some
  say the Hunger is restless."), "since ... was given" after a gift taken within 15 days before it warmed. Never a number,
  and nowhere else (no tooltip, no Almanac numbers, no setting); nobody keeps the book, nobody reads, and the last reading
  stands. The page itself still holds no word of favour (`GodBookTests`).
- **The unseen rule holds**: what people hope or read is theirs, never a promise; a return is told as what was found
  where; nothing names a god as the doer except where the colony knows it, and the colony's own place names (Ducat's
  chapel) are the colony's.
- Saved: `OfferingRecord.precious`, `want`, `wantCount`, `asker`, `worth`, `fit`, `plain`; `GodLore.gifts` and `tempers`
  (modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`); the asks' marks among `WorshipBook.homeMarks` (let go once past). Dev mode: "Gods:
  someone asks to give something precious now", "Gods: what is precious here (log)", "Gods: every gift taken answered in
  kind (on, off)", "Gods: the keeper reads the gods now (log)". Tests: `Tools/Tests/OfferingGiftTests.cs`; the moods in
  `Tools/Balance/Rates.cs`.

### Revel, the Open Cup: a fifteenth god of drink, drugs and the long night (the player's go, 16 November 2026; released 0.260.0)

The player, 15 November 2026: "a new god ... a god of drugs, the god of excess partying, and so to say, of pleasures. So,
you know, smoke leaf, alcohol ... more of drugs, with the good and bad that they bring to a colony. And, you know, the god
likes to deceive or kind of play with pawns, minds and bodies, you know, like drugs do"; then "what would be interesting is
that the god could take shape inside an actual drug, and once a pawn consumes it, they will get a godly effect from it";
"and i'd like it to also have some physical shape, perhaps a devil or so?", "satyr would be awesome"; and the name, "Revel
sounds great". No loving (the player left it out). Built as the other fourteen are, every part of them, and unseen as
they are: felt at revels and feasts, in a drinker's or a smoker's high, in an addict's craving and a hangover.

- **Who he is** (`Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_Gods.xml`, `Rimfolk_God_Revel`, key `Revel`): the spirit in drink and smoke and the
  long night, generous first and a cheat after. Plain line: "The spirit in drink, smoke and the long night. He gives a
  good night first, and takes his price in the morning." Names by age: the Laughing Horn, the Merry Cheat, the Last
  Round, the pleasure signal (and the Open Cup, Old Tipple). Three stories (the last barrel he kept the songs going over
  while Hush stood outside, the sweet cup that teaches the brewer's cart as his, the wager with Ennu over who could stay
  longer at a table), sayings, believers' and scoffers' lines, letters. Allies with Ennu, rivals with Hush. Domains
  Hearth and Night (the fallback only), Capricious, revered by the Wheel and the river folk and by every age's kind and
  raiders; the goat his sacred animal. Taken now and then for the Guest, the moon or the dark (`GodLoreMath.Confused`).
- **His sign** (`Tools/make_god_signs.py`, `revel()`): a cup with a goat's horns curling up from its rim and three drops
  spilling over, in wine red and gold (`Textures/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Signs/Revel.png`; the draft sheet has a fifth row).
- **His look and his shape** (`Rimfolk_GodsOnMap_Shapes.xml`): `Rimfolk_GodShape_Revel` (never a stranger at the gate,
  never a beast: he walks only as the horned reveller, by his own code), his signs, his line tag, drawn near by people
  high or drunk and a party under way (`GodStir.Revelry`); `Rimfolk_GodLook_Revel`: a person drawn larger in wine red and
  gold, Vanilla Factions Expanded - Classical's toga and wreath (the game's robe and headdress otherwise), Ideology's bong
  smoke and twinkles, a goat's call and a beer's sound, Vanilla Memes Expanded's hedonist chant, the fairy folk's
  Scarborough Fair and Odyssey's Baubles for his track.
- **His signs** (`OmenKind.Bleat`, `SweetSmoke`, `Spilled`; `GodOmensOwn`): a goat bleating in an empty room of the colony's
  late at night, heard by someone outside it; a sweet smoke drifting through the colony where nothing burns (Ideology's
  bong smoke, pale rose); the drink in the stores found knocked over, one of it gone and a wet patch beside it. Each said
  aloud and kept in the book.
- **His presence** (`Rimfolk_GodPresence_Revel`, `PresenceEffect.Revelry`, "a merry air"; named "{NAME} at the table"):
  a sweet smoke over the place and curls of it over whoever is at their recreation, a goat calling among the houses;
  recreation fills 30 % faster at full strength (`GodPresenceOwnMath.JoyGain`, `Patch_GodPresenceJoy` on the game's
  `Need_Joy.GainJoy`), a quarter slower in his anger (the morning after). Its numbers under its label. It may stay five
  days as a great effect of his.
- **His own happenings** (`Gods/OnMap/OwnRevel.cs`, the rules in `RevelMath.cs`, in the second seven's frame: the gods' hour,
  the steps, the feast, saved with the book as `RevelState`):
  - *The long night* (`RevelLongNight`): at his feast or a party of the game's own, or with three of the colony at their
    ease round a late fire, between nine and eleven: someone says nobody is going to bed, a goat calls, and those near
    stay where they are, at their ease, the recreation coming a little at a time, until two (only the rested and fed;
    anyone tired or hungry goes). Then a good memory (+4, a day and a half), a fifth of their rest gone, and a slow
    morning (-2, half a day), someone saying so.
  - *A vision* (`RevelVision`): someone high (any of the game's or the mods' drug highs) stops and stares, says so, and
    walks out to what it showed them: true a little under half the time (a seam of ore in the rock nobody has marked,
    wild healroot), else false (a door in the ground, someone watching, a light under the ground, something buried, and
    nothing there). Told as seen; the book keeps it as their belief ("High on beer, I was shown a seam of silver in the
    rock to the east."), true or not, under the god they take it for.
