  - *A craving in the night* (`RevelCraving`): an addict asleep whose craving is on them, between midnight and three,
    wakes and goes to the stores for their drug (the game's own taking, only where their drug policy allows it for the
    addiction); someone awake who sees it says so, and the book keeps it.
  - *A stash found* (`RevelStash`): someone working far out by day comes on a few of the colony's own kind of drink or
    smoke hidden at their feet (about a hundred silver's worth at most, never a hard drug).
  - *A binge egged on* (`RevelBinge`): someone on the game's own drug binge is seen talking and laughing with an empty
    seat, a goat's call and a little of his look there; a witness says so. No chance of its own: it follows the game's
    binge, half of them.
  - *The craving eased* (`RevelLetGo`, the cure against him): at night the priest, one devoted to Revel or a friend sits
    up with an addict in withdrawal until dawn; by morning the addiction (the game's own hediff) is lifted a little
    (`LetGoEase`, it wears off that much sooner), both glad of the night (+3 and +4, two days), and the addict believes
    the craving let go of them.
  - *The horned reveller* (`RevelSatyr`): at a party, his feast, a long night or a late fire, between eight and eleven, a
    grown man of a people at peace walks in out of the dark with a cup of the colony's kind of drink, made the god's and
    shown as one (`GodAvatar`, his look) with his moment and card (named "{GOD} at the fire" only where the colony knows
    him). His shape: a satyr's, where one of the player's mods has a xenotype called so (none is active yet), else Alpha
    Genes' goat horns (`AG_ForsakenHornsGoat`, `AG_DevilsheepHorns`) or the game's own (`Headbone_MiniHorns`,
    `Headbone_CenterHorn`). He walks to someone at their ease who would take it (not a teetotaler, a child, or one their
    drug policy keeps from it), puts the cup in their hands and they drink it (it is his cup, below), and he is gone
    before dawn, nobody seeing him leave.
  - *His cup* (`RevelCup`): below.
- **The god in a cup** (`Gods/OnMap/RevelCup.cs`, the rules `RevelCupMath`): now and then (about once in two or three weeks
  a home, never with one of his waiting) Revel is in one drink or one dose of a stack of his in the colony's stores, a
  drink likelier: any one of the stack alike. It looks like any other; at most someone passing near it notices something
  small about it, once ("This beer smells sweeter than it should."). His one is followed through the game's own stacks:
  a split (hauled, carried off, eaten from, sold) takes him with the part taken off the front if he was among it; a
  merge brings him across behind the stack's own; eating takes him if he was among what was taken (`Patch_RevelCupSplit`,
  `Patch_RevelCupAbsorb`, `Patch_RevelCupIngested` on `Thing.SplitOff`, `TryAbsorbStack`, `Ingested`, behind the deep
  hooks setting, a single compare while he is in no cup). One of the colony's own who takes him gets one of his effects,
  never told in advance: two times in three his generosity (a clean high, `Rimfolk_RevelCleanHigh`, +12, ten hours, and
  no hangover for thirty; a burst of skill, an inspiration of the game's own else a sharp mind for half a day; a vision,
  as above; no fear for a day, `Rimfolk_RevelBold`); one in three his deceit (a wonderful high that turns into a hard
  crash after four hours, `Rimfolk_RevelCrash`, +16 then -10; a sudden craving, -8 for most of a day, and another of the
  same where it isn't a hard drug and their policy allows it; or, about one cup in twenty, the drug's own addiction taking
  hold at once, the game's own hediff, through the shared harm budget, `HarmKinds.GodCup`, a high and a crash when the
  budget says no). Each shown as it happens: their word, a little of his look, a message of what it did, the camera on
  them. A few hours after, the book keeps what they believe it was (`RevelCupMath.Read`): a scoffer that it was only
  strong stuff (as a doubt), one in dread that it was a trick, the rest a blessing (or only a strong batch, one in four)
  for a kindness and a trick or a curse for his deceit, a vision a true sight, under the god they take it for (maybe the
  wrong one). He leaves a cup nobody takes within a month, or one gone from the colony. Guests, prisoners and beasts take
  only the drink.
- **His touch** (`GodTouchMath.Table["Revel"]`): a light heart (`Rimfolk_GodTouch_Bless_Revel`: recreation and company
  come easier for a day), high spirits for those who saw it (their recreation filled, `TouchEffect.Merry`), a few of the
  colony's kind of drink or smoke left where it happened, an inspiration (a party frenzy, creativity), his merry air for
  five days; his anger some of the drink in the stores gone sour and spilled across the floor (`TouchEffect.Sour`). His
  return in kind (`GodTouchReturn`): drink and smoke of the colony's own kind, what it can make again first, never a hard
  drug, beer always among them. His look where he acts (`GodTouchFx`): bong smoke, twinkles, bubbles, a joint's smoke.
- **His worship** (`Rimfolk_Worship_Revel`): drink first, then drugs, then a meal; what the colony carries to him on its own
  is what it can make again (`Offerings.Pick` passes over anything precious), a dear drink or drug only when someone asks
  (0.259.0's ask). His way of taking (`OfferingWay.Cup`): drunk off in the night where it lay, the ground left wet and
  smelling of drink, a curl of sweet smoke. His hope ("give us a good night and an easy morning"), his temper in five
  bands of his own words for the keeper. His feast, the Long Night of Revel (autumn, the 8th): the barrels opened at
  dusk, the first drop poured on the ground, the fire kept until morning; that night runs long and he may come to the fire.
  His people's rite (`BeliefRite.Cup`): the first drop of a cup poured on the ground at a table or a lit fire in the
  evening. Drawn to him: chemical interest and fascination, Vanilla Traits Expanded's drunken master, joyous, a love of
  cooking or talk, a past as a brewer, a barkeep, a vintner, a distiller, an entertainer.
- **In the world** (`Rimfolk_GodWays_Revel`): his kindness the colony's brewing barrels ready overnight, days early
  (`GodBlessing.Cask`, the game's own barrels); his anger some of the drink in the stores turned sour (`GodWrath.Sour`); his
  blessing on a body the open cup (`Rimfolk_GodGift_Revel`: more pleasure in everything, people warm to them); a dream of
  a horned man at the end of the bed with a cup in each hand; on the warm side of the quarrel with Hush's cold. His hand
  seen in a brewer's cart at the gate, a feast at a camp, music on the air (`GodHandsMath`).
- **His saints** (`SaintsMath.OwnWords`, `ByOwnWords`): a faith's deity of wine, revelry, the tavern, pleasure or the high
  life (Ideology's high life, Vanilla Memes Expanded's party life, Alpha Memes' epicureans) is his; he is tied by a
  deity's own words only, never by its domains, so the faiths' older ties keep. Never one of the damned.
- **Every age its form, from the whole of the player's mods** (`Gods/OnMap/RevelGoods.cs`): his drink and drugs are read
  from every def loaded (the game's and the DLCs' beer, smokeleaf, psychite tea, ambrosia, psilocap; Vanilla Brewing
  Expanded's spirits, cocktails, coffees and teas; Vanilla Factions' mead, wine, rum, opium and chemshine; Alpha Crafts'
  kvass and sake; Rim Bees' mead; whatever else is loaded), never by a list of names: a drug that isn't medicine. What
  the colony can make again now comes first (its benches with the research done, its barrels, a mod's stills: 0.259.0's
  reading), then what its age knows (no newer than the colony, nothing dearer than 70 a piece), beer last. Who is high,
  addicted or craving is the game's own highs, addictions and needs, every mod's.
- **The unseen rule holds**: no word of what he wants; a card names him only where the colony knows him; what happens is
  told as seen; the cup looks like any other; the book keeps beliefs, never the truth. The harm is only the game's own
  drugs (their highs, hangovers, addictions and overdoses), taken by the colony's people themselves as their drug policy
  allows, and the cup's addiction through the shared budget.
- Saved: `OwnHappeningsBook.revel` (single records: the night, a vision, a craving, a binge seen, a night sat up, the
  horned reveller, the cup and who took it); the happenings' list one longer for each (`Tools/save_estimate.py`). Dev mode:
  "Gods: Revel's long night now", "... vision now", "... craving in the night now", "... stash found now", "... binge
  egged on now", "... craving eased now", "... horned reveller now", "Gods: Revel in a cup in the stores now", "Gods: where is
  Revel's cup (log)", "Gods: Revel's next cup does...". Tests: `Tools/Tests/RevelTests.cs` (and every test that counts the
  gods); the moods in `Tools/Balance/Rates.cs`.

### The gods among the colony's people and the world (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.278.0)

The player on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "your content proposal overall sounds really good ... I just want
additional God events, more immersion, more just further also building up on the gods in general, how they're
integrated, the effects they have, the relations between pawns, the kind of events that generated from it", and "first
do all the integrations that you proposed in your document". Built: C6, C7, C8, C12, C14, C15, C18, C26 and C29 of part
C. The code is `Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/Among/`; the pure rules `GodsAmongMath` (linked into the tests); the saved state
`GodsAmongBook` (a game component, its hour and day with the gods' own, `GodBook.Hourly`/`Daily`, its steps only while
something is under way); the defs `Defs/GodDefs/Rimfolk_GodsAmong.xml` and
`Defs/RoomTemplateDefs/Rimfolk_RoomTemplates_GodRooms.xml`; the words `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_GodsAmong.xml`. The
gods stay unseen in all of it: a god is named only as a speaker's own name for it or the colony's page, everything in the
book is someone's (seen, told, believed), and nothing says what a god wants.

- **C6, a vowed pilgrimage that really walks out** (`VowPilgrimage.cs`). The vow's hour (`Vows.TrySetOut`) first looks for
  a holy place of the vower's god within one to six days' road (`GodsAmongMath.InReach`): a town of a people that holds
  the god (`Gods.Of`), the pilgrim fellowship's town (`PeoplesMath.Pilgrims`), an old shrine by a landmark; the town of a
  people that holds it first, the others only when much nearer (`RoadWeight`). They go as a season away
  (`SeasonAway.Send`, key `vowpilgrim`, the old shrine's people the colony's own faction): the walk to the edge, a
  caravan of one, one to three days there, a caravan home. The message on setting out says where and about how many
  days. There, the pilgrimage is made (the worship book's mark, so the vow is kept when they are home, `Vows.Daily`);
  home, something of the place at their feet (Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Relics and Artifacts' inert statuette, idol,
  medallion or amulet from a town, polished rock or fossil from an old shrine, the fellowship's shell from theirs, else
  `Rimfolk_PilgrimToken`), the book hears that people's name for the god (`GodLore.Heard`, how "Pilgrim"), and within six
  days, at supper (17 to 22 o'clock) beside someone, they tell one piece of that people's tale by that name
  (`GodTales.Tell`'s new `asName`). From a town, the fellowship's cough through the harm budget (`HarmKinds.PilgrimCough`),
  shown. Someone the colony can't spare (`PeopleEvents2.MayLeave`), or no place in reach: the walk on the colony's land as
  before. The vow's hour never interrupts one already setting out.
- **C7, Murmur and the fishers** (`MurmurFishers.cs`). A postfix on the game's catch (`FishingUtility.GetCatchesFor`): a
  colonist who holds to Murmur (`PawnGodsMath.HoldsFrom`, not in dread, not a scoffer) gives one fish of the morning's
  first catch (4 to 12 o'clock, once a day) back to the water, with the game's water splash at the spot. They keep it as
  their small rite (belief), say a word (once in three days), and someone near in sight may say they saw it; the book
  keeps it as theirs once in ten days, and their journal. That day `Rimfolk_MurmurFishBiting` (half a day): Odyssey's
  `FishingYield` +0.1 and Vanilla Fishing Expanded's `VCEF_FishingLuckOffset` +0.02, each `MayRequire`. The mod's
  `VCEF_Fisherman` draws toward Murmur (`PawnGodsMath.TraitDraws`, 22), and what the water gives back
  (`OwnMurmur.GiveBack`) may leave two to four fish of the mod's (else the game's own) on the mud.
- **C8, Ducat and what the colony owes** (`DucatDebts.cs`). `WorldLedger.Set` tells it of every move: a debt the colony
  owes (a `Tie.Kind.Debt` from a colony: a scenario's silver, an enclave's dues; a debt of honour the colony owes,
  `FavoursOwed.ColonyOwes`) kept is Paid, broken is Lapsed (`GodsAmongMath.Turn`), three times in four followed so.
  Paid: the next morning (5 to 10 o'clock) one gold coin outside the bedroom door of the one who carried the payment
  (the debt's own colonist at home, else the quartermaster, else the best talker; the colony's gate when they have no
  room of their own), found by whoever passes (`OwnHappenings.Found`, the gods' own happenings' look), and the next trade
  caravan, once settled at its spot, stays half a day longer (its lord's own timer, `TriggerData_TicksPassed`), with a
  plain message. Lapsed: the next trader at the gate drives a hard bargain for a day (-0.05 on
  `Pawn.TradePriceImprovementOffsetForPlayer`), with a plain message and "(drives a hard bargain today)" in Rimfolk's
  trade window. Ducat is never named; the coin goes into the book as whoever found it took it.
- **C12, the keeper at work** (`KeeperAtWork.cs`, `GodLoreAmong.cs`). When the book writes something seen from others'
  eyes at a place on a home map (`Gods.Remember`, `Gods.Moment`), and the keeper (`GodLore.Keeper`) wasn't among them and
  is within 90 cells, the keeper walks out when free (within eight hours), stands and looks, says one line in the old
  voice (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodsAmong_Keeper`), and the entry counts them among those who saw and adds their words in the
  keeper's voice (`CC_GA_KeeperLooked_*`). In the evening (18 to 22), with new entries since they last wrote and not two days running, the keeper
  goes to Vanilla Books Expanded's writer's or typewriter's table, else a table to eat at, else a lectern, and writes
  (`Rimfolk_Keeper_Write`, `JobDriver_KeeperWrites`: a little longer for each new entry, an hour and a half at most), with
  a line on sitting down and their journal after.
- **C14, the raiders' gods, heard at the wall** (`RaidersGods.cs`). A raid (the game's `TryExecute`) of a people that holds
  gods, seven in ten: its cry waits up to 18 hours, until a raider is within 38 cells and in sight of one of the colony;
  then they cry their people's war god (else the god they swear by) by their own name for it
  (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodsAmong_RaiderCry`), and the book sets it down as "so a raider of the Ashen Banner cried at our wall"
  (`GodLore.Heard`'s new words key, `CC_GodLore_Cried_*`), with the name heard. A prisoner talking with their warden (a
  postfix on `Pawn_InteractionsTracker.TryInteractWith`) tells a piece of their gods' tales one time in five, once in two
  days at most (how "Cell"). Raids waiting for their cry are not saved.
- **C15, the dead's own god at the grave** (`GraveGods.cs`). On a colonist's death (a `Pawn.Kill` postfix) the god they
  held most is kept five days; at their eulogy (`GodDeeds.Funeral`, now returning the line) the speaker gives them to it
  in one sentence in the old voice (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodsAmong_Grave`), said over their head and added to the eulogy's
  letter. Those of the colony who grieve the dead and hold the same god get `Rimfolk_Thought_GivenToOurGod` (+3, six
  days). The book keeps it as the speaker's belief ("Ana rests in Hush's keeping now") by the colony's name for the god,
  or "in the keeping of the god she held" when the colony has none, and, named, a rite in its chapter.
- **C18, named seasons taken for a god's doing** (`SeasonGods.cs`). When the weather book names a season
  (`WeatherBook.EndQuarter`), the gods its kind is tied to (`GodsAmongMath.GodsFor`: cold Hush; heat Helios or Smoulder,
  a warm winter Helios; storms Cirrus; wet Murmur; dry Helios or Murmur): the believer who holds one of them most says
  it over their head and the book keeps it as their belief; another who holds another of them, beside them, says so to
  their face, both hold their own the harder (`BeliefEvent.Bickered`) and the book keeps both; a doubter beside them
  answers and the book keeps the doubt (`GodLore.Disputed`). The season goes among the hands a neighbour's letter may
  write of, and is kept (`SeasonTaken`, twelve at most); the year after, in the first six days of the same quarter, the
  council is asked (`Rimfolk_Dlm_SeasonDay`, the flavour style): keep a day for the god at its place (words there with
  whoever comes, the book's rite), or let it pass (the one who asked goes there alone). Both play out.
- **C26, a shrine room for each god** (`GodRooms.cs`, `RoomTemplateDef.god`, `godLabel`, `godPurpose`, `openSky`). Eleven
  rooms: Hollin's garden shrine (pots round bare ground for a tree), Smoulder's stone room with braziers and Dragons
  Descent's dragon statue, Bellwether's standing stone (Alpha Memes' or VFE Props and Decor's megalith), Morel's dark
  cellar of pots, Cirrus's obelisk court, Hush's white room with Alpha Memes' urns, Helios's sun court of columns,
  Selene's moon garden with Alpha Props' obelisk fountain, Tamiu's tomb shrine (a sarcophagus, Alpha Memes' Kemetic
  slab), Murmur's well-house (Dubs Bad Hygiene's well), Pip's machine shrine (Ideology's terminal). Each has a piece of
  the game's own it can't do without; the mods' pieces are used where the colony can build them. `RoomMenu.Entries`
  shows one only once the book has a page for its god (`GodsAmongMath.RoomShown`), labelled by the colony's name for it;
  `openSky` rooms mark their floor no-roof when planned (`TemplatePlanner.Execute`). Their words picture the god as the
  people do, never what it wants.
- **C29, midwinter with Vanilla Christmas Expanded** (`Midwinter.cs`). The colony's midwinter is the calendar keeping the
  winter god's festival (Hush or Selene; `CalendarKeeping.KeepDay`) or the midwinter custom (its day, or its question's
  first two answers, `DilemmaEffect_Midwinter`). With the mod loaded, that day: by day, where the snow is deep near home,
  someone makes a snowman with the game's own job, finished as the mod's snow sculpture (theirs, its quality by their
  art); at dusk someone walks to a festive tree and switches every tree and string of fairy lamps on (said plainly when
  there is no power), or stands a while at one already lit; at supper the cook carries the gingerbread, eggnog and hot
  cocoa from the stores to the festive feast table (else the dining table) and sets them out beside it; after supper the
  eldest takes the presents from the stores and hands one to each of the colony at home, person by person, each thinking
  a little better of them (`Rimfolk_Thought_MidwinterPresent`, +6 opinion). Each part only with its things, and the
  words say only what was done. The winter god's own festival play-out (C1, another build) is untouched: this runs
  beside it from the calendar's keeping.

Harm: only the fellowship's cough from a crowded town (C6), already in the budget. Dev mode: "Gods among: ..." for each.
Not checked without the game: the catch hook's list, the trader lord's timer, a sculpture from a snowman, the trade
window's line, the shrine rooms' layouts with the mods' pieces.

### The gods between the colony's people, and the gods' variety (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.281.0)

The player on the content update: "In general, I just want additional God events, more immersion, more just further also
building up on the gods in general, how they're integrated, the effects they have, the relations between pawns, the kind
of events that generated from it ... And then also, just variety", and "first do all the integrations that you proposed
in your document before we add additional content variety". With the integrations released (0.278.0, 0.278.1, 0.279.1,
0.280.0), this is the first of the variety, the gods first: C5, C9, C10, C11, C13, C23 and C31 of part C of
`docs/content-update-proposals.md`, and, beyond the doc, thirty-one new happenings of the gods' own (two or more for each
of the fifteen) that set the colony's people toward or against each other. The gods stay unseen in all of it: a card's
words never name a god; a letter's title names it only where the colony knows it was that god (`Gods.CardName`), the
Hunger never; what people say is their own guess, one sentence a bubble; the colony's book keeps it as its witness saw
it; nothing shows a favour, a want or a rule.

**The gods between the colony's people** (`Source/ColonyCouncil/Gods/OnMap/Between/`; the pure rules
`Gods/OnMap/OwnBetweenMath.cs`, linked into the tests). Each is an `OwnHappening` like the gods' others (added at the end
of the list, so a save keeps its order), on the gods' pace (`OwnHappeningsMath.BetweenPaceOf`: its own gap, a chance
growing after it, never without a reason in the world, a near god a little likelier, `GodTouch.Turn` giving the other
gods their turn; those that follow something, a fight, a fine piece, a sealed body, a newcomer, a hunt, an insult, at
their own chance once a gap is past, `FollowChance`). The frame (`Between.cs`): one scene at a home at a time
(`BetweenState`, saved with the gods' own happenings' book, its lists kept small); the kinds looked at in the gods' hour
in a random order; who stands where (`BetweenStance`: holding the god, a rival's, another's, none, doubting it all); the
card in three wordings (`CC_GodB_<happening>_Text`, `_2`, `_3`, `TextVariants`), shown with the god's own look where it
acted (`GodTouchFx`) and the camera; the book (`CC_GodB_Saw_<happening>`, so those who saw it feel it by their belief,
`GodTouch`; listed in `GodTouchMath.OwnEffectKeys`, so the touch's random effect never comes on top), a doubter's word set
beside it (`GodLore.Disputed`); and how it ends between the two (`BetweenOutcome`): closer, a quarrel (each held to their
god the harder, `BeliefEvent.Bickered`), made it up (the old quarrel's memories let go), ashamed, resentful, wary, laughed
at, a kindness remembered; each a memory of the other in the game's own opinions (`Rimfolk_Between_*`, small: +6 to +8,
-4 to -6; ashamed -3 and proud +3 are moods), a plain line in the news in three wordings and the journals. Dev mode: "Gods:
<god>'s ... now" for each (`Gods/OwnBetweenDebug.cs`). No harm: nobody is hurt, no fight.

- **Hollin.** *The saplings between them* (`HollinBound`): two who had an angering fight find two saplings side by side
  at the next dawn between where they sleep, and stand at them together: made it up, unless one scoffs (a quarrel).
  *Brambles round the stump* (`HollinStumps`): one who felled twelve trees or more in fifteen days while few were planted
  finds brambles round their last stump; one who holds her walks out with them: ashamed, or, for a doubter or a rival's
  man, a quarrel.
- **Smoulder.** *The forge flares* (`SmoulderPraise`): a masterwork (half the time) or a legend (nearly always) makes the
  bench throw heat and sparks; the maker is proud, and the next-best hand at that work walks over and resents it.
  *Pulled back from the fall* (`SmoulderNearMiss`): two at work under the mountain close together; the rock grumbles,
  one pulls the other back and a scatter of stones comes down where they stood (rubble, never on anyone); a kindness
  remembered.
- **Bellwether.** *The old one and the child* (`BellwetherTold`): at dusk the eldest takes a child to the edge and tells
  of the white beast, and the wild grazers drift close round them; closer. *The hunter who let it go* (`BellwetherSpared`):
  on a hunt, while the colony has ten days of food and never by a scoffer, the beast turns and looks and the hunter lets
  it walk off the land; at home one who holds the Old Horn says they did right (closer), else the cook grumbles about the
  meat (a quarrel).
- **Morel.** *Whose rot is it* (`MorelWasted`): food let go to rot at home; the cook and another walk to it: if either
  holds her and neither scoffs, they carry it out to the soil together (closer), else they argue whose fault it was.
  *Threads on the sealed stone* (`MorelSealed`): one of the colony dead lately sealed in a sarcophagus; at dawn white
  threads over the stone (her own drawn threads); one who holds her and one who holds Tamiu or Hush (or a doubter)
  argue over it.
- **Ennu.** *A bowl for the newcomer* (`EnnuWelcomed`): someone joins; the colony's kindest carries a meal from the
  stores and sits with them (a kindness remembered); one near who already dislikes the newcomer hears a word from them
  and is ashamed. *Waiting up for the late one* (`EnnuWaitedUp`): one out far on the land late at night; the one who
  likes them best waits at the colony's edge with a light until they come in; closer.
- **Pip.** *It wanted both of them* (`PipTwoHands`): a machine broken four hours or more with nobody at it; two lay
  their hands on it together and it starts again with a spark, no part used; closer, or a quarrel when one scoffs at it.
  *Talking to the machine* (`PipTalked`): one who holds the Hum talks to a machine or a bench, a doubter walks over to
  laugh, the machine hums and brightens, and the doubter is shaken a little; a good sport laughs along, else it stings.
- **Cirrus.** *A star for two* (`CirrusTwoWatchers`): at night under a clear sky two out of doors watch a star cross
  (a line of small lights across the sky); closer. *A shape in the clouds* (`CirrusCloudShape`): two under a clouded sky
  each see their own god's shape: of the same god closer, of two gods a quarrel, a doubter's laugh.
- **Hush.** *A coat for the cold one* (`HushCoat`): one taking a chill while a warmer coat lies in the stores; one who
  holds her (else the one who likes them best) carries it out, they put it on, and the frost round them melts; a
  kindness remembered. *Quiet asked on the cold night* (`HushNoise`): a winter night, someone loud at a party, a game or
  a long talk; one who holds her asks for quiet: the faithful say sorry and stop, the rest grumble and stop, a doubter or
  the Open Cup's own refuses, and they argue.
- **Undertow** (never named). *Seen whispering at the edge* (`UndertowWhisper`): late at night one with a deep grudge
  (opinion -50) or in despair walks to a dark place at the edge and whispers into the dark; another awake sees it and is
  wary of them after. *The light let go out* (`UndertowLampOut`): in the small hours a fuelled light by a sleeper goes
  out; in the morning the sleeper and another argue whose it was to keep, unless they are good friends.
- **Helios.** *Out into the sun* (`HeliosSun`, C9). *His light on both alike* (`HeliosAlike`): at a clear noon two at
  odds out of doors near each other; the light lies gold on both, and one who holds the Giver (one of them, or someone
  near) says he gives to all alike: they make it up, unless one scoffs. *Called into the shade* (`HeliosShade`): a hot
  noon (33 degrees or more); a friend calls one working in the sun into the shade, and they sit together a while; closer.
- **Selene.** *Sorry in the morning* (`SeleneSorry`): one who insulted another today stands out under a moon at least
  half full in the night, and in the morning goes to say sorry: taken (made it up) unless the hurt runs deep (opinion
  below -40, a quarrel). *The same dream at breakfast* (`SeleneSameDream`): two rested in the morning tell the same dream:
  friends closer, others uneasy.
- **Tamiu.** *A cat on the grave* (`MogGraveCat`): at dusk a cat (the colony's, else a stray who goes again after) sits
  on the grave of one dead within two seasons, and the two who loved them most sit with it; closer. *Riddles at supper*
  (`MogRiddle`): two quick minds trade riddles; the better wit mostly wins (luck between equals), is proud, and a cat
  walks at their heel the evening through; a good loser closer, a sore one resentful.
- **Murmur.** *A splash at the water* (`MurmurSplash`): on a hot afternoon two walk down to the still water and one
  splashes the other; frogs (Odyssey's bullfrogs) come up croaking; a good sport splashes back, else they take offence.
  *A frog in the bedroom* (`MurmurFrogIn`): in the rain, with Odyssey's bullfrog, a frog in a bedroom; the sleeper and
  another come: of one mind about it they laugh and see it out, else one who holds the toad would leave it be and they
  argue; it hops off into the wet.
- **Ducat.** *A coin passed on* (`DucatPassed`): a gold coin by one of the colony, carried to the one lowest in spirits,
  who passes it on a day later, and the third leaves it for the stores; each given it remembers the kindness. *The
  miser's silver scattered* (`DucatMiser`): one with a greedy heart sits up counting the stores' silver, and by morning
  it lies in little heaps (none lost); someone laughs at them: ashamed, or, for a doubter, stung.
- **Revel.** *One cup between them* (`RevelRivalsCup`): late in the evening two at odds; one carries a drink from the
  stores and sets it down by the other, who drinks it as their drug policy and faith allow (`FirstPot.WillDrink`): made
  it up; one who won't says so. *A wager lost* (`RevelWager`): two drunk late make a wager, and in the morning the loser
  scrubs the winner's room: a good loser closer, a sore one laughed at.

**C9, out into the sun** (`HeliosSun`, a fourth happening of his): on a clear, warm noon (11 to 14 o'clock, 15 to 34
degrees, never a heat wave), one who holds the Giver (else the best doctor) walks someone getting over an illness or an
ailment, up and about and not to be kept abed (`HealthAIUtility.ShouldSeekMedicalRest`, so Rimfolk's bed rest), out into
the sun; they sit an hour together, and the illness moves on a little (severity eased by 0.06, once); the one walked out
remembers the kindness. Its pace: six days apart, about every three when called for.

**C31, three wordings for every god happening card** (`Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_GodCards_Wordings.xml`): the
second and third wording of each of the 99 cards of the gods' own happenings, the gods on the map and the festivals (the
first in each god's own file), the same placeholders, plain words; each told through `TextVariants.Vary` where it is made
(`OwnHappenings.Card`, each god's own file, the gods on the map, the festivals). The new happenings' cards and lines are
in three wordings from the start.

**C5, four more vows** (`Gods/Worship/VowsSeason.cs`): a life goal each, set by the devout or the priest to the god they
hold, only to the gods its words are for (`WorshipMath.VowFits`), for a season (15 days), kept on the map by the vower's
own walk and broken by what anyone can see: *a lamp kept lit* (Pip, Selene, Helios, the Hunger; a light within eight
cells of the god's place: each day they fill it from the stores when it burns below six tenths, or walk over and see to
it; broken the night it goes out or is gone); *a tree a week* (Hollin: a sapling set by hand near its place each week;
broken by a week with none, or by felling a tree); *plain bread* (Hush, Morel: simple meals only, a word over their head
once a day; broken by a fine or a lavish meal eaten); *every caller fed* (Ennu, Ducat: when callers stand at the gate, a
meal from the stores set down by one of them; broken when a party leaves unfed). New `VowKind`s at the end of the list;
the vow's lamp and counts saved on its record; the life goals' text in the flavour style (`Rimfolk_Worship_Goals.xml`).

**C10, the gods' rarest gifts** (`Gods/Touch/GodRareGifts.cs`, `GodRareGiftsMath.cs`): after one of a god's great effects
(not an anger), half the time once two colony-years (120 days) have passed since the last, a named weapon of Possessed
Weapons lies where it happened in a ring of scorched ground (ash), masterwork: the glacial cleaver for Hush, the
lightning javelin for Cirrus, the volcanic maul or the craghammer for Smoulder, the verdant bow for Hollin, the gilded
arquebus for Ducat, the shrouded dagger for Tamiu, the sanctified sword for Helios, the automaton crossbow for Pip. After
Smoulder's waking, on the same wait, half the time a warm drake's egg of Dragons Descent (`DD_EggDrakeFertilized`) lies
among the fallen rock of the deep and hatches as the colony's. The words say what lay there (three wordings), never
whose; the book keeps it. The weapons are the mod's persona weapons with the game's own bonds and traits (the mod's
JavelinShock and RockSmash hit whoever the javelin or the craghammer strikes, and its GhostlySickness belongs to the
ghostly flintlock, not given): Rimfolk adds no harm. None without the mods.

**C11, who is drawn to which god** (`PawnGodsMath.XenotypeDraws`): the proposal's 28 rows (the animusen to Hush, the
malachai and the wretch to the Hunger, the lapis to Smoulder, the uredd and the åskbarn to Cirrus, the taukai, the
helixan and the archon to Pip, the hiveling and the insector to Morel, the ocularkin to Hollin, the saurid to Helios, the
highmate and the waster to Revel, the fleetkind to Ennu, the avaloi to Selene, Paws of Interest's kinds by their own, the
awakened apes to Bellwether), and, decided here, Paws of Interest's Skitty (a kitten) to Tamiu and Goodra (a rain dragon)
to Murmur. As belief, never favour; each checked against the player's active xenotypes.

**C13, more council questions of faith** (`Gods/Worship/WorshipCouncilMore.cs`, `Rimfolk_Worship_Dilemmas_More.xml`, in
the flavour style): *the shrine in the way* (a blueprint or frame of the colony's against a god's place: moved with a rite,
the place marked to be taken up; the plan drawn round it, those blueprints cancelled; or taken down, undedicated and
marked to come down); *the feast in a hard season* (a god's festival tomorrow with under five days of food or a raid in
the last three days: kept with less, no offering carried and no guests sent for, `Festivals.Kept`; the rite only, held
that evening and the day itself not kept, `ColonyCalendar`; or let pass when it comes); *the scoffer at the rite*
(someone who laughed at a god before its faithful lately, a "mocked" mark from `FaithHeart`: kept from its rites for
fifteen days, left out of the festival's gathering; set to carry the next offering, which they carry; or let be); *a
shrine nobody keeps* (a god's place whose god nobody at home holds: kept and swept, given to the god of the one asking,
who walks out and says the words, `Shrines.Ask`; or let fall, undedicated). Each answer plays out on the map
(`Tools/playout_audit.py` counts the new effects).

**C23, telling the bees** (`Immersion/TellingBees.cs`, `TellingBeesMath.cs`): when one of the colony dies, or someone new
joins, the one who tends the hives most (Alpha Bees' own beekeeping priority, then skill with animals; else the best with
animals) walks round up to four of Alpha Bees' beehouses (`RB_Beehouse`, `RB_AdvancedBeehouse`), stands a moment at each,
and tells them, one sentence at the first (`JobDriver_TellBees`). After a death the teller's grief eases a little
(`Rimfolk_Bees_Told`, +2 for two days); a journal line and a plain line in the news. No penalty if nobody goes: the news
waits three days and is let go. Under the small habits setting; never without Alpha Bees. Dev mode: "Bees: ...".

Harm: none (no wound, no fight, no illness; the rare gifts' weapons are the mod's own). Saved: `BetweenState` (scenes,
woodcutters, newcomers welcomed, fights and insults answered, sealed stones seen) and `TellingBeesBook` (news waiting,
newcomers told), each kept small and modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`; the vows' record and the offering's asked
carrier gain a field each. Not checked without the game: the happenings' timing at the colony's hours, the jobs' walking
and standing, the frog and the cat strays' leaving, the coat put on, the shrine taken up and the frames cancelled, the
drake's egg hatching as the colony's, Alpha Bees' hives reached.

### Text variety: the gods' thin pools (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.286.0)

The player on the content update: "In general, I just want additional God events, more immersion, more just further also
building up on the gods in general ... And then also, just variety". The gods' part of the second text round: C32 to C36
of `docs/content-update-proposals.md`, about 630 new lines and no line rewritten. The counts were taken again first, since
0.281.0 had added the gods' variety after the proposals were written. The gods stay unseen in all of it: a line names a
god only where its pool already does (by the colony's or the speaker's name for it), what people say is their own belief,
and nothing shows a favour, a want or a rule.

- **C32, the gods' own lines** (`Rimfolk_Gods.xml`): each of the fifteen has three more scoffers' answers (plain, and
  untagged, so they answer a gift, a sign or a wrath alike; 3 to 6), two more lines on what it is and two on how it is
  seen, told at the fire and set down in the book in the old voice ("{GOD} speaketh through the dryads, one word and then
  another"; 3 to 5 each, after the three already told in order), and three more lines for a neighbour's letter about its
  hand at the colony (2 to 5, Tamiu's 3 to 6), in the letters' flavour style and neutral about what the hand was.
- **C33, worship talk** (plain, but the vows and the pilgrimage in the life goals' style): each god's way of taking an
  offering has three more remarks (one for the one who holds that god, `mine`, one for anyone else, `theirs`, one for
  either) and one more for a scoffer, and the visitor given Ducat's gift three more (42 to 97); each presence four more
  remarks, one of them for when the colony is sure whose it is (90 to 150); each true dream two more (15 to 29). Every thin
  pool of the proposal's table brought to eight lines: the beast given, the precious gift asked, granted and refused, the
  gift answered, the pilgrim setting off and arriving, a place dedicated, a crisis of faith and its journal, the scoffer
  answered, the couple's bickering over the rain, a vow kept and broken, the words at a god's place; dread, a shrine lost,
  keeping away, rival devotees, the won-over's journal; the saints' statue, naming, words and remembering; the shared
  memory of a god seen, the god's beast beckoning, the stranger's thanks, Tamiu's stare, the visitor at a god's mark; and
  the festival on the calendar let pass, talked over and written up. The vow in `Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_Vow` was already at
  nine (0.281.0 added four). Of 0.281.0's own pools, the vows of a season said day by day (`Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_VowKeep`)
  had three lines a vow, said every day for fifteen days: brought to eight a vow. The happenings between the colony's
  people (`Rimfolk_Pool_GodBetween_Say`) say one to three lines at each beat of a scene, once a scene and scenes days
  apart, and their cards already come in three wordings: left for now.
- **C34, scripture in the old voice** (the player's "the only thing i don't mind and even enjoy, is old medieval writing
  ... especially the relitions", and the go on the whole list): 102 lines tagged `[olde]` beside the plain ones, every one
  in the old words ("Hear me, {GOD}, as thou hast heard our elders before us"), still saying plainly what it means: the
  prayers (36, for each moment and each god), thanks (14), a festival's rite (18, each domain), the words at a god's place
  (10), the saints' prayers (14) and their feasts (10). Who says them (`WorshipMath.OldVoice`, `Worship.OldVoice`): the
  priest, the keeper of the colony's book of the gods (`GodLore.Keeper`), a devout elder (sixty or more in human years),
  and a believer of a faith of the old ages (with Ideology, a faith another people of the bow and the spear or of the
  sword and the keep holds as its own); never a scoffer. `Worship.LineWith`, where every worship and saints' line is
  picked, adds the tag for them, so a tagged line can only reach them, and their moment's old line weighs more than its
  plain one; everyone else keeps the plain words. Each festival's `festivalDishes` is a phrase in the messages and the
  book, not spoken, and stays as it is.
- **The words at a god's place, a fix** (`DilemmaEffect_ShrineWords`): the council's answers that hold words at a god's
  place (a year begun for a god, a temple vowed, a rite, a shrine moved, swept or let go) drew their lines from
  `Rimfolk_Pool_Worship_RiteWords` through the gathering, which fills in no god, so its lines showed the god's
  placeholder. They are now filled in when the answer is given, for the one who leads them (`Worship.Lines`, in the old
  voice where they speak it), and the gathering says those.
- **C35, the gods' camps** (`Rimfolk_GodsWorld_Camps.xml`, the camps' flavour style): the pilgrims' camp and the hermit
  seer's each have eight arrival texts (4 and 3 before), eight lines over their heads (6 and 5) and eight words for their
  moments (the pilgrims' prayer and grief, 4; the seer's foretelling, 2). The seer still names no god.
- **C36, weather talk and the land's journals** (plain; `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Lines_LandMore.xml`, extensions of
  the pools): the lightning rod, the tornado's journal, the flinch at lightning, the record dry and wet spells, the warm
  spell and the forecasts of cloud, dust and a wrong one brought to eight plain lines (3 to 6 before, counting the
  everyday add-ons); and the journals of a pack's alpha brought down, the region's legend won over or brought down, a
  nemesis let go, a pet that stood guard, an animal asleep at the foot of the bed, an oath sworn against a beast, and the
  calendar's companion and first foal talked over, to eight (2 to 5 before). The herd's journals (the leader gone, its
  last season, the spring's first young, the new leader) and a pet's farewell, counted with their extensions since, were
  already at ten to twelve.

Tests: `Tools/Tests/WorshipTests.cs` (who speaks the old voice; the set beside the plain lines in each pool, each line in
the old words; the tag given in `Worship.LineWith`; the words at a god's place filled in). No new saved state, no harm.
Not checked without the game: how often each of the four says an old line rather than a plain one, and the words at a
god's place said by the one who leads them.

### The world brought home (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.280.0)

The player on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "your content proposal overall sounds really good. You can go ahead with
this in the order you think makes most sense ... more immersion ... the relations between pawns, the kind of events that
generated from it", and "first do all the integrations that you proposed in your document before we add additional
content variety". Built: B1, B2, B3, B23, B25, B26 and B32 of part B, the first of its integrations. The code is
`Source/ColonyCouncil/World/Home/` (`WorldHome.cs`: `WorldSeason`, `WorldSteer`, `RoadNews`, `WorldApart`, `GreatTaken`;
`WorldQuestions.cs`, `WorldScenes.cs`, `WorldHomeBook.cs`, `WorldHomeDebug.cs`); the pure rules `WorldHomeMath` (linked
into the tests); the saved state `WorldHomeBook` (a game component: the vows and the dyed clothes) and the world events'
own flags (kept apart, a side backed, a great one set down). Its hour is the world events' own (`WorldHome.Hourly`, from
`WorldSituations` at its tick): no new clock. Words in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_WorldHome.xml`.

- **B1, world events in the peoples' own ways.** `WorldSituationDef` has two new lists, `theirs` and `theirEnds`: a
  paragraph under the start letter, and one under whichever ending's letter, told only when the world event falls on one of
  Rimfolk's 23 peoples and a line tagged with that people's calling fits (`WorldSituationWorker.Theirs`, picked tagged
  only; an ending's key is the tag `end:KEY`, so a robbed caravan's line differs). Each of the 33 world events that prefer a
  people (the patches' `<calling>`) has one of each for its people; the six hard ones (plague, famine, hard winter, flood,
  great fire, mourning) have one for every people (205 lines, the world events' flavour style). A plague at the
  hospitallers' town fills their sickhouse and the priors ask for linen; a famine among the herding folk has herds sold at
  a loss and the elders eating last; the great fire takes the Kiln Guild's kilns. A line that names no calling is a
  config error (`WorldHomeMath.ForAPeople`).
- **B2, world events steer the quests and storylines offered.** `<rimfolk>` modifiers on 21 world events raise the home
  quests' and storylines' first parts that fit them (the plague the sickness storyline, the lent healer and the order's
  medicine; the drought the well; the bandit road, a bandit lord's fall and the warlord the raiders settling nearby and the
  outlaw; markets closed, a blood feud and a war between neighbours the two towns' quarrel; the great fire and the war the
  children from the burned village; the drovers, the great herds and the murrain the strayed herd and the sick animal; a
  holy year and a great pilgrimage the relic; a people in mourning the lost founder's grave; the assize the prisoner kept
  and the dispute judged; a great fair and a season of songs the musicians and the wedding piece; a year without a summer
  and a hard winter the seed grain kept cold). Such a first part is steered (`WorldSteer.For`): while it is cast, the
  world event's own people are four times as likely to be the ones who ask (`Arrivals.Friendly`,
  `MissionPeoples.Grateful`, `WorldSteer.Weight`); its lines are picked with `ws:KIND`, `wsdef:DEFNAME`, `ws:steered` and
  `ws:theirs` (at the asker's own people), and the lines written for the season (41 on 17 first parts, plain words) are
  preferred over the rest when one fits (`WorldSteer.Prefer`). `{WSNAME}` is the world event, `{WSPLACE}` where it is
  ("the region" when it has no place). The pace of one storyline at a time holds.
- **B3, messengers tell the road's news.** As a courier sets the bag down at the mailbag (or hands an answer over at the
  gate), and as the post rider, the mail run or any carrier drops the post's bag (`MailIn.Delivered`), a world event on
  their road (their own people's first, else the nearest whose place lies near the colony, near their town, or not far out
  of the way between: `WorldHomeMath.OnRoad`) is told, three times in four, in one sentence from `Rimfolk_CourierLines`
  tagged `[road]` with its kind or name and `[ws:theirs]` at their own town (44 lines): "The ford below Ashford is under
  water, I came round by the hill." Else their usual word. `{PLACE}`, `{NAME}`, `{FACTION}` are the world event's.
- **B23, what the colony is known for draws the quests and camps that fit it.** `RenownMath.Events` takes the quests and
  first parts of the proposal's table (healers the lent healer, the order's medicine and the sickness storyline; fighters
  the trainee, the outlaw, the camp guard and the Banner's muster; hosts the musicians, the dignitary and the festival;
  traders the factor's goods and the league's escort; makers the wedding piece, the smith, the glass apprentice and the
  journeyman's year; the faithful the relic, the shrine and the hostel's bread), and a new table, `RenownMath.Camps`, the
  camps (the field sickhouse, the travelling healer and the healers; the war party and a hired guard; players and
  minstrels; merchants from afar and the salt caravan; the smith; pilgrims and penitents), each by how far the name carries
  (`BandFactor`: a quarter more in a town's reach, to three quarters among the peoples; `CampKindDef.WeightNow` through
  `Renown.CampFactor`).
- **B25, encounters of the region's hard times.** `EncounterDef` has `situations` (world event kinds or defNames: only
  in their season) and `scene` (`WorldScenes`): what must be true on the map and plays out as it is told. Fourteen
  (`Defs/EncounterDefs/Rimfolk_Encounters_WorldTimes.xml`, plain): in a plague a visitor keeps their distance, and another
  asks after the fever; in a famine a hungry visitor slips food from the stores into their pack (`pocket`: food of the
  stores within twelve cells of them, one piece moved into their pack) and the colonist lets it go or tells them to keep it,
  and a trader looks for grain; in a drought a visitor asks where the water is; in a holy year or a great pilgrimage a
  pilgrim kneels at the colony's holy place (`kneel`: a god's place, a ritual focus, an altar or a shrine; they walk to it
  and kneel a while, `Rimfolk_WH_KneelAt`) and another asks a colonist's name to pray for; in a war between neighbours two
  visitors of the two sides share a fire (`sides`: one of each side near the same lit fire or running heater; both sit at
  it a while); with a comet a visitor and a colonist watch it (`sky`: night, both under the open sky); at a great fair a
  visitor shows a ribbon won; with the drovers or the great herds a drover's dog runs at the colony's hens and they scatter
  (`dog`: a dog of the visitor's group, the colony's hens; the dog runs, the hens flee); on the ice road or in a hard
  winter a carter with frostnipped hands warms them at the colony's fire (`warm`: a lit fire or a heater within twenty
  cells); in a season of songs a visitor hums the song about the colony (`hum`: a note over their head); in a mourning a
  visitor asks a colonist to say their dead's names. `{SITUATION}`, `{SITUATIONPLACE}`, `{SITUATIONPEOPLE}` name the
  world event (`WorldSeason.Fill`), `{B}` the other side's visitor.
- **B26, council questions the world brings home.** `DilemmaDef` has `situations` (only in their season,
  `DilemmaWorker.CanHappenNow`; asked before the rest in it, as a season's questions are). Five
  (`Defs/DilemmaDefs/Rimfolk_Dilemmas_WorldHome.xml`, the council questions' flavour style), each answer doing what it
  says: in a plague the colony's best doctor asks to keep apart from travellers while it lasts (`WorldApart`: the
  sickness at the gate and the couriers who arrive sick half as often, `WorldHomeMath.ApartChance` in `Harm/Carriers.cs`;
  no moments with visitors or traders; each group of them a point of goodwill cooler, the game's message saying why); in a
  holy year the most devout (the gods on: of a god they hold; else their faith) vows a vigil day each week while it lasts
  (`WorldHomeBook.vows`: each week, from the morning, most of the working day at their god's place, an altar, else the
  gathering spot, a `DilemmaEffect_Vigil` from code; once kept, belief in their god as for a vow kept, or their faith
  steadier, and `Rimfolk_WH_VigilKept`; at the end a word of how many were kept); in a war between neighbours a colonist
  with ties to one side (family among them, their people's good memory of them by name, a faith shared:
  `WorldHomeMath.SideTie`) wants the colony to back it, a friend of the other side objects, and backing a side sets the
  war's flag (`backFaction`, `backEnemy`) so that only that side's asks come (the other side's beats forbid it; goodwill
  +5 and -4); in a mourning everyone at home wears dark grey (`DilemmaEffect_WorldMourning`: each colonist's outermost body
  garment that takes a colour, its colour kept and put back when the mourning ends unless dyed since; goodwill +4 with the
  mourning people); at a great fair a fair day at home (a gathering with music from mid-morning and the day off for
  everyone).
- **B32, the region's great events in the colony's book of the gods, as the colony believes.** When a great world event is
  new (plague, comet, bumper harvest, great fire, a year without a summer, famine, flood, drought, hard winter, murrain:
  `WorldHomeMath.Great`), once within its first three days, nearly two times in three, the most devout of those who hold a
  god their people tie to it (`WorldHomeMath.GreatGods`: the fever Morel's or Undertow's, the comet Cirrus's or
  Selene's, the harvest Hollin's or Helios's...) says over their head whose doing it was, and the book keeps it as their
  belief in the gods' book's old voice ("The gray cough at Ashford came of the Soft Mother, and not of chance.",
  `CC_WH_Great_Belief_*`), under the name they call the god (an unknown god unnamed); another who takes it for another god
  says so beside them, and each holds their own the harder; one who believes none of it answers, and the book keeps the
  doubt (`GreatTaken`, as `SeasonGods` for a named season). Only who believes it: the gods stay unseen.

Decided here (open in the proposals): B1's "a line in the six hard ones" is one start paragraph for each of the 23 peoples
in each of the six, and the ending paragraphs are for the preferring world events (a flood's and a mourning's included);
a people's paragraph is added under the letter's own text rather than replacing it, so it always shows when one fits.
B2's steered people are four times as likely; the season's lines are preferred whenever one fits. B3 covers the couriers'
deliveries, the answers they bring and every carrier of the post's bag; three times in four. B25's fourteen are the
proposal's nine and five more of the same seasons; "lets it go or speaks" is two ways of telling one scene, the food in
their pack either way. B26's "keep the gate quiet" stays in the colonist's words only; the colours are what the answer
does. B32 takes ten great world events, not five.

Harm: none. Dev mode: "World home: ..." for each. Not checked without the game: the steered first letters in the
Quests tab, a dog's run and the hens' scatter, the visitors' kneeling and warming jobs under their lords, the dyed
clothes' colours and their return, how often each comes in a real colony.

### The region's years and the camps (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.280.2)

The content update's world integrations, part 3, with the same go as "The world brought home" ("first do all the
integrations that you proposed in your document before we add additional content variety"). Built: B5, B11, B13, B19
and B27 of `docs/content-update-proposals.md`, part B. The pure rules are `RegionPricesMath`, the region part of
`HamletMath`, `RaidersCampSignsMath`, `TakenInMath` and `CallsFromHomeMath` (linked into the tests,
`Tools/Tests/RegionYearsTests.cs`); the words are `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_RegionYears.xml`. No new clock: the
prices are read when a price is, the hamlet and the raiders' camp on their own day and hour, those taken in on the
region's hour (`RegionBook`).

- **B5, traders' prices follow the region's hard and good years** (`World/Region/RegionPrices.cs`). While a world event
  runs, every trader of its people (their caravans and visitors' traders on the colony's map, a caravan of the colony's at
  their town) asks and pays a quarter more for what it makes scarce: food in a famine, a blight, a locust year, a year
  without a summer or a drought; medicine in a plague or with medicine gone scarce; steel with iron gone scarce or in a war
  between neighbours; wood after a great fire or a flood, in rebuilding and during a great work; cloth and leather in a
  sickness of the herds or with the markets closed. In a bumper year their food is a fifth cheaper. A war between
  neighbours and closed markets touch both peoples (the event's `{ENEMY}` too). What a thing is comes from the game's own
  facts (medicine before food, so herbal medicine is no food; food people eat, not a drug or a corpse; the steel; woody,
  fabric and leathery stuff). It rides on the moot's season prices (`Patch_SeasonPrices`, 0.274.0): one factor on the
  price, the moot's (for every trader) times the region's (by the trader's people), kept within half and one and a half,
  so the two never pull against each other, and buying and selling move together as the moot's do. The price's hover in
  the trade window (the game's and Rimfolk's own, `Tradeable.GetPriceTooltip`) says why: "Food dear at Ashford (famine):
  25% more with the Ashford Union, buying or selling.", the other side of a war unplaced, and the moot's ruling too. With
  world events off nothing moves.
- **B11, the hamlet's hard seasons follow the region** (`World/Region/HamletLife.cs`, `HamletWords.cs`). The nearest
  running world event within 15 tiles of the hamlet's town (its own town, its tile, or its people's nearest town) that
  brings a need decides what a hard season's ask is for: a doctor in a plague; food in a famine, a blight, a locust year,
  a drought or a year without a summer; tools and timber (by the colony's age, as before) after a great fire, a flood or
  in rebuilding. With one near, the hamlet asks already below a fortune of 30 rather than 20 (help comes due a little
  sooner; the gap between asks holds). The letter opens with what happened ("The plague at Ashford has reached the families
  of Little Ford."), and once the help is out, their courier who comes to the gate for it says so aloud, once ("The fever
  at Ashford has put half of Little Ford in bed."). A bumper harvest near makes the harvest's carter bring half again as
  much, and the message says why. The ask's world event and place are saved on the hamlet (`hardEvent`, `hardWhere`,
  `wordUntil`).
- **B13, signs of the raiders' camp on the map** (`World/Region/RaidersCampSigns.cs`, `TakenIn.cs`).
  - Scouts: when a found camp's raid comes due, two of its people (its plainest fighters) come in at the map's edge on its
    side first, walk ten cells or so in, stand and look toward the colony for an hour or so (`Rimfolk_CampScoutWatch`,
    never the waiting job that strikes at a passer-by), then walk off; the message names the side. The raid follows an
    hour or two after they were first seen, from the cell they came in at, once they are gone, and its letter says so;
    held back by another fight it waits, and is given up half a day late. Hurt, the scouts leave at once and defend
    themselves as they go (the game's own leaving duty); they never start a fight. With no edge or scout to be had, the
    raid comes as before.
  - The runaway: once in a found camp's life, from its third day, a 5% chance a day: a captive who ran from it (one of a
    people at peace with the colony, likelier one at war with the camp's) comes in from the camp's side with two or three
    bruises, cuts and scratches from before, sits at the gate and asks for a bed (`Rimfolk_Evt_CampRunaway`, never from
    the storyteller). Taken in, they are the colony's guest, sent to a bed (or carried to one if they go down), tended by
    its doctors, and walk home well or after twenty days; their people think 6 better of the colony and remember it (the
    deed `rescued`, naming the doctor who tended them most when they leave), and the camp's next raid comes sooner (its
    mean days between raids halved once). Sent on, they limp off.
  - The smoke: at dusk (the 18th hour), every three days at most, half the time, someone of the colony out of doors by a
    wall, a fence or a door (the marshal first, then anyone drafted) says the camp's smoke is up again, and which way.
- **B19, camps' herds, dogs and goods from the full mod pool** (`Defs/CampDefs/`). `MayRequire` kinds beside the game's
  own in each list (the game's the fallback): Megafauna's aurochs, Alpha Animals' chameleon yak and thunderox in the herders', drovers' and
  calving camps; Vanilla Christmas Expanded's megareindeer in the herders' winter camp and among a snowbound caravan's
  beasts; Vanilla Animals Expanded's camel and Indian elephant as pack beasts; its German shepherd, beagle and French
  bulldog at a camp's heels (a camp's dog is now any that fits, not the first); one of its cats, or the game's, with the
  hermit. Goods, the mod's first and the game's after it (a camp's goods take the first that exists): the salt caravan's
  salt (Vanilla Cooking Expanded's, else pemmican) at its stall and, new for a camp, always in its trader's pack
  (`CampKindDef.traderGoods`, beyond its people's own stock); the herb-gatherers' tea leaves (Vanilla Brewing Expanded's,
  else berries); raw honey at the market's stall and in its trader's pack (Vanilla Factions Expanded - Medieval 2's or
  Alpha Bees', else berries at the stall). All checked by `Tools/poolcheck.py`.
- **B27, answer a call to arms from home** (`Diplomacy/CallsFromHome.cs`, `World/Region/TakenIn.cs`). A defense partner's
  call, a liege's call for levies and a creditor's call for fighters (`ChoiceLetter_CallToArms`) have two more answers,
  each greyed out with its reason when it can't be given:
  - supplies in place of fighters: 60 raw food (else 20 meals), 6 medicine and up to two spare weapons from storage (not
    biocoded, bonded or a relic), each carried out to the gate by the colony's people for their runners (the couriers);
    under fealty from the medieval age on, a season's tribute in silver in place of service, carried out the same way (a
    tribal colony sends supplies);
  - their wounded taken in: two to four of them come up the road a day to three later, hurt from their fight (gunshots
    from the industrial age on, cuts and stabs before it, and bruises; never so many that they can't walk in or would
    bleed out first), and lie in the colony's beds as its guests until well (`TakenIn`); their people remember the doctor
    who tended them most (the deed `tended`, once: the game's own count of a guest gone home is left out for them). Greyed
    out with nobody who can doctor.

  Either keeps the colony's word as a smaller kept word than fighters: the pact's call is cleared, the debt settled, the
  levies counted as sent, each remembered at half a fighter's weight (`keptWord` 5, `levies` 4) and written in the
  history.

Decided here (open in the proposals): B5's percents (a quarter dearer, a fifth cheaper) and its reach (every trader of
the world event's people, wherever the event is, since the proposal reads "by people"); the hover's words. B11's reach (15
tiles) and "a little sooner" (asks below 30, not 20); the carter's word comes from their courier at the gate when the
help is collected. B13's lead is an hour or two; the scouts are seen before every raid of a found camp; the runaway's
chance; "sooner" halves the mean days to the next raid once; the defense planner is not changed (the message and the
raid's letter name the side). B19's megareindeer also goes with the snowbound caravan; a camp's own trader goods are new.
B27's amounts; weapons only as many as there are; a pact's "smaller kept word" is half the deed; the wounded come a day to
three later and make for the beds themselves (a colonist carries anyone who goes down).

Harm: the runaway's and the wounded's injuries are from before they came, shown on their health; any who die do so by
the game's own rules, with a message. The scouts don't fight unless attacked; the raid is the camp's own, at its own
rate, a little sooner once after a runaway taken in. Dev mode: "Region's years: what moves the traders' prices now",
"Hamlet: a hard season's ask now" (follows a world event near it), "Hamlet: a hard season's ask in a region's hard
year...", "Raiders' camp: its scouts now (the raid follows them)", "Raiders' camp: a runaway at the gate now", "Raiders'
camp: the smoke at dusk, said now", "Taken in: ..." (who is in the beds, the wounded on their way come now, a call to
arms' wounded come now...), "Camps: one with the mods' beasts and goods here now...". Not checked without the game: the trade window's hover and the advice's marks with a moved
price, the courier saying the carter's word, the scouts' standing and walking off under their lord and the turrets' answer
to them, a guest's bed rest and going home (the game's own guest rules beside `TakenIn`'s), the camps' mod beasts in the
weather.

### The world's variety: new world events, camps and encounters (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.282.0)

The player on the content update: "just variety, further kind of events, camps, world events, normal storyteller events,
dilemmas, etc. ... So for the content update, yes, I want more events, camps, world events, and dilemmas, but first do
all the integrations that you proposed in your document before we add additional content variety." With the
integrations released (0.278.0 to 0.280.2), this is the first round of the variety for the world: B6, B7, B8, B15, B20,
B21, B24 and B28 of `docs/content-update-proposals.md`, part B, as proposed, and six world events and six camps more of
the lead's own choosing in the player's direction, each tied into what exists. The code is `Source/ColonyCouncil/World/
Variety/` (`VarietyWorkers.cs` the world events' workers, `GamesDay.cs`, `Pardon.cs`, `VarietyDebug.cs`), the camps'
ways `Camps/CampVariety.cs`, the singing `Diplomacy/FeastContests.cs` and `FeastSinging.cs`, the stud visit
`Missions/Workers_MissionStud.cs`; the pure rules `VarietyMath` (and FeastMath's hopes and singing; linked into the tests,
`Tools/Tests/WorldVarietyTests.cs`). Nothing new is saved: the world events' own flags, the camps' own state (the pickers'
roll, `CampWorkState`), the stud visit's mission record and the feast's plan carry it. Words: `Languages/English/Keyed/
Rimfolk_WorldVariety.xml`; the world events, camps and the council's question in their flavour style, the encounters,
the stud visit and the messages plain.

Every world event of this round takes its people's age as a tag (`SituationWorker_Variety`: [theirTribal],
[theirMedieval], [theirIndustrial], [theirSpacer]), so its names and letters have each age's form, and [bound] when its
people is bound to the colony by a tie (`PeopleTies.Bound`: a pact, a marriage, a ward, an envoy, fealty, a debt of
honour); one that prefers one of Rimfolk's peoples has a start and an ending paragraph in their ways (B1's `theirs` and
`theirEnds`). A world event's worker may now make it likelier for the moment (`WorldSituationWorker.WeightFactor`, read by
`WorldSituations.Weight`), and a camp kind's `situationKinds` may name one world event by its defName as well as a kind
(`CampKinds.Situation`).

- **B6, two more scarcities.** Cloth gone scarce (`Rimfolk_WS_ClothScarce`, kind scarcity) comes on its own, or three times
  as readily within 40 days of a sickness in the herds or markets closed, taking over that world event's people with
  [after:defName] lines (`SituationWorker_ClothScarce`). A tailor of theirs at the gate buys cloth at twice its worth or
  its plain worth; an old tailor teaches a colonist a way of making coats out of worn ones (a lesson at the gate, Crafting).
  Timber gone scarce (`Rimfolk_WS_TimberScarce`, kind scarcity) follows a great fire, a flood, rebuilding or a great work
  (`after`): timber bought dear (carried out, nearly twice its worth, or given), and a young carpenter's apprentice asks
  the colony's best builder for a day's teaching (a lesson at the gate, Construction). Shearers come more often while cloth
  is scarce, woodcutters while timber is (their `situationKinds`, by name); their traders pay more for cloth and leather,
  or wood, at their towns (B5's `RegionPricesMath`, as for iron and medicine).
- **B7, a season of games** (`Rimfolk_WS_Games`, kind games, spring to fall). A town within reach holds its games in its
  age's form: the gathering games, a tourney, an athletics meet, a league season. The region's best is one of theirs ({X},
  made for it and named in the ending). Travelling champions stop three times as often (`Council_Evt_Champion`), a games
  team camps on the road. The colony may hold a games day (`DilemmaEffect_GamesDay`, `GamesDay.cs`): two young people of
  the first people and one of the second (the event's `{ENEMY}`, at peace with both), or three of one, each with one or two
  friends (the feast's retinue), come in two days on the first fine morning for the feast's bouts, race and a shooting
  match where the colony has targets, eat at the colony's table and stay the night: a feast of its own purpose
  (`FeastPurpose.Games`: its own arrival and card words, no notables, no hopes). A colonist who wins a contest there is
  named in the games' ending ([ourWin], `GamesHooks` on `Feasts.StageChanged`) and counts it for their own name as any
  contest won at a feast. Not offered while guests are coming for another feast. Harm: the bouts' real blow at the feast's
  own rate, under the shared cap.
- **B8, a pardon proclaimed** (`Rimfolk_WS_Pardon`, kind pardon). After a kind new head (the succession's follow-up, its
  flag "kind"), or while a holy year runs (by that year's own people, [holyYear]; `SituationWorker_Pardon`). Outlaws walk
  home past the colony (on the road), one asks a meal at the gate (carried out to them). Only when the colony holds
  prisoners of theirs, they ask that those walk home under it: the wardens walk them out by the game's own release
  (`DilemmaEffect_PardonRelease`), so their people's goodwill and memory ("released") and the debt of honour that follows
  are the game's and Rimfolk's own. While it lasts no bounty hunters come and the outlaw quest is a third as likely; a camp
  of outlaws walking home may stop a night.
- **B15, the peoples' own encounters** (`Defs/EncounterDefs/Rimfolk_Encounters_Peoples.xml`). Two moments for each of the
  23 peoples (46): `StrangerRole.calling` picks a visitor (or their trader) of that people. One of each pair is their ways
  (the Waystone Book's ink, a hospitaller looking at a colonist's old injury, a herder looking over the colony's animals, a
  pilgrim standing at the colony's graves, a scholar at its books, a river-folk knot, a warden's rule, a sexton at the
  graves, a tamer and a colony animal, a Wheel salvager at a broken machine, a reader under the night sky, the Mossborn's
  count, a soldier comparing scars, a guild mason asking after a colonist's work, a linesman at the comms console, the
  union's vote, the census-taker's notebook, the crew's log, the Helix Works asking first, a Lattice mechanitor at a colony
  mech, a Choir listener humming, a vault dweller's old part), the other how their people began, as their descriptions tell
  it. Where a moment says the visitor does something, it is true on the map and plays out: five new scenes
  (`WorldScenes`: grave, broken, beast, mech, building, with the jobs `Rimfolk_PE_StandAt` and `Rimfolk_PE_LookOver`), the
  old ones (sky, hum), and a colonist's own state (an old injury, a passion, able to fight).
- **B20, beekeepers on the move** (`Rimfolk_Camp_Beekeepers`, spring and summer). Decided: they come only with Alpha Bees,
  whose beehouse is their hive (two set at the edge of the camp, built by them and taken with them); with VFE Medieval 2
  too, its honey and mead are among their goods. They tend the hives by day, sell honey, wax and mead at their stall, and on
  asks a crock of honey or their wax (the first of the mods' that exists), a colonist's afternoon at their hives (a job
  beside the beehouse, Animals, so the game's own bee-sting ailment comes at its own rule), and a queen (temperate, or
  woodland for a home among trees) only once the colony has Alpha Bees' basic beekeeping. Decided: no ask to keep fires and
  axes from the hives, as nothing on the map would hold it.
- **B21, mushroom and truffle pickers** (`Rimfolk_Camp_MushroomPickers`). In the fall, or within six days of the colony's
  own mushrooms after rain, by the woods (`needs` woods; `CampWorker_MushroomPickers`). Their gathering takes the land's
  caps first (`CampKindDef.gathers`: Vanilla Plants Expanded - Mushrooms' healtruffle, timbercap and glowcap, the caves'
  agarilux and bryolux), else what grows wild; they sell Alpha Animals' black truffles (else raw fungus) and raw fungus,
  with their truffle pig or dog. One stay in four, one of them eats a cap that looked right and wasn't: the game's food
  poisoning, on them, told, and they ask for the colony's doctor (the camps' own tend at their fire).
- **B24, a stud visit** (`Rimfolk_Mission_StudVisit`). A herding people (the herders preferred) asks the colony to let one
  of their animals stand in its pen for five to seven days, of a kind the colony keeps that the game breeds by mating
  (mods' kinds included; egg layers left out). Their male with the colony's females, or their female with the colony's
  male; while it stands it is the colony's, so the game's own mating pairs them. Theirs: if one of the colony's is
  pregnant by him when their drover comes back, the young is the colony's and their courier takes a fee (a seventh of his
  worth, 30 to 200). Ours: if she has taken, their courier brings one of the young to the gate once it is born (the rest of
  her gestation and a few days). By letter, the colony may ask them for silver for the keep instead (half the fee, no fee
  and no young owed). Dead or lost, it ends badly; bonded to a colonist, they leave it.
- **B28, a feast's guests hope for their own people's contest, and a singing contest.** By calling (`FeastMath.HopeOfCalling`):
  the hunt for the hunters, herders and grovekeepers; the bouts for the mercenaries, drillers, citizens and crew; the tables
  for the traders, brokers, scholars, artisans, seers, and (decided) the editors and mechanitors; the race for the
  salvagers, linesmen, tamers, and (decided) the fishers; a fine meal and music for the pilgrims, sextons, healers,
  listeners, and (decided) the vault's folk. Any other people hopes by its age, the Empire by its own ways. The singing
  (`ContestKind.Singing`): up to six singers, guests and colonists in turn, each sings one song at the colony's instrument
  (the game's or a mod's, its own music playing while they sing) or, without one, by a fire, each with a word as they start;
  the best by Artistic and half Social, two more for an instrument, and up to four of luck. It answers a hope of music, as a
  concert does, and a neighbour's feast of such a people holds one.

Six world events more (`Defs/WorldSituationDefs/Rimfolk_WS_Variety5.xml`):
- **A hiring fair** (kind hiring, spring and fall): the young of the region walk past to find places (the gathering of the
  young, a hiring fair, a labour exchange, a crew call), one asks at the gate whether the colony has a place (taken in, or
  sent on); the young hands camp on the road; the peoples' own ways of hiring.
- **A town's founding day** (kind jubilee): a people at peace keeps the day its town began; a runner asks a gift for it
  (silver carried out), good wishes, or, when the town is within three tiles, a colonist who goes to sit at it (away two
  days); each of the 23 peoples tells how its ways began, in a start and an ending paragraph, as its description has it.
- **The roads gone to mud** (kind mud, spring, the road league preferred): caravans and visitors fewer; a carter sells a
  load of potatoes that would spoil for half its worth (paid and set down at the gate); travellers stuck by the mud ask two
  nights indoors; carters sit it out in a camp on the colony's land.
- **Falling stars** (kind stars, the Stormglass Conclave preferred): a finder sells a piece of a fallen star at the gate
  (star-iron for a colony of the old ways, plasteel for a later one); star-watchers camp under the colony's sky; the
  colony's believers take it for a god's doing (one of B32's great events, Cirrus or Selene, in the book as they believe
  it); a council question asks for a night out under the stars (a gathering outdoors).
- **The great burying** (kind burial, the Quiet Bell preferred): a flood opens an old battlefield and its people bury the
  dead; a sexton asks linen for the shrouds (cloth carried out); when the colony has unburied enemy dead on its land,
  sextons with their beast ask to take them (the undertakers' own load and carry, `DilemmaEffect_BuryingTake`).
- **The bridge down** (kind bridge, the river folk preferred): travellers go the long way round past the colony; timber for
  the new bridge bought dear or given; travellers rest a night by the wall; carters camp; wood is dear at their towns.

Six camps more (`Defs/CampDefs/Rimfolk_CampKinds_Variety4.xml`):
- **Hands on the road** (with a hiring fair): young people walking to find places, a night or two; they work for their
  supper (most will hire), one may stay.
- **Stranded carters** (spring and fall, ten times as often in the mud or with a bridge down): they wait out the road and
  sell from their load; the colony can send hot meals over.
- **Gleaners** (fall, more in a hungry year, drawn by a generous colony): a family asks to walk the colony's harvested
  rows (three of them in the fields for a couple of hours); the colony can send a sack of food.
- **A games team** (with the games): young people training on their way; a colonist can train with them (Melee).
- **Outlaws walking home** (only with a pardon): a night's camp on the way home; food for the road.
- **Star-watchers** (with falling stars or a comet): they lie out under the open sky from dusk to one and sleep by day
  (`CampWorker_StarWatchers`); a colonist can watch with them in the evening (Intellectual).

Harm: the games day's bouts at the feast's own rate; a sting now and then for a colonist at the beekeepers' hives by the
game's own ailment; a picker's food poisoning on them, one stay in four, shown. Nothing else new hurts anyone.

Dev mode: "World variety: start one of the new world events now...", "... one of the new camps here now...", "... a
people's own encounter now...", "... a stud visit offered now", "... the stud visit's days up now", "... what the pardon
would cover here (log)"; the feast's own "a feast with a people's notables, set for today..." holds the singing among its
contests. Not checked without the game: the games day's young people at the gate and in the contests, the pardon's walk
out, the new scenes' jobs on visitors under their lords, the beehouses built and taken down by the beekeepers, a colonist's
sting at them, the pickers' preference among the caps, the poisoned picker's ask, the star-watchers' nights, the stud's
mating and the young one's arrival, a singer at an instrument with its music, and how often each comes in a real colony.

### Text variety: the world's thin pools (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.287.0)

The player on the content update: "your content proposal overall sounds really good. You can go ahead with this in the
order you think makes most sense ... And then also, just variety, further kind of events, camps, world events, normal
storyteller events, dilemmas, etc. Just more of them." Text round 2, the world's part: B9, B10, B16, B18 and B30 of
`docs/content-update-proposals.md`, part B, as written there, each marked **Built** there with what was decided. Every
pool was recounted first, since 0.282.0 had added ten world events, eight camps and 46 encounters after the proposals
were counted; those of 0.282.0's as thin as the ones named were brought to the same floor. Words only, apart from one
small fact for B10. The world events' letters and the camps' arrivals, joins and help in the flavour style CLAUDE.md
keeps for them; talk, the camps' bubbles and the encounters plain, one sentence a line where said aloud. New lines only:
no old line was changed.

- **B9, more ways to begin and end** (`Defs/WorldSituationDefs/`). The 17 named world events and five of 0.282.0's
  (falling stars, the great burying, the bridge down, the roads gone to mud, timber gone scarce): start letters to four,
