  each beat of one line a second, ending lines to three (an ending of one line a second). The new start letters go by
  their people's age ([theirLowtech], [theirHightech], and the newest's [theirTribal] and the like) or the season, so a
  steelworks is never a medieval people's and a rockfall in the pass never a spacer's; a beat with no words (an arrival
  or the game's own incident alone) keeps none. Every beat line says what the map shows: the patrol at the gate, the
  finder with the case, the carter with the empty cart. 82 lines.
- **B10, talk of the world events nobody mentioned** (`Defs/OutsiderTalkDefs/Rimfolk_OutsiderTalks_WorldTold.xml`). The
  twelve named (Blight, ColdYear, DryLaw, GreatCaravan, GreatWork, Legend, MedicineScarce, NeighborsWar, NewTownMet,
  SonBand, TownRaid, Trek), famine, plague and a hard winter, and all ten of 0.282.0's, which had none either: three
  pieces each, 75. One for a visitor whose own people it is (`ws:DEFNAME`, `situation:theirs`), one for a visitor of
  another people (`heard:ws:DEFNAME`), one once it is over (`ended:ws:DEFNAME`, said by its own people, or by anyone for
  one of the region's own). A visitor of another people knew of no world event but their own and the region's (the facts
  skip another people's, `Facts.Situations`), so the piece for them needed a fact: the newest world event of another
  people now gives `heard`, `heard:bad` or `heard:good`, `heard:ws:DEFNAME` and {HEARD}, {HEARDPLACE}, {HEARDPEOPLE}
  (`FactsMath.SituationRank`, `FactsMath.Heard`, `FactsMath.AddHeard`, tested in `Tools/Tests/FactsTests.cs`), news from
  the road, at most 1.2 current against their own's 3. Nothing else reads it, so no old piece is said differently.
- **B16, each people's own talk** (`Rimfolk_OutsiderTalks_PeoplesDays.xml`, `_PeoplesDays2.xml`). Six pieces more for
  each of the 23 peoples (138): their working day, food and drink, their young, their town (`town`, {TOWN}), the other
  peoples and the colony as they see it. The other peoples by the real relations in the save, with the conditions the
  talk already has and no new code: their war (`their:war`, {WAR}; `war:ourfoe` when their foe is the colony's too), a
  peace of theirs made lately (`their:peace`, {PEACEWITH}) or at war with nobody who counts (`!their:war`), each turn's
  alternatives kept apart so the piece follows one branch. The colony as they see it by their regard (`likesus`, `wary`)
  and what is true (`small`, `colony:animals`, `their:ahead`). A line that names a tool or a weapon of one age has the
  other age's form ([their:lowtech] pike and crossbow, else the guns), as a people's age changes at its own pace. The
  founding stories were left alone (done in 0.277.2).
- **B18, the peoples' own camps, fuller words** (`Defs/CampDefs/Rimfolk_CampKinds_PeopleEvents*.xml`). The 26 camps to
  four arrival texts, two joins, nine bubble lines, and two help texts and six moment lines where those are said: a help
  told in the camp's own words (tales, milk, fish, show; medicine, wood, mend and meat are told by the shared lines, so
  a kind's own line for them never shows), a moment its camp's ways say (`SayMoment`). The enclave's pad and the Banner's
  company give no help (`helpChance` 0); the field sickhouse's moments are never said, its round and gift being a
  farewell walk's and a left gift's it doesn't have. The eight camps of 0.282.0 (`_Variety4.xml`) to the same floor for
  arrivals, joins and bubbles; of their moments only the carters' mending and the games team's kill are ever said, so
  only those got more. New arrival texts say nothing of cold or snow, which the colony's land may not have in winter, and
  name gear only where the people's own gear has it (the Circuit's sashes, the Line's oilskins, the vault's numbers).
  26 camps: arrivals 56 to 105, joins 26 to 52, help 27 to 51, bubbles 132 to 234, moments 102 to 154.
- **B30, the thinnest encounters** (`Defs/EncounterDefs/`). Two texts more for each of the 25 named, by season, weather
  and time of day where they cross them, and for each of the 46 peoples' own encounters of 0.282.0 (all at two): 142.
  Where an encounter plays out a scene, the new text tells that scene and no more (a herder at one of the colony's
  animals, a pilgrim or a sexton at a grave, a scholar at the books, a salvager at the broken machine, a reader under the
  open sky, a linesman at the comms console, a mechanitor at a mech, a listener humming).

Found and left as they were, for the lead: the help lines of a kind's own for medicine, wood, mend and meat are never
shown (`CampCarry`, `CampLife.DoHelp` and `CampRequests.MendGear` tell those by the shared lines `CC_Camp_Help_*`): the
pilgrims' hostel's [medicine], the boat-builders' [wood], the Wheel's yard's [mend] and all eight of 0.282.0's camps'
help lines; and moment lines no code says: the hostel's [gift], the field sickhouse's [round] and [gift], and the
[carry] and [gift] lines of six of 0.282.0's camps (no camp good of theirs is carried out, none leaves a gift). Routing
them through `HelpText` would show some lines that claim more than happens (the travellers' herbs, the boat-builders'
logs carried over), so it was not done here.

Nothing new is saved. Not checked without the game: how the new lines read among the old in a real colony; a visitor of
a third people speaking of another people's world event (the fact is read by the talk as any other); the other-peoples
pieces with a people at war with a rough people, at peace with all, and just after a peace.

### Four small asks (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.222.0)

- **Decrees rest less:** every decree waits 70 % of its own rest before it can be declared again (`DecreeMath.CooldownShare`,
  `RestDays`, never under a day), and the colony's understanding lets off from that as before.
- **Builders leave trees to the cutters** (`Building/BuildersTrees.cs`, `BuildersTreesMath`): a tree in the way of a
  blueprint or frame a builder took on themselves is marked with the game's own cut mark and the builder goes on to
  another build; they cut it themselves when no other build is free, nobody at the home has plant cutting on, the player
  ordered the build, or it has waited marked half a day. Only trees; only builds; behind the deep hooks setting.
- **Ratings on Deep Storage's contents** (`Weapons/StorageContentsRatings.cs`): LWM's Deep Storage "Contents" tab (weapon
  racks, lockers, cabinets) gets the gear tab's rating badge and card button at the end of each weapon and apparel row,
  read by name and standing down without the mod; the gear tab's settings cover it.
- **Medics carry medicine** (`Health/MedicKits.cs`, `MedicKitsMath`; setting "Medics carry medicine"): every six hours the
  best few medics of each home (by Medical, doctoring on; one up to four colonists, two up to eight, three beyond) are
  given the game's own carry medicine: two or three of herbal or industrial, whichever the home can spare most of, the
  glitterworld kind kept home, never below one a colonist (four at least) and two for each one sick. A stock the player
  set is left alone for good; Rimfolk's is put back when someone stops being one of the medics. Said once a medic.

### A guest may join when the council says so (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.226.1)

An event's "join the colony" (`DilemmaEffect_Recruit`) takes a Hospitality guest in like anyone else: the council's
answer comes before the guest tab. It goes through Hospitality's own recruiting (`GuestWill.RecruitNow`, past the
council's own objection, no goodwill price of its own), so the guest's stay closes as its Recruit button closes it; without
that method, the guest leaves its guests' lord and is recruited by the game. The right-click "Invite" stays Hospitality's
for its guests.

### Ways to play: eight storytellers and the story direction (the player's request, 12 November 2026; released 0.227.0)

**Raids at the classic pace (the player, 12 November 2026, after 0.227.0: "many of the storytellers reduce raids, which is
not necessary").** Every way's big and small threat cycles run at Cassandra's own (on 4.6 days, off 6): The Long Road,
Neighbours and Lean Years no longer lengthen the quiet; What You Sow's deeds no longer thin the raids
(`StoryWaysMath.DeedThreatAccept` is 1, the deeds decide who comes through the raid reasons); Crossroads' raids no longer
thin by wealth (raid points still grow with it). Old Powers keeps its stranger threats (now about every 40 days) and runs
its raids a little slower (off 7.3) so the two together stay at the classic pace. The Turning Year and Rise and Fall
shape the pace over the year and the arc around the classic mean, as before. Released 0.227.1.

The player: "i'd like you to create new and interesting storytellers. that can enhance existing or make up new ways to
play the game & directions", then "if they don't have an image that's totally fine, and they also don't have to be this
"character" with a name etc., i find that strange anyways", then "halt the current tasks to do the storytellers first!".
Of the ten proposed (docs/storytellers-proposals.md), "leave out small hours, the frontier": eight are built, as
storytellers and as a direction over any storyteller. And the rule that binds every one of them: "but the storytellers
will still always include a chance for any kind of event, right? not that i lock myself out of some of them".

**What a way is.** A StorytellerDef on the game's `BaseStoryteller` (its endgame and DLC quests, the deep drill, the
anima and polux trees, Gauranlen pods, the monolith, and whatever other mods patch onto it, Medieval Overhaul's
mineshaft among them), with the game's own difficulty settings, named for what it does, no character and no portrait:
a plain plate with its name on Rimfolk's ground (`Tools/make_storyteller_plates.py`: 580 by 620, the size the game draws
it, and 228 by 244 for the list, twice its size). Its parts are the game's own comps tuned to its way, Rimfolk's own
comps where the game's can't say it (below), and a `StoryWayExtension`: Rimfolk's levers on its own happenings, a shape
(the seasons, the colony's deeds, the long arc), kinds of world situation it leans to, kinds of everyday hurt it leans
to. Each description says plainly how it plays and ends "It shifts the odds this way but shuts nothing out: every kind of event
can still come."

**The levers** (`Story/StoryLevers.cs`, `StoryWaysMath.Keys`), each a factor on Rimfolk's own rate, read through
`StoryDirection.Factor(key)`: the direction's when one is chosen in the settings, else the storyteller's when it is one
of Rimfolk's, else 1 (the raids' reasons 0). The season, the deeds or the arc shape it as the way is
(`StoryWaysMath.Combine`). The seams:

| Lever | What it moves | Where |
|---|---|---|
| visitors, challenges, pasts, nature, fights | Rimfolk's events by group (fights: those that may end in one) | `HappeningTracker.StorytellerFactor` (the storyteller's pools) and `Weight` (Rimfolk's own timer), by `StoryDirection.HappeningFactor` |
| camps | a camp on an open morning | `TravelLand.CampChance` |
| traders | trading camps among the camps; a town's market caravans | `CampTracker` (the kind's pick), `Dealings.MarketHour` |
| letters | the world writing first | `WorldWrites.Daily` |
| favours | debts called in; a people's call to arms | `FavourAsks.Daily`, `CallsToArms` |
| missions | Rimfolk's missions in both pools | `MissionPool.Factor` |
| situations | how soon the next world event (and, by `SituationFactor`, which kinds: three times the weight for a leaned kind) | `WorldSituations.Interval`, `Weight` |
| gods | the gods' doings that hurt no one (pilgrims, seers, invitations, envoys, quarrels, asks, blessings, gifts) and a god's visit to a mark | `GodWorld.Lean` at those callers, `GodMarks`; wrath, a god's beasts and lightning, the void's hunger and a holy war keep `GodWorld.Factor` |
| arcs | a personal story beginning | `ArcTracker.TryStart` |
| memory | the size of a deed the peoples remember | `FactionMemory.Note` |
| allies | a people at peace sending fighters | `WarCamps.Hourly` |
| schemes | a scheme against the colony | `Schemes.Daily` |
| raidReasons | the share of the storyteller's raids sent without a people that come from the one with the most reason | `Patch_Story_RaidReasons` on `IncidentWorker_RaidEnemy.TryResolveRaidFaction` (with the deeper hooks) |
| joiners, beasts, finds, feasts, performers, arms | Rimfolk's events by their kind (15 November 2026; the section below): someone may join (`addsPeople`), and the kinds a def `leans`; beasts also the colonists' moments with animals, feasts the steward's feast, arms a people's call to arms | `StoryDirection.HappeningFactor`, `EncounterTracker.HourAt`, `Feasts.Daily`, `CallsToArms.PactHour` |

The everyday hurts: a way's `harmLean` tilts the shared budget's weight toward its kinds (`Harm.Reckon`, the tilt in
the shared weight and in each pass), so the hurts move between kinds and their total stays the budget.

**Two rules.** A way leans toward something and shuts nothing out: no lever, shape or share of a storyteller
part goes below `StoryWaysMath.Floor` (a quarter); the raids' reasons are a share of who comes, never more than
`MaxRaidReasons` (0.85), and only from a people that could have come anyway; every incident category of the game and
the player's mods keeps a route under every way (the tests check each def against docs/player-mods: ThreatBig,
ThreatSmall, Misc, FactionArrival and OrbitalVisitor beyond the named arrivals, at 25 and 40 days, AllyAssistance,
GiveQuest, ShipChunkDrop, both diseases, the Settlers' LTS softly at 60 days; Special, DeepDrillInfestation and
EndGame_ShipEscape by their named parts, Council_WorldEvent by Rimfolk's timer, GR_HybridRaid by its mod's code), and
no comp disallows an incident by def, tag or category (only the raid beacon's map keeps its own raids, as the game's
own storytellers do). Harm keeps the game's own rate: a lever on what hurts (fights, schemes) is never above 1, a shape
that moves it about over a year or an arc averages 1 or less, each way's big threats come at the classic pace or less
over a year, an arc or the worst deeds, its sickness about as often as the game's own.

**Rimfolk's own parts** (`Story/StoryComps.cs`): `WayCycle` (the game's on-off cycle, its share of the peak by the
shape: the Turning Year's seasons 0.3, 0.55, 0.75, 1; What You Sow's deeds 0.65 kind to 1 cruel; Rise and Fall's arc
0.45, 0.6, 1 for a war or 0.7, 0.3; and Crossroads' threat points, half to all), `WayDisease` (the game's sickness, its
chance moved by the shape and the same over a year: spring 2.2, the rest 0.6; Rise and Fall's plague trouble 2.6),
`WayPicks` (named happenings about every so many days, by season, phase and trouble, the last one a tenth as likely
for 20 days), `WayVisits` (the game's faction interaction by the shape: traders in autumn, by the deeds, by the arc;
a quarter at least), `WayOmen` (Rise and Fall's word of the trouble: a world situation of its kinds a few days into the
omens, `OmenDay`, once an arc, when one may start). Nothing is saved: the season, the deeds (the peoples' memory, good
turns against wrongs, read once a day) and the arc (days since settling, its trouble set by the world's seed, never
the same twice running) are read when asked.

| Way | Its parts (besides the game's caravans, quests, misc, sickness, orbital traders and the stranger in black) | Rimfolk's levers |
|---|---|---|
| The Long Road | big and small threats 4.6 days on, 9.4 off; caravan meetings every 6 days and small threats every 12 on the road; quests every 8 days, one or two; travellers 9, traders 6 a year | visitors 1.2, camps 1.5, traders 1.2, letters, favours and missions 1.6, situations 1.3; roads, towns, rushes, tolls; hurts: on the road and at the gate |
| Neighbours | threats 4.6 on, 7.4 off; friends sent in danger 25 a year; visitors 6 | visitors 1.4, letters 1.5, favours 1.6, memory 1.25, allies 1.8, situations 1.2, fights 0.8, raidReasons 0.85; feuds, wars, courts, creeds, levies, exiles, sellswords; hurts: the hated trader, the guest of rank, a challenge, the gate |

From the player's own mods, softly (`MayRequire` on each pick's incident, checked by poolcheck against docs/player-mods'
active rows), only events their own mods fire by chance: Vanilla Events Expanded (crops sprouting, drought, whiteout,
scorch, long night, psychic hum, stimulation and bloom, meteor shower), Seasonal Weather (wildfire), Vanilla Plants
Expanded - Flowers (weeds), Alpha Biomes (acid rain), A RimWorld of Magic (mana surge and storm), Vanilla Races
Expanded - Archon (psychic storm). Left out on purpose: Odyssey's drought (fired by hand, never by chance), Ideology's
skylantern (a ritual's), Anomaly's harbinger tree (the monolith's), Royalty's mech cluster (not uncanny), Alpha Animals'
eclipse and the blood moon (no chance of their own), Factional War's assault (a battle on the home map: harm).

**The direction** (`CouncilSettings.storyDirection`, a dropdown on What's on, "Story direction": none or one of the
fourteen, a note per choice) leans any storyteller with the way's levers, its shape, its world situations, its hurts and
its raids' reasons; the storyteller keeps its own parts and pace. With one of Rimfolk's as the storyteller, a direction
chosen leans instead of the storyteller's own. Both apply at once in a running game.

**Old Powers and the gods.** The gods are unseen: the way only leans the world toward the uncanny. Its description,
note and Almanac line never name or explain a god; the gods' own doings that hurt no one come more often, the rest at
their own rate.

**Balance** (`Tools/Balance -- --storytellers`, 400 runs, the game's wealth-by-time and points curves for six
colonists): big threats a year in the first year and the two after, against the classic storyteller's 7.4 and 8.2:
The Long Road 5.9 and 6.2, Neighbours 6.4 and 7.5, The Turning Year 7.9 and 8.1, What You Sow 5.1 and 5.7 kind, 6.4
and 7.0 of no name, 7.2 and 8.0 cruel, Old Powers 7.3 and 7.7 (with 7.1 and 7.8 omens and strange happenings), Lean
Years 5.2 and 5.6 (with 7.6 and 8.0 hardships), Rise and Fall 6.9 and 8.3 (the trouble's year), Crossroads 3.8 and 5.7;
sickness 0.6 to 1.1 a year against the classic 0.8 and 1.1; traders from 2.2 (What You Sow, cruel) and 2.3 (Lean
Years) to 11 and 12 (Crossroads) against 4.6 and 5. A way above the classic pace over the years fails the run.

**What only the game can show**: the storyteller screen with the plates, each comp's firings in a real colony
(Rimfolk's parts follow the game's own rules, checked by the tests and the balance tool but not run in the game), the
raid aimed by reason and its letter's line, the omen's world situation, and the direction changing a running game.

### Six more ways to play, and Rise and Fall a year each way (the player's request, 15 November 2026; released 0.253.0)

The player: "I would like to have some more additional storytellers and perhaps also improving potentially the one we
already created ... I like to kind of change the storyteller up every now and then. So if something like this is
integrated, then only think of maybe a season as the biggest time frame ... I'm not really looking for some with fewer
rates. You can always just use the base rate level, and the description should be kind of informative about what the
impact is"; then "rise and fall, just do 1 year rise and 1 year fall ... And the turning year you can leave as it is.
And I like all the new proposals, storytellers"; and the go, "alright, i'd like the storytellers and fixes/small
improvements". The Turning Year and the other seven's levers are as they were (whether the eight's below-base levers go
back to base was answered on 19 November 2026: the section "The storytellers' levers below the base rate" below).

**The six** (`StoryWay.OpenGate` to `FeastDays`, added at the end of the enum so saves and settings keep the first
eight's numbers; `StoryWaysMath.AtBaseOrMore`; `listOrder` 69 to 74; their plates by `Tools/make_storyteller_plates.py`).
Each is a whole storyteller on `BaseStoryteller` with every part the eight have (every kind of event routed, nothing
disallowed but the raid beacon's own map), and stricter rules, which StoryWaysTests holds them to: every lever 1 or more,
the harm levers exactly 1 and no raid aimed by reason; no shape (nothing longer than a season: no `WayCycle`,
`WayDisease`, `WayVisits` or `WayOmen`, no pick held to a season or a phase); the big and small threats on the classic
cycle exactly (4.6 days on, 6 off), the game's own sickness, traders, visitors, travellers and friends at the classic
storyteller's numbers or more; their picks never a threat (no predators, maddened animals or raids by name). What they
change is how often their own kind of thing comes:

| Way | Its own parts (beside the classic ones) | Rimfolk's levers and world events |
|---|---|---|
| Open Gate | joiners every 10 days (`WayPicks`: the wanderer, the refugee pod, the wild man, Royalty's wanderer with abasia, Vanilla Events Expanded's wild men, Vanilla Gravship Expanded's escape pod, Hospitality's happy guest who joins), weighed by the game's sense of how many people the colony should have; quests every 20 days (`WayQuests`: Royalty's guests who stay and join and refugees to shelter, the downed refugee); visitors 6 a year | visitors 1.3, joiners 2.5 |
| Home and Hearth | none | arcs 2, pasts 2, challenges 1.6, feasts 2 |
| The Wilds | the land's animals every 6 days (herds, thrumbos, farm animals, self-taming, ambrosia; Vanilla Events Expanded's caravan and battle animals and wild crops; Alpha Animals' behemoth; Vanilla Animals Expanded - Endangered's extinct animals; PokéWorld's herds and young) | nature 1.8, beasts 2.5; herds, beast, drove |
| Windfalls | what falls every 8 days (cargo pods, ship chunks, a meteorite; Vanilla Events Expanded's apparel and weapon pods); ruins found every 30 days (Go Explore's lost city, Real Ruins' pristine ruins); quests every 15 days (the item stash, Ideology's ancient complex, Real Ruins' abandoned base, Odyssey's gravship wreckage, orbital stash and orbital wreck) | finds 2.5; wreck, ruins |
| Sellswords | quests every 15 days (the bandit camp, Royalty's mission against one, Vanilla Factions Expanded - Settlers' wanted outlaw, Medieval 2's skirmish and siege camp, A RimWorld of Magic's arcane bandits, Empire's deserters' hideout); Go Explore's prison camp every 40 days | arms 2.5; sellswords |
| Feast Days | none | feasts 2.5, performers 2.5; fair, moot, harvest, songs |

**The new levers** (`StoryWaysMath`: `Joiners`, `Beasts`, `Finds`, `Feasts`, `Performers`, `Arms`; `StoryLevers`;
`LeanKeys`). Rimfolk's events say their kind: `HappeningExtension.addsPeople` (someone may join) and the new
`HappeningExtension.leans` (a list of `beasts`, `finds`, `feasts`, `performers`, `arms`; a config error names any other).
`StoryDirection.HappeningFactor` takes the group's lever times the strongest lever of its kinds
(`StoryWaysMath.HappeningLean`, within the floor and three times; an event of two kinds counted once; one that may end
in a fight still takes the fights lever alone). Tagged (70 events and missions): beasts 29 (the great beast and its
young, the strange creature, the omen beast, the rut, the birds' return, the thirsty herd, orphaned young, the wild one
at the pens, strays, the herd crossing, the wild one, the clutch, hunt or tame, the herders' young beast, the lame
beast, the egg-trader, the tamer's bout and stray, spring calving, the drove crossing and drovers, the animal doctor,
the Wardens' hunt, the rare Pokémon, the runaway, a young beast to raise, the Circuit's foal); finds 20 (the treasure
map, the buried cache, the sealed crate, lost cargo, the crashed drone, the door in the hill, the old map, star iron,
starfall, a child's and a pet's find, the wild harvest, an inheritance, and the gifts: food from the allies, help from
old friends, an old debt repaid, old friends' seed, kindness repaid, the plague's thanks, the first harvest shared);
feasts 9 (the camp's feast, the harvest fair, the table game, the gambler, a wedding at the colony, the ice fair, the
longest night, a neighbour's great day, a town's day); performers 6 (the storyteller, the players, the fiddler, the
spirit-singer, the fortune teller, the play about the colony); arms 6 (the champion, the rematch, the wanted prisoner,
the Banner's squad, the Republic's call, the Banner's muster). Left out on purpose: the pen raider (a predator), the
old shell and the twitching scrap (harm), the signal (a lure), the rich seam (the deep's nests). Other seams: beasts
also the encounters with pets and calm wild animals (`EncounterTracker.HourAt`, their hourly chance); feasts the
steward's suggestion of a feast with guests (`Feasts.Daily`, the roll over the lever; still once a season, with offices
on); arms a people's call to arms (`CallsToArms.PactHour`, `ArmsDaily` times favours times arms).

**Rimfolk's two new parts of a storyteller** (`Story/StoryComps.cs`). `WayPicks` now weighs each pick by the game's own
population factors (`IncidentChanceFactor_CurrentPopulation`, `IncidentChanceFactor_PopulationIntent`; 1 for the
eight's picks, none of which brings people) and comes only that share of the time (`StoryWaysMath.PickAccept`, the sum
after against the sum before, never past every time), so Open Gate's joiners thin out as the game's own do for a
colony it thinks big enough. `WayQuests` (new): about every `mtbDays` one of its named quest scripts (soft by
`MayRequire`) that is a natural random quest the game can run now (`QuestScriptDef.CanRun`), by its weight times the
game's own (`NaturalRandomQuestChooser.GetNaturalRandomSelectionWeight`: points, earliest day, refire, recency), one
that brings people times the game's own share for it (`PopulationIncreasingQuestChance`, a third counting as every
time), fired as the game's own `GiveQuest_Random` with `parms.questScriptDef` set: offered, accepted or not, played and
ended as any random quest.

**Rise and Fall a year each way.** The arc stays 120 days; the rise is its first year (`GrowthEnd` = `YearDays` = 60,
growth throughout), the fall its second: 20 days of omens (the trouble's word a few days in, `OmenDay` 2 to 10), 20 of
trouble, 20 of rebuilding at its end (`OmenEnd` 80, `TroubleEnd` 100; `StoryWaysMath.FallYear`). Its tables are as they
were; over the arc its threats average 0.50 of the peak (the test's 0.4 to 0.6, the classic pace or less), sickness 0.93
of the game's own (0.9 to 1.05), fights 0.82 and schemes 0.87. Its description says it plainly ("one year of growth,
then one year of trouble").

**The Almanac's page** ("ways to play", keywords unchanged) explains how a storyteller works (parts as clocks for kinds of
event, each drawing from every event of its kind by its own chance, so a mod's events come with their kind) and how
every kind keeps its chance (the base storyteller, a route for each kind with the rare kinds' long clocks, nothing
forbidden, the levers' floor and ceiling, harm at the game's rate, raids aimed at most 85%), a table of all fourteen,
and a section for each. The old number 55 (the growth's old length) is gone from it on purpose.

**Balance** (`Tools/Balance -- --storytellers`, 400 runs; `WayQuests` now counted with the quests): big threats a year
in the first year and the two after, against the classic 7.4 and 8.2: Rise and Fall 6.6 and 8.3; the six 7.4 to 7.6 and
8.2 to 8.3 (the classic cycle); their own picks a year: Open Gate 5.0 and 5.8 (before the game's population factors,
which only the game knows), The Wilds 8.6 and 9.4, Windfalls 8.1 and 8.9, Sellswords 1.0 and 1.5; quests a year: Open
Gate 10.4 and 13.0, Windfalls 10.8 and 14.0, Sellswords 10.7 and 14.0 against the classic 8.1 and 10.0.

**What only the game can show**: the six on the storyteller screen with their plates; each part's firings in a real
colony (the picks' and quests' `CanFireNow` and `CanRun`, which only the game knows: an escape pod only where Vanilla
Gravship Expanded allows it, an orbital quest only with a way to orbit, the Banner's squad only with the Banner in the
world); the population factors thinning Open Gate's joiners; the direction changing a running game.

### The storytellers' levers below the base rate, kept only where they fit (the player's answer, 19 November 2026; released 0.266.8)

The question left open in 0.253.0 was whether the first eight's levers below the base rate go back to it. The player:
"Some storytellers and fewer traders and fewer fights. That's also good. Depending, you know, if it's fitting for the
scenario, it should also just be reflected in the description." So a way brings something less often than the base
game only where that is what the way is about, and its description on the storyteller screen says what; everything
else is at the base rate. The base rate is 1 for Rimfolk's levers and the classic storyteller's numbers for the game's
own parts (`Tools/Balance/StorytellerSim.cs`, from the game's def): 5 traders, 4 visitors and 6 travellers a year,
friends in a fight 15, an orbital trader every 15 days, the home's everyday happenings about every 4.8 days. A way
shaped by the seasons or the arc is taken over its year or its arc; What You Sow at a colony of no name and at both
ends of the deeds. Within 2% counts as at the base rate. The threats and sickness are not part of this: they keep the
classic pace or less, as before.

| Way | Below the base rate before | Decided | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Long Road | nothing | its description now says "Nothing comes less often than in the base game" and names what it brings more of that it didn't say: traders (6 a year and Rimfolk's 1.2), travellers (9) and the region's news sooner (situations 1.3) | |
| Neighbours | fights 0.8 | **back to 1**; nothing below now, and said; the description now also names its trade (6 traders a year), the peoples' stronger memory (1.25) and the region's news (situations 1.2) | Rimfolk's events that may end in a fight (revenge, debts called in, tribute, an old enemy) are this way's own story: fewer of them goes against it |
| The Turning Year | the seasons' dips (winter camps 0.3, traders 0.4; spring fights 0.5), each averaging 1 over a year; the everyday happenings every 6 days, with the season's own every 12 | **kept**, as the player said on 15 November 2026 ("the turning year you can leave as it is"); the description now says winter's few traders or camps, the season's happenings in place of some everyday ones, and traders and visitors about as often as the classic over a year (5.25 and 3.99) | the seasons are the way |
| What You Sow | a cruel colony's traders, visitors, camps, letters, favours, missions and friends in a fight; a kind colony's fights 0.6 and schemes 0.4; a colony of no name's traders 4.4 a year, visitors 3.85 and friends 13.2 (0.55 of the peaks 8, 7 and 24) | cruel and kind **kept**, each said; **no name back to the base rate**: `StoryWaysMath.DeedNoName` 0.625 gives 5 traders, 4.4 visitors and 15 friends | the colony's deeds coming back to it is the way; a colony nobody knows anything about has done nothing to get fewer |
| Old Powers | fights 0.7; the everyday happenings every 6 days, with omens every 8; raids a little slower, strange threats making up the rest | **kept**, all said | the danger is strange rather than other people; the omens are the strange things the way brings (everyday happenings and omens together come more often than the classic's everyday ones); raids with the strange threats keep the classic pace, as before |
| Lean Years | Rimfolk's traders 0.5, camps 0.8, visitors 0.8 and fights 0.7; the game's traders 2.5 a year, visitors 3, travellers 5, an orbital trader every 21 days; the everyday happenings every 7 days | **kept**, each said in the description, the orbital traders' "half as often" on the Almanac page put right (two thirds) | lean years: fewer people come by, fewer good things turn up, and the danger is the land more than other people |
| Rise and Fall | over the arc fights 0.82, schemes 0.87 and situations 0.95 (the good years lighter, the trouble heavier, fewer new world events while it runs); friends in a fight 0.6 of 18 a year in the growth and the omens (10.8 a year, 13.2 over the arc) | fights, schemes and situations **kept** and said, with the trouble's few traders, visitors and camps; **friends back to the base rate**: 0.85 of 18 in the good years (15.3), all 18 in the trouble and the rebuilding (16.2 over the arc) | the good years lighter and the trouble heavier are the arc, and the trouble is the region's news; the good years had no reason to send fewer friends |

**The direction** (the levers over any storyteller): Neighbours no longer lowers fights; the notes say "fewer fights"

### The old powers' own strange happenings (the player's go, 14 November 2026; released 0.240.0)

The player: "i like the old powers storyteller and want you to do some more more events in this style, including the gods
and using ressources from rimworld of magic", then "do ... more old powers style events". Item 7 of
`docs/storytellers-proposals.md` made into happenings of its own: fourteen uncanny happenings, each played out on the map,
fewer threats but stranger ones, under every storyteller and leaning to Old Powers. The gods stay unseen, harm stays in
the shared budget, and every one takes the colony's age's form.

- **The frame** (`Source/ColonyCouncil/OldPowers/OldPowers.cs`): looked at in the world events' hour
  (`HappeningTracker.Hourly`, `OldPowers.Hourly`), with Rimfolk's world events on, at each home on the ground with no
  fight on. With nothing under way and the last of any at least four days back (`OldPowersMath.SpacingDays`), each
  happening whose hours it is (`HoursOf`: the seer and the pilgrims in the morning, the beast and the dead at dusk, most at
  night) and whose call holds has its chance, one at most. One under way at a time (`OldPowersBook.play`, an
  `OldPowerPlay`), its short steps on their own due tick (`OldPowersBook.Due`; nothing at all ticks with none under way), let
  go when it ends so nothing of it stays in the save. Words through `OldPowers.T` and `Aged` (the colony's age, tribal to
  spacer, `CC_OldP_..._0` to `_3`), lines through the pool `Rimfolk_Pool_OldPowersSaid` (`OldPowers.Line`: only lines
  tagged with every tag of the moment, in the colony's era; one sentence over the head, `Speech.Say`), cards through
  `Tell.Letter`, news lines through `Tell.Minor`.
- **The pace** (`OldPowersMath.PaceOf`, `DayChance`, `CheckChance`): the gods' rules (`GodPaceMath`): each its own gap (18
  to 36 days), its chance small at the end of the gap and growing over a ramp, nothing on a call that is nearly always
  true (`GodPaceMath.Trigger`: none means never, however free), a strong reason 2.2 times as likely. The ways' lever
  `StoryWaysMath.Uncanny` (`StoryLevers.uncanny`) makes each look three times as likely under Old Powers or its story
  direction (`<uncanny>3</uncanny>`), 1 under every other way and storyteller; with the gaps and the spacing that comes to
  about one in three weeks at a home under any storyteller and one in ten days under Old Powers (the tests' model).
- **The fourteen** (`OldPowersMath.OldPower`, saved in this order):
  - *The seer of the season* (`OldPowersVisitors.cs`; a season's last two days, strongly with a frost or the heat coming):
    a seer of a people at peace (A RimWorld of Magic's arcane fold, `Seers`, six times likelier; a people of seers next)
    walks in on a visit, with the Chronomancer class where the mod has it, sits at the colony's middle and casts in the
    age's way (bones in the ashes, painted cards, a pendulum over a map, readings on a screen); someone free sits to
    listen; one word at a time over the seer's head, then the card with each word and its plain fact, all true
    (`SeerWords`: the next season's warmth from the map's twelfths, whether crops grow, the stores short or enough, blades
    when the storyteller's queue holds a fight within fifteen days).
  - *Everything faced one way* (`OldPowersNight.cs`; midnight, strongly the night after a death of the colony, else a
    clear night with no moon): everyone and every beast awake stops and faces one way for ten seconds, shadows running
    out that way; after a death toward where the dead lie (at dawn someone goes and stands there), else toward the edge
    of the land (at dawn someone walks out and finds an old worn thing of the colony's age there, `OwnMurmur.OldThing`).
  - *The humming stone* (dusk, a psychic sky strongly, a thunderstorm): a stone chunk near the middle, else the rock face
    nearest, hums till five in the morning; the beasts keep away; someone lays a hand on it (a mage's mana filled); those
    asleep within fourteen cells dream of it.
  - *The sealed scroll* (`OldPowersFinds.cs`; someone of the colony in a room of the old ruins not searched before):
    something sealed lies in the dust and they walk over and kneel by it: A RimWorld of Magic's spell scroll or now and
    then its grimoire; else a tome (Anomaly) or a textbook in an older colony, a schematic or a textbook in a newer one.
    Each room gives one at most (`OldPowersBook.searched`).
  - *The casters lit up* (A RimWorld of Magic's mana storm or surge, Vanilla Events Expanded's psychic bloom,
    stimulation or overdrive strongly, an aurora): the colony's mages (their mana filled), psycasters (half their
    psyfocus) and those psychically sensitive enough light up where they stand; at the shared budget's rate one is
    burned across the hands by the light (`Harm.Injure`, `HarmKinds.Uncanny`), and the card says so.
  - *The wandering enchanter* (a season's first three days, never in winter, strongly with a caster in the colony, only
    with a piece below masterwork and the silver for it): an enchanter (A RimWorld of Magic's Enchanter class where the
    mod has it; in the age's form, a rune-carver to a nanite smith) offers to work the colony's finest carried weapon or
    worn piece up one grade (`EnchantPrice`: 60 to 600 silver); asked by its own letter (`ChoiceLetter_OldPowers`,
    `Rimfolk_OldPowersLetter`) when the letters' gap allows, it walks on unanswered; yes, the bearer walks over, the two
    stand an hour over it with the light running along it, the silver comes out of the stores.
  - *The thing under the ground* (a long wet run strongly, a shorter one or the thaw): a knock under open earth near the
    middle one night, the ground cracking the next, and on the third morning it comes up (`PickFind`, leaning from the
    last finds): an old cache (silver and an old worn thing), something precious of the colony's age (`ThingRoles`, the
    player's whole pool), A RimWorld of Magic's raw magicyte (with a minor enchanting gem now and then); or with Anomaly,
    harm on and the shared budget's roll, one or two of the game's shamblers climbing out and coming for the colony (a
    small threat's card). Someone walks over to look.
  - *The dead on the road* (dusk, strongly within three days of a death of the colony, else a night with no moon while
    the void is awake or the dead lie unburied): a line of pale figures walks a road across the land past the colony and
    off it; those who see it stop and watch. With Anomaly, harm on and the shared budget's roll, the game's small
    shambler swarm walks it instead (a small share of the threat points, its own letter under the old powers' words).
  - *Pilgrims passing* (`OldPowersVisitors.cs`; spring's or autumn's first three days, strongly under an eclipse or an
    aurora): three to five pilgrims of a people at peace (a people of pilgrims likelier) stop at the colony's oldest grave,
    else its oldest tree, else its middle, pray there in turn, leave a carving of their people's age from the player's
    whole pool, and walk on.
  - *Another sky* (a clear night in the deep of summer or winter, strongly under an aurora): till five in the morning the
    night sky is violet with green-white shadows (`GameCondition_OtherSky`, `Rimfolk_OldP_OtherSky`), stars wrong,
    stargazing three times as likely and the gladder; those out of doors stop and look up.
  - *The animal that spoke* (`OldPowersFinds.cs`; dusk, strongly after the colony's hunters took four beasts in five days,
    else a full moon): a wild animal walks up to someone out of doors, stands before them and says one true sentence
    (`BeastWordOf`: the beasts taken, a fight coming, that they are sick, hungry, worn out or unhappy, else that something
    old is watching), then walks off like any other animal.
  - *A god going by* (evening, strongly a god of the colony drawn very near, else drawn near on a night with no moon; never
    while a coming, a presence or omens are under way): the god's own signs (round 2, `GodShapes.Omens`) one after another
    from ten at night, two hours apart, through the gods' own omens; at dawn the one who keeps it most looks out and says
    it went by, the colony's book keeps what they saw (`GodsOnMapWords.Saw`), and its own presence (round 2) stays a while
    as it goes (`PresenceKind.Depart`, `OldPowersMath.PassLingers`: where it has one that isn't held only while the god
    walks the land, and no other presence is on), named as the colony knows it, as the gods' own quiet presence is.
  - *The pale wolves* (`OldPowersNight.cs`; a full moon on a clear night, strongly in winter or with snow lying): a wolf
    howls far off (A RimWorld of Magic's `TM_WolfHowl`, else the game's warg), and five to eight pale wolves (its spirit
    wolves, `Mote_SpiritWolf_North` to `_West`, each drawn running the way it runs; else a pale light) run once round the
    colony 22 cells out and off the land; the beasts near stand and watch, those of the colony out of doors who see them
    stop and look ("saw the pale wolves", +2). At dawn someone walks out to where they ran and looks: no tracks, the snow
    smooth where there is snow.
  - *Eyes in the dark* (`OldPowersNight.cs`; a foggy night strongly, else a night with no moon in autumn or winter): three
    to six pairs of eyes catch the light at the edge of the dark 14 to 24 cells round the colony (two small glints side by
    side, low to the ground, A RimWorld of Magic's grey twinkle tinted), on places the colony's light doesn't reach;
    those out of doors who can see a pair stop and look ("felt watched", -2). After about a minute the one handiest in a
    fight, awake and free, walks out to the nearest pair, and as they come close every pair goes out, with nothing there;
    unwalked to, they go out at first light or after four hours.
- **Harm** (`HarmKinds.Uncanny`, "something uncanny that turns on someone (old powers)", system `oldPowers`, on with the
  world events, weight 0.004): the caster's burn, the shamblers on the road, the dead from under the ground, each rolled
  through `Harm.Roll` against the shared budget at the game's rate and told on a card. Nothing else hurts anyone; the
  pale wolves and the eyes never do.
- **The gods unseen**: a card names a god only through `Gods.CardName` (the colony knows it was that god) and
  `GodsOnMapWords.Title`; else "Signs in the night" and "some say something went past"; the presence after dawn is
  veiled unless the colony knows the god. The animal's "something old is watching" names nothing.
- **Ages**: the seer's casting, the ruin the scroll lies in, the enchanter's trade and another sky's stars each have four
  forms (`Aged`); the lines carry era tags where an age speaks its own way; the finds are of the colony's age.
- **The player's mods** (by name, the active rows of `docs/player-mods`, the game's own where one isn't loaded): A
  RimWorld of Magic's motes (casting circles, glowing runes, mana puffs, arcane waves, psionic current, ghosts, shadows,
  twinkles, holy light, earth cracks, its spirit wolves), sounds (gong, power-up, low vibration, low wind, soft
  explosion, wolf howl, its sermon), scrolls and grimoire, raw magicyte and minor enchanting gems, its Chronomancer and
  Enchanter classes, its arcane fold, its mana storm and surge; Vanilla Events Expanded's and Vanilla Psycasts Expanded's
  psychic skies, the Archon's psychic storm; Anomaly's shamblers and tomes; Royalty's psycasters and anima sound.
- **Dev actions** ("Rimfolk", `OldPowersDebug.cs`): one a happening ("Old powers: ... now"), the next step now, and the
  pace in the log.
- **Saved**: `OldPowersBook` (a game component): when each last came (fourteen), the last of any, the short memory of the
  forms (`GodPaceMath.Memory`), the ruins' rooms searched (`RuinsKept`), the one under way (its pilgrims, five at most,
  and the eyes' places, six at most). Modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.
- **What only the game can show**: the motes in view (the wolves' drawings upright and running the right way, the
  eyes' glints at the edge of the light), the seer's and the enchanter's visits with their lords, the bearer and the
  enchanter standing an hour, everything facing one way at once, the shamblers' letter under the old powers' words, the
  presence after dawn, and how often they come in a real colony.

### Checking a new game version

One DLL serves every supported version: it is built against the 1.6 references into `1.6/Assemblies`, and on 1.7
the game falls back to that folder. A new game version can break that DLL in ways the compiler never sees, because a
built DLL finds every game method, field and override by exact name and signature when it loads, Harmony finds its
targets by name, and constants and enum values are baked in as numbers. To check a new version (1.7 as the example):

1. **Build against it.** Add the version to the `RimRef` switch at the top of `Source/ColonyCouncil/ColonyCouncil.csproj`
   (its `Krafs.Rimworld.Ref` version and target framework), then `dotnet build -c Release -p:RimRef=1.7` in
   `Source/ColonyCouncil`. It goes to `bin/1.7/` and ships nowhere. Errors are source changes the new version needs;
   obsolete warnings are members to move off.
2. **Check the shipped DLL against it**, from the repository root:
   `dotnet run -c Release --project Tools/ApiDiff -- 1.6/Assemblies/ColonyCouncil.dll 1.6.4871 1.7.4977-alpha.2`.
   It lists every type, method, field, constant, override, Harmony patch target (with the patch's parameter names)
   and by-name lookup the DLL uses that the new version lacks or changed, and where each is used. `--all` also lists
   the ones that are fine. Exit code 0 means nothing changed. It works for any two versions, or any two folders of
   reference assemblies.
3. **Check the XML against the new def classes:** the DefValidator with the new references, the new build and, for a
   game on .NET, the runtime's reference pack as the fourth argument:
   `dotnet Tools/DefValidator/bin/Release/net8.0/DefValidator.dll . ~/.nuget/packages/krafs.rimworld.ref/1.7.4977-alpha.2/ref/net10.0 Source/ColonyCouncil/bin/1.7/ColonyCouncil.dll <dotnet>/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/10.0.x/ref/net10.0`.
4. **If something changed,** keep one DLL where at all possible: avoid the changed member, or reach it through
   reflection with a fallback, inside a try/catch. Only if that can't work: a `LoadFolders.xml` with a version
   folder holding a DLL built with `-p:RimRef=<version>` (`Install Rimfolk.bat` already copies a `1.7` folder and
   `LoadFolders.xml` when they exist).
5. **Then** add the version to `supportedVersions` in `About/About.xml`.

What the tools can't see: what a transpiler expects inside a game method (reference assemblies have no method bodies;
Rimfolk's one transpiler, on the Needs tab tooltip, falls back to a postfix), other mods' types, and vanilla def
names (game data, not code). Those need a look in game.

**1.7 (October 2026, Krafs.Rimworld.Ref 1.7.4977-alpha.2).** 1.7 runs on .NET 10 with a new engine layer (the
UnityEngine types come from `UnityStubs`), but the game's own API is nearly the same as 1.6. The 1.7 build compiles
with no errors and no new warnings, and the DefValidator's report is identical. ApiDiff finds nothing the 1.6 DLL
uses that 1.7 lacks or changed: 883 types, 5,183 methods and fields (game, Unity and runtime), 1,115 constants, 1,333
overrides, 28 Harmony patches, 9 by-name lookups. On the types Rimfolk names, the only difference is 14 old
`TextureFormat` members it doesn't use. The other direction doesn't hold: a DLL built against 1.7 calls things 1.6
lacks (UnityStubs' own `Texture ==`, .NET's `MaxBy` and string-interpolation handler), so the 1.7 build must never
go into the 1.6 folder.
