## Jobs of no kind (the player's report, 20 November 2026; released 0.275.2)

The player, after a medal at the gate: "the whole map screen turned gray essentially while I was unpausing the game. Once
I paused, the map just returned to normal, but as soon as I unpause, everything turns gray again", then, in a later save,
"there's an invisible pawn here". Three of Rimfolk's lists of its own jobs (`NightWalkDefOf` in `Harm/NightWalks.cs`,
`HarmSixDefOf`, `HarmSevenDefOf`) lacked the game's `[DefOf]` mark, so the game never filled them: the sleepwalk and the
restless walk, the dawn walk, the muster post, the dare and the shooing of a visitor, the practice walk and a visitor's
sneak to the stores were made as jobs of no kind. The game took such a job but couldn't make its driver. In the player's
game the open gates' visitor (`GateTroubles.Sneak`, the guard of the Republic's clerk) got one: he was drawn as his name
only (drawing him threw, and the game skips a pawn it can't draw), stood at the gate for good, and every frame in which
time passed his facing read the missing driver and threw before the map was drawn, so the map stayed grey until the
game was paused. The job was saved with him.

- The three lists carry the mark; `JobGuardTests` checks that every class Rimfolk asks the game to fill
  (`EnsureInitializedInCtor`) carries it and that each of Rimfolk's own defs it names exists.
- `Lean/JobGuard.cs`: `Patch_JobGuard`, a prefix on `Pawn_JobTracker.StartJob`, refuses a job of no kind from anyone
  (told once in the log), and `JobGuard.Repair`, from `CouncilGameComponent.FinalizeInit`, sends a pawn with a job of no
  kind or without its driver back to choosing a job when a game loads, and takes such jobs out of the queues.
- Since harm parts 5 to 7 (7 November 2026) none of those eight walks had played out: each try left the pawn so, or
  failed with an error. They now play out as written in their sections above.

## The medal read at the gate, and visitors' errands past a barred door (the player's report, 20 November 2026; released 0.276.2)

The player chose "Gather everyone who is free at the gate to hear it" on the Last Republic's medal, and nobody went
anywhere: the medal was given in the same tick as the answer. Their save shows why. The clerk had walked in from the
map's edge 141 ticks before and was still on her way to the gate; the errand Rimfolk set going was the clerk walking to
the colonist wherever they were (`PeopleEvents8.Errand`, a `CanReach` from the clerk to the colonist). The visitors' keep
out (`Visitors/KeepOut.cs`, 13 November 2026) had looked at the map 101 ticks after the clerk came and 40 before the
answer (its look runs at tick 131 of every 250), and from then each door of the colony's bedrooms and cold stores was
forbidden to her as a forbidden door is to a colonist. The errand never started (no lord was made for it: the save's
next lord id follows the visit's and the leaving's), the clerk was up, the colonist (Avila) was neither drafted nor in a
break, so the reach failed; the game lets a friendly visitor open the colony's doors, and those keep-out doors are the
ones that stop one. Avila was indoors and awake (out of doors last about two hours before, no sleep ended since, and
showering in another's bedroom half an hour later), so most likely in a room with a bed. The citation was given there and
then (`Award`), unseen. The same pattern sat in other errands of the peoples' events.

- **Meeting at the gate** (`PeopleEvents8.Meet`, `MeetSpot`, `Beside`, `SendOut`, `Release`; the rules in
  `PeopleEvents8Math`: `MeetRange` 4 cells, `MeetWaitTicks` three hours, `MeetSends` 4, `Step`, `Met`). The meeting
  place is the gate spot (`PeoplesD.GateSpot`), else the spot the visit was taking them to, else where the visitor
  stands: never a place in the colony. The visitor, on an errand lord there (`LordJob_VisitOnErrand`), goes to it and
  waits for the colonist (`JobDriver_PEv8Work`: with a meeting place, TargetB, it goes there first and waits until the
  colonist is within four cells, at most three hours); the colonist walks out to stand two or three cells from it
  (`Rimfolk_PEv8_StandBy`, kept in the visit's `touched` and let go when it is over). Then the work at them is done there.
- **The medal** (`RepublicMedal`): the clerk goes on to the gate; the colonist walks out to her; the guard stands by;
  with the second answer up to eight free colonists stand round; once the colonist is there she reads the citation for
  an hour and pins on the medal, and those within nine cells heard it. The visit's hour sends the colonist out again if a
  meal or a fight pulled them away (when they can be interrupted), and sets the meeting going again if it stopped (four
  times). With the hours out before the colonist could come (a door they can't pass, a long break, a fight), the clerk
  says "Then the citation goes into the record unread" and goes home, and a message says the colonist could not get out
  to the gate (`CC_PEv8_MedalLeft`): no medal, no memory of it, and another deed may bring the clerk again. With the
  play-outs off it is given at once, as before.
- **A target behind a barred door** (`JobDriver_PEv8Work`): a target of the work the visitor can't reach is passed over
  for the next one in the queue, so the clerk's roll at the vote and the officers' walk of the ship go on past a voter
  or a part in a bedroom; the roll starts with a voter the clerk can reach (`VoteObserver.Begin`).
- **The other errands of rounds 5 to 10**, looked over for the same fault (a visitor sent to a colonist or to a thing in
  the colony, the event done there and then when the way is barred):
  - *A gene taken out*, *a whole xenogerm* (round 8): the sequencer goes straight to the colonist when nothing bars the
    way, else the colonist walks out to the sequencer and the work is done at the meeting place (`PeopleEvents8.WorkOn`).
    Stopped, it is set going again; with the hours out before it could be done, the sequencer leaves at the gate the
    silver and genepacks the colony paid and goes home, told (`PeopleEvents8.Undone`, `CC_PEv8_WorkUndone(Paid)`).
  - *A sleeper of theirs* (round 8): the runner's way to the casket is open through a bedroom
    (`Peoples/PeopleErrands.cs`, below); still no way (a cold store, someone asleep in the room), the colony's best
    doctor opens it and the sleeper walks out to the runner (`CC_PEv8_SleeperHomeOpened` says who opened it).
  - *The colony's gravship* (round 8): the ship's bedrooms are open to the officers for the walk; with no part they can
    reach they log it from outside and the words say so (`CC_PEv8_GravOutside`, no pilot's memory, no lesson; the part
    from the hull's stores set down where they stood).
  - *An observer at the vote* (round 8): the roll passes over a voter the clerk can't get to.
  - *The master's mark* (round 7): the master's way to the piece is open through a bedroom; a master who can't get to it
    waits at the gate and is sent again each hour, and with the hours out goes home without a verdict, told
    (`CC_PEv7_MarkNoWay`), never judged unseen.
  - *A voice for the colony* (round 7): the operator's way to the radio is open through a bedroom; a radio they couldn't
    get to (or were kept from) isn't used, and the call goes by runner, the words saying so.
  - *A shout in the mind* and *the warden of the quiet* (round 9): the listener's and the warden's way to the one they sit
    with is open through a bedroom; with no way to them they wait at the gate and the hour tries again, never the break
    ended or the day's good done unseen; a listener who never got to a colonist still in their break says so
    (`CC_PEv9_ShoutNoWay`).
  - *Mending tonight* (round 5): the crew mends only what they can get to, so a building in a bedroom never holds a mender
    up all night, and with nothing else left they go.
  - Looked over and not sharing the fault: the field lab's sequencers wait until the colonist is in reach; the art handed
    on and the hearings at the wood moot and the road toll meet at the gate already; the camps' work is on open ground; the
    copyist and the lessons try again each day; the feral mech is called to the gate first.
- **Errands the colony said yes to** (`Peoples/PeopleErrands.cs`, `PeopleErrands.Ways`, read by `KeepOut.Care`): as for
  a doctor's work, the bedroom where the errand is lies open to the one sent (the master's piece, the radio, the casket,
  the ship's parts, the one sat with); a cold store stays shut, and so does a bedroom where one of the colony sleeps. Each
  of those errands refreshes the keep out's look as it starts (`KeepOut.Refresh`), so the way counts at once.
- Tests: `PeopleEvents8Tests` (the hour's steps, the meeting's range and the places round it, and the seams).

## Colony life's integrations, part 2: wishes, ambitions and the calendar (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.279.2)

The player on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "your content proposal overall sounds really good. You can go ahead with
this in the order you think makes most sense ... more immersion ... the relations between pawns, the kind of events that
generated from it", and "first do all the integrations that you proposed in your document before we add additional
content variety". Seven items of part A, each built as proposed there: A10, A12, A13, A14, A17, A27, A29. The code is in
`Source/ColonyCouncil/ColonyLife/`; the pure rules in `ColonyLifeMath.cs` (Tools/Tests: `ColonyLifeTests`). What is kept
between passes (`LifeBook`, saved with the council as `CouncilGameComponent.life`): a wished-for thing still to be tried
out, lines still to be said at a gathering under way, the aims said aloud this year, the ambitions reached since the year
was last read aloud, the record keeper and the year last read; each list short (see "Save size"). The try-outs and the
readings ride on the play-outs' own 250-tick pass (`PlayOutTracker`: `LifeBook.Tick`, and `LifeBook.PlayDone` when a plan
is over), so there is no pass of their own.

- **A10, a place for the group** (`GroupPlaces.cs`, `Rimfolk_Wishes_ColonyLife.xml`). A close group (cohesion at the card's
  "close", `GroupMath.CloseAt`) with its anchor and two more at home asks for the place its habit needs, when the colony
  has none and can build one: the fireside a fire pit or campfire with two seats within four cells, the readers a
  bookcase with a seat in its room, the game night a game table, the musicians an instrument, the faithful an altar or a
  shrine. Which habit: the first of the group's habits, in its own order, that wants a place of its own
  (`GroupPlaceMath.FirstWanting`; decided here: the proposal's "first habit" read so, since no group kind lists reading or
  music first). The anchor makes the wish (`WishWorker_GroupPlace`, subject `group:<id>:<kind>`) and every member at home
  is put on it as a co-signer (`WishWorker.OnMade`, a new hook called as a wish is made); the request is picked again
  with a `[place:...]` tag. What counts is read from the whole mod pool by kind (a fire by its name as the gatherings'
  fire is, a bookcase by the game's class or its name, a game table by the game's own kinds of games, an instrument by the
  game's class, a shrine by the game's altar flag or its name; Vanilla Furniture Expanded's props never), the game's own
  first ([sbz] Bookcase's shelves and VFE Core's stone campfire among the rest). When it is met (`WishWorker.OnMet`, a new
  hook called by `Grant`) the place is the group's (`SocialGroup.placeId`, `placeKind`, saved), a note goes in its
  history, and its first evening there is set going: the group's gathering, round the fire or at the place itself, with
  the habit's own lines, counted in the week's gatherings. From then on `GroupHabits.Daily` calls the group to its own
  place for that habit, the habits without a gathering of their own (reading, music, prayer) included; the habit's pill on
  the card says so. The place gone, a new one of the kind counts; none, the group is called as before.
- **A12, the wished-for thing tried out** (`TryOuts.cs`, `Rimfolk_TryOut`). A lasting wish met for a thing, a bed or a room
  (the promise watch's own kinds) no longer has its thanks said at once: with answers playing out on the map, the one it
  was for goes to it in their free time within a day (`Together.FreeTime`, free to be called, nothing pressing), the
  newest of the kept things they can reach, and sits in it, lies on the bed a moment, warms up at a fire or heater, looks
  over anything else, or walks into the room and looks round; the thanks are said there, and a friend nearby (opinion 20
  or more, really together) admires it a third of the time. Nothing to reach, or the day out: the thanks where they are,
  as before. A group's place has its own first evening instead.
- **A13, a wish talked up finds backers** (`TalkBacking.cs`, `InteractionWorker_TalkAboutWish.Interacted`). When the game's
  own conversation brings up an open wish many may back (`allowPetition`), the listener joins it there and then if they
  would want the same (the wish's own rule raises it for them now, the same subject; same colony; not on its cooldown):
  half the time, more for a friend and less for someone at odds (the wish roll's own bond), once a day at most for the
  wish (`Wish.talkBackedDay`). A line from each over the other's head, a word in the news and the chronicle, the deadline
  two days on, as a co-signer does. Who would want the same is the meeting's own rule for "any other business"
  (`CouncilGameComponent.WantsSame`, A6, `Ambitions/MeetingBusiness.cs`), so a wish talked up and a petition read out at
  the meeting find the same backers; joining does what the roll's co-signing does (`CoSign`), with a line each.
- **A14, an ambition reached, seen on the map and kept on the calendar** (`AmbitionScenes.cs`, the ambition defs). Every
  ambition now has its scene (`achievedEffects`), led by the seat whose work it is when there is a holder at home
  (`AmbitionDef.sceneOffice`: the physician shows everyone round a new ward or infirmary, the marshal walks the defenses
  at dusk, the herdmaster the barn, the quartermaster the stores, the peacemaker the toast to harmony, the elder the first
  lesson) or by the one who proposed it. What was built is stood by (`AmbitionGoal.Showpiece`: the finest room of its kind
  and its piece, the newest of the things built, the cooler, the sun lamp, the art; for rooms of their own, the
  proposer's own bed), so the words name it ("Harper shows everyone round the new ward: the colony gathers by the
  hospital bed."). The kinds: a look round what was built (rooms, the cold store, the cells, the art, the place of study,
  the throne room, the way to hear from outside); a walk round the colony's edge at dusk (the defenses, the guns, the
  traps, the stone walls, the way in); a supper (the larder, the greenhouse, the clean kitchen, a year made ready, hot
  meals, plenty); an evening under the new lights; a quiet hour at the graves; the first lesson at the new desks for the
  children; a walk out in the new coats; a fire from the winter's wood or for the score settled; a toast for the rest (a
  calm season, harmony, the council, friends abroad, a master's hand). The letter says when (`PlayWords.Planned`). The day
  goes on the colony calendar as a day of its own kind (`CalendarKind.Ambition`, named by `AmbitionDef.dayLabel`, "the
  day the hospital was finished"; weight 22 to 42 by effort and days, `AmbitionDayMath`; three at most), kept by walking
  out to what was built (`DayWay.Walk`, its thing and place kept like a camp's gift) or with a supper when nothing was,
  toward a tradition as the other days are; it ends quietly when what was built is gone (or, with nothing built, when
  nobody who reached it lives). The proposer writes the day in their journal; its letter, talk and pass lines are its
  own (`Council_Cal_*_Ambition`). The ambitions reached are kept for the year read aloud.
- **A17, Vanilla Aspirations Expanded's aims** (`ModAims.cs`, `Patch_ModAimLetter`). The mod's letter that an aim was
  reached (`VAspirE_Fulfilled`, by name) is read as it comes: the aim is the one of the mod's whose label the letter's
  words name (`ModAimsMath.Match`, the longest). A journal line always; for an aim the colony would toast, the closest
  friend raises a cup to them at the next gathering (`Stage.Cup`, the toast's own words, since the mod's labels are aims,
  not deeds), the chronicle and the year's annals note it, and the deed "reached a life goal" is told round the colony.
  Not toasted (decided here, from the mod's 76 aims): killing someone, an overdose, human meat, a rival dead, pain sought
  out, being disliked, luciferium and opium, blackout drunk, being digested, burn scars, the flesh's dark arts, becoming
  inhuman, being entombed, a sanguophage's or a chainsaw's change, a lover's bed, the joywire, deserting; and an aim the
  letter doesn't name. The heart's need for purpose counts the mod's fulfilment need, -10 empty to +10 full
  (`ModAimsMath.Purpose`), and Rimfolk's own life goals are taken up a third less often by someone who has the mod's aims
  (`GoalMath.ModAimsFactor` in `AspirationTracker.TryChoose`).
- **A27, the year's first supper** (`FirstSupper.cs`, `Rimfolk_Dilemmas_Customs_ColonyLife.xml`). A custom of the year's
  first days (`CustomConditions.lastDayOfYear` 7; any season, since the year's first days are spring in one place and
  autumn in another), asked by someone with a life goal, kept on the calendar and toward a tradition like the other
  customs. "Everyone says it, at one supper": the supper (the one feast engine, `DilemmaEffect_FirstSupper`), and at the
  table, every ten seconds or so, the next one there with a life goal says it in one line; someone without one may
  choose one there and then from what fits them (`AspirationTracker.ChooseAtSupper`, spark "supper") and say it; a backer
  at the table may answer. "Only those who want to": those with a goal say it, nobody takes one up. "Not this year". When
  the supper is over, each who said theirs and each there who backs them (opinion 20 or more) grow a little closer; each
  speaker writes it in their journal. The year letter reads back up to five, each as it turned out (reached, still at it,
  let go, died before it). Text: the question in the flavour style, the lines at table plain, one sentence each.
- **A29, the year read aloud** (`YearRead.cs`). On the landing's anniversary, after the year letter is written, its writer
  reads three to five lines of it that evening (who came, who was lost, what the colony finished, an aim from the first
  supper kept, a name the colony uses, and as filler the raids, how many there are and which year it was:
  `YearReadMath.Pick`), one sentence every ten seconds or so while they are at the table: at the founding day's own
  gathering when one is planned for that evening, else at a short gathering of words of its own. Those there remember it
  together (`Rimfolk_Mem_YearRead`, brought up in talk later) and the writer writes a line of it. The council's answer
  "Make A keeper of the colony's record" now makes them the colony's record keeper (`DilemmaEffect_RecordKeeper`): they
  write the year from then on (`AnnalsTracker.Author`), which counts toward the Annalist's name as any writing of it does,
  and the letter opens with it. With Vanilla Books Expanded (by name) and a writer's or typewriter table, the writer first
  writes it up there in the day (a visit to the table), and it becomes a book called after the year ("The second year",
  the game's novel, of the writer's quality) set on a bookcase of the colony's with room, else by the table; with the
  mod's printing researched, its newspaper. Without the mod, the reading alone.
- Words: wishes and the custom's question in the flavour style; the lines said aloud plain, one sentence each
  (`ImmersionTests`); the calendar, journals, messages and the interface plain. No harm in any of it.
- Dev actions ("Rimfolk", `LifeDebug.cs`): a group asks for its place, a group's first evening at its place now, a
  colonist tries out a thing now, a wish talked up to someone near, the ambition under way reached now, an aim of their
  own reached, the year's first supper asked now or set going now, the year read aloud tonight, make a colonist the
  record keeper.

## Colony life's variety, part 2: life, customs, stories and the colony's own events (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.285.0)

The player on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "just variety, further kind of events, camps, world events, normal
storyteller events, dilemmas, etc. ... yes, I want more events, camps, world events, and dilemmas, but first do all the
integrations". With the integrations all released (0.278.0 to 0.280.2), the variety of colony life, part 2: A8, A11, A15,
A16, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26 and A28 of part A, each built as proposed there, and beyond the doc, in the player's
direction ("normal storyteller events"), twelve events of the colony's everyday life and six personal stories. The code is
in `Source/ColonyCouncil/LifeVariety/`; the pure rules in `LifeVarietyMath.cs` (Tools/Tests: `LifeVarietyTests`). What is
kept between passes (`LifeVarietyBook`, saved with the council as `CouncilGameComponent.lifeVariety`): who first asked for
each custom the colony keeps, where a season of kept promises stands, the children lately given a toy, the giving day under
way and the years the giving day and the elders' day were last kept, and the giving day's gifts of the last days; each list
short (see "Save size"). Its passes: once a day with the council's second half (`LifeVariety.Daily`: the seats' sparks),
once an hour with its life (`LifeVariety.Hourly`: the giving day's lamps and end), and the play-outs' own 250-tick pass
(`LifeVariety.Tick`: the giving day's walks).

- **A8, coming of age: four more paths** (`Rimfolk_Dilemmas_ComingOfAge_More.xml`). Beside the workshop, the healer, the
  scholar and the wall: the fields, the kitchen, the animals and building, each a real mentorship in the social web and a
  first lesson on the map (`DilemmaEffect_Mentorship`, `DilemmaEffect_Lesson`), with the other choice (another work's
  experience) and letting them choose. A path that is a seat's work names it (`<seat>`: the fields the reeve's, the
  animals the herdmaster's), and the seat's holder at home teaches when they could (`DilemmaWorker_ComingOfAge` takes them
  as B before the colony's best at the work). Council questions, the flavour style.
- **A11, a toy for the little one** (`ToyWish.cs`, `Rimfolk_Wish_Toy`). A grown-up fond of a child of three to twelve at
  home (a parent, an elder of sixty or more, or anyone with an opinion of 30 of the child, all alike, never one at odds:
  `ToyMath.MayAsk`; nothing follows family lines) asks for a toy made at the bench: Vanilla Christmas Expanded's wooden,
  plushie or metal toy where the colony can make one (its recipe researched, its bench built or buildable), else a small
  sculpture. One wish for a child at a time, and not for one given a toy in the last forty days. Met when one is made after
  the wish (the count of them on the map grows): the one who asked takes the newest by hand to the child (`LifeHands.Give`,
  the play-out engine's own handing over, waiting for both to be free), and the child has the mod's toy memory when it is a
  memory (by name), else Rimfolk's "a toy of my own" (+6, an opinion of the asker); the asker "gave a child a toy".
  Wishes, the flavour style.
- **A15, three ambitions of the colony's people** (`ColonyAmbitions.cs`, `Rimfolk_Ambitions_LifeVariety.xml`). Nobody left
  out (`Goal_NobodyOutside`): every grown colonist at home in a group or with a friend (both opinions 40, or the social
  web's friendship 30), pitched when two or more stand outside, its progress the share inside, met only with nobody
  outside; a supper for everyone, led by the steward. A season of kept promises (`Goal_KeptPromises`): fifteen days running
  with no promised wish let lapse and two promises kept along the way (the colony's counts on the standings; the counts
  when the season began kept in the book), pitched while someone still minds a broken promise; a toast led by the speaker.
  A lighter season (`Goal_LighterSeason`): fifteen days with nobody at home worn down or near breaking (the heart's strain
  of 55 or more), pitched when someone is; an easy evening by the fire led by the peacemaker. Each keeps its day on the
  calendar as every ambition does (A14). Ambitions, the flavour style.
- **A16, life goals for the other seats** (`SeatSparks.cs`, `Rimfolk_Aspirations_Seats.xml`). The reeve's, the
  peacemaker's, the keeper of days', the herdmaster's, the chaplain's, the warden of guests' and an elder's seat (an elder's
  from 45), each sparked by losing an election and by the seat's own work: once a day each colonist's record behind it is
  read against yesterday's (twenty plants harvested in a day, a quarrel mended, a day of the calendar kept, an animal
  tamed, a rite led, a camp greeted, a student taught to stand alone: `SeatSparkMath`), never for the seat they hold; the
  elder's also by a child born. `AspirationWorker_SeatOpen` wants a seat only while it is open to the colony (the
  chaplain's needs its own faith). A goal of a seat already leans the vote (`BondsMath.SeatWant`; the check now takes the
  new worker too). Life goals, the flavour style.
- **A22, marks from the colony's own life** (`LifeMarksDeeds.cs`, `Rimfolk_PersonaMarks_ColonyLife.xml`). Five turning
  points, each read by nature as the other marks are: a life goal reached (pride and outlook; the proud more pride,
  `Aspirations.Fulfil`), an idea of theirs built (openness and pride, the ambition they proposed reached,
  `Ambitions.Complete`), a custom they first asked for become a tradition (warmth, openness down a little: the council's
  customs note who asked the first time one was kept, `LifeVarietyBook.NoteFirstAsker`), a year in a seat with the promise
  kept (pride and trust, the promise judged kept at the yearly election, `SeatRecords.Judged`), a personal story that ended
  well (warmth and outlook, `ArcTracker.Complete`). The marks write their own journal lines (plain).
- **A23, deeds and names of the council's life** (`LifeMarksDeeds.cs`, `Rimfolk_Deeds_Council.xml`,
  `Rimfolk_Epithets_Council.xml`, `Rimfolk_Records_Council.xml`). Deeds told round the colony: kept a promise in a seat and
  broke one (judged at the yearly election), spoke up for someone before the council (the one named objecting when the
  council is asked to send someone away); stepped down from a seat is A3's own deed (`CouncilLife/StepDown.cs`,
  `Rimfolk_Deeds_CouncilLife.xml`), not made twice. Records of days in the seats that had none, counted with the names each day (the
  quartermaster's, the reeve's, the herdmaster's, the steward's, the elders'), and names at 120 days, as Old Doc and Old
  Iron are: Old Keys, Old Furrow, the Drover, the Host, the Old Voice; and Word-Kept for two promises in a seat judged
  kept. Plain.
- **A24, group habits from the colony's pastimes** (`Social/Groups/GroupHabits.cs`, `Rimfolk_GroupHabits_Pastimes.xml`).
  Four habits kept as they come, as reading and music are: fishing together (Odyssey's and PokéWorld's fishing), the hot
  water (Dubs Bad Hygiene's hydrotherapy, its pool's water, a hot tub or a sauna, ReGrowth's hot spring), a pot of tea or
  coffee in the same room (any coffee or tea a mod adds, the morning cup's own rule), cards, chess or darts (the game's
  poker and chess, Vanilla Furniture Expanded's dartboard). Each is something a friendship group may be named for ("the
  anglers", "the tea table"), and the kinds that keep it list it after their own (the hunters and the fields fishing, the
  elders, the kitchen, the gentle and friends the cup, the young, the gentle and the merry the hot water, the merry, the
  bold, the comrades and the scholars the games). Plain, spoken lines one sentence each.
- **A25, social events and talk of the council's seasons** (`CouncilSeasons.cs`, `Rimfolk_SocialEvents_CouncilSeasons.xml`,
  `Rimfolk_Topics_Vote.xml`). Seven social events (`SocialEventDef.council`): help with the speech (a candidate and a friend
  not standing against them), the seat handed over (the one who lost it to the new holder, within six days, never while
  they are in part 1's story "after the vote", whose own stage is that word), a promise
  remembered (the holder's election promise going well by the vote's own test) or thrown back (going badly), backing
  different candidates (by the vote's own lean), a petition talked over by two of its signers, an elder's word to a young
  holder. And a talk topic, "the vote", only while an election is under way, about its most contested seat, with lines on
  whom the speaker leans to read from the vote's own lean (`OfficeTracker.Leaning`, without the day's luck: themselves,
  the holder, someone else, or undecided when two are within a hair); talking never moves the vote. Plain.
- **A26, the giving day** (`GivingDay.cs`, `Rimfolk_Dilemmas_Customs_LifeVariety.xml`). A winter custom, asked once a winter
  at a home, kept on the calendar and three years running a tradition. "The giving day, for everyone": names drawn so
  everyone at home gives one and gets one (`GivingMath.Draw`, never themselves), and for each a gift chosen from the stores
  by what the one it's for wants or lacks (`GivingMath.Order`: a child a toy, then something sweet; someone bare-headed in
  winter something warm; a reader a book; someone who may drink a drink, never one their faith or their own rule forbids;
  then a carving, then something sweet), worth 400 silver at most: Vanilla Christmas Expanded's toys, gingerbread, milk and
  cookies, eggnog and hot cocoa and warm hat and jacket, Vanilla Apparel Expanded's scarf, the game's tuque, novel,
  textbook, chocolate and beer, any mod's coffee or tea, a small sculpture packed in the stores; every age by what its
  stores hold. From one in the afternoon each giver walks to the stores and takes theirs into their pack; the supper (the one
  feast engine), the mod's fairy lamps switched on at it (unless midwinter lit them today); after it, from seven, each walks
  over to the one theirs is for and hands it over with a line (and maybe a thanks), a memory and a little closeness. The
  evening over, what wasn't handed round is set down by its giver, and the day is told. "The children only": each child a
  gift from the grown-up fondest of them who has given least (`GivingMath.ForChildren`). Midwinter (C29) hands no presents
  of its own while the giving day is under way at the home, so the two never double. With the faith's festive feast
  (Vanilla Christmas Expanded's `VCE_FestiveFeast`), once the giving day is on the calendar, the gifts follow the feast at
  once and that winter's question isn't asked (decided here: the calendar spends it without blame).
- **A28, the elders' day** (`EldersDay.cs`, same file). An autumn custom with two colonists of sixty or more at home or the
  elder's seat held, asked by someone under thirty, once an autumn. "The whole day": the colony's children (four at most)
  each make a small sculpture for one of the elders in turn and carry it over (the answers' own making and handing over);
  at supper the cup is raised to the elders, and each elder there tells one thing from their life, one line every ten
  seconds or so (the gatherings' readings, `ReadingKind.Elders`), someone at the table answering now and then; those who
  told theirs are glad of it and the others grow a little closer to them. "Supper only": the supper and the tales.
  Decided here: the proposal's head of the table and serving first aren't claimed, since the feast engine seats nobody;
  the cup raised to them and their tales are what is seen.
- **Twelve events of the colony's everyday life** (`ColonyEvents.cs`, `Rimfolk_Events_ColonyLife.xml`), each from what is
  on the map and tied into what exists, each answer played out with the engine's own; none brings harm:
  - a quarrel at supper: two at odds both ways at the supper hours; the peacemaker (else the best talker) sits them down at
    a table (counted as a quarrel mended, a spark for the peacemaker's goal), or they are kept apart, or left to it;
  - the newcomer at the edge: someone here twenty days or less outside every group; a group's anchor brings them to an
    evening of the group, or keeps them a seat at supper;
  - the student's first piece: a mentorship's student made something excellent or better; a toast to it led by the teacher,
    or a word between the two (the coming-of-age apprenticeships bring these);
  - short in the stores: under five days of food with something to bring in; a work party at the harvest, or wild food
    marked for gathering (the quartermaster speaks when there is one);
  - a wish left waiting: a wish more than half its time gone with no promise, and a friend asks; the council promises it
    (as the player's own "Promise" does), says it must wait, or says nothing;
  - the old song: an elder of sixty or more remembers a song of an evening; sung at the fire with music, or taught to a child;
  - a vow in the storm: after a storm, a colonist who holds a god with a shrine of it at home says they vowed to keep a
    night's watch there; the watch kept (alone or with a friend), or the work first. Their belief: the god is named as they
    call it, and nothing says it heard;
  - a group's evening off: a close group not gathered for a week asks for an evening, led by its anchor;
  - the child's question: a child asks why the colony keeps one of its days (or how it began); told the story by a grown-up
    fond of them, or a lesson;
  - a broken promise still sore: someone minds a broken promise and a friend asks; the speaker (else the best talker) says
    sorry at supper, or the friend takes them for a walk;
  - hands for the last field: autumn with thirty plants or more ripe in the fields, never within ten days of the council's
    question "every hand to the harvest" (part 1's); a work party, the reeve and one more, or the growers alone;
  - a night with the herd: an animal of the colony near its time; the herdmaster (else the best handler) sits up with it.
  Event cards, plain words.
- **Six personal stories** (`ColonyStories.cs`, `Rimfolk_Arcs_ColonyLife.xml`), in the flavour style:
  - a custom of their own: the one who first asked for a custom, until it is kept a second year and becomes a tradition
    (let pass, it comes to nothing);
  - a promise waited on: a promised wish still open after four days, hopeful, restless, kept (let lapse, nothing);
  - ready for the seat: a life goal of a seat, practising its work, standing for it at an election, holding it (an election
    lost ends it);
  - a prayer for a friend: a believer with a shrine of their god and a close friend laid up; sitting with them, and when the
    friend is well, taking it as the god's answer and giving thanks at the shrine (their belief, never the colony's
    knowledge);
  - an unexpected gift: a gift on the giving day from someone they thought little of, a word of thanks, and friends;
  - the year's aim: a goal said aloud at the year's first supper, halfway, reached.
- Words: council questions (the paths, the customs), wishes, ambitions, life goals and personal stories in the flavour style
  as restored in 0.276.0; event cards, social events, talk, deeds, names, marks, journals, messages and the interface
  plain; spoken lines one sentence each. No em dashes or exclamation marks. No harm in any of it.
- Dev actions ("Rimfolk", "Colony life 2: ...", `LifeVarietyDebug.cs`): a new coming-of-age path asked for, a toy for a
  child asked now, an ambition of the colony's people under way now, a seat's life goal for someone, the seats' sparks read
  now, a mark of the colony's own life, a deed of the council's life, a social event of the council's seasons (who fits),
  the giving day's gifts now (everyone or the children, no supper), ask a custom now, the elders' supper set going now,
  one of the colony's own events now, one of the new personal stories for someone.

## The land and its life (the player's go, 20 November 2026; released 0.279.1)

The player on `docs/content-update-proposals.md`: "your content proposal overall sounds really good. You can go ahead
with this in the order you think makes most sense ... more immersion", and "first do all the integrations that you
proposed in your document before we add additional content variety". Built as part C proposes them: C19, C20, C21, C22,
C24, C28 and C30, each marked **Built** there. Harm: none of it hurts anyone. Every age: nothing here is switched off
for an age; the cup and the herd's sale take what the colony has.

**C19, after the storm: a work party for every disaster** (`Weather/AfterStorm.cs`, `AfterStormMath.cs`). The weather
record's hour (`WeatherBook.Hour`) asks `AfterStorm.OnNow` what is happening: Seasonal Weather's earthquake (its
condition), a flashstorm (the game's, or the storytellers' map-wide one), Rimfolk's hail while it falls, a tornado on the
map (the game's own `Tornado` thing, which Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's tornado alley sends) and a flood (Odyssey's
`SeasonalFlood` thing, which stands on the map until the water subsides, read in the 1.6 code; Vanilla Landmarks
Expanded's `VEE_TidalFlooding` condition). What began is counted for the year's annals; what ended has a party wait one to
three hours (`DelayHours`). Vanilla Events Expanded's earthquake comes and goes in a moment, so a postfix on the game's
`IncidentWorker.TryExecute` notes it (`Patch_AfterStorm_TryExecute`, with the deeper hooks). When its time comes, on a
quiet map, and for a flashstorm with no fire left in the home area, the one best at the work leads three others in a
work party (`DilemmaEffect_WorkParty`, the game's own jobs, hours 6 to 20):

| Disaster | Leads | The party's work |
|---|---|---|
| Earthquake | best builder | mend, rebuild what the game marked, patch roofs, clean, haul |
| Tornado | best builder | the same |
| Flashstorm | best grower | the burnt trees in and round the home area and the fields marked for cutting (`MarkBurnt`), cut, ash cleaned, sowing where the season allows |
| Hail | best grower | sow where it flattened the young crops (the hail destroys those, so nothing is left to cut), bring in the ripe |
| Flood | best builder | haul what the water left lying about, clean |

Only when there is work (something damaged or a blueprint for a quake or a tornado; burnt trees or ash for a flashstorm;
growing weather and cells to sow for hail; filth or things to haul for a flood); a party still waiting after two days
is let go, four wait at most. When the party has done some of the work the chronicle keeps it with its leader
(`PlayOut.afterward` "afterstorm:kind", `AfterStorm.Over`). The year's annals say "The earth shook twice, and hail fell
on the fields once." from `disasters`, this year's and last year's counts as a short line. The old quake party
(`WeatherDisasters.QuakeOver`) is folded in; an older save's quake count and the earthquake or tornado going on are
carried over once on loading. Decided here: the leader by building or growing as the work is; hail's "broken crops cut"
became sowing again, since Rimfolk's hail destroys the young crops it flattens; a flood's "stores moved up" became the
water's leavings carried back to the stores, the game's own hauling.

**C20, the advisor remembers last winter** (`Advisor/AdvisorLastWinter.cs`, `WeatherMath.WinterBefore`). The record now
counts each season's days too cold to grow (a mean below 6 °C, the advisor's own measure of winter, `ColdBelow`), days
below freezing all day, and days the snow lay on most of the open land (`WeatherDay.cover`: the hour's look at every tenth
cell each way of unroofed land, half or more under a layer of 0.1). Last winter is the four quadrums before the one now,
seasons begun before the count was kept left out (`WeatherQuarter.counted`), spoken of only after 20 days of it and some
cold. The firewood note adds "Last winter the cold here lasted 19 days, and the coldest night was -24 °C; at today's
fires the wood in store lasts 11 such days" (the fires' own burn a day), the winter stores note how few of those days
froze, the herd's feed note the snow and the days the hay lasts, the herd in the cold note the coldest night and the
frozen days. Decided here: "its longest cold" read as the days the cold lasted, since the record keeps quadrums and a
cold spell running from one into the next is the same winter.

**C21, the autumn count of the herd** (`Animals/HerdCount.cs`, `HerdStoryMath`'s count; `Rimfolk_Dlm_HerdCount`). Each
autumn, once a year, with four head or more, between 8 and 15 on a quiet map, the herdmaster (else the best with animals)
walks the pens: a round of the herd (`DilemmaEffect_Rounds.herd`, `PlayRounds.Herd`: up to eight of the herd, nearest
first, a few minutes by each, a counting line said aloud from `Rimfolk_Pool_HerdCount`). When it is done
(`PlayAfter` "herdcount") the herd's story keeps the count and its leader (`HerdStory.head`, `headYear`, `headLeader`),
the colony is told the head by kind against last autumn's, and the chronicle keeps it. The council's question then waits
two days for its turn (`askUntil`), its texts in the flavour style with the head, the days the hay and kibble last and last
winter's cold (`[lastwinter]`; the winter ahead by the climate before the record has one): keep them all; sell the
yearlings to the next traders (`DilemmaEffect_HerdSell`: past their first stage and under a year old, nobody's own, not
bonded, named or carrying young, eight at most, kept for a season in `HerdStory.sellIds`; marked to sell in the trade
window, `TradeAdvice` reading pawn rows for them; when a trade caravan stops at its spot the counter visits the pens for
them and the colony is told; a sale is the player's, by the game's Accept, and the chronicle keeps it); or some of the
oldest to the butcher (`DilemmaEffect_HerdOldest`: the game's slaughter designation, never the leader, anyone's own,
bonded, named or carrying young, a male and a female of each kind kept; one when the hay lasts, the share it falls short
by when it doesn't, four and a third of the herd at most, `SlaughterCount`). Decided here: the question asked as the
planting day's and the seasons' are, after the count; "yearlings" as under a year old; the oldest never the herd's leader;
a sale lapses after 30 days with a message; the counter only visits the pens when the traders come (Rimfolk never sells
by itself, and an animal led out of its pen is roped back by the game's handlers).

**C22, the colony's animals at the line** (`Defense/DefenseLinesWatch.cs`, `DefenseLineMath`). While a raid is on, the
watch follows the colony's animals too: each one's own records when first seen (`PawnsDowned`, `Kills`), the line it fights
at (it went for a raider since the last look, within 30 cells of a gate), and one downed or killed near a line, counted
there once. At the raid's end each is counted at its line with the enemies it brought down (the greater of its downings
and kills, `Brought`), and the kind's word kept when all were one kind. A lesson "Keep the dogs back from the line: three
of the colony's animals were downed or killed there" when two or more fell (or one that brought nobody down), and a note
"The dogs held their ground here" beside the lessons when they brought enemies down and none fell. An animal that brought
one down has it on its card (`AnimalTempers.Noted`) and its person writes it (`Rimfolk_Journal_AnimalAtLine`), unless the
fight came to them (the pets' own heroics, `Strangers/Pets.cs`, say that). The game's own rules for animals in fights
are untouched; nothing is added to the harm budget.

**C28, the lines in today's weather** (`UI/DefenseLinesPanel.cs`, `DefenseLinesWatch`). Read in the 1.6 code
(`Verse/ShotReport.HitReportFor`): the aim of every shot is multiplied by the weather's accuracy factor
(`WeatherManager.CurWeatherAccuracyMultiplier`, eased between weathers) when the shooter or the target is unroofed, for
any shooter, turrets too, unless a unique weapon ignores accuracy maluses; melee is not a shot. While today's weather
takes a tenth or more off, a line's card says so in percent ("at 50% of its usual aim" in fog), a raid that comes in it
has one message saying so, and the raid's lessons keep a note ("The raid came in fog") beside the others
(`Lesson.Weather`, `DefenseLineRaid.weather`, `aim`). A held line keeps its art tale beside the two notes
(`ArtTalesMath.Held`).

**C24, a cup for the sick** (`Immersion/SickCup.cs`, `SickCupMath.cs`). Once an hour (the council's), in waking hours (7
to 21), on a quiet home map, one set going every two hours at most: someone with a cold, a cough or a sore throat (a head
or chest cold, a smoke, rimrot, post-flu, pollution, lingering, smoker's or spore cough, showing) who hasn't had a cup
today is brought one by the colonist at their leisure (`SmallHabits.CanListen`), not ill themselves, who thinks best of
them (opinion 0 or more). The first of the player's drinks in the stores the sick one will have (`FirstPot.WillDrink`:
the drug policy, a faith, teetotalism): Vanilla Brewing Expanded - Coffees and Teas' mint, lemon, breakfast, green and earl
grey teas, Vanilla Brewing Expanded's tea, Vanilla Christmas Expanded's hot cocoa, Alpha Bees' honey, Vanilla Factions
Expanded - Medieval 2's raw honey. The bringer carries it over (`JobDriver_SickCup`), sets it down beside them with a line
(`Rimfolk_Pool_SickCup`, by tea, cocoa or honey), and the sick one drinks it there (the game's `Ingest`). The ailment's
severity eases by 0.04 (some five hours off a head cold; one almost gone is left to go), and the two think a little better
of each other (`Rimfolk_SickCup_Got`, `_Gave`, two days). Under the "Small habits" setting; none of it without one of the
mods. Decided here: Vanilla Cooking Expanded has no honey in the player's mods (the proposal's `VCE_Honey`), so the
honey is Alpha Bees' and Vanilla Factions Expanded - Medieval 2's; the teas the mods have besides the three named are
brought too, mint and lemon first; no vanilla fallback, since the game has no hot drink (as with the first pot).

**C30, the Almanac's pages for the mods** (`Defs/AlmanacArticleDefs/Almanac_Mods_I_Integrations.xml`,
`Defs/IntegrationDefs/Council_Mods_Support.xml`). New pages for the mods these integrations and the gods' two rounds use
that had none: Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Dryads, Dragons Descent, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded, Vanilla Christmas
Expanded and Vanilla Factions Expanded - Medieval 2, each what the mod is and what the colony's people do with it, no god
said to do anything; the "With Rimfolk" of Vanilla Brewing Expanded, Alpha Bees, Vanilla Events Expanded, Vanilla Cooking
Expanded (Vanilla Fishing Expanded's fishers) and the weather, animals, defense lines and ailments pages brought up to
date; rows in the compatibility table for each (and the three existing rows extended). Possessed Weapons, Sanguinary
Animals and Demigryphs have no page: no integration built uses them.

**A ninth art tale** (the lead's addition): a named season a believer took for a god's doing (C18's `SeasonGods.Named`),
`Rimfolk_Tale_SeasonTaken`: the believer, the season's name, the god by `ArtTales.GodWords` and said as the believer's
view, once in a quadrum at most at a home.

- **Saved:** `WeatherBook` (`stormsOn`, `afterWaiting`, `disasters`, short lines; the days' `cover` and the seasons'
  cold, frozen and snow days in their packed lines), `HerdStory` (`countYear`, `headYear`, `head`, `headLeader`,
  `askUntil`, `sellIds` modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`, `sellUntil`), `DefenseLineRaid` (`animalsFought`,
  `animalsBrought`, `animalsDowned`, `animalKind`, `weather`, `aim`). An older save loads with none of it.
- **Dev mode** ("Rimfolk", "Land: ..."): a disaster's work party now; last winter as the advisor reads it; a made-up last
  winter; the herd's autumn count now; its question now; traders stop for the yearlings now; a raid's notes on the first
  defense line; a cup for a colonist, ill (a head cold given if they have nothing).
- **Tests:** `LandLifeTests` (the rules, the defs, the words, the player's mods, the seams), the three pools in
  `ImmersionTests`, the ninth tale in `GodsIntegrationTests`.

## Ticking

Every system keeps its own clock; nothing is merged into one scheduler. What they share is the list of ticks in
`Source/ColonyCouncil/Lean/Sched.cs`: each hourly pass has a tick of the hour to itself, at least 90 ticks from the
next, and none lands on a tick of the short 250-tick passes (Tools/Tests checks both). The council's hour, which used to
run twenty-odd systems on one tick, runs in four parts in its old order, and its day in two halves, so the first hour of
a day (where most daily work happens) is spread over the hour too. The per-colonist passes (the heart, ailments, health
stories) take a tenth of the colony every 250 ticks (`Sched.Slices`, by ID), so each colonist still comes round once
an hour and no tick carries the whole colony. "Tick" below is the tick of the hour (0 to 2499), of the 250-tick cycle
or of the day.

What many passes ask about a map is worked out once and shared (`Lean/MapFacts.cs`): whether a threat is on the map (as
of this 250-tick stretch), the homes and their seat (the same, `Lean/Homes.cs`), and for the hour the colonists at
home, the days of food, the medicine and the colony's beds. The first pass to ask in its stretch works it out; the
rest read it. The heart's map context, decrees, the life checks behind dilemmas, the advisor, ambition goals,
autonomy, encounters, social events, nuisances, the calendar, Rimfolk's events, world situations, scenarios, story
chains, nemeses, camps, play-outs, the fights pass and the worn-out episode read from it. (A downed victim after a fight is still judged at that moment.)
`Lean/Fresh.cs` holds the rules for how long such an answer holds; Tools/Tests checks them.

**Worked out when asked, not on a clock.** The advisor's advice (24 checks on a map) is refreshed at most once an hour,
when the alert or the council tab reads it; the inspector's strain line is built when the heart changes; Rimfolk's tabs
and pages rebuild their models every half second to second while open (UiCache, the Mood, Story and Culture tabs' and
the Social tab column's own caches).

**Called by the game often (no clock of their own).** These must stay cheap:
- *The ways' levers* (`StoryDirection.Factor`, asked by Rimfolk's events' chances in the storyteller's pools, the camps'
  morning, the harm budget's reckoning every 250 ticks and the rest at their own passes): the active way is the
  direction's def (a dictionary lookup) or the storyteller's extension, then a few multiplications; the deeds are read
  once a day.
- *Situational moods* (asked for every colonist every few seconds): heart strain, the colony's ways, decrees, trust,
  quirks, vendettas, heirlooms, a goal within reach, the comet, everyday pressures, ailments and
  convalescence. Each answers from data worked out on the hour (a dictionary or a short loop, no LINQ), and the
  convalescent moods look at the hediff before anything else. The colony's ways keep each colonist's approval until
  the ways move (or 250 ticks, `Lean/Fresh.cs`).
- *The social tie mood* (asked for every pair of colonists): one dictionary lookup in an index rebuilt only when ties
  change.
- *Mood totals*: Rimfolk's memories scale themselves (a small moment carries its own size), and the postfix on
  `ThoughtHandler.MoodOffsetOfGroup` applies good things growing ordinary, a share per kind worked out at most every
  250 ticks per colonist (`GoodLife.Refresh`). A
  decree's mood finds its decree in a map built once.
- *Global work speed* (StatPart_HeartStrain): one dictionary lookup.
- *Conversation weights*: each Rimfolk interaction is weighed every time two colonists talk; def-name endings, a
  moment's tie kind and need are read once. Gossip picks its story once per pair every 250 ticks (an opinion and a
  sight check once per subject, only for a story that could win). Conversations work out all their topics' shares
  once per pair and tick (the topic's scene once an hour per map, the news' heat every 250 ticks).
- *The reputation opinion* (asked for every pair of colonists): one dictionary lookup in what each makes of the other,
  worked out again only when a deed or a knower changes (at most every 30 ticks) and once an hour for fading.
- *Per frame*: the inspector line (a string join), the Needs tab's extra tooltip lines and its summary line (each
  cached half a second), the
- *Per frame*: the colonist bar's badges (a dictionary lookup per portrait, the facts worked out once a second), the
  inspector line (a string join), the Needs tab's extra tooltip lines (cached half a second), the
  Social tab's width (a cached model and a field write), its rows' extra tooltip line (cached a second per pair), alert
  labels (rebuilt only when they change), the slow-time buttons (labels translated once, tooltips only on hover), a
  lucky thing's inspect line and description (a lookup by thing id, nothing while no thing is lucky). Windows and tabs
  keep a model and draw from it: the floor picker keeps each floor's research, cost, material, stats and tooltip for a
  second (at once again after a pick), the decree page lays out its cards with what stands in a decree's way once a
  second, the Mood tab builds its groups, rows, headings and hint buttons with its half-second model and draws only
  the rows in sight, the Almanac's cards their
  "Column: value" lines with their layout.
- *Picking a line*: every line Rimfolk says goes through Flavor, which takes each tagged line apart once
  (`Lean/LineTags.cs`, with what a shipped line needs besides its tags, `Lean/ShippedLines.cs`, looked up the first time)
  and only compares after that; the moment's tags (trait:, skill:, weather:) are built once per def.
- *Defs by name*: looked up once and kept (`Lean/DefRef.cs`), misses too; caches keyed by defs start over each game.
- *Harmony patches on the game's own events* (a memory gained, a meal eaten, a death, a letter, a raid, a goodwill
  change, a trade, a quest's end): run when the event happens. Only the wind guard patches a tick method
  (`WindManager.WindManagerTick`, a few checks).

Ailments and health stories, once on one tick of the hour each, are spread like the heart. Ailments count the colony's
serious illnesses before every slice (as they did before every hour's rolls) and give at most one new one in the
colony's room for it, so a colonist's rolls see the colony as it is; the catching clock still runs once an hour on its
old tick.

**Where to look.** `Tools/perf_audit.py` reads the code and ranks every entry point by estimated cost (how often it
runs times what it does, loops weighed by what they go over): `docs/perf-audit.md`, with the ranking before this pass
beside it. Estimates, not measurements; a profiler pass in a long save is still to come.

**Rimfolk's clock (measured).** Every pass with a slot in `Sched` (hourly, every 250 ticks, waiting, daily, the
people log) is timed where it runs: `Lean/PassClock.cs` reads `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp` before and after it (a struct
scope, nothing allocated) and keeps per pass its runs and time in this in-game hour and day and the ones before
(rolled on by game ticks), and the worst run since loading; nothing is saved. The table of passes is
`Lean/PassClockMath.cs` (Tools/Tests: every slot has a pass, every pass is timed); systems sharing a slot (four at 149)
have a pass each. Timing changes nothing a pass does: same tick, same order, no random numbers, exceptions as before.
The dev window "Rimfolk's clock" (Debug actions, Rimfolk) lists the passes by cost, with runs and milliseconds in the
last whole hour and day (the one so far until the clock has seen a whole one), the average and worst run, the totals
and Rimfolk's average share of a tick (60 ticks are a second at normal speed), then the sizes of the main saved stores
and the world's objects and pawns; hover a line for when it runs. Its model is built at most every half second.

There is no dispatcher: each system still checks its own tick. One component running the passes would move them to
its own place in the game's loop over components, past work that can share their tick in components whose place
differs from save to save (a talk's next line every 15 ticks, the visual touches every 30, the council meeting every
60, the ailments' and health stories' queued work on any tick), so it would not be provably the same; and the game
calls every component's tick anyway, so it would save one comparison per component per tick.

## Save size

Everything Rimfolk saves has a fixed size, a cap, or is pruned of the dead, the departed and the old. The caps are in
`Source/ColonyCouncil/Lean/Caps.cs` and the trackers themselves. "Known" means a pawn the game still has (alive or dead,
on a map, in the world or in a caravan), so such a record is let go when the game itself lets go of the pawn.

| Saved | Cap or pruning |
|---|---|
| Chronicle | none of its own: the colony's view of the world history below (`Chronicle.cs`); an older save's 300-line list is read on load and taken into the history |
| Journals | 60 lines each; journals of those no longer with the colony: the 30 written in most lately; grief already written about: cleared at 500; everyday moments: forgotten after 24 days |
| Annals | the year in progress (from one landing day to the next, reset by the year's letter); 40 written years |
| Day samples (history) | 120 days |
| Wishes | open ones only; recent wishes 20 days or 60; cooldowns dropped once over |
| Trust | one record per colonist, the gone dropped daily; 8 log lines; grants of the last 30 days |
| Social web | ties of the dead dropped daily, of those gone faded out; 40 lost bonds; pair tones (moment memory) forgotten after 4 quiet days or when one of the two is gone; one short line per pair of colonists who met (Social/Bonds.cs: how well they know each other, fights side by side, seats lost), dropped once the two have not both been among the colony's people for 60 days |
| Groups | groups of 3 to 9, the dead and departed dropped daily (and anyone the game has let go of, at saving, so no reference is saved to nobody), a group ended when fewer than two are left; 14 history lines, 10 former names and the rivalries with groups still there each; newcomers 40 days at most; 12 past groups (those the game still knows); work samples of colonists only, 6 kinds each |
| Dreams | 80 recent dreams (a discarded dreamer kept by name only); omens until they come; dream counts of known pawns. The session-only maps (last dream, untold dream) drop the dead and whatever is too old to matter |
| Life goals | goals of the dead and departed end daily; finished ones of the dead kept 3 years, of discarded pawns dropped; counters of known pawns; sparks 30 days; a goal chosen by a change of heart is marked (one value) |
| Secrets | one per colonist, ended with their death; who was rolled for one: known pawns only |
| Vendettas | 40 settled; avengers dead or discarded dropped; eulogies until given |
| Quirks | 2 per colonist, the dead and discarded dropped; fights and falls only within the longest quirk window. Sights (the pyre), the lamp's visits and a juggler's last turn are held for the session only, a few days at most |
| Legacy | heirlooms until the heir dies or is discarded, or the thing is lost; children waiting to come of age: known pawns only; came of age: 6 days |
| Nemeses | 30 that have ended |
| Pets | animals known: the dead get their farewell, the discarded are dropped |
| The animals' natures | by id, never by reference: temperaments 300 (unseen 120 days let go), pairs, friends and rivals 80 (pairs first; apart 40 days, or a friend missed 30 days, let go), animals gone alive 30 with their handler (120 days, or the handler dead) |
| Autonomy | who acted when: the last 2 days, not the dead; plans until built |
| Rimfolk's events | raids until they come; the departed 2 years (unless asked about); memos 3 years (children's 10), used ones a day; quests already told of: those the game still keeps; the event timer, one per home (a home lost takes its own) |
| Magic among the peoples | the visitors of the peoples who cast a spell for the colony this visit, by id, dropped when they leave the homes, forty at most (Peoples/Magic/PeoplesMagicWatch.cs) |
| Homes | one entry per colonist who has been on a home (the last home they lived on), forgotten once they're dead, discarded or no longer the colony's; the stored seat; the homes at the last look |
| World ledger | its own ties (grudges, favours, good words, claims, the scenario's debt, fealty, a notable's and a regular's regard): three of a kind between the same two, sixty of a kind (three hundred regards), closed ones dropped after sixty days; a grudge's dead ten at most over all peoples, two years; persons while a notable, named by a tie or kept in the world, with their reasons; towns while a notable lives there or while they stand within the region map's reach of a home (the nearest 40 a home), a gone one two years; the founding families of new towns, two per town, six members each by first name, going with the town's record; the towns being built within reach, six at most, dropped when built or gone; the counter for ledger numbers |
| The region | one part per colony (when a new town last wrote to it and last welcomed it), a lost home's kept 30 days; the towns in detail and remoteness are worked out, not saved |
| World history | 800 entries (every chronicle line, every answer with its six values, the peoples' deeds, the ledger's ties); everyday ones past sixty days folded into one per actor, kind and season; milestones (the chronicle's) kept longest; over the bound older seasons' summaries go first, the newest 200 always stay |
| Everyday pressures | per colonist, the gone dropped daily; 12 meals; frames and plans while they stand |
| Character | 5 ways; 30 recent shifts; the colony's traits one per trait, today's tallies emptied each day; the colony's one name as last looked at, one line |
| Decrees, dilemmas, offices, names, encounters, ambitions | one entry per def, office or title, and how each name held holds (one line per name) (decrees, dilemmas, offices and ambitions for each colony's council; a lost home's kept 30 days); a curfew's night hours per colonist while it lasts, then only for those away (the dead, those no longer the colony's and those the game no longer knows let go); the colony's founders: those here in its first two days |
| Heart | one per colonist, the gone dropped hourly |
| Character marks | a person's record (sides moved, marks, views): the colony's own people the game still knows, empty records dropped at saving; 12 marks per person (small ones go first, each let go after its keeping, turning points three times as long); what the marks watch: per person, the last 8 fights won (a year), their addictions and their last breakdown (5 days), known pawns only; skills mastered: known pawns, 800 at most |
| Traits that change | changes made: known pawns only, 8 per person, 200 in all; what each colonist is watched for: deeds counted 240 days (12 per kind), 10 snapshots of a few records, when they were last unsettled; the once-in-a-colony changes (2 keys) |
| Ailments | by pawn: last ailments 120 days, known pawns only; by hediff: only hediffs colonists still have; illnesses and injuries an ailment may follow: until over or healed, known pawns only; the shared illness budget: one ledger per home (a debt or two, each paid, let go as the game's own comes all the same, or let go within two to five years; the game's last disease and skip; the counts; the last record line), gone with the home or once all of it is older than a debt is kept |
| Hurts from everyday life | each colonist's last Rimfolk-made hurt, pruned past three days (daily and at saving); each home's last evening drill, a map gone dropped; what the day's work counted and the evening's bouts not saved |
| Health stories | healers, beds, convalescence, hard times not over yet: known pawns only; losses 30 days; tends 3 days; setbacks and trust lines 20 days; visits 30 days; cases while the patient lives |
| Calendar | at most 12 days written by the colony and 8 named by the player (traditions and the founding day stay); days about people who are gone let go; days taken off by hand grow only with the player's clicks; who is away and each colonist's hunt: the colony's own only; crops grown: one per crop |
| Personal stories | stories under way; 200 past; eulogies until given |
| Camps | one camp; its lists (and the asks made of it) go with it, pruned of the gone at saving |
| Journeys | one plan at a time: its travellers, animals, packing list, the last hours' steps done and the timetable hours it changed, all gone when they set off or it's called off |
| World situations | 2 running; 40 past, each with what followed from it (once per def) |
| Story chains, missions | chains 120 days after they end; missions 2 days |
| Answers playing out | waiting ones 10 at most, done ones dropped (their people, places, hunt and search routes with them); how the last 30 went, for the dilemmas page; the colony's pace, one count a home (gatherings of the last ten days, the season's custom, life goals' toasts waiting five days at most), homes no longer ours dropped |
| Defense lines | per home map, gone with it; only the lines the player makes: one mark per step done or set aside, 24 plans, the last 5 raids (4 downed and 3 lessons each); the raid under way only while it lasts |
| Scenario parts | fixed by the scenario (its days, its seats) |
| Faction memory | 12 deeds per people (the settled and the faintest make way); a deed is dropped once it fades below 1, and with its people when they're gone; who tended or freed whom: 60 notes, 30 days, dropped when the stranger dies |
| Faith (the people) | one record per colonist whose faith moved or is watched (when talk last swayed or steadied them, their last crisis, the demand of their faith weighing on them), known pawns only, empty ones dropped; 5 faith moments each, 120 days; crises waiting to be felt, one per kind per colonist, 6 days; which pairs talked about faith lately not saved |
| Views and shared memories | views with the person's record (`PawnPersona.stances`), a view about a newcomer let go once they've been here 60 days or are gone; shared memories 8 per pair, 3 of one kind, and 600 in all (the faintest go at once past 660, and at saving the faded ones and those of people the game no longer knows); a fight is remembered only by those seen side by side in it, 3 partners each; the talk's news 40 notes, a month at most; who talked to whom lately and talks under way not saved |
| Reputation | 10 deeds per colonist and 220 in all (the faintest make way), 30 knowers a deed; a deed faded to nearly nothing is dropped, and daily those of the dead and departed and anything the dead knew; one packed number per colonist for the names told |
| Faith and the council | each faith's last evening of faith (one per faith, let go after 60 days or with the faith); the evening waiting to be held (one); the faith a decree names; who heard which faith spoken for lately (one per colonist, 30 days, 40 at most) |
| Other mods' people | best-friend pairs of known pawns, 200 at most |
| Advisor (per map) | 60 days of wealth samples |

How big it gets: `Tools/save_estimate.py` models every saved collection (293) with its rule and plays five in-game
years in a colony of 20 (`docs/save-size.md`). Nothing grows without end; Rimfolk's part of a five-year save comes to
about 2.2 MB: a fifth of it the journals, and about as much again people's records and their shared memories.
`--strict` fails on a saved collection with no model, so a new one needs its rule written down.

Pawn references: a saved reference to a pawn the game has discarded is written as nothing, so every such record was
already dropped on the next load. The trackers above now drop or forget them while playing too, so a long session
doesn't hold on to pawns the game has let go of. No storage format changed.

## Roadmap

**Done in 0.1**
- Advisor with 14 checks and rotating tips, plus an alert for urgent advice.
- 23 wish types, six tones each, petitions, Kind colonists asking for others, ascetics
  skipping luxuries, Gentle / Demanding / Advisor-only modes.
- Council meetings with three pitched ambitions, heckling, rewards for success.
- Room templates with ghost placement, rotation, material choice and "find a good spot".
- Personal touches in colonists' own bedrooms.
- Royalty (noble room requirements), Biotech (children) and Odyssey (space maps) handled.

**Done in 0.2**
- Room planner panel (works from the council tab and the "rooms" button in the bottom bar): rotate, mirror,
  move the door, per-element materials, furniture variants, cost against stock, site clearing (cut, mine,
  replace own buildings, smooth stone) with queued blueprints. 32 templates with good-practice tips.
- Trust, promises, refusals, reminders, self-help, jealousy, event-triggered wishes, data-driven effects,
  tagged context-aware lines and scenes.
- Physical council meetings: a gathering lord job at a fitting venue, pitches and banter above heads, votes,
  and a decision letter at the end.
- Ten more advisor checks from good-practice research; 31 ambitions.
- The Almanac tab (framework; content being written from wiki-checked research).

**Done in 0.3**
- Counterweights to permanent good mood: rising standards, decrees that trade mood for output, dilemmas with
  real costs, bitter colonists who may walk out.
- Decree petitions, names (epithets), anniversaries, yearly annals, personal journals.

**Done in 0.4 (Rimfolk)**
- Traditions: seasonal choices repeated become expected.
- Council offices with yearly elections.
- The social web: friends, rivals, comrades, mentors and circles that form and fade from opinion, battles and
  council decisions, daily social events, social dilemmas, and bonds feeding back into votes, objections,
  petitions and trust.
- Dreams drawn from each colonist's recent memories, injuries, bonds and losses; most are flavour (mood,
  journal, a line told over breakfast), a few change something, and rare omens schedule the incident they
  foretell.

**Feelings and strain**
- Strain under mood (bands, a mood of its own, a work speed part, darker dreams, a day off at the end of the rope),
  twenty data-driven feelings that nudge wishes, moments, dreams and strain, four needs of the heart, the days of rest
  decree, and the Heart section of the Mood tab, the inspector line and RimHUD lines.

**Ideas for later**
- Ambition chains (multi-step goals across seasons).
- More Ideology hooks (precept-driven wishes, ritual spaces).
- Translations.

---

## References and prior art

No existing mod was found that does pawn-driven building requests or a colony advisor
in this form. Closest:

- ["Dream and Desire" idea thread](https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/2697015438/3199243752762917307):
  pawns wanting specific apparel and equipment based on traits and backstory (concept only, as far as we could tell).
- [RimWorld Wiki: Expectations](https://rimworldwiki.com/wiki/Expectations) and [Thoughts list](https://rimworldwiki.com/wiki/Thoughts_list): the vanilla systems the wishes build on.
- [RimWorld Wiki: Colony Building Guide](https://rimworldwiki.com/wiki/Colony_Building_Guide): its "current plan and next plan" advice is what the Advisor tries to automate.
- Design inspirations: The Sims 2 wants and fears, Dwarf Fortress noble mandates, Frostpunk promises.
